Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, may He be exalted and remembered, words: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfill [your] contracts﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "O you who have believed, fulfill," He, may His praise be lofty, means: O you who have acknowledged the oneness of God, submitted to Him in servitude, surrendered to Him divinity [In the printed edition: "al-Uluhiyya," but I have kept what is in the manuscript], and affirmed His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in his prophethood and in what has come to them from their Lord of the laws of His religion: "fulfill the contracts." That is: fulfill the covenants you have made with your Lord and the contracts you have concluded with Him, by which you have imposed rights upon yourselves and obligated yourselves to God with duties. Complete them by fulfilling, perfecting and completing what you have bound yourselves to toward God, and toward whomever among you you have contracted with, by what you have made binding upon yourselves toward him. Do not break them, so as to annul them after their confirmation. [See the explanation of "awfa" above: 1:557; 3:348; 6:526.]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the "contracts" which God, may His praise be lofty, commanded to be fulfilled in this verse, after all of them agreed that the meaning of "contracts" is covenants.

Some of them said: they are the contracts by which the people of the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyya) bound one another to support, back and assist one another against whoever sought to wrong them or intended them harm; and that is the meaning of the "alliance" (hilf) which they used to contract among themselves.

Those who said that the meaning of "contracts" is covenants:

10893 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "fulfill the contracts": he said, meaning: the covenants.

10894 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, may He be mighty and majestic: "fulfill the contracts," he said: the covenants.

10895 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10896 – Sufyan related to us, he said: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, the same. [Report 10896: in the manuscript: "Sufyan related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Sufyan related to us, from a man..." which is an error and a slip; it is a recurring chain in the tafsir: Sufyan ibn Waki', from his father Waki', from Sufyan al-Thawri.]

10897 – Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: Ubayd Allah related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: We sat with Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, and with him there was a man who was speaking to them, and he said: "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts," and he said: they are the covenants. [Report 10897: "Ubayd Allah" is Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-Absi, known as Badhdham; his biography has passed under nos. 2092, 2219, 5796, 7758. In the printed edition it reads here "Ubayd Allah from Ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi," which is an error, corrected in the following chains nos. 10935, 10957, 10963.]

10898 – Al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "fulfill the contracts," he said: the covenants.

10899 – Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts," he said: they are the covenants.

10900 – It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: "fulfill the contracts," [meaning] the covenants.

10901 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada regarding His words "fulfill the contracts," he said: the covenants.

10902 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "fulfill the contracts," he said: they are the covenants.

10903 – Al-Harith related to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: I heard al-Thawri say: "fulfill the contracts," he said: the covenants.

10904 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "al-'Uqud" is the plural of "'aqd," and the origin of "al-'aqd" is tying a thing to another, which is joining it to it, as a rope is tied to a rope when it is joined to it by a knot. It is said from it: "So-and-so contracted (a'qada) between him and so-and-so a contract ('aqd), and he contracts it," and from it is the saying of al-Hutay'a:

A people who, when they contract a covenant for their neighbour, / they tighten the 'inaj and tighten above it the karab

[Diwan: 6; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:145; Lisan (k-r-b) ('-n-j). From his qasida that he composed about al-Zibriqan ibn Badr and Baghid ibn Amir of the Banu Anf al-Naqa, in which he praised Baghid and his people, saying: "A people who are the nose, and others are the tail, / and who equates the tail with the nose of the she-camel!
A people whose neighbour sleeps with eyes at rest, / when they twist the strands of their tent-ropes into a rope,
A people who, when they contract…..."]

This is a proverb he struck. He says: when they make a contract and a pledge of protection for the neighbour, they make the contract firm upon themselves, so that he is more content in his eye through their support of him and their protection of his honour and property. The example is given by the bucket, with which one draws water and benefits. The "'inaj" is a cord that is fastened to the bottom of the bucket, then fastened to its handle or to one of its ears, so that when the bucket's main rope breaks, the 'inaj holds the bucket from falling into the well. The "karab" is the rope tied onto the bucket after the "mannin," which is the first rope; when the mannin breaks, the karab remains. This is the proverb: they secured it for him by the covenant, as they secured his bucket with a rope after a rope, so that it is safe from severing.

That is when he makes a pact with him concerning a matter and covenants with him to fulfill to him what he has contracted with him, of protection and guarantee, or support, or marriage, or sale, or partnership, or other contracts.

* *

Mention of those who said the meaning we have mentioned concerning the intended sense of His words "fulfill the contracts":

10905 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts," i.e., the contract of the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyya). It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: "Fulfill the contract of the jahiliyya, but do not create a contract in Islam." And it was mentioned to us that Furat ibn Hayyan al-Ijli asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the alliance of the jahiliyya, and the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps you are asking about the alliance of Lakhm and Taym Allah?" He said: "Yes, O Prophet of God!" He said: "Islam only increases it in strength."

10906 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatada: "fulfill the contracts," he said: the contracts of the jahiliyya: the alliance.

* *

Others said: rather, they are the oaths which God took from His servants by faith in Him and obedience to Him, concerning what He made lawful for them and forbade them.

Those who said that:

10907 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abd Allah informed us, he said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words "fulfill the contracts," he said, meaning: what He made lawful and what He forbade, and what He prescribed, and what He set limits to in the whole Qur'an, so do not betray and do not break. Then he emphasized that by saying: "And those who break the covenant of God after its ratification and sever what God has commanded to be joined…" up to "the evil abode" [Qur'an 13:35].

10908 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "fulfill the contracts," [meaning] what God has bound upon the servants of what He made lawful for them and forbade them.

* *

Others said: rather, they are the contracts which people make among themselves, and which a person binds upon himself.

Those who said that:

10909 – Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, he said: my father related to me, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from his brother Abd Allah ibn Ubayda, who said: The contracts are five: the bond of oaths, the bond of marriage, the bond of covenant, the bond of sale, and the bond of alliance.

10910 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Waki' related to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi – or from his brother Abd Allah ibn Ubayda – similarly.

10911 – Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts": the bond of covenant, the bond of oath, the bond of alliance, the bond of partnership, and the bond of marriage. He said: these are the contracts, five.

10912 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Utba ibn Sa'id al-Hims related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, he said: my father related to us, regarding the saying of God, may He be mighty and majestic: "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts," he said: the contracts are five: the bond of marriage, the bond of partnership, the bond of oath, the bond of covenant, and the bond of alliance. [Report 10912: "Utba ibn Sa'id al-Hims" passed under no. 8966.]

* *

Others said: rather, this verse is a command from God, may He be exalted, to the People of the Book to fulfill what their covenant was taken for, from acting upon what is in the Torah and the Gospel concerning the confirmation of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what has come to them from God.

Those who said that:

10913 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij: "fulfill the contracts," he said: the covenants which God took from the People of the Book: that they would act upon what has come to them.

10914 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: al-Layth related to me, he said: Yunus related to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I read the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) which he wrote to Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Najran [In the printed edition: "sent him to Najran," but I have kept what is in the manuscript]; the letter was with Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, and in it: "This is a declaration from God and His Messenger: 'O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts,'" and he wrote the verses from it until reaching "Indeed God is swift in reckoning." [Report 10914: Abu Ja'far related the letter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in al-Tarikh 3:157; it is in Ibn Hisham's Sira 4:241, Futuh al-Buldan of al-Baladhuri: 77, and elsewhere.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in our view is what Ibn Abbas said, and that its meaning is: Fulfill, O you who have believed, the contracts of God which He made obligatory upon you, and which He established concerning what He made lawful for you and forbade you, and imposed His obligation upon you, and clarified its limits for you.

We have only said that this is more correct than the other sayings because God, may His praise be lofty, followed that clarification of what He made lawful and forbidden for His servants, and what He made obligatory upon them of His duties. Thus it was known by that that His words "fulfill the contracts" are a command from Him to His servants to act upon what He imposed upon them of His duties and contracts following that, and a prohibition from Him to them against breaking what He has contracted upon them from Him; and also that His words "fulfill the contracts" are a command from Him to fulfill every contract He permitted, so it is not permissible for anything of it to be excluded unless a proof of the particular exclusion is established, to which submission is obligatory. Since the matter in this is as we have described, there is no sense in the saying of one who directs this to the meaning of commanding the fulfillment of some of the contracts which God commanded to be fulfilled, to the exclusion of others.

* *

As for His words "awfu" (fulfill), the Arabs have two dialects concerning it:
One of them is "awfu," from the speaker's saying: "I fulfilled to so-and-so his covenant, I fulfill to him it."
The other is from their saying: "I fulfilled to him his covenant, I fulfill (afi)."
[See the explanation of "awfa" above: 1:557–559; 3:348; 6:526.]

And "fulfilling the covenant" (al-iyfa' bil-'ahd) is completing it according to the permissible conditions to which it was contracted.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning "beheemat al-an'am" (the beasts of grazing livestock) which God, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned in this verse as having made lawful for us.

Some of them said: they are all the livestock animals.

Those who said that:

10915 – Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, he said: Abd al-A'la related to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: "beheemat al-an'am" are the camels, cattle and sheep.

10916 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock": he said: all of the livestock.

10917 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ibn Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock," he said: all of the livestock.

10918 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas regarding His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock," he said: all of the livestock. [Omitted from numbering: 10919.]

10920 – It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "beheemat al-an'am," they are the livestock.

* *

Others said: rather, by His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock" He meant the fetuses of livestock found in the bellies of their mothers when they are slaughtered or sacrificed, [being] carrion.

Those who said that:

10921 – Al-Harith ibn Muhammad related to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz related to us, he said: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fazari informed us, from Atiyya al-Awfi, from Ibn Umar regarding His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock": he said: what is in their bellies. I said: If it comes out dead, does one eat it? He said: Yes.

10922 – Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Zakariyya related to us, from Idris al-Awdi, from Atiyya, from Ibn Umar similarly – and he added in it: he said: Yes, it is in the position of its lungs and its liver.

10923 – Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki' related to us, both said: Jarir related to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The fetus is from the beasts of grazing livestock, so eat it.

10924 – Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: my father related to us, from Mis'ar – and Sufyan, from Qabus – from his father, from Ibn Abbas: that a cow was slaughtered and a fetus was found in its belly, and Ibn Abbas took hold of the fetus's tail and said: this is from the beasts of grazing livestock that have been made lawful for you.

10925 – Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is from the beasts of grazing livestock.

10926 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Asim and Mu'ammal both related to us, both said: Sufyan related to us, from Qabus, from his father, who said: We slaughtered a cow, and in its belly there was a fetus; we asked Ibn Abbas, and he said: this is from the beasts of grazing livestock.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two sayings in this regard is the saying of the one who said: by His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock" He meant all the livestock: their fetuses, their young, and their adults. Because the Arabs do not hesitate to call all of that "beheema" and "bahaim," and God did not specify any part of it over another. So it remains on its generality and apparent meaning, until a proof of its specification is established, to which submission is obligatory.

* *

As for "al-an'am" (the grazing livestock), it is, in the Arabs' usage, a name specifically for camels, cattle and sheep, as His, may His praise be lofty, words state: ﴿And the livestock He created for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat﴾ [Qur'an 16:5], then He said: ﴿And the horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment﴾ [Qur'an 16:8], distinguishing the kind of livestock from other kinds of animals. [See the explanation of "al-an'am" above: 6:254.]

As for "its beasts" (bahaimuha), they are its young. We have only said that the adults among them also bear the name "beheema," just as the young do, because the meaning of the saying "beheemat al-an'am" is like His words "young of the livestock." Since the meaning of birth does not drop from it after maturity, likewise the name "beheema" does not drop from it after maturity.

* *

Some people have said: "beheemat al-an'am" refers to their wild ones, like gazelles, wild cattle and wild asses. [This is the saying of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:298.]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning what God, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by His words "except what is recited to you." Some of them said: God meant by that: "Lawful for you are the young of the camels, cattle and sheep, except what God made clear to you in what is recited to you by His words: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion and blood﴾" – the verse [Qur'an 5:3].

Those who said that:

10927 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "beheemat al-an'am, except what is recited to you": except carrion and what is mentioned with it.

10928 – Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words "Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you": i.e., of the carrion which God forbade and set forth concerning it.

10929 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: "except what is recited to you," he said: except carrion and what over which the name of God has not been mentioned.

[1093]

Part 2 of 2 of the Commentary of al-Tabari on Surah 5, Verse 1.

10930. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿except what is recited to you﴾: the carrion, the blood, and the flesh of swine.

10931. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you﴾: the carrion and the flesh of swine.

10932. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you﴾: it is the carrion, the blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked.

* *

Others said: Rather, what Allah excepted by His saying ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ is the swine.

Mention of those who said that:

10933. Abdullah ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿except what is recited to you﴾, he said: the swine.

10934. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿except what is recited to you﴾: meaning, the swine.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this matter is the interpretation of those who said: "It means: except what is recited to you of Allah's prohibition of what He forbade you by His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you is carrion﴾," the verse. This is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepted from what He permitted to His servants of the beasts of cattle, that which He forbade them from it. And what He forbade them from it is what He clarified in His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 3]. And even if Allah forbade it to us, it is not from the beasts of cattle so that it would be excepted from them. Therefore, excepting what was forbidden to us, which is included in the whole that precedes the exception, is more fitting than excepting what was forbidden that was not included in the whole that precedes the exception.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿not violating the game while you are in the state of ihram; indeed, Allah ordains what He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "O you who have believed, fulfill the contracts" = "not violating the game while you are in ihram" = "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle." So that, according to their view, is from the postponed that means the preposed. Thus "ghayr" is in the accusative = according to the view of those who hold this opinion = as a circumstantial accusative (hal) of what is in His saying "fulfill," referring to "those who have believed."

The interpretation of the speech according to their school: O believers, fulfill the covenants of Allah which He made binding upon you in His Book, not violating the game while you are in ihram.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, the wild ones, such as gazelles, cattle and asses = "not violating the game," not deeming its hunting lawful, "while you are in ihram, except what is recited to you." So "ghayr," according to these, is in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the "kaf and mim" in His saying "lakum" (for you), with the sense: Lawful for you, O those who have believed, are the beasts of cattle, not deeming their hunting lawful while you are in your state of ihram. [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 298.]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Lawful for you are all the beasts of cattle "except what is recited to you," except that which is of the wild kind, for it is game, and it is not lawful for you while you are in ihram. Thus, whoever said this directed the speech toward the meaning: Lawful for you are all the beasts of cattle "except what is recited to you," except what is made clear to you of their wild kind, not deeming their hunting lawful while you are in ihram. So "ghayr" is in the accusative, according to them, as a circumstantial accusative from the "kaf and mim" in His saying "except what is recited to you."

Mention of those who said that:

10935. Sufyan ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: We sat with Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, and with him was a man, and he spoke to them and said: "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle," [as] game, "not violating the game while you are in ihram," then it is forbidden to you. He meant: wild cattle, gazelles, and the like. [See the chain previously mentioned, no. 10897, where it was "from Ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi"; this is the correct chain, which I verified with him. It will come again as nos. 10957, 10963.]

10936. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas regarding His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you, not violating the game while you are in ihram﴾, he said: All cattle are lawful, except that which is of the wild kind, for it is game, and it is not lawful when one is in ihram.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in this matter, in accordance with what the interpretation of the interpreters agrees upon regarding His saying "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle," that they are the cattle and their unborn young and their suckling young, and in accordance with the indication of the apparent sense of the revelation, is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: Fulfill the covenants, not violating the game while you are in ihram. Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle in your state of ihram or in your other states, except what is recited to you as forbidden of them: the carrion and the blood, and that over which other than Allah has been invoked.

This is because His saying "except what is recited to you," if its meaning were "except the game," it would have been said: "except what is recited to you of the game, not violating it." In Allah's not joining His saying "except what is recited to you" with what you mentioned, and in His mentioning the game explicitly in His saying "not violating the game," lies the clearest evidence that His saying "except what is recited to you" is a complete statement whose narrative is self-contained, and that the meaning of His saying "not violating the game" is separate from it.

Likewise, if His saying "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle" were intended to refer to wild animals, there would be no purpose in repeating the mention of the game in His saying "not violating the game," since it had been mentioned before. It would have been said: "Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle except what is recited to you, not violating its hunters while you are in ihram." In His explicit mention of the game in His saying "not violating the game" lies the clearer proof of the soundness of what we have said regarding its meaning.

* *

If someone says: Indeed the Arabs sometimes explicitly mention a thing by its name even when its name has already been mentioned? It is said: That is from their practice in cases of poetic necessity, and it is not the eloquent, commonly used form of their speech. And directing the speech of Allah toward the most eloquent of the dialects of those in whose language His speech was revealed is more fitting, where a way to it is found, than diverting it to something else.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: O you who have believed, fulfill the covenants of Allah which He has made binding upon you, concerning what He forbade and permitted, not violating the game during your state of ihram. Thus, in what He has permitted to you of the beasts of cattle that are slaughtered, apart from their carrion, there is ample provision for you, and independence from the game while you are in ihram.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah ordains what He wills (1)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Indeed Allah decrees among His creation what He wills [See the explanation of "ordains" previously: p. 324, footnote 3] of making lawful what He wishes to make lawful, forbidding what He wishes to forbid, obligating upon them what He wills to obligate, and His other rulings and decrees. So fulfill, O believers, toward Him, in what He has made binding upon you of making lawful what He made lawful for you and forbidding what He forbade you, and His other covenants, and do not break them or annul them. As:

10937. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah ordains what He wills﴾: Indeed Allah ordains what He wills among His creation, and clarifies to His servants, and imposes His obligations, sets His limits, commands obedience to Him, and forbids disobedience to Him.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of Allah's saying: "Do not violate the rites of Allah."

Some of them said its meaning is: Do not violate the sacred prohibitions of Allah, and do not transgress His limits = as if they directed "the rites" toward the landmarks, and interpreted "Do not violate the rites of Allah" as the landmarks of Allah's limits, His commands, His prohibitions and His obligations.

[Mention of those who said that]: [The text between the parentheses is an addition not found in the manuscript or the printed edition; I have included it following Abu Ja'far's method in his commentary.]

10938. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Habib al-Mu'allim narrated to us, from Ata': that he was asked about "the rites of Allah," and he said: The sacred prohibitions of Allah, avoiding the wrath of Allah, and following His obedience; that is "the rites of Allah."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: [In the printed and manuscript editions: "the meaning of His saying," which does not stand, and what I have adopted is more fitting to the correct sense.] Do not violate the sanctuary of Allah = as if they directed the meaning of His saying "the rites of Allah" to: the landmarks of the sacred precinct of Allah among the lands.

Mention of those who said that:

10939. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah," he said: As for "the rites of Allah," it is the sanctuary of Allah.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Do not violate the rites of the Hajj and thereby waste them = and as if they directed the interpretation of that to: Do not violate the landmarks of Allah's limits which He set for you in your Hajj.

Mention of those who said that:

10940. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His saying: "Do not violate the rites of Allah," he said: The rites of the Hajj.

10941. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah," he said: The polytheists used to perform Hajj to the Sacred House, offer sacrificial animals, honor the sanctity of the holy places, and trade during their pilgrimage. The Muslims wished to attack them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Do not violate the rites of Allah."

10942. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of Allah: "The rites of Allah": al-Safa and al-Marwah, the offering, and the camels; all of this is among "the rites of Allah."

10943. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to me, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Do not violate what Allah has forbidden you during your state of ihram.

Mention of those who said that:

10944. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Do not violate the rites of Allah," he said: "The rites of Allah" are what Allah has forbidden you from touching while you are in ihram.

* *

= And it seems that those who held this view directed the interpretation of that to: Do not violate the landmarks of Allah's limits which He forbade you during your ihram.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations of His saying "Do not violate the rites of Allah" is the saying of Ata' which we have mentioned [This is the report previously cited as no. 10938] in directing its meaning to: Do not violate the sacred prohibitions of Allah, and do not neglect His obligations.

* *

Because "al-sha'a'ir" is the plural of "sha'irah," and "sha'irah" is a form of "fa'ilah" from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so has become aware of this matter" (sha'ara bihi), if he knew of it. Thus "al-sha'a'ir" means the landmarks, from that. [See the explanation of "the rites of Allah" previously, vol. 3: 226-228.]

* *

If that is so, then the meaning of the speech is: Do not deem lawful, O you who have believed, the landmarks of Allah. This includes all of Allah's landmarks in the rites of the Hajj: such as forbidding what Allah has prohibited from being struck upon the one in ihram, neglecting what He forbade neglecting therein, and what He forbade of violating the sacred prohibitions of His sanctuary, and His other limits, obligations, lawful and unlawful matters, because all of that is among His landmarks and rites which He made as signs between truth and falsehood, by which His lawful and unlawful, His commands and prohibitions, are known.

And we only said that this view is more correct for the interpretation of His exalted saying "Do not violate the rites of Allah," because Allah prohibited the deeming lawful of His rites and landmarks of His limits and making them lawful in a general prohibition, without specifying any part of that over another. So it is not permissible for anyone to direct the meaning of that toward the particular except with a proof which must be accepted, and there is no such proof for that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 2 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His words: ﴿Nor the sacred month﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "Nor the sacred month," may He be exalted, He means: do not make lawful (istihlal) the sacred month by fighting your enemies among the polytheists in it. [[In the printed edition: "by fighting them in it," the correct reading being from the manuscript.]] It is like His words: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it. Say: Fighting in it is a great (sin)﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 217].

* *

Ibn 'Abbas and others said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

10945. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "Nor the sacred month," he said: i.e., do not make lawful fighting in it.

10946. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: The polytheist in that time was not barred from the House, so they were commanded not to fight in the sacred month or near the House.

* *

As for "the sacred month" that Allah meant by His words "Nor the sacred month," it is Rajab of Mudar, a month in which Mudar used to forbid fighting.

* *

It has also been said that in this place it is Dhu al-Qa'dah.

Mention of those who said this:

10947. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah, who said: It is Dhu al-Qa'dah.

* *

We have already shown the evidence for the correctness of what we have said on this earlier, in the interpretation of His words: "They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it." [[See what preceded under "the sacred month" (4:229, 300 and following), which is the place he mentioned, and before it (3:575-579). And the explanation of "the month" previously (3:440).]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Nor the offering, nor the garlands﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for "the offering" (al-hady), it is what a person presents of a camel, cow, sheep or other animal to the House of Allah, seeking nearness to Allah and seeking His reward. [[See the explanation of "al-hady" previously (4:24-25).]]

* *

Allah, mighty and majestic, says: Do not make that lawful, so that you seize it from its people by force [[In the printed edition: "so that you seize its people upon it," and in the manuscript as I have written it, except that "ʿalayhi" is written with a yā', with a fatḥa on the ʿayn and a fatḥa on the lām; it is evident that the "yā'" is really a "bā'", and that the copyist, seeing it vocalized in the parent copy, copied the vowel marks and added the diacritic dots on his own. This, and the correct sense of the speech, also requires what I have established.]] and do not prevent them from bringing what they have offered of that to the place that Allah, mighty and majestic, made its place within His Ka'bah.

It has been transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas that "al-hady" is an offering only so long as it is not garlanded.

10948. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me this, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "Nor the offering," he said: The offering is what is not garlanded; and one who has vowed to offer it and garland it.

* *

As for His words "nor the garlands," it means: do not make lawful the garlands either.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the "garlands" whose making lawful Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade.

Some of them said: By "garlands" is meant the garlands of the offering. They said: Allah, mighty and majestic, by His words "Nor the offering, nor the garlands," intended: do not make lawful the offerings, both those garlanded and those not garlanded. So His words "nor the offering" refer to what is not garlanded of the offerings; "nor the garlands" refer to what is garlanded of them. They said: By His words "nor the garlands" He indicated the meaning of what He intended of the prohibition against making lawful the garlanded offerings.

Mention of those who said this:

10949. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "nor the garlands," he said: The garlands are the garlanded offerings. When a man garlands his offering he has entered the state of ihram. If he does that while wearing his shirt, let him take it off.

* *

Others said: By that is meant the garlands that the polytheists used to hang around themselves when they wished to perform Hajj, coming toward Makkah, made of the bark of the samur tree [["Bark of the tree" (with kasra on the lām): its peel. "Samur" (with fatha on the sīn and damma on the mīm): a kind of tree with small leaves and short thorns, which has a yellow fruit that people eat, and among the acacia-type trees there is none with better timber. It is carried to the villages, and houses are roofed with it.]] and, when they went out from it returning to their dwellings, of hair.

Mention of those who said this:

10950. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "Do not make lawful the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month": He said: In the Jahiliyyah a man, when he left his house wanting Hajj, would garland himself with samur, and no one would confront him. When he returned he would garland himself with a garland of hair, and no one would confront him.

* *

Others said: Rather, a man among them would garland himself, when he wished to leave the Haram, or had left, with bark of a tree of the Haram, and by that he would be safe from the rest of the tribes of the Arabs, who might confront him with harm.

Mention of those who said this:

10951. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from 'Ata': "And the garlands": He said: They used to garland themselves with bark of the tree of the Haram, and by that they were safe when they left the Haram. Then it was revealed: "Do not make lawful the rites of Allah," the verse, "nor the offering nor the garlands."

10952. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the garlands": He said: "The garlands" is the bark on the necks of people and animals, a security for them.

10953. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10954. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "Nor the offering, nor the garlands": He said: The Arabs used to garland themselves with bark of the trees of Makkah. A man would remain in his place until the sacred months ended, and when he wished to return to his family, he would garland himself and his she-camel with bark of the tree, and so be safe until he reached his family.

10955. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And the garlands": He said: "The garlands": a man would take bark from a tree of the Haram and garland himself with it, then go wherever he wished, and be safe by that. That is the "garlands."

* *

Others said: Allah only forbade the believers, by His words "nor the garlands," from pulling up any of the trees of the Haram and garlanding themselves with it, as the polytheists used to do in their Jahiliyyah.

Mention of those who said this:

10956. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata regarding His words "Nor the offering, nor the garlands": The polytheists used to take from the trees of Makkah, from the bark of the samur, and garland themselves with it, and be safe by it from the people. So Allah forbade that its trees be uprooted and garlanded.

10957. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: We sat with Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, and with him was a man who related to them regarding His words "and the garlands," saying: The polytheists used to take from the trees of Makkah, from the bark of the samur, and garland themselves, and be safe by it among the people. So Allah, mighty of mention, forbade that its trees be pulled up and garlanded.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What is more appropriate as the interpretation of His words "and the garlands," since it is conjoined to the beginning of the speech, and there is nothing in the speech indicating its separation from its beginning, nor that He meant by it a prohibition on garlanding or making garlands from anything, is that its meaning is: and do not make the garlands lawful.

If that is its more appropriate interpretation, then it is known that it is a prohibition from Allah, mention be His, against making lawful the sanctity of the garlanded one, whether that be an offering or a person, rather than the sanctity of the garland itself. Allah, mighty of mention, indicated by His forbidding the sanctity of the garland the meaning of the sanctity of the garlanded one we have mentioned, so He sufficed with mentioning "the garlands" rather than "the garlanded one," since the meaning of what was intended was understood by those addressed.

* *

So the meaning of the verse, given that the matter is as we have described, is: O you who believe, do not make lawful the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the one who garlands himself with the garlands of the Haram. [[In the printed edition: "nor the garlanded one in both its forms," which has no meaning, and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. That is: the one who garlands himself with a garland of tree bark or hair, to be safe, as mentioned above; see the following paragraph.]]

* *

Some poets, in their poetry, have mentioned what we have mentioned from those who interpreted "the garlands" as the garlands of the bark of the trees of the Haram which the people of the Jahiliyyah used to wear. He said, censuring two men who had killed two men who had garlanded themselves with that, [[The speaker is Hudhayfah ibn Anas al-Hudhali.]]:

*Did you not kill the two al-Hirjayn when they made you blind, twisting the braided bark with their hands?* [[Ash'ar al-Hudhaliyyin 3:19; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 1120; Lisan (h-r-j). "Al-Hirj" (with kasra on the hā' and sukun on the rā'): the wood-pigeon; they said: by the two al-Hirjayn he meant two white men like wood-pigeons, either because whiteness is their colour, or he meant by that their nobility. The commentator on his diwan said: "al-Hirjan may also be two men called al-Hirjan." "Amarra al-habl" means: he twisted the rope. "Al-lihā'" is the bark of trees. "Al-mudaffar" is the one braided into plaits.

Abu Ja'far mentioned that the poem concerns two men who killed two men, and he related "Did you not kill," whereas in the sources it is "Did you not kill (plural)," which is what the context of the poem indicates, for its beginning before this verse is: *Alā abligha jull al-sawārī wa Jābiran / wa abligh banī dhī al-sahm 'annī wa Ya'marā*; *wa qūlā lahum 'annī maqālata shā'irin / alamma bi-qawlin lam yuḥāwil li-yafkharā*; *la'allakum lammā qataltum dhakartum / wa lan tatrukū an taqtulū man ta'ammarā*. So the whole poem uses the plural pronoun. Its cause was that Jundab, brother of al-Bariq ibn 'Iyad al-Lihyani, killed Qays and Salim, sons of 'Amir ibn 'Urayb al-Kinanis, and Salim killed Jundab, the two striking one another.]

"Al-Hirjan" are likewise the ones killed. The meaning of His words "a'warāka-mā" is: they made you vulnerable to their nakedness/weakness. [[Abu Ja'far's version, as he explained it, "a'warākumā"; the diwan's version is "a'wara lakum," which is in the context of Mash'ar; the version in the Lisan is "a'radā lakum," and it is also related as "'awwara lakum" with the wāw doubled. This on the basis that this version has "a'wara" transitive, whereas what is written in the lexicons is "a'wara laka al-shay'" (it exposed the thing to you), so one who is "mu'awwar."]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿Nor those making for the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure﴾ [[The printed and manuscript texts read: "nor those making for the Sacred House," and the commentary on the rest of the verse does not come at this point. I have added what he explains here. This is, moreover, because he will return to its explanation again on p. 479. This is very strange, and I do not know how it occurred to Abu Ja'far; perhaps he forgot, or he was taken by the weariness people feel at this point, then returned to it without changing, then began the discussion of the rest of the verse, leaving what had passed.]]

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may He be mentioned and exalted, "nor those making for the Sacred House," He means: do not make lawful those who intend and aim for the Sacred House. [[The printed and manuscript texts read: "do not make lawful those intending the House," which is an error, as the context shows. The correct reading is what I have given.]]

* *

One says from it: "I aimed at such-and-such," if one intends and aims for it; and some say "yamamtuhu" [[See the explanation of "amma yaummu" previously (5:558; 8:407). His saying "yamamtuhu" is triliteral, with fatha on the yā' and the first mīm and sukun on the second: like "ḍaraba."]] as the poet said:

*Indeed I, thus, when a land displeases me, / I turn the chest of my camel to another land.* [[I do not know who said it.]]

* *

"And the Sacred House" is the House of Allah which is in Makkah, and I have explained previously why it is called "the Sacred." [[See what preceded, 3:44-51.]]

* *

"Seeking bounty from their Lord" means: seeking profits in their trade from Allah. "And good pleasure" means: and that Allah be pleased with them for their rites.

* *

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning a man from the Banu Rabi'ah called "al-Hutam."

Mention of those who said this:

10958. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: al-Hutam ibn Hind al-Bakri, then one of the Banu Qays ibn Tha'labah, came [["Al-Hutam" is a laqab; his name is "Shurayh ibn Dabi'ah ibn Shurahbil ibn 'Amr ibn Murthid ibn Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Dabi'ah ibn Qays ibn Tha'labah, of Bakr ibn Wa'il" (Jamharat al-Ansab: 301). This al-Hutam went out in the Apostasy (ridda), in the eleventh year, with those who followed him from Bakr ibn Wa'il, and those who joined him of non-apostates who had remained disbelievers; he led them until they alighted at al-Qatif and Hajar, and he seduced the Khatt and those in it of the Zutt and the Sayabija. He besieged the Muslims with a severe siege. The Muslims gathered together to al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami, and all the polytheists gathered to al-Hutam. Then the Muslims attacked them by night and killed al-Hutam and those with him, in a long report (see Tarikh al-Tabari 3:254-260).

As for his saying here "al-Hutam ibn Hind," he brought up the mention of his mother in the poetry that follows; the name of his father is what has passed just now, and she is "Hind bint Hassan ibn 'Amr ibn Murthid" (Raghbat al-Amil 4:75).]] to the Prophet ﷺ alone, leaving his horses outside Madinah. He invited him, saying: To what do you invite? He informed him, and the Prophet ﷺ had said to his companions: a man of Rabi'ah will enter upon you today, speaking with the tongue of a devil. When the Prophet ﷺ informed him, he said: Consider, perhaps I will embrace Islam and I have someone to consult. So he left from his presence, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: He entered with the face of a disbeliever, and he left with the rear of a traitor! He passed by a herd of the herds of Madinah and drove it off, taking it away while chanting [[They differed greatly over the attribution of this poetry. al-Tabrizi in the Sharh al-Hamasah (1:185) transmitted a report from Rashid ibn Rumayd al-'Anazi (with fatha on the 'ayn and sukun on the nūn) of the Banu 'Anz ibn Wa'il, without doubt in that. al-Tabrizi said: "He said it in the raid of al-Hutam, who is Shurayh ibn Shurahbil ibn 'Amr ibn Murthid; he raided the Yemen, killed Wali'ah ibn Ma'd Yakrib, brother of Qays, and took captive the daughter of Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib, sister of al-Ash'ath ibn Qays. al-Ash'ath sent offering to ransom her, for every braid of hers a hundred camels. Al-Hutam did not do it, and she died with him of thirst." (See also al-Aghani 14:44.)

It is also attributed to al-Aghlab al-'Ijli, and to al-Akhnas ibn Shihab, and to Jabir ibn Hunayy al-Taghlibi. See that in the edition of our teacher al-Rajkoti, Simt al-La'ali: 729. Perhaps "al-Hutam" recited it praising himself for what he did in driving the herd.]]:

*The night has wrapped her with a driver, al-Hutam, / not a shepherd of camels nor of sheep,* / *nor a butcher upon the slaughtering-block,* / *they lay asleep while the son of Hind did not sleep,* / *he lies struggling with her, a youth like an arrow-shaft,* / *thick-shinned, his feet smooth.* [[al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin 2:308; al-Aghani 14:44; Hamasat Abi Tammam 1:184; Hamasat Ibn al-Shajari: 38; al-Kamil 1:224 (attributed to al-Hutam at p. 227); al-Khayl li-Ibn al-A'rabi 86; Lisan (h-t-m), and others. Before this verse: *Hadha awān al-shadd, fa-shtaddī Zīm*; "Zim" is the name of a mare. His words "hutam" mean one who drives very hard; they say of the driver who leaves no speed or haste undone: "hutam." "Al-wadm" is what meat is laid on when cut, of wood or something else. "Al-zalam" (with fatha on the zāy and lām, or with damma on the zāy) is the singular of "al-azlam," which are the arrows of gambling. He means: he is like the arrow in its hardness, thinness and smoothness. "Khadlaj al-saqayn": full-shinned; this is not good in men, and the correct version is what Ibn al-A'rabi related: *muhaffaf al-kashhayn khaffaq al-qadam*, i.e., lean of waist, with rapidly flapping feet — "khaffaq al-qadam" meaning his feet strike the ground in quick succession from his speed as he drives the camels. Abu Ja'far's version "mamsuh al-qadam" means: the sole of his foot has no hollow; the underside of his foot is level, smooth and soft, with no cracks or fissures. It has come in the description of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "musayyah al-qadamayn" (smooth-footed).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 2 (part 2 of 3):

Then he came back in the following year as a pilgrim, having garlanded his animals and dedicated them as offerings, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to send to him, so this verse was revealed, until [Allah said]: "nor the sacred House." Some of his Companions said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, leave him to us, for he is our companion!" He said: "He has garlanded [his animal]!" They said: "That is only something we used to do in the Jahiliyyah!" He refused them, so this verse was revealed.

10959- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, who said: al-Hutam, brother of the Banu Dubayʿah ibn Thaʿlabah al-Bakri, came to Madinah with a caravan carrying food, and he sold it. Then he entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, pledged allegiance to him, and embraced Islam. When he turned to leave, [the Prophet] looked at him and said to those around him: "He came to me with the face of a wicked man, and he departed with the back of a treacherous one!" When he reached al-Yamamah he apostatized from Islam, and he set out in a caravan of his carrying food in Dhu al-Qaʿdah, intending Makkah. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of him, a group of the Muhajirun and the Ansar prepared to set out against him in order to seize his caravan, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah," the verse, and the people desisted.

= Ibn Jurayj said, concerning His words "nor the sacred House": He forbids [harming] the pilgrims, that their paths be cut off. He said: That is because al-Hutam came to the Prophet ﷺ to scout and observe, and said: "I am a summoner of a people, so present to me what you say." He said to him: "I invite you to Allah, that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and that you establish the prayer, pay the zakah, fast the month of Ramadan, and perform the pilgrimage to the House." Al-Hutam said: "There is harshness in this matter of yours. I will return to my people and mention to them what you have mentioned; if they accept it, I will accept it with them, and if they turn away, I will be with them." He said: "Go." When he left, he said: "He came to me with the face of a disbeliever, and he let me go from his presence with the back of a treacherous one, and this man is not a Muslim!" Then he passed by a herd belonging to the people of Madinah and drove it off. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pursued him but he escaped them, and he reached al-Yamamah. The pilgrimage season came, and he prepared to set out, and he was of great trade, so they asked permission to intercept him and take what he had. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those making for the sacred House."

10960- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "nor those making for the sacred House," the verse: This was on the day of the Conquest. People from among the polytheists came intending the House, [entering the state of ihram] for ʿumrah, and the Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are polytheists just like those [before]; we will not leave them unless we raid them." So the Qur'an was revealed: "nor those making for the sacred House."

10961- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "nor those making for the sacred House," meaning: one who sets out as a pilgrim.

10962- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning His words "nor those making for the sacred House," meaning: the pilgrims.

10963- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, who said: We sat with Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, and with him was a man, and he related to them concerning His words "nor those making for the sacred House," he said: those who intend the House.

* *

Then the scholars differed concerning what was abrogated from this verse, after their consensus that part of it is abrogated.

Some of them said: all of it was abrogated.

Those who said this:

10964- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from ʿAmir, who said: Nothing of [Surat] al-Ma'idah was abrogated except this verse: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands."

10965- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah," it was abrogated by: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" [Surat al-Tawbah: 5].

10966- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Bayan, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: Nothing of Surat al-Ma'idah was abrogated except this verse: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah."

10967- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His words "do not violate the rites of Allah nor the sacred month," the verse, he said: It is abrogated. He said: The polytheist in that time was not hindered from the House, so they were commanded not to fight in the sacred months, nor at the House, and His words abrogated it: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them." [Note: this is the continuation of the report no. 10950, and will come below as no. 10976, as a single report; Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh: 115.]

10968- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "do not violate the rites of Allah," up to His words "nor those making for the sacred House," he said: It was abrogated by [Surat] Bara'ah: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them."

10969- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

10970- Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit: "do not violate the rites of Allah nor the sacred month nor the offering nor the garlands," he said: This is something that was forbidden, and was left as it is. [Note: "Jarir" is Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Dabbi, who has appeared many times. In the printed edition it read "Juwaybir," which is a gross error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

10971- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah nor the sacred month nor the offering nor the garlands nor those making for the sacred House," he said: All of this was abrogated; its abrogation was by His command to fight them all together. [He means His words, Exalted is He: "And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together" (Surat al-Tawbah: 36).]

* *

Others said: What was abrogated from this verse is His words "nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those making for the sacred House."

Those who said this:

10972- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I read to Ibn Abi ʿArubah, and he said: Thus I heard it from Qatadah: "Those making for the sacred House" was abrogated from [Surat] al-Ma'idah; it was abrogated by [Surat] Bara'ah. Allah says: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them," and He says: "It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while bearing witness against themselves to disbelief" [Surat al-Tawbah: 17], and He says: "Indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this their year" [Surat al-Tawbah: 28]. That was the year in which Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage, and he proclaimed in it the adhan. [In the manuscript: "proclaimed upon it the adhan", with "ʿalayhi" and above it "fihi". By "adhan" is meant His words, Exalted is He: "And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger" (Surat al-Tawbah: 3).]

10973- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Qatadah, his words: "O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah," the verse, he said: From it was abrogated "nor those making for the sacred House," it was abrogated by [Surat] Bara'ah, which said: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them," and he related like the report of ʿAbdah.

10974- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It was revealed concerning al-Hutam: "nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those making for the sacred House," then Allah abrogated it, saying: "And kill them wherever you overtake them" [Surat al-Baqarah: 191]. [See the account of "al-Hutam" above, nos. 10958, 10959.]

10975- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: "do not violate the rites of Allah," up to His words "nor those making for the House," [the believers and the polytheists used to make pilgrimage to the House] together; so Allah forbade the believers from preventing anyone from performing pilgrimage to the House or from obstructing him, whether believer or unbeliever. Then Allah revealed after this: "Indeed the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this their year" [Surat al-Tawbah: 28], and He said: "It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah" [Surat al-Tawbah: 17], and He said: "The mosques of Allah are maintained only by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day" [Surat al-Tawbah: 18], and thus He expelled the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque. [Note: the words in brackets are an addition from the narration of Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh: 115, where he narrated this report with this same chain, and the text is not coherent without them.]

10976- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "do not violate the rites of Allah nor the sacred month," the verse, he said: It is abrogated. The man in the Jahiliyyah, when he went out from his house intending the pilgrimage, would garland himself with the thorn-tree (samur), and no one would meet him. And when he returned, he would garland himself with a garland of hair, and no one would meet him. And the polytheist in that time was not hindered from the House. They were commanded not to fight in the sacred months, nor at the House, and His words abrogated it: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them." [Note: this is what came in the two earlier reports: 10950 and 10967.]

* *

Others said: Nothing of that was abrogated, except the garlands which people in the Jahiliyyah used to wear made of tree bark.

Those who said this:

10977- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "do not violate the rites of Allah nor the sacred month," the verse, he said: The Companions of Muhammad ﷺ said: All of this was an action of the Jahiliyyah, its performance and its observance; so Allah forbade all of that in Islam, except the bark of the garlands, and that was left [permitted]. [That is, Allah made its lawfulness forbidden in Islam, except the bark of the garlands, which has been abrogated.] "Nor those making for the sacred House": so Allah forbade everyone from frightening them.

10978- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar [al-Tabari] said: The most correct of these views, in terms of soundness, is the view of the one who said: Allah abrogated from this verse His words "nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands, nor those making for the sacred House," because all agree that Allah has permitted fighting the people of polytheism in the sacred months and in the other months of the whole year. Likewise they agree that if a polytheist had hung from his neck or arms the bark of all the trees of the Sacred Precinct, that would not be a safeguard for him against being killed, if no covenant of protection from the Muslims or safe-conduct had preceded for him. And we have already explained the meaning of "garlands" elsewhere, in other than this place. [See what has preceded, pp. 467–470.]

As for His words "nor those making for the sacred House," its apparent meaning admits: "do not violate the sanctity of those making for the sacred House from among the people of polytheism and of Islam," since it is general to all who make for the House. And when that is admissible, and the people of polytheism are included among them, there is no doubt that His words "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them" abrogate it, because it is impermissible for the command to kill them and the prohibition of killing them to coexist in one state and one time. And in the consensus of all that Allah's ruling concerning the polytheists of the warring party is that they be killed, whether they make for the Sacred House or the Holy House [Jerusalem], in the sacred months or otherwise, is known: the prohibition of killing them when they make for the Sacred House is abrogated. It also admits: "nor those making for the Sacred House from among the polytheists."

This is also the view of most of the exegetes.

And if what is meant is the polytheists of the warring party, then that too is undoubtedly abrogated.

* *

Since that is so, and there is no clear disagreement among them about it, and what has become widely established among them as proof is authoritative, then it is obligatory, even if that admits a meaning other than what they said, to accept what their transmission has widely established as sound.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure"

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words "seeking" [yabtaghun] he means: they seek and desire. "Bounty" [fadl] means profits in trade. "Good pleasure" [ridwan] means the pleasure of Allah with them, so that there does not befall them, in this world, the punishment that befell other nations in the immediacy of their worldly life, for their pilgrimage to His House. [The interpretation of this verse has passed on pp. 471–472, as I mentioned in the footnote 1, p. 471; and see the interpretation of "seeking" (ibtigha') above, 9:319, note 3, and the references there. The interpretation of "bounty" appears in the language indexes above. The interpretation of "good pleasure" (ridwan) appears above, 6:262.]

* *

The exegetes said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

10979- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure," he said: They are the polytheists, seeking Allah's bounty and good pleasure in what suits their worldly life.

10980- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I read to Ibn Abi ʿArubah, and he said: Thus I heard it from Qatadah concerning His words: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure." The bounty and good pleasure they seek are that their livelihoods in this world be made good, and that the punishment not be hastened upon them in it.

10981- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure," meaning: they seek the pleasure of Allah through their pilgrimage.

10982- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, who said: We sat with Mutarrif ibn al-Shikhkhir, and with him was a man, and he related to them concerning His words: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure," he said: Trade in the pilgrimage, and good pleasure in the pilgrimage.

10983- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abu Umayyah, who said: Ibn ʿUmar was asked about a man who makes pilgrimage and carries goods with him, and he said: There is no harm in it; and he recited this verse: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure." [Note: the report 10983: "Abu Umayyah al-Taymi", who is actually "Abu Umamah al-Taymi". Ibn Maʿin said: "Trustworthy, his name is not known." al-Bukhari said in al-Kuna: "Abu Umamah; Shuʿbah said: Abu Umayyah heard Ibn ʿUmar. Al-ʿAla' and Shuʿbah narrated from him. It is said his name is ʿAmr ibn Asma'." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 4, and Ibn Abi Hatim under "Abu Umamah" and "Abu Umayyah", two entries 4/2/330, 331.]

10984- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "seeking bounty from their Lord and good pleasure," he said: They seek reward and trade.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt"

Abu Jaʿfar said: By this, His words, may His praise be exalted, mean: And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt the game which I forbade you to hunt while you were in the state of ihram. That is: there is no blame upon you for hunting it; hunt if you wish then, for the reason for which I had forbidden it to you during your ihram has ceased.

* *

All the exegetes said what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

10985- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Mujahid that he said: It is a dispensation [rukhsah], meaning His words: "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt."

10986- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from al-Qasim, from Mujahid who said: Five [rulings] in the Book of Allah are dispensations, not obligations; he mentioned: "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt"; he said: Whoever wishes does it, and whoever wishes does not do it.

[10987] Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abū Khālid narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from ʿAṭāʾ, the like of it.

[10988] Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥuṣayn, from Mujāhid, regarding "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt": he said, "When he has come out of ihram, if he wishes he may hunt, and if he wishes he may not hunt."

[10989] Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from a man, from Mujāhid: that he did not consider eating from the sacrificial animal of tamattuʿ (hady al-mutʿa) obligatory, and he would interpret this verse, "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt," as [equivalent to] ﴿So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land﴾ [Surah al-Jumuʿah: 10]. [[He means by his saying "he would interpret this verse," that he would explain it in the manner of the other verse: "When the prayer has been concluded, whoever wishes may leave the mosque, and whoever wishes may sit," a concession from God.]]
* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And let not hatred of a people⁠—﴾
Abū Jaʿfar said: By His saying, "And let not [it] incite you" (wa lā yajrimannakum), He, may His praise be exalted, means: "let it not impel you" (wa lā yaḥmilannakum), as:

[10990] Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying, "And let not hatred of a people incite you," he said: "Let not the hatred of a people impel you."

[10991] Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah regarding His saying, "And let not hatred of a people incite you," i.e., "let it not impel you."
* *

As for the people of linguistic knowledge, they differed in its interpretation.

Some of the Basran grammarians said: the meaning of His saying, "let it not incite you" (lā yajrimannakum), is "let it not make right for you" (lā yuḥiqqanna lakum), because His saying ﴿Without doubt, for them is the Fire﴾ [Surah al-Naḥl: 62] means "it is right that for them is the Fire." [[This is the view of al-Akhfash, as mentioned by the author of Lisān al-ʿArab, entry (jrm).]]
* *

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: its meaning is "let it not impel you." He said: it is said, "So-and-so impelled me (jarramanī) to do such-and-such," meaning he impelled me to it.
* *

All of them cited the verse of a poet: [[He is Abū Asmāʾ ibn al-Ḍarība. It is also said that it belongs to ʿAṭiyya ibn ʿAfīf, and Sībawayh attributed it to al-Fazārī without identifying him.]]

"Indeed you struck Abū ʿUyayna a blow, / after which Fazāra made it right (jarmat) that they should be angry."

[[Sībawayh 1:469; Majāz al-Qurʾān of Abū ʿUbayda 1:147; Mushkil al-Qurʾān: 418; al-Fākhir: 200; al-Jawālīqī: 163; al-Baṭalyawsī: 313; al-Khizāna 4:310; Lisān (jrm). The occasion of the poem: Kurz al-ʿUqaylī killed Abū ʿUyayna Ḥiṣn ibn Ḥudhayfa ibn Badr al-Fazārī on the day of Ḥājir. When Kurz was killed, the poet composed an elegy addressing him: "O Kurz, you have indeed been killed by a knight, / a champion, when the warriors fled and turned tail." "Jabbaba al-rajulu tajbīban": if he fled and went off swiftly. Al-Bakrī in Muʿjam mā istaʿjam narrated that he said: "O Kurz, you have indeed slain a knight, / a champion, when the warriors fled, tested." And it seems to be a different poem than this one.]]

So each group interpreted it according to the meaning they derived from the Qur'an. Those who said "lā yajrimannakum" means "let it not make right for you" took the meaning of the poet's "jarmat Fazāra" to be: the blow made anger right for Fazāra.

Those who said it means "let it not impel you" took the meaning in the verse, "jarmat Fazāra an yaghḍabū," to be: Fazāra was impelled to be angry.
* *

Another Kufan said: the meaning of His saying, "lā yajrimannakum," is "let it not earn for you" (lā yaksibannakum) the hatred of a people.

The interpretation of the speaker of this view, regarding the poet's verse, "jarmat Fazāra," is: Fazāra earned (kasabat) that they should be angry. He said: I heard the Arabs say, "so-and-so is the earner (jarīmat) of his family," meaning: their earner; and "he went out seeking (yajrimuhum)," meaning: earning for them. [[The speaker of this is al-Farrāʾ in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 1:299.]]
* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: These views we have related from those from whom we have related them are close in meaning. For whoever impels a man to hate another man has earned him hatred, and whoever earns him hatred has made it right for him.

Given that this is so, the clearest in conveying the meaning of the word is what Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said, namely their rendering of His saying, "And let not the hatred of a people incite you," i.e., let not the hatred of a people impel you to transgression.
* *

The readers differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of the cities recited: ﴿wa lā yajrimannakum﴾ with a fatḥa on the "yāʾ" [i.e., "yajrimannakum"], from "jaramtuhu ajrimuhu."
* *

Some Kufan readers [[See al-Farrāʾ's Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 1:299.]], namely Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash, recited it: "wa lā yujrimannakum" with a ḍamma on the "yāʾ," from "ajramtuhu ajrimuhu, wa huwa yujrimunī."

[10992] Ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, both saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, that he recited: ﴿wa lā yujrimannakum﴾ with a ḍamma on the "yāʾ".
* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The reading closer to correctness of the two is the reading of those who recite "wa lā yajrimannakum" with a fatḥa on the "yāʾ," because it is widely transmitted among the readers of the cities, the other reading is anomalous, and it is the well-known, prevalent dialect among the Arabs, though "ajrama yujrimu" has been heard from some of them, albeit as an anomaly. The recitation of the Qur'an in the most eloquent dialects is more deserving and more fitting than otherwise. From the dialect of those who said "jaramtu," is the poet's verse: [[Attributed to al-Farazdaq, and not in his Dīwān.]]

"O you who complain of ʿUkl, and what they earned (jaramat)
toward the tribes of killing and despair..."

[[Majālis Thaʿlab: 49, 50; al-Aḍdād of Ibn al-Anbārī: 85. The verse has a raised rhyme; after the verse: "Thus we are, when there is turmoil, / we are captured and we kill until people submit." "Hamarraja": confusion and strife. Thaʿlab narrated these two verses, then said, without specifying to whom this report refers: "I said to him (i.e., to al-Farazdaq): why did you say 'min qatlin wa ibʾās'? He said: how should I do otherwise, since I said 'until people submit'? I said: why did you raise it? He said: with what will grieve you and burden you!"

Then Abū al-ʿAbbās Thaʿlab said: "He raised it only because the verb did not appear after it, as you say, 'I struck Zayd and ʿAmr,' the verb not appearing, so you raise it, and as you say, 'I struck Zayd and ʿAmr is struck.']]
* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿the hatred of a people﴾
The readers differed in its recitation.

Some recited "shanaʾān" with the "shīn" and "nūn" both vowelled with fatḥa, meaning "the hatred of a people," directing it to the verbal noun of the form "faʿalān," like "al-ṭayarān," "al-naslān," "al-ʿaslān," "al-ramalān."
* *

Others recited it: ﴿shanʾānu qawmin﴾ with the "nūn" sukūn and the "shīn" fatḥa, meaning the noun, directing its meaning to: "let not the hated (baghīḍ) of a people impel you," so that "shanʾān" comes out on the pattern "faʿlān," because its "faʿal" is "faʿila," as one says "sakrān" from "sakira," and "ʿaṭshān" from "ʿaṭisha," and similar nouns. [[His saying "faʿal" the first time refers to the past verb; the second "faʿal" is the morphological pattern, on the pattern "sakr," with a kasra on the ʿayn.]]
* *
