Another of the grammarians rejected this and said: "Min" is only used for a meaning that is understood, which speech cannot do without and which is not fitting without it, since it indicates partiality. He used to say: The meaning of the saying "There was (min) rain" and "There was (min) talk" is: Was there rain (min) raining among you? Was there talk (min) being spoken among you? [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "talk talk among you"; the correct reading is what I have given. The speaker means that "There was rain..." is an answer to someone's question: "Was there rain raining among you?"]] He used to say: The meaning of "And He will remove from you (min) your misdeeds" is: "And He will remove from you (some of) your misdeeds, whatever He wills and desires." As for His saying "And He sends down from the sky (min) mountains in which is (min) hail," he permits dropping "min" from "min barad" (of hail), but does not permit dropping it from "al-jibal" (mountains). He interprets the meaning as: "And He sends down from the sky the likes of mountains of hail." Then "min" was introduced before "barad," because "barad" is, in his view, a specifier (mufassar) for "the likes" (al-amthal), that is, "the likes of mountains," while "mountains" has been placed in the position of "the likes," and "mountains" are mountains of hail. So he does not permit dropping "min" from "al-jibal," because it indicates that what is in the sky from which hail is sent down is likes of mountains of hail. He permitted dropping "min" from "al-barad," because "al-barad" is a specifier for "al-amthal," just as you say: "I have two ratls of oil" and "I have two ratls of (min) oil," and you do not have "the ratl," but you have the measure. So "min" enters the specifier and leaves it. Likewise, according to the speaker of this view: "From the sky, from the likes of mountains," and it is not mountains. He said: If it were "He sent down from mountains in the sky of hail, mountains," then the first "mountains" in the sky and the second "mountains" could be dropped. You say: "I ate (min) the food," meaning: I ate (min) the food, food; then you drop "food" and do not drop "min."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that "min" only enters speech for an understood meaning, and it may be dropped in some speech where there is need for it, because what appears of the speech indicates it. As for its being in speech for no meaning that its inclusion adds, we have already shown earlier that this is not permissible in what is sound of speech. [[See the earlier passages referred to in the note: 2, p. 569.]]

Its function in His saying "So eat of what they hold back for you" is partiality, since the hunting animals hold back for their owners what God has made lawful for them of its flesh, and has forbidden them its dung and its blood. So He, exalted is His praise, said: "So eat" (of what your hunting animals hold back for you) = the good things that I have made lawful for you of their flesh, not what I have forbidden you of its filth, such as dung, blood, and the like, which I have not made good for you. This is the meaning of "min" entering there.

As for His saying "And He will remove from you (min) your misdeeds," we have already shown the reason for its occurrence earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See above 5: 586, and the other passages in the earlier note, p. 569, no. 2.]]

As for its occurrence in His saying "And He sends down from the sky (min) mountains," we will explain it when we come to it, God willing. [[See vol. 18: 118, 119 (Bulaq edition) of this tafsir (exegesis). Abu Ja'far did not fulfill what he promised, since he did not explain it adequately where he referred to it. The printed edition here had "God willing, exalted is He"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

The discussion of His saying: "And mention the name of God over it"

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise: "And mention the name of God over it" [the verse has "upon it" (alayhi)], He means: over what your hunting animals hold back for you of the game. As:

11218. Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying "And mention the name of God over it," he said: When you release your animals, say: "In the name of God." And if you forget, there is no blame.

11219. Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: "And mention the name of God over it." He said: When you release it, say the name of God over it as you release it at the game.

* *

The discussion of His saying: "And fear God. Indeed, God is swift in reckoning" (4)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise: Fear God, O people, in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you. So beware of Him in this, lest you proceed against His command, and lest you eat of the game of untrained hunting animals, or of what they have not held back for you of their game and have held back for themselves, or eat of what the name of God was not mentioned over, of game and slaughtered animals, which the idolaters, the worshippers of idols, and those who do not affirm God's oneness among His creation have hunted, or slaughtered. For God has forbidden you that, so avoid it.

Then He frightened them if they did what He had forbidden them of that and of other things. He said: Know that God is swift in His reckoning for whoever takes Him to account for His blessings upon you, and for the gratitude of the grateful among you to their Lord for what He has bestowed upon him by obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade. For He preserves all of that among you, and encompasses it, nothing of it is hidden from Him. He will reward the obedient among you for his obedience, and the disobedient for his disobedience, and He has explained to you the reward of both groups. [[In the printed edition: "for His blessing..."; I have kept the manuscript. See the explanation of "swift in reckoning" in the earlier volume 7: 501, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The discussion of His saying: "This day the good things have been made lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them" [Q. 5:5]

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "This day the good things have been made lawful for you," this day I have made lawful for you, O believers, the lawful among the slaughtered animals and foods, and not the foul among them.

And His saying: "And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you," meaning the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, who were given the Torah and the Gospel and had it revealed to them, and who followed them or one of them, "is lawful for you," that is: lawful for you to eat, apart from the slaughtered animals of all other polytheists who have no scripture, such as the Arab polytheists and the worshippers of idols and images. As for whoever among them does not affirm God's oneness, may His remembrance be exalted, and does not follow the religion of the People of the Book, the slaughtered animals of such people are forbidden to you.

* *

Then they differed about whom God, exalted is His remembrance, meant by His saying "the food of those who were given the Scripture," among the People of the Book.

Some of them said: God meant by that the slaughtered animal of every Scripturist who had the Torah and the Gospel revealed to him, or who entered their religion, following their faith, and forbidding what they forbade and permitting what they permitted, whether from them or from other nations of all kinds.

Those who said this:

11220. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid related to us, saying: Khusayf related to us, saying: 'Ikrimah related to us, saying: Ibn 'Abbas was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, and he recited this verse: "O you who believe, do not take the Jews" up to His saying: "And whoever of you allies with them, then he is one of them" [Q. 5:51].

11221. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

11222. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn 'Uthmah related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah: that they did not see any harm in the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, nor in marrying their women, and they recited: "And whoever of you allies with them, then he is one of them."

11223. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: that they did not see any harm in the slaughtered animal of the Christians of Bani Taghlib.

11224. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Husayn, from al-Sha'bi: that he did not see any harm in the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, and he recited: "And your Lord was not forgetful" [Q. 19:64].

11225. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, both saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ibn Shihab related to me, regarding the slaughtered animal of the Christians of the Arabs, he said: It is eaten because in religion they are People of the Book, and they mention the name of God.

11226. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj related to us, saying: 'Ata said: They only adhere to the religion of that Scripture. [[In the printed edition: "they only read that Scripture"; in the manuscript: "they only adhere between that"; I have taken the correct reading as: that they follow the religion of that Scripture.]]

11227. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: I asked al-Hakam, Hammad, and Qatadah about the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, and they said: There is no harm in them. He said: al-Hakam recited: "And among them are unlettered people who know not the Scripture except wishful fancies" [Q. 2:78].

11228. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Eat from the slaughtered animals of Bani Taghlib, and marry from their women, for God said in His Book: "O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; some of them are allies of others. And whoever of you allies with them, then he is one of them" [Q. 5:51]. So if they were not of them except by alliance, they would be of them.

11229. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah: that al-Hasan did not see any harm in the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, and he used to say: They adopted a religion, so that is their religion.

* *

Others said: By "those who were given the Scripture" in this verse, He meant only those upon whom the Torah and the Gospel were revealed, from the Children of Israel and their descendants. As for those who entered among them from other nations, following their religion while not being of the Children of Israel, this verse does not refer to them, and they are not among those whose slaughtered animals are lawful to eat, since they are not among those given the Scripture before the Muslims. This was the view of Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i. al-Rabi' related this from him. He interpreted in this the saying of those among the Companions and Successors who disliked the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians. [[See al-Umm 2: 196.]]

* *

Mention of those who forbade the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians.

11230. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from 'Ubaydah, who said: 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not eat the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, for they only cling to Christianity through drinking wine. [[Report: al-Shafi'i related it in al-Umm 2: 196, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 9: 284. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in (al-Fath 9: 549) and said: "al-Shafi'i and 'Abd al-Razzaq related it with sound chains."]]

11231. Ya'qub related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, from 'Ali who said: Do not eat the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Bani Taghlib, for they have not adhered to anything of Christianity except drinking wine.

11232. Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr related to us, saying: Hisham related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah who said: I asked 'Ali about the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians, and he said: Their slaughtered animals are not eaten, for they have not clung to anything of their religion except drinking wine.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 4 (part 5 of 5):**

11233. Ali ibn Said al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Abis narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: Ali forbade us from the slaughter of the Christians of the Arabs.

[[Report 11233: "Ali ibn Said ibn Masruq al-Kindi," previously mentioned under nos. 1184 and 2784.
And "Ali ibn Abis al-Asadi" is weak (da'if), but may be considered (yu'tabar bihi). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Abu al-Bakhtari" is Said ibn Firuz al-Ta'i, previously mentioned under nos. 175 and 1497.]]

11234. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Qassab, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ali relate, from Ali, that he disliked the slaughter of the Christians of the Banu Taghlib.

11235. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not eat the slaughter of the Christians of the Arabs or the slaughter of the Christians of Armenia.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: These reports from Ali, may God be pleased with him, only indicate that he forbade the slaughter of the Christians of the Banu Taghlib because they were not upon Christianity, since they abandoned making lawful what the Christians make lawful and making unlawful what they make unlawful, except for wine. Whoever claims a religion (muntahilan millatan) without adhering to any part of it is closer to disavowing it than to joining it and its people. Therefore Ali forbade eating the slaughter of the Christians of the Banu Taghlib, not because they were not of the Children of Israel.

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "man kana muntahilan..." without a waw at the beginning of the sentence, which is an error; the correct reading includes it.]]

[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "fahuwa ila al-bara'a minha aqrabu ila al-luhuq..." with "minhu" omitted, which is a serious corruption; the correct reading includes it.]]

When this is so, and it is a consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars (al-hujja) that there is no harm in the slaughter of every Christian or Jew who adheres to the religion of Christianity or Judaism, then he makes lawful what they make lawful and unlawful what they make unlawful, whether they are from the Children of Israel or from others, then clearly wrong is what al-Shafi'i said on this matter, and his interpretation in His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, that it refers to the slaughter of those given the Book, the Torah and the Gospel, from the Children of Israel.

[[Context: When this is so, and it is a consensus of the authoritative scholars... then clearly wrong is what al-Shafi'i said...]]

And the correct view, which opposes his interpretation, and the saying of those who say that the slaughter of every Jew and Christian is lawful, of whatever kind of the children of Adam they are.

* *

As for the "food" which God said: ﴿And the food of those given the Book﴾, it is the slaughtered animals.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

11236. Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: The slaughtered animals.

11237. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: Their slaughtered animals.

11238. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, similarly.

11239. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym and Qabisa narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, similarly.

11240. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Layth, from Mujahid, similarly.

[[Report 11240: "Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi al-Abdi," previously mentioned under no. 6456.
And "Abu Sinan" is Said ibn Sinan al-Shaybani, previously mentioned under no. 175.]]

11241. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

11242. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: The slaughter of the People of the Book.

11243. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim regarding His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: Their slaughtered animals.

11244. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, with its like.

11245. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, similarly.

11246. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, similarly.

11247. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym and Qabisa narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, similarly.

11248. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: Their slaughtered animals.

11249. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, similarly.

[[Report 11249: "al-Mu'alla ibn Asad al-Ammi," the memorizer (al-hafiz), trustworthy (al-thiqa); al-Bukhari narrated from him, and the others narrated through an intermediary. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and previously appeared without biography under no. 7232.]]

11250. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Said narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, that is: their slaughtered animals.

11251. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, as for their food, it is the slaughtered animals.

11252. It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, he said: God made lawful to us their food and their women.

11253. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: As for His saying: ﴿And the food of those given the Book is lawful for you﴾, He made lawful to us their food and their women.

11254. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked him, meaning Ibn Zayd, about what was slaughtered for churches and had God's name pronounced over it. He said: God made lawful to us the food of the People of the Book and did not exempt anything from it.

[[In the printed edition: "meaning Ibn Yazid," which is a clear error; this is a recurring isnad in the tafsir.]]

11255. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Abu al-Zahiriyya Hudayr ibn Kurayb, from Abu al-Aswad, from Umayr ibn al-Aswad: that he asked Abu al-Darda' about a ram slaughtered for a church called "Jirjis," which they had given as a gift to it: Shall we eat from it? Abu al-Darda' said: "O God, pardon!" They are People of the Book; their food is lawful for us, and our food is lawful for them! And he ordered him to eat it. And as for His saying: ﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾, it means: your slaughtered animals, O believers, are lawful for the People of the Book.

[[Report 11255: "Mu'awiya," is Mu'awiya ibn Salih ibn Hudayr al-Himsi al-Hadrami, previously mentioned under nos. 186, 187, 2072, and 8472.
And "Abu al-Zahiriyya," who is "Hudayr ibn Kurayb al-Hadrami, or al-Himyari." He narrated from Hudhayfa, Abu al-Darda', Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, and other Companions. Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated from him, and others. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, God willing, and narrated much hadith." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 2/1/91.
There is a difficulty in this isnad. Its apparent meaning is that Abu al-Zahiriyya Hudayr ibn Kurayb narrated the report from "Abu al-Aswad, from Umayr ibn al-Aswad," and this is impossible, since Abu al-Zahiriyya narrates directly from Abu al-Darda'. My strong opinion is that there is a lacuna or a gap (saqt aw kharm) in the sources of this tafsir at this point, and that the isnad ended at "Hudayr ibn Kurayb," the report of Hudayr ibn Kurayb from Abu al-Darda' dropped out, and another isnad began, which we do not know, ending at Abu al-Aswad from Umayr ibn al-Aswad, that he asked Abu al-Darda'... etc. The correctness of this will become apparent in what follows.
And "Abu al-Aswad" in this following isnad: I have not identified who among those known by the kunya Abu al-Aswad this is.
As for "Umayr ibn al-Aswad al-Ansi," Ibn Hajar claimed that he is "Amr ibn al-Aswad," and so he is biographed under that name in al-Tahdhib (8:4), and that they are one man. He said: He narrated from Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Ubada ibn al-Samit, and other Companions. Ibn Abi Hatim said in 3/1/375: "Umayr ibn al-Aswad al-Ansi al-Shami," heard Ubada, Abu al-Darda', and Umm Haram. Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrated from him; I heard my father say that." He also biographed "Amr ibn al-Aswad al-Qays," and said: "He narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Mas'ud, and Ubada ibn al-Samit. Mujahid and Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrated from him..." So he clearly distinguished between "Amr ibn al-Aswad al-Qays" and "Umayr ibn al-Aswad al-Ansi."
Ibn Sa'd did likewise in al-Tabaqat 7/2/153, distinguishing between them, saying: "Umayr ibn al-Aswad: he asked Abu al-Darda' about the food of the People of the Book. He narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and he was of few narrations, trustworthy."
Then he composed another biography: "And Amr ibn al-Aswad al-Sakuni: he narrated from Umar and Mu'adh, and he has hadiths."
I do not know from where the Hafiz Ibn Hajar made them one man!!
It has been established by what Ibn Sa'd narrated that this report is from the hadith of Umayr ibn al-Aswad, that he asked Abu al-Darda', and that it is another hadith, other than the hadith of Hudayr ibn Kurayb Abu al-Zahiriyya.
Moreover, I did not find this report, or these two reports, anywhere else. Ibn Kathir omitted its narration in his tafsir, and al-Suyuti also omitted it in al-Durr al-Manthur. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

**On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And chaste women from among the believing women, and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their bridal payments﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "And chaste women from among the believing women," the Mighty and Majestic means: it is permitted for you, O believers, to marry chaste women from among the believing women, meaning the free women among them. "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," meaning: and the free women from among those who were given the Scripture, namely the Jews and Christians who adhered to what is in the Torah and the Gospel before you, O believers in Muhammad ﷺ from among the Arabs and all other people, is also permitted for you to marry. "When you have given them their bridal payments" means: when you have given those whom you marry, from among your chaste women and their chaste women, "their bridal payments," which are their dowries.

* *

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the chaste women whom Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, meant by His saying: "And chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you."

Some of them said: He meant only the free women, whether they were chaste or unchaste. Those who held this view permitted marriage to a free woman, whether she was a believer or a Scripturary (kitabiyyah) from among the Jews and Christians, of whatever peoples they were, provided that she was a Scripturary, whether she was unchaste or chaste.

And they forbade marrying the slave women (imā') of the People of the Book in every case, because Allah, Mighty is His praise, made the condition of marrying slave women to be faith, by His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then [he may marry] from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 25].

Those who said this:

11256. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture," he said: "From the free women."

11257. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "From the free women."

11258. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab: that a man divorced his wife, and his sister was proposed to him in marriage, and she had committed some misconduct (uhdathat). So he came to 'Umar and mentioned to him what she had done. 'Umar said: "What have you seen from her?" He said: "I have seen nothing from her but good!" He said: "Marry her, and do not disclose it."

11259. Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: 'Amir narrated to us, saying: A woman from among us, from Hamdan, committed fornication. He said: The "musaddiq" of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ flogged her with the prescribed punishment (hadd), then she repented. They came to 'Umar and said: "Shall we marry her? What a bad thing was her affair!" 'Umar said: "If it reaches me that you have mentioned anything of that, I will punish you with a severe punishment."

[The "musaddiq" is the agent who collects the zakat (charity) from its people.]

11260. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab: that a man wished to marry off his sister, and she said: "I fear that I will disgrace my father, for I have committed fornication!" So he came to 'Umar and said: "Has she not repented?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then marry her."

11261. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi: that Nubaysha, a woman from Hamdan, committed fornication, and she wanted to slaughter herself. He said: They caught her and treated her, and she recovered. They mentioned that to 'Umar, and he said: "Marry her in the marriage of a chaste Muslim woman."

11262. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir: that a man from the people of Yemen had a sister who committed a grave sin (fahishah), so she drew a blade across her jugular veins, but she was caught, and her wound was treated until she recovered. Then her paternal uncle moved with his family until he came to Medina, and she recited the Qur'an and devoted herself to worship, until she became one of the most devout of their women. She was proposed to by her uncle's family, but he disliked to conceal her affair and disliked to disclose the affair of his brother's daughter. So he came to 'Umar and mentioned that to him. 'Umar said: "If you had disclosed it about her, I would have punished you! When a righteous man comes to you whom you are pleased with, marry her to him."

11263. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir: that a slave girl in Yemen, who was called "Nubaysha," committed a grave sin, and he mentioned something similar.

11264. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Isma'il informed us, from 'Amir, who said: A man came to 'Umar and said: "A daughter of mine was buried alive in the Jahiliyyah, but I dug her out before she died, and she reached Islam. When she embraced Islam, she committed one of the prohibited acts of Allah (hadd min hudud Allah). She went to a knife to slaughter herself with it, and I caught her after she had cut some of her jugular veins. I treated her until she recovered. Then she came with a sincere repentance, and now she is being proposed to me, O Commander of the Believers. Shall I inform of her affair as it happened?" 'Umar said: "Would you inform of her affair? You intend to expose what Allah has concealed! By Allah, if you inform anyone among the people of her affair, I will make you a lesson for the people of the cities! Rather, marry her in the marriage of a chaste Muslim woman."

[The "awdaj" is the plural of "wadaj" (with two fatḥahs): a vein running from the head to the throat, and the awdaj are the veins surrounding the windpipe.]

11265. Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Marwan narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi, who said: A man came to 'Umar and mentioned something similar.

11266. Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from Abu al-Zubayr: that a man proposed to a man for his sister, and he informed him that she had committed some misconduct (uhdathat). This reached 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he struck the man and said: "What is it to you to report it? Marry her and be silent."

[These past reports are a great etiquette (adab) of this religion and a guidance of the people of faith. They were commanded to it and they followed it. Then after them came successors who were ignorant of the matter of their religion, and they went to an extreme excess in regarding as abominable the lapse of one of the people of faith who had slipped, so that a man among them killed his daughter, his sister, and whoever had guardianship over her. They did not do this except after they had departed from the highway of faith in the rest of what Allah had commanded them, and they held fast to the grave excess, and thought that this was part of their religion and their manliness. This is evidence that every laxity in religion is met on the other side by excess in religiosity that is not of religion! May Allah have mercy on 'Umar ibn al-Khattab; how perceptive he was of people and how merciful toward them.]

11267. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I had resolved not to leave anyone who committed a grave sin in Islam to marry a chaste woman!" Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, shirk is greater than that, and it may be accepted from him if he repents!"

* *

Others said: Allah only meant by His saying, "And chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," the chaste women of both groups, whether they were slave women or free women. Those who held this view permitted marriage to the slave women of the People of the Book who adhere to their religion, on the basis of this verse, and they forbade marriage to adulterous women (baghaya) from among the believers and the People of the Book.

Those who said this:

11268. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "The chaste ones."

11269. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, similarly.

11270. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Amir: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she does not commit adultery, and that she performs the ritual bath from major impurity (janabah)."

11271. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Amir: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she performs the ritual bath from major impurity, and that she guards her private part."

11272. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Mutarrif, from a man, from al-Sha'bi regarding His saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "The chastity of a Jewish or Christian woman is that she does not commit adultery, and that she performs the ritual bath from major impurity."

11273. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi regarding His saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "Her chastity is that she performs the ritual bath from major impurity, and that she guards her private part from fornication."

11274. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, saying: Mutarrif informed us, from 'Amir, similarly.

11275. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding His saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture": "The chaste ones."

11276. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And chaste women from among the believing women and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," he said: "As for 'the chaste women,' they are the chaste ones."

11277. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that a woman took her male slave (mamluk) as a partner (ittakhadhat mamlukaha) [meaning: she gave him access to herself and took him as a concubine, as if he were her husband], and said: "I interpreted the Book of Allah: 'or what your right hands possess.'" He said: So 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was brought to her, and some of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "You have interpreted a verse of the Book of Allah other than its proper meaning." He said: So he exiled the slave (gharraba al-'abd) and shaved his head. And he said: "You are forbidden to every Muslim after him."

[Her saying "ittakhadhat mamlukaha" means she enabled him to have access to her and took him as a concubine, as if he were her husband. "Gharraba" means exile. "Jazz ra's" means he cut his hair; it does not mean he was killed.]

11278. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibrahim, that he said regarding a woman who commits fornication before she has been consummated with: she has no dowry, and they are separated.

11279. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, regarding a virgin who commits fornication: she is struck one hundred lashes, exiled for a year, and returns to her husband what she took from him.

11280. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, similarly.

11281. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath informed us, from al-Hasan, similarly.

11282. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus: that al-Hasan used to say: "If a man sees from his wife an act of grave sin and is certain of it, then he must not keep her."

11283. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Maysarah, who said: "The male and female slaves of the People of the Book have the status of their free women."

* *

Then the scholars of interpretation differed concerning the ruling of His saying, Mighty is His remembrance: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," whether it is general or specific.

Some of them said: It is general regarding the chaste women among them, because "al-muhsanat" means the chaste ones. And a Muslim may marry any free woman and any slave woman of the People of the Book, whether she is from a belligerent people (harbiyyah) or a protected people (dhimmiyyah).

They argued for this on the basis of the apparent meaning of His exalted saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you," and that what is meant by them is the chaste ones, whoever of them they might be. This is the view of one who said: "al-muhsanat" in this place means: the chaste ones.

* *

Others said: Rather, those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, meant by His saying: "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you" are the free women among them, and the verse is general in regard to all of them. So the marriage of all free Jewish and Christian women is permitted, whether they are belligerent or protected, from whatever peoples of the Jews and Christians they are. This is the view of a group of the earlier and later scholars.

Those who said this:

11284. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan: that both of them saw no harm in marrying Jewish and Christian women, and they said: "Allah permitted it with knowledge."

* *

Others among them said: Rather, He meant by that the marriage of the Scripturary women from the Children of Israel specifically, to the exclusion of the other peoples who adhered to Judaism and Christianity. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and of those who say as he says. [See al-Umm 5:6, where he says: "The marriage of free women of the Arabs who adhered to the religion of Judaism and Christianity is not permitted, because the origin of their religion was the Hanifiyyah (pure monotheism), then they went astray into the worship of idols, and they only transferred to the religion of the People of the Book after that, not because they were the ones who adhered to the Torah and the Gospel and then strayed from them and innovated in them; rather they strayed from the Hanifiyyah, and they were not like that. Their slaughtered animals are not permitted, and likewise every non-Arab whose ancestral religion was the worship of idols and who was not from the two well-known groups of Scripture, the Torah and the Gospel, and then adopted their religion, the marriage to their women is not permitted." See also Sunan al-Bayhaqi 7:173.]

* *

Others said: Rather, this refers to the women of the People of the Book who have a covenant (dhimmah) and a pact with the Muslims. As for the people of war (ahl al-harb), their women are forbidden to the Muslims.

Those who said this:

11285. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, saying: al-Fazari narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Among the women of the People of the Book, some are lawful to us, and some are not lawful to us." Then he recited: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah (poll tax) willingly while they are humbled﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 29]. "So whoever pays the jizyah, his women are lawful to us, and whoever does not pay the jizyah, his women are not lawful to us." Al-Hakam said: "I mentioned that to Ibrahim, and he was pleased with it."

[Report 11285: Muhammad ibn 'Uqbah ibn al-Mughirah al-Shaybani, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Tahhan. He narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, Sawwar ibn Mus'ab, and others. Al-Bukhari and Abu Kurayb and others narrated from him. Al-Bukhari said: "Known for his narrations." Abu Hatim said: "Not well known." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-thiqat). Ibn Hajar said: "In al-Bukhari he has only two narrations: one in the Friday prayer, as a corroboration, and the other in al-I'tisam, connected." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/1/200.

"Al-Fazari" is Abu Ishaq al-Fazari: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith ibn Asma' ibn Kharijah al-Fazari, the trustworthy imam. It passed as no. 3833.

"Sufyan ibn Husayn al-Wasiti" passed as nos. 3471, 6462.]

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 5 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter, in our view, is the opinion of those who said: by His saying, "and the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you," He meant free believing women and women of the People of the Book. This is because God, may His praise be exalted, did not permit marrying slave women who are free in the state in which He permitted the others to them, unless they are believers. So He, may His mention be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then [he may marry] from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 25], so He permitted from them only believing women. Had it been intended by His saying, "and the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book," the chaste ones, then the chaste among their slave women would have entered into the permission, and the unchaste among their free women and the free women of the people of faith would have been excluded from it. But God has made lawful to us the free believing women, even if they have committed an indecency, by His saying: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your male and female servants﴾ [Surah an-Nur: 32]. We have already shown the corruption of the opinion of the one who said, "It is not lawful to marry a woman among the believing women or the People of the Book who has committed indecency, for the believers," in another place, with what has sufficed to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[See what has passed, 8: 189, 190.]]
= Thus the marriage of the free women of the Muslims and of the People of the Book is lawful for the believers, whether they have committed indecency or not, whether they are dhimmi or harbi, after being in a place where the one marrying does not fear for his child that he will be compelled to disbelief, according to the apparent meaning of God's saying, may He be exalted: "and the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you."
* *
As for the statement of the one who said, "It means by that the women of the Children of Israel, only their Scripture-possessing women," [[He means the statement of al-Shafi'i mentioned previously, pp. 587, 588, note: 1.]] this is an opinion that does not require occupying oneself with explaining it, because of its anomaly and its departure from what the scholars of the Ummah are upon, namely the permissibility of the women of all the Jews and Christians. We have shown the corruption of the opinion of the one who holds this view on the basis of analogy in another place, sufficiently, so we disliked repeating it. [[See what has passed, 4: 362-369.]]
* *
As for His saying, "when you have given them their wages," the "ajr" is the compensation that the husband gives the woman for enjoying her, and it is the dowry. [[See the explanation of "ajr" in the language indices mentioned previously.]] As:-
11286 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, "when you have given them their wages," he said: meaning their dowries.
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿chaste, not unlawful fornicators, nor those who take secret lovers﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: It is made lawful for you the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you, while you are chaste, not unlawful fornicators, nor those who take secret lovers.
By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "chaste," he means: chaste ones; "not unlawful fornicators," meaning: not openly committing fornication with every immoral woman, which is adultery; "nor those who take secret lovers," he says: nor those who are single-minded with one prostitute, who has taken her as a lover and she has taken him, and he has taken her as a mistress whom he commits adultery with.
* *
We have explained the meaning of "ihsan" (chastity) and its aspects, and the meaning of "sifah" (fornication) and "khidn" (secret lover), in another place, with what has sufficed to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "ihsan" in what has passed, 8: 151-169 / then 8: 185-190 = and the explanation of "sifah" in what has passed, 8: 174, 175, 193-195 = and the explanation of "khidn" in what has passed, 8: 193-195.]] And it is as follows:-
11287 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "chaste, not unlawful fornicators," meaning: they marry them with the dowry and the "bayyinah" [["Bayyinah" was mentioned in the two reports numbered 9002 and 9008 (see 8: 161, note 1 = then p. 162 note 2). It has appeared to me here that by His saying "bayyinah" he meant the public announcement of the marriage. Review what I wrote there, for I am in doubt about all of that.]], not unlawful fornicators openly committing adultery, "nor those who take secret lovers," meaning: those who conceal their adultery.
11288 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: God made lawful to us two kinds of chaste women: a believing chaste woman, and a chaste woman from the People of the Book. "Nor those who take secret lovers": one who has a secret lover, one who has a single companion.
11289 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Hasan, who said: A man asked him: Does a man marry a woman from the People of the Book? He said: What has he to do with the People of the Book, when God has given the Muslim women in abundance! If he must do so, then let him aim for her as a chaste woman, not an unlawful fornicator. The man said: And what is the unlawful fornicator? He said: She is the one who, when a man glances at her with his eye, follows him. [[The report 11289: "Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah al-Qaysi," "Abu Sa'id al-Basri," narrated from his father, Thabit al-Bunani, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and others. Narrated from him al-Thawri and Shu'bah, who died before him, then a large group of trustworthy narrators, from the trustworthy ones of Basra. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers﴾ (5)
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," He means: whoever denies what God commanded to be believed in, namely the affirmation of God's oneness, the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and what he brought from God. This is "the faith" about which God, may His praise be exalted, said: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless." He says: then the reward of his deed that he did in the world, hoping to attain by it a station with God, has become void. [[See the explanation of "habita" (become void) in what has passed, 4: 317 / 6: 287.]] "And he is in the Hereafter among the losers," he says: he is in the Hereafter among the perishing, those who cheated themselves of their share of God's reward through their disbelief in Muhammad and their deeds not in obedience to God. [[See the explanation of "al-khasir" and "al-khusran" in what has passed, 9: 224, note 3, and the references there.]]
* *
It has been mentioned that His saying, "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," refers to the People of the Book, and that it was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on account of a people who were scrupulous about marrying the women of the People of the Book when it was said to them: "This day the good things have been made lawful to you... and the food of those who were given the Book is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them, and [lawful are] the chaste women from among the believing women and the chaste women from among those who were given the Book before you."
Those who said that:
11290 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that some Muslims said: How can we marry their women, meaning the women of the People of the Book, while they are upon other than our religion? So God, may His mention be exalted, revealed: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless, and he is in the Hereafter among the losers," and then God made their marriage lawful with knowledge.
* *
And the people of interpretation have said in the same sense as what we have said regarding the interpretation of "the faith."
Those who said that:
11291 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless," he said: "God," the faith. [[In the printed edition: "he said: by the faith, by God," different from what is in the manuscript, and it is correct.]]
11292 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Wasil, from 'Ata: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," he said: "The faith" is monotheism.
11293 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," he said: in God.
11294 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
11295 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless," he said: whoever disbelieves in God.
11296 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," he said: whoever disbelieves in God.
11297 - Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," he said: the disbelief in God.
11298 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
11299 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deed has become worthless," he said: God, may He be glorified, informed that "the faith" is the firmest handhold, and that He does not accept any deed except with it, and that He does not forbid Paradise except to the one who abandons it.
* *
If someone says to us: What is the meaning of the interpretation of those who directed His saying, "And whoever disbelieves in the faith," to the meaning: "And whoever disbelieves in God"? It is said: The meaning of their interpretation is thus, that "the faith" is affirmation of God and His messengers and what He sent them with of His religion, and "disbelief" is the denial of that. They said: So the meaning of "disbelief in the faith" is the denial of God and the denial of His oneness. They explained the meaning of the word by what is intended by it, and they turned away from explaining the word according to the literal reality of its wording and its apparent sense in the recitation.
If someone says: Then what is its interpretation according to its apparent sense and the literal reality of its wording?
It is said: Its interpretation is: And whoever refuses faith in God, and refuses His oneness and obedience to Him in what He commanded and forbade, then his deed has become worthless. That is because "kufr" (disbelief) is denial in the speech of the Arabs, and "iman" (faith) is affirmation and acknowledgment. Whoever refuses to affirm the oneness of God and to acknowledge it, he is among the disbelievers. [[See the explanation of "kufr" and "iman" in the language indices.]] That is the interpretation of the speech according to its proper sense.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is His Remembrance: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer while you are not in a state of ritual purity for prayer, then wash your faces with water and your hands up to the elbows.

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed regarding His words, "when you rise to prayer": Does it refer to every state in which one rises to it, or to some of them? And which states of rising to it are meant?

Some of them said, in line with what we have said, that it refers to some states of rising to prayer and not all states, and that the state intended is rising to it without being in a state of purity (tuhr).

Mention of those who said this:

11300. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, who said: Ikrimah was asked about the words of Allah, "When you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows." [He was asked:] Should one perform ablution at every hour? He said: Ibn Abbas said: "There is no ablution except from a minor impurity (hadath)."

11301. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani say: I heard Ikrimah say: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas used to pray the prayers with one ablution. [[Note on hadith 11301: Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani. al-Bukhari said: "He heard Ikrimah; it is mursal (a narration in which the Companion is omitted from the chain). Yahya al-Qattan narrated from him and said: there was nothing wrong with him." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Shu'bah narrated from him, and Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan." Al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/423, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/283. It will come in the following report. In reports 11322 and 11323 [and the following], and in report 11322, it is noted that "Sufyan ibn Habib" narrated from him. See the comment on the following report.]]

11302. Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, from Mas'ud ibn Ali, from Ikrimah, who said: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas used to say: "Pray with your ablution as long as you have not broken it." [[Note on hadith 11302: Sufyan ibn Habib al-Basri, who was knowledgeable in the hadith of Shu'bah and Ibn Abi Arubah. He is listed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/91, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/228, but his biography does not mention that he narrated from Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani. The report of Mas'ud is from the narration of Shu'bah, as passed in the previous report, so I fear that its isnad is "Sufyan ibn Habib, from Shu'bah, from Mas'ud ibn Ali." See the comment on the previous report and the comment on the following report, 11322.]]

11303. Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, who said: Sulaym ibn Akhdar informed us, who said: Ibn Awn informed us, from Muhammad, who said: I said to Ubaydah al-Salmani: What necessitates ablution? He said: The hadath.

11304. Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Waqi' ibn Sahban, from Yazid ibn Tarif, or Tarif ibn Yazid: that they were with Abu Musa on the bank of the Tigris, and they performed ablution and prayed the noon prayer. When the call was made for the afternoon prayer, some men got up to perform ablution from the Tigris. He said: "There is no ablution except for one who has broken it."

11305. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Tarif ibn Ziyad, or Ziyad ibn Tarif, from Waqi' ibn Sahban: that he witnessed Abu Musa pray the noon prayer with his companions, then they sat in circles on the bank of the Tigris. The call was made for the afternoon prayer, and men got up to perform ablution. Abu Musa said: "There is no ablution except for one who has broken it."

11306. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Qatadah narrate, from Waqi' ibn Sahban, from Tarif ibn Yazid, or Yazid ibn Tarif, who said: I was with Abu Musa on the bank of the Tigris, and he mentioned something similar.

11307. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Waqi' ibn Sahban, from Tarif ibn Yazid, or Yazid ibn Tarif, from Abu Musa, the like of it. [[Note on reports 11304–11307: These are four isnads for one report. Three of them agree on the narrator from Abu Musa, who is "Tarif ibn Yazid," despite the disagreement over his name. Report 11305 stands alone in making the narrator from Abu Musa "Waqi' ibn Sahban," and it appears to be an inverted isnad (maqlub), since in the other three isnads the narrator from Abu Musa is the one who narrates from "Tarif ibn Yazid."

As for Waqi' ibn Sahban, al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 4/2/189 and said: "He is counted among the Basrans, Abu Aqil. Qatadah and Thabit al-Bunani narrated from him," and added nothing. Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/49 said: "He narrated from Usayr ibn Jabir. Qatadah, Thabit al-Bunani and Humayd al-Tawil narrated from him. Ibn al-Mubarak used to say: 'Waqi' ibn Sahban,' without a nun, and not 'Sahban.' I heard my father say that."

As for Tarif ibn Yazid al-Hanafi, he is mentioned in Lisan al-Mizan 3:209, and al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 2/2/358 mentioned him and said nothing more than: "Tarif ibn Yazid al-Hanafi, from Abu Musa." Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/493 mentioned him, with a blank space in his biography marked by dots, and said: "He narrated from Abu Musa; ... narrated from him ... I heard my father say: both are unknown (majhulan)." The Hafiz said in Lisan al-Mizan: "Tarif ibn Yazid, from Abu Musa" is unknown (majhul), and so is his teacher. End of quotation.

Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the Tabi'un (Successors) in al-Thiqat, saying: "al-Hanafi, narrated from him the people of Yamamah." The implication of mentioning him among the Successors is that his teacher Abu Musa is al-Ash'ari.

Ibn Abi Hatim's book does not state that the teacher of Tarif is "unknown." Ibn Hajar's objection is correct, for the unknown person is the one who narrates from Tarif, not his teacher.

The disagreement over his name, "Yazid ibn Tarif," "Tarif ibn Ziyad," or "Ziyad ibn Tarif," is not mentioned in the other books; this is among what the tafsir of Abu Ja'far contributes.

It has become clear from the books of biographies that the isnad of 11305 is inverted, beyond doubt.]]

11308. Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, who said: Abu Khalid narrated to us, who said: I performed ablution with Abu al-Aliyah for the noon or afternoon prayer, and I said: "Shall I pray with this ablution of mine, since I will not return to my family until the 'Atamah (the night prayer)?" Abu al-Aliyah said: "There is no harm." And he taught us: "When a person performs ablution, he remains in his ablution until he breaks it by a hadath."

11309. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Ibn Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Ablution without a hadath is transgression (i'tida')." [[Note on reports 11309 and 11310: Ibn Kathir mentioned these two reports in his tafsir 3:84, saying: "As for what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: 'Ablution without a hadath is transgression' — it is strange (gharib) from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Furthermore, it is to be understood as meaning that whoever believes it to be obligatory is a transgressor. As for its legislation as recommended (istihbab), the Sunnah has shown that."]]

11310. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, who said: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id, the like of it. [[Note: the same as the note on report 11309.]]

11311. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, who said: I saw Ibrahim pray with one ablution: the noon prayer, the afternoon prayer, and the sunset prayer.

11312. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Uthram narrated to us, who said: al-A'mash narrated to us, who said: I was with Yahya, and I would pray the prayers with one ablution. He said: And Ibrahim did likewise.

11313. Sawwar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Hasan asked about a man who performs ablution and then prays all the prayers with one ablution. He said: "There is no harm in it, as long as he does not break it."

11314. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: He prays the prayers with one ablution as long as he does not break it.

11315. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Za'idah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Umarah, who said: al-Aswad used to pray the prayers with one ablution. [[Note on report 11315: "al-A'mash" is Sulayman ibn Mihran, who has passed many times. "Umarah" is Umarah ibn Umayr al-Taymi, passed as reports 3294 and 5789. "al-Aswad" is al-Aswad ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i, passed as reports 3299, 4888 and 8267.]]

11316. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding the words, "O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer": he says: "when you rise while you are not in a state of purity."

11317. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Umarah, from al-Aswad: that he had a qa'b (a small wooden bowl) the size of a man's fill of water [["al-Qa'b": a small concave wooden cup, enough to quench a man's thirst]], and he would perform ablution, then pray all the prayers with that ablution.

11318. Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka'i informed us, who said: al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir narrated to us, who said: I saw Jabir ibn Abd Allah pray the prayers with one ablution. When he urinated or broke his ablution, he would perform ablution and wipe over his socks with the remainder of his purifying water. I said: "Abu Abd Allah, is this something you do by your own opinion?" He said: "Rather, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do it, so I do it as I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do it." [[Note on report 11318: Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa al-Khutali, the teacher of al-Tabari. He narrated from Hisham ibn Muhammad al-Kalbi and al-Walid ibn Salih; Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated from him. He is in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/15. Abu Ja'far narrated from him in al-Tarikh 6:21.

Ziyad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka'i. Ahmad said: "There is nothing wrong with him; his hadith is the hadith of truthful people." Waki' said: "He is too noble to lie." He is in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 2/1/329.

al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashshir al-Ansari, who heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah and Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar. Ibn Mu'in said: "Weak." Ibn Adi said: "Most of his hadith is not corroborated." He is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/114, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/66.

The hadith was narrated by Ibn Majah 1:170, no. 511, from Isma'il ibn Tawbah, from Ziyad ibn Abd Allah, with the same wording. See Ibn Kathir's tafsir 3:83.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning is: O you who have believed, when you rise from your sleep to prayer.

Mention of those who said this:

11319. al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: someone who heard Malik ibn Anas narrate, from Zayd ibn Aslam, informed me of his words, "O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer": He said: "That is, when you rise from sleep."

11320. Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us: that Malik ibn Anas informed him, from Zayd ibn Aslam, the like of it. [[The two reports 11319 and 11320: see al-Muwatta, p. 21.]]

11321. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, his words, "when you rise to prayer, wash your faces": he said, "when you rise to prayer from sleep."

* *

Others said: Rather, this refers to every state in which a person rises to his prayer, that he renews purity for it.

Mention of those who said this:

11322. Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, from Mas'ud ibn Ali, who said: I asked Ikrimah, and I said: "O Abu Abd Allah, I perform ablution for the dawn prayer, then I go to the market and the noon prayer comes due, so shall I pray?" He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows." [[Note on report 11322: Sufyan ibn Habib and Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani. See the comment on the two preceding reports, 11301 and 11302.

His words in answer to the question: "He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say ..." and his recitation of the verse after that, without mentioning Ali's action, are permissible in such a context. It is as though he said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib used to do the like of that and recite this verse." See the next report.]]

11323. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, who said: I heard Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani say: I heard Ikrimah say: "Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) used to perform ablution at every prayer, and he would recite this verse: 'O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces ...' to the end of the verse." [[Note on report 11323: Mas'ud ibn Ali al-Shaybani. See the comment on the preceding report.

Ibn Kathir narrated this report in his tafsir 3:83–84, and along with it the reports 11326 and 11327, and said: "These are good chains from Ali; some of them strengthen others."]]

11324. Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, who said: Azhar narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Ibn Sirin: that the caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer.

11325. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab performed ablution with a light excess (tajawwuz), and he said: "This is the ablution of one who has not broken it." [[Note on report 11325: Ibn Abi Adi is Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Adi, passed as reports 5440 and 6497. Humayd is Humayd al-Tawil, who has passed many times. Anas is Anas ibn Malik.

Ibn Kathir narrated this report in his tafsir 3:84, from this place in al-Tabari, and said: "This isnad is sahih."]]

11326. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, who said: Shu'bah informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzal, who said: I saw Ali pray the noon prayer, then he sat with the people in al-Rahbah. Then water was brought to him, and he washed his face and hands, then wiped his head and feet, and said: "This is the ablution of one who has not broken it." [[Note on report 11326: Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah al-Hilali al-Zarrad, trustworthy, from the junior Successors, passed as reports 503 and 504.

al-Nazzal is al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah al-Hilali, whose companionship (suhbah) is disputed. He narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) (it is said he is mursal), and from Uthman, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and others. He is trustworthy and one of the senior Successors.

This report has a sahih isnad. See the comment on the preceding report, 11323. Ibn Kathir narrated it in his tafsir 3:83–84. It was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad through several chains, under nos. 583, 1005, 1173, 1174, 1222, 1315, 1366, and my brother Sayyid Ahmad took it out there.]]

11327. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, who said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: that Ali measured out (iktala) from a jar and performed ablution with a light excess, and said: "This is the ablution of one who has not broken it." [[Note on report 11327: See the comment on the preceding report 11323. Ibn Kathir narrated it in his tafsir 3:84.

"Iktala" is derived from "kayl al-ta'am wa ghayrihi" (measuring food and other things), and here he means that he took from the water the amount sufficient for his ablution. It is a correct Arabic metaphor.

"Al-hubb" (with a dammah on the h) is a large jar, or a cistern in which water is kept.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this was a command from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet (ﷺ) and to the believers in him, that they should perform ablution for every prayer, and then that was abrogated (nusikha) by a lightening (of the obligation).

Mention of those who said this:

11328. Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatawani narrated to me, who said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban al-Ansari, then al-Mazini, of the clan of Mazin al-Najjar, narrated to me, and he said to Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar: "Inform me about Abd Allah's ablution for every prayer, whether he was in a state of purity or not; from whom did he take it?" He said: "Asma bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab narrated it to me: that Abd Allah ibn Hanzalah ibn Abi Amir, al-Ghasil, narrated to her that the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to perform ablution at every prayer; that was difficult for him, so he was commanded to use the siwak (tooth-stick), and the ablution was lifted from him except for one who has broken it." Abd Allah used to think that he had strength for it, so he would perform ablution. [[Note on report 11328: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatawani, who is Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi Ziyad, passed as reports 2247 and 5796.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Zuhri, passed as reports 4314 and 5493.

His father Ibrahim ibn Sa'd ibn Ibrahim al-Zuhri, passed as report 4314, and he was among the people of Madinah with the most hadith in his time. al-Bukhari said: "Ibrahim ibn Hamzah said to me: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd had from Ibn Ishaq about seventeen thousand hadiths on rulings, apart from the maghazi (expeditions)." He is in al-Tahdhib.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 2 of 7):**

"Ibn Ishaq" is Muhammad ibn Ishaq, author of the *Maghazi* (the military expeditions of the Prophet). He has passed by many times, and the authentication of him by my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad has already passed. In the manuscript and the printed edition here it reads "ʿan Abi Ishaq," which is an error. The correct reading is from Sunan Abi Dawud and from Ibn Kathir.

"Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban al-Ansari al-Mazini" is a jurist, trustworthy, and a narrator of many hadith. The imams narrated from him. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*.

"Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab" is trustworthy but a narrator of few hadith. It is said that he was older than his brother "Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar." They did not mention in his biography that he narrated from Asma bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab, nor that Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban narrated from him. Rather, they mentioned that in the biography of his brother "Abd Allah," as you will see in the takhrij (source-tracing).

As for his brother "Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab," he narrated from Asma bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab, and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban narrated from him. Ibn Sad said: "Trustworthy, narrator of few hadith." It was said that he was the eldest son of Abd Allah ibn Umar, and that he was among the nobles and notables of Quraysh. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*.

As for "Asma bint Zayd ibn al-Khattab," she narrated from "Abd Allah ibn Handhala," and "Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar" narrated from her. She was the wife of her paternal cousin "Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab." When he was killed, she did not remarry after him until she died. Ibn Hibban and Ibn Mandah mentioned her among the Companions (sahaba). However, the hafiz Ibn Hajar rejected that. See her biography in *al-Isaba*, in the second section on women's biographies. She is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*.

"Abd Allah ibn Handhala ibn Abi Amir al-Rahib": his father is "Handhala," the one whom the angels washed (ghasil al-malaika), as he was washed the day he was killed at Uhud. The better formulation would be "...ibn Handhala ibn Abi Amir, Ibn al-Ghasil." Abu Amir is the monk (al-rahib) whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named "the wicked" (al-fasiq). "Abd Allah ibn Handhala" is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*.

In the manuscript and printed edition it reads "Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn Handhala," with the addition of "ibn Zayd," which is a pure error, possibly a slip by the copyist.

As for "Abd Allah" mentioned in this report without a patronymic (nisba), the one asked about his ablution, he is "Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab," the Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

This report was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, 1:43, no. 48, through Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta'i, from Ahmad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar. Then Abu Dawud said: "Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah." He means this narration, which Abu Ja'far narrated in this isnad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar.

It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, 1:37, 38. Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir, 3:83, cited it from the narration of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from Yaqub ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim ibn Sad, in the same wording as al-Tabari's narration, "Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar." He also cited Abu Dawud's narration, "Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar," and then said: "Whichever it is, it is a sound isnad, and Ibn Ishaq explicitly stated transmission (tahdith) and hearing (sama) from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, so the concern of tadlis (concealment of defects in transmission) is removed. However, the hafiz Ibn Asakir said: it was narrated by Salama ibn al-Fadl and Ali ibn Mujahid, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Yazid ibn Rukana, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, with the same wording. And Allah knows best."

This isnad mentioned by Ibn Asakir is the following isnad.

**11329.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Yazid ibn Rukana, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban al-Ansari told me, who said: I said to Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar: "Inform me about the ablution of Abd Allah for every prayer," and then he mentioned something similar.

[Note on the report 11329: it is a repetition of the preceding one. "Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Yazid ibn Rukana ibn Abd Yazid ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf." Abu Dawud and Ibn Main said: "Trustworthy." Ibn Sad said: "He was a narrator of few hadith." He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*. See the commentary on the preceding report.]

**11330.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqama ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution for every prayer. Then, in the year of the Conquest, he prayed the prayers with one ablution and wiped over his leather socks (khuffayn). Umar said: "You have done something you did not used to do!" He said: "I did it deliberately."

[Note on report 11330: "Yahya" is Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan. "Abd al-Rahman" is Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. "Sufyan" is al-Thawri. "Alqama ibn Martad al-Hadrami" narrated from Zir ibn Hubaysh, Tariq ibn Shihab, Sulayman ibn Buraida, and others. Shu'ba, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Mis'ar narrated from him. Trustworthy and firm in hadith. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*. "Sulayman ibn Buraida ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami," brother of "Abd Allah ibn Buraida." He narrated from his father, Imran ibn Husayn, and Aisha. Alqama ibn Martad, Muharib ibn Dithar, and others narrated from him. Ahmad said, on the authority of Waki: "They say that Sulayman ibn Buraida was sounder in hadith than his brother and more reliable." Trustworthy; he is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*. His father: "Buraida ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami," who embraced Islam before Badr but did not attend it; he attended Khaybar and the Conquest of Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ appointed him over the alms (sadaqat) of his people. He settled in Medina, then moved to Basra, then to Merv, where he died. This report Abu Ja'far will narrate by another route, no. 11333.
