Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 5:350 through Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sufyan, similarly; and 5:358 through Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, similarly; and he also narrated it 5:351 through Waki, from Sufyan, similarly. Muslim narrated it 3:176, 177 through Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from Sufyan; and through Muhammad ibn Hatim (and the wording is his), from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sufyan, similarly. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, 1:82, no. 172, through Musaddad, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, similarly. al-Nasa'i narrated it, 1:86, through Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, from Yahya, similarly. al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan, 1:162, through Ibn Wahb, from Sufyan, similarly, and through al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad, from Sufyan. He also narrated it 1:271 through Abu Dawud in his Sunan, and through Ali ibn Qadim, from Sufyan. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan, 1:89, 90 (with the commentary of my brother Ahmad), and commented on it, mentioning the differences among the narrators, as will come. However, the hadith of al-Thawri from Alqama ibn Martad is marfu' and mawsul (traced to the Prophet and continuous in isnad), and no one among the narrators disagreed about it. The disagreement was only over the hadith of al-Thawri from Muharib ibn Dithar, as will come.]

**11331.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution for every prayer. Then, on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, he prayed all the prayers with one ablution.

[Note on report 11331: "Muharib ibn Dithar ibn Kurdus al-Sadusi." Trustworthy; the Four (authors of the canonical collections) narrated from him. Simak ibn Harb said: "When a man among the people of the Jahiliyya had six qualities, they made him their chief: forbearance, patience, generosity, courage, eloquence, and humility; and these are not made complete in Islam except with chastity. And they were completed in this man," meaning Muharib ibn Dithar. This report Abu Ja'far narrated as marfu' and mawsul through two routes: this one and no. 11334. Ibn Majah narrated it, 1:170, no. 510, through Waki, from Sufyan, from Muharib ibn Dithar, marfu' and mawsul. al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, 1:89, 90, discussed the narration of Sufyan from Muharib ibn Dithar, and pointed to its narration as marfu' and mawsul, and as mursal (with a missing Companion) through Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and others, from Sufyan, from Muharib ibn Dithar, marfu' and mawsul. [He repeated the same.] He said, "This is more sound than the hadith of Waki." Al-Tabari added in report 11334 his narration through Mu'awiya ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, marfu' and mawsul. "Mu'awiya ibn Hisham" is trustworthy. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad said: "This narration was considered weaker (marjuh) by al-Tirmidhi, who held that the narration of those who transmitted it from al-Thawri, the paternal uncle of Muharib, from Sulayman as mursal, is more sound. We do not agree with him on that, because the hadith is well known from Sulayman, from his father. Waki is trustworthy and a hafiz. It is apparent that al-Thawri sometimes narrated the hadith from Muharib as mawsul, as Waki narrated it from him, and sometimes as mursal, as others narrated it from him."]

**11332.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, that the Prophet ﷺ used to perform ablution, and then he mentioned something similar.

[Note on report 11332: This is the mursal narration of the preceding report, the one to which al-Tirmidhi pointed, as we have stated.]

**11333.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Alqama ibn Martad, from Ibn Buraida, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed all the prayers with one ablution. Then Umar said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, have you done something you did not use to do?" He said: "I did it deliberately, O Umar."

[Note on report 11333: This is another route for the preceding report no. 11330, and we pointed to it there. "Mu'awiya ibn Hisham al-Asadi al-Qassar," who passed at no. 2997. Trustworthy; Abu Dawud and Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy. Ahmad said: "He makes many mistakes."]

**11334.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Sulayman ibn Buraida, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution for every prayer. When he conquered Mecca, he prayed the noon prayer, the afternoon prayer, the sunset prayer, and the night prayer with one ablution.

[Note on report 11334: This is another route for the hadith of Waki from Sufyan, which we took out at no. 11331, and to which we pointed there.]

**11335.** Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the noon prayer, the afternoon prayer, the sunset prayer, and the night prayer with one ablution.

[Note on report 11335: A hadith of very weak isnad. "al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Fazari," who passed at nos. 249, 5523, 5792. He was accused of fabricating hadith; they abandoned him. Ibn Hibban said: "He used to revile the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ, and narrated from trustworthy transmitters things that are fabricated (mawdu'at)." "Mis'ar" is Mis'ar ibn Kidam, a well-known trustworthy man, one of the leading scholars. He passed at nos. 503, 504, 1974, 5729, 6172.]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions in this matter, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: Allah meant by His saying "When you rise to prayer, wash your faces..." every state of a person rising to prayer. But it is a command of obligation to wash what Allah commanded to be washed by the one rising to his prayer after a minor impurity (hadath) from him that nullifies his purity, and before renewing the ablution after it. And it is a command of recommendation (nadb) for the one who was already in a state of purity that preceded, and from whom no impurity has occurred afterward that nullifies his purity. That is why, before the Conquest of Mecca, he (peace be upon him) used to perform ablution for every prayer, and then on that day he prayed all the prayers with one ablution, in order to teach his community that what he (peace be upon him) used to do of renewing purity for every prayer was only from him as an acceptance of excellence, and a preference of his for the more beloved of the two matters to Allah, and a hastening on his part to what his Lord recommended to him. It was not that this was obligatory upon him.

If someone supposes that in the hadith we mentioned from Abd Allah ibn Handhala, that the Prophet ﷺ commanded ablution at every prayer [see report no. 11328] is an indication contrary to what we said, namely that this was a recommendation for the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his Companions, and it seemed to him that this was obligatory, then he has supposed what is not correct. [The structure of this sentence: "If someone supposes ... and it seemed to him ... then he has supposed what is not correct."]

That is because the statement of one who says "Allah commanded His Prophet with such and such" is open to several meanings: the command of obligation, guidance, recommendation, permission, and unrestricted command. Since it is open to the aspects we have mentioned, the most appropriate of its aspects is the one upon whose soundness the proof is agreed, not one for which there is no evidence establishing the truth of its claimant. [The phrase "haqiqat mudda'ihi" means "haqq mudda'ihi" (the right of its claimant). The use of "haqiqa" in the sense of "haqq" was followed by Abu Ja'far in this book, and the editors have changed "haqiqa" to "haqiyya," as it appears here in the printed edition, contrary to the manuscript. See what has passed: 8:568, note 1; then 592, note 7; then 9:336, note 4; then 360, note 4.]

The proof has agreed that Allah, mighty and majestic, did not obligate upon His Prophet ﷺ nor upon His servants the obligation of ablution for every prayer and then abrogated that. In their agreement upon this lies the clear indication of the soundness of what we have said: that the Prophet's ﷺ act of doing this was, as we described, out of preference for doing what Allah, remembered be He, recommended to do and recommended to His believing servants by His saying: "O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows..." to the end of the verse. And that his leaving it in that state in which he left it was a concession (tarkhis) for his community, and an announcement from him to them that this was not obligatory on him nor on them, except from a minor impurity that requires the nullification of purity to be renewed.

Reports have been narrated similar to what we have said on this matter:

**11336.** Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Amr ibn Amir, from Anas: that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a small wooden bowl (qa'b) and performed ablution from it. He said: I asked Anas: "Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution for every prayer?" He said: "Yes!" I said: "And you?" He said: "We used to pray the prayers with one ablution."

[Note on report 11336: "Amr ibn Amir al-Ansari" narrated from Anas ibn Malik. Abu al-Zinad, Shu'ba, Sufyan al-Thawri, Mis'ar, and Sharik narrated from him. Trustworthy, sound in hadith. The Four narrated from him. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib* and in Ibn Abi Hatim, 3/1/249. See the rest of the commentary.

This report was narrated by al-Bukhari (al-Fath, 1:272, 273) through Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Amr ibn Amir; and through Musaddad, from Yahya, from Sufyan al-Thawri.

Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, 1:81, no. 171, through Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sharik, from Amr ibn Amir al-Bajali. Muhammad said: he is Abu Asad ibn Amr. He said: I asked Anas, similarly. Now, "Amr ibn Amir al-Bajali" is different from "Amr ibn Amir al-Ansari," and apparently Muhammad ibn Isa made a mistake. See *al-Tahdhib* under "Amr ibn Amir al-Bajali."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it, 1:88 (with the commentary of my brother Ahmad), through Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Amir. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan, 1:85, through Khalid, from Shu'ba, from Amr ibn Amir, like this route of Abu Ja'far.

Ibn Majah narrated it, 1:170, no. 509, through Sharik, from Amr ibn Amir.

al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 1:162, through al-Firyabi, from Sufyan.

Ahmad narrated it through Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Amir al-Ansari. See the *Tafsir* of Ibn Kathir (3:84).]

[[The report 11338: "Abu Sa'id al-Baghdadi" passed at no. 6684 as "Abu Sa'id ibn Yushu' al-Baghdadi," for whom I found no biography; then he passed at no. 6690 as "Abu Sa'id al-Baghdadi" as here.

* *

Some people have said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) as a notification from God to him that there is no ablution (wudu') incumbent upon him unless he rises to his prayer, and not for any other of all the actions. This is because, when he had a minor ritual impurity (hadath), he would refrain from all actions until he performed ablution. So God permitted, through this verse, that he do every act that occurred to him after the impurity, except prayer, whether he had performed ablution or not, and commanded him to perform ablution when he rose to prayer, before beginning it.

Mention of those who said this:

11339. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) urinated, we would speak to him and he would not answer us, and we would greet him with salam and he would not return it to us, until he came to his dwelling and performed ablution like his ablution for prayer. We said: "O Messenger of God, we speak to you and you do not answer us, and we greet you and you do not return it?" He said: "Until the verse of the dispensation was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer...﴾," the verse.

[[Report 11339: This is a problematic report (khabar mushkil), and despite its problem it is weak in isnad, due to the weakness of Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. He is very weak, accused of lying, as my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad showed at no. 2340.
The first point is that its isnad in the printed edition was as follows: "Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Sufyan, from Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from his father."
In the manuscript: "Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham, from Shaybān, from Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father."
The printed edition departs from the manuscript, putting "Sufyan" in place of "Shaybān," and "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas" in place of "Abdullah ibn Alqamah al-Faghwa'." I do not know from where the copyist of Abu Ja'far's *Tafsir* got this. Ibn Kathir certainly transmitted it from a copy of Abu Ja'far's *Tafsir*, and in it is "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas."
I will begin by mentioning what I have found in the books available to me that mention this report and its isnad.
1. Al-Tahawi narrated it in *Ma'ani al-Athar* 1:53 through Ibn Abi Dawud, who said: "Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Shaybān, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father..."
2. Ibn Kathir narrated it in his *Tafsir* 3:84, from Ibn Jarir's *Tafsir*, saying: "Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from his father..."
Then he said: "Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Kurayb, similarly."
3. Al-Jassas narrated it in *Ahkam al-Qur'an* 2:329, saying: "Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah, from his father..."
4. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in *al-Isabah*, in the biography of "Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa' al-Khuza'i," saying: "Mutayyin, al-Tahawi, and al-Daraqutni narrated it through Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Hazm, from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father..."
5. Ibn al-Athir mentioned it in *Usd al-Ghabah* 4:14, in the biography of "Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa' al-Khuza'i," saying: "Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm narrated from Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father..."
6. Al-Haythami cited it in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* 1:276, saying: "And from Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa'... al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Kabir*, and in it is Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is weak."
7. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas mentioned it in *al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh*, p. 119, saying: "The hadith of Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father, that he said..." This is an unquestionable error, since the printed *al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh* is very badly printed. The correct reading is "the hadith of Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa', from his father..." In the printed edition: "Alqamah ibn al-Qa'wa," which is an unquestionable distortion.
8. Al-Suyuti cited it in *al-Durr al-Manthur*, saying: "Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani narrated it, with a weak chain, from Alqamah ibn Safwan..."
So, as you see, there is very great disagreement in the isnads of this report.
The first disagreement: concerning the one from whom Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated. In the printed edition, Ibn Kathir, and al-Jassas's *Ahkam al-Qur'an*, he narrated it from "Sufyan," who is al-Thawri, as al-Jassas made explicit. In the manuscript, and al-Tahawi's *Ma'ani al-Athar*, he narrated it from "Shaybān," who is al-Nahwi. Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrates from both of them. Sufyan al-Thawri and Shaybān al-Nahwi both narrate from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi. It is possible that Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated it from both of them, from Jabir, sometimes from this one and sometimes from that one.
The second disagreement: concerning the one from whom "Sufyan" or "Shaybān" narrated. In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, from Amr ibn Hazm," which is an unquestionable error, because the hadith revolves around "Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi," as appears in all the references.
The third disagreement: concerning the one from whom "Jabir al-Ju'fi" narrated, which al-Tahawi mentioned in *Ma'ani al-Athar*: that it is from "Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm." So it seems Jabir narrated it from this "Abdullah ibn Muhammad," from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, as Ibn al-Athir said in *Usd al-Ghabah*. As for what Ibn Kathir transmitted from a copy of Abu Ja'far's *Tafsir*, that it is "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm," this agrees with what appears in al-Jassas's *Ahkam al-Qur'an* and in Ibn Hajar's *al-Isabah*, with a difference that does not matter in the abbreviation of the name.
So al-Tahawi alone added "Abdullah ibn Muhammad" in this isnad, and we do not know who he is. I fear that there is an error in the printed edition of *Ma'ani al-Athar*.
The fourth disagreement is connected to the third, concerning the narrator from "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa'": is it "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm," as in Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir*, al-Jassas's *Ahkam al-Qur'an*, and *al-Isabah*, or is it his father "Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm," as in al-Tahawi's isnad and as Ibn al-Athir mentioned in *Usd al-Ghabah*?
The fifth disagreement: the printed edition and Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* made the Successor (tabi'i) who narrated from his father "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas." Al-Suyuti alone in *al-Durr al-Manthur* made his father, the Companion, "Alqamah ibn Safwan." Both are unquestionable errors, by the evidence of the consensus of all the other narrators that this report is from the hadith of "Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa' al-Khuza'i."
For all of this, I changed what is in the printed edition: I made "Shaybān" in place of "Sufyan," agreeing with the manuscript and *Ma'ani al-Athar*. And I made "Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm," agreeing with Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir*, al-Jassas's *Ahkam al-Qur'an*, and Ibn Hajar's *al-Isabah*. And I made "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa'" in place of "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas," agreeing with all the other reports except Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti.
As for the men of the isnad, they are:
"Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham al-Asadi al-Qassar," trustworthy. Passed at no. 2997.
And "Sufyan," as we stated in the first disagreement, is Sufyan al-Thawri, the trustworthy Imam, who has passed many times.
As for "Shaybān," he is "Abu Mu'awiyah Shaybān al-Nahwi," and he is "Shaybān ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi," a trustworthy Imam. He has passed many times, at nos. 2340, 4898, 5280, 9222, 9223, 9456.
As for "Jabir," he is "Jabir ibn Yazid ibn al-Harith al-Ju'fi," very weak, accused of lying.
He has passed at nos. 764, 858, 2340, 3074, 5423, 7350.
And "Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm," trustworthy. Passed at no. 4808.
As for his father, "Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm," trustworthy. Passed at no. 2031.
And "Abdullah ibn Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa' al-Khuza'i," who narrated from his father. Zayd ibn Aslam and Muslim ibn Nabhan narrated from him. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/121.
And his father: "Alqamah ibn al-Faghwa' al-Khuza'i," guide of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Tabuk. He heard the Prophet (ﷺ). He narrated from Umar. His son Abdullah narrated from him. He is biographed in *al-Isabah*, *Usd al-Ghabah*, Ibn Sa'd's *Tabaqat* 4/2/32 and then 5:340, al-Bukhari's *al-Kabir* 4/1/39, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/404.
The takhrij of the report has passed in what we wrote earlier. It is in the same wording as al-Tabari's, except for a few minor letters, and except what came in al-Jassas's narration in *Ahkam al-Qur'an*. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

* *

The discussion of the words of His exalted mention: ﴿So wash your faces﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) disagreed about the limit of "the face" which God commanded to be washed, by His words to the one who rises to prayer: "When you rise to prayer, wash your faces."

Some of them said: It is what appears of the human skin from the hairline of the head, [["Qusas al-sha'r" (with its qaf vowelled in three ways) is the end of its growth at the front of the head.]] descending to the end of the chin lengthwise, and what lies between the ears widthwise. They said: As for the ear, and what is hidden inside the mouth, the nose and the eye, these are not part of the face, and washing them is not obligatory, nor is washing any part of them in ablution. [[In the printed edition: "It is not part of the face or other than it, and I do not like washing that." In the manuscript: "It is not part of the face and other than it, obligatory to wash that," with the right side of the letter "ghayr" joined to something resembling a single ha'. The editor did what he did to corrupt this phrase, without honesty or sense.]] They said: As for what the hair covers of it, like the chin covered by the beard, and the temples covered by the sideburns of the beard, then letting water flow over that hair suffices for washing what lies beneath it of the skin of the face. [[In the printed edition: "It suffices in place of washing," and what is in the manuscript is the good reading that the earlier scholars followed.]] For "the face," in their view, is what comes into the sight of the one who looks, and faces it, [[In the manuscript: "it is hidden from the sight of the one who looks," which is a distortion; in the printed edition it was corrected to "what appears to the sight of the one who looks." I found the reading as I have recorded it: "'an al-shay' ya'inu 'annan wa 'unnan" means it presented itself and appeared before you.]] to the exclusion of other things.

Mention of those who said this:

11340. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: What flows over the beard of water suffices for it.

[[Report 11340: In the manuscript: "from Ma'mar," and in the printed edition: "from Ma'mar"; the correct reading is what I have recorded.
"Umar ibn Ubayd ibn Abi Umayyah al-Tanafisi," passed at no. 8979.
And "Mughirah" is "Mughirah ibn Miqsam al-Dabbi," passed many times. His narration from "Ibrahim al-Nakha'i" is recorded in the tafsir. See the reports that follow this.
This same isnad has passed at no. 8979.]]
