11348. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from al-Hasan, that he did not pass his fingers through his beard.

11349. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, that he did not pass his fingers through his beard when he performed ablution.

11350. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

11351. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: Washing the beard is not from the Sunnah.

11352. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Isa ibn Yazid, from Amr, from al-Hasan: that when he performed ablution, he did not let the water reach the roots of his beard.

11353. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Abu Shaybah Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zubaydi, who said: I asked Ibrahim: "Should I pass my fingers through my beard with water when I perform ablution?" He said: "No, what suffices you is what your hand has passed over."
[[Reports 11346 and 11353: see the note above.]]

11354. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: I asked Shu'bah about passing the fingers through the beard in ablution, and he said: al-Mughirah said, Ibrahim said: What flows of water from his face onto his beard suffices for it.

11355. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Rushdin narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Umar narrated to us: that Ibn Shihab and Rabi'ah performed ablution, and they let water flow over their beards, and I did not see either of them pass his fingers through his beard.

11356. Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I asked Sa'id ibn Abd al-'Aziz about rubbing the cheeks (arak al-'arid) in ablution, and he said: "That is not obligatory. I saw Makhul perform ablution without doing that." [[Report 11356: "Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi" is "Abu al-Walid al-Qurashi," as in report 11359. He is "Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Bakkar ibn Abd al-Malik ibn al-Walid ibn Bisr ibn Artat al-Qurashi," and he is called "al-Bisri," in reference to his grandfather, and it is said "al-Amiri," because he is of the descendants of "Mu'ays ibn Amir ibn Lu'ayy." Trustworthy and truthful. Biographed in *al-Tahdhib*.]]

11357. Abu al-Walid Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir informed me, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: Rubbing the cheeks in ablution is not obligatory. [[Report 11357: "Sa'id ibn Bashir al-Azdi," passed at nos. 126, 5439, 9632.]]

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah al-Māʾidah, verse 6 (part 4 of 7):**

11358. Abū al-Walīd told us, saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad informed me, from al-Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "It is sufficient for him that the water has passed over his beard." [[Athar 11358: "Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad" is "Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Asmāʾ ibn Khārijah," "Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī." Mentioned earlier as no. 3833 and 11285.]]

11359. Abū al-Walīd al-Qurashī told us, saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿah informed me, from Sulaymān ibn Abī Zaynab, who said: "I asked al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad: 'How should I treat my beard when I perform wuḍūʾ?' He said: 'I am not one of those who wash their beards.'" [[Athar 11359: "Sulaymān ibn Abī Zaynab al-Sabaʾī al-Shāmī," from whom Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb al-Miṣrī narrated. Biographied in al-Kabīr 2/2/15 and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 2/1/118. In the manuscript and printed edition it reads "Salmān ibn Abī Zaynab," which is an error beyond doubt.]]

11360. Abū al-Walīd told us, saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Abū ʿAmr said: "Rubbing the sides of the beard and interlacing the beard (tashbīk) is not obligatory in wuḍūʾ." [["ʿArk al-liḥyah" means rubbing it. As for "tashbīk al-liḥyah," its description rarely appears in lexicography books, but it is clear from the traditions. al-Bayhaqī related in al-Sunan 1:55, from Ibn ʿUmar: "When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed wuḍūʾ, he would rub his sides somewhat, then he would interlace his beard with his fingers from beneath it," meaning that he inserted his fingers into it spread apart, interlacing them within it.]]

* *

Mention of those who said what we have related from the people of this position concerning washing what is inside the mouth and nose.

11361. Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bashīr, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Were it not for the licking of the lips (talammuẓ) during prayer, I would not have rinsed my mouth." [[Athar 11361: "ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Bashīr al-Baṣrī," who narrated from ʿIkrimah and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mussāwir, among others. Narrated from him Layth ibn Abī Sulaym, Sufyān al-Thawrī, Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiyah, and others; he is trustworthy (thiqah). Biographied in al-Tahdhīb.
"Talammuẓ": moving the tongue in the mouth after eating, as if following the remnants of food between the teeth.]]

11362. Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Idrīs told us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik say: "ʿAṭāʾ was asked about a man who prayed without rinsing his mouth. He said: 'What is not named in the Book suffices him.'"

11363. Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Mughīrah, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "Rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose are not obligatory in wuḍūʾ."

11364. Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: al-Ṣabbāḥ told us, from Abū Sinān, who said: "al-Ḍaḥḥāk used to forbid us from rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose in wuḍūʾ during Ramaḍān."

11365. Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Idrīs told us, saying: I heard Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said: "If one forgets rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose, [he is to act thus]: if he remembers after having entered the prayer, let him continue in his prayer; but if he has not yet entered it, let him rinse his mouth and sniff water into his nose."

11366. Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm told me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, from Shuʿbah, who said: "I asked al-Ḥakam and Qatādah about a man who, while in prayer, remembered that he had not rinsed his mouth nor sniffed water into his nose. He said: 'He continues in his prayer.'"

* *

Mention of those who said what we have related from the people of this position: that the two ears are not part of the face.

11367. Yazīd ibn Makhlad al-Wāsiṭī told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Ghaylān, who said: "I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: 'The two ears are from the head.'" [[Athar 11367: "Yazīd ibn Makhlad al-Wāsiṭī," Abū Khidāsh, narrated from Hushaym and Bishr ibn Mubashshir. Narrated from him Ibrāhīm ibn Yūsuf al-Hasanjānī and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Junayd. Biographied in Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/2/291.
"Ghaylān" is "Ghaylān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Wāsiṭī," mawlā of Quraysh (mawlā of the Banū Makhzūm). He heard Ibn ʿUmar; Shuʿbah and Hushaym heard from him. Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, who said: "I heard my father say: Ghaylān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, mawlā of Quraysh, from whom Hushaym narrated to us, whom Shuʿbah narrated from, is dearer to me than Suhayl ibn Dhakwān." Biographied in al-Kabīr 4/1/105 and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/2/53. See also the following traditions: 11368 and 11370.]]

11368. ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Abī ʿUmayy told us, saying: Abū Muṭarrif [....] told us, saying: Ghaylān, mawlā of the Banū Makhzūm, told us, saying: "I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: 'The two ears are from the head.'" [[Athar 11368: "ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn Abī ʿUmayr al-Dahhān, or al-Dahqān," the teacher of al-Ṭabarī. Mentioned earlier as no. 7578. "Abū Muṭarrif," known by that kunyah, is "Ibn Abī al-Wazīr": "Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn Muṭarrif al-Hāshimī," who narrated from Sharīk, Hushaym, and others; he is trustworthy. Biographied in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/1/178, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/1/20.
I have placed a dot after it because I consider it likely that he narrated this from "Hushaym," as in the preceding tradition and tradition 11370, since the axis (madār) of this report is on "Hushaym, from Ghaylān."
See "Ghaylān, mawlā of the Banū Makhzūm," in the commentary on the preceding tradition.]]

11369. al-Ḥasan ibn ʿArafah told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd told us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The two ears are from the head. So when you wipe the head, wipe them."

11370. Yaʿqūb told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Ghaylān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, mawlā of Quraysh, informed me, who said: "I heard Ibn ʿUmar; a questioner asked him: 'A man performed wuḍūʾ and forgot to wipe his ears.' He said: 'The two ears are from the head,' and he did not see any harm in it." [[Athar 11370: "Ghaylān ibn ʿAbd Allāh, mawlā of Quraysh." See the commentary on the two preceding traditions.]]

11371. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam told me, saying: Ayyūb ibn Suwayd told us — (ḥāʾ) — and Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, both from Sufyān, from Sālim Abī al-Naḍr, from Saʿīd ibn Marjānah, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said: "The two ears are from the head."

11372. Ibn al-Muthannā told me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarīr told me, saying: Shuʿbah told us, from a man, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The two ears are from the head."

11373. Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah told us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The two ears are from the head." [[Athar 11373: "ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah ibn Zuhayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judʿān," or "ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān," attributed to his grandfather. Mentioned earlier as nos. 40, 4897, 6495, 9293, and 10275.
"Yūsuf ibn Mihrān al-Baṣrī," narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Jābir. ʿAlī ibn Zayd ibn Judʿān narrated from him. Aḥmad said: "He is not known, and I know of no one who narrated from him except ʿAlī ibn Zayd." Ibn Saʿd said: "Trustworthy, few traditions." Biographied in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/2/375, Ibn Saʿd 7/1/161, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/2/229.]]

11374. Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah told us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who both said: "The two ears are from the head."

11375. Ibn al-Muthannā told us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdiyy told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, who said: "The two ears are from the head" — from al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd.

11376. Abū al-Walīd al-Dimashqī told us, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abū ʿAmr informed me, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The two ears are from the head."

11377. Abū al-Walīd told us, saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿah informed me, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Ibn ʿUmar, the like of it. [[Athārān 11376 and 11377: "Abū al-Walīd al-Dimashqī" is "Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Qurashī." See the preceding traditions 11356–11360.]]

11378. Ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Hārūn told us, from ʿĪsā ibn Yazīd, from ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan, who said: "The two ears are from the head."

11379. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bazīʿ told me, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd told us, from Sinān ibn Rabīʿah, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Umāmah — or from Abū Hurayrah; Ibn Bazīʿ was uncertain — that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The two ears are from the head." [[Athar 11379 to 11381: "Muʿallā ibn Manṣūr al-Rāzī," in the second chain, narrated from Mālik, Muḥammad ibn Maymūn al-Zaʿfarānī, Ḥammād ibn Zayd, Hushaym, and others. al-Bukhārī narrated from him, and he is mentioned in al-Kabīr without any criticism recorded. Ibn Maʿīn, Abū Ḥātim, Ibn Ḥibbān, and others considered him trustworthy, though some have spoken about him. Biographied in al-Tahdhīb.
"Sinān ibn Rabīʿah al-Bāhilī, Abū Rabīʿah ṣāḥib al-Sābarī," narrated from Anas, Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, and others. The two Ḥammāds narrated from him. Ibn Maʿīn said: "Not strong." Abū Ḥātim said: "A shaykh with unstable traditions." Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the trustworthy. al-Bukhārī related from him in the Ṣaḥīḥ in conjunction with others.
"Shahr ibn Ḥawshab al-Ashʿarī," a Successor (tābiʿī). My brother, al-Sayyid Aḥmad, declared him trustworthy in earlier references, nos. 1489, 5244, 6650–6652.
This report was related by Aḥmad in al-Musnad 5:258, 264, 268, at length; by Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan 1:68, no. 134; by Ibn Mājah 1:152, no. 444; by al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan 1:66, 67; and by al-Tirmidhī in al-Sunan (commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Aḥmad) 1:53–55, in a similar form. He said: "Scholars have exhaustively investigated this phrase: is it an insertion (mudraj) from the words of Abū Umāmah, or is it attributed to the Prophet? Many of them preferred that it is an insertion." See al-Talkhīs (p. 33) and Naṣb al-Rāyah (1:10–12). My preferred view is that the tradition is authentic, for it has been related through several routes with chains, some of which are good, and they corroborate one another." He then expanded at length on it.
As for the doubt of Shakk ibn Bazīʿ in the first tradition, it is apparent that it is an error on the part of Ibn Bazīʿ, and that the correct version is "from Abū Umāmah," not "from Abū Hurayrah." The report of Abū Hurayrah will come after this, no. 11383.]]

11380. Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Muʿallā ibn Manṣūr told us, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from Sinān ibn Rabīʿah, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Umāmah, who said: "The two ears are from the head." — Ḥammād said: "I do not know whether this is from Abū Umāmah or from the Prophet (ﷺ)."

11381. Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Abū Usāmah told us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd told me, saying: Sinān ibn Rabīʿah Abū Rabīʿah told me, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Umāmah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The two ears are from the head."

11382. Abū al-Walīd al-Dimashqī told us, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj and others informed me, from Sulaymān ibn Mūsā, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The two ears are from the head." [[Athar 11382: "Sulaymān ibn Mūsā al-Umawī," Abū Hishām al-Ashdaq, the jurist of the people of Syria in his time. Trustworthy and firm, but he narrates traditions that he alone transmits and that no one else narrates. Biographied in al-Tahdhīb.
This report is mursal (its chain omits a Companion), although Sulaymān ibn Mūsā did narrate from Abū Umāmah.]]

11383. al-Ḥasan ibn Shabīb told us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Hāshim ibn al-Barīd told us, saying: Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim told us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The two ears are from the head.'" [[Athar 11383: "al-Ḥasan ibn Shabīb ibn Rāshid ibn Maṭar," Abū ʿAlī al-Muʾaddib, a teacher of al-Ṭabarī, mentioned earlier as no. 9642; he is not strong.
"ʿAlī ibn Hāshim ibn al-Barīd al-Barīdī al-ʿĀʾidhī." He has two traditions in Muslim. A number of imams narrated from him; some declared him trustworthy and some weak. Biographied in al-Tahdhīb.
"Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-Makkī," his trustworthiness was mentioned earlier, no. 5417.
Ibn Mājah 1:152, no. 445, related the report of Abū Hurayrah through the route of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlāthah, from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayrah. They declared it weak because of the weakness of ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥuṣayn and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlāthah.]]

11384. Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah told us, saying: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb told us, from Yūnus, that al-Ḥasan said: "The two ears are from the head."

* *

Others said: "The face" is everything beneath the place where head-hair grows to the end of the chin in length, and from ear to ear in breadth; what appears to the eye of the beholder, and what is hidden of it, namely the places where the hair of the beard grows on the chin and on the sides of the face, and what is within the mouth and nose, and what faces the face from the two ears. All of this, in their view, is part of "the face" which God commanded to be washed by His saying: ﴿Wash your faces﴾. They said: "If the one performing wuḍūʾ leaves any part of that unwashed, his prayer with that wuḍūʾ is not valid for him."

Mention of those who said that:

11385. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Bakr and Abū ʿĀṣim told me, both saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Nāfiʿ informed me that Ibn ʿUmar used to moisten the roots of his beard's hair and insert his fingers deep into the roots of the hair until the dripping (qaṭarān) of water from it became abundant. [[In the printed edition, in both traditions, it reads "until the drops (al-qaṭarāt) became abundant," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.
"Qaṭara al-māʾ yaqṭuru qaṭran wa quṭūran wa qaṭarānan": it flowed and went on continuously.]]

11386. Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah told us, saying: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Nāfiʿ, mawlā of Ibn ʿUmar, informed me, that Ibn ʿUmar used to insert his hands into his beard until the dripping became abundant from it. [[In the printed edition, in both traditions, it reads "until the drops (al-qaṭarāt) became abundant," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.
"Qaṭara al-māʾ yaqṭuru qaṭran wa quṭūran wa qaṭarānan": it flowed and went on continuously.]]

11387. ʿImrān ibn Mūsā told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wārith told us, from Saʿīd, who said: Layth told us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: when he performed wuḍūʾ, he would comb his beard (khallala liḥyatahu) until he reached the roots of the hair.

11388. Ibn Abī al-Shawārib told us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Muʿallā ibn Jābir al-Luqaytī told us, saying: al-Azraq ibn Qays informed me, saying: "I saw Ibn ʿUmar perform wuḍūʾ, and he combed his beard." [[Athar 11388: "Yazīd" is "Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ," mentioned many times earlier.
"Muʿallā ibn Jābir Muslim al-Luqaytī," declared trustworthy by Ibn Ḥibbān, and al-Bukhārī mentioned no criticism of him. Biographied in al-Kabīr 4/1/394, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/1/332, and Taʿjīl al-Manfaʿah: 409.
"al-Azraq ibn Qays al-Ḥārithī," trustworthy. Biographied in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/2/69, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/339.]]

11389. Yaʿqūb told us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, saying: Layth informed us, from Nāfiʿ, that Ibn ʿUmar used to comb his beard with water until it reached the roots of the hair.

11390. Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Bakr told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj told us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr informed me, that his father, ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, when he performed wuḍūʾ, would insert his fingers into the roots of the facial hair, working them between the hairs at their roots, rubbing the skin with his fingers. — ʿAbd Allāh gestured to me as the man had informed him, as it was described from him. [[Athar 11390: "Muḥammad ibn Bakr ibn ʿUthmān al-Barsānī," mentioned earlier as no. 5438.
As for his words, "as the man had informed him, as it was described from him," I am in doubt about them, but thus they came in the manuscript as well.]]

11391. Abū al-Walīd told us, saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Abū ʿAmr told us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that when he performed wuḍūʾ, he would rub his sides somewhat, and at times he would interlace his beard with his fingers, and at other times he would leave it. [[Athar 11391: al-Bayhaqī related it in al-Sunan 1:55, through the route of ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Qays, from Nāfiʿ, in the same form. See the explanation of "tashbīk al-liḥyah" in the preceding pages, p. 29, note 1, under tradition 11360.]]

11392. Abū al-Walīd and ʿAlī ibn Sahl told us, both saying: al-Walīd told us, saying: Abū ʿAmr said, and ʿAbdah informed me, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, something similar to that.

11393. Ibn Bashshār told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from Muslim, who said: "I saw Ibn Abī Laylā perform wuḍūʾ and wash his beard, and he said: 'Whoever among you is able to make the water reach the roots of the hair, let him do so.'"

11394. Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah told us, saying: Sufyān ibn Ḥabīb told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: "It is incumbent upon him to moisten the roots of the hair."

11395. Ibn Abī al-Shawārib told us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ told us, saying: Shuʿbah told us, from al-Ḥakam, who said: "Mujāhid used to comb his beard."

11396. Ḥumayd told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid: that he used to comb his beard when he performed wuḍūʾ.

11397. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā told us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿbah told us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

11398. Ibn al-Muthannā told us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdiyy told us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

11399. Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Shubrumah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "What is the matter with the beard being washed before it grows, but when it has grown it is not washed?" [[Athar 11399: "Abū Dāwūd al-Ḥafarī" (with an unpointed ḥāʾ) is "ʿUmar ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbayd," mentioned earlier as no. 863.]]

11400. Ibn al-Muthannā told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb told us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh told us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that he used to comb his beard when he performed wuḍūʾ.

١١٤٠١ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Layth, from Tawus: that he used to comb his beard with his fingers (takhlil al-lihya).

١١٤٠٢ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Ibn Sirin: that he used to comb his beard with his fingers.

١١٤٠٣ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, the same.

١١٤٠٤ - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: I asked Shu'ba about combing the beard in wudu', and he mentioned from al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba: that Mujahid used to comb his beard.

١١٤٠٥ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Ma'ruf, who said: I saw Ibn Sirin perform wudu' and he combed his beard.

١١٤٠٦ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Ibn Sirin, the same.

١١٤٠٧ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, from al-Dahhak, who said: I saw him combing his beard.

١١٤٠٨ - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Abu al-Ash'hab, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, from Zayd al-Khudri, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) perform wudu' and he combed his beard. I said: "Why do you do this, O Prophet of God?" He said: "My Lord commanded me to do so."

[[The report: 11408. "Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Kula'i", al-Wasiti, narrated from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, and Abu al-Ash'hab Ja'far ibn Hayyan al-Sa'di, and others. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, and other imams narrated from him. Ahmad said: "He was reliable (thabt) in hadith." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Abu al-Ash'hab" is: "Ja'far ibn Hayyan al-Sa'di al-'Utaridi", who narrated from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, al-Hasan al-Basri, and others. Trustworthy (thiqa), biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha al-Makhzumi", who narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, 'Amr ibn al-Harith, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr; Shu'ba and the two Sufyans and others narrated from him. Trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib.
As for "Zayd al-Khudri", I have not found a biography for him, and I do not know who he is. I fear there is confusion in the isnad, or that the name has been corrupted.
As for "Yazid al-Raqashi", he is "Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqashi", weak (da'if); he has passed under numbers 6654, 6728, 7757.
The narration of this report from Yazid al-Raqashi from Anas will come under numbers 11409 and 11411.
This report depends on Yazid al-Raqashi, so its isnad is weak.
Ibn Majah narrated this report in his Sunan 1:149, number 431, by way of Yahya ibn Kathir, Abu al-Nadr, Sahib al-Basri, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, with different wording. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak as mursal (a report whose chain skips the Companion) from Anas, by way of Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha also from Anas. Al-Bayhaqi pointed to it in al-Sunan 1:54.]]

١١٤٠٩ - Tamim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Salam ibn Salm, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra - or: Yazid al-Raqashi - from Anas, who said: I performed wudu' for the Prophet (ﷺ), and he inserted his fingers from beneath his chin (hanak), and combed his beard, and said: "With this my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, commanded me."

[[The report: 1140
9. Another route for the report of Yazid al-Raqashi from Anas.
"Salam ibn Salm al-Mada'ini", also said to be "Salama ibn Sulaym" and "Ibn Sulayman"; the correct one is the first, namely "Salam al-Tawil". Most of his narrations are from "Zayd al-'Ammi". Narrated from him 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi. Ahmad said: "He narrated disapproved (munkar) hadiths." Al-Bukhari said: "They abandoned him." Al-Nasa'i said: "He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is not written." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
In the printed edition it was "Salam ibn Sulaym", and I have established what is in the manuscript.
"Zayd al-'Ammi" is "Zayd ibn al-Hawwari", judge of Herat. He narrated from Anas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, and others. Spoken of critically (mutakallam fihi). Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Mu'awiya ibn Qurra al-Muzani", Abu Iyas, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), one of the wise men.
This hadith is weak because of the weakness of Salam ibn Salm.
"Al-hanak": what is beneath the chin of a human or other.]]

١١٤١٠ - Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Salam ibn Salm al-Madini, who said: Zayd al-'Ammi narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to it.

[[The report: 11410. "Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi", the teacher of al-Tabari, passed under number 405, 718, 9155.
"Al-Muharibi" is "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad", trustworthy. Passed under 221, 875.
"Salam ibn Salm al-Madini" is the one who passed in the earlier report, and in the references he is attributed as "al-Mada'ini".
In the manuscript here it was "Salm ibn Salam al-Madini", and this is an undoubted scribal error.
This report too has a weak isnad, like the one before it.]]

١١٤١١ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Ubayda al-Haddad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Thurwan narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Thus my Lord commanded me!" And he inserted his fingers into his beard and combed it.

[[The report: 11411. It is a repetition of the two earlier reports, 11408 and 11409, by another route.
"Abu 'Ubayda al-Haddad" is "'Abd al-Wahid ibn Wasil al-Sadusi", trustworthy, one of Ahmad's teachers, passed under 3023, 9837.
"Musa ibn Thurwan al-'Ijli" (with the three-dotted tha'), also said to be "Musa ibn Sarwan" and "Musa ibn Farwan" (with fa'). Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir 4/1/281, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/138.
In the manuscript and printed edition it was "Shurwan" (with the shin), which is an error.
This report is weak because of the weakness of Yazid al-Raqashi.]]

١١٤١٢ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham and 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ilyas, from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from Umm Salama: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed wudu' and combed his beard.

[[The report: 11412. "Mu'awiya ibn Hisham" and "'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-'Absi", who passed many times.
"Khalid ibn Ilyas ibn Sakhr al-Qurashi al-'Adawi, al-Madani", from the descendants of 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy. Al-Bukhari said: "He is nothing (laysa bi-shay')." Ahmad said: "Abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith)." Biographed in al-Dhahabi's Mizan al-I'tidal 1:295, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/129, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/321.
"'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' al-Makhzumi", mawla of Umm Salama, a trustworthy Successor. Passed under 5398.
This report was cited by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1:235, and he said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir. In it is Khalid ibn Ilyas, and I have not seen anyone who biographed him." He was brief, for we have already mentioned who biographed him.]]

١١٤١٣ - 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hurr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Sawra, from Abu Ayyub, who said: We saw the Prophet (ﷺ) perform wudu', and he combed his beard.

[[The report: 11413. "'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hurr" is "'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Hurr ibn Za'laan", known as Ibn Ashkab al-Akbar, trustworthy, biographed in Tarikh Baghdad 11:392, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/179.
"Muhammad ibn Rabi'a al-Kilabi al-Ru'asi", trustworthy, passed under 181, 6860.
"Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib al-Raqashi". Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Al-Bukhari said: "Disapproved in hadith (munkar al-hadith)." Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/173, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/30.
"Abu Sawra", the nephew of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Al-Bukhari said: "Disapproved in hadith; he narrates disapproved reports from Abu Ayyub which no one corroborates." Al-Tirmidhi in al-'Ilal, citing al-Bukhari, said: "It is not known that Abu Sawra heard from Abu Ayyub." Biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/388.
This report is weak, because of the weakness of Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib and Abu Sawra.
Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan 1:149, number 433, by way of Isma'il ibn 'Abd Allah al-Raqqi from Muhammad ibn Rabi'a, with it, similar. Al-Zayla'i weakened it in Nasb al-Raya 1:24.
This report will come with another isnad, number 11418.]]

١١٤١٤ - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umama: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) combed his beard."

[[The report: 11414. "Zayd ibn Hubab al-'Akli", trustworthy. Passed under 2185, 5350, 8165. In the printed edition it was "Zayd ibn Hibban", which is a pure error.
"'Umar ibn Sulayman": thus it came in the printed edition; in Nasb al-Raya it is "'Umar ibn Sulayman al-Bahili", and in the manuscript "'Amr ibn Sulayman". I do not know how this agreement occurred in the commentary and in Nasb al-Raya, which cites al-Tabarani in his Mu'jam and Ibn Abi Shayba in his Musannaf!! It is nearly certain that he is "'Umar ibn Sulaym al-Bahili", who narrates from Abu Ghalib, the companion of Abu Umama, and it is he whom Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrates from, as in his biography in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/112, 113. Abu Zur'a said: "Truthful (saduq)," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. I do not know whether they overlooked that the name of his father is disputed: "Sulaym" or "Sulayman"?
"Abu Ghalib", the companion of Abu Umama, known by his kunya. Ibn Ma'in said: "Sound in hadith (salih al-hadith)." Al-Tirmidhi graded some of his hadiths good and authenticated some of them. Ibn Hibban said: "It is not permissible to argue with him except in what agrees with the trustworthy narrators." Some weakened him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This report was cited by al-Zayla'i in Nasb al-Raya 1:25, who said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in his Mu'jam, and Ibn Abi Shayba in his Musannaf; al-Tabarani: 'Anbasa ibn Ghannam narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Sulayman al-Bahili narrated to us, from Ibn Ghalib (the correct: from Abu Ghalib), from Abu Umama ...'" The hadith.
Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1:235, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and in it is al-Salt ibn Dinar, who is abandoned (matruk)." This appears to be another isnad of al-Tabarani, other than the one al-Zayla'i cited in Nasb al-Raya.]]

١١٤١٥ - Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim Abi Umayya: that Hassan ibn Bilal al-Muzani saw 'Ammar ibn Yasir perform wudu' and comb his beard. It was said to him: "Do you do this?" He said: "I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do it."

[[The report: 11415. "Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Damghani", teacher of al-Tabari, passed under 3225. "Sufyan" is Ibn 'Uyayna.
"'Abd al-Karim Abu Umayya" is "'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Makhariq", who narrated from Anas ibn Malik, Tawus, Hassan ibn Bilal, and others. He is weak, spoken of critically. Al-Bukhari and Ibn 'Uyayna denied that 'Abd al-Karim heard from Hassan ibn Bilal the hadith about combing. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Hassan ibn Bilal al-Muzani" narrated from 'Ammar ibn Yasir. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This report was narrated by Ibn Majah 1:148, number 429, al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1:149, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi number 645, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan 1:44 (with the commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad), and my brother has fully discussed it there. See also al-Zayla'i's Nasb al-Raya 1:24.]]

١١٤١٦ - Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Qays informed me, from Yazid al-Raqashi and Qatada: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when he performed wudu', would rub his cheeks (aridayh) and interlace his beard with his fingers.

[[The report: 11416. "Abu al-Walid" is "Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qurashi"; see what has passed in the notes on the reports 11356 - 11360.
"Al-Walid" is "al-Walid ibn Muslim"; see what has also passed.
"'Abd al-Wahid ibn Qays al-Sulami al-Aftas al-Nahwi". He narrated from Abu Umama, Nafi' mawla of Ibn 'Umar, and Yazid al-Raqashi. Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i narrated from him. They spoke against him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
See the explanation of "interlacing the beard (tashbik al-lihya)" in what has passed: 11360, 11391.]]

١١٤١٧ - Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Abu Mahdi Sa'id ibn Sinan informed me, from Abu al-Zahiriya, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to it.

[[The report: 11417. "Abu Mahdi", "Sa'id ibn Sinan al-Hanafi", narrated from his father, Abu al-Zahiriya, and others. Narrated from him Bishr ibn Bakr al-Tinnisi, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Walid ibn Muslim, and others. Ahmad said: "Weak (da'if)." Ibn Ma'in said: "Not trustworthy." Al-Jawzajani said: "I fear that his hadiths are fabricated (mawdu'a); they do not resemble the hadiths of people." Muslim said in al-Kuna: "Disapproved in hadith (munkar al-hadith)." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Abu al-Zahiriya" is "Hudayr ibn Kurayb al-Hadrami", who narrated from Hudhayfa, Abu al-Darda', and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Trustworthy. Passed under 11255.
"Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami", a trustworthy senior Successor, who was of the pre-Islamic era (jahili). Passed under 7009. This report is mursal.]]

١١٤١٨ - Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi Abu 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Wasil al-Raqashi narrated to me, from Abu Sawda - thus said al-Ahmasi - from Abu Ayyub, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed wudu', he would rinse his mouth and wipe his beard from beneath with water.

[[The report: 11418. "Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi", passed shortly before, number 11410.
"Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi", Abu 'Abd Allah al-Ahdab, a known trustworthy narrator, passed under 405, 9155.
"Wasil al-Raqashi" is "Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib al-Raqashi", passed under 11413.
"Abu Sawda": it is in fact "Abu Sawra" (with the ra'), as passed in number 11413, and it was al-Ahmasi, the teacher of al-Tabari, who said it that way, and he erred. In the printed edition it was "Abu Sawra" with the ra', which is a correction without meaning. The correct form is from the manuscript, though it is an error in fact.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 5:417, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi, similar to it, in full.
It is weak in isnad, like its brother that passed, number 11413.]]

* *

Mention of those who said what we have related from them, from the people of this view, regarding washing what is inside the nose and mouth.

١١٤١٩ - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: I heard Mujahid say: "Istinshaq (snuffing water into the nose) is half of wudu'."

١١٤٢٠ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Shu'ba, who said: I asked Hammad about a man who remembered, while in prayer, that he had not rinsed his mouth nor snuffed water into his nose. Hammad said: "He should turn, rinse his mouth and snuff water into his nose."

١١٤٢١ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Sabbah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, who said: I came to Kufa and came to Hammad and asked him about that - meaning: about one who left out rinsing the mouth and snuffing the nose and prayed - and he said: "I think he must repeat the prayer."

١١٤٢٢ - Hamid ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: Qatada used to say: "If he leaves out rinsing the mouth, or snuffing the nose, or his ear, or a part of his foot, until he enters into his prayer, he should turn away, perform wudu', and repeat his prayer."

[[In the printed edition: "fa-innahu yantaqilu" (he moves), which is a pure error; in the manuscript it is as I have written it, undotted.
It is said: "fanfatala fulan 'an salatihi, aw min salatihi" meaning: he turned away. And it is said: "fatala wajhahu 'an al-qawm": he turned it away and diverted it.]]

* *

Mention of those who said what we have related from them, from the people of this view, that what faces forward of the two ears is part of the face, and what turns to the back is part of the head.

١١٤٢٣ - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: What faces forward of the two ears is from the face, and what turns back is from the head.

١١٤٢٤ - Hamid ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to me, from al-Hakam and Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, concerning the two ears: their inner part is from the face, and their outer part is from the head.

١١٤٢٥ - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The front of the two ears is from the face, and their back is from the head.

١١٤٢٦ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from al-Hakam and Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, the same, except that he said: "the inner part of the two ears."

١١٤٢٧ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, the same, except that he said: "the inner part of the two ears."

١١٤٢٨ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, the same.

١١٤٢٩ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The inner part of the two ears is from the face, and their outer part is from the head.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 6 of 7):

1. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us. [ح] And Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us. Both of them said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Yazid ibn Rukana narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "Shall I not perform ablution for you as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed it?" He said: We said: "Yes!" So he performed ablution, and when he washed his face, he pressed his two thumbs to what came forward of his ears. He said: Then, when he wiped his head, he wiped his ears from their backs. [[The report: 1143 0 – "Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Yazid ibn Rukana": trustworthy (thiqa), already mentioned under no. 11329.
And "Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani" is "Ubayd Allah ibn al-Aswad", and it is said "Ubayd Allah ibn al-Asad", the stepson of Maymuna, who narrated from her and from Ibn 'Abbas. Trustworthy.
This report was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 1: 64, no. 117, and Ahmad in his Musnad no. 625, in a fuller form. Al-Bukhari weakened this hadith and said: "I do not know what this is," but my brother, Sayyid Ahmad, authenticated it in his commentary on this report in the Musnad.]]
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter, in our view, is the statement of those who said: the "face" that Allah, mighty is His remembrance, commanded to be washed by one standing to prayer is: everything that slopes down from the roots of the hair of the head to the end of the chin in length, and what lies between the two ears in breadth, which is apparent to the eye of the observer, excluding what is hidden within the mouth, the nose and the eye, and excluding what is covered by the hair of the beard, the sideburns and the moustache, so that it is concealed from the sight of observers, and excluding the ears.

We only said that this is more correct, although what lies beneath the hair of the beard and moustache was a "face" that must be washed before the hair that conceals it from the eyes of observers of the one standing to prayer grows, because all of them agree that the two eyes are part of the face. Then they, despite their agreement on that, agree that washing what covers them of their eyelids, without bringing water to what is beneath the eyelids of them, is sufficient.

Since that was by their consensus, based on the Messenger's (ﷺ) instruction to his community regarding that, then the parallel to that is: everything in the places of ablution of the body of the son of Adam that is covered by something from the very creation of the body, which does not let water reach it except with difficulty, toil and treatment, by analogy with what we mentioned regarding the ruling on the two eyes in that respect.

If that is so, then there is no doubt that the like of the two eyes in the difficulty of bringing water to them during ablution is what is hidden within the nose and the mouth, the hair of the beard, the temples, and the moustache, because all of that does not let water reach it except with treatment to bring water to it, akin to or greater than the difficulty of treating the two pupils to bring water to them.

And if that is so, it is clear that the washing by those among the Companions and the Successors who washed what is beneath the roots of the hair of the beard, the sideburns and the moustache, and what is hidden within the nose and the mouth, was only out of preference for the more difficult of the two matters for them: washing that or leaving it, just as Ibn 'Umar preferred to wash what is beneath the eyelids of the eyes with water, by pouring water into them. This is not on the basis that that was, in his view, an obligatory duty. As for the one who thought that their doing of that was on the basis of obligation and duty, he has opposed their methodology in that by his statement and neglected the path of analogy, because analogy is what we described of likening the disputed matter to the agreed-upon ruling concerning the two eyes. And there is no report from any one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that obliged the one who leaves out bringing water in his ablution to the roots of his beard and sideburns, and the one who leaves out rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose, to repeat his prayer if he prayed with that purification. In that is the clearest evidence for the soundness of what we have said: that their doing of what they did in that was out of preference of the better of the two acts, leaving it or washing it.

If someone supposes that in the reports narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said:

1143 1 – "When one of you performs ablution, let him sniff water into his nose." [[The report: 1143 1 – This is a report whose chain of narration was not mentioned; see a similar wording in al-Bukhari (Fath 1: 229).]]

= is evidence for the obligation of sniffing water into the nose, then in the consensus of the authoritative scholars that this is not an obligatory duty, such that the one who leaves it must repeat the prayer he prayed before washing it, there is what suffices without elaborating further on it.
* *

As for the two ears, in their consensus that leaving them unwashed, or washing what faces forward of them together with the face, does not invalidate the prayer of one who prays with the purification in which he left them unwashed, together with their unanimous agreement that if he left washing any part of his face that must be washed in his ablution, his prayer would not be valid with that purification, there is an indication that the ruling on that is what the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, whose statement we have mentioned: that they are not part of the face, unlike what al-Sha'bi said.
* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And your hands up to the elbows﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed over "the elbows" (al-marafiq), whether they are part of the hand that must be washed or not, after their unanimous agreement that washing the hand up to them is obligatory.

Malik ibn Anas said, when he was asked about the words of Allah: "Wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows" – do you think one should pass over the two elbows in ablution? He said: What He commanded is that one reaches the "two elbows." Blessed and exalted is He said: "Wash your faces," so this one washes behind it!! [[In the printed edition: "madhhab hadha yaghsilu khalfahu", and the first editor found it problematic, rightly so. It is likewise poorly written in the manuscript, and the correct reading is "fa-dhahaba", and this sentence expresses amazement at one who was told "Wash your faces" and then set about washing what is behind the face, i.e., the back of the neck.]] It was said to him: But one washes up to the elbows and the ankles, not going beyond them? He said: I do not know "what is not beyond them." As for what He commanded that one reaches, this is: up to the elbows and the ankles. Al-Yunus narrated to us from Ashhab, from him.
* *

Al-Shafi'i said: I know of no dissenter on the point that the elbows are included in what is washed, as if he is inclined to hold that its meaning is: "Wash your faces and your hands up to the point that the elbows are washed." Al-Rabi' narrated this to us from him. [[This entire passage is the text of al-Shafi'i in al-Umm 1: 22, except that it has: "as if they went to the view that its meaning ..."]]
* *

Others said: Allah only obliged, by His saying "and your hands up to the elbows," the washing of the two hands up to the two elbows. The two elbows are the limit of what Allah obliged washing of from the end of the hand, and the limit is not included within the defined scope, just as the night is not included in what Allah, exalted is He, obliged on His servants of fasting by His saying: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 187], because the night is the limit of the fasting person's fast; when it reaches him, he has fulfilled what is upon him. They said: Likewise the elbows in His saying "Wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows" are the limit of what Allah obliged washing of in the hand. This is the view of Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl. [["Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl ibn Qays al-'Anbari", Abu al-Hudhayl, companion of Abu Hanifa. He was among the people of hadith, then opinion came to dominate him, and he became one of Abu Hanifa's companions.]]
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that washing the two hands up to the elbows is part of the obligatory duty, which if one leaves it or part of it, his prayer is not valid while leaving its washing. As for the elbows and what lies beyond them, washing that is part of the recommended (nadb) acts to which the Prophet (ﷺ) urged his community by his saying:

1143 2 – "My community will be the radiant ones, with white marks from the traces of ablution, so whoever among you is able to extend his radiance, let him do so." [[This is a sound hadith, whose chain was not mentioned; al-Bukhari narrated it (Fath 1: 207, 208), with the wording: "Indeed my community will be called on the Day of Resurrection radiant and marked," with the like of this meaning.
And "al-Ghurr" is the plural of "aghurr", meaning one with a blaze (ghurra), (with the ghayn vowelled and the ra' doubled), which is a white patch found on the forehead of a horse. By it is meant the light that will be on the faces of the people of faith in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he brought, and who were guided by his guidance.
And "al-muhajjalun" is from "al-tahjil", which is the whiteness found on three of the legs of a horse. These are the marks of the believers who followed him (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection.]] = so the prayer of one who leaves washing them and washing what lies beyond them is not invalidated, for what we have already explained before: that every limit delimited by "ila" (to, until) may in the speech of the Arabs admit of the limit being included within the scope and of its being excluded from it. And when the speech admits of that, it is not permissible for anyone to rule that it is included in it, except for one whose opposition is not permissible concerning what he has clarified and decided, and no ruling is issued that the elbows are included in what must be washed in our view, from one whose ruling must be accepted in full.
* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And wipe over your heads﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed over the manner of the "wiping" (mash) that Allah commanded by His saying "and wipe over your heads."

Some of them said: wipe with whatever part of your heads you see fit to wipe with water when you stand to prayer.

Mention of those who said that:

1143 3 – Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdhami narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Hafs, who said: The wiping of the head was mentioned in the presence of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and he said: "O Nafi', how did Ibn 'Umar wipe?" He said: "One single wipe" – and he described that he wiped the front of his head toward his face – and al-Qasim said: "Ibn 'Umar is the most knowledgeable and most learned of us."

1143 4 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Nafi' informed me that Ibn 'Umar, when he performed ablution, would return his right palm to the water and place them in it, then wipe with his two hands the front of his head.

1143 5 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkir narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Nafi' informed me that Ibn 'Umar used to place the inner part of his right palm on the water, [[In the printed edition: "kana yada'u bitna kaffayhi 'ala al-ma'", and I wonder how the editor permitted himself to turn "kaffahu al-yumna" into "kaffayhi"? Was it because the copyist wrote in the following sentence "then he does not shake them off, then wipes with them" in the dual? The copyist erred in the dual of the pronoun, and I have returned it to the correct reading with the singular pronoun.]] not shaking it off, then wipe with it between his two horns up to the forehead once, and then he would not add to it in all of that any wiping other than one single wiping, moving from the forehead toward the horn. [["Al-qarn" is the edge and side of the head, and they are two horns, one to the right and one to the left.]]

1143 6 – Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: that when he performed ablution he wiped the front of his head.

1143 7 – Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from 'Abd al-A'la al-Tha'labi, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: It suffices you to wipe the front of your head if you are wearing a turban. [["I'tamara al-rajulu ya'tamiru, fa-huwa mu'tamir": when a man wraps a turban, he is muta'imm. And "al-'imara" (with the ayn vowelled): everything on the head, whether a turban, a cap, a crown, or other.]] And so does the woman.

1143 8 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Nafi', who said: I saw Ibn 'Umar wipe his crown (bayafukh) with one wipe. Sufyan said: If he wiped one hair, it suffices him – meaning one.

1143 9 – Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, who said: Whatever parts of your head you touch with water, it suffices you. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "mastu al-ma'", which is an error, see the following report.]]

1143 10 – Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Zabyan narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Whatever parts of your head you touch with water, it suffices you. [[Report 1143 10: In the printed edition it read "... from al-Sha'bi, the like of it", without the wording of the report being established; it is established in the manuscript, so I returned it to its place.]]

1143 11 – Al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Azraq, from al-Sha'bi, the like of it. [[Report 1143 11: The earlier printed edition placed this report after the following one, and it erred.]]

1143 12 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar used to wipe his head thus – and Ayyub placed his palm in the middle of his head, then drew it over the front of his head.

1143 13 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: If he wipes his head with one finger, it suffices him. [[Report 1143 13: "Zayd ibn al-Hubab" was mentioned shortly before under no. 11414, and in the manuscript and printed edition it read "Yazid ibn al-Hubab", which is an error.]]

1143 14 – Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I said to Abu 'Amr: What is sufficient of wiping the head? He said: That you wipe the front of your head to the nape, is more beloved to me.

1143 15 – Al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to me, from his father, from him, the like of it.
* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: wipe over all of your heads. They said: If he does not wipe over all of his head with water, his prayer with that ablution is not valid for him.

Mention of those who said that:

1143 16 – Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ashhab narrated to us, saying: Malik said: Whoever wipes only part of his head and does not cover all of it, must repeat the prayer, in the same position as one who washed only part of his face or part of his forearm. He said: Malik was asked about wiping the head, and he said: One begins from the front of the face, then turns the two hands to the back of the neck, then returns them to where he began.
* *

Others said: wiping the head is not sufficient with less than three fingers. This is the view of Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad.
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that Allah, mighty is His praise, commanded the wiping of the head of one standing to prayer together with the rest of what He commanded to be washed or wiped with it, and did not set a limit for that which it is not permissible to fall short of or exceed. Since that is so, whatever part of his head the one performing ablution wipes, deserving by his wiping that it be said "he wiped his head," he has fulfilled what Allah obliged of wiping that, by its falling within what is incumbent on him under the name "one who wipes his head" when he stands to prayer. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "ism mamsaha", and the correct reading is what I have recorded.]]
* *

If someone says to us: Allah has said regarding tayammum: ﴿So wipe your faces and your hands﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 43] – is wiping part of the face and hands sufficient in tayammum?

It is said to him: Whatever is wiped of that with dust, concerning which the scholars have disputed – some said "it suffices him for tayammum" and some said "it does not suffice him" – it suffices him, for it falls within the name "those who wipe with it."

And whatever of that there is consensus is not sufficient, is accepted as what the proof has brought down transmitted from its Prophet (ﷺ). No argument can be made against us in that, since it is part of our position that what has come in the verses of the Book in general terms regarding a meaning, the obligation is to rule that it is upon its generality, until something that must be accepted specifies it. If something is specified from it, what was specified is outside its apparent scope, and the rest of it remains under the ruling of generality. [[See the interpretation of the tayammum verse in 8: 410–425.]]

We have already explained the reason that makes the saying correct concerning that in another place, in a way that suffices without repeating it here. [[See the discussion on specification and generality earlier, 2: 207, 539; 4: 134; 5: 40, 130, and in many other scattered places.]]
* *

And the "head" that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, commanded wiping with by His saying "and wipe over your heads and your feet up to the ankles" is the place where the hair of the head grows, excluding what goes beyond that to the back of the neck, from what is turned away, and excluding what slopes down from that from the direction of the face to the forehead.
* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And your feet up to the ankles﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed in the reading of this.

A group of the readers of the Hijaz and Iraq read it: ﴿and your feet up to the ankles﴾ with a fatha (nasb), so its interpretation is: when you stand to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows and your feet up to the ankles, and wipe over your heads. When it is recited thus, it is from the delayed element whose meaning is the preceding, and the "feet" (al-arjul) are in the accusative, conjoined to "the hands" (al-aydi). Those who recite it thus interpreted that Allah, mighty is His praise, only commanded His servants to wash the feet, not to wipe them.
* *

Mention of those who said: Allah meant by His saying "and your feet up to the ankles" the washing.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 7 of 7):**

11447 - Ḥumayd ibn Mas'adah said: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, who said: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, that a man prayed while there was a spot the size of a fingernail on the top of his foot. When he finished his prayer, Umar said to him: "Repeat your ablution and your prayer."

Abu Ja'far narrated from him in the History 2: 40, "Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, from Sufyan". Biographed in al-Tahdhib.

11469 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Ata, who said: "I have not seen anyone wiping over the feet."

11470 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to me, who said: Hammad narrated to us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Mujahid, that he recited: "And your feet up to the ankles" (﴿وَأرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾) with the accusative, and said: "It has returned to washing."

11471 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, who said: I heard al-A'mash recite: "And your feet" (﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾) with the accusative.

11472 - Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ashhab informed us, who said: Malik was asked about the saying of Allah: "And wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles" - is it "arjulakum" or "arjulikum"? He said: "It is only washing, not wiping; the feet are not wiped, they are washed." It was said to him: "What do you think of one who wipes them, will that suffice him?" He said: "No."

11473 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, who said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: "And wipe your heads and your feet" (﴿وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾), he said: "Wash them, washing."

[[The author's speech has been abridged due to its great length.]]

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾ (7)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, means by this: [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "He, may His praise be great, means by His words", but the context requires what has been adopted.]] And remember the favour of Allah upon you, O believers, through the contracts that you made to Allah on your own selves. And remember His favour upon you in this, in that He guided you from the contracts to that which is pleasing (to Him), and enabled you to that which is your salvation from misguidance and ruin, among other abundant blessings. As [reported]:

11550 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And remember the favour of Allah upon you," he said: "The favours are the bounties of Allah."

11551 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words: "and His covenant with which He bound you," it means: and remember also, O believers, among the favours of Allah that He bestowed upon you, "His covenant with which He bound you," that is, His pledge that He made with you.[[See the explanation of "covenant" (al-mithaq) in what preceded, 9:363, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the "covenant" mentioned by God in this verse: which of His covenants did He mean?

Some of them said: He meant by it the covenant of Allah with which He bound the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to hear and obey him in what they liked and disliked, and to act upon everything that Allah and His Messenger commanded them.

Mention of those who said that:

11552 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: "And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'," the verse. He means: when Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ and revealed the Book to him, [["hayth" here is used in place of "heen". Al-Asma'i said: "Among what the common and the elite err in is the section on 'heen' and 'hayth'; the scholars erred in it, such as Abu 'Ubaydah and Sibawayh." Abu Hatim said: "I saw in the book of Sibawayh many things where he makes heen = hayth", and likewise in the book of Abu 'Ubaydah in his own hand. Abu Hatim said: Know that "heen" and "hayth" are adverbs: "heen" is an adverb of time, and "hayth" is an adverb of place, and each of them has a limit it does not exceed, but most people have made them both "hayth".

Then see al-Akhfash's view that "hayth" is an adverb of time, in al-Khizanah 3:162. The matter requires further research; this is not its place.]] and they said: "We believed in the Prophet ﷺ and in the Book, [[In the printed edition: "in the Prophet and the Book", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] and we acknowledged what is in the Torah." So Allah reminded them of the covenant they acknowledged against themselves, and commanded them to fulfil it.

11553 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey'," he said: He took our covenant and we said: "We hear and we obey," upon faith in Him and acknowledgment of Him and His Messenger.

* *

Others said: Rather, He, may His praise be great, meant by it: His covenant that He took from His servants when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam ﷺ and made them testify against themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify."

Mention of those who said that:

11554 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "and His covenant with which He bound you," he said: That with which He bound the children of Adam in the loins of Adam.

11555 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, namely that its meaning is: "And remember," O believers, "the favour of Allah upon you," which He bestowed upon you by guiding you to Islam, "and His covenant with which He bound you," that is, His pledge that He made with you when you pledged allegiance to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to hear and obey him in ease and hardship, in what you like and dislike, and in difficulty and ease, "when you said, 'We hear,'" what you told us, and what you took from us of covenants, "and we obey you" in what you commanded us and what you forbade us from. And He bestowed upon you also by granting you success in accepting that from Him by your saying to Him, "We hear and we obey." He says: So fulfil for Allah, O believers, His covenant with which He bound you, and His favour which He bestowed upon you in this, by your acknowledgment against yourselves of hearing Him and obeying Him in what He commanded you and what He forbade you. He will fulfil for you what He guaranteed to you of fulfilment if you fulfil to Him His covenant: the completion of His favour upon you, your entry into His Paradise, His bestowing upon you eternal abiding in the abode of His honour, and your rescue from His punishment and painful torment.

We only said that this is more correct than the view of those who said: "It means the covenant taken from them in the loins of Adam, may Allah's blessings be upon him," because Allah, may His praise be great, mentioned immediately after the reminder to the believers His covenant with which He bound them, the covenant with which He bound the People of the Torah, after He had revealed His Book to His Prophet Musa ﷺ, concerning what He commanded them and forbade them in it,[[His words "fiha", i.e., in the Torah; the context is: "His covenant with which He bound the People of the Torah... in it".]] so He said: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders﴾, and the verses following it [Surah al-Ma'idah: 12], alerting thereby the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Muhammad, to the stations of their portion of fulfilment to Allah in what He bound them to, and informing them of the evil outcome of the People of the Book in their squandering what they squandered of His covenant with which He bound them in His command and His prohibition, and in honouring His prophets and messengers, warning them against breaking their pledges, lest there befall them what befell the covenant-breakers among the People of the Book before them.

So it was, since what He reminded them of, admonished them with, and forbade them from doing the like of its action, was the covenant of a people whose covenant was taken after the sending of the Messenger to them and the revelation of the Book upon them, it was necessary that the state in which the covenant was taken and the admonished be like the state of those who were admonished by it. And when that is so, the correctness of what we have said on this matter and the falsity of its opposite become clear.

* *

As for His words: "And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts," it is a warning from Allah, may His name be exalted, to the believers who were among His Messenger's companions ﷺ, [[In the printed edition: "to the believers who surrounded His Messenger", differing from the manuscript, and it is pure correctness and classical Arabic; in place of "kanu" it has "alladhi atafu".]] and a threat to them that they break the covenant of Allah with which He bound them concerning His Messenger [[In the printed edition: "and a threat to them", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is pure correctness.]] and their pledge which they made in it, by concealing in themselves the opposite of what they displayed with their tongues. [[His words "by concealing..." are linked to "that they break the covenant of Allah...", by concealing.]]

He, may His praise be great, says to them: Fear Allah, O believers, be mindful of Him, lest you change His pledge and break His covenant with which He bound you, or oppose what you guaranteed to Him by your saying "We hear and we obey," by concealing in yourselves other than fulfilment of that. For Allah is aware of the inner contents of your breasts,[[See the explanation of "dhat al-sudur" in what preceded, 7:155, 325.]] and knowing of what your souls conceal; nothing of that is hidden from Him, so there would befall you from His punishment what you cannot bear, as befell those before you from the Jews, of transformation and various kinds of vengeance, and you would come in your return to the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment.

The interpretation of His words, mighty is His remembrance: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do" [Qur'an 5:8].

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be glorified, means by this: O you who have believed in Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad, let it be among your characteristics and qualities to be steadfast for Allah, witnesses of justice concerning your allies and your enemies, [In the printed edition: "li-wilayatihim" (for their guardianship), and "lakum" (for you) is omitted; I have restored it from the manuscript.] and do not be unjust in your judgments and actions, so that you transgress what I have set for you concerning your enemies because of their enmity toward you, and do not fall short in what I have set for you of My rulings and limits concerning your allies because of their guardianship over you. [See the explanation of "al-qist" above, 9:301, note 5, and the references there.] Rather, in all of them, halt at My limit, and act toward them according to My command.

* *

As for His words: "And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just" — He says: Do not let the enmity of a people lead you to be unjust in your judgment concerning them and in your conduct among them, so that you act unjustly toward them because of the enmity between you and them.

* *

We have already mentioned the reports from the people of interpretation concerning the meaning of His words: "Be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice" [Qur'an 4:135], and concerning His words: "And do not let the hatred of a people..." [Qur'an 5:2], and the differing of those who differ regarding the recitation of that, and which view is closer to the truth in its interpretation and recitation — by the evidences indicating its soundness, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [See what has preceded, 9:301, the first verse; then the second, 9:483–487.]

* *

It has been said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when the Jews intended to kill him.

Mention of those who said that:

11556 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness" — it was revealed concerning the Jews of Khaybar, who intended to kill the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Juraij said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the Jews seeking their help regarding a blood-money payment, and they resolved to kill him; so that is His words: "And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just..." to the end of the verse.

* *

The interpretation of His words, mighty is His remembrance: "Be just; that is nearer to righteousness, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do" [Qur'an 5:8].

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be glorified, by His words "Be just" means: O believers, be just toward every person among the people, whether an ally or an enemy to you, so compel them to what I have commanded you to compel them to of My rulings, and do not be unjust toward any of them concerning it.

* *

As for His words: "That is nearer to righteousness" — by "that" He means: justice toward them is nearer to you, O believers, to righteousness; that is, to your being, in the sight of Allah, by your practicing it, among the people of righteousness, who are the people of fear and caution before Allah, lest they oppose Him in any part of His command or commit any of His disobediences. [See the explanation of "al-'adl" and "al-taqwa" in the language indexes above.]

* *

Mighty is His praise: He described "justice" as nearer to righteousness than injustice because whoever is just is obedient to Allah through his justice, and whoever is obedient to Allah is without doubt among the people of righteousness; and whoever is unjust is disobedient to Allah, and whoever is disobedient to Allah is far from his righteousness.

* *

He used "that is nearer" to refer to the act [By "the act" he means the verbal noun of the action, as above shortly, p. 82, note 2; see the index of terms.], and the Arabs refer to actions with "huwa" and "dhalika" when they refer to them with these words, as He, mighty is His praise, said: "fa-huwa khayrun lakum" [Qur'an 2:271] and "dhalikum azka lakum" [Qur'an 2:232]. [In the printed edition: "huwa khayrun lakum," and in the manuscript "huwa" is omitted; what I have written is the text of the verse of al-Baqarah 2:271; review this in 5:582 above. See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:303.] Had "huwa" not been in the sentence, "aqrab" would have been in the accusative, and it would have been said: "i'dilu aqraba li-l-taqwa," as it was said: "intahu khayran lakum" [Qur'an 4:171]. [See what has preceded, 9:413–415.]

* *

As for His words: "And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do" — He means: Beware, O believers, lest you be unjust toward His servants, transgressing in them His judgment and decree which He has made clear to you, so that His punishment befalls you and you deserve His painful retribution. "Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do" — that is, Allah has knowledge and awareness of what you do, O believers, regarding what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, whether by acting upon it or acting contrary to it, counting all of that against you, until He recompenses you for it: the good-doer among you with his good, and the evil-doer with his evil. So beware of doing evil. [See the explanation of "khabir" in the language indexes above.]

Commentary on the verse: "Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward" (5:9)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds" — Allah promises, O people, those who affirm Allah and His Messenger, and acknowledge what came to them from their Lord, and act upon what Allah made them pledge, and fulfil the covenants which they contracted with Him by their saying, "We will hear and we will obey Allah and His Messenger." So they heard the command and prohibition of Allah and obeyed Him, acting upon what Allah commanded them and refraining from what He forbade them. [See the explanation of "righteous deeds" (al-salihat) in the earlier indexes of language.]

And by His saying, "for them is forgiveness" — for those who fulfilled the covenants and the pact which their Lord made with them — "forgiveness," which is the concealing of their past sins from them and covering them with His pardon, and His leaving off punishing them for them and exposing them because of them. [See the explanation of "forgiveness" (al-maghfirah) in the earlier indexes of language.] "And a great reward" — he says: and for them, along with His pardon of their past sins, is a recompense for their deeds which they performed and their fulfilment of the covenants which they contracted with their Lord: "a great reward." "Great" (al-azim) means that its extent from Him is not limited, and its end is known only to Him, exalted is His remembrance. [See the explanation of "reward" (al-ajr) and "great" (azim) in the earlier indexes of language.]

* *

If someone says: Allah, may His majesty be glorified, informed in this verse that He promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, but He did not state what He promised them. So where is the report of what was promised?

It is said: Yes (bala). [The word "bala" is used as an answer to a negative statement, as in His saying, "Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes (bala)." Thus they said, and Ibn Hisham said in al-Mughni under the entry on "bala": "But it has occurred in the books of hadith that it is used to answer a plain interrogative. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in the Book of Faith, that he, peace be upon him, said to his companions: 'Are you content that you should be a quarter of the people of Paradise?' They said: 'Yes (bala).' In Sahih Muslim, in the Book of Gifts: 'Would it please you that they be equal to you in righteousness?' He said: 'Yes!' He said: 'Then no.' And also in it: he said, 'Are you the one who met me in Mecca?' So he said to him: 'Yes (bala).'"

For this reason al-Tabari used it in answer to an interrogative which contains no negation, as though he counted the questioner's question as a denial, because of its mention in the verse, so he said in answer "bala," meaning: it is not as you suppose. See what has preceded at 2:280 and 2:510, and what will come in the report no. 11818.] Indeed He has informed of what was promised, and what was promised is His saying, "for them is forgiveness and a great reward."

If he says: But His saying, "for them is forgiveness and a great reward" is an independent statement, and if it were what was promised it would have been said, "Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward," and "for them" would not have been included. The inclusion of "for them" indicates the beginning of speech and the conclusion of the report about the promise!

It is said: Although its apparent meaning is as you have mentioned, it is among those things where the indication of what is manifest in the speech is relied upon for what is hidden of its meaning, with the omission of some mention that has been left out of it. The meaning of the speech is: Allah promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that He would forgive them and reward them with a great reward. For it is the practice of the Arabs to accompany "promise" with "an" (that) and to govern it with it, but "an" was dropped because "promise" is a form of speech.
