And it is the practice with "speech" that what follows it of statements in sentences is begun, and the predicate sentence is mentioned after it, relying on the indication of the apparent speech upon its meaning, and turning the promise — which agrees with speech in meaning though it differs in its wording — toward its meaning [The context: "and turning the promise... toward its meaning," i.e., toward the meaning of "speech."] so it is as if it were said: "Allah said: For those who believe and do righteous deeds is forgiveness and a great reward."

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was only said, "Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward," with regard to the promise with which they were promised. So the meaning of the speech, according to the interpretation of the speaker of this view, is: Allah's promise to those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward, [in what He promised them]. [In this place the printed edition and the manuscript give only the text of the verse; I have supplied the completion of the statement from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi, 6:110, where he follows it with the words: "and this meaning is from al-Hasan," so I do not know whether I have hit upon the right reading or whether I have missed it!]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 10 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs — those are the companions of the Blaze﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "Those who disbelieve" — meaning those who deny the oneness of God and break His covenant and the agreements they contracted with Him — "and deny Our signs" — meaning they deny the proofs and arguments of God that indicate His oneness, which the messengers brought and others besides them — "those are the companions of the Blaze" — meaning: those who have this description are the people of the "Blaze," that is, the people of the Fire who abide therein forever and never leave it. [Refer to the explanation of "disbelief" (kufr), "signs" (ayat), and "companions of the Blaze" in the earlier word indices.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you, but He withheld their hands from you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise: [The printed and manuscript editions read: "By that, exalted is His praise: O you who believe, affirm..," I have restored what the context of Abu Ja'far's usage throughout his exegesis requires; it is most likely a poor abbreviation by the copyist.] "O you who believe" — O you who affirm the oneness of God and the messengership of His Messenger ﷺ and what came to them from their Lord — "remember the favour of God upon you" — remember the blessing God bestowed upon you, so thank Him for it by fulfilling to Him His covenant which He made with you, and the agreements you contracted with your Prophet ﷺ. Then He described the favour for which He commanded them to give thanks, along with His other favours, saying: it is His withholding from you the hands of the people who intended to seize you, so He turned them away from you and prevented them from what they wished to do to you. [Refer to the explanation of "withholding" (kaff) earlier: 8:548 / 9:29 = and "concern" (hamm) has likewise been discussed earlier: 9:199.]

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the nature of this favour which God, exalted is His praise, reminded the companions of His Prophet ﷺ of, and commanded them to thank Him for.

Some of them said: It is God's rescue of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions from what the Jews of the Banu al-Nadir had determined to do when they came to them seeking help with the blood-money (diyah) of the two men of the Banu Amir whom Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed. [The "hamalah" (with a fatha on the ḥa') is the blood-money and fine that a group bears on behalf of another group, undertaking to pay it; one says "tahammala al-hamalah" and "istahmala al-qawm," meaning he asked them to help him with his hamalah, which is the blood-money he had taken responsibility for.]

Mention of those who said this:

11557 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ went out to the Banu al-Nadir seeking their help regarding the blood-money of the two men of the Banu Amir whom Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed. When he came to them, some of them withdrew with one another and said: "You will not find Muhammad closer than he is now. Who among you will climb onto this house and drop a rock on him, so that he relieves us of him?" Amr ibn Jahhash ibn Ka'b said: "I will." [The "ẓahara 'ala al-bayt" means he climbed upon it, i.e., mounted its roof. In the printed edition it read: "fa-mirū rajulan yaẓhar" and neither it nor the manuscript contains "I will," so the copyist changed it because of the corruption of his script at this point. The correct reading is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.] The news reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he left them, so God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed concerning them and what he and his people intended: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you..." to the end of the verse. [Report 11557: it is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:211, 212; then it comes there in a different wording 3:199-200.]

11558 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: "When a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you," he said: The Jews — the Prophet ﷺ entered upon them a garden of theirs, ["al-ha'it" is an orchard of palm trees, enclosed by a wall.] while his companions were behind its wall, and he sought their help regarding a debt of blood-money he had incurred, then he rose from their presence. They conspired among themselves to kill him, so he went out walking backwards, looking at them, then he called his companions one by one until they gathered to him.

11559 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you, but He withheld their hands from you": the Jews, when the Prophet ﷺ entered a garden of theirs, and his companions were behind a wall of theirs, he sought their help regarding a fine, in the blood-money which he had incurred, then he rose from their presence. They conspired among themselves to kill him, so he went out walking sideways, looking at them with fear of them [ "mu'tarid(an)" means he took to the right and the left, inclining his face toward them as he looked, walking this way and that, his gait not straight on the road], then he called his companions one by one until they gathered to him. God, exalted and majestic, said: "So He withheld their hands from you, and fear God; and upon God let the believers rely." [In the printed edition: "fi maghram diyah," as in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:266. In the manuscript: "fi al-diyah" with the definite article, so I judged that the word "allati" (which) had fallen out of the text, and I restored it.]

11560 - Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ came to the Banu al-Nadir seeking their help regarding a blood-money that had fallen on him, and with him were Abu Bakr, Umar and Ali. He said: "Help me with a blood-money that has fallen on me." They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, it is time for you to come to us and ask us a need! Sit until we feed you and give you what you ask of us!" The Messenger of God ﷺ sat, and his companions waited for him. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who was the chief of the people and who had said to the Messenger of God ﷺ what he had said, came, and Huyayy said to his companions: "You will not see him closer than he is now. Throw stones on him and kill him, and you will never see evil again!" They came to a great millstone of theirs to throw it upon him, but God withheld their hands from it, until Gabriel ﷺ came to him and raised him from that place. God, exalted and majestic, revealed: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you, but He withheld their hands from you, and fear God; and upon God let the believers rely." So God, exalted is His remembrance, informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they had intended for him.

11561 - Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Abd Allah ibn Kathir: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you" to the end of the verse, he said: The Jews. The Prophet ﷺ entered upon them a garden, and sought their help regarding a debt he had incurred, so they conspired among themselves to kill him, and he rose from their presence and went out walking sideways, looking at them with fear of them, then he called his companions one by one until they gathered to him. ["Mu'tarid(an)" means he took to the right and the left, inclining his face toward them as he looked, walking this way and that, his gait not straight on the road.]

11562 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ikrimah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Ansari, one of the Banu al-Najjar and one of the nuqaba' on the night of 'Aqabah, [the nuqaba' being the chiefs] with thirty riders from the Muhajirun and the Ansar. They set out and met Amir ibn al-Tufayl ibn Malik ibn Ja'far at the well of Ma'unah, which is one of the waters of the Banu Amir. They fought, and al-Mundhir and his companions were killed except three men who were searching for a stray of theirs. They were not alerted except by birds circling in the sky, from between whose beaks dripped clots of blood. ["al-'alaq" (with two fathas) means thick clotted pieces of blood before it dries.] One of the three said: "Our companions have been slain, by the Merciful!" Then he turned, running swiftly until he met a man, ["ishtadda" means he ran with great speed.] and they exchanged two blows; when the blow reached him, he raised his head to the sky, opened his eyes, and said: "God is greatest, Paradise and the Lord of the worlds!" He was called "A'naqa li-yamut" ["A'naqa li-yamut" and "al-mu'naqa li-yamut" — it is said that he is al-Mundhir ibn Amr al-Ansari, and it is said that he is Haram ibn Milhan al-Najjari. "A'naqa al-rajul i'naqan" means he hastened with great haste until he overtook people; he was named thus because he hastened to his place of falling, may God be pleased with him.] The other two companions returned and met two men from the Banu Sulaym, between whom and the Prophet ﷺ and their people there was a truce; they claimed to them that they belonged to the Banu Amir, and the two killed them. Their people came to the Prophet ﷺ seeking the blood-money, so he went out with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talhah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, until they entered upon Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and the Jews of al-Nadir, and sought their help regarding the blood-money of the two. He said: The Jews gathered to kill the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions, and they pretended to be preparing food. ["al-Sani'ah" and "al-Sani'" are food prepared and readied for hospitality and honour.] Gabriel ﷺ came to him with what the Jews had agreed upon of treachery, [in the printed edition: "ajma'at 'alayhi," and I have restored what is in the manuscript.] so he went out and then called Ali and said: "Do not leave your place; whoever comes out to you from my companions and asks you about me, say: 'He has gone toward Medina, so overtake him.'" [In the manuscript: "wajjah al-Madinah," omitting "ila"; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.] He said: They began passing by Ali, and he would order them as he had been ordered, until the last of them came to him; then he followed them. That is His saying: "And you will not cease to discover treachery from them" [Surat al-Ma'idah: 13].

11563 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik regarding His saying: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you, but He withheld their hands from you," he said: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions, when they wanted to betray the Messenger of God ﷺ.

* *

Others said: Rather, the favour that God mentioned in this verse, for which He commanded the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ to give thanks, is that the Jews had determined to kill the Prophet ﷺ through a meal to which they had invited him, so God, exalted and majestic, informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they intended, and he and his companions refrained from accepting their invitation.

Mention of those who said this:

11564 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you" to His saying: "but He withheld their hands from you." That was because some people of the Jews prepared a meal for the Messenger of God and his companions, intending to kill him when the food came; God revealed to him their plan, so the food did not come, and he commanded his companions, so they did not go to it. [In the printed edition: "wa-amara ashabahu fa-abawhu," and "abawhu" here is a weak construction. In the manuscript: "fa-atawhu" with dots. This contradicts what is in the subject heading, since it says "so he and his companions refrained from accepting their invitation"; so I preferred to restore the text of al-Durr al-Manthur 1:266, which matches the heading. Al-Suyuti transmitted it from Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim by this same chain.]

* *

Others said: God, exalted is His praise, meant by that: the favour He bestowed upon the believers by informing His Prophet ﷺ of what their enemy and the enemy of the believers among the polytheists had intended on the day of Batn Nakhl, of deceiving them and attacking them when they became occupied with their prayer and prostrated in it; and by His teaching His Prophet ﷺ to be wary of his enemy during his prayer, by teaching him the prayer of fear.

Mention of those who said this:

11565 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayn narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you" to the end of the verse. It was mentioned to us that it was revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ while he was at Batn Nakhl in the seventh expedition, [thus he said: "in the seventh expedition," whereas in many reports it is "the ninth expedition," which is "the expedition of Dhi Amr" in Najd; see Ibn Sa'd 2/1/24, and Imta' al-Asma' of al-Maqrizi 1:110, 111. See the commentary on the following report and the earlier report no. 10340, which reports that the prayer of fear was in the seventh year.] that the Banu Tha'labah and the Banu Muharib wanted to ambush him, and God informed him of that. It was mentioned to us that a man volunteered to kill him, and came to the Prophet of God ﷺ while his sword was placed down, and said: "Shall I take it, O Prophet of God?" He said: "Take it!" He said: "Shall I draw it?" He said: "Yes!" So he drew it and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "God protects me from you!" The companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ threatened him and spoke harshly to him, so he sheathed the sword, ["shama al-sayf" means he sheathed it. It is one of the words with opposite meanings; it is also said "shama al-sayf" meaning he drew it.] and the Prophet of God ﷺ ordered his companions to depart, and then the prayer of fear was revealed to him at that time. [Report 11565: this report about "the prayer of fear" was not mentioned by Abu Ja'far under the prayer of fear earlier, 5:237-250, nor in 9:123-166.]

11566 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who mentioned it from Abu Salamah, from Jabir: that the Prophet ﷺ stopped at a place and the people scattered among the 'idah trees seeking shade beneath them, ["al-'idah" (with a kasrah on the 'ayn) is a name applied to large thorny trees whose thorns are strong, under which people seek shade.] and the Prophet ﷺ hung his weapon on a tree. A Bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of God ﷺ, took it and drew it, then approached the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Who will protect you from me?" While the Prophet ﷺ said: "God." The Bedouin sheathed the sword ["shama al-sayf" means he sheathed it. It is one of the words with opposite meanings; it is also said "shama al-sayf" meaning he drew it.] and the Prophet ﷺ called his companions and informed them of the account of the Bedouin, while he was sitting beside him and did not punish him. Ma'mar said: Qatadah used to mention something similar, and he mentioned that a group of Arabs wanted to ambush the Messenger of God ﷺ, so they sent this Bedouin. He interpreted: "Remember the favour of God upon you when a people determined to stretch out their hands toward you," to the end of the verse. [Report 11566: "Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf" has been mentioned repeatedly. In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "Ibn Abi Salamah," with the extra "ibn," and the correct form is to delete it, as in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3:101.

This report from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir is in Musnad Ahmad 3:311, from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: "Abd Allah narrated to us: I found this hadith in my father's book in his own handwriting, and I heard it in another place: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, saying: Shu'ayb informed me, from al-Zuhri: Sinan ibn Abi Sinan al-Du'ali and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me that Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari..." and he related the report in a wording other than this, at length.

Then Ahmad also narrated it 3:364, through 'Affan ibn Aban, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Jabir, in a wording other than that one.

Ahmad also narrated the report of Jabir at length and in detail, through Abu Bishr, from Sulayman ibn Qays, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was attacked by Muharib of Khasafah at Nakhl; Musnad 3:364, 365, then 390.

It is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 7:329-331), with several chains. Muslim related it in his Sahih, 15:44, 45, with the chain of al-Tabari and Ahmad.

See also what Abu Ja'far related from the hadith of Jabir earlier under no. 10325.

Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 3:101, after relating Abu Ja'far's report about this passage from the Tafsir: "This Bedouin was Ghawrath ibn al-Harith, established in the Sahih."]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this is the saying of one who said: By the favour that God mentioned in this verse, He meant His favour upon the believers in Him and His Messenger, which He bestowed upon them by rescuing their Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from what the Jews of the Banu al-Nadir had determined regarding his killing and the killing of those with him, on the day the Prophet of God ﷺ went out to them concerning the blood-money which he had taken responsibility for regarding the two slain men of Amr ibn Umayya.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 10 (part 2 of 2):

We have said that this interpretation is more deserving of being considered correct because God, may His praise be exalted, followed the mention of that with a reproach to the Jews for their deeds and the ugliness of their actions, and their betrayal of their Lord and His prophets. Then He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to pardon them and to overlook their great ignorance. Thus it was known from this that he ﷺ was not commanded to pardon them and overlook their conduct following His saying: ﴿that they might stretch out their hands towards you﴾, while others than them were stretching out their hands towards them. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and from others than them were stretching out their hands towards them," with the addition of "min" (from), which is a severe corruption of the meaning; the correct reading is to omit "min," as the flow of the discourse indicates. The waw in "wa-ghayruhum" is the waw of circumstance (waw al-hal).]] For if those who intended to stretch out their hands towards them had been others, it would have been fitting for the command to pardon and overlook to be directed at them, not at those who had no such mention made of them. Likewise, the attribute of betrayal would have been applied to them in this context, not to those for whom no betrayal had been mentioned. In this there is an indication of the correctness of what we have decided is correct among the interpretations on this matter, rather than what contradicts it.

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And fear Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ (11)**

[[The beginning of the verse, namely "And fear Allah," was omitted from the manuscript and the printed edition, so I have restored it.]] Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: Beware of Allah, O believers, lest you oppose Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and lest you break the covenant He has made with you, so that you deserve from Him a punishment you cannot withstand. "And upon Allah let the believers rely" means: Let them entrust the reins of their affairs to Allah, submit to His decree, and trust in His help and support. [[See the explanation of "tawakkul" (reliance, trust in God) above, vol. 8, p. 566, note 3, and the references there.]] This applies to those who acknowledge the oneness of Allah and the mission of His Messenger, and who act according to His commands and prohibitions, for that is part of the perfection of their religion and the completion of their faith. And when they do this, He will protect them, guard them, and keep them safe from whoever intends them harm, just as He protected you and defended you, O believers, against the Jews who resolved to stretch out their hands against you. This was His protection of you, since you were people of faith in Him and His Messenger, rather than others. [[His words "rather than others" mean: just as He protected and defended you, rather than others.]] Indeed, no one other than Him can repel an evil that your Lord intends for you, nor can anyone bring you a benefit that He has not decreed for you.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 5, Verse 12 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders (nuqaba').﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This verse was revealed as information from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to His Prophet ﷺ and to the believers in him, about the characteristics of those among the Jews who intended to stretch out their hands against them. Like what:

11567: Al-Harith ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Mubarak related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel," he said: "The Jews, the People of the Book."

* *

[The phrase "and that which they intended" (wa-anna al-ladhi hammu bihi) is coordinated with His saying "to inform him... of the characteristics of those who intended..., and that which they intended," this being the structure of the sentence.] And that which they intended of treachery and breaking the covenant between them and Him is among their attributes, the attributes of their forebears, and their characters and the characters of their ancestors of old. [The phrase "and as a proof..." (wa-ihtijajan) is coordinated with His earlier saying: "And this verse was revealed as information..."] And as a proof to His Prophet ﷺ against the Jews, by informing him of what was known to them, apart from the Arabs, of their hidden matters and their concealed knowledge, and as a rebuke to the Jews for their persistence in error and their insistence on disbelief, despite their knowledge of the wrongness of what they remain upon.

Allah says to His Prophet ﷺ: Do not regard as great the matter of those among these Jews who intended to stretch out their hands against you, nor the treachery they attempted and intended against you, for that is among the characteristics of their forebears and ancestors; they could be nothing but upon the path of their first and the way of their predecessors. Then the Exalted One, may His remembrance be exalted, began the report about some of their treacheries, betrayals, audacity against their Lord, and breaking of the covenant which their Creator had made with them, [the printed edition reads: "which you (they) were made to pledge by their own means," which the editor did not read well from the manuscript, as it was undotted, so he distorted it, which led to the ruin of the entire phrase], along with the blessings with which He favored them and the honors whose gratitude was placed upon them as a necessity. So He said: "And Allah had already taken the covenant of the predecessors of those who intended to stretch out their hands against you from among the Jews, the Children of Israel," O assembly of believers, to fulfill to Him His covenants and obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them. [See the explanation of "taking the covenant" in what has preceded, p. 91, note 2, and the references there.] As:

11568: Harith... [In the original: Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam al-'Asqalani related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His saying: "And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel," he said: Allah took their covenants that they should devote themselves sincerely to Him and not worship other than Him.]

* *

"And We raised among them twelve leaders (nuqaba')." What is meant by that: And We raised among them twelve guarantors who undertook on their behalf the fulfillment to Allah of what they had pledged to Him of covenants concerning what He commanded them and what He forbade them.

The word "naqib" (nuqaba', leader) in the speech of the Arabs is like the 'arif (overseer) over a people, except that it is above the 'arif. It is said of it: "Naqaba fulan 'ala bani fulan, fa-huwa yanqubu naqban" [the printed text and manuscript both read: "naqban", and this is an extremely unusual verbal noun, not mentioned by the Arabic lexicons; it is permissible but very weak, and I fear it may be an error by copyists, and that the correct form, on which the lexicon books agree, is "naqaba" (with a kasra on the nun) as the verbal noun of this verb. As for the verbal noun of the verb that follows it, it is with a fatha on the nun. Sibawayh said: "al-naqaba with a kasra is the noun, and with a fatha is the verbal noun, like al-wilaya and al-wilaya."] So when it is intended that he was not a naqib and then became one, it is said: "Qad naqaba, fa-huwa yanqubu naqaba." [And from 'arif: "'arafa 'alayhim, ya'rufu 'irafa." As for "al-manakib," they are like assistants who accompany the 'urafa', their singular being "minkab."]

It was said by some scholars of Arabic: He is the trustworthy guarantor over the people. [See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:156.]

* *

As for the exegetes, they differed among themselves regarding its interpretation.

Some of them said: He is the witness over his people.

Those who said this:

11569: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders," one man from each tribe, a witness over his people.

* *

And others said: "The naqib" is the trustworthy one.

Those who said this:

11570: It was narrated to me from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: "The nuqaba'" are the trustworthy ones.

11571: Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same.

* *

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, had commanded Musa, His Prophet ﷺ, to send the twelve nuqaba' from his people, the Children of Israel, to the land of the tyrants in Syria, to spy out for Musa their news [the printed text reads "to spy" with a jim, while "tahassus" with a ha' means seeking and investigating news. In the revelation: "O my sons, go and seek out (tahassasu) news of Yusuf and his brother."], when He intended their destruction, and that He would bequeath their land and their homes to Musa and his people, and make them dwellings for the Children of Israel after He had saved them from Pharaoh and his people and brought them out of the land of Egypt. So Musa sent those whom Allah had commanded him to send from the nuqaba' to it, as:

11572: Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Allah commanded the Children of Israel to march to Ariha, which is the land of Bayt al-Maqdis. They marched until, when they were near them, Musa sent twelve nuqaba' from all the tribes of the Children of Israel. They set out wishing to bring him news of the tyrants. There met them a man from among the giants called "'Aj," who seized the twelve and put them in his waistband [al-hujzah (with a dammah and then a sukun) is the place where the waist-wrap is tied. Glory be to God!! How exaggerated these narrators from the Israelite traditions were!!] and on his head a bundle of firewood. [The printed text reads: "a bundle (hizmah) of firewood," which the editor did not read well even though the manuscript is clear. I have set it down as it matches the manuscript of Tabari's History. And what will come under number 11656. And "al-hamlah" (with a fatha on the ha') is the amount that the carrier carries, just as one says "qabdah" for the amount the hand grips. I have not found this word explained in any book.] He went with them to his wife and said: Look at these people who claim they want to fight us!! He threw them down before her and said: Shall I not grind them under my foot! His wife said: Rather, release them so that they may inform their people of what they saw. He did so. When the people went out, some of them said to others: O people, if you inform the Children of Israel of the news of the people, they will apostatize from the Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him. But conceal it and inform the Prophet of Allah, and they (Musa and Harun) will see their own opinion! [By "the Prophet of Allah" is meant Musa and Harun, peace be upon them. The printed text had: "what they both see," and the correct reading is from the manuscript and the History.] So some of them took covenant from others to conceal this. Then they returned, and ten of them set out and broke the pact. A man would inform his brother and father of what he had seen of the matter of "'Aj" [this addition between brackets is from Tabari's History]. Two men among them concealed it. They came to Musa and Harun and informed them of the news. That is when Allah says: "And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders." [See what I have written on p. 92, note 1, regarding "haythu" and "hina."] [The report 11572 is the remainder of the report which Abu Ja'far narrated earlier as number 991, and it is in Tabari's History 1:221, 222. Its beginning will come as number 11656.]

11573: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's saying: "twelve leaders," one man from each tribe of the Children of Israel, whom Musa sent to the tyrants. They found that two of them could enter into the sleeve of one of them, and they would throw them down (yulqunahum ilqa'an) [in the manuscript: "yulfunahum alfan," undotted and unclear; in the printed text here: "yulfunahum lafan," and it will come under number 11660, as I have written it, in both the manuscript and the printed text. See the following report, 11574, and the commentary on it.], and a cluster of their grapes could be carried only by five persons on a pole [in the manuscript: "five breaths between them on a pole," and in the printed text: "five persons between them on a pole." I have set down what is in the Tafsir of al-Baghawi (margin of Ibn Kathir 3:104), as it is closer to this context. See what will come, the report number 11573.], and a pomegranate's half, when its seeds were removed, could be entered by five or four persons. The nuqaba' returned, each of them forbidding his tribe from fighting them, except Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalab ibn Yafinah, [in the printed text: "Wa-Kalib ibn Yufuna," and I have set down what is in the manuscript, which has it here undotted, but it will come in the manuscript under number 11666 as I have written it here. See what has passed, 5:272. In the History 1:222: "Kalub ibn Yufunah, and it was said: Kalab ibn Yufunah, the son-in-law of Musa." Part of this report will come abridged under number 11660.] who were urging the tribes to fight the tyrants and to struggle against them. They disobeyed these two and obeyed the others.

11574: Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar, except that he said: "from the Children of Israel, men," and he also said: "they would throw them down (yulqunahuma)." [In the printed text: "yulfifunaha," although in the manuscript as I have set it down it is clearly dotted. See the comment on the earlier report, p. 112, note 7, and the following report, 11660.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 12 (part 2 of 3):

11575 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Musa was commanded to lead the Children of Israel toward the Holy Land, and [God] said: "I have indeed written it for you as an abode, a dwelling place and a home, so go forth to it, and strive against whoever of the enemy is in it, for I will be your helper against them. And take from your people twelve leaders (nuqaba'), one leader from each tribe (sibt), who will be responsible for his people in fulfilling what they have been commanded. And say to them: God says to you: ﴿Indeed I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakat...﴾ to His words ﴿...then he has indeed strayed from the right way﴾." Musa took from them twelve leaders, whom he chose from the tribes as guarantors over their peoples for what they were undertaking, to fulfil His covenant and pact. And from each tribe he took its best and most trustworthy man. God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And God had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders.﴾ So Musa set out with them toward the Holy Land by God's command, until they alighted in the wilderness of al-Tih between Egypt and Syria, which is a land with no tree (khamar) and no shade [in the printed edition: "no tree and no shade"; in the manuscript: "ḥ‘r"; the correct reading is what has been recorded, as in the report already passed: 992. The khamar (with two fathas) is everything that covers you of trees, buildings or other things]. Musa called upon his Lord when the heat afflicted them, and He shaded them with clouds, and he prayed for their provision, and God sent down upon them manna and quails. [Up to this point it has already passed in an earlier report, number 992.] God commanded Musa, saying: "Send men to spy out (yatahassasun) the land of Canaan, which was given to the Children of Israel," one man from each tribe. So Musa sent all the chiefs among them, [and God, mighty and majestic, sent from the desert of Paran with the word of God, and they were the chiefs of the Children of Israel]. [This sentence between brackets is from the manuscript, and the printer of the edition omitted it. It is an unintelligible phrase, and I have not been able to determine its correct form, nor to connect the speech with what precedes and follows. What is in the people's book (the Old Testament), in the Book of Numbers, chapter 13, is: "So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the word of the LORD." Every possibility of corruption, distortion or deficiency in the wording I attempted to apply to this sentence so that it would be correct; there emerged a weakly constructed reading, so I left it to one who is able to set it right, or who can find its correct form from another source than the sources before me.] These are the names of the group whom God, mighty is His praise, sent from the Children of Israel to the land of Syria, as the people of the Torah mention, to scout it for the Children of Israel: from the tribe of Reuben: "Shamun ibn Zakwun" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Ra'uben: Shama‘ ibn Zakkur," as in al-Muhabbar. In the printed edition and Ibn Kathir: "ibn Rakun," and in al-Qurtubi: "Rakub." In the manuscript it is read as I have written it]. And from the tribe of Simeon: "Shafat ibn Hurri" [In the people's book: "...ibn Hawri." In al-Muhabbar: "Sharfut ibn Hawri," and in al-Qurtubi: "Shawqut ibn Hawri."]. And from the tribe of Judah: "Kalib ibn Yufanna" [In the people's book: "...ibn Yufunnah." In al-Muhabbar: "Kawlib..," and in al-Qurtubi: "Yawqana."]. And from the tribe of Atin: "Yajail ibn Yusuf" [In the people's book: "And from the tribe of Yassakar: Yajal ibn Yusuf." In the printed edition here was "And from the tribe of Kadh: Mikha'il ibn Yusuf," and I do not know where the printer of the edition got it. In Ibn Kathir: "And from the tribe of Atin: Mikha'il ibn Yusuf," and I did not find a tribe "Atin," but this is how it is written in the manuscript of the tafsir, as I have transcribed it, unpointed; and in it also "Muhamil," unpointed, and what I have recorded is the correct reading of it. As for al-Muhabbar, it is: "And from the tribe of Isakhar: Yughul ibn Yusuf," and in al-Qurtubi: "And from the tribe of al-Sahir: Yughul ibn Yusuf." This tribe is what al-Tabari mentioned from Muhammad ibn Ishaq earlier, number 2107: "Yashjar," which is "Yassakar." So there is no doubt that "Abin" in the manuscript of the tafsir is "Yashjar" or "Ashjar," but I have left it as it is in the manuscript.] And from the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Ephraim: "Yusha ibn Nun" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Ephraim: Hosea ibn Nun," but in the manuscript of the tafsir it is written "Yusha" here, and it would have been better to write "Hosea" here, because it will come at the end of the report that he was named "Hosea" on that day, "Yusha".] And from the tribe of Benjamin: "Falat ibn Rafun" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Benjamin: Palti ibn Rafu." In the manuscript: "ibn Dafun," in the printed edition: "ibn Dhunun," in Ibn Kathir: "Faltam ibn Dafun," in al-Muhabbar: "Yalta ibn Radfu," and in al-Qurtubi: "Yalza ibn Rawqu."] And from the tribe of Zebulun: "Jaddi ibn Sawdi" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Zebulun: Gaddi'el ibn Sudi," and in the manuscript "Jaddi ibn Sawshi," but Ibn Kathir transmitted it in his tafsir from al-Tabari: "Jaddi ibn Shawra," so it is clear that "Sawshi" is a distortion of "Sawdi." In the printed edition it was "Karabil ibn Sawdi," and in al-Muhabbar "Kadayil ibn Shawdhi," and in al-Qurtubi: "Karabil ibn Sawra."] And from the tribe of Manasseh, son of Joseph: "Jaddi ibn Sawsa" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh: Gaddi ibn Susi," and in Ibn Kathir: "ibn Musa," an error. In al-Muhabbar: "Kadi ibn Sawsi," and in al-Qurtubi and the printed edition: "Sawsha."] And from the tribe of Dan: "Hamla'il ibn Jamal" [In the people's book: "...‘Amina’il ibn Jamalli," and in Ibn Kathir: "Khamla'il ibn Hamal," and in al-Muhabbar: "‘Amayil ibn Kamla," and in al-Qurtubi: "‘Amail ibn Kasl."] And from the tribe of Asher: "Satur ibn Mulkil" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Asher: Setur ibn Mikha'il," and in the printed edition: "Asher: Sabur," so I have recorded what is in the manuscript, which is unpointed. In Ibn Kathir: "Asher: Satur ibn Mulkil." In al-Muhabbar: "And from the tribe of Ushir: Shatur ibn Mikha'il," "Shir: Satur."] And from the tribe of Naphtali: "Nahi ibn Wafsi" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Naphtali: Nahiyah ibn Wafsa," and in the printed edition: "Mahar ibn Waqsa," and in the manuscript: "And from the tribe of Thafatha, Abi Bahr ibn Wafsi," and the correct reading is what I have recorded. In Ibn Kathir: "Bahr ibn Waqsi." In al-Muhabbar: "Yahya ibn Waqsi," and in al-Qurtubi: "Yuhanna ibn Waqusha."] And from the tribe of Gad: "Jawalail ibn Miki" [In the people's book: "from the tribe of Gad: Ja'u'il ibn Maki," and in the manuscript: "And from the tribe of Dar: Jawla'il ibn Munkad," and in the printed edition: "And from the tribe of Yasakhar: Hawlayil ibn Munkad," and in Ibn Kathir's tafsir: "And from the tribe of Yasakhar: Layil ibn Makid," and in al-Muhabbar: "And from the tribe of Jadh: Kawa'il ibn Mukha," and in al-Qurtubi: "And from the tribe of Kadh: Kawal ibn Mukha." I have therefore written "Jad" in place of "Dar" in the manuscript, from the names of the tribes in Ibn Ishaq's transmission in the report already passed, number 2107. And I have read "Munkad" and "Miki" because they are closer to "Maki" and "Mukha."]

Moreover, Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 3:103 cited the names of these leaders, and said: "I have seen in the fourth book of the Torah an enumeration of the leaders over the tribes of the Children of Israel, and names different from what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, and God knows best." But it became clear upon review that what Ibn Ishaq mentioned is what is found in the copy of the Torah that is before us. As for what Ibn Kathir transmitted, it is completely different from what is in Ibn Ishaq's report and from what came in the people's book. There is no doubt that the Torah that was in Ibn Kathir's hand is other than the one we have of the people's book.]

= So these are the names of those whom Musa sent to spy out the land for him (=) [In the printed edition: "yatajassasun" with a jim; see what has passed on p. 111, note 1, and p. 114, note 3.] And on that day he named "Hosea ibn Nun": "Yusha ibn Nun" [In the printed edition and the manuscript, this first name is "Yusha," but the manuscript is unpointed, and the correct form is "Hosea," as I have recorded it. See p. 115, note 2.] = Then he sent them and said to them: "Go up toward the sun, leave the mountain, and see what is in the land, and what people dwell in it: are they strong or weak, few or many? And look at their land in which they dwell: is it fat or lean? Does it have trees or not? Go through, and bring back to us some fruit of that land." And that was at the time when the first grapes ripen (ashjana bakr thamarat al-‘inab). [In the printed edition: "...Is it fertile or has trees; bring us fruit of that land," the editor judged what is in the manuscript unreadable and omitted it. In the manuscript it was: "Asmaseh hiya am dhat shajar am la ihbaru wa-hmilu ilaina..." I saw that it should be read in this way, as support from what came in the people's book, in the Book of Numbers, chapter 13: "And what is the land like: is it fat or lean? Is there wood in it or not? And be strong and take some fruit of the land."

It is said: "a fat land" — of good soil, few stones, strong in producing plants. And it is said: "a lean land," thin. And "al-mahazil" are the barren places; therefore I preferred to put "hazilah" (lean) as it came in the people's book with this meaning, even though the lexicons omitted it or the text did not specify it.

In the printed edition it was: "And that was at the beginning of what was named for them of that, the fruit of the grape," which is a poor and objectionable alteration. The manuscript reads: "And that was at the first of what was named (summa) the first-fruit of the grape," but the copyist did not read "sumn" well, and altered it without care. What is in the people's book reads: "As for the days, they were the days of the first-fruits of the grapes." So I deduced from it the correct reading of the manuscript and read: "awwal ma ashjana bakr thamarat al-‘inab" ("when the first grapes ripened").

And "al-shajanah" (with a kasrah and a sukun) is a branch of a grape cluster that ripens entirely. It is said of it: "ashjana al-karm" — its clusters ripened and became good.

As for his saying "bakr al-‘inab" — "bakr" of everything is its beginning. This is correct in Arabic, although they have specified the fruits that ripen first with the phrase "bakurat al-thamarah" (first-ripened fruit).]

11576 - Muhammad ibn Sa‘d related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ‘Abbas, regarding his words: ﴿And We raised among them twelve leaders﴾ — they were from the Children of Israel, whom Musa sent to scout the city for him. They set out and looked at the city, and they came back with a single grape from their fruit, a load for a man [al-waqr (with a kasrah on the waw and a sukun on the qaf) is a load. In the hadith of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and the Magians: "They threw down the load of a mule or two mules," meaning the load of one mule or two mules]. They said: "Estimate the strength and might of this people from this fruit of theirs!" At that, they were tested, and they said: "We are not able to fight," ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting here﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 24].

11577 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj al-Marwazi, who said: I heard Abu Mu‘adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid saying, concerning His words: ﴿And We raised among them twelve leaders﴾: God commanded the Children of Israel to proceed to the Holy Land with their prophet Musa, peace be upon him. When they were near the city, Musa said to them: "Enter it!" But they refused and were cowardly, and they sent twelve leaders to look at them. They set out and looked, and came back with a single grape from their fruit, a load for a man. They said: "Estimate the strength and might of this people [in the printed edition in both places: 'qadaru'; the good reading is from the manuscript] — this is their fruit!!" At that they said to Musa: ﴿Go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting here﴾.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And God said: Indeed I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend God a goodly loan...﴾

Abu Ja‘far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed I am with you" — that is, I am your helper against your enemy and My enemy, whom I commanded you to fight [see the explanation of "ma‘a" (with) in what has passed: 3:213–214 / 5:353], if you fight them and fulfil My covenant and pact that I took from you.

* *

In the speech there is an omitted element, which the revealed speech has made unnecessary to mention. The meaning of the speech is: "God said to them: Indeed I am with you" — so "to them" was dropped, relying on His words: "And God had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel," since the preceding report concerned a people identified by name, so it was known that what follows in the speech concerning them is about them, since the discourse was not turned away from them to others.

* *

Then our Lord, mighty is His praise, began the oath, saying: an oath: "If you establish, O company of the Children of Israel, the prayer" — "and give zakat," that is, you give it to those whom I commanded to give it — "and believe in My messengers," that is: you confirm what My messengers brought you of the laws of My religion.

Al-Rabi‘ ibn Anas used to say: This is an address from God to the twelve leaders.

11578 - It was related to me from ‘Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja‘far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi‘ ibn Anas: that Musa, peace be upon him, said to the twelve leaders: "Go to them" — meaning the giants (al-jabbarin) — "and tell me their story and their affair, and do not fear, for God is with you if you establish prayer, give zakat, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend God a goodly loan."

* *

Abu Ja‘far said: What al-Rabi‘ said on this matter is not far from the truth; however, among God's decrees over all His creation is that He is the helper of whoever obeys Him, and the protector of whoever follows His command, avoids His disobedience, and shuns His sins [in the printed edition: "wa-jafa dhunubahu" (and he deserted his sins); in the manuscript: "wa-‘amma dhunubahu" (and he disregarded his sins); I saw fit to read it as "tahamma" (and he shunned), for it is in my judgment better and clearer in the meaning of guarding against sins and keeping away from them]. Since this is so, and since obedience to Him includes establishing prayer, giving zakat, belief in the messengers, and all that He urged the people to, it was known that the expiation of misdeeds through that and admission into the gardens is by it, and He did not restrict it to the twelve leaders, excluding the rest of the Children of Israel. So it is more fitting and more appropriate that it be an exhortation to all the people and an encouragement to them in what He encouraged them to, than that it be an exhortation to some and an encouragement to a particular group rather than the general public.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿and you honour them (wa-‘azzartumuhum)﴾.

Some of them said: its interpretation is: "and you help them."

Those who said that:

11579 - Muhammad ibn ‘Amr related to me, saying: Abu ‘Asim related to us, saying: ‘Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words: ﴿and you honour them﴾, he said: "you help them."

11580 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

11581 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi concerning His words: ﴿and you honour them﴾, he said: "you help them with the sword."

* *

Others said: it is obedience and help.

Those who said that:

11582 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd saying concerning His words: ﴿and you honour them﴾: "al-ta‘ziz" and "al-tawqir" — obedience and help.

* *

The grammarians differed in its interpretation.

It is reported from Yunus [al-Harmari] that he used to say its interpretation is: "you praised them." [The words "Yunus [al-Harmari]" are thus in the manuscript and the printed edition, and they are problematic. For either it is a nisba (attributive name) to which he was attributed, and the nisba of Yunus ibn Habib is "the grammarian," and his affiliation by clientage is "al-Dabbi," being a client of "Bilal ibn Harmi of the Banu Dabi‘ah ibn Bajalah" (al-Naqa’ih: 323), and I do not think it is distorted from any of these; or it is a nisba to a place, and Yunus was from the people of Jabal (with a fatha on the jim and a doubled ba' with a damma) (see Tabaqat al-Nahwiyyin of al-Zubaydi: 48). Nor is it a distortion of this either. Perhaps a researcher will find its correct form, so I left it as it is. This, with the fact that Abu ‘Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an mentioned only his name, and al-Tabari transmits this from Abu ‘Ubaydah.]

11583 - I was told this from Abu ‘Ubaydah Ma‘mar ibn al-Muthanna, from him [see Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu ‘Ubaydah 1:157].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 12 (part 3 of 3):

* *
Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: the meaning of that is "you helped them, aided them, honored them, revered them, and strengthened them," and he recited in support of this (the poet unknown): [[I do not know who said it.]]
"How many a noble, generous man belongs to them, and how many a lion who is honored in the assembly (al-nadi)?" [[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:157. "Al-nadi" means the gathering of the people, for as long as they are gathered in it; when they disperse from it, it is no longer a nadi. Similar is "al-nadi" (the assembly).
And among the strangest of strange things is the explanation of one who explained this line by saying: "'Allahum', with a kasra on the lam and a sukun on the ha', is the old bull... perhaps the word is a corruption of the word shahm." This is a confusion beyond compare, so avoid the like of it.]] Al-Farra' used to say: "al-'azr" is repelling. "'Azartuhu" means I repelled him: when you see someone oppressing and you say to him, "Fear God," or you forbid him, that is "al-'azr."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The view I hold most correct among these opinions is the view of the one who said: "The meaning of that is: you helped them." This is because God, may His praise be mighty, said in "Surat al-Fath": ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner, that you may believe in God and His Messenger, and support him and honor him﴾ [Surat al-Fath: 8, 9]. So "tawqir" is glorification. Since that is so, the statement on this matter is only some of what we have mentioned from the opinions we have related from those from whom we related them. And if it is invalid that its meaning is glorification, and support may be by hand and by tongue, and support by hand is defending him with the sword and other things, and support by tongue is good praise and defending his honor, then it is correct that it is support, since support encompasses the meaning of every speaker who said something about it from what we have related.
* *
As for His saying: "and lend God a goodly loan," He means: and spend in the way of God, and that is in fighting His enemy and your enemy. "A goodly loan" means: and spend what you spend in His way, so that you are right in your spending what you spend in that, and you do not transgress in it the limits of God and what He urged you to and exhorted you to, toward something other than it. [[See the explanation of "al-qard" and "al-qard al-hasan" in what has preceded, 5:282, 283. His saying "toward something other than it" is connected to his saying "and you did not transgress in it..."]]
* *
If someone says to us: How did He say "and lend God a goodly loan" and not "iqrad hasan," when you know that the verbal noun of "aqrradtu" is "al-iqrad"?
It is said: If that were said, it would be correct, but His saying "qardan hasanan" brought a verbal noun from its meaning, not from its wording. This is because in His saying "aqrada" there is the meaning of "qarada," just as in "a'ta" there is the meaning of "akhadha." So the meaning of the speech is: "and you lent God a goodly loan." A parallel to this is: ﴿And God has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾ [Surat Nuh: 17], since "anbatakum" carries the meaning of "fa-nabattum" (so you grew). And as Imru' al-Qays said:
"I tamed her, and she submitted to a difficult humbling!" [[His Diwan: 141, and others. Before the line, he says to his companion after he rose toward her like the rising of a water bubble: I swore to her by God an oath of a sinner that they slept, and there was neither talk nor one who stayed awake... Then when we disputed the talk and she yielded, she bent toward a branch with clusters, leaning... And we came to the pleasant part, and our talk grew soft, and I tamed her, and she submitted, a difficult humbling!! "Raada al-dabbah aw ghayriha yarudduha": he trod it, tamed it, and taught it to walk.]]
Since "radtu" carries the meaning of "adhlaltu" (I humbled), "al-idhlal" came as a verbal noun from its meaning, not from its wording. [[See what has preceded, 5:533, 534. This has been mentioned in 5:282, 283, "yuqridu Allah qardan hasanan," but the discussion there was not completed. This is one of the sections where Abu Ja'far abridged his tafsir.]]
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may His mention be mighty: ﴿Surely I will expiate from you your misdeeds and surely I will admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may His praise be mighty, means the Children of Israel. He, may His praise be mighty, says to them: If you establish the prayer, O people who gave Me your covenant to fulfill obedience to Me and follow My command, and you give the zakat, and you do all else I promised you for My Paradise, "surely I will expiate from you your misdeeds," meaning: I will cover with My pardon for you and My forgiveness of your punishment, for your past sins which you committed between Me and you, [[The construction of the sentence: "I will cover with My pardon for you... your sins..."]] for your sins which preceded from you, such as the worship of the calf and other grave sins. [[See the explanation of "al-takfir" and "al-sayyi'at" in what has preceded in the language indexes, root (k-f-r) and (s-w-').]]
"And surely I will admit you," while covering that from you with My favor on the Day of Resurrection, "into gardens beneath which rivers flow."
* *
So "al-jannat" means the orchards. [[See the explanation of "al-jannat" in what has preceded in the language indexes, root (j-n-n).]]
* *
I only said that the meaning of His saying "la-ukaffiranna" is la-ughattiyanna (I will cover), because "kufr" means denial, covering, and concealment, as Labid said:
"In a night whose clouds concealed the stars" [[Its full line and its takhrij were preceded in 1:255.]]
meaning: "covered them." So "al-takfir" is the "taf'il" form from "al-kafr."
* *
The people of Arabic grammar differed regarding the meaning of the "lam" in His saying "la-ukaffiranna."
Some grammarians of Basra said: The first "lam" is for the meaning of an oath, meaning the "lam" in His saying "la-in aqamtum al-salat." He said: the second is the meaning of another oath.
* *
Some grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, the first "lam" took the place of the oath, so it sufficed for the oath. He means by "the first lam": "la-in aqamtum al-salat." He said: the second "lam," meaning His saying "la-ukaffiranna 'ankum sayyi'atikum," is the answer to it, meaning the "lam" in His saying "la-in aqamtum al-salat." He argued for his statement that "la-in aqamtum al-salat" is not complete and is not independent of His saying "la-ukaffiranna 'ankum sayyi'atikum." Since that is so, it is not permissible that His saying "la-ukaffiranna 'ankum sayyi'atikum" be a fresh oath; rather it must be the answer to the oath, since the oath is not independent of it.
* *
His saying: ﴿And rivers flow beneath them﴾ means: rivers flow beneath the trees of these orchards which He admitted you into.
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may His mention be mighty: ﴿So whoever disbelieves after that among you has certainly strayed from the right way﴾ (12)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His mention be mighty, says: Whoever among you, O company of the Children of Israel, denies any of what I commanded you and abandons it, or commits what I forbade you and does it after My taking your covenant to fulfill obedience to Me and avoid disobedience to Me, "then he has certainly strayed from the right way," meaning: he has missed the aim of the clear path and has deviated from the course of the straight way.
* *
"Al-dalal" is riding without guidance, and we have explained that with its evidences in other than this place. [[See the explanation of "al-dalal" in what has preceded, 2:495, 496; 6:66, 584, and other places; seek them in the language indexes.]]
* *
His saying "sawa'" means: the middle; and "al-sabil" is the road.
* *
We have explained the interpretation of all of that in other than this place, so it suffices from repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "sawa' al-sabil" in what has preceded, 2:496, 497, and the language indexes under (s-w-y) and (s-b-l).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 13 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿So for their breaking their covenant We cursed them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, do not be amazed at these Jews who intended to stretch out their hands toward you and your companions, and who broke the covenant between you and them, treacherously, against you and your companions. For that is among their habits and the habits of their predecessors. Among that: I took the covenant of their predecessors, at the time of Moses (ﷺ), to obey Me, and I sent from among them twelve chieftains, chosen from all of them, to spy out the news of the tyrants, and I promised them victory over them, and that I would make them inherit their land, their homes and their wealth, after I had shown them the signs and proofs (such as the destruction of Pharaoh and his people in the sea, the splitting of the sea for them, and the rest of the proofs) that I had shown them, [[The context: "after I had shown them the proofs and signs... that I had shown them," and what lies between the two lines is an explanatory insertion.]] so they broke the covenant they had pledged to Me and violated My agreement, so I cursed them for breaking their covenant. Since this was the deed of their best men, despite My favours upon them, do not be surprised at the like of it from their worst men.
* *
There is an omission in the speech, which is indicated by the apparent meaning, and the sense of the speech is: "Whoever among you disbelieves after that has indeed strayed from the right path." They broke the covenant, so We cursed them: "So for their breaking their covenant We cursed them." He suffices with His saying "So for their breaking their covenant" in place of the mention of "they broke." [[See the explanation of "the breaking" (al-naqd) above, vol. 9, p. 363.]]
* *
His saying, exalted is His remembrance, "So for their breaking their covenant," means: by their breaking their covenant, as Qatadah said.
11584 - Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "So for their breaking their covenant We cursed them," he says: by their breaking their covenant We cursed them. [[Report 11584: in the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Kathir told us, saying: Yazid told us," which is an error; it is a circular chain (isnad dā'ir) appearing in the tafsir.]]
11585 - al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "So for their breaking their covenant" — it is the covenant that God took from the people of the Torah, and they broke it.
* *
We have mentioned the meaning of "cursing" (al-la'n) in another place. [[See the explanation of "cursing" above, vol. 9, p. 213, note 3, and the references there.]]
* *
The "ha' and mim" in His saying "So for their breaking" refer back to the mention of the Children of Israel before.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾
Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.
The majority of the readers of Madinah, some of the people of Makkah, Basrah and Kufah recited it: ﴿qasiyah﴾ with an alif,
* *
according to the pattern of "fa'ilah" from "the hardness of the heart," from the saying of the speaker: "his heart became hard (qasa), so he is hardening (yaqsu) and he is hard (qasin)," and that is when it becomes harsh and firm and dry and solid, as the rajaz poet said: "I have grown hard, and my contemporaries have grown hard." [[Its takhrij was mentioned above, vol. 2, p. 233; see also Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 158.]]
* *
So the interpretation of the speech according to this reading: We cursed those of the Children of Israel who broke My covenant and did not fulfil My agreement, by their breaking the covenant they had pledged to Me, "and We made their hearts hard," harsh and dry from faith in Me and success in obeying Me, stripped of compassion and mercy.
* *
And the majority of the readers of Kufah recited it: ﴿qasiyyah﴾ .
* *
Then those who recited it thus differed about its interpretation.
Some of them said: the meaning of that is the meaning of "hardness," because "fa'iilah" is more emphatic in dispraise than "fa'ilah," so we chose the reading "qasiyah" over "qasiyah" for that reason.
* *
Others among them said: rather, the meaning of "qasiyyah" is other than the meaning of "hardness," and "al-qasiyyah" in this place means: hearts whose faith in God is not pure, but whose faith is mixed with disbelief, like the "qasiyyah" dirhams, whose silver is mixed with an adulterant of copper or lead or other things, as Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:
"Its neighings in the deaf rocks are like the cries of the qasiyyat in the hands of the money-changers." [[Al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 1024, 1025; Amali al-Qali 1: 28; Simt al-La'ali: 128, 931; al-Lisan (amara, sahala). From his elegy on the wrongfully slain Commander of the Faithful, Dhu al-Nurayn 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, in which he says: "Alas for my soul, if what they claim is true... and what today would return my lament!! If 'Uthman has come to rest beneath a stone, like the watcher of the wild asses above the high mound..." (The poem continues with descriptions of the digging of the grave, the spades, and the rocks, which the commentator explains, including that "al-salam" means the rocks.)]] He describes by that the sound of the spades of those who dug the grave of 'Uthman upon the rocks, which are "al-silam."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two readings to me is the reading of the one who recites "And We made their hearts qasiyyah" in the pattern of "fa'iilah," because it is more emphatic in dispraise of the people than "qasiyah." And the more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who interprets it as "fa'iilah" from "hardness," as one says "a pure soul" (nafs zakiyyah) and "a purifying one" (zakiyah), and "a witnessing woman" (imra'ah shahidah) and "a witnessing one" (shahidah), because God, exalted is His praise, described the people by their breaking their covenant and their disbelief in Him, and did not describe them with anything of faith, so that their hearts would be described as having faith mixed with disbelief, like the qasiyyah dirhams whose silver is mixed with an adulterant.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾
Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We made the hearts of these people who broke Our covenants from the Children of Israel qasiyyah, stripped of good, with success lifted from them, so they do not believe and are not guided. Because God, exalted and majestic, removed success and faith from their hearts, they distort the speech of their Lord which He revealed to their prophet Moses (ﷺ), namely the Torah, changing it, and they write with their hands other than what God, mighty and majestic, revealed to their prophet, then they say to the ignorant people: [[In the printed text: "wa-yaqulun," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] "This is the speech of God that He revealed to His prophet Moses (ﷺ), and the Torah that He inspired to him." [[See the explanation of "distorting words from their places" above, vol. 2, p. 248 / vol. 8, pp. 430-432.]] This is from the description of the generations that came after Moses among the Jews, some of whom reached the time of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). But God, exalted is His remembrance, included them in the number of those whose report He began concerning those of them who met Moses, since they were of their sons and on their path in lying against God, slandering Him, and breaking the covenants that He took from them in the Torah, as:
11586 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "They distort the words from their places," he means: the limits of God in the Torah. And they say: "If Muhammad commands you with what you are upon, accept it; and if he opposes you, beware."
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of﴾
He, exalted is His remembrance, means by His saying "and they forgot a portion" and abandoned a share, like His saying: ﴿They forgot God, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 67], i.e., they abandoned God's command, so God abandoned them. [[See the explanation of "forgetting" above, vol. 2, pp. 9, 476; vol. 5, p. 164; vol. 6, pp. 133-135.]]
* *
The explanation of that with its evidences has passed in another place, so repeating it is unnecessary. [[See the earlier note, and the explanation of "portion" (hazz) in the language indices above.]]
* *
According to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have spoken.
Those who said that:
11587 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of," he says: they abandoned a share.
11588 - al-Harith told me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, saying: Mubarak ibn Fudalah told us, from al-Hasan concerning His saying: "And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of," he said: they abandoned the handholds of their religion and the obligations of God, mighty is His praise, without which deeds are not accepted. [["Al-wazha'if" is the plural of "wazifah," which is of everything what is allotted to it each day of provision, food, fodder or drink. Then they said: "he assigned the thing upon himself," i.e., imposed it upon it, and they said: "upon him is each day a wazifah of work," i.e., what is imposed upon him as work on this day. By al-Hasan's words "the obligations of God," he meant His duties that He imposed upon His servants in faith in Him, obedience to Him, and sincerity of intention toward Him, glory to Him. This is a term that should be noted in the lexicons, from the speech of al-Hasan, may God be pleased with him.]]
..............................................
................................................ [[These dots indicate a lacuna or gap in the copies made by the scribe of the manuscript. He wrote at the beginning of the explanation of this part of the verse: "And they forgot a portion," then continued Abu Ja'far's speech to the end of the report numbered 11588.
Then he began thereafter thus: "The interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: 'of what they were reminded of'" — then he went on to explain the next part of the verse, which is: "And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them." That part of the verse was not written, though its explanation was. It is evident from this that the scribe forgot the explanation of "of what they were reminded of," and it fell out. He also did not mention the verse whose explanation is Abu Ja'far's speech.
Moreover, see the meaning of "reminding" above, vol. 5, p. 580; vol. 6, pp. 62-65, 211.]]
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them﴾
Abu Ja'far said: Blessed and exalted is He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And you will not cease, O Muhammad, to discover from the Jews, whose report I have told you, of their breaking My covenant and violating My agreement, despite My favours upon them and My blessing upon them, the like of that treachery and deceit, "except a few of them," except a few of them [did not betray]. [[In the printed text, it stops at "except a few of them" and drops "except a few of them who did not betray." In the manuscript, the scribe dropped "did not betray" and wrote "except a few of them, except a few of them." I have restored "did not betray" and placed it in brackets, from its later statement that it is an exception from the "ha' and mim" in "treachery from them."]]
* *
"Al-khā'inah" in this place means: the treachery; it is placed in the position of the verbal noun, as one says "khati'ah" for "khati'ah" (sin), and "qa'ilah" for "qaylulah" (midday rest). [[In the printed text: "khati'ah, for al-khati'un," which seems to have been considered odd; in Abu Ja'far's commentary (vol. 29, p. 33, Bulaq edition) on His saying "and the overturned cities with the sin," he said: "with the sin, meaning with the sin." Abu Ja'far wrote it thus, as you see, although I do not like this example. I would rather he said it is a verbal noun that came on the pattern "fa'ilah," like "al-'afiyah." Unless Abu Ja'far meant that "khati'ah" is a verbal noun on "fa'iilah," like "al-shabibah" and "al-fadihah" and similar, which is rare.]]
* *
His saying "except a few of them" is an exception from the "ha' and mim" in His saying "over a treachery from them."
* *
According to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have spoken.
Those who said that:
11589 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "And you will not cease to discover treachery from them," he said: over treachery, lying and wickedness.
11590 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning the saying of God, mighty and majestic: "And you will not cease to discover treachery from them," he said: they are Jews like what they intended against the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day he entered their enclosure.
11591 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.
11592 - al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said concerning His saying: "And you will not cease to discover treachery from them": from the Jews, like what they intended against the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day he came to them.
* *
Some of those who speak said: [[How greatly Abu Ja'far disapproves of the sayings of Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, to the point of mentioning him anonymously in various ways! And this that follows is the exact text of Abu 'Ubaydah's words in Majaz al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 158.]] The meaning of that is: "And you will not cease to discover a treacherous one from them," he said: the Arabs add a "ha'" at the end of the masculine, as in their saying "he is a transmitter (rawiyah) of poetry" and "a man who is a scholar ('allamah)," and he recited: [[He is a man from the Sawaqit, of the Banu Abi Bakr ibn Kilab. The "Sawaqit" are those who approach al-Yamamah to trade dates.]]
"You told yourself of loyalty, but you were not
A treacherous one for deceit, with a hand that is seized."
[[Al-Kamil of al-Mubarrad 1: 211; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 158; Islah al-Mantiq: 295; al-Lisan (sabi', ghall, khawn). This is from a poem of his with a story: when this poet came to al-Yamamah he had with him a handsome brother, and he stayed as a protected neighbour of 'Umayr ibn Salma. Qarin, the brother of 'Umayr, said to the Kilabi: "Do not bring your brother to our tents," fearing for his beauty. Qarin saw him between their tents later, while his brother 'Umayr was absent, and killed him. The Kilabi came to the grave of Salma (father of 'Umayr and Qarin) and sought protection there, saying: "If you seek protection from al-Yamamah, seek it from Zayd ibn Yarbu' and the family of Mujammi'..." (The verses continue, describing the events.) Then Qarin fled to the notables of Banu Hanifah (namely Zayd ibn Yarbu' and the family of Mujammi'), and they brought the Kilabi double blood-money, but he refused to accept it. When 'Umayr arrived, his mother said to him: "Do not kill your brother, and send to the Kilabi all of your wealth," but the Kilabi refused to accept. So 'Umayr took his brother Qarin and killed him, and said: "We killed our brother to keep faith with our neighbour, and our father's graves were once protected..." His mother said to 'Umayr: "You count excuses, there is no excuse in them, and whoever kills his brother has done a shameful thing." And his saying "akhu al-zamanah" means the affliction, meaning his weakness in exacting his revenge. "'Umayyatan" and "Dal'a" are places in the land of this Kilabi. His saying "maghul al-isba'" is a metaphor for treachery and theft; "aghalla yaghullu" means to betray a trust stealthily. Some say "maghul al-isba'" is in the accusative as a vocative.]] He said "khā'inah" and he was addressing a man.
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct interpretation of this matter is the view we have related from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil). This is because God, may He be exalted, meant by this verse the people of the Jews of Banu al-Nadir who intended to kill the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to them seeking their help regarding the blood-money of the two men from Banu 'Amir. God, may His remembrance be exalted, then informed him of what they had intended. Then He, may His praise be great, after making known to him the reports of their forebears and informing him of the course of their predecessors, and that the last of them follows the path of the first in treachery and deceit, lest their act weigh heavily upon the Prophet of God (ﷺ), said, may His praise be great: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them, except a few of them﴾... meaning, He did not intend that he would not cease to discover a single treacherous man among them. This is because the report began concerning their group, as it was said: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people determined to extend their hands toward you﴾, and then it was said: ﴿And you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾. Since the beginning was about the group, concluding with the group is more appropriate. [[In the printed edition: "فلتختم بالجماعة أولى" (then let it conclude with the group, more appropriate), and I do not know why it alters the correct reading!]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good﴾ (13)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to pardon these people among the Jews who intended to extend their hands toward him. God, may He be mighty and majestic, says to him: Pardon, O Muhammad, these Jews for what they intended of extending their hands toward you and your Companions with killing, and overlook their crime by abandoning the pursuit of what they dislike, for I love one who excels in pardon and forgiveness toward one who has wronged him.
