[[See the explanation of "al-'afw" in the preceding indices of language = and the explanation of "al-safh" above, 2:503 = and the explanation of "al-muhsinin" in the indices of language above.]]

* *

Qatadah used to say: this is abrogated (mansukhah). He said: it was abrogated by the verse of Bara'ah: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day...﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 29], and so on.

11593 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "So pardon them and overlook," he said: It was abrogated by: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful﴾.

11594 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah: "So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good." He was not commanded at that time to fight them, so God, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded him to pardon them and overlook. Then that was abrogated in Bara'ah, when He said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful, and do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 29]. They are the People of the Book, so God, may His praise be great, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to fight them until they submit or agree to pay the jizyah.

11595 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I read to Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, something similar.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Qatadah said is not impossible, but the abrogating command beyond doubt is that which negates all meanings of what preceded it. As for what does not negate all of it, there is no way to know it is abrogating except by a report from God, may He be mighty and majestic, or from His Messenger (ﷺ). There is nothing in His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ that indicates a command to negate the meanings of forbearance and pardon toward the Jews.

Since that is so, and since it was permissible, along with their acknowledgment of subjugation and their payment of the jizyah after fighting, to command pardon toward them for a treachery they intended or a breach they resolved upon, so long as they do not take up war apart from paying the jizyah and refuse the obligatory rulings upon them, it was not necessary to judge that His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day...﴾ abrogates His saying: "So pardon them and overlook. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good."

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And from those who said, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of.﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We took from the Christians a covenant to obey Me, to perform My obligations, to follow My messengers and to believe in them. But they pursued, in the covenant I had taken from them, the course of the misguided nation of the Jews. Thus they altered their religion as those did, and they broke it as those broke theirs, [[In the printed edition: "ونقضوا" (they broke). I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] and they abandoned their portion of My covenant that I had taken from them, to fulfil My pledge, and they neglected My command." [[See the discussion of "taking the covenant" (akhdh al-mithaq) above, p. 110, note 1, and the references there. And the discussion of "forgetting" (al-nisyan) and "portion" (al-hazz) above, p. 129, notes 3, 4, and the references there. And the discussion of "reminding" (al-tadhkir) above, p. 130, note 2, and the references there.]]

As related:

11596. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And from those who said, "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of﴾: "They forgot the Book of God among them, and the covenant God had made with them, and the command God had given them."

11597. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who said: "The Christians said the same as the Jews said, and they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of."

* *

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "So We stirred up among them," He means: We incited and cast [enmity] among them, just as one sets one thing against another.

He, may His praise be exalted, says: When these Christians, whose covenant I had taken to fulfil My pledge, abandoned their portion of what I had enjoined upon them of My command and My prohibition, I stirred up enmity and hatred among them.

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the manner of God's stirring up enmity and hatred among them.

Some of them said: His stirring them up was through the divergent desires (ahwa') that arose among them.

Those who said this:

11598. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, regarding His words "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred," he said: "These are the differing desires and mutual hatred, and that is the stirring up."

11599. Sufyan ibn WakI' told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, who said: I heard al-Nakha'i say: "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred": "He stirred some of them against others through disputes, through argument over religion."

11600. al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told me, saying: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Taymi, regarding His words "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred," he said: "I do not see the 'stirring up' in this verse as anything other than differing desires." And Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: "Disputes over religion nullify deeds."

* *

Others said: Rather, that is the enmity that exists among them and the hatred.

Those who said this:

11601. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection," the verse: "When this people abandoned the Book of God, disobeyed His messengers, neglected His obligations, and rendered His limits void, He cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection, through their deeds, evil deeds. Had the people taken up the Book of God and His command, they would not have separated nor hated one another."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations in my view is the interpretation of the one who said: "He stirred among them through the desires that arose among them," as Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said, because the enmity among the Christians is only due to their disagreement about what they say concerning the Messiah, and that is desires, not revelation from God.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by the "ha' and mim" (the pronoun "them") in His words "So We stirred up among them."

Some said: It refers to the Jews and the Christians. The meaning of the speech according to their view and interpretation is: "So We stirred up enmity between the Jews and the Christians, because they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of."

Those who said this:

11602. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who also said regarding the Christians: "But they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of." So when they did that, God, may He be exalted, stirred up enmity and hatred between them and the Jews until the Day of Resurrection.

11603. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection": "They are the Jews and the Christians." Ibn Zayd said: "Like when you incite two animals against each other."

11604. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of God "So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred": "The Jews and the Christians."

11605. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

11606. al-Qasim told me, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Abu Sufyan told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "They are the Jews and the Christians; God stirred up enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection."

* *

Others said: Rather, God meant by this the Christians alone. They said: The meaning is: "So We stirred up enmity among the Christians, as a punishment for their forgetting a portion of what they had been reminded of." They said: The "ha' and mim" in "among them" refers back to the Christians alone, not the Jews.

Those who said this:

11607. al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far." The correct form is "'Abd Allah," as I have written it. He is "'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi," who has occurred hundreds of times in the preceding chains.]] from his father, from al-Rabi': "God, may His remembrance be exalted, had enjoined upon the Children of Israel: 'Do not exchange My signs for a small price, and teach the wisdom, and do not take a wage for it.' Only a few of them complied. They took bribes in judgment and transgressed the limits. So He said regarding the Jews, when they judged by other than what God had commanded: ﴿And We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 64]. And He said regarding the Christians: 'But they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of, so We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.'"

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations of the verse in my view is what al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: that what is meant by the stirring up among them is the Christians, specifically in this verse. And the "ha' and mim" refer to the Christians alone, not the Jews. This is because the mention of the "stirring up" in God's report about the Christians comes after the conclusion of His report about the Jews, and after His beginning His report about the Christians. So for it to refer to the Christians alone is more appropriate than for it to refer to both groups, for the reason we have mentioned. [[In the printed edition: "فأن لا يكون ذلك معنيا به إلا النصارى خاصة" (that it not be meant except for the Christians alone), which is a statement free of Arabic sense. In the manuscript: "فلا يكون ذلك معنيا به إلا النصارى خاصة," which is similar, but a slip by the copyist, who wrote "فلأن يكون" and "فلا يكون" and then added "إلا". All of this is corrupt; the correct reading is what I have adopted.]]

* *

If someone says: What is the enmity that exists among the Christians, such that the meaning is specific to it? It is said: That is the enmity of the Nestorians toward the Jacobites and the Melkites, and the Melkites toward the Nestorians and the Jacobites. [[In the printed edition: "ذلك عداوة النسطورية واليعقوبية والملكية النسطورية واليعقوبية," which is devoid of meaning. The correct reading is from the manuscript: meaning the enmity of these toward those, and of those toward these.]] What the one who said, "It means: God's stirring up between the Jews and the Christians," said is not far off, but this is closer in my view and more fitting to the interpretation of the verse, for the reason we have mentioned.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And God will soon inform them of what they used to do﴾ (14)**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Pardon these people who intended to stretch out their hands against you and your companions, and overlook it. For God, the Mighty and Majestic, is beyond taking vengeance upon them, and God will inform them, when they are brought before Him in their return, of what they used to do in the world: their breaking of His covenant, their violation of His pledge, their alteration of His Book, and their distortion of His command and prohibition. Then He will punish them for that according to what they deserve."

* *

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the Book and pardoning much﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to a group of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, who were in the era of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "O People of the Book," the Jews and the Christians, "Our Messenger has come to you," meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), as:

11608. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding "O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you": "It is Muhammad (ﷺ)."

* *

As for His words "making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the Book," He says: Muhammad, Our Messenger, makes clear to you much of what you used to conceal from people and did not make clear to them of what is in your Book. Among what they used to hide of their Book, which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made clear to the people, was the stoning of the married adulterers.

* *

It has been said: This verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) making that clear to the people, from their concealing it from their Book.

Those who said this:

11609. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever denies stoning has denied the Qur'an without realizing it." Regarding His words "O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you much of what you used to hide of the Book," the stoning was among what they concealed. [[Report 11609: Yahya ibn Wadih is Abu Tumaylah, who has occurred many times, including at no. 392. Al-Husayn ibn Waqid al-Marwazi is trustworthy (thiqah), occurring at nos. 481 and 6311. Yazid al-Nahwi is Yazid ibn Abi Sa'id al-Nahwi al-Marwazi, trustworthy, occurring at no. 6311. This is a sound chain, and its takhrij will come in the following report.]]

11610. 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabbawayh told us, informing us: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Yazid told us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same. [[Report 11610: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabbawayh al-Khuza'i is trustworthy, occurring at nos. 1909, 4612, 4923. 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq ibn Dinar is trustworthy, one of Ahmad's teachers, occurring at nos. 1591, 1909, 9951. In the manuscript and printed edition here it reads "'Ali ibn al-Husayn," which is a plain error. This is also a sound chain, a repetition of the previous one. This report was recorded by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 4: 359 through the route of 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, with the same wording, and he said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 269, adding attribution to Ibn al-Durays, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Note: see the hadiths on stoning below at nos. 11921–11924.]]

11611. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words "O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you," up to His words "a straight path," who said: "The Jews came to the Prophet of God asking him about stoning, and they gathered in a house. He said: 'Who among you is most knowledgeable?' They pointed to Ibn Suriya. He said: 'Are you the most knowledgeable of them?' He said: 'Ask whatever you wish.' He said: 'Are you the most knowledgeable of them?' He said: 'They claim that is so!' So he adjured him by Him who sent down the Torah to Moses, and by Him who raised the Mount, and he adjured him by the covenants that were taken from them, until he was seized by a shiver [afkal]. [[Afkal (on the pattern af'al): a trembling that comes over a person from cold, fear, or other causes; it has no verb form. Ibn Barri recited: "By your life, bring us song, for your companions have not been... then she sang, playing her sieve, a song with a trembling in it."]] Then he said: 'Our women are beautiful women, so killing became common among us, so we shortened the matter [akhsurah]. [[Regarding "fa-ikhtasarna akhsurah": it appears thus in the manuscript too. In the tafsir of Abu Hayyan 3: 447 it reads "fa-ikhtasarna fa-jaladna mi'at mi'at" (so we shortened and flogged a hundred each), omitting "akhsurah." I have found no mention of this word in the lexicon with the meaning of shortening. What appears in the books is "al-khusayri" (with u on the kha, fath on the sad, sukun on the ya, then a fath on the ra), meaning removing the superfluous from anything, like "al-ikhtisar." Perhaps the correct phrase is "fa-ikhtasarna khusayri," meaning a shortening of the stoning judgment. I have left what is in the printed edition and manuscript, lest there be a distortion in the word that I have not identified.]] So we flogged a hundred, shaved the heads, and differentiated the heads toward the animals [[In Abu Hayyan's tafsir: "wa-khalafna bayna al-ru'us 'ala al-dabarat," which seems to be an error.]] = I think he said: the camels." He said: So he [Muhammad] judged them to be stoned, and God revealed concerning them: "O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you," the verse. And this verse: ﴿When they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you talk to them about what God has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?"﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 76]. [[Report 11611: In this report, the occasion of revelation of Surah al-Baqarah 76 is mentioned, which Abu Ja'far did not mention in his commentary on that verse there (2: 250–254), though it could be another aspect of the interpretation of that verse, and could be meant as "stoning." This is further evidence of Abu Ja'far's abridgment of his tafsir, which is also one of the features of his method in abridging.]]

* *

As for His words "and pardoning much," He means by "pardoning" that He leaves off punishing you for much of what you used to hide of your Book, which God sent down to you, namely the Torah, so that you do not act upon it until God commands you to be held to account for it. [[See the discussion of "al-'afw" (pardon) above in the lexical indices.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 15:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying: ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be great, says to those among the People of the Book whom He addresses: "There has certainly come to you," O People of the Torah and the Gospel, "from Allah a light," meaning by the light Muhammad (ﷺ), through whom Allah illuminated the truth, made Islam manifest, and obliterated polytheism. He is a light for whoever is guided by his light, clarifying the truth. And from his illuminating of the truth is his making clear to the Jews much of what they used to conceal of the Book. [[See the explanation of "light" above, 9:428.]]

* *

As for His saying, "and a clear Book," He, may His praise be great, says: There has come to you from Allah, exalted is He, the light by which He has illuminated for you the landmarks of the truth, "and a clear Book," meaning a book containing a clarification of what they differed about among themselves: concerning the oneness of Allah, His lawful and unlawful, and the laws of His religion. It is the Qur'an which He sent down upon our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), which makes clear to people all that they need of the matters of their religion, and explains it to them, so that they may know its truth from its falsehood. [[See the explanation of "clear" in the word indexes of earlier volumes.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 16:

The interpretation of His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Whereby Allah guides those who pursue His good pleasure to the ways of peace﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty and majestic is He, means: Allah guides by this clear Book that came from Allah, majestic is His majesty. By His saying "whereby Allah guides," He means: Allah gives guidance by it and makes firm by it. [See the explanation of "yahdi" (guides) in the earlier linguistic indexes.] The "ha" (pronoun) in His saying "bihi" (by it) refers back to "the Book," and "those who pursue His good pleasure" means: those who pursue the pleasure of Allah. [See the explanation of "ridwan" (good pleasure) in the earlier volumes: 6:262 / 9:480.]

* *

Scholars differed about the meaning of "ridha" (pleasure) from Allah, mighty and majestic.

Some of them said: Allah's pleasure with a thing is His acceptance of it, His praise and His commendation. They said: So He accepts faith, and attests to it as pure, and commends the believer for faith, and describes faith as light, guidance and distinction. [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "wa fadl" with the dotted letter (ḍād); but "al-fasl" here is the correct meaning, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood.]

* *

Others said: The meaning of "ridha" from Allah, mighty and majestic, is an understood meaning, which is the opposite of anger, and it is one of His attributes, according to what is understood from the meanings of "ridha," which is the opposite of anger. This is not praise, because praise and commendation are speech, and only what is pleased with is praised and commended. They said: So "ridha" is a meaning, while "commendation" and "praise" are a meaning that is not it.

* *

By His saying "subul al-salam" (the ways of peace) He means: the paths of peace. [See the explanation of "sabil" (way) in the earlier linguistic indexes.] And "al-Salam" is Allah, mighty is His remembrance.

11612 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Whoever pursues His good pleasure, the ways of peace": the way of Allah which He legislated for His servants and called them to, and sent His messengers with, and it is Islam, which no deed is accepted from anyone except with it, not Judaism, nor Christianity, nor Zoroastrianism.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And brings them out of darkness into light by His permission﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His remembrance, says: Allah guides by this clear Book, whoever pursues the good pleasure of Allah, to the ways of peace and the laws of His religion. "And brings them out": He says: and brings out whoever pursues His good pleasure. The "ha" and "mim" in "wa yukhrijuhum" (and brings them out) refer to those mentioned: "from darkness into light," meaning: from the darknesses of unbelief and polytheism to the light of Islam and its radiance. [See the explanation of "from darkness into light" in the earlier volume 5:424-426.] "By His permission" means: by the permission of Allah, mighty and majestic. And "His permission" in this place means: His making faith beloved to him, lifting the seal of disbelief from his heart and the seal of polytheism from it, and His granting him success in perceiving the ways of peace. [See the explanation of "idhn" (permission) in the earlier volume 8:516, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And guides them to a straight path﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His remembrance, by His saying "wa yahdihim" (and guides them), means: guides them and makes them firm [See the explanation of "yahdi" in the linguistic indexes.] "to a straight path," meaning: to a straight way, which is the upright religion of Allah in which there is no crookedness. [See the explanation of "al-sirat al-mustaqim" (the straight path) in the earlier volume 8:529, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿Certainly, they have disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a censure from Allah, mighty is His remembrance, of the Christians and Christianity, who went astray from the ways of peace, and an argument from Him for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) against their slander upon him by their claim that He has a son.

He, whose praise is majestic, says: I swear, certainly they have disbelieved who say: Indeed Allah is the Messiah son of Mary. Their "disbelief" in that is their covering over the truth by their refusal to negate offspring from Allah, mighty and majestic, and their claim that the Messiah is Allah, a slander and a lie against Him. [See the explanation of "kufr" (disbelief) in the earlier linguistic indexes.]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-Masih" (the Messiah) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [See the explanation of "al-Masih" in the earlier volume 9:417, note 1, and the references there.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 17:

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Say: Who then has any power against Allah if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth altogether?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to the Christians who have slandered Me and strayed from the right path with their claim that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary: "Who then has any power against Allah?" That is: who is able to repel anything of the command of Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, and turn it back when He has decreed it?

* *

[This is an explanation that you rarely find in the books of lexicography.] It is derived from the saying of the speaker: "I had power over so-and-so's affair" (malaktu 'ala fulan amrahu), when he becomes unable to carry out any matter except by him.

* *

As for His words: "if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth altogether," that means: who is able to turn back anything of the command of Allah, if He wishes to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, by annihilating him from the earth, and annihilating his mother Mary, and annihilating all the creatures on the earth altogether? [See the explanation of "destruction" (al-ihlak) earlier, 4:239, 240; 9:430.]

* *

He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to these ignorant Christians: If the Messiah were as you claim, that he is God, and that is not the case, he would have been able to repel the command of Allah when it came to him to destroy him and destroy his mother. Yet He destroyed his mother and he was not able to repel His command concerning her when that happened. In that is a lesson for you if you would take heed, and a proof against you if you would reason: that the Messiah is a human being like the rest of the children of Adam, and that Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, is the One who is not overcome, not subdued, and whose command cannot be turned back; rather He is the Living, the Everlasting, the Self-Subsisting, who gives life and causes death, who originates and annihilates, and He is living and does not die.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. He creates what He wills.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may He be blessed and exalted, means: To Allah belongs the disposal of what is in the heavens and the earth and what is between them [See the explanation of "dominion" (al-mulk) earlier, 8:48, note 3, and the references there.] – that is: and what is between the heaven and the earth – He destroys whom He wills of that and preserves what He wills of it, brings into existence what He wills and annihilates what He loves, and no obstacle prevents Him from anything of that which He wills, and no repeller repels Him from it; He carries out His judgment among them and executes His decree among them – not the Messiah, whom, if his Lord wished to destroy him and his mother, he would not have been able to repel what his Lord intended for him of that.

* *

He, may He be mighty and majestic, says: How can one be a god who is worshipped when he is unable to repel what others intend for him of evil, and unable to avert the destruction that has befallen him? Rather, the God who is worshipped is the One to whom belongs the dominion of everything, and in whose hand is the disposal of all who are in the heavens and the earth and what is between them.

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: "and what is between them," although He mentioned "the heavens" in the plural and did not say "and what is between them" (feminine plural), because the meaning is: what is between these two kinds of things, as the herdsman (al-Ra'i) said:

*Taraqa, fa-tilka hamahimi, uqriyuhuma... qulusan lawaqiha ka-l-qisiyyi wa-hulla*

[From his qasida in Jamharat ash'ar al-'Arab: 173, and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 118, 160. He says to his daughter Khulayda: "When she saw my sleeplessness and the length of my wandering..." (the rest of the poem is cited there). "Al-hamahim": the cares. "Qulus" is the plural of "qalus": young she-camels. "Lawaqih": pregnant, plural of "laqih". "Hul" is the plural of "ha'il", the she-camel that has not conceived for a year or two or several years; likewise every pregnant one whose pregnancy has ceased. He means: I make the lodging of these cares camels of these qualities, as if they were bows strung from the length of their journeys, and I strike with them the wastelands.

The evidence Tabari intended is that he said "fa-tilka hamahimi" (those are my cares), having previously mentioned "hammani" (two cares), then returned afterwards, saying "uqriyuhuma" (I make them lodge), and said "hamahimi" in the plural. See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 118, 160.]

So he said "tarqa" (they two came at night), speaking of two things, then said "fa-tilka hamahimi," returning to the sense of the statement.

* *

As for His words: "He creates what He wills," He, may His praise be exalted, means: He originates and brings into existence what He wills, bringing it out from the state of non-existence into the state of existence, and none but Allah, the One, the Subduer, is able to do that. He only means by that that to Him belongs the management of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and their disposal, and their annihilation and extinction, and the bringing into existence of what He wills of that which is neither existent nor originated. He means: this belongs to no one other than Me. So how have you claimed, O liars, that the Messiah is a god, when he is not able to do any of that, but is unable even to repel harm from himself or from his mother, or to bring benefit to her, except by My permission?

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (17)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah, the Worshipped, is the One who is capable of everything, and the Owner of everything, whom nothing He wills can defeat, and nothing He seeks can overpower, the One able to destroy the Messiah and his mother and everyone on the earth altogether – not the powerless one who cannot prevent himself from harm that has come upon him from Allah, nor prevent his mother from destruction. [See the explanation of "competent" (qadir) earlier in the indexes of language.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 18:

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And the Jews and the Christians said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved. Say, 'Why then does He punish you for your sins?'"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, mighty and majestic, about a people among the Jews and the Christians who said this statement.

* *

It has been mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas the naming of those among the Jews who said that.

11613 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or 'Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Nu'man ibn Adaa [[In the printed edition: "Nu'man ibn Ahhi, and Yahra ibn 'Amr..", and in the manuscript: "Uthman ibn Asar and Yahwa ibn 'Amr ..", and both are errors; the correct form is from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] and Bahri ibn 'Amr and Shas ibn 'Adi came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they spoke with him, and the Messenger of God ﷺ spoke with them, and invited them to God and warned them of His vengeance. They said: "Do you frighten us, O Muhammad?! By God, we are the sons of God and His beloved!" [[In the manuscript: "We are the sons of God and His beloved, but you are human beings among those He created", which is without doubt a scribe's hastiness.]] It is like the saying of the Christians, so God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning them: "And the Jews and the Christians said, 'We are the sons of God and His beloved'," to the end of the verse. [[The report: 11613 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 212, and it follows the earlier report numbered 11557.]]

* *

And al-Suddi used to say about this:

11614 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And the Jews and the Christians said, 'We are the sons of God and His beloved'." As for "the sons of God," they said: God revealed to Israel that a son of yours [[In the manuscript: "to the children of Israel, that a son of yours is of the offspring, so He will cause them to enter the Fire", which is a confusion without meaning; its correct form is probably what is in the printed edition.]] will enter the Fire, and they will remain in it forty days until He purifies them and consumes their sins; then a caller will call out: "Bring out every circumcised one of the children of Israel," and He will bring them out. This is His saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 24]. As for the Christians, a group of them said to the Messiah: "Son of God." [[The report: 11614 - This report has not passed in the interpretation of the verse of Surah al-Baqarah: 80 (2: 274-278), nor the verse of Surah Al 'Imran: 24 (6: 292, 293). This is also among the evidences of Abu Ja'far's abridgment of his tafsir.]]

* *

The Arabs, when they boast, may express a report in the form of a report about a group, even if what they boast of was done by only one of them. So they say: "We are the generous noble ones," whereas the generous one among them is only one of them, and the doer is other than the speaker. As Jarir said:

"We pierced Abu Mandusah the smith with spears, and blood flowed from the protector of Bayba, pure and fresh."

[[Diwan: 372; Naqa'id: 693; al-Lisan (bayb) (mawr) (nds). "Nadasa": to stab lightly. "Abu Mandusah" is Murrah ibn Sufyan ibn Mujashi', grandfather of al-Farazdaq, killed by Banu Yarbu' — Jarir's people — on the first day of al-Kilab. "Al-Qayn" is a nickname for the kin of al-Farazdaq, used in satire. "Jarbayba" is al-Summah ibn al-Harith al-Jushami, killed by Tha'labah ibn Hisn, and he was under the protection of al-Harith ibn Bayba ibn Qart ibn Sufyan ibn Mujashi', of al-Farazdaq's kin. "The blood moved on the face of the earth": flowed and stirred, came and went. "Nāqi'" means fresh, not yet dried.]]

He said "nadasna" (we pierced), whereas the one who pierced was a man other than them, from Jarir's people, so he expressed the report in the form of a report about a group, one of whom he was. Thus God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed of the Christians that they said this, in this manner, God willing.

* *

His words "and His beloved" are the plural of "habib" (beloved).

* *

God says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say" to these liars who slander their Lord: "Then why does He punish you" — your Lord — "for your sins?" That is: For what reason does your Lord punish you for your sins, if the matter is as you claim, that you are His sons and His beloved? For the beloved does not punish his beloved, and you acknowledge that He punishes you? That is because the Jews said: God will punish us for forty days, the number of days we worshipped the calf, [[See what has passed, 6: 292.]] and then He will bring us all out of it. So God said to Muhammad ﷺ: Say to them: If you are, as you say, the sons of God and His beloved, then why does He punish you for your sins? He, may His remembrance be exalted, makes them know that they are people of slander and lies against God, mighty and majestic.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Nay, you are but human beings of those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His praise be exalted, He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say to them: The matter is not as you claim, that you are the sons of God and His beloved. "Nay, you are but human beings of those He has created," that is: of the offspring of Adam. God created you like the rest of the children of Adam. If you do good, you will be rewarded for your good, as the rest of the children of Adam are rewarded for their good; and if you do evil, you will be requited for your evil, as others are requited for it. You have nothing with God beyond what others have of His creation. He forgives whom He wills of those who have faith in Him their sins, so He pardons him by His grace, and covers them for him by His mercy, so He does not punish him for them.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "forgiveness" in another place with its evidences, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what has passed, 2: 109, 110, then the rest of the lexical indices.]]

* *

"And punishes whom He wills": that is, He is just toward whomever He wills of His creation, so He punishes him for his sins, and exposes him for them before all witnesses, not concealing them from him.

* *

This is only a warning from God, mighty and majestic, to these Jews and Christians who rely on the status of their righteous predecessors with God, whom God preferred by their obedience to Him, chose for their hastening to His pleasure, and for their patience in what befell them in it. He says to them: Do not be deceived by those people's position with Me and their station with Me, for they only attained what they attained from Me through obedience to Me and preferring My pleasure over their desires — not through wishful thinking. So strive in My obedience, submit to My command, and desist from what I have forbidden you. For I forgive the sins of whom I will forgive among the people of My obedience, and I punish whom I will punish among the people of My disobedience — not for one whose forebears' nearness to Me has drawn close, while he is an enemy to Me and opposed to My command and prohibition.

* *

Al-Suddi used to say about this:

11615 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills," he said: He guides whom He wills of you in this world so He forgives him, and causes whom He wills of you to die in his disbelief so He punishes him.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the final return﴾ (18)

Abu Ja'far said: He says: To God belongs the management of what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them, and its disposal, and in His hand is the command, and to Him belongs the dominion. He turns it as He wills and manages it as He loves, with no partner to Him in any of it, and no one has dominion with Him over it. So know, O you who say "We are the sons of God and His beloved," that if He punishes you for your sins, there will be no preventer for you from Him, nor a repeller of Him for you, for there is no kinship between anyone and Him that He would show favor to him by reason of it, nor does anyone have dominion over anything apart from Him, so as to stand between Him and Him, if He wills to punish him for his sins. And to Him is the destination and return of every thing. So fear Him, O deceivers, His punishment of you for your sins after your return to Him, and do not be deceived by wishful thinking and the merits of fathers and forebears.

The Interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you [the truth] after a interval [of no messengers], lest you say, "There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or warner."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "O People of the Scripture," He, may His praise be exalted, means the Jews who were living among the emigrants of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day this verse was revealed. That is because they, or some of them, as has been reported, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited them to believe in him and in what had come to them from Allah, said: "Allah has not sent any prophet after Moses, nor has He revealed any scripture after the Torah!"

11616 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Sa'd ibn Ubadah and Uqbah ibn Wahb said to the Jews: "O assembly of Jews, fear Allah! By Allah, you know that he is the Messenger of Allah! You used to mention him to us before his mission and describe him to us by his attributes!" Rafi' ibn Huraymilah and Wahb ibn Yahuda [[In the printed edition: "Rafi' ibn Harmalah"; in the manuscript: "Nafi' ibn Harmalah"; I have adopted what is in the Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] said: "We did not say this to you, and Allah has not revealed any scripture after Moses, nor has He sent any bringer of good tidings or warner after him!" [[In the manuscript: "nor has He sent a bringer of good tidings and a warner," and the correct reading is that of the printed edition as in the Sirat Ibn Hisham.]] So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed in [regard to] their statement [[The addition in parentheses is from the Sirat Ibn Hisham.]]: "O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you [the truth] after an interval of messengers, lest you say, 'There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or warner.' Certainly there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and Allah is over all things competent." [[Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:212, which follows the earlier report no. 11613.]]

* *

By His words, "There has come to you Our Messenger," He means: Muhammad ﷺ has come to you, Our Messenger. "Making clear to you" means: he makes the truth known to you, clarifies for you the signs of guidance, and guides you to the approved religion of Allah, as

11617 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "There has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after an interval of messengers," that he is Muhammad ﷺ, who came with the Criterion (al-Furqan) by which Allah distinguishes between truth and falsehood; in it is Allah's clarification, His light and His guidance, and a safeguard for whoever holds to it.

* *

"After an interval of messengers" means: after a break in the sending of messengers. "Interval" (fatrah) in this context means a break. That is, "Our Messenger has come to you, making clear to you truth and guidance, after a break in messengers."

* *

"Fatrah" is the form "fa'lah" from the saying of the speaker, "This matter slackened (fatara) and slackens (yaftur) fatur," which is when it calms and subsides. Likewise "fatrah" in this place means calm: the calm of the coming of messengers, which is their cessation.

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the length of that interval, and the transmissions from Qatadah differ on this. Ma'mar related from him:

11618 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "after an interval of messengers," who said: Between Jesus and Muhammad ﷺ there were five hundred and sixty years.

* *

Sa'id ibn Abi Urwah related from him:

11619 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: The interval was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both; it was mentioned to us that it was six hundred years, or as much as Allah willed, and Allah knows best.

11620 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from his companions, regarding His words, "There has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after an interval of messengers," who said: Between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, there were five hundred and forty years. Ma'mar said: Qatadah said: five hundred and sixty years.

* *

Others said:

11621 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, "after an interval of messengers," that the interval was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, four hundred and some thirty years.

By His words, "lest you say, 'There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or warner'," [He means] lest you say it, and so that you will not say it, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 176], meaning: lest you go astray, and so that you will not go astray.

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: "There has come to you Our Messenger, making clear to you after an interval of messengers, so that you will not say, 'There came not to us any bringer of good tidings or warner.'" He, may His remembrance be exalted, informs them that He has cut off their excuse by His Messenger ﷺ and has conveyed the proof fully to them. [[See what has preceded, 9:445, 446.]]

By "bringer of good tidings" (bashir) is meant the one who gives good news to whoever obeys Allah, believes in Him and His Messenger, and acts upon what He brought from Allah, with His great reward in the Hereafter. [[See the discussion of "bishara" above, 9:318, note 2, and the references there.]] And by "warner" (nadhir) is meant the one who warns whoever disobeys Him, denies His Messenger ﷺ, and acts contrary to what he was brought from Allah regarding His commands and prohibitions, with a painful punishment he cannot bear in his return and a severe torment on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

The Interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿So there has certainly come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (19)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, says to these Jews whose description we have given: We have given you an excuse and established the proof against you through Our Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, whom We sent to you to make clear to you what was unclear to you of the matters of your religion, so that you would not say, "No messenger came to us from You clarifying for us what we are upon of error." So there has come to you from Me a Messenger who gives good news to whoever believes in Me, acts upon what I have commanded him, and refrains from what I have forbidden; and who warns whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command. I am the One Capable of all things: I am able to punish whoever disobeys Me and to reward whoever obeys Me. So fear My punishment for your disobedience to Me and your denial of My Messenger, and seek My reward for your obedience to Me and your belief in My bringer of good tidings and warner, for I am the One whom nothing He wills can overpower, and from whom nothing He seeks escapes. [[See the discussion of "qadir" in the indexes of language above.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 20:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is also an informing from God to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning the long persistence of these Jews in error, their distance from the truth, their poor choice for themselves, their great opposition to their prophets, and their slowness in turning back to right guidance, despite the abundance of God's blessings upon them and the succession of His bounties and favours to them. [By this] He consoles His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) regarding what befalls him from their mistreatment and what he suffers from them for the sake of God. God says to him (ﷺ): Do not grieve over what has afflicted you from them, for turning away from God, distance from the truth, and that which is of no benefit to them in this world and the next, are among their habits and the habits of their forefathers and ancestors. Take comfort in what your brother Moses (ﷺ) encountered from them, and remember when Moses said to them: "O my people, remember the favour of God upon you." That is: remember God's bounties among you and His blessings before you. [[See the explanation of "favour" (ni'mah) in the earlier language indexes.]] As follows:

11622 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, regarding "remember the favour of God upon you," he said: His bounties among you and His days.

[[Report 11622: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn Usamah al-Asadi al-Humaydi. He related from Ibn 'Uyaynah, al-Shafi'i and that generation. He related from al-Bukhari. Previously cited under no. 9914.]]

11623 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words "remember the favour of God upon you," he said: God's well-being (al-'afiyah).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have chosen what we have said because God did not specify any particular kind of favour, but generalised by mentioning "favours," so it includes well-being and other things, since "well-being" is one of the meanings of "favours."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His praise: ﴿when He set up prophets among you and made you kings﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His praise, means by this that Moses reminded his people from the Children of Israel of God's days among them and His bounties before them, urging them thereby to obey God's command to fight the tyrants, [[In the printed edition: "fa-harradhahum bi-dhalika," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] so he said to them: Remember God's favour upon you in that He preferred you, by setting among you prophets who bring you His revelation and inform you of the unseen news, [[In the printed edition: "wa-yukhbirunakum bi-ayatihi al-ghayb," which is meaningless; the manuscript reads "bi-ayatina al-ghayb," and the correct reading is what I have given.]] and did not give that to anyone else in your time. [[See the explanation of "prophet" (nabi) in earlier volumes, and elsewhere in the language indexes.]]

It has been said: The prophets whom Moses reminded them were set among them are those whom Moses chose when he went up the mountain, namely the seventy whom God mentioned when He said: ﴿And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 155].

* *

"And made you kings": He subjugated for you others as servants who serve you.

* *

It has been said: Moses only said this to them because, in that era, no one other than them had anyone among the children of Adam serving him.

Those who said this:

11624 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "And when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favour of God upon you when He set up prophets among you and made you kings,'" he said: We used to be told that they were the first for whom servants were subjugated among the children of Adam, and they became kings.

* *

Others said: Anyone who owns a house, a servant, and a wife is a "king," whoever he may be among people.

Those who said this:

11625 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Hani' informed us that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli say: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and a man asked him, saying: Are we not among the poor emigrants? 'Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife you take refuge with? He said: Yes! He said: Do you have a dwelling you live in? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are among the rich! He said: But I have a servant. He said: Then you are among the kings. [[Report 11625: Abu Hani' is Humayd ibn Hani' al-Khawlani al-Misri, a trustworthy Successor. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli is 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ma'afiri, a trustworthy Successor. This is a sound hadith, related by Muslim in his Sahih, 18:109-110, through Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh, from Ibn Wahb, with its chain, in full. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:270 limited himself to saying "related by Sa'id ibn Mansur" and mentioned only that.]]

11626 - Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar related to us, saying: Abu Dhamrah Anas ibn 'Iyad related to us, saying: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say: "And made you kings," so I do not know except that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Whoever has a house and a servant is a king. [[Report 11626: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar is Tabari's teacher, previously cited under no. 7855. Anas ibn 'Iyad ibn Dhamrah is trustworthy, previously cited under nos. 7, 1679. The hadith is recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:270 without attribution to Ibn Jarir; he attributed it to al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in al-Muwaffaqiyat, and to Abu Dawud in his Marasil. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 3:112-113 and said: "This is a mursal, gharib hadith."]]

11627 - Sufyan ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan: that he recited this verse, "And made you kings," and said: Is kingship anything other than a mount, a servant, and a house?

Those who held this view said: Moses only said that to them because they owned houses and servants, and had wives and spouses.

Those who said this:

11628 - Sufyan ibn WakI' and Ibn Humayd related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, [he said: I think from al-Hakam], regarding "And made you kings": he said: When a man among the Children of Israel had a house, a wife, and a servant, he was counted a king.

11629 - Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan [transmission switch]; and Sufyan related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, regarding "And made you kings": he said: The house, the wife, and the servant. Sufyan said: Or two of the three. [In the printed edition: "wa-ithnatayn" with a waw; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

11630 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words "And made you kings," he said: The house and the servant.

11631 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam or another, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words "And made you kings," he said: The wife, the servant, and the house.

11632 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words "And made you kings," he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses.

11633 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Hajjaj ibn Tamim, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding God's words "And made you kings," he said: A man among the Children of Israel who had a wife, a servant, and a house was called a king. [[Report 11633: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Tanafisi related from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir; trustworthy and truthful. Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir is Muhammad ibn Khazim al-Tamimi, trustworthy, prolific in narration, who used tadlis. Hajjaj ibn Tamim al-Jazari related from Maymun ibn Mihran; al-Nasa'i said "not trustworthy," al-Azdi said "weak," al-Uqayli said "he related from Maymun ibn Mihran hadiths not corroborated," and Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat said "he related from Maymun ibn Mihran, and Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir related from him." In the manuscript and printed edition it reads "Hajjaj ibn Nu'aym," which is a plain error as you see.]]

11634 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding his words "And made you kings," he said: Their kingship is the servants. Qatadah said: They were the first to own servants.

11635 - Al-Harith ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid: "And made you kings," he said: He made for you wives, servants, and houses.

* *

Others said: By His words "And made you kings" He meant that they would own themselves, their families, and their wealth.

Those who said this:

11636 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And made you kings": a man among you owns himself, his family, and his property.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿and gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds﴾ (20)

Abu Ja'far said: Scholars differed about who was addressed by this address.

Some said: It refers to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

11637 - Sufyan ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds," they both said: The community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

Others said: It refers to the people of Moses (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

11638 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: They are the people of Moses.

11639 - Al-Harith ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds," he said: They were among his people at that time. [[Report 11639: This report is related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:311-312, through Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from al-A'mash, at length. Its wording is: "alladhina hum bayna dhahrani'him yawma'idhin" [those who were among them at that time]. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed. The wording in Tabari's text is "hum bayna dhahrani'hi yawma'idhin," with the pronoun in the singular, as if it refers to the "world" among which they were at that time. Al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:269, adding attribution to al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

* *

Then they differed about what it is that God gave them that He had not given anyone among the worlds.

Some said: It is the manna and quails, the stone, and the cloud. [["The stone" means the stone that Moses struck with his staff, from which twelve springs gushed forth. See above 2:119-122.]]

Those who said this:

11640 - Sufyan ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds," he said: The manna and quails, the stone, and the cloud.

11641 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds," meaning: the people of that era, the manna and quails, the stone, and the cloud.

* *

Others said: It is the house, the servant, and the wife.

Those who said this:

11642 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari related to us, from Talhah ibn 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds," he said: The man who has a house, a servant, and a wife. [[Report 11642: Bishr ibn al-Sari al-Basri, Abu 'Amr al-Afwah, trustworthy and prolific in narration; the group related from him, and he was among the teachers of Ahmad. Talhah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman al-Hadrami related from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others; very weak. Ahmad said: "Nothing, abandoned in hadith." Ibn 'Adi said: "Trustworthy people related from him, but most of what he narrates is not corroborated." Ibn Hibban said: "It is not lawful to write his hadith or narrate from him, except as a matter of wonder."]]

11643 - Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds": the manna and quails, the stone, and the cloud.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in my view is the statement of the one who said: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds" is within the context of His words "remember the favour of God upon you," and is conjoined to it. [[The printer of the edition did not understand Abu Ja'far's Arabic, so he rendered the sentence as: "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds, an address to the Children of Israel since it came in the context of His words 'remember the favour of God upon you' = and conjoined to it," altering, adding, and failing in trust!!]]

There is nothing in the speech indicating that "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds" is diverted from the people addressed at the beginning of the verse. Given that, it is more appropriate that it be an address to them than to say it is diverted from them to others.

If someone supposes that "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds" cannot be an address to them, [In the printed edition: "la yajuzu an takuna khitaban li-Bani Isra'il," with the addition "li-Bani Isra'il"; in the manuscript: "an takuna lahu khitaban," and the correct reading is what I have given.] since the community of Muhammad has been given, through its Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), from God's honour, what no one else has been given, [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "min karamat Allah nabiyyaha 'alayhi al-salam Muhammadan ma lam yu'ta ahadan ghayrahum," and I have adopted the manuscript's addition, and read "bi-nabiyyiha" with a ba' at its beginning, and "ahadan" as "ahad," which is the plain correct form.] and they are among the worlds [The context: "If someone supposes... then he has supposed other than the correct." then he has supposed other than the correct. That is because His words "And gave you what He had not given anyone among the worlds" are an address from Moses (peace be upon him) to his people on that day, and by it he meant the worlds of his time, not the worlds of every time. Nothing of God's blessings and honour that his people received was given to anyone among the worlds at that time. [The context: "And nothing of God's blessings and honour was given in that era... to anyone among the worlds."] So the speech of him (peace be upon him) went out in that manner, not to all [world] of every time. [See the explanation of "the worlds" (al-'alamin) in earlier volumes: 1:143-146, 2:23-26, 5:375, 6:393.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 21:

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, saying: ﴿O my people, enter the holy land which God has prescribed for you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from God, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning the words of Musa (ﷺ) to his people from the Children of Israel, and his command to them, by the command of God to him, to enter the holy land.

* *

Then the exegetes differed concerning the land which He meant by "the holy land."

Some of them said: He meant by that al-Tur (Mount Sinai) and what surrounds it.

Those who said this:

11644 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "the holy land," al-Tur and what surrounds it.

11645 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

11646 - al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "Enter the holy land," he said: al-Tur and what surrounds it.

* *

Others said: It is al-Sham (Syria).

Those who said this:

11647 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada concerning His saying: "the holy land," he said: It is al-Sham.

* *

Others said: It is the land of Jericho (Ariha).

Those who said this:

11648 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "Enter the holy land which God has prescribed for you," he said: Jericho.

11649 - Yusuf ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It is Jericho.

11650 - Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is Jericho.

* *

It was also said: "the holy land" is Damascus, Palestine and part of the Jordan.

* *

By His saying "holy" he meant purified and blessed, [[See the explanation of "taqdis" (sanctification) in what has preceded, 1:475, 476 / 2:322.]] as:

11651 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "the holy land," he said: the blessed.

11652 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings, in the view of truth, is that it be said: It is the holy land, as the Prophet of God Musa (peace be upon him) said, because to say that it is one land rather than another cannot have its truth known except by report, and there is no report to this effect that permits one to testify to it with certainty. Nevertheless, it will not fall outside being among the land that lies between the Euphrates and the Arish of Egypt, by the consensus of all the exegetes, the historians and the scholars of reports on this.

* *

By His saying "which God has prescribed for you" he means: which He recorded in the Preserved Tablet as dwellings and abodes for you, apart from the tyrants who are in it. [[See the explanation of "kataba" (prescribed) in what has preceded, 9:262, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

If someone says: How then did He say "which God has prescribed for you," when you know that they did not enter it, by His saying: "Indeed it is forbidden to them" (5:26)? How can it be recorded in the Preserved Tablet that it is dwellings for them, while their residing in it is forbidden to them?

It is said: It was prescribed for the Children of Israel as a home and dwellings, and they did dwell in it and settle in it and it became theirs, as God, may He be exalted and glorified, said. Musa said to them: "Enter the holy land which God has prescribed for you," meaning by it: which God prescribed for the Children of Israel, =and those whom Musa commanded to enter it were from the Children of Israel= and he (ﷺ) did not mean that God, may His remembrance be exalted, prescribed it for those whom he commanded to enter it by their individual persons.

And if someone said: It was prescribed for some of them and for a select group among them, so the speech is brought out in generality while the meaning is specific, since Yusha and Kalib had entered it [[In the printed edition: "Yusha' and Kullab"; see what has preceded p. 113 note 2.]] and they were among those addressed by this saying, that would also be a sound interpretation.

* *

Ibn Ishaq said the like of what we have said about this.

11653 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq: "which God prescribed for you," which God granted you.

* *

al-Suddi used to say: The meaning of "kataba" (prescribed) in this place is in the sense of: commanded.

11654 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to us with this, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Enter the holy land which God has prescribed for you," which God commanded you with.

* *

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, saying: ﴿And do not turn back on your heels, for you will become losers﴾ (21)

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from God, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning the saying of Musa (peace be upon him) to his people from the Children of Israel, when he commanded them, by the command of God, may His remembrance be exalted, to him, to enter the holy land: he said to them: Proceed, O people, to the command of God which He commanded you with, of entering the holy land. ="And do not turn back" means: do not retreat backward, turning away [[See the explanation of "irtadda" (turn back) in what has preceded, 3:163 / 4:316.]] ="on your heels" meaning: behind you, [[See the explanation of "adbar" (heels) in what has preceded, 7:109.]] but proceed forward to the command of God which He commanded you with, of entering upon the people whom God commanded you to fight and to attack in their land, and that God, may His remembrance be exalted, has prescribed it for you as a dwelling and a settled place.

By His saying "then you will turn back losers," he means: you will return disappointed and perished. [[See the explanation of "inqalaba" (turn back) in what has preceded, 3:163 / 7:414. In the manuscript and the printed edition this phrase read: "that you will turn away disappointed thus," and I have preferred that the correct reading is what is given here.

"Hulluk" is the plural of "halik" (perishing). And the explanation of "al-khasara" (loss) as "perdition" has passed.]]

* *

We have explained the meaning of "al-khasara" (loss) in other than this place, with its evidences that make repetition of it here unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "al-khasara" in what has preceded, 9:224, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

If someone says: What was the meaning of Musa's saying to his people, when he commanded them to enter the holy land: "Do not turn back on your heels, for you will become losers" — does one who does not enter a land that was made for him deserve loss? It is said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, had commanded them to fight those in it who were of the unbelievers in Him and imposed on them entering it, [[In the printed edition: "kana amrahu," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] so the people deserved loss by their abandoning what God imposed on them, in two respects: The first: squandering the obligation of jihad which God, may His remembrance be exalted, had imposed on them. The second: opposing the command of God in their refusal to enter the land, and their saying to their prophet Musa (ﷺ) when he said to them: "Enter the holy land": "Indeed we will never enter it while they are in it. So if they leave it, then we will enter."

* *

Qatada used to say about this:

11655 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "O my people, enter the holy land which God has prescribed for you": they were commanded with it, just as they were commanded with prayer, zakat, Hajj and 'Umrah.

**The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿They said, "O Musa, indeed in it there are a people of giants (jabbarin)."﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may His praise be exalted, about the reply of the people of Musa (peace be upon him) when he commanded them to enter the Holy Land. They refused to comply with what he commanded them, and they made excuses to him by saying: "Indeed, in the Holy Land you command us to enter, there is a people of giants (jabbarin) against whom we have no strength to fight, and no power to face them." They named them "jabbarin" because, as has been reported to us, they were, through the severity of their force and the greatness of their bodies, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "bi-shiddat batshihim" (with the severity of their force); the context requires what is adopted here.]] superior to all other peoples.

The root of "jabbar" is one who sets right his own affairs and the affairs of others. Then it came to be used for everyone who draws benefit to himself, rightly or wrongly, seeking to set his own affairs right. Thus the one who transgresses against what is not his, out of tyranny over people, subjugation of them, and insolence toward his Lord, is called "jabbar." It is in fact a form of "fa'-al" (fa'-‘āl) from their saying: "Fulan jabara this break," when he set it right and mended it. From this is the verse of the rajaz-poet: [[He is al-'Ajjaj.]]

*Qad jabara al-dina al-ilahu fa-jabar / wa 'awwara al-Rahmanu man wallá al-'awar*

[[Diwanuhu: 15, and al-Lisan (jbr) ('wr). This is the opening of his rajaz by which he praised 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar al-Taymi. Some of its verses have passed, and we have mentioned its story earlier; see 1: 190 / 2: 157 / 3: 229 / 4: 321. His saying "qad jabara al-dina al-ilah" comes from their saying "jabartu al-'azm" (transitive), "fa-jabar" (intransitive), meaning the bone itself was set. "Al-'awar" in this verse means the ugliness and corruption of a matter and abandoning the truth in it, not the "'awar" of the eye. "'Awara al-shay'" means it made it ugly. He is supplicating and saying: may God disgrace whoever follows corruption and faces it with his face. From their saying "walia al-shay' wa-tawallahu," meaning he followed it; and in the Revelation: "wa-li-kullin wijhatun huwa muwalliha" (2:148), meaning facing it and following it. This is the explanation of the verse, without confusion in its interpretation.]]

That is, "The God has set the religion right, so it became upright." Among the names of God, may His remembrance be exalted, is "al-Jabbar," because He is the one who sets right the affairs of His servants and who overpowers them by His power.

* *

Among what I have mentioned about the greatness of their bodies is:

11656 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a story he mentioned about the affair of Musa and the Children of Israel. He said: Then he commanded them to march toward Jericho (Arihá), which is the land of Bayt al-Maqdis, so they marched. When they were close to them, Musa sent twelve nuqaba' (chiefs) from all the tribes of the Children of Israel, and they set out wishing to bring him news of the jabbarin. A man from the jabbarin met them, called "'Aj." [[In the printed edition: "'Awj," but what is in the manuscript is adopted, and it agrees with what preceded at no. 11572 and with Tarikh al-Tabari.]] He seized the twelve and put them in his waistband, and on his head was a bundle of firewood. He went with them to his wife and said: "Look at these people who claim they want to fight us!" He threw them down before her. He said: "Shall I not crush them under my foot?" His wife said: "No, rather let them go until they inform their people of what they saw!" So he did that. [[The report: 11656 – it passed at length as no. 11572, and it is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 221, 222.]]

11657 – 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id said, 'Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Musa was commanded to enter the city of the jabbarin. He said: So Musa set out with those who were with him until he alighted near the city, which is Arihá. He sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him news of the people. He said: They entered the city and saw a dreadful thing of their form, their bodies and their greatness. They entered an orchard belonging to one of them. The owner of the orchard came to pick fruit from his orchard, and he began picking fruit and looking at their traces, and followed them. Whenever he came upon one of them, he seized him and put him in his sleeve with the fruit, and went to their king and scattered them before him. The king said: "You have seen our state and our affair; go and inform your companion." He said: So they returned to Musa and informed him of what they had witnessed of their affair.

11658 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Indeed in it there is a people of giants": it has been mentioned to us that they had bodies and forms that were not possessed by others.

11659 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi', who said: Indeed Musa (peace be upon him) said to his people: "Indeed I will send men who will bring me news of them." He took one man from each tribe, so they were twelve chiefs, and he said: "Go to them, and tell me their account and their affair, and do not fear; indeed God is with you as long as you establish the prayer, give the zakat, believe in His messengers, support them, and lend God a goodly loan." Indeed the people set out until they fell upon them, and they saw peoples who had bodies wondrous in size and strength. It was mentioned that one of the jabbarin saw them, and they did not hesitate to conceal themselves when they saw the wonder. That giant seized men from them and went to their chief and threw them before him, and they were amazed and laughed at them. One of them said: "These people claimed that they intended to attack you!" [[In the printed edition: "inna hā'ulā'" without the fa'; what is in the manuscript is adopted.]] And had it not been for what God averted from them, they would have been killed. They returned to Musa (peace be upon him) and related the wonder to him.
