11660 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the word of God: "twelve chiefs," one man from each tribe of the Children of Israel, whom Musa sent to the jabbarin. They found that into the sleeve of one of them, two of them could enter; they would throw them in. No cluster of their grapes could be carried except by five persons together on a pole; and into half of a pomegranate, when its seeds were removed, five persons, or four, could enter. [[The report: 11660 – this report passed as nos. 11573 and 11574.]]

11661 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

11662 – Muhammad ibn al-Wazir ibn Qays narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: "Indeed in it there is a people of giants," he said: rabble, who have no portion. [[The report: 11662 – "Muhammad ibn Wazir ibn Qays al-Wasiti," who narrated from his father, Ibn 'Uyaynah, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, and others. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from him, and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/115.

And his father "Wazir ibn Qays al-Wasiti," who narrated from Juwaybir. Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/44.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And indeed we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then indeed we will enter.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about the words of the people of Musa to Musa, in reply to his saying to them: "Enter the Holy Land which God has prescribed for you." They said: "Indeed we will never enter it until they leave it," meaning: [until there leaves] from the Holy Land the jabbarin who are in it, [[What is between the brackets is an addition required by the context.]] out of cowardice on their part and dread of fighting them. And they said to him: If these jabbarin leave it, we will enter it; otherwise we are unable to enter it while they are in it, for we have no strength against them and no hands. [[In the printed edition: "wa-la yad" (and no hand); in the manuscript: "wa-la yadan," unpointed.]]

11663 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, that Kaleb ibn Yafna silenced the people (al-sha'b) from Musa (peace be upon him) and said to them: "Indeed we will overcome the land and inherit it, and indeed we have strength against them!" As for those who were with him, they said: "We cannot reach that people, because they are bolder than us!" Then those spies informed the Children of Israel of the news and said: "Indeed we passed through a land and examined it, and behold, it devours its inhabitants, and we saw its men were tall, and we saw the jabbarin, the sons of jabbarin, and we were in their eyes like locusts!" The assembly of the Children of Israel trembled, and they raised their voices in weeping. The people wept that night, and they whispered against Musa and Harun, [["waswasa 'alayhi" – its explanation is found in report no. 11697, p. 195, note 7.]] and said to them both: "Would that we had died in the land of Egypt! Or would that we might die in this wilderness, and God had not brought us into this land to fall in war, so that our women, our children and our baggage become spoils! Had we remained seated in the land of Egypt, it would have been better for us!" And a man would say to his companions: "Come, let us appoint a leader over ourselves and return to Egypt."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 23:

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, words: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour, said﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the two righteous men from the people of Musa: "Yusha' ibn Nun" and "Kalib ibn Yafuna," that they fulfilled to Musa what he had charged them with, namely not informing his people, the Children of Israel, whom he had commanded to enter the Holy Land (the land of the Canaanites) among the tyrants, of what they had seen and witnessed of the great violence and enormous stature of the tyrants. Allah, may He be exalted, described them as being among those who fear Allah and watch over Him in His commands and prohibitions, as:

11664 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us [ḥ]; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan [ḥ]; and Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾, he said: Kalab ibn Yafuna [in the printed edition in both places: "Yawfana," and in the manuscript in both places: "Fanya"; see p. 113, note 2], and Yusha' ibn Nun.

11665 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: ﴿two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalab ibn Yafuna [in the printed edition: "Yawfana," in the manuscript: "Fanyah"; see the note on the report 11573], and they were of the leaders (nuqaba').

11666 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding a story he mentioned, he said: The leaders returned, all of them forbidding their tribe from fighting them, except Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yafunah [in the printed edition: "Yawfana," in the manuscript: "Fanyah"; see the note on the report 11573], who commanded the tribes to fight the tyrants and struggle against them, but they disobeyed them and obeyed the others; so they are the two men on whom Allah bestowed His favour. [Report 11666: this report has passed as number 11573, and its beginning has passed shortly as number 11660.]

11667 - Ibn Humayd and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the like of the hadith of Ibn Bashshar, from Ibn Mahdi, except that Ibn Humayd said in his hadith: they were of the twelve leaders.

11668 - 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id said, 'Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding a story he mentioned: They returned — meaning the twelve leaders — to Musa and informed him of what they had witnessed of their affair. Musa said to them: Keep their matter secret and do not tell anyone of the army about it, for if you inform them of this report they will lose heart and not enter the city. ["Fashila": to be cowardly and to shrink back.] He said: So each one of them went and informed his relative and his cousin, except these two men — Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yawfana — for they concealed it and did not tell anyone about it. These are the two of whom Allah, may He be exalted, said: "Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour," up to His words: "and between the wicked people."

11669 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾, and they are the two who concealed it: Yusha' ibn Nun, the young man of Musa [in the manuscript: "Huwa Yusha' ibn al-Nun," and I think the original was "Hawsha' ibn Nun," as previously mentioned on p. 113, note 2. In the printed edition here it was "Nun," and I have kept what is in the manuscript], and Kalub ibn Yawfana, the in-law of Musa.

11670 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾: Kalub, and Yusha' ibn al-Nun, the young man of Musa [in the printed edition: "ibn Nun," in both places; I have kept what is in the manuscript].

11671 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾, and the two men on whom Allah bestowed His favour from the Children of Israel were: Yusha' ibn al-Nun and Kalub ibn Yawfana.

11672 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾. It was mentioned to us that the two men were Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib.

11673 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': that Musa said to the leaders when they returned and reported the wonder to him: "Do not tell anyone what you have seen; Allah will surely open it for you and make you prevail over it after what you have seen." And the people spread the report among the Children of Israel, and two men arose from among those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour ["in the manuscript: 'fa-qama rajulan huma alladhan yakhafun..', and what is in the printed edition is correct"], one of whom, as we have heard, was Yusha' ibn Nun, the young man of Musa, and the other Kalib. They said: "Enter upon them by the gate" up to "if you are believers." ["In the printed edition: 'Enter upon them by the gate, if you are believers,' which is not correct; the correct form is from the manuscript."]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: "Two men of those who feared."

The readers of the Hijaz, Iraq and Syria recited it: ﴿Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾, with a fatha on the "ya'" of "yakhafun," according to the interpretation we mentioned earlier from those we cited, that they were Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib, from the people of Musa, of those who fear Allah, and that Allah bestowed on them success.

* *

Qatadah used to say: in some recitations it is: ﴿Two men of those who feared Allah, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾.

11674 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah [ḥ]; and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour," in some letters: ﴿those who feared Allah, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾.

* *

This also indicates the soundness of the interpretation of those who interpreted it as we mentioned from him, that they were Yusha' and Kalib.

* *

It is also reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he used to recite it: ﴿Two men of those who are made to fear﴾ with a damma on the "ya'" ﴿on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾.

11675 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me with this, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub [and we do not know that he heard from him], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that he used to recite it with a damma on the "ya'" of: ﴿yukhafun﴾.

It seems that Sa'id, in this recitation, went to the view that the two men about whom Allah reported that they said to the Children of Israel, "Enter upon them by the gate, for when you have entered it you will surely be victorious," were from the family of the tyrants, and had embraced Islam and followed Musa, so they were from the offspring of the tyrants whom the Children of Israel feared, even though they were opposed to them in religion. ["In the manuscript: 'fa-hum min awlad al-jabbarin,' and the correct is what is in the printed edition." "In the printed edition: 'wa-in kanu lahum fi al-din mukhalifin,' and in the manuscript: 'wa-in kanu lahum fi al-dunya mukhalifin,' and the pure correct is what I have adopted."]

* *

This interpretation has been reported similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.

11676 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Enter the holy land which Allah has prescribed for you, and do not turn back on your heels, for you will become losers﴾: He said: it is the city of the tyrants. When Musa and his people alighted there, he sent out from among them twelve men — and they are the leaders whose sending was mentioned ["in the printed edition: 'dhikr na't-hum,' in the manuscript: 'dhikr ba'thahum,' and I read it 'ba'thatahum,' meaning what came in the previous verse of this surah: 10, 'And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders'"] — to bring them news of them. They set out, and a man of the tyrants met them, put them in his garment, carried them until he brought them to the city, and called out to his people, and they gathered to him. They said: Who are you? They said: We are the people of Musa; he sent us to you to bring him news of you! They gave them a grape of a size equal to a man's load ["al-waqr" (with a kasra and sukun): the load and weight], and said to them: Go to Musa and his people and say to them: Measure the measure of their fruit! When they came to them, they said to Musa: "Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting here!" "Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour said," and they were from the people of the city, who had embraced Islam and followed Musa and Harun, and they said to Musa: "Enter upon them by the gate, for when you have entered it you will surely be victorious; and upon Allah rely, if you are believers."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: According to this recitation and this interpretation, none of the twelve leaders concealed what Musa had commanded them to conceal from the Children of Israel of what they had seen and witnessed of the great bodies of the tyrants, their violence, and the wonder of their affairs; rather they spread all of it. The one who said to the people and to Musa, "Enter upon them by the gate," was two men from the offspring of those whom the Children of Israel used to fear, and whom they dreaded entering upon among the tyrants, who had embraced Islam and followed the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations in our view is the recitation of the one who recited: ﴿of those who fear, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour﴾, due to the consensus of the readers of the major cities upon it. What is widely transmitted through recitation from them is a proof that may not be opposed, while what a single reporter alone transmits is liable to error and inadvertence. Furthermore, the consensus of the proof on its interpretation, that they were two men from the companions of Musa from the Children of Israel, and that they were Yusha' and Kalib, is sufficient to dispense with citing evidence for the soundness of the recitation with a fatha on the "ya'" in that, and the corruption of other than it. This is the sound interpretation in our view, due to the consensus upon it that we have mentioned.

* *

As for His words, "on whom Allah had bestowed His favour," it means: Allah bestowed His favour on them by obedience to Allah in obeying His prophet Musa, peace be upon him, and their compliance with his command, and their restraint from what he forbade them, namely spreading what they had witnessed of the wondrous affair of the tyrants among the Children of Israel, which the other companion leaders who were with them had reported.

* *

It has been said that the meaning of this is: Allah bestowed His favour on them with fear.

Those who said this:

11677 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Tamim narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, from Sahl ibn 'Ali regarding His words: "Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour," he said: Allah bestowed His favour on them with fear. ["Khalaf ibn Tamim ibn Abi 'Attab al-Tamimi," Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, a trustworthy and devout man. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/180, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/370. "Ishaq ibn al-Qasim" I did not find. As for "Sahl ibn 'Ali," I did not find anyone of that name except "Sahl ibn 'Ali al-Marwazi," who narrated from al-Mubarak; the people of Marw narrated his speech and were courteous due to his piety. Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/203.]

* *

Al-Dahhak said something similar to what we have said, and a group other than him.

11678 - Narrated to me from al-Husayn, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say, narrating to me, 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "Two men of those who feared, on whom Allah had bestowed His favour": with guidance, so He guided them, and they were upon the religion of Musa, and they were in the city of the tyrants.

* *

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, words: ﴿Enter upon them by the gate, for when you have entered it you will surely be victorious﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the saying of the two men who feared Allah to the Children of Israel, when they were cowardly and afraid to enter upon the tyrants, after they heard their report, and the leaders who spread what they had witnessed of their affair informed them, and said: "In it there are tyrannical people, and we will never enter it until they leave it." So the two said to them: Enter upon them, O people, the gate of their city, for Allah is with you, He is your helper, and when you enter the gate you will overcome them, as:

11679 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge of the first Book, who said: When the Children of Israel intended to turn back to Egypt, when the leaders informed them of what they had reported about the matter of the tyrants, Musa and Harun fell on their faces in prostration before the company of the Children of Israel, and Yusha' ibn Nun and Kalib ibn Yafuna tore their garments, and they were of the spies of the land, and said to the company of the Children of Israel: "The land which we passed through and examined is very good; our Lord is pleased with us and has given it to us, and it truly flows with milk and honey [in the printed edition and the manuscript: 'wa-innaha lam takun tafid laban wa-'asalan,' which does not make sense, while what came in the people's book, in Numbers, chapter 13: 'and truly it flows with milk and honey,' and in chapter 14, which is the text of this speech in Arabic: 'and gives us it, a land that flows with milk and honey.' So I deleted 'lam takun' and put dots in its place, lest the word be distorted from something I did not know.] But do one thing: do not disobey Allah, and do not fear the people who are in it, for they are our bread, and given into our hands [in the printed edition: 'fa-innahum jubana mudaffa'un,' and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in the people's book, Numbers, chapter 14. By his words 'khubzana,' he means they are our food and spoil, as we say in Arabic.] Their pride has departed from them [in the printed edition: 'in harabnahum dhahabat minhum,' and I do not know what this is. In the manuscript: 'in harabahum dhahabat minhum.' I saw fit to read it so, for I saw in the people's book: 'their shade has departed from them, and the Lord is with us,' as if he means: what had been constantly with them of boldness, strength, violence and awe has gone away.

Moreover, it is useful to compare this report from Ibn Ishaq with the translation of the Torah that is in our hands, for these reports from Ibn Ishaq are undoubtedly from his early translation of the Torah. Perhaps a researcher who traces this report from Ibn Ishaq and others and compares it with the translation existing now would find great historical benefits, and benefits concerning the methods of translation in the past and present.] And Allah is with us, so do not fear them." So a group of the Children of Israel wanted to stone them with stones.

11680 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that they sent twelve men, one man from each tribe, as spies for them, to bring them news of the people. Ten of them made their people cowardly and made the entering upon them hateful to them. But the two men commanded their people to enter, and to follow the command of Allah, and encouraged them to it, and informed their people that they would be victorious if they did so.

11681 - al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding Allah's words: "upon them the gate," [meaning] the town of the tyrants.

* *

The interpretation of His, may His praise be exalted, words: ﴿And upon Allah rely, if you are believers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is also information from Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, about the saying of the two men who feared Allah, that they said to the people of Musa, encouraging them and urging them to proceed to the command of Allah by entering upon the tyrants in their city: Rely, O people, upon Allah in your entering upon them. They say to them: Trust in Allah, for He is with you if you obey Him in what He commanded you of jihad against your enemy. By their saying "if you are believers" they meant: if you are those who believe your Prophet ﷺ in what he informed you from your Lord of victory and triumph over them, and in other than that of his reports from his Lord, and believers that your Lord is able to fulfill for you what He promised you of establishing you in the lands of His enemy and your enemy.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."﴾ (5:24)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the statement of the chieftains of the people of Moses to Moses, when they were encouraged to fight their enemy and were promised Allah's help if they advanced against them and entered the gate of their city. They said to him, "Indeed, we will never enter it," meaning: we will never enter their city.

The "ha" and "alif" in His saying "we will never enter it" refer to "the city."

By their saying "never" they mean: throughout our lives [see the explanation of "abadan" in what has preceded, 9:227]. "As long as they are within it" means: as long as the tyrants remain in that city which Allah had prescribed for them and commanded them to enter. "So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here" means: we will not come with you, O Moses, if you go to them to fight them, but we will leave you to go alone, you and your Lord, and fight them.

Some of them said concerning this: the meaning of the speech is not, "Go, you, and let your Lord go with you and fight," but rather its meaning is: "Go, you, O Moses, and let your Lord help you." That is because it is not permissible for Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to be described as going. [This is the view of Abu 'Ubaidah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:160, in meaning and not in wording.]

This would only need seeking an explanation if the report were about believing people. But as for a people who opposed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, and His Messenger, there is no basis for seeking an explanation for their words concerning what they said about Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and slandered Him, except in a way that resembles their disbelief and misguidance.

It has been reported from al-Miqdad that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) something contrary to what the people of Moses said to Moses.

11682 - Sufyan ibn WakI' narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us; and Hannad narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us; from Sufyan, from Mukhariq, from Tariq: that al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We do not say as the Children of Israel said, 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here,' but we say: go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you."

[Note on the report 11682: "Mukhariq" is Mukhariq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Jabir al-Bajali al-Ahmasi, and it is said Mukhariq ibn Khalifah; he is biographied in al-Tahdhib.

"Tariq" is Tariq ibn Shihab ibn 'Abd Shams al-Bajali al-Ahmasi, who saw the Prophet (ﷺ), narrated from him as a mursal report, narrated from the four Caliphs, and was among the companions of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. It has passed under number 9744.

This report has been transmitted through the route of Tariq, in both full and abridged forms. Al-Bukhari narrated it abridged, as mursal and as mawsul, in his Sahih (al-Fath 8:205), and narrated it in full and as mawsul (al-Fath 7:223-227). Ahmad narrated it in full in the Musnad of Ibn Mas'ud under numbers 3698, 4070, 4376.

This report concerns the Prophet's (ﷺ) consultation of his companions before Badr, when he reached al-Safra and it reached him that the Quraysh had set out for Badr and that Abu Sufyan had escaped with what he had, so he consulted the people. See the story in full in the books of biography. Then see the following report, and that this was on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah.]

11683 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the polytheists blocked the sacrificial animals and they were prevented from their rites: "Indeed, I am going with the sacrificial animals, and I will slaughter them at the House!" Then al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad said to him: "Indeed, by Allah, we will not be like the chieftains of the Children of Israel when they said to their prophet, 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.' Rather: go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting with you!" When the companions of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) heard it, they followed suit in that.

[Note on report 11683: In the manuscript this report was written twice with its chain and text. The first time it was written up to his words "indeed, we are fighting with you," then it was written again with its chain, and completed in full to the end. It appears that the scribe stopped at this point, then returned to write, and the report before it also ended with "indeed, we are fighting with you," so he thought the one he had written was the first report, and so he wrote the report again with its chain from beginning to end.]

* *

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, and a group other than them used to say: they only said this statement to Moses, peace be upon him, when the matter of the tyrants and the severity of their might became clear to them.

11684 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded the Children of Israel to travel to the Holy Land with their prophet Moses, peace be upon him. When they were near the city, Moses said to them, "Enter it," but they refused and lost their nerve, and they sent twelve chieftains to look at them. They set out and looked, and they brought back a single fruit from their fruits, the load of a man, and they said: "Consider the strength and might of this people, this is their fruit!" At that point they said to Moses, "Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here."

11685 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: 'Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

The commentary on the words of Allah, exalted is His praise: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people."﴾ (25)

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Allah, mighty and majestic, about what the people of Musa said when his people said to him what they said, from their words: "Indeed we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here." He said at that, and he was angry at their saying to him, supplicating: "O Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother." He means by that: I am not able to compel anyone to what I love and desire of Your obedience and of following Your command and Your prohibition, except myself and my brother.

* *

It is from the speech of the speaker: "I do not possess any of the matter except such-and-such," meaning: I am not able to do anything other than that.

* *

By his saying, "so part us from the defiantly disobedient people," he means: judge between us and them with a judgment from You that You pass concerning us and them, so that You distance them from us.

* *

It is from the speech of the speaker: "I separated between these two things," meaning: I divided between them, from the words of the rajaz poet:

O Lord, so part him and me,
As much as You parted two.

[The commentator's note: this is probably the rajaz of Hubayna ibn Tarif al-Ukli, who had a long account with Layla al-Akhyaliyya. Abu Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an (1:160) has it this way. The manuscript reads "O Lord, so part" and the printed edition corrected it to match Majaz al-Qur'an. I did not find the rajaz in this exact wording. The poem in this transmission has no witness value.]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

11686 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "so part us from the defiantly disobedient people," he says: judge between us and them.

11687 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "so part us from the defiantly disobedient people," he says: judge between us and them.

11688 – Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Musa (ﷺ) became angry when the people said to him, "So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here." So he invoked against them and said, "My Lord, indeed I do not possess except myself and my brother, so part us from the defiantly disobedient people." And it was a hastiness from Musa, which he was hasty about.

11689 – It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: "so part us from the defiantly disobedient people," he says: judge between us and them, and open between us and them. All of this, the man says: "judge between us."

So Allah's judgment between him and them was that He named them "defiantly disobedient."

* *

By His saying "the defiantly disobedient," He means those who went out from faith in Allah and in Him to disbelief in Allah and in Him.

* *

We have already shown, in what has passed, that the meaning of "fisq" is going out from one thing to another, in a way that suffices without repeating it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 26 (part 1 of 2):**

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿He said, "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about what governs "the forty" (al-arba'in).

Some of them said: What governs it is His words, "forbidden" (muharramah). God, may His majesty and praise be exalted, only forbade to those people of the folk of Moses who disobeyed Him, opposed His command, and refused to fight the tyrants [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "God forbade to the people..." The context requires what is given here, with "upon" added.]] the entering of their city for forty years. [[The word "entering" (dukhul) is in the accusative as the object of "forbade." The printed edition had "and the entering of their city," which is an undoubted error, and the sentence does not stand.]] Then He conquered it for them and settled them in it, and destroyed the tyrants after a battle waged by them, after the forty years had passed and they had come out of the wandering. [[The printed edition has "after the forty years had been completed," which differs from the manuscript for no reason.]]

1169o0 [number 11690]: Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: When the people said what they said, and Moses invoked against them, God revealed to Moses: "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land, so do not grieve over the defiant people." They were then, as is mentioned, six hundred thousand fighting men. He made them "defiant" because of their disobedience. They remained for forty years within a distance of six farsakhs, or less, walking each day earnestly in order to get out of it, until they grew weary and alighted, and behold, they were in the same dwelling from which they had set out. [[The printed edition has "until they reached evening and alighted," and I have kept the manuscript reading, which is correct.]] They complained to Moses of what had been done to them, so He sent down to them the manna and the quails, and they were given clothing that remained with them, so that a youth who grew up would be with it in the same form. [[His words "that remained with them" seem to mean that their garments did not wear out but kept lasting. The printed edition and the manuscript had "grew up" without a waw, and I added it because the context requires it.]] Moses asked his Lord to give them water, so there was brought the stone of Sinai, a white stone, which, whenever the people alighted, he struck with his staff, and there gushed from it twelve springs, for each tribe a spring, "each people knew their drinking place." Then, when the forty years were over, and it had been a punishment for what they had transgressed and disobeyed, He revealed to Moses: "Command them to proceed to the holy land, for God has sufficed them against their enemy. Tell them that when they come to the sanctuary they should enter by the gate, prostrate when they enter, and say 'hittah' [forgive us]." Their saying "hittah" meant that their sins be removed from them. But most of the people refused and disobeyed, and they prostrated on their cheeks and said "hintah" (wheat). Then God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿But those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from heaven because they defiantly transgressed﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 59]. [[This report: 11690. It seems to be the report whose chain Abu Ja'far mentioned previously without completing it, number 993. I do not know whether he did that for brevity or whether the report fell out from there.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, what governs "the forty" is "they will wander bewildered in the land." They said: The meaning of the speech is: He said, "It is forbidden to them forever; they will wander bewildered in the land for forty years." They said: No one among those who said, "We will never enter it so long as they are in it; so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here," entered the city of the tyrants, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, forbade it to them. They said: Only Joshua and Caleb entered it from those people, the two who said to them, "Enter upon them by the gate, for when you have entered it, you will be the victors," along with the children of those whom God forbade to enter it, and God caused them to wander, so none of them entered it.

Mention of those who said that:

1169 1 [number 11691]: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, saying: Abu Hilal told us, from Qatadah, concerning the words of God, may His majesty be exalted, "It is forbidden to them": he said: forever.

11692: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, saying: Abu Hilal told us, from Qatadah, concerning God's words, "they will wander bewildered in the land": he said: forty years.

11693: Al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Harun al-Nahwi told us, saying: al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit told me, from Ikrimah, concerning His words, "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land": he said: the prohibition is the wilderness (al-tih). [[Report 11693: "Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Azdi al-Farahidi." "Harun al-Nahwi" is "Harun ibn Musa al-Azdi," al-A'war. "Al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharrit." All are trustworthy and passed earlier together under number 4985. This report Abu Ja'far narrated in his History 1: 225, 226. In the printed edition here it read "the prohibition, without end," which is a very reprehensible alteration. In the manuscript it reads "the prohibition, the endpoint," and I preferred the reading "al-tih" (the wilderness). It is said: "a land of tih and tihā'," and it is said that "tih" is the plural of "tihā'," which is the desert in which one gets lost. In Tabari's History 1: 226 it reads: "the prohibition: the wandering (al-tih)."]]

11694: Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, who said: Moses became angry at his people and invoked against them, saying: "My Lord, I have no power except over myself and my brother," the verse, and God, may His majesty and praise be exalted, said: "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land." When the wandering was imposed upon them, Moses regretted it. His people who had been obeying him [with him] came to him and said to him: "What have you done to us, Moses!" So they remained in the wandering. When they came out of the wandering, the manna and quails were lifted, and they ate from the herbs. Moses met 'Awj, [[In the printed edition: "'Awaj" in this place and everywhere that follows; I have kept the manuscript reading.]] and Moses leapt into the sky ten cubits, [[In the printed edition: "then he leapt"; the editor had not read the manuscript well, since it is undotted. "Nazā yanzū nazwan" means to leap. It is as I have written it in Tabari's History 2: 223.]] for his staff was ten cubits and his height was ten cubits, and he struck the ankle of 'Awj and killed him. [[At this point ends what Abu Ja'far narrated in his History 1: 223. [[The parenthetical addition here is from the History of Tabari, and the sentence cannot stand without it.]] And none remained [among] those who refused to enter the city of the tyrants with Moses, except that he died and did not witness the conquest. Then, when the forty years had ended, God, may His majesty be exalted, sent Joshua son of Nun as a prophet, [[The printed edition has "ibn Nun."]] and he informed them that he was a prophet and that God had commanded him to fight the tyrants. They pledged allegiance to him and believed him, so he defeated the tyrants, and they stormed in upon them, killing them, [[The printed edition has "fighting them"; I kept the manuscript. In Tabari's History: "they killed them."]] so the band of the Children of Israel would gather around a man's neck, striking it without cutting it through. [[Report 11694: Abu Ja'far narrated this report in separated pieces between his History and his Tafsir, as you have seen in the earlier notes. From the place I pointed to on page 192, note 5, to this place, Abu Ja'far narrated it in the History 1: 225.]]

11695: Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham told me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Sufyan told us, saying: Abu Sa'id said, [[In the manuscript: "Abu Sa'd," which is an error; see the earlier report number 11668.]] from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God, may His majesty be exalted, said, when Moses invoked: "It is forbidden to them for forty years; they will wander bewildered in the land." [[In the printed edition: "He said: when Moses invoked, God said: 'It is forbidden...'," which differs from the manuscript, although it agrees with Tabari's History.]] He said: So they entered the wandering, and everyone who entered the wandering who had passed twenty years of age died in the wandering. [[In the manuscript: "had passed the twenty years"; the printed edition agrees with what is in the History.]]

He said: Moses died in the wandering, and Aaron died before him. He said: So they remained in their wandering for forty years, and Joshua, with those who remained with him, rose against the city of the tyrants, and Joshua conquered the city. [[Report 11695: This report Abu Ja'far narrated in his History 1: 225.]]

11696: Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, who said: God, may His praise be exalted, said: "It is forbidden to them for forty years," [the villages] were forbidden to them, so they did not alight at any village and were not able to do so; they only followed the wells for forty years, [["Al-atwa'" is the plural of "tawy" (with a fatha on the ta', a kasra on the waw, and shadda on the ya'), which is the well lined with stones. It is an adjective of the pattern "fa'il" in the sense of "maf'ul" that passed into being a noun, which is why they made its plural on the pattern "af'al," as they said: "sharif" and "ashraf," "yatim" and "aytam."]] and it is mentioned to us that Moses, peace be upon him, died during the forty years, and that none of them entered Jerusalem except their children and the two men who said what they said. [[Report 11696: Abu Ja'far narrated it in the History 1: 225, except his words "they only follow the wells."]]

11697: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: A man of knowledge of the first Book told me, who said: When the Children of Israel did what they did, [namely] their disobedience to their prophet, and their intention toward Caleb and Joshua, when they commanded them to enter the city of the tyrants, and they said to them what they said, the greatness of God appeared in the cloud over the door of the Tent of the Assemblies (qubbat al-zumar) upon all the Children of Israel. [[In the printed edition: "upon fire in which was the sign," which has no meaning. In the manuscript: "upon him the sign," all undotted; its correct reading, as I have given it, is "door," since "door of the Tent of Meeting" occurs frequently in the book of the people, as in the book of Numbers, chapter ten, for example. "Tent of Meeting" is the phrase that appears in Ibn Ishaq's report as "qubbat al-zumar." "Zumar" is the plural of "zumrah," which means group. What Ibn Ishaq narrates here corresponds in the book of Numbers, chapter fourteen: "Then the glory of the Lord appeared at the Tent of Meeting." Thus it is established that the "Tent of Meeting" is the "qubbat al-zumar." "Qubbah" among the Arabs is a round tent of leather.

This report of Ibn Ishaq, in full, is another translation of chapter fourteen of the Book of Numbers. It is useful to consult it, as I mentioned on page 183, note 2. I will endeavor to explain some of the differences of translation here.]] Then He, may His praise be exalted, said to Moses: "How long will this people disobey Me? And how long will they not believe in all the signs which I have placed among them? I will strike them with death and destroy them, and make of you a people greater and mightier than them." [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "I will strike them with death." In the book of the people it is "with pestilence," and it is not far off that the word "death" is a corruption of "pestilence."]] Moses said: "The people of Egypt from whom You brought this people by Your power will hear it, and the inhabitants of this land who have heard that You, God, are among this people, [will say]. If You kill this entire people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your name will say: 'This people was killed because they could not enter the land which He created for them, so He slew them in the wilderness.' But let Your hands be raised and Your recompense be magnified, O Lord, as You spoke and said to them: 'Your patience is long and Your blessings are many, and You forgive sins and do not destroy.' And You preserve [the sin] of the fathers upon the sons and the sons' sons to three and four generations. [[In the printed edition: "to three generations and four"; I kept the manuscript. "Al-ahqab" is the plural of "huqb" (with a damma and sukun, or two dammas), which means an age, said to be eighty years, and said to be more. As for what is between the parentheses, I have deduced it from the book of the people, since the speech is not correct without it. It is in their book: "Rather He will place the sin of the fathers upon the sons to the third and fourth generation."]] So forgive, O Lord, the iniquities of this people by the abundance of Your blessings, as You forgave them from the time You brought them out of the land of Egypt until now." Then God, may His praise be exalted, said to Moses, may God bless him: "I have forgiven them by your word, but I am living, [[In the printed edition: "But now has come that I am God," which differs from the manuscript, since its reader did not read it well. It is as I have given it, and it is also in the book of the people: "But as I live, the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord."]] and I have filled the whole earth with My praise. [But] those people who have seen My praise and My signs which I did in the land of Egypt and in the deserts, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Has not the people..." The context requires what is given here, and it has the same meaning in the book of the people.]] and tested Me ten times and did not obey Me, [[In the printed edition: "and asked Me ten times." "Ibtala" means to test; the book of the people has "and tested Me ten times."]] will not see the land which I swore to their fathers, [[In the printed edition: "which I created," which is not correct in meaning but is false. In the manuscript it is undotted, and in the book of the people it is "swore," as it appears in the manuscript's spelling, and as I have given it. The old translation agrees on this, as does this translation before us. The meaning is: the land which I swore to their fathers by My might and majesty that I would make it for their children.]] and whoever angered Me will not see it. But as for My servant Caleb, who had a spirit with Me and followed My desire, I will bring him into the land which he entered, and his offspring will see it."

[Continued:] And the Amalekites and the Canaanites were sitting in the mountains; then they rose and moved into the deserts on the road of the Sea of Suf. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "on the road of Yahrusun," which is a corruption and a distortion. The correct reading is what I have given. "Bahr Suf" is the one known as the "Red Sea," and the Arabs knew it as "Bahr al-Qulzum." "Al-Qulzum" was an ancient city near Aylah and Sinai. "Al-Suf" may be an ancient pronunciation of the Arabs' "al-Sayf" (with a kasra on the sin), which is the sea coast, and perhaps a place there was named after it, so the sea was attributed to it.]] God, may He be exalted and mighty, spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them: "How long will this band, this evil band, whisper against Me? I have heard the whisperings of the Children of Israel." ["Whispered against him" and "whispering" passed in report number 11663, and I did not explain them there.

The original root of *al-waswasah* is a sound from the wind, or the sound of ornaments, reeds and the like. *Al-waswasah* also means a hidden, confused speech that cannot be made out. "Waswasa al-rajul" means that the man spoke words he did not make clear. This is undoubtedly a translation intended to express abundant hidden and ambiguous talk, which the people pass among themselves while complaining. In the translation of the people in the book before us, the corresponding phrase is: "I have heard the complaining of the children of Israel.."[[In the Jewish book: "I have heard the complaining of the children of Israel.."]] And He said: "I will surely do to you as you have spoken to Me,"[[In the book of the people it reads thus: "I will surely do to you as you have spoken in My ears."]] "and your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness, and according to your number,"[[In the printed edition: "wa-hisabikum" (and your reckoning). I have retained what is in the manuscript, meaning: like your number, that is, all of you. In the book of the people: "all those numbered among you according to your number."]] "from twenty years old and upward, because you have murmured against Me,"[[See the explanation of "al-waswasah" above, p. 195, no. 7.]] "you shall not enter the land which I lifted [My hand] to give you a dwelling in it, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. And your little ones who did not know good from evil, they shall enter the land, and I know them. To them I will give the land which I desired for them. But your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness, and you shall wander in this wilderness according to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days, a year for each day, and you shall bear your iniquities forty years, and you shall know that you murmured before Me. I am God who does this to this assembly, the children of Israel, who gathered against Me, that in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die."[[In the printed edition: "...they have come, that I am God..... who have promised..... that they shall wander....", and I have restored what is in the manuscript. In the book of the people: "...you shall know My withdrawal. I, the LORD, have spoken; surely I will do this to all this wicked congregation that has gathered against Me. In this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die."]] Therein they shall die.

As for the men whom Moses had sent to spy out the land, who then stirred up the congregation by spreading an evil report about the land, they all died suddenly by plague; but Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh lived, of those men who went to spy out the land.

When Moses, peace be upon him, spoke all these words to the children of Israel, the people mourned greatly. They rose early and went up to the top of the mountain,[[In the printed edition: "to the top of the mountain"; I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] and said: "We will go up to the land of which He spoke, for we have sinned." But Moses said to them: "Why do you transgress the word of God? This will not succeed for you. Do not go up, for God is not among you; you will be defeated before your enemies, for the Amalekites and the Canaanites are before you, and you will fall by the sword, because you have turned away from God, and God will not be with you." Yet they presumed to go up to the mountain top; but the ark of the covenant of God and Moses did not depart from the camp,[[In the printed edition: "i.e., from the wisdom", and the correct reading is what I have given, since the "ark" was in a tent. The word in the manuscript is not clearly written. See the description of the "tent" in which the ark was kept in the dictionary of their book.]] that is, from the tent. Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and struck them, and beat them down, and destroyed them.[[This is where the fourteenth chapter of the Book of Numbers ends. It has become clear that what Ibn Ishaq narrated is another translation of this chapter. The language of Ibn Ishaq's translation differs completely from the wording of Ibn Ishaq in the rest of what he wrote of the biographies, and it contains phrases, sentences and expressions which I have no doubt were the work of an ancient translator. Muhammad ibn Ishaq died around the year 150 AH, so this translation which he related from some scholars of the First Book was undoubtedly undertaken by men before this date, that is, in the first century AH. This is an important matter, which I hope to pursue later until I establish a date for it that may reveal the truth about this ancient translation.]] So God, may His remembrance be exalted, made them wander in the wilderness forty years because of their disobedience, until those who had deserved God's disobedience in that matter had perished.

He said: When the young ones among their offspring grew up, and their fathers died, and the forty years in which they had wandered were completed,[[In the printed edition: "which they wandered (tataihu)" with two taas; I have retained what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:226.]] and Moses led them, with Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh (who, they claim, was the brother-in-law of Moses' sister Miriam, daughter of Imran, and of Aaron, being their in-law), Joshua son of Nun advanced with the children of Israel to Jericho, and entered it with them, and slew the giants who were in it. Then Moses entered it with the children of Israel, and he remained there as long as God willed, then God took him to Himself, and no creature knows his grave.[[From the beginning of his words, "When the young ones grew up," to this point, it is related in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:226.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this matter, in my view, is the saying of him who said: "the forty" is in the accusative governed by "forbidden" (muharramah), and that His words "it shall be forbidden to them for forty years" refer to all the people of Moses, not some of them to the exclusion of others. For God, may His remembrance be exalted, addressed that people in general and did not single out some of them over others. God, may His praise be exalted, fulfilled what He had promised them of punishment, and He made them wander forty years, and He forbade all of them, during the forty years in which they remained wandering, to enter the holy land, so none of them entered it, neither small nor great, neither righteous nor wicked, until the years in which God, mighty and majestic, had forbidden them to enter had ended. Then He permitted those of them who remained, and their offspring, to enter it with the Prophet of God Moses and the two men upon whom God had bestowed favor, and the Prophet of God Moses, peace be upon him, conquered the city of the giants, God willing, with Joshua at its head. This is because the scholars of the reports of the ancients agree that Og son of Anak was slain by Moses, peace be upon him.[[In the printed edition: "Og son of Anaq"; I have retained what is in the manuscript. See what has passed, that he related his name as "Aj" on p. 192, note 2.]] Had his killing occurred before their going forth into the wilderness, and he being the greatest of the giants in stature, the children of Israel would not have feared the giants with the fear that appeared in them. But that happened, God willing, after the death of the generation which feared and disobeyed its Lord, and refused to enter the city of the giants.

Furthermore: the scholars of the reports of the ancients agree that Balaam son of Beor[[In the printed edition: "Ba'urra'"; I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] was among those who aided the giants by supplication against Moses. It is inconceivable that this occurred while the people of Moses were holding back from fighting and striving against them, because aid is only needed by one who is sought; but since no one was seeking them, there is no reason for the need of it.

1169 8 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf, who said: The bed of Og was eight hundred cubits, and the stature of Moses was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits, and he leaped into the sky ten cubits, so he struck Og and hit his ankle, and he fell dead, and he became a bridge for the people who passed over him.[[In the printed edition: "ten cubits" in the three places; I have retained what is in the manuscript, and both are correct, since "dhira'" (cubit) is feminine but may also be treated as masculine.]] [[The report 11698: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:223.]]

1169 9 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The staff of Moses was ten cubits, and his leap was ten cubits, and his height was ten cubits, so he leaped and struck the ankle of Og and killed him, and it became a bridge for the people of the Nile for a year.[[In the printed edition: "ten cubits" in the three places; I have retained what is in the manuscript, and both are correct, since "dhira'" (cubit) is feminine but may also be treated as masculine.]] [[The report 11699: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:223.

Moreover, all that Abu Ja'far related of the reports about Og, and similar things that have passed concerning the enormous size of these giants, are only exaggerations which they received from the people of the earlier Book, and they saw no harm in relating them. They are false reports on which no reliance is placed.]]

* *

The meaning of "they wander (yatihun) in the land" is that they are bewildered in it and go astray. From this comes the saying about a man who strays from the path of truth: "a wanderer (tai)." Their wandering was this: they would rise every morning for forty years, striving toward a distance of about six farsakhs in order to leave that place, and by evening they would find themselves at the very spot where they had begun their journey.

1170 0 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me this, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi'.[[The report 11700: see the report that has passed, no. 11690.]]

1170 1 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The children of Israel wandered forty years; they would rise in the morning where they had been in the evening, and be in the evening where they had risen in the morning, during their wandering.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿So do not grieve over the defiant people﴾ (26)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "so do not grieve (fa-la ta'sa)," He means: do not be sad.
It is said of this: "Asiya fulan 'ala kadha ya'sa asan" and "qad asaytu min kadha," meaning: I grieved over such and such. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

Halting by them, my companions held their mounts over me,
saying: "Do not perish from grief, but take heart."[[His Diwan: 125, from his famous mu'allaqah.]]

That is: do not perish from sorrow.

* *

According to what we have said on this matter, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said this:

1170 2 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "fa-la ta'sa" means: "so do not grieve."

1170 3 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So do not grieve over the defiant people." He said: When the wandering was imposed upon them, Moses, peace be upon him, was grieved; and when he grieved, God revealed to him: "So do not grieve over the defiant people," that is, do not grieve over the people whom I have named "defiant," so he did not grieve.[[The report 11703 is part of a report that has passed long ago, no. 991. The publisher of the first printed edition omitted "fa-lam yahzan" (so he did not grieve), because in the manuscript it was "fa-la tahzan" (do not grieve); he thought it a repetition and deleted it, but it is confirmed as I have written it in the report that has passed, 991.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 27 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His, the Mighty and Majestic's, words: ﴿And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and was not accepted from the other. He said: "I will surely kill you." He said: "Allah accepts only from the righteous."﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Recite to these Jews, who intended to stretch out their hands against you, and to your companions with you, [the first printed edition's publisher misunderstood this phrase, making it "recite to these who intended to stretch out their hands against you, upon you and upon your companions with you," adding "upon you" and changing "with you" to "with them," thereby taking the speech out of Abu Ja'far's Arabic into a speech washed of its Arabic. The sense of the speech is: "Recite to these Jews... and to your companions with them." So glory be to Him who gave the publishers power over the writers!!] and inform them of the evil outcome of injustice and treachery, and the bad consequence of betrayal and breaking the covenant, [Al-khatr: it is the worst of treachery and the most vile deception. In a hadith: "No people betrayed a covenant except that the enemy was given power over them," and in the revelation: "And none deny Our signs except every treacherous ingrate." The publisher of the printed edition did not read "al-khatr" well, and put "al-jawr" (injustice) in its place.] and what is the recompense of the covenant-breaker and the reward of the one who fulfils [the covenant], [The phrase "the news of the two sons of Adam" is in the accusative, as the object of His words "recite to these Jews." What lies between the two lines is an interjected clause for clarification. See the interpretation of "yatlu" (recites) in what has preceded: 2:409, 411; 3:569; 6:86; 7:466; 7:97. And the interpretation of "naba'" (news) in what has preceded: 1:488, 489; 6:259, 404.] the news of the two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, and what the matter of the obedient one of them, who fulfilled his covenant with his Lord, came to, and what the matter of the disobedient one of them, who breached and broke his covenant, came to. [In the printed edition: "al-ja'ir" (the oppressor). See the interpretation of "al-khatr" in what has preceded, note 2. In the manuscript it is undotted.] So let the Jews, by that, know the bitter result of their treachery and their breaking of the covenant between you and them, [In the printed edition: "wa-khamat ghibb 'aduwwihim" (the bad outcome of their enemy), which is corrupt and faulty. In the manuscript it is undotted, as I have written it.] and their intention to do what they intended of stretching out their hands to you and to your companions. For you and for them [that is, the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions] in the goodness of My reward and the greatness of My recompense for fulfilling the covenant, by which I rewarded the slain one who fulfilled his covenant from the two sons of Adam, and by which I punished the killer who broke his covenant, is a beautiful consolation. [The context: "For you and for them... a beautiful consolation."]

* *

The people of knowledge differed concerning the cause of the two sons of Adam offering the offering, the cause of Allah's acceptance of what was accepted from him, and who the two who offered were.

Some of them said: That was by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to them both to offer it, and the cause of acceptance was that the one whose offering was accepted offered the best of his property, and the other offered the worst of his property. And the two who offered were the two sons of Adam from his loins: one of them Habil, and the other Qabil.

Those who said this:

11704. Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', who said: It reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer, one of them was a owner of sheep, and a lamb had been born to him among his flock, [“unnija” (passive voice), meaning: was born. And “al-hamal” (with two fathas): the young sheep.] and he loved it so much that he would prefer it at night, and would carry it on his back out of love, until he had no property more beloved to him than it. When he was commanded to offer, he offered it to Allah, and Allah accepted it from him. It kept grazing in Paradise until Ibrahim's son was ransomed with it, may Allah's blessings be upon them both. [Report 11704: “Hisham ibn Sa'd al-Madani,” trustworthy, though they spoke about him regarding his memory; he passed as no. 5490. In the printed edition here was “ibn Sa'id,” and the correct form is from the manuscript. “Isma'il ibn Rafi' ibn 'Uwaymir al-Madani al-Qass,” very weak; he passed as no. 4039.]

11705. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Awf told us, from Abu al-Mughira, from Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The two sons of Adam who offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other, one of them was an owner of tillage, and the other an owner of sheep. And they were commanded to offer an offering. The owner of sheep offered the most noble, fattest, and finest of his sheep, giving his soul willingly. And the owner of tillage offered the worst of his tillage, [al-kawzan, and al-zuwan.] —“al-kawzan”, thus in the printed edition and the manuscript; in the History of al-Tabari it is “al-kawdhar,” and I did not find it in anything before me of the books. What I found is that “al-dawsar” is a plant like the plants of crops, having a spike and fine dark grain, found in wheat, and it is said to be “al-zuwan.” And “al-zuwan” (with a damma on the z) is what comes out of food and is thrown away, which is the bad part of it. It is said: it is a grain mixed with wheat, which the people of al-Sham call “al-shaylam.”—not giving his soul willingly. And Allah accepted the offering of the owner of sheep, and did not accept the offering of the owner of tillage. Their story was what Allah related in His Book. And he said: By Allah, the one killed was indeed the stronger of the two men, but scrupulousness prevented him from stretching out his hand against his brother. [Report 11705: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1:71, and it will come as no. 11727, abridged. In the printed edition here: “an yabsut yadahu ila akhihi” (that he stretch out his hand to his brother), with an added “yadahu”, which is not in the manuscript, nor in the History, nor in this report that he will narrate again later.]

* *

Others said: That was not from their own command by Allah's command to them.

Those who said this:

11706. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Their case was that there was no poor person who was given charity, and the offering was only offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said: "If only we offered an offering!" When a man offered an offering and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was pleased with it, He sent a fire to him which consumed it. And if Allah was not pleased with it, the fire died down. So they offered an offering: one of them was a shepherd, and the other a farmer. The owner of sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crop. [In the printed edition: “abghada zar'ahu” (the worst of his crop), which differs from the manuscript, and agrees with the History. By his words “some of his crop” he means what happened to him, not chosen as his brother chose. It is like his words in report no. 11709: “a crop from his crop.”] Then the fire came and descended between them, and consumed the sheep and left the crop. And the son of Adam said to his brother: "Will you walk among the people, when they know that you offered an offering and it is accepted from you, and mine is rejected? By Allah, people will not look at me and at you, while you are better than me!!" He said: "I will surely kill you!" His brother said to him: "What is my fault? Allah only accepts from the righteous." [Report 11706: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1:71, and it will come as no. 11750, with an addition at the end.]

11707. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih told us, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: "When they offered an offering," he said: The two sons of Adam, Habil and Qabil, of Adam's loins. One of them offered a sheep, and the other offered herbage. The offering of the owner of the sheep was accepted, so his companion killed him.

11708. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

11709. Al-Harith told me, saying: Abd al-Aziz told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they offered an offering," he said: Habil and Qabil. Habil offered a she-goat, one of the best of his flock, and Qabil offered a crop from his crop. He said: The fire consumed the she-goat and did not consume the crop. So he said: "I will surely kill you!" He said: "Allah only accepts from the righteous."

11710. Al-Harith told me, saying: Abd al-Aziz told us, saying: a man told us, who heard Mujahid regarding His words: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they offered an offering," he said: It is Habil and Qabil, of Adam's loins. They offered an offering: one of them offered a sheep from his flock, and the other offered herbage. The offering of the owner of the sheep was accepted, so he said to his companion: "I will surely kill you!" And he killed him. So Allah tied one of his legs by its shin to its thigh until the Day of Resurrection, and made his face turn toward the sun wherever it turned, with a fence of ice upon him in winter, and a fence of fire upon him in summer, and with him seven angels: whenever one angel departs, another comes.

11711. Sufyan told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan = [and] Hannad told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other," he said: This one offered a ram, and this one offered a heap of food, [“al-sabr” (with a damma on the s and a fatha on the b), the plural of “sabra” (with a damma then sukun): a heap of food without measure or weight. It is said: “I bought the thing sabra,” meaning without measure or weight. In the printed edition: “sabra,” and I have restored what is in the manuscript.] so it was accepted from one of them. He said: It was accepted from the owner of the sheep, and was not accepted from the other.

11712. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they offered an offering, and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other," he said: There were two men of the sons of Adam; it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other.

11713. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Ubayd Allah told us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Ata': "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth," he said: One of them was named Qabil and the other Habil. One was an owner of sheep and the other an owner of crops. This one offered a lamb from the best of his sheep, and this one offered from the worst of his crop. [In the printed edition: “min ardi'a zar'ihi” (from the most wretched of his crop)?—the printed edition has "min aradi'a zar'ihi" in a corrupt form; I have restored what is in the manuscript.] He said: So fire descended and consumed the lamb, and he said to his brother: "I will surely kill you!"

11714. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salama told us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of knowledge of the first Book: that Adam ordered his son Qabil to marry his sister, Habil's twin, and ordered Habil to marry his sister, Qabil's twin. [In the printed edition in both places: "tawwama" (twin). I have restored the manuscript. In the History of al-Tabari: "tawwamatuhu". "Al-tawam", "al-tu'am" and "al-tu'am" (with a kasra or sukun), are of all animals: the one born together with another in one womb, from two upward, male or female, or a male with a female. It is also said: "tawam" for the male, and "tawama" for the female. In the manuscript and the printed edition, in all places, it is "Qabil." But in the History it is in all places "Qayn" in place of "Qabil," and they are one. So I left what is in the printed edition and the manuscript as it is, even if it differs from what Abu Ja'far narrated in the History.] So Habil submitted and was content with that, but Qabil refused and disliked it, out of pride regarding Habil's sister, and he turned away from Habil's sister and said: We are the offspring of Paradise, and they are of the offspring of the earth, and I have more right to my sister! = And some people of knowledge of the first Book say: Qabil's sister was one of the most beautiful people, so he begrudged her to his brother and wanted her for himself. Allah knows best which of these was the case. So his father said to him: "My son, she is not lawful for you!" But Qabil refused to accept this from his father's words. His father said to him: "My son, then offer an offering, and your brother Habil will offer an offering, and whichever of you Allah accepts his offering, he has more right to her." Qabil was in charge of sowing the land, and Habil was in charge of tending the livestock. Qabil offered wheat, and Habil offered the firstborn of his flock = and some say: he offered a cow. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent a white fire which consumed Habil's offering and left Qabil's offering, and by that the offering was known to be accepted when it was accepted. [Report 11714: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1:70.]

11715. Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi as he related, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas = and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud = and from some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): No child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, [In the printed edition: "kana.." without a waw; I have restored the manuscript.] so he would marry the boy of one womb to the girl of another womb, and marry the girl of one womb to the boy of the other womb, until two sons were born to him, called Qabil and Habil. Qabil was an owner of tillage, and Habil was an owner of livestock. Qabil was the elder of the two, and he had a sister more beautiful than Habil's sister. Habil asked to marry Qabil's sister, but Qabil refused and said: She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I have more right to marry her! So his father ordered him to marry her to Habil, but he refused. They offered an offering to Allah to see which of them had more right to the girl. Adam at that time had gone away from them to Mecca to look at it. Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, said to Adam: "O Adam, do you know that I have a House on the earth?" He said: "No, O Allah!" He said: "Indeed I have a House in Mecca, so go to it." So Adam said to the sky: "Guard my son with trust," but it refused. He said to the earth, and it refused. He said to the mountains, and they refused. And he said to Qabil, and he said: "Yes, you go and return, and you will find your family as will please you." When Adam set out, they offered an offering. Qabil used to boast over him, saying: "I have more right to her than you; she is my sister, and I am older than you, and I am the executor of my father!" When they offered, Habil offered a fat young ram, [“al-jadha'a” from sheep and goats: a young one that has not completed its year.] and Qabil offered a bundle of ears of grain; he found among them one great ear, and he rubbed it and ate it. Then fire descended and consumed Habil's offering, and left Qabil's offering. He became angry and said: "I will surely kill you, so that you will not marry my sister!" Habil said: "Allah only accepts from the righteous." [Report 11715: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History 1:68, 69.]

11716. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth," it was mentioned to us that they were Habil and Qabil. As for Habil, he was an owner of livestock; he aimed at the best of his livestock and offered it, and fire descended upon him and consumed it. And when an offering was accepted from them, fire would descend upon it and consume it; and if it was rejected from them, the birds and beasts of prey would eat it. As for Qabil, he was an owner of crops; he aimed at the most wretched of his crop and offered it, and fire did not descend upon him. So at that he envied his brother and said: "I will surely kill you!" He said: "Allah only accepts from the righteous."

11717. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth," he said: They are Habil and Qabil. He said: One of them was an owner of crops and the other an owner of livestock. One of them brought the best of his property, and the other brought the worst of his property. Then fire came and consumed the offering of one of them, who was Habil, and left the offering of the other. So he envied him and said: "I will surely kill you!"

11718. Sufyan told us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "When they offered an offering," he said: This one offered crops, and that one offered a she-goat, and the fire left the crops and consumed the she-goat. ["Al-'anaq": the female of goats, as long as it has not completed a year.]

* *

Others said: The two who offered an offering, whose story Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, related in this verse, were two men from the Children of Israel, not from the offspring of Adam's loins.

Those who said this:

11719. Ibn Waki' told us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf told us, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan, who said: The two men in the Qur'an, of whom Allah said: "And recite to them the news of the two sons of Adam, in truth," were from the Children of Israel, and they were not sons of Adam by his loins; the offering was only among the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die. [Report 11719: "Sahl ibn Yusuf al-Anmati," who narrated from Ibn 'Awn, 'Awf al-A'rabi, Humayd al-Tawil, and others. Ahmad, Yahya ibn Ma'in, Muhammad ibn Bashshar, and others narrated from him. He is in the biographical entries of al-Tahdhib. This report was narrated by Abu Ja'far in his History 1:71. The refutation of what al-Hasan said will come later, pp. 219, 220.]

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 27 (part 2 of 2):
