Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this matter, in my view, is that the two who offered the offering were the two sons of Adam from his own loins, not from his descendants among the Children of Israel. This is because Allah, mighty and majestic, is exalted above addressing His servants with something that gives them no benefit, and those addressed by this verse knew that the offering brought near to Allah was only from the children of Adam, to the exclusion of the angels, the devils, and the rest of creation other than them. Since this was known to them, it follows that if "the two sons of Adam" whom Allah mentioned in His Book were not intended to be his two sons from his own loins, His mentioning them, may His majesty be exalted, would have given them no benefit they did not already have. And since it is impossible that He should address them with an address that conveys no meaning to them, it is known that by "the two sons of Adam" He meant [the two sons of Adam from his own loins], not the sons of his sons whose lineage is remote from him, [[In the printed edition, without the addition between the brackets. As for the manuscript, the sentence was not sound; it was written thus: "that He meant by the two sons of Adam from his own loins the sons of his sons whose lineage is remote from him." The correct reading is the addition I have made between the brackets, and the addition of "la" (not) as was done in the previous printed edition.]] with the consensus of the scholars of reports, histories, and the knowledge of interpretation, that they were the two sons of Adam from his own loins, in the time and age of Adam, and that is sufficient as evidence.
* *
We have mentioned many of those from whom this view is expressly reported, and we will mention many who have not been mentioned, if Allah wills.
1. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Hassam ibn al-Mișakk narrated to us, from Ammar al-Duhni, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained a hundred years grieving, not laughing. Then he was brought and it was said to him: "May Allah greet you and cause you to be happy!" He said: "Bayyaka" [i.e. "may He cause you to be happy" in the sense of being a pleasing gift?], which made you laugh. [[Report 11720: "Hassam ibn Misak ibn Zalim ibn Shaytan al-Azdi." He narrated from al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and Nafi' the client of Ibn Umar. Narrated from him Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Hushaym, Yazid ibn Harun, and others. They declared him weak, until Ibn Ma'in said: "He was frequently mistaken, grossly erring, until he went beyond the limit of being used as a proof." Biography in al-Tahdhib.]]
2. Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam wept and said:
The lands have changed, and whoever is upon them,
So the color of the earth is dusty and ugly.
Every thing of color and taste has changed,
And the brightness of the beautiful face has diminished.
Then Adam, peace be upon him, was answered:
O Abu Habil, both have been killed together,
And the living has become like the slaughtered dead.
He came with a boldness he once had,
Upon fear, so he came shouting with it. [[Report 11721: "Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Kufi." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "A liar, wicked." Khalid ibn al-Hayyaj said: "I heard my father say: I saw Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim; even if a crow had flown over his head, he would have come with a hadith about it! He said: he was a liar who fabricated hadith from his own mind." Biography in al-Kabir 4/1/109, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/57, and in Lisan al-Mizan and Mizan al-I'tidal.
In the manuscript and the printed edition, "from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim" dropped out of the chain, and I added it from Abu Ja'far's chain in his history 1:72, where he narrated the report.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for the matter of their offering what they offered, the correct statement is that it should be said: Allah, mighty is His remembrance, informed His servants about the two that they had offered, and He did not inform that their offering what they offered was by a command from Allah to them, nor not by His command. It is possible that it was by Allah's command to them to do so, and it is possible that it was not by His command. However, whichever it was, they offered it only seeking nearness to Allah, if Allah wills.
* *
As for the interpretation of His words, "He said: I will surely kill you," its meaning is: the one whose offering was not accepted said to the one whose offering was accepted, "I will surely kill you," so the mention of "the one whose offering was accepted" and "the one whose offering was rejected" was omitted, being sufficient with what had already been mentioned of them, to avoid repeating it. Likewise, the mention of "the one whose offering was accepted" was omitted along with His words, "He said: Allah only accepts from the righteous."
* *
A report similar to what we have said on this has been related from Ibn Abbas.
3. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "He said: I will surely kill you." His brother said: What is my fault? Allah only accepts from the righteous. [[Report 11722: this is the conclusion of the earlier report numbered 11706.]]
4. Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words, "Allah only accepts from the righteous," he said: He says: If you had feared Allah in your offering, it would have been accepted from you; you brought an offering adulterated with the worst of what you had, and I brought an offering that is good, with the best of what I had. He said: And he [Cain] had said: Allah accepts from you and does not accept from me!
* *
By His words, "from the righteous," He means those who fear Allah and dread Him, by performing what He imposed on them of His obligations and avoiding what He forbade them of disobedience. [[See the explanation of "ittaqa" in the previous linguistic indices (w-q-y).]]
* *
Some scholars of interpretation have said that "the righteous" in this place are those who guarded against shirk.
Mention of who said that:
5. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, he said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak concerning His words, "Allah only accepts from the righteous," that they guard against shirk.
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "qurban (offering)" earlier, and that it is "al-fu'lan" from the saying of the speaker "qarraba," just as "al-Furqan" is "al-fu'lan" from "faraqa," and "al-'Udwan" from "'adā." [[See what has passed, 7:448.]]
* *
The offerings of the past nations before our community were like the charities and zakat among us, except that their offerings were known, as it is reported, by which offering was accepted and which was not accepted, by the fire consuming what was accepted, and the fire leaving what was not accepted. [[See the two earlier reports: 8310, 8311.]] And "qurban" in our community refers to righteous deeds: prayer, fasting, charity to the needy, and paying the obligatory zakat. There is no way to know in this world which of them is accepted and which is rejected. [[The pronoun in "lahā" refers to "ummatunā" (our community).]]
* *
It is reported about Amir ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari that when death approached him he wept, and it was said to him: What makes you weep? You were such-and-such! He said: What makes me weep is that I hear Allah say: "Allah only accepts from the righteous."
6. Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muqaddami narrated to me this, he said: Sa'id ibn Amir narrated to me, from Hammam, from one he named, from Amir. [[Report 11725: "Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Ata al-Muqaddami," previously mentioned under numbers 6225 and 6809. "Sa'id ibn Amir al-Dab'i," trustworthy and reliable. Biography in al-Tahdhib. "Hammam" is "Hammam ibn Yahya ibn Dinar al-Azdi," trustworthy and truthful. Biography in al-Tahdhib. "Amir ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari" is "Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd Qays al-Anbari," also said to be "Amir ibn Abd Qays," one of the eight ascetics, who were: Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd Qays, Uways al-Qarani, Harim ibn Hayyan, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Masruq ibn al-Ajda', al-Aswad ibn Yazid, Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, and al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri. See his biography in Hilyat al-Awliya' 2:87-95, and Kitab al-Zuhd of Ahmad ibn Hanbal: 218-228. I did not find this report in his reports in the two books.]]
* *
Some of them have said: The offering of the righteous is the prayer.
7. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Imran ibn Sulayman, from Adi ibn Thabit, who said: The offering of the righteous is the prayer. [[Report 11726: "Imran ibn Sulayman al-Qaysi," mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. Biography in Lisan al-Mizan. "Adi ibn Thabit al-Ansari," trustworthy, except that he had Shi'i leanings. He died in the year 116. Biography in al-Tahdhib.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 28:

The interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you. Indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the slain one of the two sons of Adam, that he said to his brother, when his brother who was the killer said to him, "I will surely kill you": ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me﴾, meaning, if you extend your hand toward me, ﴿I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you﴾, meaning, I am not one who extends his hand toward you [[See the explanation of "basṭ" (stretching out) above, p. 100.]] to kill you.

* *

Scholars have differed about the reason why the slain one said this to his brother, and did not prevent what he did to him. Some of them said: he said that to inform his brother, the killer, that he did not consider it lawful to kill him, nor to stretch out his hand against him in a way Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had not permitted him.

[[In the printed edition: "bima lam ya'dhan Allah bihi" (by what Allah had not permitted), omitting what is established in the manuscript; I do not know why this was done!!]]

Those who said this:

11727 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from Abu al-Mughirah, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that he said: By Allah, the slain man was indeed the stronger of the two men, but scruple prevented him from stretching out his hand against his brother.

[[The report 11727 appeared earlier in full as no. 11705, see the comment there.]]

11728 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you﴾, meaning: I will not retaliate, and I will surely withhold my hand from you.

* *

Others said: he did not prevent him from what he intended of killing him, and said what he said to him, as Allah related in His Book: [except that] Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, had decreed upon them that one who is intended to be killed by another should not resist the one who wishes to do so.

[[The addition in brackets is necessary for the syntax of this sentence.]]

Those who said this:

11729 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: a man who heard Mujahid say, regarding His words: ﴿If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand toward you to kill you﴾, Mujahid said: it had been prescribed for them that when a man wished to kill another man, he would leave him and not resist him.

[[In the printed edition: "kataba Allah 'alayhim" (Allah had prescribed for them), but I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views on this matter is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, had forbidden them to kill a soul without a soul, unjustly, and the slain one said to his brother: ﴿I shall not stretch my hand toward you if you stretch your hand toward me﴾, because it was just as forbidden for him to kill his brother as it was forbidden for his brother the killer to kill him. As for refraining from killing him when he intended to kill him, there is no evidence that when the killer intended to kill him and resolved upon it, the slain one knew what he was resolved upon and attempting, and so left off repelling him from himself. Rather, a group of the people of knowledge have mentioned that he killed him by ambush, having stalked him while he slept, and crushed his head with a rock. [[See the following reports, nos. 11746–11749.]] Since that is possible, and there is no indication in the verse that he was commanded to leave off preventing his brother from killing him, it is not permissible to claim what is not in the verse, except with proof that must be accepted.

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, it means: I fear Allah regarding the stretching out of my hand toward you, if I were to stretch it to kill you, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: the Owner of all creation, that He would punish me for stretching my hand toward you. [[See the explanation of "rabb" (Lord) and "al-'alamun" (the worlds) in the earlier lexical indices.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 29:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your own sin and thus be among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin of killing me, and your sin in disobeying Allah and your other disobediences." [[In the printed edition: "and your sin in disobeying Allah with other than that of your disobediences," which is a statement that does not hold together; there is no doubt that the correct reading is what I have set down.]]

Mention of those who said this:

11730 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me [[In the printed edition: "Muhammad ibn Harun," which is an undoubted error; its correct form is in the manuscript.]] who said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi in his report, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas; and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud; and from some companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," meaning: the sin of my killing, along with your sin which is upon your neck, "and thus be among the companions of the Fire."

11731 - Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he said: by your killing me, and your sin before that.

11732 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he said: with the sin of my killing and your sin.

11733 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he says: I wish that upon you would be your wrongdoing and my blood, that you would bear both of them together.

11734 - al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he says: I wish that you would bear your killing of me, "and your sin," he said: by what was from you before that.

11735 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he said: As for "your sin," it is the sin that he committed before the killing of the soul, meaning his brother; and as for "his sin," it is his killing of his brother.

* *

It is as if the proponents of this view directed the interpretation of His words, "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," to: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear the sin of my killing" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "that is: indeed I wish..", and the correct reading is what I have set down.]], so "the killing" was omitted and "the sin" was mentioned alone, since its meaning was understood by those addressed.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin, so that you bear its burden, and your sin in killing me." This is a view I found from Mujahid, and I fear it is an error, because the sound transmission from him is what we have already mentioned.

Mention of those who said this:

11736 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin and your sin," he says: I wish that upon you would be my sin and my blood, so that you would bear both of them together.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding this is that it should be said: its interpretation is: "Indeed, I wish that you would turn away with your sin in killing me" [[See the explanation of "bā'" (to bear/return) above, 2:138, 7:116, 7:366, and the explanation of "al-ithm" (sin) in the lexical indices.]] — and that is the meaning of His words, "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin." As for the meaning of "and your sin," it is his sin apart from his killing, namely his disobedience to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, in deeds other than that.

We said that this is the correct view because of the consensus of the people of interpretation upon it. For Allah, exalted is His remembrance, has informed us that every doer, his deed's recompense is for him or against him. And if that is His ruling among His creatures, it is not permissible that the sins of the slain be taken from the killer; rather the killer is taken for his sin of unlawful killing and all the other sins of disobedience he committed himself, not for what his victim carried.

* *

If someone says: Is not the killing of a human being by another a disobedience to Allah on the part of the killer? It is said: Yes, and how great a disobedience it is!

If he says: If it is a disobedience to Allah, mighty and majestic, how could the slain want that for him and say, "Indeed, I wish that you would bear my sin," when you have stated that its interpretation is: "Indeed, I wish that you would bear the sin of my killing"? [It is said:] its meaning is: Indeed, I wish that you would bear the sin of my killing if you kill me, for I do not kill you; but if you kill me, then I wish that you would bear the sin of your disobedience to Allah in killing me. And if he kills him, then he will undoubtedly bear it by the judgment of Allah, so his wishing that does not necessitate his entering into error.

* *

By His words, "and thus be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers," he means: "and thus be, by your killing me, among the inhabitants of the Blazing Fire and its eternal fuel" [[See the explanation of "companions of the Fire" above, 2:286, 4:317, 5:429, 6:14, 7:133-134.]] — "and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers," meaning: and the Fire is the reward of those who abandon the path of truth, who deviate from the straight way, and who transgress what was allotted to them toward what was not allotted to them. [[See the explanation of "jaza'" and "al-zalimun" above in the lexical indices.]]

This indicates that Allah, exalted is His remembrance, had commanded and forbidden Adam after He sent him down to the earth, and promised and threatened. Had that not been so, the slain would not have said to the killer, "and thus be among the companions of the Fire" by killing me, nor would he have informed him that that is the recompense of the wrongdoers. Mujahid used to say: One of the killer's legs is tied to its shank at the thigh from that day until the Day of Resurrection, and his face is toward the sun wherever it turns; in summer he has an enclosure of fire upon him, and in winter an enclosure of ice upon him.

11737 - al-Qasim narrated to us with this, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said that. He said: And Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Indeed we find that the son of Adam, the killer, shares with the people of the Fire a precise share of punishment, upon him is half of their punishment." [[The report: 11737 — Abu Ja'far narrated it earlier under number 11710, by another route. This addition from Abdullah ibn Amr is not in it.]]

* *

And there has been reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, similar to what was reported from Abdullah ibn Amr, a report.

11738 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us — and Sufyan narrated to us, who said: Jarir and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us — and Hannad narrated to us, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us — all of them, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "No soul is killed unjustly except that upon the first son of Adam is a portion of it, because he was the first to establish killing."

11739 - Sufyan narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to us — and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us — all of them, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.

11740 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to us, from Hasan ibn Salih, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i who said: "No one is killed unjustly except that upon the first son of Adam, and upon Satan, is a portion of it."

11741 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Hakim ibn Hakim, that he was told from Abdullah ibn Amr that he used to say: "Indeed the most wretched of men is the son of Adam who killed his brother; no blood has been shed on the earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection except that there reaches him some of it, because he was the first to establish killing."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This report which we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ shows that the view which al-Hasan stated about the two sons of Adam mentioned by Allah in this passage, that they are not sons of Adam by his loins but two men from the Children of Israel, and that the view attributed to him that the first to die was Adam, and that the offering which the fire consumed was only among the Children of Israel, is an error. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has informed about this killer who killed his brother that he was the first to establish killing. And killing certainly existed before Israel, so how could it be before his descendants! It is an error to say: the first to establish killing was a man from the Children of Israel.

Given that this is so, it is known that the correct view is the view of those who said: "He is the son of Adam by his loins," because he was the first to establish killing, so Allah made obligatory for him the punishment which we have related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So his soul made him consider the killing of his brother acceptable, and he killed him, and became among the losers﴾ (30).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "fa-taw'at" (so it made acceptable), He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: it complied with him and assisted him in it. [[In the printed edition: "fa-aqamathu wa-sa'adathu...", while in the manuscript as I have written it, though it is undotted. One says "ataytuhu 'ala hadha al-amr mu'atat" (I complied with him in this matter), if I agreed with him and obeyed him. They said: "The common people say: wataytuhu (I complied with him). They said: Do not say wataytuhu except in a dialect of the people of Yemen. Similar to it are asaytu, akaltu, and amartu. They made it a waw by softening the hamza in: yuwakil, yuwamir, and the like."]]

* *

It is from "fa''altu" (intensive form) from "al-taw'" (obedience), from the saying of the speaker: "tawa'anee hadha al-amr" (this matter became compliant to me), when it submitted to him.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation.

Some of them said: its meaning is: his soul encouraged him to kill his brother.

Those who said this:

11742 - Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi and Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid: "fa-taw'at lahu nafsuhu," he said: encouraged. [[The narration: 11742 - "Anbasa" is "Anbasa ibn Sa'id ibn al-Durays al-Asadi," who has passed many times, including nos. 224, 3356, 5385.

And "Ibn Abi Layla" is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla," who has passed many times. Nos. 32, 33, 631, 3914, 5434.

In the chain here, in the manuscript and the printed edition, it reads: "from Anbasa ibn Abi Layla," which is an undoubted error; this chain has passed many times, see for example no. 631.]]

11743 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "fa-taw'at lahu nafsuhu," he said: she encouraged him.

11744 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "fa-taw'at lahu nafsuhu qatla akhihi," he said: it encouraged him to kill his brother.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: it adorned it for him.

Those who said this:

11745 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "fa-taw'at lahu nafsuhu," he said: his soul adorned for him the killing of his brother, so he killed him.

* *

Then they differed concerning the manner of his killing him, how it was, and the cause for which he killed him.

* *

Some of them said: he found him sleeping and crushed his head with a rock.

Those who said this:

11746 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, as is mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas; and from Murra, from Abdullah; and from some men among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "fa-taw'at lahu nafsuhu qatla akhihi" — he sought him to kill him, but the boy escaped from him into the mountain peaks. Then one day he came upon him while he was tending his sheep in a mountain, and he was asleep, so he lifted a rock and crushed his head with it, and he died, and he left him in the open.

* *

And some of them said:

11747 - Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali narrated to me, saying: I heard Ash'ath al-Sijistani say: I heard Ibn Juraij say: The son of Adam who killed his companion did not know how to kill him, so Iblis appeared to him in the form of a bird, and he took a bird and cut off its head, [[In the printed edition: "faqasa'a ra'sahu," which is not correct; I have affirmed what is in the manuscript. He meant "cut its head," teaching him cutting the head in killing, then teaching him crushing in killing. Two forms of killing.]] then placed it between two stones and crushed its head, and so he taught him killing.

11748 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: He killed him where he was tending the sheep. He came to him, and did not know how to kill him, [[In the printed edition: "fa-ata," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript.]] so he twisted his neck and seized his head. Then Iblis descended, took an animal or a bird, placed its head on a rock, then took another rock and crushed its head with it, while the son of Adam, the killer, watched. Then he took his brother, placed his head on a rock, and took another rock and crushed his head with it.

11749 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: A man narrated to us who heard Mujahid say, and he mentioned something similar.

11750 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the fire consumed the offering of the son of Adam whose offering was accepted, the other said to his brother: Will you walk among people when they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you, while mine was rejected? By God, people will not look at me or at you, and you are better than me! So he said: "I will surely kill you." His brother said to him: What is my fault? "Indeed, Allah accepts only from the righteous." He threatened him with the Fire, but he did not desist nor restrain himself. "So his soul made him consider the killing of his brother acceptable, and he killed him, and became among the losers." [[The narration: 11750 - it has passed in parts as nos. 11706, 11722.]]

11751 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym informed me, saying: I went out with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, throwing the pebbles at the Jamrah, and he was veiled, leaning on my hand, until when we came opposite the place of Samura al-Sawwaf, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "bi-manzil Samura al-Surraf" with a raa, and I have affirmed what is in Tarikh al-Tabari. I do not know what this is, as I have found no place with this name in the references available to me. "Samura al-Sarraf" is the name of a man, and I do not know who he is.]] he stopped and related to me from Ibn Abbas, who said: He forbade that a man marry a woman whose brother is her twin, and marry her to another of her brothers. Every birth would produce a man and a woman. A beautiful woman was born, and an ugly, unattractive woman was born. The brother of the ugly one said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they offered an offering, and it was accepted from the owner of the ram, but was not accepted from the owner of the crops, so he killed him. That ram remained held by Allah, mighty and majestic, until He brought it out as a ransom for Isaac, and he slaughtered it on this rock at Thabir, at the place of Samura al-Sawwaf, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "bi-manzil Samura al-Surraf" with a raa, and I have affirmed what is in Tarikh al-Tabari...]] which is on your right when you throw the pebbles. Ibn Juraij said: Others related a similar story. He said: The children of Adam continued in this practice until four fathers had passed, then he married his paternal uncle's daughter, and the marriage of sisters ceased. [[The narration: 11751 - Abu Ja'far narrated it in his history 1:69.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is that it should be said: Allah, mighty is His remembrance, has informed us that the killer killed his brother, and we have no report that conclusively establishes the manner of his killing him. It is possible that it was as al-Suddi mentioned in his report, and it is possible that it was as Mujahid mentioned, and Allah knows best which of these it was. Only, the killing certainly took place.

* *

As for His saying: "fa-asbaha min al-khasirin," its interpretation is: the killer of his brother, from the two sons of Adam, became among the party of the losers, who are those who sold their Hereafter for their worldly life, by preferring it over it, so they were cheated in their trade, defrauded in it, and failed in their transaction. [[See the explanation of "al-khasirin" and "al-khusran" above, p. 170, note 4, and the references there.]]

The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted and remembered: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness. He said, 'Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness?' And he became of the regretful." (5:31)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is also one of the proofs that the account of the two sons of Adam differs from what was related by 'Amr, from al-Hasan, [[Meaning the report no. 11719; see also what preceded at p. 219.]] because the two men whose characteristics God described in this verse, had they been from the Children of Israel, the killer would not have been ignorant of burying his brother and concealing his brother's nakedness. Rather, they were from the offspring of Adam through his loins, and the killer among them did not know God's way with His dead servants, [[In the manuscript: "fi 'ādih al-mawta" and in the printed edition: "fi 'ādat al-mawta," and this is words without meaning; the correct reading is what I have established.]] and he did not know what to do with his slain brother. It is mentioned that he carried him on his shoulder for a time until his corpse began to rot, [["Arah al-laḥm" means it became putrid and a foul smell rose from it.]] so God wished to teach him the way concerning the dead of His creation, and He appointed for him the two crows whose characteristics He described in His Book.

* *

Mention of reports from the people of interpretation concerning what the killer among the sons of Adam did with his slain brother after killing him.

11752 - Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Rawq al-Hamdani related to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He carried his brother in a leather bag on his neck for a year, until God, mighty and majestic, sent the two crows, and he saw them scratching, and said: "Am I unable to be like this crow?" and buried his brother. [[Report 11752: "Yahya ibn Abi Rawq" is Yahya ibn 'Atiyya ibn al-Harith al-Hamdani al-Kufi. Weak. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "not trustworthy." Biographed in Lisan al-Mizan and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/180. His father "Abu Rawq" is 'Atiyya ibn al-Harith al-Hamdani, trustworthy, no harm in him. Passed as no. 137, 9632.]]

11753 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness." God, mighty and majestic, sent a living crow to a dead crow, and the living crow began to conceal the nakedness of the dead crow. The son of Adam who killed his brother said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow?" to the end of the verse.

11754 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, as is mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, and from some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): When the boy died, he left him in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God, mighty and majestic, sent two brother crows, and they fought, and one killed the other. Then it dug for it and scattered earth over it. When he saw it, he said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness?" This is the saying of God: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness."

11755 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "scratching" (yabhathu): God sent a crow, which dug for another beside it, a dead one, while the son of Adam, the killer, was watching it, then it scratched earth over it until it covered it. [["Scratched earth over it" means it dug up the dirt over it and covered it with it.]]

11756 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "a crow scratching in the earth," until it dug for another dead one beside it, and buried it, while the son of Adam, the killer, was watching it, as it scratched over it until it buried it. He said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," to the end of the verse.

11757 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth," he said: God sent a crow to a crow, and they fought, and one killed the other, and it began to heap dirt upon it. [["Haratha 'alayhi al-turab yahthuhu hathwan" and "hathā 'alayhi al-turāb yahthīhi hathyan": he heaped it. The second is higher and more eloquent than the first. The first was mentioned, and "yahthu" will come in the following reports, so mentioning it here spares us mentioning it earlier and later.]] So he said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness, and so become of the regretful?"

11758 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to me, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth," he said: A crow came to a dead crow, and threw dirt over it until it concealed it, and the one who killed his brother said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," to the end of the verse.

11759 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyya, who said: When he killed him, he regretted, and he clasped him to himself until he putrefied, [["Arawaha al-laḥm" and "arāḥa": it became foul. See the note above at p. 224, note 4.]] and the birds and beasts gathered around him, waiting for when he would throw him down so they could eat him.

11760 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him," that God, mighty and majestic, sent it scratching in the earth. It was mentioned to us that they were two crows who fought, and one killed the other, and that [the other] — meaning the son of Adam — was watching, and the living one began to throw dirt over the dead one. At that point he said what he said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," to the verse: "...of the regretful."

11761 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: As for His words: "Then Allah sent a crow," he said: A crow killed a crow, and began to heap dirt on it, and the son of Adam who killed his brother, when he saw it, said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness, and so become of the regretful?"

11762 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness," he said: The crow concealed the crow. He said: He used to carry him on his shoulder for a hundred years, not knowing what to do with him, carrying him and setting him down on the ground, until he saw the crow bury the crow, and said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness, and so become of the regretful?"

11763 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad related to us, saying: Khalid related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik regarding God's words: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," he said: God, mighty and majestic, sent a crow, which began to scratch dirt over a dead crow. He said: At that point he said: "Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness, and so become of the regretful?"

11764 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth," God sent a living crow to a dead crow, and the living crow began to conceal the nakedness of the dead crow, and the son of Adam who killed his brother said: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," to the verse.

11765 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, as is related from some people of knowledge of the First Scripture, who said: When he killed him, he was struck with remorse, and did not know how to bury him. For, as they claim, he was the first slain of the sons of Adam and the first dead. [He said]: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow and conceal my brother's nakedness?" to the verse; [to His words: "Then indeed many of them after that in the earth are transgressors." He said]: [[I added what is between the brackets from Tarikh al-Tabari.]] The people of the Torah claim that Cain, when he killed his brother Abel, His Majesty said to him: "O Cain, where is your brother Abel?" He said: "I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?" God said to him: "Indeed the voice of your brother's blood cries to Me from the earth. Now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand. When you work the earth, it will no longer yield its produce to you, and you will be a fugitive and wanderer on the earth." Cain said: "My sin is too great to be forgiven!" [[In the manuscript: "He said, 'And who is my sin too great?'" and its correct form is "Qayn said: My sin is too great..." as in Tarikh, but the manuscript here followed writing "Qabil" in place of "Qayn," so the first editor of the tafsir wrote "Qabil said," which is good.]] "You have driven me out today from the face of the earth, and I will hide from before You, and I will be a fugitive and wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me!" God, mighty and majestic, said: "It is not so; whoever kills a slain will not be repaid with one, seven; but whoever kills Cain will be repaid seven-fold," [[This sentence in the printed edition read: "and whoever kills a killer will be repaid one, but will be repaid seven," which is utterly corrupt; I corrected it from Tarikh al-Tabari, but I followed the manuscript in placing "Qabil" for "Qayn," so I wrote "whoever kills Qabil."]] and God placed a sign on Cain, lest anyone who found him kill him, and Cain went out from before God, mighty and majestic, from the east of Eden, the Garden. [[The report 11765: this which Ibn Ishaq related from the words of the people of the Torah is found in their book in Genesis, in chapter 4, and it is another translation of this paragraph from this chapter. See what preceded at p. 183, note 2.]]

11766 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Khaythama, who said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, the earth soaked up his blood, and it was cursed, so the earth has never soaked up blood since. [["Nashafat al-ard al-ma' tanshifuhu nashfan" (on the pattern of 'alima ya'lamu): it drank it.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: God raised up for the killer—since he did not know what to do with his slain brother—"a crow scratching in the earth," that is, digging in the earth, stirring up its dirt. "To show him how to conceal his brother's nakedness," that is, to show him how to conceal his brother's corpse.

* *

It may be that by "nakedness" is meant the private parts, but the more common meaning of it is what I have mentioned, the corpse, and the interpretation of the people of interpretation came accordingly.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In that there is an omitted element, left unmentioned, relying on the indication of what was mentioned, and it is: "So He showed him by scratching in the earth for another dead crow and he buried it in it," and the killer said to his brother then: "Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this crow," which buried the other dead crow, "and conceal my brother's nakedness," so he buried him then, "and so became of the regretful," over what he had neglected of disobedience to God, mighty and majestic, in killing his brother. [[In the manuscript: "in killing his brother," and the correct is what is in the printed edition, or it may be: "in the killing of his brother."]]

* *

All that God, mighty and majestic, mentioned in these verses is a parable that God, mighty and majestic, struck for the sons of Adam, and by it He urged the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to practice pardon and forgiveness toward the Jews, who had intended to kill the Prophet (ﷺ) and killed them, of the Banu al-Nadir, when they came to them seeking help regarding the blood-money for the two men slain by 'Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri, and He, mighty and majestic, made known to them the wickedness of the disposition of their forebears, and the evil of their uprightness upon the path of truth, despite His many favors and blessings upon them. And He struck their example in their treachery, and the example of the believers in fulfilling their covenant with them and pardoning them, with the two sons of Adam who offered their offerings, whom God mentioned in these verses. Then that is an example for them to emulate the better of the two rather than the worse. And the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came accordingly.

11767 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: I said to Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah: Has it not reached you that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God, mighty and majestic, struck for you the two sons of Adam as a parable, so take the better of them and leave the worse of them"? He said: Yes.

11768 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The two sons of Adam were struck as a parable for this community, so take the good of them."

11769 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God struck for you the two sons of Adam as a parable, so take from the better of them and leave the evil." [[The reports 11767–11769: these three are mursal reports; I have not found any of them in the collections of the Sunna.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 32 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted, mentioned: ﴿Because of that, We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely; and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "Because of that," He, the Exalted, means: because of the misdeed (jarr), the wrongdoing (jarIrah) and the crime (janayah) of that one [of the two sons of Adam], that is: because of the misdeed which the killer of his brother from the two sons of Adam, whose story We have related, committed, and the crime which he perpetrated, "We prescribed for the Children of Israel."
* *
It is said of this: "ajiltu hadha al-amr" (I drew this matter toward myself), meaning: I drew it to myself and earned it, "ajaltuhu lahu ajlan," like your saying, "akhadhtuhu akhdhan" (I took it, taking). From this is the saying of the poet: [[Abu 'Ubaydah attributed it in Majaz al-Qur'an, saying: "Said al-Khanwt, who is Tawbah ibn Mudarris, of the Banu Malik ibn Sa'd ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim. He was called al-Khanwt by al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, because al-Ahnaf spoke to him but he did not answer him, out of contempt for him, so he said: 'Your companion here is al-Khanwt!' Al-Khanwt means: the arrogant one who takes himself away, who belittles people."
"Al-Khanwt" (with a kasra on the kha', a shaddah on the nun, and a sukun on the waw).
Al-Amidi mentioned it in al-Mu'talif wal-Mukhtalif, p. 68, and said: "His two brothers were killed... so he sought revenge for them... and he grieved for his two brothers with severe grief... and he would not stop weeping for his two brothers, so al-Ahnaf asked him to desist, but he refused, so he named him al-Khanwt, which is the one whom anger or weeping prevents from speaking."
Al-Tibrizi in Sharh Islah al-Mantiq, and al-Shantamari in his commentary on the Diwan of Zuhayr, attributed it to Khuwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the one mentioned in the report of Dhat al-Nuhayn.
It was added to the poetry of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma in his Diwan (Shantamari's commentary).]] 
And the people of a tent, righteous, between whom there is discord, they have fought over a quick thing, and I am the one who postpones it. [[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:163 (with references), and Sharh Islah al-Mantiq 1:14, and Sharh Shi'r Zuhayr by al-Shantamari: 33, and Lisan (ajl), and in a version of Ibn Barri, in Lisan: "And the people of a tent, safe, I afflicted them with a precious quick thing, I am the one who postpones it. And I came hastening, asking the people about their property, asking you about the thing of which you are ignorant." The first hemistich of the second verse is also reported: "So I came among those who strive, asking about them." In the manuscript: "qad isrimu" (unpointed), and the correct reading is from the references.]] By his saying, "I am the one who postpones it," he means: I am the one who draws that upon him and the one who commits it.
* *
So the meaning of the speech is: because of the crime of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly, We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever among them kills a soul unjustly, not for a soul that was killed, he is to be slain in retaliation (qisas) [[See the explanation of "kataba" above, p. 169, note 1, and the references there.]] "or for corruption in the land," meaning: or who kills a soul among them without corruption that it committed in the land, so he deserves to be killed for it. And "its corruption in the land" occurs only through warring against Allah and His Messenger and terrorizing the highway. [[See the explanation of "corruption in the land" above: 1:287, 406; 4:238, 239, 243, 424; 5:372; 6:477.]]
* *
In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said:
Mention of those who said that:
11770 – I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words, "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel": he means: because of the son of Adam who killed his brother unjustly.
* *
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: "Whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely."

Some of them said: the meaning of that is: whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever supports the arm of a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.
Mention of those who said that:
11771 – Abu 'Ammar al-Husayn ibn Huraith al-Marwazi told us, who said: al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, "Whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever supports the arm of a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely, and whoever kills a prophet or a just imam, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. [[Report 11771: "Abu 'Ammar al-Marwazi" is al-Husayn ibn Huraith ibn al-Hasan ibn Thabit. He narrated from Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fadl ibn Musa, Ibn Abi Hazim, Ibn 'Uyaynah, and others. The whole group narrated from him except Ibn Majah. Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/389, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/50.
"Al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Sinani," Abu 'Abdullah al-Marwazi. Trustworthy and firm; the whole group narrated from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Al-Husayn ibn Waqid al-Marwazi," has passed as no. 4810, 6311.]]
11772 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, who said: my father told me, who said: my paternal uncle told me, who said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words, "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he says: whoever kills one soul which I have made sacred, it is like one who kills mankind entirely. "And whoever saves it," he says: whoever abstains from killing one soul which I have made sacred, out of fear of Me, and preserves it from being killed, it is like the preservation of all mankind; meaning by that the prophets.
* *
Others said: "Whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," with regard to the sin on the one who is killed, "and whoever saves it," that is, rescues it from destruction, "it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," with regard to the one rescued.
Mention of those who said that:
11773 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, who said: Ahmad told us, who said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, as related from Abu Malik; and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas; and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from 'Abdullah; and from some companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning His words: "Whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," with regard to the one killed, he says: in sin; "and whoever saves it," rescuing it from destruction, "it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," with regard to the one rescued.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: the killer of a soul that is forbidden to be killed, his killing of it is like one who slays mankind entirely, and whoever spares it from being killed, has spared himself from having killed mankind entirely.
Mention of those who said that:
11774 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: my father told us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever refrains from killing it has saved it. "Whoever kills a soul other than for a soul, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: and whoever destroys it.
11775 – al-Harith told me, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, who said: Sufyan told us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: whoever destroys a soul, it is as if he had killed mankind entirely; and whoever saves it and is spared from its wrong, by not killing it, [[In the printed edition: "wa salima min talabiha" (from its pursuit); I have adopted the manuscript reading, which is correct.]] has been spared from the killing of all mankind.
11776 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "It is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he did not kill it, and all mankind has been spared from him, he killed no one.
11777 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: Suwayd told us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Awza'i, who said: 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah informed us: I asked Mujahid, or heard him being asked, about His words, "Whoever kills a soul, other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: Even if he killed all mankind, his recompense would be Hell, abiding therein; Allah would be angry with him, curse him, and prepare for him a great punishment. [[This is an embedding of the verse of Surat al-Nisa: 93.]]
11778 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: Suwayd told us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj by reading, from al-A'raj, [[In the printed edition: "qira'ah 'an al-A'raj"; I have adopted the manuscript.]] from Mujahid concerning His words, "It is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: The one who kills a believing soul deliberately, Allah has made his recompense Hell, and Allah is angry with him, curses him, and prepares for him a great punishment. He says: even if he killed all mankind, he would not receive more than the like of that punishment. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever kills no one, the people are relieved of him.
11779 – Sufyan told us, who said: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: he destroyed his soul. [[In the printed edition: "awbaqa nafsan"; I have adopted the manuscript.]]
11780 – Sufyan told us, who said: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: in sin.
11780 (repeated numbering) – Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Jarir told us, from Layth, from Mujahid: "Whoever kills a soul other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," and His words: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surat al-Nisa: 93], he said: he goes to Hell by killing the believer, just as if he had killed all mankind he would go to Hell.
11781 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, who said: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: it is as he said. And He said: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely": its saving is not killing a soul which Allah has forbidden; that is the one who has saved mankind entirely, meaning: whoever forbids its killing except by right, mankind is saved from him entirely.
11782 – Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Hakkam told us, from 'Anbasah, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid: "And whoever saves it," he said: whoever forbids it and does not kill it.
11783 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: my father told us, from al-'Ala', who said: I heard Mujahid say: "Whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever refrains from killing it has saved it.
11784 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, who said: Abu 'Asim told us, who said: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "It is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: it is like the one in al-Nisa: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell﴾ [Surat al-Nisa: 93], regarding its recompense.
11785 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, who said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "It is as if he had slain mankind entirely," like the one in Surat al-Nisa, ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ regarding its recompense; "and whoever saves it," and does not kill anyone, the people have been given life from him.
11786 – Hannad told us, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid concerning His words: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: he turned to his companions and said: it is this and this. [[He apparently means by "it is this and this" that killing a sacred soul without right or corruption in the land is killing all mankind, and saving it is saving all mankind.]]
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: whoever kills a soul other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, because he becomes liable to retaliation (qawad) and qisas for it, like the liability he would incur had he slain mankind entirely.
Mention of those who said that:
11787 – Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely," he said: he becomes liable for killing as if he had killed all mankind. He said: my father used to say this.
* *
Others said that the meaning of His words "and whoever saves it" is: whoever pardons one who is owed retaliation from him, and does not kill him.
Mention of those who said that:
11788 – Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he says: whoever saves it, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gives him a reward like that of one who saved all mankind; "saves it" by not killing it and pardoning it. He said: that refers to the guardian of the slain, and the slain himself pardons him before he dies. He said: my father used to say this.
11789 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, who said: Mu'ammal told us, who said: Sufyan told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan concerning His words: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever pardons.
11790 – Sufyan told us, who said: 'Abd al-A'la told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever has a close relative killed and pardons his blood. [["Al-hamim": a close relative.]]
11791 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: pardon after power.
* *
Others said: the meaning of His words "and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely" is: whoever rescues it from drowning or burning.
["Al-harq" (both vowels open): fire and its flame, like "al-hariq." In a hadith: "Burning, drowning, and being struck by the wind are martyrdom" (all with open vowels).]
Mention of those who said that:
11792 – Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: whoever rescues it from drowning, burning, or destruction.
11793 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: my father told us; and Hannad told us, who said: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "And whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," he said: from drowning, burning, or collapse. ["Al-hadm" (both vowels open): a demolished building; in the hadith of the martyrs: "and the one killed by a collapse is a martyr."]
11794 – al-Harith told me, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz told us, who said: Isra'il told us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "And whoever saves it," he said: rescues it.
* *
Al-Dahhak said:
11795 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Abu 'Amir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Whoever kills a soul other than for a soul," he said: whether he abstains or does not abstain. [He apparently means: whether he refrains from killing it, or does not refrain but did not kill, it is as if he had given life to all mankind.]
11796 – I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman told me: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: "It is as if he had given life to all mankind," he says: if he had not killed him, he would have given life to mankind, not having permitted what is forbidden.
* *
Qatadah and al-Hasan said regarding this:
11797 – Ibn WakI' told us, who said: 'Abd al-A'la told us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "Whoever kills a soul other than for a soul or for corruption in the land," he said: that is a great matter.
11798 – Bishr told us, who said: Yazid told us, who said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul," to the end of the verse: whoever kills it without a soul or corruption he has caused, "it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely." By Allah, its reward is great, and its burden is great! So give it life, O son of Adam, with what you have, and give it life with your pardon if you are able; there is no power except by Allah. We know of no one whose blood is lawful from a Muslim of the people of this qibla except by one of three: a man who disbelieves after his Islam, for whom the penalty is death; or who commits adultery after being married, for whom the penalty is stoning; or who kills deliberately, for whom the penalty is qawad.
11799 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, who said: Qatadah recited: "Whoever kills a soul other than for a soul, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely, and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely," and said: By Allah, its reward is great, and by Allah, its burden is great!
11800 – al-Muthanna told me, who said: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Salam ibn Miskin, who said: Sulayman ibn 'Ali al-Rab'i told me, who said: I asked al-Hasan: "Because of that We prescribed for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul other than for a soul," to the end of the verse: "Is it for us, O Abu Sa'id, as it was for the Children of Israel?" He said: Yes, by Him besides whom there is no god, as it was for the Children of Israel! Did the blood of the Children of Israel become more honored with Allah than our blood? [[Report 11800: "Salam ibn Miskin ibn Rabi'ah al-Azdi," Abu Rawh, trustworthy; has passed as no. 692. And "Sulayman ibn 'Ali al-Rab'i al-Azdi," trustworthy; biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

Narrated to me: al-Muthanna, who said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sa'id ibn Zayd, who said: I heard Khalid Abu al-Fadl say: I heard al-Hasan recite this verse: ﴿So his soul permitted him to kill his brother﴾ up to His saying ﴿and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved all mankind﴾. Then he said: By Allah, He magnified the burden (of sin) as you hear, and by Allah, He encouraged the reward as you hear! O son of Adam, if you think that were you to kill all people, you would have from your deed what saves you from the Fire, then by Allah your own soul has lied to you, and Satan has lied to you. [[The report: 11801. "Sa'id ibn Zayd ibn Dirham al-Azdi," brother of Hammad ibn Zayd. The scholars spoke about him, but they deemed him trustworthy, saying: "truthful, retentive." The most just thing said about him is what Ibn Hibban said: "He was truthful and retentive, but among those who would err and confuse in reports, so that he is not to be used as proof when he narrates alone." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/432, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/21.
And "Khalid, Abu al-Fadl." Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 2/1/153: "Khalid ibn Abi al-Fadl, he heard al-Hasan. Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated from him his saying... and his kunya is Khalid ibn Rabah Abu al-Fadl, so I do not know whether this is he or not." It seems al-Bukhari means this report.
Then he biographed "Khalid ibn Rabah al-Hudhali" 2/1/136, and said: "Waki' heard from him," and did not mention "Sa'id ibn Zayd." And he said: "Yazid ibn Harun said: Khalid ibn Rabah Abu al-Fadl informed us."
As for Ibn Abi Hatim, he biographed in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil 1/2/346: "Khalid ibn al-Fadl. He narrated from al-Hasan. Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated from him. I heard my father say that."
Then he biographed in 1/2/330: "Khalid ibn Rabah al-Hudhali, Abu al-Fadl... he narrated from al-Hasan...," and did not mention among those who narrated from him "Sa'id ibn Zayd."
Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also biographed him in Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah: 112, and in Lisan al-Mizan 2: 374, "Khalid ibn Rabah al-Hudhali, Abu al-Fadl al-Basri," and he transmitted from Ibn Hibban in al-Du'afa' that his kunya is "Abu al-Fadl," then said: "When he mentioned him in the third class of the trustworthy, he said: Khalid ibn Rabah Abu al-Fadl, narrates from al-Hasan. Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated from him." Ibn Hajar said: "I do not know; did he think it was another, or was he inconsistent about him?"
As for his biography in Lisan al-Mizan, it does not mention his kunya there, and it transmits some of what came in Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah.
It appears that "Khalidan Abu al-Fadl" is "Khalid ibn Rabah al-Hudhali" himself, and that what came in Ibn Abi Hatim, "Khalid ibn al-Fadl," is an error or a mistake. It also appears that he (al-Bukhari) paused regarding "Khalid ibn Abi al-Fadl," and preferred that it be an error by the transmitters, and that the narrator is "Khalid Abu al-Fadl," who is "Khalid ibn Rabah al-Hudhali" himself.]]

11802 - Hannad narrated to us, who said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿it is as if he had killed all mankind﴾, he said: a burden (of sin); ﴿and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved all mankind﴾, he said: a reward.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of the one who said: The interpretation of that is: whoever kills a believing soul without a soul having been killed by it, so that it deserves retaliation and execution in return for it, or without corruption in the earth, by warring against Allah and His Messenger and warring against the believers in it, then it is as if he had killed all mankind in what he deserves of the great punishment from Allah, mighty is His remembrance, just as his Lord threatened that for the one who does it, by His saying: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 93].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and whoever saves it, it is as if he had saved all mankind﴾, the most fitting interpretation of it is the saying of the one who said: whoever forbids the killing of one whose killing Allah, mighty is His remembrance, has forbidden, by himself, and does not precede to kill him, then he has given life to mankind from himself by their safety from him, and that is his giving life to it. This is similar to the report of Allah, mighty is His remembrance, about the one who disputed with Abraham regarding his Lord when Abraham said to him: ﴿My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. He said: I give life and cause death﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 258]. So the meaning of the disbeliever's saying "I give life" was: I leave alive whom I am able to kill; and in his saying "and cause death," [[In the printed and manuscript editions here: "I give life and cause death," and there is no doubt that "and cause death" is a repetition, so I left it out.]] killing whoever he kills. [[See what preceded: 5: 432.]] Likewise the meaning of "giving life" in His saying "and whoever saves it" is: people are safe from his killing them, except what Allah has permitted to kill of them, ﴿so it is as if he had given life to all mankind﴾.

And we only said that this is the most fitting interpretation of the verse, because no soul whose killing stands in for the killing of all souls in immediate harm, and its giving life does not stand in for giving life to all souls in immediate benefit. So it was known by that that the meaning of "giving life" is the safety of all souls from him, because whoever does not precede against one soul, all souls are safe from him; and that the one soul whose killing stands in for all of them is only in the burden (of sin), because no soul among the souls of the children of Adam has its loss standing in for the loss of all of them, though the loss of some of them is more general in harm than the loss of some. [[See the explanation of "giving life" in what preceded: 5: 432, and what follows.]]

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His saying, mighty is His remembrance: ﴿And We had certainly sent to them Our messengers with clear evidences. Then indeed many of them, after that, in the earth are transgressors﴾ (32).

Abu Ja'far said: This is an oath from Allah, mighty is His praise, by which He swears that His messengers, may Allah's blessings be upon them, had come to the Children of Israel whose stories Allah related and whose news He mentioned in the verses that preceded, from His saying: "O you who believe, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people intended to extend their hands to you" up to this place, "with clear evidences," meaning: with clear signs and evident proofs of the truth of what they were sent with to them, and the correctness of what they called them to of belief in them and performing Allah's obligations upon them.

Allah, mighty is His remembrance, says: "Then indeed many of them, after that, in the earth are transgressors," meaning: that many of the Children of Israel.

* *

The "ha' and mim" in His saying "Then indeed many of them" refer to the Children of Israel, and likewise in His saying "And We had certainly sent to them."

* *

"After that" means: after the coming of Allah's messengers with the clear evidences. [[See the explanation of "clear evidences" in what preceded: 9: 360, note 1, and the references there.]]

"In the earth are transgressors" means: they are in the earth doers of Allah's acts of disobedience, violators of Allah's command and prohibition, opponents of Allah and His messengers by following their desires, and opposing their prophets; and that was their transgression in the earth. [[See the explanation of "transgression" in what preceded: 7: 272, 579.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 33 (part 1 of 5):

The interpretation of His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth [to cause] corruption is only that they be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides or be exiled from the land. That is a disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an explanation from Allah, mighty is His mention, of the ruling on "corruption on earth," which He mentioned in His words: "Because of that, We ordained for the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul, unless for a soul or for corruption in the land..." He informs His servants of what the one who causes corruption on earth deserves of punishment and retribution. He, blessed and exalted, said: there is no penalty for him in this world except killing, crucifixion, cutting off the hand and foot from opposite sides, or banishment from the land, as a disgrace for them. As for the Hereafter, if he does not repent in this world, then there is a great punishment.
* *
Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about who this verse was revealed concerning.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a people among the People of the Book who had a covenant (mu'adi'ah) with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they broke the covenant and spread corruption in the land, so Allah made His Prophet ﷺ aware of the ruling concerning them.

Those who said this:
11803 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon the earth [to cause] corruption," he said: There were a people among the People of the Book who had a pact and covenant with the Prophet ﷺ; they broke the covenant and spread corruption in the land, so Allah gave His Messenger the choice: if he wished, he could kill them, and if he wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides.

11804 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: There was a people who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they broke the covenant, cut off the road, and spread corruption in the land, so Allah, mighty and majestic, gave His Prophet ﷺ the choice regarding them: if he wished, he could kill them, if he wished, he could crucify them, and if he wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides.

11805 - It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, and he mentioned something similar.
* *
Others said: It was revealed concerning a people among the polytheists.

Those who said this:
11806 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger" up to "indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." This verse was revealed concerning the polytheists; whoever of them repents before you gain power over him, there is no path against him. This verse does not protect a Muslim man from the prescribed punishment (hadd): if he kills, or causes corruption in the land, or wages war against Allah and His Messenger, and then joins the disbelievers before he is overpowered, that does not prevent the prescribed punishment that befits his offense from being carried out upon him. [[Narration: 11806 - "Yazid" is "Yazid al-Nahwi," "Yazid ibn Abi Sa'id al-Nahwi al-Marwazi," already mentioned under no. 6311. In the printed edition it was written here as "Zayd," which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. It was also related by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 7: 101 with similar wording, and by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 4: 187, no. 4372, and it will come under no. 11872.]]

11807 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan: "Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger," he said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.
* *
Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning a people from 'Uraynah and 'Ukl, who apostatized from Islam and waged war against Allah and His Messenger.

[Those who said that:]
11808 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas: that a group of 'Ukl and 'Uraynah came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are people of livestock, and we were not people of cultivated land [["people of livestock" (ahl dar'): people of camels and sheep. "Dar'" is the udder of every animal with hooves or cloven hooves, meaning they were people of the desert; "people of cultivated land" (ahl rif): people of crops and tilling, i.e., settled people. "Rif" is the land near water in the land of the Arabs and elsewhere.]], and we found Medina unhealthy [["istawkhamu al-madinah": they found it burdensome, and its air did not agree with their bodies, so they fell ill.]]." So the Prophet ﷺ commanded that they be given a herd (dhawd) and a shepherd [["dhawd": a herd of camels, from three to nine.]], and commanded them to go out with them and drink from their milk and urine. But they killed the shepherd of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, drove off the herd, and disbelieved after their Islam.
