["In the printed edition: 'bi-l-zina' (with fornication); I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is correct."] "Except those who repent before you gain power over them": in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ).

11875 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: There was a people between whom and the Messenger (ﷺ) there was a covenant, but they broke the pact, cut off the road, and caused corruption on earth. So Allah gave His Prophet (ﷺ) the choice regarding them: if he wished, he could kill them; if he wished, he could crucify them; if he wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. Whoever repents before you gain power over him, that is accepted from him.

11876 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words, "The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger," the verse... He mentioned something similar to the saying of al-Dahhak, except that he said: If he comes repentant and enters into Islam, it is accepted from him, and he is not held to account for what he did before.

11877 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning "Except those who repent before you gain power over them": He said: This is for the people of polytheism, when they commit anything of this kind during their polytheism, then repent and embrace Islam; then Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

11878 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ata al-Khurasani and Qatadah: As for His words, "Except those who repent before you gain power over them," this is for the people of polytheism. Whoever of the polytheists takes something from the Muslims while being at war with them, seizing property and shedding blood, and then repents before you gain power over him, what has passed is forgiven him.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse concerns those to whom the judgment of it applies, namely those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger: the brigands (hurrab) from among the people of Islam, ["Al-hurrab" is the plural of "harib," and "al-harib" is the usurper, plunderer, who strips people of their clothing. It seems that by it he means here the description of "one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger," and his causing corruption on earth. See what will come on p. 282, comment 2.] who cut off the road while remaining in their Islam, then seek safe conduct (ista'mana) and are granted security for the crimes they committed, while still being at war with the Muslims; and whoever of them does this as an apostate from Islam, ["His words, 'and whoever does this...' are connected to his words, 'the brigands from among the people of Islam...' meaning: this and that."] then joins the abode of war, then seeks safe conduct and is granted it. They said: So when the ruler grants him security for the crimes he committed earlier, no claim (tiba'ah) belongs against him for blood or property that he took before his repentance and before the ruler's grant of safe conduct to him.

Mention of those who said this:

11879 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, he said: al-Walid narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah informed me, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Amir al-Sha'bi: that Harithah ibn Badr went out as a warrior, terrorized the road, shed blood, and took property. Then he came repentant before he was overpowered, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) accepted his repentance and granted him an open safe conduct for what he had inflicted of blood or property.

11880 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi: that Harithah ibn Badr waged war during the time of Ali ibn Abi Talib, then came to al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and asked him to seek safe conduct for him from Ali, but he refused. Then he came to Ibn Ja'far, and he refused him too. ["That is Abd Allah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib."] Then he went to Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani, who granted him safe conduct and took him under his protection. He said to him: Seek safe conduct for me from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: When Ali had prayed the morning prayer, ["'al-Ghadah' means the dawn prayer."] Sa'id ibn Qays came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger? He said: That they be killed, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off on opposite sides, or be banished from the land. He said: Then he said: "Except those who repent before you gain power over them." Sa'id said: Even if it is Harithah ibn Badr? He said: Even if it is Harithah ibn Badr! He said: So here is Harithah ibn Badr, who has come repentant; is he secure? He said: Yes! So he brought him, and he pledged allegiance to him, accepted that from him, and wrote him a safe conduct. ["In the printed edition and manuscript: 'istaamana ila' — the correct form is what I have adopted."]

11881 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Harithah ibn Badr had corrupted the land and waged war, then repented. Ali was spoken to on his behalf, but he did not grant him security. So he came to Sa'id ibn Qays and spoke to him. Sa'id ibn Qays went to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you say about one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger? [He recited the whole verse.] He said: Tell me, what about one who repents before you gain power over him? He said: I say as Allah said. He said: Then it is Harithah ibn Badr! He said: So Ali granted him security, and Harithah said:

Ala ablighā Hamdāna in laqītumā... ʿalā al-nā'yi lā yaslamu ʿaduwwun yaʿībuhā
La-ʿamru abīhā inna Hamadāna tattaqī... al-ilāha wa-yaqḍī bi-l-kitābi khaṭībuhā

[Translation of the verses: Mind you, when you meet them, convey to Hamdan, despite distance, that no enemy who reproaches them shall be safe. By the life of her father, Hamdan fears God, and her orator judges by the Book.

"The reports 11879–11881: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' al-Dawsi' is trustworthy, though some have spoken of him; he has passed as no. 1614. As for 'Harithah ibn Badr ibn Husayn al-Ghudani,' from the Banu Ghudanah ibn Yarbu', he was among the knights and notables and chiefs of the Banu Tamim. He was daring and fond of wine. He was eloquent, articulate, knowledgeable of people's histories and days, sweet-tongued, a poet, and given to humor, so Ziyad was fond of his company all his life (al-Aghani 21:25). As for 'Sa'id ibn Qays al-Hamdani,' he is from the Banu Amr ibn al-Sabi', and was the chief of Hamdan in his time. When Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, granted safe conduct to Harithah ibn Badr, he stood on the pulpit and said: 'O people, I had vowed the blood of Harithah ibn Badr, so whoever meets him, let him not molest him.' Sa'id ibn Qays went to Harithah, informed him, equipped him, clothed him, and gave him a generous reward. When Harithah wished to depart for Basra, Sa'id ibn Qays escorted him with a thousand riders, and provisioned and equipped him. As for the two verses, they are in the History of Ibn Asakir 3:430, with slight variation in their transmission. As for his words, 'and her orator judges by the Book,' he apparently meant by the orator of Hamdan the great jurist Masruq ibn al-Ajda' al-Hamdani, companion of Ali and Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both. He seems to allude with this verse to what is reported of Masruq, that on the day of Siffin he came, stood between the two lines, and said: 'O people, listen!' Then he said: 'What do you think, if a herald called to you from heaven, you heard his speech and saw him, and he said: Allah forbids you from what you are engaged in, would you obey him?' They said: 'Yes!' He said: 'By Allah, Gabriel came down with this to Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then he continued saying such things, and recited: 'O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood, except it be trade by mutual consent among you, and do not kill yourselves; indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you' (4:29). Then he slipped away among the people and departed." (Ibn Sa'd 6:52).]

11882 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning His words, "Except those who repent before you gain power over them." Their repentance before being overpowered is that he writes to the ruler seeking safe conduct for what he killed and corrupted on earth: "If he does not grant me security regarding that, I will increase my corruption, killing, and seizing of property more than I did before." It is incumbent upon the ruler, as a right, to grant him security regarding that. When the ruler grants him security, he comes and places his hand in the ruler's hand, and no one among the people may pursue him, nor seize him for blood he shed, nor property he took. Whatever property he has is his, so that he does not kill the believers again and corrupt. If he returns to Allah, exalted and glorified is He, then He is his Protector, and He will take him to account for what he did; his repentance is between him and the ruler and the people. If the ruler seizes him, and he has repented to Allah before the ruler granted him security, as he claims, then the prescribed penalty shall be carried out against him.

11883 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, he said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who informed me, from Makhul, that he said: ["So it is in the printed edition and manuscript: 'akhbarani Makhul annahu qal' (Makhul informed me that he said); I incline to think the correct form is 'an Makhul annahu qal' (from Makhul that he said), see the earlier chains, nos. 3997, 4129, 5359, 8966."] If the ruler gives him a safe conduct, he is secure, and no prescribed penalty is to be carried out against him for what he had inflicted.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: Every brigand who comes repentant before being overpowered, whether he sought safe conduct from the ruler and was granted it or not, after he comes submitting and abandoning war.

["'Al-hurrab' is the plural of 'harib'; see its explanation above, p. 279, comment 1."]

Mention of those who said this:

11884 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Amir, who said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa, who was governor of Kufa during the caliphate of Uthman, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer, and said: O Abu Musa, this is the station of one who seeks refuge in you. I am so-and-so ibn so-and-so of Murad. I had waged war against Allah and His Messenger, and strove on earth, and I have repented before you gain power over me! Abu Musa stood and said: This is so-and-so ibn so-and-so, who had waged war against Allah and His Messenger, and strove on earth to cause corruption, and he repented before he was overpowered; so whoever meets him, let him not molest him except with good. The man remained as long as Allah willed, then he went out, and Allah, exalted and glorified is He, overtook him for his sins, and he was killed.

11885 - Al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from al-Sha'bi, who said: A man came to Abu Musa, and he related something similar.

11886 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, he said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, he said: I said to Malik: What do you say about this brigand who has terrorized the road, and shed blood and taken property, then joined the abode of war, or sheltered in the lands of Islam, then came repentant before he was overpowered? He said: His repentance is accepted. I said: So he is not pursued for anything of his offenses? He said: No, except that if property of a specific person is found with him, it is returned to its owner, or the guardian of someone he killed in his warfare demands retribution for the blood, proven by evidence or confession, and he is executed for it. As for the bloodshed he committed and whose guardians did not demand it, the ruler shall not pursue him for anything. Ali said: al-Walid said: I mentioned this to Abu Amr, and he said: His repentance is accepted if he waged war against the common people and the rulers, having harmed them by his warfare, brandished his weapon, and shed blood and taken property, and had a stronghold or a faction to which he could resort, or joined the abode of war and apostatized from Islam, or remained upon it, then came repentant before he was overpowered; his repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything of it.

11887 - Ali narrated to me, he said: al-Walid narrated to us, he said: Abu Amr said: I heard Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri say that.

11888 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, he said: al-Walid narrated to us, he said: I mentioned the saying of Abu Amr and Malik to al-Layth ibn Sa'd on this question, and he said: If he openly declares war against the common people and the rulers, and sheds blood and takes property, and his warfare prevents judgment being passed against him, or he joins the abode of war, then comes repentant before he is overpowered, his repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything of his offenses in his warfare, whether private or public bloodshed, even if his guardian demands it. ["In the printed edition: 'lil-'amma' (for the common people); the correct form is from the manuscript."] ["'Al-hukumah 'alayhi' means the judgment against him."]

11889 - Ali narrated to me, he said: al-Walid narrated to us, he said: al-Layth said, and likewise Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is the governor among us, related to me: that Ali al-Asadi waged war, terrorized the road, and shed blood and took property; the rulers and the common people pursued him, but he evaded and was not overpowered until he came repentant. That was because he heard a man reciting this verse: "Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah" (39:53). He stopped by him and said: O servant of Allah, repeat its recitation. He repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword, then came repentant, until he reached Medina at the pre-dawn hour, bathed, then came to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and prayed the dawn prayer, then sat with Abu Hurayrah among his companions. When it became light, the people recognized him and stood up toward him. He said: You have no way against me; I came repentant before you gain power over me! Abu Hurayrah said: He is right. Abu Hurayrah took him by the hand until he came to Marwan ibn al-Hakam during his governorship of Medina in the time of Mu'awiyah, and said: This is Ali; he came repentant, and you have no way against him, nor any killing. He said: So he was left alone regarding all of that. ["His words 'fa-turika' (he was left) are in the passive, as if he means that he was not held to account for any of all the offenses he committed while waging war against Allah and His Messenger."] He said: Then Ali went out repentant, striving in the path of Allah at sea, and they met the Romans; they brought his ship near a ship of theirs, and he stormed the Romans' ship, and they were routed from him to their other ship; it capsized with them and him, and they all drowned. ["Report 11889: 'Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani, the governor': I did not know who he was. And 'Ali al-Asadi': I did not know him either. It seems to me that a chain like this has passed before, but its reference has escaped me; whoever finds it, let him establish it here, for perhaps it will reveal this governor mentioned in this report."]

11890 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Mutarrif ibn Ma'qil narrated to us, he said: I heard Ata say concerning a man who stole and came repentant without being apprehended: Is there a prescribed penalty against him? He said: No! Then he said: "Except those who repent before you gain power over them," the verse. ["Report 11890: 'Mutarrif ibn Ma'qil al-Shaqari al-Sa'di,' also said to be 'al-Bahili,' Abu Bakr. He related from al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, and Ata. Ahmad said: 'He was trustworthy and more.' He is biographed in al-Kabir 4/1/397, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/315, and Lisan al-Mizan 6:48."]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 34 (part 2 of 2):

11891 - Ibn al-Barqi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr related to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, [and] they both said: If he comes repentant, having neither seized property nor shed blood, he is left alone. This is what God meant by His words: ﴿except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾. He meant by that that he has neither shed blood nor seized property. [[The report 11891: "Abu Sakhr" is Humayd ibn Ziyad ibn Abi al-Makhariq, al-Kharrat, previously mentioned under nos. 4325, 5386, 8391. In the printed edition and manuscript here it was "Abu Sakhrah" with a taʼ at the end, but it was correctly given earlier as no. 11867.
"Abu Mu'awiyah" is ʻAmmar ibn Mu'awiyah al-Duhni, also previously mentioned under nos. 909, 4325, 5386.]]
* *
Others said: Rather, by the exception in that [verse] he meant the one who repents from his waging war against God and His Messenger and his striving in the land to cause corruption, after he has joined the abode of disbelief in his warfare. As for when his brigandage and warfare take place while he resides in the abode of Islam, [[See what I said about "al-Hirabah" (brigandage), p. 252, note 2, and p. 256, note 2.]] and he is among the mass of the community, then his repentance does not remove from him any of the prescribed punishments of God, mighty and majestic, nor any of the rights of the Muslims and the covenant-holders; rather, he is held to account for that.
Mention of those who said this:
11892 - Ali ibn Sahl related to me, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Isma'il informed me, from Hisham ibn ʻUrwah: that he informed him that they asked ʻUrwah about one who acted as a highway robber within Islam and incurred prescribed punishments, then came repentant. He said: His repentance is not accepted. If it were accepted from them, they would become emboldened against it, and it would be great corruption. But if he fled to the enemy and then came repentant, I would not impose any punishment upon him.
* *
A view contrary to this has been transmitted from ʻUrwah, namely:
11893 - Ali related to me, saying: al-Walid related to us, saying: One who heard Hisham ibn ʻUrwah informed me, from ʻUrwah, who said: The prescribed punishment for what he fled from is enforced upon him, and no one may grant him safe-conduct regarding it. He means: one who incurs a prescribed punishment, then flees and joins the disbelievers, then comes repentant.
* *
Others said: If his brigandage and warfare took place in the abode of Islam, [[See p. 285, note 2.]] and he was without a protected group to which he could turn, and then came repentant before being captured, his repentance does not remove from him any punishment or any rights of people. But if his brigandage and warfare took place in the abode of Islam, or he had joined the abode of disbelief, yet in all of that he was turning to a group that protected him from whoever sought him among the rulers of the Muslims, and then came repentant before being captured, his repentance removes from him all that occurred from his offenses during that period of brigandage, except that if he incurred a prescribed punishment or ordered his companions to commit an act deserving punishment, [["The companions" (al-rufqah) means his comrades with whom he travels and to whom he turns, who are his group.]] or a debt owed to a Muslim or a covenant-holder, and he was not seeking refuge in a group protecting him, then he is held to account for what he committed of that, and his repentance does not remove it from him.
Mention of those who said this:
11894 - Ali ibn Sahl related to me, saying: al-Walid related to us, saying: Abu ʻAmr said: When a highwayman or a band of highwaymen cut the road and commit whatever bloodshed and seizure of property they commit, and they have no group to which they turn nor any protection, and they find safety only by entering into the mass of their community and the multitude of their common people, and then come repentant before being captured, their repentance is not accepted, and the prescribed punishment for what they did is enforced upon them.
11895 - Ali related to me, saying: al-Walid related to us, saying: I mentioned to Abu ʻAmr the statement of ʻUrwah: "The prescribed punishment for what he fled from is enforced upon him, and no one may grant him safe-conduct regarding it." Abu ʻAmr said: If he fled from his offense within the abode of Islam and the ruler granted him safe-conduct, the safe-conduct is not valid. If he joined the abode of war and then asked a ruler for safe-conduct concerning his offenses, it is not proper for the ruler to grant him safe-conduct. If the ruler granted him safe-conduct while not knowing of his offenses, he is safe. If someone comes seeking him for blood or property, he is returned to his place of safety, and if he refuses to return, he is safe and is not to be touched. He said: If he grants him safe-conduct for his offenses while knowing them, the ruler is liable, and it is obligatory upon him to pay the blood-money ["al-ʻaql," the compensation for the crime] for whatever blood or property he had seized, and he has sinned in suspending those prescribed punishments and bloodshed, and his affair rests with God, mighty and majestic. He said: Abu ʻAmr also said: When that occurs, and he had a protective force or a group to which he turned, or he joined the abode of war and apostatized from Islam, or he remained upon it, and then came repentant before being captured, his repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything from his offenses that he committed in his warfare, unless some specific property remaining with him is found, in which case it is returned to its owner.
11896 - Ali related to me, saying: al-Walid related to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah informed me, from Rabi'ah, who said: His repentance is accepted, and he is not pursued for anything from his offenses in his warfare, unless someone seeks him for a blood-debt he incurred during his peace before his warfare, in which case he is subject to retaliation for it.
11897 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mu'ammar al-Raqqi related to us, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, from al-Hakam ibn ʻUtaybah, who said: May God fight al-Hajjaj! He was truly learned! He granted safe-conduct to a man from his warfare, and said: Look, did he commit anything before his going out?
* *
Others said: His repentance removes from him the prescribed punishment of God that became obligatory upon him through his warfare, but does not drop from him the rights of the children of Adam.
Among those who said this is al-Shafi'i.
11898 - Al-Rabi' related this to us from him.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in my judgment is the view of the one who said: The repentance of the warring rebel who protects himself, or protects himself with a group with him, before being captured, removes from him the consequences of this world that were incumbent upon him during the days of his warfare and brigandage, [[See "al-Hirabah" previously, p. 285, note 2.]] of the prescribed punishments of God, and of necessary compensation, retaliation and qisas, except for what remains in his hand of the property of the Muslims and the covenant-holders in its specific form, which is returned to its people. This is due to the consensus of all that this is the ruling for a protected group waging war against God and His Messenger, striving in the land to cause corruption, by way of apostasy from Islam. Likewise is the ruling for every protected person who strives in the land to cause corruption, whether they are a group or one individual.
As for one who conceals his theft, and who robs by way of catching someone off guard, [["Ightafala al-rajul" means he seized the opportunity of his carelessness and took what he took. This is a form that the lexicographers did not record; they recorded "taghaffala" (with shaddah on the fa'), and "istaghfalahu," meaning he watched for his heedlessness. What Abu Ja'far used is sound by analogy and by Arabic usage, and I have seen Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani, author of al-Aghani, also use it, as in al-Aghani 2:99, in the reports on ʻAdi ibn Zayd the poet, where he mentioned his grandfather "Zayd ibn Ayyub" and his killing, and among what he said: "Then the Bedouin ightafala Zayd ibn Ayyub, shot him with an arrow which lodged between his shoulders, and split his heart."
In the printed edition here it read "ʻala wajh ighfal min sariqah," which is not correct by Arabic analogy, so as to alter what was in the manuscript. In the manuscript it is undotted, and this is the correct reading.]] and the one who draws a weapon in an open place against some travelers on the road, and who, when pursued, is unable to resist, then God's ruling upon him, whether he repents or does not repent, stands, along with the rights of the one whose property he took, or who struck his guardian with a killing or a treacherous assault that was seized; and his repentance concerns what is between him and God, mighty and majestic. This is by analogy with the consensus of all that if he committed any of that against the Muslims while they were at peace with him, and then they became at war with him, his warfare against them would not remove from him any right of God, exalted is His mention, nor of any human being. Likewise, his ruling is the same when he commits that in an open place or by stealth, while he is not protected by the ruler through his own person if the ruler seeks him, nor does he have a protecting group to which he can turn.
In His words: ﴿except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾ there is clear evidence for one who is granted understanding of it that the ruling God mentioned concerning the warriors applies to Muslims and covenant-holders, not to polytheists who have set themselves up as enemies to the Muslims in war. This is because if it were a ruling only for polytheist combatants, and not for Muslims or their protected people, then their conversion to Islam or repentance after we gain power over them would not remove from them what killing was due from them before their conversion and repentance, and what the Muslims have against the polytheist combatants. Yet there is a consensus among the Muslims that the conversion of a polytheist combatant removes from him, after the Muslims gain power over him, what his conversion would have removed from him had it occurred before they gained power over him. This indicates that the correct view on this matter is the view of the one who said: "By the verse on the warriors in this place is meant the warriors of the people of the religion or of the protected covenant, [["Al-hirab" is the plural of "harib," and the discussion of it was given previously on p. 279, note 1, so refer back to it. In the printed edition it read "hirab ahl al-Islam," and in the manuscript "ahl al-Milla," and the correct reading of it is what I have written.]] excluding whoever else among the polytheist combatants."
* *
As for His words: ﴿so know that God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, its meaning is: know, O believers, that God does not hold to account those from the people of war who repent to God and His Messenger, who strive in the land to cause corruption, nor others, for their sins; rather He pardons them, covering them and not disgracing them with them through punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and He is Merciful toward them in His pardon of them and His leaving aside punishing them for them. [[See the explanation of "Ghafur" (Forgiving) and "Rahim" (Merciful) in the language indices above.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 35–36:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, His majesty, the Mighty, means: O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger concerning what they have informed you of, and the reward He has promised and the punishment He has threatened [[In the printed edition: "and the reward He promised them", but I have kept what is in the manuscript, as it is pure correctness.]] "Fear Allah" means: respond to Allah regarding what He has commanded you and forbidden you, by obeying Him in that, and make your faith and your belief in your Lord and your Prophet true through righteous deeds [[See the explanation of "ittaqu" (fear/guard) in the indices of language earlier (w-q-y).]] "And seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him," meaning: seek nearness to Him by acting in what pleases Him. [[See the explanation of "ibtaghā" earlier, 9:480, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Al-wasilah is the form "fa'ilah" from the speaker's saying "I sought a means (tawassaltu) to so-and-so by such-and-such," meaning: I drew near to him. From this is the saying of Antarah:

Indeed, men have a means (wasilah) to you... if they take you, then adorn yourself with kohl and henna.

[[Poetry of the Six Pre-Islamic Poets: 396; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:165; al-Khizanah 3:11; and others, from verses of his that he said to his wife, when she kept mentioning his horses and blaming him for a mare he favoured over all his other horses and gave the milk of his camels to drink: "Do not mention my colt and what I have fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of a mangy camel. Indeed the evening drink is for him, and you are a disgrace, so lament as you wish, then grieve." "The old wine lied, and cold water in a skin..., if you were asking me for an evening drink, then go away." "Indeed men have..." "And your mount will be the camel-saddle and its rigging, while the son of the ostrich will be my mount on that day!" He threatens her with divorce if she persists in blaming him about his mare, for his mare is his fortress and refuge. As for her, she is hardly taken captive in war before she adorns herself with kohl and henna for whoever has taken her. He says: if they take you, you adorn yourself with kohl and henna for them.]]

By "al-wasilah" is meant nearness (qurbah). From this is the saying of another:

When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union, and the purity between us and the means (wasail) returns.

[[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:164.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

11899 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness through deeds.

11900 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Sufyan narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Talhah, from Ata': "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11901 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means to Him," he said: it is the request and the nearness. [[In the printed edition: "it is the request", but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

11902 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying: "And seek the means to Him," meaning: draw near to Him by obeying Him and acting in what pleases Him.

11902 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And seek the means to Him," nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

11903 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11904 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir regarding his saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11905 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: love; love one another for Allah. And he recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means (al-wasilah) to their Lord﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 57].

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And strive in His way that you may succeed﴾ (35)

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: And strive, O believers, against your enemies and His enemies, in His way, meaning in His religion and His law which He has legislated for His servants, and it is Islam. [[See the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way) earlier in the indices of language.]] That is: exert yourselves in fighting them and compelling them to enter the upright, submitting religion. ﴿That you may succeed﴾ means: so that you may prosper and attain lasting survival and eternity in His gardens. [[See the explanation of "jahada" earlier, 4:318.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-falah" (success) earlier with its evidences, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "al-falah" earlier, 1:249, 250; 3:561; 7:91, 509.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved—if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ (36)

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty says: Indeed, those who denied the lordship of their Lord and worshipped other than Him, from the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf, and from others who worshipped idols and images, and died upon that before repentance—if they had the possession of all that is on the earth and its double with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of Allah upon them for abandoning His command and worshipping other than Him on the Day of Resurrection, and they ransomed themselves with all that, it would not be accepted from them as a ransom or compensation for their punishment and retribution; rather He will punish them in the boiling water on the Day of Resurrection with a painful torment for them.

This is only an informing from Allah, His majesty, to the Jews who were among the surroundings of the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that they and others of the polytheists who associate with Him are equal in His sight regarding the painful punishment and the great retribution due to them. That is because they used to say: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, deluded by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and lying against Him. So He, exalted is His remembrance, refuted them with this verse and what follows it, and cut off their hope, saying to them and to all the disbelievers in Him and His Messenger: "Indeed, those who disbelieved, if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment. They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment." His majesty says to them: So do not hope, O disbelievers, for the acceptance of ransom from you, nor for your exit from the Fire by the intercession of your fathers before Me after your entering it, if you die upon your disbelief in which you are; but repent to Allah with a sincere repentance. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse earlier in the indices of language.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 35–36:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, His majesty, the Mighty, means: O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger concerning what they have informed you of, and the reward He has promised and the punishment He has threatened [[In the printed edition: "and the reward He promised them", but I have kept what is in the manuscript, as it is pure correctness.]] "Fear Allah" means: respond to Allah regarding what He has commanded you and forbidden you, by obeying Him in that, and make your faith and your belief in your Lord and your Prophet true through righteous deeds [[See the explanation of "ittaqu" (fear/guard) in the indices of language earlier (w-q-y).]] "And seek the means (al-wasilah) to Him," meaning: seek nearness to Him by acting in what pleases Him. [[See the explanation of "ibtaghā" earlier, 9:480, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Al-wasilah is the form "fa'ilah" from the speaker's saying "I sought a means (tawassaltu) to so-and-so by such-and-such," meaning: I drew near to him. From this is the saying of Antarah:

Indeed, men have a means (wasilah) to you... if they take you, then adorn yourself with kohl and henna.

[[Poetry of the Six Pre-Islamic Poets: 396; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:165; al-Khizanah 3:11; and others, from verses of his that he said to his wife, when she kept mentioning his horses and blaming him for a mare he favoured over all his other horses and gave the milk of his camels to drink: "Do not mention my colt and what I have fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of a mangy camel. Indeed the evening drink is for him, and you are a disgrace, so lament as you wish, then grieve." "The old wine lied, and cold water in a skin..., if you were asking me for an evening drink, then go away." "Indeed men have..." "And your mount will be the camel-saddle and its rigging, while the son of the ostrich will be my mount on that day!" He threatens her with divorce if she persists in blaming him about his mare, for his mare is his fortress and refuge. As for her, she is hardly taken captive in war before she adorns herself with kohl and henna for whoever has taken her. He says: if they take you, you adorn yourself with kohl and henna for them.]]

By "al-wasilah" is meant nearness (qurbah). From this is the saying of another:

When the slanderers are heedless, we return to our union, and the purity between us and the means (wasail) returns.

[[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah 1:164.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

11899 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us = and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness through deeds.

11900 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Sufyan narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Talhah, from Ata': "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11901 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means to Him," he said: it is the request and the nearness. [[In the printed edition: "it is the request", but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

11902 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying: "And seek the means to Him," meaning: draw near to Him by obeying Him and acting in what pleases Him.

11902 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And seek the means to Him," nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

11903 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11904 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir regarding his saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: nearness.

11905 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And seek the means to Him," he said: love; love one another for Allah. And he recited: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek the means (al-wasilah) to their Lord﴾ [Surah al-Isra': 57].

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And strive in His way that you may succeed﴾ (35)

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: And strive, O believers, against your enemies and His enemies, in His way, meaning in His religion and His law which He has legislated for His servants, and it is Islam. [[See the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way) earlier in the indices of language.]] That is: exert yourselves in fighting them and compelling them to enter the upright, submitting religion. ﴿That you may succeed﴾ means: so that you may prosper and attain lasting survival and eternity in His gardens. [[See the explanation of "jahada" earlier, 4:318.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-falah" (success) earlier with its evidences, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "al-falah" earlier, 1:249, 250; 3:561; 7:91, 509.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved—if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ (36)

Abu Ja'far said: His majesty says: Indeed, those who denied the lordship of their Lord and worshipped other than Him, from the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf, and from others who worshipped idols and images, and died upon that before repentance—if they had the possession of all that is on the earth and its double with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of Allah upon them for abandoning His command and worshipping other than Him on the Day of Resurrection, and they ransomed themselves with all that, it would not be accepted from them as a ransom or compensation for their punishment and retribution; rather He will punish them in the boiling water on the Day of Resurrection with a painful torment for them.

This is only an informing from Allah, His majesty, to the Jews who were among the surroundings of the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that they and others of the polytheists who associate with Him are equal in His sight regarding the painful punishment and the great retribution due to them. That is because they used to say: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, deluded by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and lying against Him. So He, exalted is His remembrance, refuted them with this verse and what follows it, and cut off their hope, saying to them and to all the disbelievers in Him and His Messenger: "Indeed, those who disbelieved, if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment. They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not be out of it, and for them is a lasting punishment." His majesty says to them: So do not hope, O disbelievers, for the acceptance of ransom from you, nor for your exit from the Fire by the intercession of your fathers before Me after your entering it, if you die upon your disbelief in which you are; but repent to Allah with a sincere repentance. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse earlier in the indices of language.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 37:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it, and theirs is a lasting punishment﴾ (5:37).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "They wish to come out of the Fire," may He be exalted in praise, He means: those who disbelieved in their Lord on the Day of Resurrection wish to come out of the Fire after entering it. "And they will not come out of it" means: "Theirs is a lasting punishment" — that is, a punishment that is perpetual, fixed, which will never leave them nor be lifted from them, ever, as the poet said, whose composer I have not identified: [[I have not identified who composed it.]]

Indeed, for you on the Day of al-Sh'b, from me,
is a punishment, lasting, remaining upon you. [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1:165.]]

And the people of ta'wil (exegesis) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Among those who said this:

11906 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah: that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said to Ibn Abbas, may Allah have mercy on him: "Blind of sight, blind of heart! You claim that a people will come out of the Fire, while Allah, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿and they will not come out of it﴾?" Ibn Abbas said: "Woe to you! Read what comes before it! This is for the disbelievers." [[In the printed edition: "O blind of sight, blind of heart, you claim...." It seems Nafi' is addressing Ibn Abbas, and this is strange to come from Nafi', given his boldness and insolence! In the manuscript it reads: "ma 'ami al-basar a'mA al-qalb, bra'um", written without dots, so I decided to read it as I have recorded it, as a report to Ibn Abbas about the one who says this.]]

The Interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (5:38).

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: "Whoever steals from a man or a woman, then cut off his hand, O people." It is for this reason that "the thief, male or female" is in the nominative, because they are not specified. Had it been intended to refer to a particular male thief and a particular female thief, the grammatical form would have been the accusative.

* *

It has been related from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite it: ﴿And the male thieves and the female thieves﴾.

11907 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Ibn Awn, from Ibrahim, who said: "In our recitation" – and at times he said: "In the recitation of Abdullah" – ﴿And the male thieves and the female thieves, cut off their right hands﴾.

11908 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn Awn, from Ibrahim: "In our recitation: ﴿And the male thieves and the female thieves, cut off their right hands﴾."

* *

This is evidence for the soundness of what we have said regarding its meaning, and for the soundness of the nominative case in it, and that "the thief, male or female" are in the nominative by their action, as I have described, for the reasons I have described.

* *

And He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "Cut off their hands," and the meaning is: their right hands, as:

11909 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Cut off their hands," the right ones.

11910 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir, who said: In the recitation of Abdullah: ﴿And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands﴾.

* *

Then they differed concerning the "thief" whom Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, meant.

Some of them said: He meant the thief of three dirhams or more. This is the view of a group of the people of Medina, among them Malik ibn Anas and those who held his view. They argued for their view by the fact that:

11911 - The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut off the hand for a shield whose value was three dirhams. [[Report: 11911 – related without a chain. Malik related it from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, in the Muwatta: 831; al-Bukhari related it through Malik (al-Fath 2: 93–94), and Muslim related it through him too, in his Sahih 11: 184, 185.

"Al-mijann" is the shield, because it covers its bearer, i.e., shields him.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, He meant the thief of a quarter dinar or its value. Among those who said this were al-Awza'i and those who held his view. They argued for their view by the report transmitted from Aisha, who said:

11912 - The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Amputation is for a quarter dinar or more."[[Report: 11912 – he also cited it here without a chain, and it has passed on p. 266, note no. 1.

This report was related by al-Bukhari through his chains (al-Fath 12: 89–91), and by Muslim through his chains in his Sahih 11: 180–183.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, He meant the thief of ten dirhams or more. Among those who said this were Abu Hanifah and his companions. They argued for this by the report transmitted from Abdullah ibn Amr and Ibn Abbas:

11913 - That the Prophet (ﷺ) cut off the hand for a shield whose value was ten dirhams. [[Report: 11913 – the report of Ibn Abbas was related by al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 2: 93. In the manuscript and the printed edition it stated that this report is also transmitted from "Abdullah ibn Umar"; I did not find the narration with that attribution from "Ibn Umar." Rather, the narration they relied upon in the books of the companions of Abu Hanifah is what "Abdullah ibn Amr" said, transmitted from him by "Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather." Ahmad related it in al-Musnad under no. 6900; see my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad's takhrij there. See also al-Tahawi's Ma'ani al-Athar 1: 93, and al-Jassas's Ahkam al-Quran 2: 417. Therefore I have corrected what precedes this report to "Abdullah ibn Amr," not as it was in the printed edition and manuscript, "Ibn Umar."]]

* *

Others said: Rather, He meant the thief of little or much. They argued for this on the basis that the verse is on its apparent meaning, and that no one has the right to specify any part of it except by a proof that must be accepted. [[In the printed edition: "and that it is not permitted for anyone," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] They said: No report has been authenticated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that this applies only to a specific category of thieves. They said: The reports concerning what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cut off for are confused and varied, and no one has related from him that a thief of a single dirham was brought to him and he released him; rather, they related from him only that he cut off for a shield whose value was three dirhams. They said: It is possible that, had a thief been brought to him for something worth a dang, he would have cut off his hand. They said: Ibn al-Zubayr cut off a hand for a dirham.

* *

It has been related from Ibn Abbas that he said: The verse is general.

11914 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min related to us, from Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His words: "The thief, male or female," is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general. [[Report: 11914 – Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalid al-Hanafi al-Marwazi, judge of Marw. Abu Hatim said: "There is no harm in him," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.

And Najdah ibn Nufay' al-Hanafi, who related from Ibn Abbas. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is the view of those who say: "The verse refers to a specific category of thieves, namely those who steal a quarter dinar or more, or its value," because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Amputation is for a quarter dinar or more." I have thoroughly mentioned the views of those who differ on this matter, together with their reasons for their views, and the clarification of which is closest to the truth, with its evidences, [[In the printed edition: "and the allusion regarding which is closest to the truth," and al-Tabari would never say such a thing. In the manuscript: "and the thief regarding which is closest to the truth," a hideous distortion from the haste of the copyist; the correct reading is what I have adopted.]] in my book "The Book of Theft," and I disliked lengthening this book by repeating that here.

* *

As for His words: "As a recompense for what they earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah," He says: a retribution for them for their theft and their acts of stealing through disobedience to Allah [[See the explanation of "recompense" in the earlier indices of language (jaza)

and the explanation of "earned" earlier, 9:196, note 1 and the references there.]], "an exemplary punishment from Allah": a punishment from Allah for their thievery. [[See the explanation of "nakal" earlier, 2:176–177 / 8:580.]]

* *

Qatadah used to say about this:

11915 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "The thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they earned, an exemplary punishment from Allah. And Allah is Mighty and Wise": Do not show pity toward them by establishing the prescribed punishments upon them, for by Allah, Allah never commanded a matter except that it is righteous, and never forbade a matter except that it is corruption. [[Rather, we have come upon a time in which the prescribed punishments have been suspended, under the pretext of showing mercy to whoever has committed one of Allah's prescribed punishments. The tongues of a people of base origin grew long, and they dared against Allah with their slanders, claiming that the mercy they call for toward the people of the prescribed punishments is righteousness, and that what Allah commanded is corruption!! O Allah, deliver us from a time in which the wicked boast of their authority, and the people of faith are diminished by their sins.]]

* *

Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "Be harsh with the thieves; cut off their hands one by one, and their feet one by one."

* *

As for His words: "And Allah is Mighty and Wise," He, may His praise be exalted, says: "And Allah is Mighty" in His retribution against this male thief and female thief and others of the people of His disobedience, "Wise" in His judgment concerning them and His decree upon them. [[See the explanation of "Mighty" earlier, 9:378, note 2, and the references there.

And the explanation of "Wise" earlier in the indices of language.]]

He says: So do not be remiss, O believers, in carrying out My judgment against thieves and others among the people of crimes upon whom I have obligated prescribed punishments in this world as a penalty for them, for by My wisdom I have decreed that upon them, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "for by My judgment I decreed ...," and what I have adopted is better here.]] and by My knowledge of what is righteous for them and for you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 39:

The interpretation of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His praise be great, says: "But whoever repents" from among these thieves, meaning: whoever turns back from what Allah dislikes of his disobedience toward Him, to what He is pleased with of his obedience [[See the explanation of "tawbah" (repentance) in the indices of linguistic terms in earlier volumes.]] "after his wrongdoing", and "his wrongdoing" is his transgression and his doing what Allah has forbidden him, namely stealing the property of people [[See the explanation of "zulm" (wrongdoing) in the indices of linguistic terms in earlier volumes.]] "and reforms" [[I added the words of the Exalted, "and reforms", to complete the context of Abu Ja'far, as he followed in his tafsir; they are not in the manuscript nor in the printed edition.]] meaning: he reforms himself by compelling it toward what is disagreeable to it in obedience to Allah, and by repenting to Him from what he was upon of disobedience. [[See the explanation of "islah" (reform) in earlier volumes, vol. 9, p. 340, note 5, and the references there.]]

Mujahid used to say, as has been related to us: his repentance in this place is the prescribed punishment (hadd) that is carried out upon him.

............................................................................

...................................... [[I have placed these dots because I judged that Mujahid's statement has dropped out, either from the copyist or from Abu Ja'far himself, since the report that follows it is from Ibn 'Abbas, not from Mujahid.]]

* *

11916 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms", then He turns to him, meaning: the prescribed punishment (hadd). [[In the printed edition: "He says: He turns to him by the hadd", and I have retained what is in the manuscript, which is correct. It means that Allah's turning to him is after the prescribed punishment carried out upon him for his repentance.]]

11917 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Musa ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Huyayy ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: A woman stole some jewelry, and those whose property she had stolen came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this woman has stolen from us!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Cut off her right hand." The woman said: "Is there any repentance (for me)?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Today you are as free of your sin as on the day your mother bore you!" He said: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed Allah will turn to him." [[Report 11917: "Musa ibn Dawud al-Dabbi", a trustworthy narrator among the teachers of Ahmad, previously mentioned at no. 10190. "Ibn Lahi'ah", previously mentioned many times.

"Huyayy ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Shurayh al-Ma'afiri al-Hubuli al-Misri". The four compilers related from him; he is trustworthy. Ahmad criticised him and said: "He has odd reports (manakir)." Al-Bukhari said: "There is something to examine in him." Ibn Ma'in said: "There is no harm in him." Ibn 'Adi said: "I hope there is no harm in him when a trustworthy narrator relates from him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

"Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli" is "'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Ma'afiri", a trustworthy Successor. Previously mentioned at nos. 6657 and 9483.

This report was related by Ahmad in his Musnad at no. 6657, by the route of Hasan ibn Musa from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Huyayy, in full detail, and my brother Sayyid Ahmad graded it there and said: "Its chain is sound."

Ibn Kathir transmitted it in his tafsir, 3: 152, then quoted the narration of Ahmad, then said: "This woman is the Makhzumite who stole, and her story is established in the two Sahihs, through the narration of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah." Then see Fath al-Bari (12: 76–86) and Sahih Muslim, 11: 186–188.

The woman who stole was "Fatimah bint al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Asad ibn Hilal ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum" (Ibn Sa'd, 8: 192). The Hafiz Ibn Hajar has fully set out her account in his explanation of this hadith in al-Fath.]]

* *

As for His saying "indeed Allah will turn to him": meaning, indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, returns him to what He loves and is pleased with, from what He dislikes and abhors of his disobedience.

* *

As for His saying "indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful": meaning, indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, covers over the sins of whoever repents and turns back from his disobedience to His obedience, by pardoning him from punishment for them on the Day of Resurrection, and by not exposing him for them before the witnesses of all creation, "and Merciful" toward him and toward His servants who turn back to Him from their sins. [[See the explanation of "Ghafur" (Forgiving) and "Rahim" (Merciful) in earlier volumes in the indices of linguistic terms.]]

Commentary on the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (5:40)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, whose praise is great, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do these people not know—[meaning those who said] "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days" [[In the printed edition it reads: "Do these people who said ... those who claimed", while in the manuscript it reads: "Do these people who said ... those who claimed." I have adopted what is in the manuscript and added "meaning" between brackets, as I believe it was dropped by the copyist.]]—those who claim that they are the sons of Allah and His beloved—that Allah manages what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and directs and creates it; nothing in either of them that He wills is beyond Him, because all of that is His dominion, and the affair of it belongs to Him. There is no kinship between Him and anything in them or in either of them, such that He would show favour to someone because of a relationship to Him and save him from His punishment while he is an unbeliever and opposes His command and prohibition, or admit him to the Fire while he is obedient to Him, due to the remoteness of his kinship to Him. Rather, He punishes whom He wills of His creatures in this world for their disobedience, by killing, sinking into the earth, transformation, and other kinds of His punishment; and He forgives whom He wills of them in this world by accepting their repentance from their unbelief and disobedience, rescuing them from ruin and saving them from punishment. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾: that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is capable of punishing whom He wills of His creatures for their disobedience, and of forgiving whom He wills of them by rescuing them from ruin through accepting their repentance and in all other matters, because the creation is His creation, the dominion is His dominion, and the servants are His servants.

* *

As for His words, ﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [[For the explanation of the words of this verse, see its parallels earlier, in the language indexes.]], it is addressed to Him (ﷺ), and what is meant by it are the groups of the Children of Israel I have mentioned, who were in the city of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and its surroundings. We have already demonstrated the Arabs' use of the like of this in their speech, with its evidence, earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [[See what preceded: 2:484–488.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 41 (part 1 of 3):

On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of meaning) of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, "We believe," but their hearts have not believed﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of ta'wil differed about who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir, when he said to the Banu Qurayzah, when the Prophet ﷺ besieged them: "It is only slaughter, so do not come down under the judgment of Sa'd."

Those who said this:

11918 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed." He said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar, (it is claimed that he was Abu Lubabah), to whom the Banu Qurayzah gestured on the day of the siege, "What is the matter? And upon what shall we come down?" So he gestured to them that it was slaughter.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning a man of the Jews who asked a man of the Muslims, who was asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about his ruling regarding a killing he had committed.

Those who said this:

11919 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Amir: "Let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief." He said: A man of the Jews had been killed by a man of his own religion. The killer said to their allies among the Muslims: "Ask Muhammad ﷺ for me. If he is sent with the blood-money (diyah), we will bring our dispute to him, and if he orders us to kill, we will not go to him."
[Editor's note: In the printed edition: "fa-in kana yaqdi bil-diyah" (if he judges by the blood-money), differing from the manuscript, which I have adopted. His words "bu'ith bil-diyah" (passive voice): that he was given authority in his mission and prophethood to rule in such matters by blood-money rather than retaliation.]
11920 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Zakariyya, from Amir, similarly.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Suriya, because he apostatized after his acceptance of Islam.

Those who said this:

11921 - Hannad and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Zuhri told me: I heard a man from Mazinah narrate, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that Abu Hurayrah related to them that the rabbis of the Jews gathered in the bayt al-midras (the house where the Jews studied their books) when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah. A man among them had committed adultery after being married, with a Jewish woman who was also married. They said: "Go with this man and this woman to Muhammad ﷺ, ask him what the ruling is concerning them, and make him the judge over them. If he rules over them with your practice of tahmim (blackening the face) — and it is flogging with a rope of palm fiber coated with tar, then their faces are blackened, then they are placed on two donkeys, with their faces turned toward the donkeys' rear — then follow him, for he is only a king. But if he rules over them with stoning, beware of him, lest he take from you what is in your hands." They came to him and said: "O Muhammad, this man has committed adultery after being married, with a woman who was also married. Judge between them, for we have made you the judge over them."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked until he came to their rabbis in the bayt al-midras, and said: "O assembly of Jews, bring out your most knowledgeable men to me." They brought out to him Abd Allah ibn Suriya al-A'war. (Some of the Banu Qurayzah related that they had brought out to him that day, along with Ibn Suriya, Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab and Wahb ibn Yahudha, and said: "These are our scholars!") The Messenger of Allah ﷺ questioned them until he established their matter, until they said to Ibn Suriya: "This is the most knowledgeable of those remaining about the Torah."
[Editor's note: Ibn Hisham said in his Sirah: from his words "and al-Zuhri related to me, some of the Banu Qurayzah" up to "the most knowledgeable of those remaining about the Torah" is from Ibn Ishaq's words. What follows of the hadith before it is from the previous narration. Therefore I have placed all of that between two lines.]
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then took him aside. He was a young man, among the youngest of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pressed the question upon him, saying: "O Ibn Suriya, I adjure you by Allah and remind you of His favours upon the Children of Israel. Do you know that Allah ruled in the Torah that one who commits adultery after being married is to be stoned?" He said: "Yes, by Allah! O Abu al-Qasim, they certainly know that you are a prophet sent, but they envy you!"

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and ordered that the two of them be stoned at the door of his mosque, in the area of the Banu Ghanm ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar.
[Editor's note: In the printed edition and the manuscript: "in the Banu Uthman ibn Ghalib ibn al-Najjar", which is a clear error; the correct reading is what I have adopted from Ibn Hisham's Sirah and others. al-Najjar had no son called "Ghalib," nor did Malik ibn al-Najjar have a son called "Uthman."]
Then Ibn Suriya disbelieved after that, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed."
[Editor's note: Report 11921: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 213, 214, in which it follows the earlier report here numbered 11616. This report was narrated by Ahmad in abridged form. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 4: 216-218, nos. 4450, 4451, with wording other than this, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 8: 246, 247. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3: 156. It will come later as nos. 11923, 11924.]

11922 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, [transmission marker] and Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, [transmission marker] and Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ubaydah ibn Humayd narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by a Jewish man who had been blackened and flogged. [Editor's note: In the printed edition: "marra 'ala al-Nabi" with the addition of "ala" as in the other narrations; I have retained what was in the manuscript. Al-muhamm is the one whose face is blackened. "Hammama al-rajul tahmiman" means he blackened his face with coal, which is charcoal.] So the Prophet ﷺ summoned a man of their scholars and said: "Is this how you find the punishment for fornication among you?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "I adjure you by He who sent down the Torah to Musa: is this how you find the punishment for adultery among you?" He said: "No. Had you not adjured me by this, I would not have told you. Rather it is stoning. But adultery became widespread among our nobles, so when we seized a noble we left him, and when we seized a weak man we enforced the punishment upon him. So we said: 'Come, let us gather and put something in place of stoning, so that it applies to the noble and the base alike.' So we established blackening and flogging in place of stoning!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "I am the first to revive your command, since they have caused it to die!" [Editor's note: In the printed edition: "Allahumma inni ana awwal," and I have retained what was in the manuscript, which is similar in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh: 130.] So he ordered him to be stoned, and Allah revealed: "Let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief," to the end of the verse.
[Editor's note: Report 11922: Abu Ja'far narrated it by three chains from al-A'mash. It will come later, nos. 12034, 12036, by way of al-Qasim, from al-Husayn, from Abu Mu'awiyah, and by way of Hannad from Abu Mu'awiyah. Ubaydah ibn Humayd ibn Suhayb al-Taymi was mentioned earlier at nos. 2781, 2998, 8783; the printed edition had "Ubaydah ibn Ubayd," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. Abd Allah ibn Murrah al-Hamdani al-Kharifi was mentioned earlier at no. 8208. This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 11: 209, 210, Ahmad in his Musnad 4: 286, al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 8: 246, Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh: 130, and Abu Dawud in his Sunan 4: 215, no. 4448. Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsir, after citing Ahmad's report, said: "Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains from al-A'mash, by the same." See the continuation of this report at nos. 11939 and 12022.]

11923 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mu'ammar, from al-Zuhri, who said: I was sitting with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and with Sa'id was a man honouring him. He was a man from Mazinah whose father had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and he was one of the companions of Abu Hurayrah. He said: Abu Hurayrah said: "I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ..."

11924 - [transmission marker] and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: A man from Mazinah informed me, one of those who follow knowledge and retain it, who narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that Abu Hurayrah said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man of the Jews came to him. They had consulted among themselves about a companion of theirs who had committed adultery after being married. [Editor's note: In the printed edition: "qad ashiru fi sahib lahum" (they had pointed at a companion of theirs), while the manuscript has "shawaru" (they consulted), which is weak here, so I read it as "tashawaru."] Some of them said to others: 'This Prophet has been sent, and you know that stoning was prescribed upon you in the Torah, but you concealed it and agreed among yourselves on a punishment short of it. Let us go and ask this Prophet. If he rules for us with what was prescribed for us in the Torah, of stoning, we will abandon that, for we have abandoned it in the Torah, and it is more deserving of being obeyed and believed!'" They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, a companion of ours who is married has committed adultery. What punishment do you see for him?" Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not return to them until he stood up, and we stood with him. He set off heading for the house of study of the Jews, until he came to them and found them studying the Torah in the bayt al-midras. He said to them: "O assembly of Jews, I adjure you by Allah who sent down the Torah to Musa: what do you find in the Torah concerning the punishment for one who commits adultery after being married?" They said: "We find that he is blackened and flogged!" Their rabbi remained silent in a corner of the house. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw his silence, he pressed him with the adjuration, so their rabbi said: "O Allah, since you have adjured us, we find that the punishment for them is stoning!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "What was the first thing you became lax about in the command of Allah?" He said: "A cousin of a king committed adultery, and he did not stone him. Then another man committed adultery among a family of people, and that king wished to stone him, but his people stood between him and the man, saying: 'By Allah, you shall not stone him until you stone so-and-so, the king's cousin!' So they agreed among themselves on a punishment short of stoning, and abandoned stoning." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Then I will judge by what is in the Torah!" So Allah revealed concerning that: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief," up to His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers."
[Editor's note: Reports 11923 and 11924: This report of al-Zuhri was narrated by Abu Ja'far earlier by way of Ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri, no. 11921. Its narration will also come with different wording, at no. 12008. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 4: 4450 by way of Mu'ammar from al-Zuhri, and at no. 4451 by way of Ibn Ishaq from al-Zuhri. Ahmad narrated it in abridged form in his Musnad, no. 7747, by way of Abd al-Razzaq, from Mu'ammar, from al-Zuhri, from a man from Mazinah. Abu Ja'far will narrate this report by way of Abd al-Razzaq later, at no. 12008. My brother, al-Sayyid Ahmad, said in his commentary: "Its chain is broken (munqati'), because of the unidentified man from Mazinah who narrated from al-Zuhri." Then he pointed in his takhrij to Abu Ja'far's narration at no. 11921, but did not refer to these two reports, nos. 11923 and 11924, nor to the following report, no. 12008. Then he cited Abd al-Razzaq's narration from Ma'mar verbatim. Then he said: "This man from Mazinah, the unidentified one, was described by al-Zuhri, in the narration of Abu Dawud, by way of Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli from al-Zuhri, as one of those who follow knowledge and retain it," as in this chain, no. 11924, and he overlooked what is in the chain of no. 11923: that he is "a man from Mazinah whose father witnessed al-Hudaybiyah." Despite all this, the man remains unidentified and unknown. Note: review what preceded in the reports on stoning, nos. 11609-11611.]

* *

Others said: Rather, the hypocrites are meant by this.

Those who said this:

11925 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abd Allah ibn Kathir, regarding His words: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed." He said: They are the hypocrites.

11926 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "They say with their mouths, 'We believe.'" He said: He means the hypocrites. "Listeners for others": he said: They are also listeners for the Jews. [Editor's note: Report 11926: In the printed edition, the section from "listeners for others" to the end of the report was omitted, while it is present in the manuscript. It seems the editor found its mention here objectionable, although it comes later in the continuation of the verse, and Mujahid's statement is not mentioned there. This is pointless.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in my opinion, [the printed edition has "wa-awla al-aqwal" without "hadhihi," which is present in the manuscript] is to say: What is meant by His words, "Let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say with their mouths, 'We believe,' but their hearts have not believed" [the printed edition and the manuscript have "'ani bidhalik," but the context requires what I adopted], is a group of the hypocrites. It is possible that Ibn Suriya was among those included in this verse, and it is possible that Abu Lubabah was, and it is possible that others besides them were. But the most authentic thing reported on this is what we mentioned earlier from the narrations of Abu Hurayrah and al-Bara' ibn Azib, because these come from two men among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
