Since that is so, the correct statement on this is to say that it refers to Abd Allah ibn Suriya.

And when that is established, the ta'wil of the verse is: "O Messenger, let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelieve in your prophethood and deny that you are a prophet to Me, from among those who say: 'We affirm you, O Muhammad, that you are a messenger sent by Allah, and we know that with certainty, by our finding your description in our Book.'" [Editor's note: His words "by our finding your description" mean: that we find your description.]

This is because in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that Ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri: [Editor's note: in the report numbered 11921], Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "By Allah, O Abu al-Qasim, they certainly know that you are a prophet sent, but they envy you!" That was, according to this report, a profession of faith in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by Ibn Suriya with his mouth, but he did not affirm it in his heart. So Allah, mighty and majestic, said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, informing him of what was in Ibn Suriya's heart and that he had not believed in his heart, saying: and his heart did not affirm that you are a messenger sent by Allah.

[Editor's note: For the explanations of "hazan" (grieve), see earlier in volume 7: 234, 418; of "sara'a" (hasten), volume 7: 130, 207, 418; and for "min afwahihim" (with their mouths), volume 7: 145-147; and for "yaqulun bi-afwahihim" (they say with their mouths), volume 7: 378, 379.]

* *

On the ta'wil of His words, mighty and majestic is He: "And among those who are Jews are listeners for falsehood, listeners for other people who have not come to you."

Abu Ja'far said: His praise be exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: O Messenger, let not the rush of those hypocrites who rush toward disbelief in you grieve you, those who display their acceptance of you with their tongues while they inwardly hold your denial, nor let the Jews' rush to deny your prophethood grieve you. [Editor's note: see the explanation of "hada" (to be Jewish) earlier, volume 2: 143, 507; volume 9: 391.] Then, mighty and majestic is He, He described their attributes. [The printed edition has "Then He, mighty is His remembrance, described their attributes," which differs from the manuscript for no useful purpose.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 41 (part 2 of 3):

He described them to him by their blameworthy attributes and their base deeds, and informed him, consoling him for the grief he suffers at their denial of him despite their knowing his truthfulness, that they are people who make lawful what is unlawful, and who consume foul food and base provisions from bribes and illicit gain, [[Meaning what will come in verse 42.]] and that they are people of falsehood and lies against God, and of distorting His Book. [[In the printed edition: "wa-tahrif kitabihi" (and distortion of His Book), while in the manuscript: "ahl al-ifk, wa-kadhib 'ala Allah, wa-tahrif kitabihi." I saw that the context requires "wa-tahrif li-kitabihi," so I have kept it.]] Then he informed him that He would bring down upon them disgrace in the immediate world and punishment in the deferred Hereafter. So He said: They are "listeners to falsehood," meaning these hypocrites among the Jews. He says: they listen to lies, and "listeners to a people else who have not come to you" – their listening to the words of their rabbis: that the ruling on a married adulterer in the Torah is blackening the face and flogging. "Listeners to a people else who have not come to you" – he says: they listen to the people of the adulterer who wanted to seek judgment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and they are the other people who had not come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and who were insistent on coming to him, as Mujahid said:
11927 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "Listeners to a people else who have not come to you" – [they are] with those who came to you.
* *
The people of interpretation differed concerning "listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else."
Some of them said: "Listeners to a people else" refers to the Jews of Fadak, and "the other people who had not come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" refers to the Jews of Medina. [[The apparent reading is that there is an error in this rendering by Abu Ja'far, and its correct form seems to be: "Some of them said: 'Listeners to a people else' – the Jews of Medina; and 'the other people who had not come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ' – the Jews of Fadak." The report itself below confirms the correctness of what he chose.]]
Mention of those who said that:
11928 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, who said: Zakariyya and Mujalid narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir, regarding His words: "And among those who are Jews are listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else," he said: the Jews of Medina. "Who have not come to you, distorting words from their places," he said: the Jews of Fadak, who say to the Jews of Medina: "If you are given this, take it."
* *
Others said: What is meant by that is a group of Jews, the relatives of the woman who committed adultery, who sent them to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the ruling concerning her. The ones who sent them are "the other people," and they are the family of the immoral woman, who had not come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Mention of those who said that:
11929 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "And among those who are Jews are listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else who have not come to you, distorting..." – that God had revealed to the Children of Israel: "If any of you commits adultery, stone him." They continued in this until a man from their nobles committed adultery. When the Children of Israel gathered to stone him, the nobles and the notables stood up and prevented it. Then a man from the weak committed adultery, and they gathered to stone him, but the weak gathered and said: "Do not stone him until you bring your companion, so that you stone both of them together!" The Children of Israel said: "This matter has become severe upon us, so come, let us correct it!" So they abandoned stoning and substituted forty lashes with a tarred rope, and they would carry him on a donkey with his face toward its tail, [[In the printed edition: "wa-yuhammimunahu wa-yahmilunahu 'ala himar" (they blacken him and carry him on a donkey), adding "wa-yuhammimunahu," which has no meaning in addition, since what comes later with the same sense is "wa-yusawwidun wajhahu" (they blacken his face). I have kept what is in the manuscript, though it reads "wa-yahmilu-hu 'ala himar."]] and they blacken his face and parade him about. They continued doing this until the Prophet ﷺ was sent and came to Medina. A woman from the nobles of the Jews named Basra committed adultery, so her father sent some men of his companions to the Prophet ﷺ, saying: "Ask him about adultery and what has been revealed concerning it, for we fear that he will disgrace us and inform them of what we have done. If he gives you the flogging, take it; but if he orders you to stone, beware of it!" They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him, and he said: "Stoning!" Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And among those who are Jews are listeners to a people else who have not come to you, distorting words from their places," when they distorted the stoning and made it flogging.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: the "listeners to falsehood" are the "listeners to a people else."
It is possible that those people were from the Jews of Medina, and what was heard for them was from the Jews of Fadak; and it is possible that they were from others. Yet whichever it was, it is a description of a people of the Jews who heard lies about God concerning the ruling on the woman who had committed adultery among them while she was married, and that its ruling in the Torah was blackening and flogging; and they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the ruling that applied to her, and they heard what the people of the immoral woman said about her before they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seeking judgment from him concerning her. They only asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that on their behalf, so that they might inform the family of the immoral woman of what his answer to them would be. If his ruling was not stoning, they would accept him as arbiter among them; but if his ruling was stoning, they would beware of him and abandon acceptance of him and his judgment.
* *
Ibn Zayd said something similar to what we have said.
11930 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else," he said: "to a people else who have not come to you from the People of the Book; these are listeners to those other people who have not come to him, saying to them lies: 'Muhammad is a liar, and this is not in the Torah, so do not believe in him.'" [[At this point, a part of the old division of the manuscript from which our copy was taken has ended. In our manuscript here is the following text:
"Its continuation, God willing, is: The discussion on the interpretation of His words: (distorting words from their places, saying, 'If you are given this, take it, and if you are not given it, beware'). And may God bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace."
Then after it begins: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Lord, make it easy."]]
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "They distort words from their places, saying, 'If you are given this, take it; and if you are not given it, beware.'"
Abu Ja'far said: God, His mention is exalted, says: These listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else among them who have not yet come to you, from the Jews, distort "the words" [[See the explanation of "distorting words from their places" in what has passed, 2:248/8:430-432/10:129.]]. Their distortion of that was changing the ruling of God, His mention is exalted, which He revealed in the Torah concerning married men and women who commit adultery, to stoning, into flogging and blackening. God, His mention is exalted, said: "They distort the words," meaning these Jews, and the meaning is the ruling of the words; so He sufficed with mentioning the report of "distorting the words" instead of mentioning "the ruling," because the listeners know its meaning. Likewise His words: "from their places," and the meaning is: from after God's placing that in its places; so He sufficed with the report of mentioning "its places," instead of mentioning "placing that," as God, His mention is exalted, said: "But righteousness is [in] one who believes in God and the Last Day" [Surah al-Baqarah: 177], and the meaning is: but righteousness is the righteousness of one who believes in God and the Last Day. [[See what has passed: 3:336-339.]]
* *
It may also be that its meaning is: they distort the words from their places, so that "ba'd" (after) is used in place of "'an" (from), as one says: "I came to you from my being free of work," meaning: after my being free from work.
* *
By His words: "If you are given this, take it; and if you are not given it, beware," these transgressing listeners to falsehood mean: if Muhammad gives you the verdict of flogging and blackening concerning our companion, "take it," meaning accept it from him; and if he does not give you that verdict but gives you the verdict of stoning, then beware.
* *
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said in interpreting that.
Mention of those who said that:
11931 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Zuhri narrated to me, saying: I heard a man from Muzayna narrating to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that Abu Hurayra told them, in a story he mentioned: "And among those who are Jews are listeners to falsehood, listeners to a people else who have not come to you," he said: [i.e., those among them who were sent] were sent and stayed behind, [[This addition in parentheses is from the Sira of Ibn Hisham.]] and they ordered them with what they had ordered them, namely the distortion of the words from their places. So He said: "They distort the words from their places, saying, 'If you are given this, take it,'" for the flogging, "and if you are not given it, beware," that is, the stoning. [[Report 11931 – Sira of Ibn Hisham 2:214; it is the continuation of the earlier report no. 11921.]]
11932 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's words: "If you are given this," if this agrees with you, take it. It is the Jews saying it to the hypocrites.
11933 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "If you are given this, take it," if this agrees with you, take it, and if it does not agree with you, beware of it. The Jews say it to the hypocrites.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be glorified and exalted: "And whoever God intends to test, you will not be able to do anything for him against God."
Abu Ja'far said: This is consolation from God, His mention is exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for his grief over the eagerness of those whose story He has related, from the Jews and the hypocrites, in this verse. He says to him, His mention is exalted: Do not let their haste toward denying your prophethood grieve you, for I have decreed upon them that they will not repent from their misguidance, [["hatama 'alayhi": he decreed it upon him and made the judgment obligatory.] nor return from their disbelief, because of what has preceded from My anger against them. Your grief over what you see of their haste toward what I have made the cause of their destruction and their deserving of My threat will not benefit them.

The meaning of "fitna" (testing, trial) in this place is: misguidance from the right path. [[See the explanation of "fitna" in what has passed: 9:123, note 1, and the references there.]]

The discussion on the interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "Those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment." (5:41)

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 41 (part 3 of 3):

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Do not let grieve you those who hasten to disbelief from among the Jews, whose description I have given you." Their hastening toward that means that God has willed their trial, and sealed their hearts, and they will never be guided. ﴿Those are the ones whom God did not will to purify their hearts.﴾ He says: these are the ones whom God did not will to cleanse from the defilement of disbelief and the filth of polytheism, with the purity of Islam and the cleanness of faith, [see the explanation of "purify" (tahara) above, 3:38-40, 393, and the indexes of vocabulary], so that they would repent. Rather, He willed for them disgrace in this world, and that is humiliation and abasement, [see the explanation of "disgrace" (khizy) above, p. 276, note 3, and the references there], and in the Hereafter the torment of Hell, ﴿abiding therein forever.﴾ [See the explanation of the remaining words of the verse in the indexes of vocabulary above.]

* *

In accordance with what we have said about the meaning of "disgrace" (khizy), a statement has been transmitted from Ikrimah.

11941 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Aqmar and others, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿Those are the ones whom God did not will to purify their hearts; for them in this world is disgrace﴾, he said: a city in Rome that will be conquered, and they will be taken captive.

[The report: 11941 – "Ali ibn al-Aqmar ibn Amr ibn al-Harith al-Hamdani", Abu al-Waza' al-Kufi. The scholars of the six books narrated from him. Trustworthy and authoritative. His biography is in al-Tahdhib.
And "Sufyan" is al-Thawri.
In the printed edition it read "Ali ibn al-Arqam," which is a clear error; its correct form is in the manuscript.]

**Commentary on the words of Allah, "Listeners to falsehood, devourers of what is unlawful (al-suḥt)"**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These Jews whose description I have given you, O Muhammad, are "listeners to falsehood and lies," and to what some of them say to others, "Muhammad is a liar and not a prophet," and what some of them say, "The punishment of a married adulterer in the Torah is flogging and blackening the face," and other falsehoods and lies. They also "accept bribes and devour them" in return for their lies against Allah and their fabrications about Him. [Note in the manuscript: "فيأكلوها" (fa-ya'kulūhā); the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]

* *

The root of "al-suḥt" is the ravenous hunger (kalab al-jūʿ). One says of it: "Fulān is masḥūt al-maʿidah" (a man whose stomach is consumed) when he is a glutton who is never found except hungry. The bribe is called "al-suḥt" by analogy: it is as if the one who takes a bribe, out of greed for taking what is given to him of that, is like the one whose stomach is consumed, out of greed for food. One says of it: "saḥtahu" and "asḥtahu," two dialectal forms reported from the Arabs. From it is the saying of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib:

*"And the bite of time, O son of Marwan, has left
of the wealth nothing but a consumed or stripped remnant."*

[Note: Diwan, p. 556; al-Naqa'id, p. 556; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', p. 19; al-Khizanah 2:347; Lisan al-Arab, under *s-ḥ-t* and *j-l-f*. It will come again in the commentary, 16:135, and elsewhere. The verse is from his famous qasidah, and before the verse is:
*"To you, Commander of the Believers, the cares of hopes have carried us,
and the vast, wandering desert of the trackless waste."*
"Al-hawjal" is the wide valley of the land. "Al-mutaʿassaf" is one traveled without knowledge or guide, so he moves through it by wandering. It is also transmitted as "aw mujarraf," which means one whom time has swept away, that is, one whose wealth it has destroyed and left poor. It is also transmitted as "illā mashtan aw mujalaf" with nominative endings on both words, as will come in 16:135 of the commentary. The grammarians have disputed this verse extensively in both its grammar and its interpretation.]

By "al-mashtat" is meant the one whom it has utterly destroyed through its consumption and corruption. From this is His saying: ﴿So He will destroy you with a punishment﴾ [Qur'an 20:61]. The Arabs say of a shaver: "Ashta al-sha'r," meaning he uprooted it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ [5:42].

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them," Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, means: if those other people who have not yet come to you, namely the people of the adulterous woman, come to you seeking judgment, then judge between them if you wish by the truth that Allah has made the judgment in the case of whoever among them committed the act of the adulterous woman; or turn away from them and leave off judging between them if you wish, and the choice is yours in that.

Some of the exegetes said the same as what we have said. Those who said so:

A man of them of low lineage committed adultery, so they stoned him. Then a man of noble rank among them committed adultery, so they blackened his face. Then they paraded him around. Then they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a fatwa, hoping he would agree with them. He said: He issued the fatwa to them concerning stoning, and they rejected it. So he commanded them to summon their rabbis and monks, and he adjured them by Allah: 'Do you find it in the Torah?' They concealed it, except for one man, the youngest of them, a one-eyed man, who said: 'They have lied to you, O Messenger of Allah; it is indeed in the Torah!'"

1194-31. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that the verse in "Surat al-Ma'idah," "And if they come to you, judge between them," was concerning the matter of stoning.

1194-32. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They came to him, meaning the Jews, regarding a woman among them who had committed adultery, asking him about her punishment. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'How do you find it written in your Torah?' They said: 'We are commanded to stone the adulteress!' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that she be stoned. Allah, blessed and exalted, has said: 'And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.'"

1194-33. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, concerning His words, "And if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them," he said: "They used to impose the hadd penalty for fornication, until a young man of them of noble rank committed adultery. Some of them said to others: 'His people will not let you stone him, but flog him and disfigure him!' So they flogged him, and they carried him on a donkey's packsaddle, with his face facing the donkey's tail. [Note: "al-ikāf" is a type of riding gear, like saddles and pack-frames.] Then another, low-born and without rank, committed adultery, and they said: 'Stone him!' Then they said: 'How did you not stone the one before him? Rather, do to this one what you did to him!' When the Prophet (ﷺ) came, they said: 'Ask him, perhaps you will find a concession from him!' So there was revealed: 'And if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them,' down to His words, 'Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.'" [Note: In the manuscript it reads "إلى أن زنى الشاب منهم" ("until the young man among them committed adultery"), but the printed edition's version is more likely correct.]

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning a slain man killed among the Jews, whom some of them had killed.

Those who said so: [The commentary continues in the next part.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 42 (part 2 of 3):

11974 - Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas that the verses in "al-Ma'idah," His saying, "So judge between them or turn away from them," up to His saying, "the just," were revealed only concerning blood-money (diyah) among the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayzah. That was because the slain of the Banu al-Nadir, who had nobility, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "kan lahum sharaf," without the waw; I have added it from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] paid the full blood-money, whereas the Qurayzah used to pay half the blood-money. They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah revealed this concerning them. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ compelled them to the truth in this matter, and made the blood-money in that case equal = and Allah knows best which of these was the case. [[The report: 11974 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 215, 216. In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham it is made clear that His saying "and Allah knows best which of these was the case" is from the words of Ibn Ishaq.
It was also narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. 3434, in abridged form.]]

11975 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Ali ibn Salih, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Qurayzah and al-Nadir were two tribes, and al-Nadir was more noble than Qurayzah. So if a man of Qurayzah killed a man of al-Nadir, he was killed for him. And if a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah, he paid one hundred wasq of dates. [["Al-wasq" (with fatha or kasra on the waw, and sukun on the sin) is the load of a camel, and it is sixty sa' by the sa' of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.]] When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, a man of al-Nadir killed a man of Qurayzah, and they said: "Hand him over to us!" They said: "Between us and you is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" So it was revealed: "And if you judge, then judge between them with justice." [[The report: 11975 - "Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-Absi," has passed many times; see nos. 2092, 2219, and others up to 9456. In the printed edition and manuscript it was "Abd Allah ibn Musa," which is a pure error.
And "Ali ibn Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy al-Hamdani" is trustworthy (thiqah). It has passed as no. 178. See a report with a meaning similar to part of it in what preceded, no. 9896, and Musnad Ahmad nos. 3212, 3434.]]

11976 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: In the judgment of Huyayy ibn Akhtab: a man of al-Nadir has two blood-money payments, [[In the printed edition: "lil-nadri," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] and a man of Qurayzah has one blood-money payment, because he was of al-Nadir. He said: Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of what is in the Torah. He said: "And We prescribed for them therein that the life is for the life," [Surah al-Ma'idah: 45], to the end of the verse. He said: When Qurayzah saw that, they were not content with the judgment of Ibn Akhtab, and said: "We will take our dispute to Muhammad!" Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them," so He gave him the choice. ["And how would they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah?" the whole verse. The custom of the nobleman, if he committed adultery with a lowborn woman, was that they would stone her alone, and they would blacken the face of the nobleman, put him on a camel, and make his face face the camel's tail. And if the lowborn man committed adultery with a noblewoman, they would stone him, and do to her that same thing. So they brought their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, and he stoned her.] He said: The Prophet ﷺ had said to them: "Who among you is most knowledgeable in the Torah?" They said: "So-and-so, the one-eyed!" So he sent for him, and he came. He said: "Are you the most knowledgeable of them in the Torah?" He said: "So the Jews claim." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I adjure you by Allah and by the Torah that He sent down to Moses on the day of Tur Sinai, do you find in the Torah concerning the two adulterers?" He said: "O Abu al-Qasim, they stone the lowborn, and they put the nobleman on a camel, blacken his face, and make his face face the camel's tail; and they stone the lowborn man if he commits adultery with a noblewoman, and do to her that same thing." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I adjure you by Allah and by the Torah that He sent down to Moses on the day of Tur Sinai, what do you find in the Torah?" He kept evading, while the Prophet ﷺ kept adjuring him by Allah and by the Torah sent down to Moses on the day of Tur Sinai, until he said: "O Abu al-Qasim, 'The married man and the married woman, if they commit adultery, then stone them outright.'" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Then it is so; take them away and stone them." Abd Allah said: [[It seems he means "Abd Allah ibn Umar," though he is not named in the report, as will come in the takhrij.]] "I was among those who stoned them, and he kept bending over her, shielding her from the stones with his body, until he died." [[The report: 11976 - The report of Abd Allah ibn Umar about the stoning of the Jewish man and Jewish woman was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, 11: 208, 209, and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 12: 148-152), whose commentary by al-Hafiz is thorough; and in Sunan Abi Dawud 4: 214, no. 4446.]]
* *
Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the ruling of this verse: is it still in effect today? And do the rulers have a choice in judging and considering between the dhimmis and those under treaty when they come to them for judgment, like the choice that was given to His Prophet ﷺ in this verse, or has that been abrogated?

Some of them said: That ruling remains in effect today; nothing has abrogated it, and rulers in every age have a choice by this verse, like the choice that Allah gave to His Messenger ﷺ.

Those who said this:

11977 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi: If someone among the polytheists refers a case to you, then if you wish, judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and if you wish, turn away from them. [[In the printed edition: "a'radtu 'anhum," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

11978 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi and Ibrahim, who both said: If the polytheists come to you and make you judge, then judge between them or turn away from them. And if you judge, judge by the judgment of the Muslims, and do not go beyond it to anything else.

11980 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: If he wishes he judges, and if he wishes he does not judge.

11981 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from al-Sha'bi, who said: If the People of the Book come to you with a matter between them, judge between them by the judgment of the Muslims, or leave them and their own people to judge among them, except in the case of theft or murder.

11982 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata' said to me: We have a choice; if we wish we judge between the People of the Book, and if we wish we turn away and do not judge between them. And if we judge between them, we judge by our judgment among us, or we leave them and their own judgment among themselves. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Shu'ayb said the same. And this is His saying: "So judge between them or turn away from them."

11983 - Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us = and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah = from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi concerning His saying: "So if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them," they both said: When they come to the ruler of the Muslims, if he wishes he judges between them, and if he wishes he turns away from them. And if he judges between them, he judges between them by what is in the Book of Allah.

11984 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "So if they come to you, then judge between them," he said: If they come to you, judge between them by what Allah has revealed, or turn away from them. So Allah gave him a concession in this matter: if he wishes he judges between them, and if he wishes he turns away from them.

11985 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, who both said: If the polytheists come to you and make you judge among them, then judge between them by the judgment of the Muslims and do not go beyond it to anything else, or turn away from them and leave them and their own people.
* *
Others said: Rather, the choice has been abrogated, and the ruler, when the People of the Dhimma refer a matter to him, must judge between them with truth, and he has no right to refrain from considering their case.

Those who said this:

11986 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri: "So if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them," it was abrogated by His saying: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed" [Surah al-Ma'idah: 49].

11987 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: It was abrogated by "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed."
