11994 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri concerning His saying: "So if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them," he said: The sunnah has passed that their rights and inheritances are referred to the people of their religion, unless they come desiring a hadd penalty, in which case they are judged between in it by the Book of Allah.

11995 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When it was revealed: "So judge between them or turn away from them," the Prophet ﷺ, if he wished, judged between them, and if he wished, turned away from them. Then it was abrogated, and He said: "So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires," and he was compelled to judge between them.

11996 - Muhammad ibn Ammar narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, who said: Two verses of this surah were abrogated, meaning "al-Ma'idah": the verse of the garlands, and His saying: "So judge between them or turn away from them." The Prophet ﷺ was given a choice: if he wished he judged, and if he wished he turned away from them, and he returned them to their own judgment, that he judge between them by what is in our Book. [[The report: 11996 - "Sa'id ibn Sulayman al-Dabbi" is Sa'dawayh, a trustworthy and reliable transmitter, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, passed as nos. 611 and 2168.
And "Abbad ibn al-Awwam al-Wasiti" is trustworthy, one of the teachers of Ahmad, passed as nos. 2853 and 5433.
And "Sufyan ibn Husayn al-Wasiti" is trustworthy; they spoke about his transmission from al-Zuhri. Passed as nos. 3471, 6462, 10723.
And "al-Hakam" is "al-Hakam ibn Utaybah," a trustworthy, renowned faqih of the Successors, passed many times.
This report was narrated by Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, through the chain of Sa'id ibn Sulayman with the same wording, traced to Ibn Abbas, and then he said: "This chain is sound, and the people of hadith include it in the Musnad."]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of those who said: The ruling of this verse is established and not abrogated, and that for rulers there is a choice in judging between the People of the Covenant when they refer to them and go to law, and in leaving off judging between them and considering their case, like the choice that Allah gave His Messenger ﷺ in this verse.

We say this is the more correct because those who claimed the ruling of this verse is abrogated asserted that it was abrogated by His saying: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed" [Surah al-Ma'idah: 49]. We have shown in our book "The Clarification on the Foundations of Rulings" (Kitab al-Bayan 'an Usul al-Ahkam) that abrogation is not abrogation unless it is the negation of another ruling in all its meanings, such that it is not permissible for both rulings to hold together with validity in any respect. This has sufficed without repeating it here. [[See his statement on "abrogation" above, 8: 12, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

Since that is so, and since it is not impossible in speech to say: "And that you judge between them by what Allah has revealed," meaning: and that I judge between them by what Allah has revealed when I judge between them, by your choosing to judge between them when you choose to, and not choosing to turn away from them, since the one addressed had already been informed by the speaker that he has the choice to judge or to refrain from judging, it was known by this that there is no indication in His saying "And that you judge between them by what Allah has revealed" that it abrogates His saying "So if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, and if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all, and if you judge, then judge between them with justice," given the possibility of that which we have described. Rather, it is evidence of the same thing that His saying "And if you judge, then judge between them with justice" indicates. [[The context: "Since that is so, and since it is not impossible ... it was known," with the passage following.]]

Since there is no evidence in the apparent wording of the revelation that one of the two verses abrogates the other, nor that the negation of one of the two matters makes the ruling of the other void, and since there is no report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that one of them abrogates the other, and no consensus of the Muslims on that, it is sound for us to say that both matters support each other, their rulings agree, and there is no abrogation of one by the other.
* *
As for His saying "And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all," its meaning is: And if you turn away, O Muhammad, from those among the People of the Book who come to you for judgment, leaving off judging between them regarding what they have brought to you for judgment, then do not judge between them in it, "they cannot harm you at all," meaning: they will have no power to harm you in religion or in worldly matters, so leave off judging between them when you choose to leave off judging between them. [[See the explanation of "al-i'rad" (turning away) above, 9: 310, footnote 1, and the references there. See the explanation of "al-darr" (harm) above, 7: 157.]]
* *
As for His saying "And if you judge, then judge between them with justice," its meaning is: And if you choose to judge and to consider, O Muhammad, between the People of the Covenant when they come to you, "then judge between them with justice," meaning fairness, and that is the judgment by what Allah has made the judgment in such a case over all of His creation, from the community of our Prophet ﷺ. [[See the explanation of "al-qist" (justice) above, p. 95, footnote 3, and the references there.]]
* *
With something close to what we have said on this, a group of the people of interpretation spoke.

Those who said this:

١١٩٩٧ - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim [al-Nakha'i] and al-Sha'bi regarding ﴿And if you judge, judge between them with justice﴾. The two said: If he judges between them, he judges by what is in the Book of God.

١١٩٩٨ - Sufyan told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Ibrahim regarding ﴿And if you judge, judge between them with justice﴾. He said: He was commanded to judge among them by stoning.

١١٩٩٩ - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-Awwam, from Ibrahim al-Taymi regarding His saying ﴿And if you judge, judge between them with justice﴾. He said: By stoning.

٢١٠٠٠ - al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿bil-qist﴾ means "with justice" (bil-adl).

١٢٠٠١ - Hannad told us, saying: Hushaym told us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Ibrahim al-Taymi regarding His saying ﴿then judge between them with justice﴾. He said: He was commanded to judge between them by stoning.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, God loves the just﴾, its meaning is: indeed God loves those who are just in their judgment between people, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-'amilin fi hukmihi bayn al-nas" (those who act in His judgment between people), which is a meaningless statement. The correct reading is what I have established; the copyist certainly garbled it.]] those who judge between them by the judgment of God which He sent down in His Book, and by His command to His prophets, may God's blessings be upon them. [[In the printed edition: "wa amara anbiya'ahu" (and He commanded His prophets), which is a disruption of the context; the correct text is from the manuscript, and the correct vocalization is what I have written: "wa amrihi" (and His command) is a noun conjoined to His saying "in His Book".]]

* *

It is said of this: "Aqsaṭa al-ḥākim fī ḥukmihi" (the judge acted justly in his judgment), [[See the explanation of "aqsaṭa" and "qasaṭa" in what preceded: 6:77, 270/7:541/9:301/10:95, 325]] when he is equitable and rules with truth, "yuqsiṭu iqsāṭan." As for "qasaṭa," its meaning is: oppression (al-jawr). [[His saying: "As for 'qasaṭa,' its meaning is 'oppression'" — this sentence is not in the manuscript, but it is indispensable, so I preferred to retain it as it is in the printed edition. In the printed edition it reads "wa iqsaṭan bihi" with the addition of "bihi," which has no meaning and is not in the manuscript.]] From it is the saying of God, may He be remembered: ﴿And as for the wrongdoers (al-qasiṭun), they will be fuel for Hell﴾ [Surah al-Jinn: 15], meaning by it: those who deviate from the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 43:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And how would they make you judge when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, means: How would these Jews, O Muhammad, make you judge between them, and accept you as a judge between them, "while they have the Torah" which I sent down to Moses, which they acknowledge to be true, and that it is My Book which I sent down to My Prophet [in the printed edition: "upon my Prophet", and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript], and that whatever judgment is in it is from My judgment; they know this and do not deny it or dispute it, and they know that My judgment in it concerning the married adulterer is stoning, and despite their practice of that, "they turn away", meaning: they abandon judgment by it after knowing My judgment in it, out of audacity toward Me and disobedience to Me. [See the explanation of "tawalla" in what has passed, 9:18, note 1, and the references there.]

This, although it is an address from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet ﷺ, is a rebuke from Him to the Jews about whom this verse was revealed. He, exalted is His remembrance, says to them: How do you acknowledge, O Jews, the judgment of My Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, while you deny his prophethood and reject him, and you abandon My judgment, which you acknowledge to be true and obligatory upon you, which Moses brought from Allah? That is: since you abandon My judgment which Moses brought, whose prophethood you acknowledge in My Book, then you are more deserving of abandoning My judgment which My Prophet Muhammad informs you is My judgment, along with your denial of his prophethood.

* *

Then He, exalted is His remembrance, said, informing about the state of these Jews whose description is given in this verse, and the state of their counterparts among those who deviate from His judgment and stray from the path of truth: "And those are not believers", meaning: one who does this deed, i.e., who turns away from the judgment of Allah which He judged in His Book sent down upon His Prophet, among His creatures, is not one who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, acknowledging His oneness and the prophethood of His Prophet ﷺ, because that is not the deed of the people of faith.

* *

The origin of "tawalla 'an al-shay'" (turning away from a thing) is "al-infiraf 'anhu" (departing from it), as in:

12002 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, regarding "then they turn away after that": "Their turning away" is what they abandoned of the Book of Allah.

12003 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And how would they make you judge when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah": he means: the limits of Allah, so He informed of His judgment in the Torah.

12004 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah": i.e., the clarification of Allah concerning what they disputed about the matter of their slain man; "then they turn away after that", the verse.

12005 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said, — meaning the Lord, exalted is His remembrance, — reproaching them: "And how would they make you judge when they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah": he says: the stoning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 44 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged for those who were Jews.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, means: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is the explanation of what these Jews asked you about regarding the ruling on married adulterers [[See the explanation of "guidance" (al-huda) in the earlier index of linguistic terms.]]. "And light" means: in it is the clarification of what had become obscure to them, and the illumination of what had become confused of the ruling. [[See the explanation of "light" (nur) earlier: 5: 424 / 9: 428 / 10: 145.]] "By it the prophets who submitted judged" means: they judged according to the ruling of the Torah on that matter, that is, regarding the matter of the two adulterers on which they had referred to the Prophet ﷺ for judgment. "The prophets who submitted," meaning those who yielded to the judgment of Allah and acknowledged it. [[See the explanation of "submission" (al-islam) earlier in the index of linguistic terms.]]

* *

Allah, exalted is His mention, meant by this our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, in his ruling on married adulterers among the Jews by stoning, and in his equating between the blood of the slain of al-Nadir and Qurayza in retaliation and blood-money; and those prophets before Muhammad judged by what was in it of the command of Allah, as:

12006 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light; by it the prophets who submitted judged," he means the Prophet ﷺ.

12007 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say when this verse was revealed: "We judge the Jews and those other than them among the people of the religions."

12008 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: A man from Muzayna narrated to us while we were with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman, [[In the printed edition: "bi-imra'a" (with a woman); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq. See the takhrij.]] and they said to one another: "Let us go to this Prophet, for he has been sent with leniency. If he gives us a ruling other than stoning, we will accept it and argue with it before Allah, saying: 'A ruling of a prophet from Your prophets!'" He said: They came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: "O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who committed adultery?" He did not speak a word to them until he came to their house of study, [[In the printed edition: "bayt al-midras"; in the manuscript: "bayt midras", with the letter "ta" written above "midras" as a sign of error. What I have written is correct, from the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq. The explanation of "bayt al-midras" has passed earlier, p. 303, note 1.]] and he stood at the door and said: "I adjure you by Allah who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah concerning one who commits adultery when he is married?" They said: "He is blackened and paraded, and flogged." "Al-tajbih" is that the two adulterers be placed on a donkey, with their napes facing each other, and be paraded around. A young man [among them] remained silent, [[What is between the brackets is an addition from the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]] and when he saw him silent, he pressed him with the adjuration. [[""Alaṭṭa bihi" means he insisted upon him; its explanation has passed earlier, p. 304, note 2. "Al-nashda" means adjuring by Allah. It is said: "nashadtuka Allah nashdatan wa nashdatan" (with the nun open or kasra) and "nashdanan" (with kasra): I adjured you by Allah.
In what my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad transmitted from the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq (the manuscript): "al-nashid"; my brother said: "In Abu Dawud: al-nashda," and in Abu Ja'far's narration from 'Abd al-Razzaq there is another difference from him. "Al-nashid" is raising the voice, so they said. In my view it is a verbal noun of "nashadtuka Allah," to be added to its verbal nouns.]] He said: "O Allah, since you adjure us, we find stoning in the Torah!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "What was the first thing you relaxed the command of Allah concerning?" [[In the printed edition: "ma irtakhasa amr Allah"; in the manuscript: "ma yuhassis" (unpointed), which is an error beyond doubt. I have written what is in the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq.]] He said: "A man of kin to a king of our kings committed adultery, so they postponed the stoning for him." [[His saying "fa-akhkhara 'anhu al-rajm" means: he removed the punishment from him; as though he kept it away from him and turned it aside from reaching him. In the report, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Umar: "Akhkhir 'anni ya 'Umar" (Turn away from me, O 'Umar). They said concerning its meaning: "It means: put your opinion or yourself aside," abbreviating for eloquence. So they were brief in explaining it, but he meant the sense of turning it away and keeping it at a distance, and in this report it is in the sense I have explained. This is among what may be added to the lexicon books, or to their clarification, according to the more correct view.]] Then a man committed adultery among the common people [[In the printed edition: "fi usra min al-nas" (in a family of the people); this is similarly in the manuscript of the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq, and likewise in the Sunan of Abu Dawud and others. They explained it saying: "al-usra: the man's clan and household, for he is strengthened by them."
However, I affirm what is clear in the manuscript: "fi uswa" with the waw, and the waw there is very clear, large-headed; I do not think the copyist put it that way on his own, but rather I believe he found the "waw" clear in the ancient copy of the Tafsir from which he transmitted, so he wrote it clearly for that reason. If what is in the manuscript is sound, it is in my view more likely than the reading "fi usra." Its meaning is that they say: "The people are equal (uswa) in this matter," that is, their state in it is one. So by his saying "fi uswa min al-nas" he meant: his state is the state of all other people, not of their nobles or of the people of the royal house among them; so he is treated as the common people are treated. And there has come in reports about the stoning of the two Jews: "When we seized the noble we left him, and when we seized the weak we imposed the prescribed punishment upon him" (see what has passed, number 11922). So by his saying "fi uswa min al-nas" he means that he was one of their weak and common people. This is more likely in my view than "fi usra min al-nas," for it would suggest that he had a clan that protects him, defends him and strengthens him through them, which is contrary to what the context of this report indicates.
Had I not found no decisive proof in hand, I would say that what is in the manuscript is the correct reading. For I recall reading a similar expression in other than this place, and I strove to find it but did not succeed. If I find it elsewhere I will record it, God willing, and it would be proof for the meaning I have explained; and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.]] So he wished to stone him, but his people stood between him and it and said: "Do not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him!" So they agreed upon this punishment among themselves. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, I judge by what is in the Torah!" So he ordered them both, and they were stoned. [[al-Zuhri said: We were told that this verse was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light; by it the prophets who submitted judged," and that the Prophet among them was (judging by it).]] [[The report: 12008. See the takhrij of this report earlier in the commentary on the two reports, numbers 11923 and 11924.
My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad transmitted it in the Musnad of Ahmad in the commentary on the report numbered 7747, from the manuscript of the Tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq, and did not point to its place here in the Tafsir of al-Tabari. I have explained the difference between the two narrations in the earlier notes.]]

12009 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima, regarding His saying: "By it the prophets who submitted judged": the Prophet ﷺ and those before him of the prophets judged by what is in it of the truth.

12010 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "By it the prophets who submitted judged," he means the Prophet ﷺ. "For those who were Jews," he means the Jews. [[See the explanation of "hada" earlier, p. 309, note 1, and the references there.]] So judge among them and do not fear them.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿And the rabbis and the scholars [judged] by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses over it.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, means: And they judge by the Torah and its rulings which Allah revealed in it in every age, according to what they were commanded to judge by in it, together with the prophets who submitted: "the rabbis and the scholars."

* *

"Al-rabbaniyyun" is the plural of "rabbani," and they are the scholars, the wise, those perceptive in governing people and managing their affairs and attending to their interests. "Al-ahbar" are the scholars.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-rabbaniyyin" earlier with its evidences and the sayings of the people of interpretation concerning it. [[See the explanation of "al-rabbaniyyun" earlier: 6: 540, 544, where there is an explanation that the one who knows language cannot do without.]]

* *

As for "al-ahbar," they are the plural of "hibr," which is the scholar who firmly knows a thing; and from it it was said of Ka'b: "Ka'b al-Ahbar."

Al-Farra' used to say: The most I have heard the Arabs say for the singular of "al-ahbar" is "hibr" with a kasra on the "ha'." [[See the explanation of "al-ahbar" earlier: 6: 541, 542 (report 7312), then p. 544.]]

* *

Some people of interpretation used to say: By "al-rabbaniyyin and al-ahbar" in this place are meant the two sons of Suriya, who acknowledged to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the ruling of Allah exalted is His mention in the Torah concerning the married adulterers.
Mention of who said that:

12011 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: There were two Jewish brothers called the two sons of Suriya, who had followed the Prophet ﷺ but had not embraced Islam, and they gave him a covenant that he would not ask them about anything in the Torah without their informing him of it. One of them was a rabbi and the other a habr. They only followed the Prophet ﷺ in order to learn from him. He called them, asked them, and they told him the matter of how it was when the noble man committed adultery and the poor man committed adultery, and how they had altered it. Then Allah revealed: "Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light; by it the prophets who submitted to those who were Jews judged," meaning the Prophet ﷺ; "and the rabbis and the scholars," they are the two sons of Suriya, "for those who were Jews." Then he mentioned the two sons of Suriya, saying: "And the rabbis and the scholars [judged] by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses over it."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter, in my view, is to say: Allah exalted is His mention informed that the Torah is judged by it by the submitting prophets for the Jews, and by the rabbis among His creatures and the scholars. It may be that by this were meant the two sons of Suriya and others besides them, but the submitting prophets and every rabbi and scholar have entered the apparent meaning of the revelation. There is no indication in the apparent meaning of the revelation that a specific group of the rabbis and scholars is meant, nor has any proof been established for that which must be accepted. So every rabbi and scholar is included in the verse by the apparent meaning of the revelation.

* *

The people of interpretation agreed with what we have said in interpreting "al-ahbar."
Mention of who said that:

12012 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salama, from al-Dahhak: "Al-rabbaniyyun" and "al-ahbar": their reciters and their jurists.

12013 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan: "The rabbis and the scholars": the jurists and the learned.

12014 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Al-rabbaniyyun": the learned jurists, and they are above "al-ahbar." [[Report 12014: see his saying from Mujahid with another chain, number 7312.]]

12015 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Al-rabbaniyyun": the jurists of the Jews; "and al-ahbar": their scholars.

12016 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima: "And the rabbis and the scholars": all of them judge by what is in it of the truth.

12017 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Al-rabbaniyyun": the rulers; "and al-ahbar": the scholars.

* *

As for His saying, "by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah," its meaning is: The submitting prophets judge by the ruling of the Torah, and the rabbis and the scholars, meaning the learned, judge by what they were deposited with of the knowledge of the Book of Allah, which is the Torah.

* *

The "ba'" in His saying "by what they were entrusted with" is connected to "al-ahbar."

* *

As for His saying, "and they were witnesses over it," it means: that the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah, judge by the Torah together with the submitting prophets for those who were Jews, and they were witnesses over the judgment of the submitting prophets for those who were Jews, that they judged over them by the Book of Allah which He sent down to His Prophet Moses and His judgment over them, [[See the explanation of "witnesses" (shuhada') earlier in the index of linguistic terms (shahida).]] as:

12018 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And they were witnesses over it," he means the rabbis and the scholars were witnesses for Muhammad ﷺ concerning what he said, that it is the truth that came from Allah, so he is the Prophet of Allah Muhammad; the Jews came to him, and he judged between them with the truth.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿So do not fear the people, but fear Me, and do not exchange My signs for a small price.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, is addressed to the scholars of the Jews and their rabbis: Do not fear the people in implementing My judgment which I have decreed upon My servants, and in enforcing it upon them as I commanded; for they cannot bring you harm or benefit except by My permission. Do not conceal the stoning which I made a ruling in the Torah on married adulterers; rather, fear Me above every person of My creation, for benefit and harm are in My hand, and fear My punishment for concealing what you were entrusted with of My Book. [[See the explanation of "fear" (al-khashya) earlier: 9: 517, note 2, and the references there.]] As:

12019 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So do not fear the people, and fear Me," he says: Do not fear the people so that you conceal what I have sent down.

* *

As for His saying, "and do not exchange My signs for a small price": He says: Do not take, by abandoning judgment according to the signs of My Book which I sent down to Moses, O scholars, a base return; and that is "the small price." [[See the explanation of "purchase" (al-ishtira') earlier: 8: 542, note 2, and the references there; and the explanation of "the small price" earlier: 7: 500, note 3, and the references there.]]

He, exalted is His mention, only meant to forbid them from consuming unlawful gain (al-suht) for their distortion of the Book of Allah and their alteration of its judgment concerning the married adulterers and other rulings which they changed seeking bribes. As:

12020 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying, "and do not exchange My signs for a small price," he said: Do not consume unlawful gain in exchange for My Book. And on another occasion, Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying, "and do not exchange My signs for a price," he said: Do not take a bribe with it. [[In the manuscript: "concerning His saying: lā tashtir thamanan, he said: lā ta'khudh bihi rishwa"; I have left what is in the printed edition as it is.]]

12021 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not exchange My signs for a small price," and do not take a little greed in exchange for concealing what I sent down. [[In the printed edition: "ta'aman qalilan" (a little food); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the earlier reports. See the earlier reports numbers 821, 2498, 8333.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers (al-kafirun). (44)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His mention, means: Whoever conceals the ruling of Allah which He sent down in His Book and made a judgment among His servants, hiding it and judging by other than it, like the judgment of the Jews concerning the married adulterers by blackening and parading, and their concealment of the stoning, [["Al-tajbih" and "al-tahmim" have had their explanation in the earlier reports and notes.]] and like their judgment in the case of some of their slain with a full blood-money and in the case of others with half the blood-money, and among the nobles by retaliation and among the lowly by blood-money; whereas Allah had equated all of them in the ruling upon them in the Torah. "Then those are the disbelievers": He says: these are the ones who did not judge by what Allah sent down in His Book, but altered and changed His ruling, and concealed the truth which He sent down in His Book. "They are the disbelievers": He says: they are the ones who covered the truth which it was incumbent upon them to uncover and clarify, and concealed it from the people, showing them something else and judging by it, for an unlawful gain they had taken from them for it. [[See the explanation of "disbeliever" (al-kafir) earlier in the index of linguistic terms (kafara).]]

* *

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the interpretation of "disbelief" (al-kufr) in this place.

Some of the scholars said something similar to what we have said, namely that it refers to the Jews who distorted the Book of Allah and changed its ruling.

Mention of those who said this:

12022. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abū Mu'āwiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allāh ibn Murra, from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers" [5:44]; "those are the wrongdoers" [5:45]; "those are the defiantly disobedient" [5:47]. He said: "These are all about the disbelievers." [Editor's note: The report 12022 was discussed at length earlier under no. 11922, and its continuation under no. 11939. Abū Ja'far (al-Ṭabarī) related it there in abridged form, and here is its full text.]

12023. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: Abū Ḥayyān narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: "The three verses in al-Mā'ida, 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers,' [and] 'those are the wrongdoers,' [and] 'those are the defiantly disobedient': none of them applies to the people of Islam; they are about the disbelievers." [Editor's note: Abū Ḥayyān is Yaḥyā ibn Sa'īd ibn Ḥayyān al-Taymī, mentioned earlier under nos. 5382, 5383, 6318, 8155. In the manuscript here it reads "Abū Ḥabbāb," and in the following report too; the reading adopted in the printed edition seems more likely. See the note on the following report.]

12024. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abū Ḥayyān, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," and "the wrongdoers" and "the defiantly disobedient." He said: "These verses were revealed concerning the People of the Book." [Editor's note: "Abū Ḥabbān" is Yaḥyā ibn Sa'īd ibn Ḥayyān al-Taymī; see the note on the preceding report. Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī narrates from al-Ḍaḥḥāk. The printed edition also has "Abī Ḥabbāb" here; see the same note.]

12025. Muḥammad ibn 'Abd al-A'lā narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Imrān ibn Ḥudayr say: Some men from Banū 'Amr ibn Sadūs came to Abū Mijlaz and said: "O Abū Mijlaz, what do you think of Allah's words: 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers'? Is it true?" He said: "Yes!" They said: "'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the wrongdoers'; is it true?" He said: "Yes!" They said: "'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the defiantly disobedient'; is it true?" He said: "Yes!" They said: "O Abū Mijlaz, do these people [the rulers] judge by what Allah has sent down?" He said: "It is their religion, which they follow, which they profess, and to which they call. If they abandon any part of it, they know they have committed a sin!" They said: "No, by Allah, but you are evading!" [Editor's note: The printed edition has "ولكنك تعرف" ("but you know"), which is a misreading; the correct reading is in the manuscript: "فرق يفرق فرقًا" meaning he became fearful and anxious.] He said: "You are more entitled to this than I am! I do not see it, and you see this and do not feel guilt. Rather, these verses were revealed concerning the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists," or something close to this.

12026. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, from 'Imrān ibn Ḥudayr, who said: A group of Ibāḍiyya sat with Abū Mijlaz. They said to him: "Allah says: 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers,' 'those are the wrongdoers,' 'those are the defiantly disobedient'!" Abū Mijlaz said: "They act on what they know" [meaning the rulers] "and they know it is a sin!" He said: "These verses were revealed only concerning the Jews!" They [the Ibāḍiyya] said: "By Allah, you know the same as what we know, but you fear them!" He said: "You are more entitled to this than we are! As for us, we do not know what you know!" [They] said: "Rather you know it, but fear of them prevents you from carrying out your affair!" [Editor's note: The context requires adding what appears in the brackets, since it is a reproach from them to Abū Mijlaz and to everyone who holds his view, in contrast with the Ibāḍiyya.] [Editor's note: The printed edition has "إنهم يعملون ما يعملون"; the manuscript has "إنه يعملون بما يعملون," and the correct reading is the one adopted here.]

[Editor's note on reports 12025 and 12026: I disavow to You, O Allah, from error. Furthermore, those of doubt and strife who have set themselves up to speak in our time have sought to excuse the rulers for abandoning judgment by what Allah has sent down, and for judging over blood, honour and property by other than the law of Allah which He sent down in His Book, and for adopting the law of the disbelievers as a legal system in the lands of Islam. When they came upon these two reports, they took them as an opinion by which they justify judging over property, honour and blood by other than what Allah has sent down, and claim that opposing the law of Allah in general judgment does not make disbelievers of those who approve of it or who act upon it.

Whoever reads these two reports cannot avoid knowing the questioner and the one questioned. Abū Mijlaz (Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd al-Shaybānī al-Sadūsī) was a trustworthy Successor (tābi'ī), and he loved 'Alī (may Allah be pleased with him). The people of Abū Mijlaz, the Banū Shaybān, were supporters of 'Alī at the battles of the Camel and Ṣiffīn. When the matter of the two arbiters (al-ḥakamān) came up at Ṣiffīn, and the Khawārij (Kharijites) separated, a group from Banū Shaybān and from Banū Sadūs ibn Shaybān ibn Dhuhl was among those who rebelled against 'Alī (may Allah be pleased with him). Those who questioned Abū Mijlaz were some men from Banū 'Amr ibn Sadūs (as in report 12025), and they were a group of Ibāḍiyya (as in report 12026). The Ibāḍiyya are one of the Ḥarūriyya branch of the Khawārij; they are the followers of 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ al-Taymī (see this commentary, vol. 7, pp. 152–153, note 1). They hold the same position as the rest of the Khawārij concerning arbitration and concerning declaring 'Alī a disbeliever for accepting the two arbiters, and that 'Alī did not judge by what Allah sent down in the matter of arbitration. Then 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ said that whoever opposes the Khawārij is a disbeliever but not a polytheist, and his companions differed with him, and the Khawārij maintained that the rulings for polytheists apply to those who oppose them.

After 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ, the Ibāḍiyya split into sects so that we do not know, in the matter of these two reports, which of these groups those questioners belonged to. However, all the Ibāḍiyya say that the abodes of those who oppose them are abodes of monotheism, except the camp of the ruler, which they regard as an abode of disbelief. They also say that everything Allah has obligated on His creatures is faith, that every major sin is ingratitude (kufr niʿma), not disbelief of polytheism, and that those who commit major sins are in the Fire forever, eternally abiding in it.

It is clear that those Ibāḍiyya who questioned Abū Mijlaz only wanted to hold him to proof regarding declaring the rulers disbelievers, because they were in the ruler's camp, and because they sometimes disobeyed or committed some of what Allah had forbidden them. That is why he said to them in the first report (no. 12025): "If they abandon any part of it, they know they have committed a sin," and he said to them in the second report: "They act on what they do and they know it is a sin."

Therefore, their question was not about what the innovators of our time argue for: judging over property, honour and blood by a law that opposes the law of the people of Islam, nor about issuing a binding law upon the people of Islam to submit to a judgment other than the judgment of Allah in His Book and upon the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ). This act is turning away from the judgment of Allah, aversion to His religion, and preferring the rulings of the people of disbelief over the judgment of Allah, the Exalted and Majestic. This is disbelief about which no one among the People of the Qiblah disagrees, despite their differences over declaring disbelief in the one who holds it and calls to it.

What we are facing today is the abandonment of the rulings of Allah entirely without exception, the preference for rulings other than His judgment in His Book and the sunna of His Prophet, and the nullification of everything in the law of Allah. The matter has reached the point of arguing for preferring the rulings of man-made law over the rulings of Allah which He sent down, and those who argue for this claim that the rulings of the Sharia were only revealed for a time other than ours, and for causes and reasons that have passed, so all the rulings have lapsed with their passing. Where is this from what we have explained of the report of Abū Mijlaz and the group of Ibāḍiyya from Banū 'Amr ibn Sadūs!

Even if the matter were as they imagined in the report of Abū Mijlaz, that they wanted to oppose the ruler in a ruling of the Sharia, it has never happened in the history of Islam that a ruler enacted a ruling and made it a binding law to judge by. That is one point. Another: a ruler who judges in a particular case by other than Allah's judgment on it either judged while ignorant, in which case his position is that of one ignorant of the Sharia; or he judged it through desire and disobedience, in which case this is a sin which repentance covers and forgiveness reaches; or he judged it while interpreting, reaching a ruling which opposes all the scholars, in which case his ruling is that of every interpreter who draws his interpretation from acknowledging the text of the Book and the sunna of the Messenger of Allah.

As for whether there was, in the time of Abū Mijlaz or before or after him, a ruler who judged a matter while denying a ruling of the Sharia, or preferring the rulings of the people of disbelief over the rulings of the people of Islam, that never happened at all. So it is impossible to direct the words of Abū Mijlaz and the Ibāḍiyya to that. Whoever argues with these two reports and others in a context other than theirs, and directs them away from their meaning, out of desire to support a ruler, or as a stratagem to justify judging by other than what Allah has sent down and imposed on His servants, his ruling in the Sharia is the ruling of one who denies a ruling of Allah. He should be asked to repent; if he persists, is obstinate, denies the judgment of Allah, and accepts the changing of the rulings, then the ruling on the disbeliever who persists in his disbelief is well known to the people of this religion. Read the words of Abū Ja'far after p. 358, from his statement "If one says," for there is a decisive statement in it. The detailed discussion of the error of those who use these two reports as evidence, and of the reports that came here in interpreting this verse, would require extensive elaboration; I have been content with what I have now written. Written by Maḥmūd Muḥammad Shākir.]

12027. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us. [And] Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān; from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Ḥudhayfa regarding His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers." He said: "The Children of Israel are indeed fine brothers for you! If you have all the sweetness, they have all the bitterness! And you will surely follow their path, [matching them] step for step (qidā al-shirāk)!" [Editor's note: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit al-Asadī, trustworthy and truthful; mentioned earlier under nos. 9012, 9035, 10423. Abū al-Bakhtarī is Sa'īd ibn Fayrūz al-Ṭā'ī, a trustworthy Successor who narrates from 'Umar, Ḥudhayfa, Salmān and Ibn Mas'ūd. Ibn Sa'd said in al-Ṭabaqāt (6:204): "Abū al-Bakhtarī narrated much hadith, transmitted it as mursal, and narrated from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but he did not hear directly from any of the senior ones. What of his narrations was by direct hearing is good, and what was 'from' (ʿan) is weak." He appeared earlier under nos. 175 and 1497; this report is therefore munqaṭiʿ (broken in its chain), because Abū al-Bakhtarī did not hear from Ḥudhayfa.

As for His words: "qidā" (with a kasra on the qāf and a fatḥa on the dāl), it is said: "he is at a spear's length from me" (qīd rumḥ, with kasra on the qāf), "qād rumḥ" and "qidā rumḥ" with the same meaning, that is: the measure of a spear. Hudba ibn al-Khashram said:

"And indeed, when death is not between me and it except the span of a palm,
I protect my nose from retreating."

"Al-shirāk" is the strap of a sandal, and it is used as a proverb for smallness and shortness. The meaning is: your affair would not differ except by the measure of such-and-such.

In the printed edition here it reads "qadr al-shirāk," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript for this report and for no. 12030.

The report of Ḥudhayfa was related by al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak (2:312–313), by way of Jarīr, from al-A'mash, from Ibrāhīm, from Hammām, who said: "We were with Ḥudhayfa, and they mentioned: 'And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers,' and a man from the group said: 'This is about the Children of Israel!' Ḥudhayfa said: 'Indeed, the Children of Israel are fine brothers! If you have the sweet, they have the bitter! No, by the One in whose hand is my soul, until you follow the sunna step by step, as the feather of an arrow follows the feather (qudhdha bi-l-qudhdha).'" Al-Ḥākim said: "This is a ṣaḥīḥ hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabī agreed. "Al-sunna" means the followed path. "Al-qudhdha" is the feathers of an arrow, arranged one against another so that it comes out even.]

12028. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abū Ḥayyān, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," and "the wrongdoers" and "the defiantly disobedient." He said: "These verses were revealed concerning the People of the Book."

12029. Hannād ibn al-Sarī narrated to us, saying: Wakī' narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, who said: It was said to Ḥudhayfa: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," and then he mentioned something like the report of Ibn Bashshār, from 'Abd al-Raḥmān.

12030. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, who said: A man asked Ḥudhayfa about these verses: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," "those are the wrongdoers," "those are the defiantly disobedient." He said: It was said: "Is that about the Children of Israel?" He said: "Indeed, the Children of Israel are fine brothers for you! If they have all the bitterness, you have all the sweetness! No, by Allah, you will surely follow their path, [matching them] step for step (qidā al-shirāk)!" [Editor's note: Two other chains for report 12027. In the last report here the printed edition reads "qadr al-shirāk"; the manuscript reading is adopted. See the earlier note.]

12031. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from a man, from 'Ikrima, who said: "These verses are about the People of the Book."

12032. Bishr ibn Mu'ādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatāda regarding His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers." He said: "It was mentioned to us that these verses were revealed concerning the Jewish victim who was among them." [Editor's note: In the printed edition: "في قيل اليهود" ("in the saying of the Jews"); the manuscript has "في قبيل اليهود" ("among the tribe of the Jews"), and the latter is correct. The account of this victim has been mentioned many times and will come shortly under no. 12037.]

12033. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima regarding His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," "the wrongdoers," and "the defiantly disobedient": for all of the People of the Book, because of what they abandoned of the Book of Allah.

12034. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Abū Mu'āwiya narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allāh ibn Murra, from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, who said: A Jewish man was passed by the Prophet (ﷺ), blackened (muḥamam) and flogged. He called them and said: "Is this how you find the punishment for one who commits adultery in your scripture?" They said: "Yes!" He called a man from among their scholars and said: "I adjure you by Allah who sent down the Torah to Mūsā, is this how you find the punishment for the adulterer in your book?" He said: "No. And if you had not adjured me by this, I would not have told you. We find its punishment in our book to be stoning (rajm), but it became widespread among our nobles, so when we seized a noble we let him go, and when we seized a commoner we enforced the punishment on him. So we said: 'Come, let us all agree on blackening the face (taḥmīm) and flogging in place of stoning.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, I am the first to revive Your command when they had let it die!" He then ordered him to be stoned. So Allah revealed: "O Messenger, let not those who race to disbelief grieve you" [5:41], up to His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers" [5:44], meaning the Jews; "those are the wrongdoers" [5:45], meaning the Jews; "those are the defiantly disobedient" [5:47], for all the disbelievers. [Editor's note: This report's full earlier treatment is under no. 11922, and it will come under no. 12036.]

12035. Yūnus ibn 'Abd al-A'lā narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers," he said: "Whoever judges by a book he wrote with his own hand, and abandons the Book of Allah, and claims that this book of his is from Allah, has disbelieved."

12036. Hannād narrated to us, saying: Abū Mu'āwiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allāh ibn Murra, from al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to the report of al-Qāsim, from al-Ḥasan. Except that Hannād said in his report: "We said: 'Come, let us agree on something we establish over the noble and the weak,' so we agreed on blackening the face and flogging in place of stoning," and the rest of the report is similar to the report of al-Qāsim. [Editor's note: The report is 12034, whose earlier treatment is under no. 11922 and no. 12034.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 44 (part 3 of 3):

12037 - Al-Rabi' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from his father, who said: We were with Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, when a man mentioned in his presence: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers" [5:44], "...they are the wrongdoers" [5:45], "...they are the defiantly disobedient" [5:47]. Ubayd Allah said: By Allah, indeed many people interpret these verses in a way they were not revealed for. They were revealed only concerning two tribes of the Jews. Then he said: They are Qurayza and al-Nadir. That is because one of the two groups had raided the other and overpowered it before the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, until they agreed and reconciled on the terms that for every slain person whom the powerful group killed from the humble group, the blood-money would be fifty wasq, ["al-Wathq" (with a fatha or kasra on the waw): the load of a camel, or sixty sa', a measure used by them.] and for every slain person whom the humble group killed from the powerful group, the blood-money would be one hundred wasq. They gave them [the humble group] fear and oppression. ["Al-Faraq" (with two fathas): fright and dread. "Al-Daym": injustice. He means: they accepted that out of fear of their assault and dread, and they consented to the oppression from them.] Then the Prophet ﷺ came while they were still in this arrangement, and both groups were humbled by the Prophet's ﷺ arrival, while the Prophet ﷺ had not yet gained dominance over them. While they were in this state, a member of the humble group killed a man from the powerful group, and the powerful group said: Give us one hundred wasq! The humble group said: Has this ever occurred between two tribes with one religion and one land, where the blood-money of some is double the blood-money of others? We only gave you this out of fear and oppression. Let us place Muhammad ﷺ between us and you. They agreed to make the Prophet ﷺ their arbiter. Then the powerful group deliberated among themselves, ["In the manuscript: 'nakarat' without dots, and what is in the printed edition fits the meaning; I know of no reading of what is in the manuscript except 'fakarat bayna-ha' (they thought between themselves), but it is faulty."] and feared that the Prophet ﷺ would not give them double what they give their own people from among them. So they sent to the Prophet ﷺ their brothers from among the hypocrites, and said to them: Inform us of Muhammad's ﷺ opinion; if he gives us what we want, we will submit to his judgement, and if he does not give us, we will beware of him and not submit to his judgement. The hypocrite went to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, exalted is His remembrance, informed the Prophet ﷺ of all that they intended in that matter. Ubayd Allah said: So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, revealed concerning them: "O Messenger, let not those who race to disbelief grieve you" [5:41], these verses entirely, until He reached: "And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein" [5:47], up to "the defiantly disobedient" [5:47]. Ubayd Allah recited that verse by verse and explained it according to what was revealed, until he finished explaining it to them in the verses. ["What is between the brackets is an addition that I consider necessary."] Then he said: The reference there is only to the Jews, and this description was revealed concerning them.

* *

Some others said: By "the disbelievers" is meant the people of Islam, by "the wrongdoers" the Jews, and by "the defiantly disobedient" the Christians.

Those who said this:

12038 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Amir, who said: "The disbelievers" was revealed concerning the Muslims, "the wrongdoers" concerning the Jews, and "the defiantly disobedient" concerning the Christians.

12039 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The disbelievers" refers to the Muslims, "the wrongdoers" to the Jews, and "the defiantly disobedient" to the Christians.

12040 - Ibn Wakī', Abu al-Sa'ib and Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shubrumah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: One verse concerns us, and two verses concern the People of the Book: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers" concerns us, and concerning them: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the wrongdoers," and "the defiantly disobedient" concerns the People of the Book.

12041 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir, the same as the report of Zakariyya from him. [i.e., no. 12038.]

12042 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha'bi: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: This is concerning the Muslims. "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the defiantly disobedient," he said: The Christians.

12043 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said, concerning these verses in "al-Ma'idah": "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: concerning us, the people of Islam. "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the wrongdoers," he said: concerning the Jews. "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the defiantly disobedient," he said: concerning the Christians.

12044 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: The first was revealed concerning the Muslims, the second concerning the Jews, and the third concerning the Christians.

12045 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Zakariyya, from al-Sha'bi, similarly.

12046 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ya'la narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Amir, similarly.

* *

Others said: Rather, by that is meant: disbelief short of disbelief, injustice short of injustice, and defiance short of defiance.

Those who said this:

12047 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', concerning His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," "...they are the wrongdoers," "...they are the defiantly disobedient," he said: disbelief short of disbelief, defiance short of defiance, and injustice short of injustice.

12048 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ata', the same.

12049 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, similarly.

12050 - Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', similarly.

12051 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', similarly.

12052 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id al-Makki, from Tawus: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It is not a disbelief that removes one from the religion.

12053 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It is disbelief in that act, and it is not disbelief in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers. [[The report 12053: the report of Tawus from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2: 313) by way of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Hisham ibn Hujayr, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas: "It is not the disbelief they go to; it is not disbelief that removes one from the religion, "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers" [5:44], a disbelief short of disbelief." This is his wording. Then he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi said: "Sahih."]]

12054 - Al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas concerning these verses: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed" — so whoever does this has disbelieved? Ibn Abbas said: If he does that, then it is disbelief in that act, and it is not like one who disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day, and such and such.

12055 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It is disbelief in that act. He said: Ibn Tawus said: And it is not like one who disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers.

12056 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from a man, from Tawus: "Then they are the disbelievers," he said: A disbelief that does not remove one from the religion. He said: Ata' said: disbelief short of disbelief, injustice short of injustice, and defiance short of defiance.

* *

Others said: Rather, these verses were revealed concerning the People of the Book, but they are meant to include all people, both Muslims and unbelievers.

Those who said this:

12057 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: These verses were revealed concerning the Children of Israel, and He approved them for this community.

12058 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It was revealed concerning the Children of Israel, and He approved it for you.

12059 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim concerning this verse: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It was revealed concerning the Children of Israel, then He approved it for these.

12060 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, and it is binding upon us.

12061 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Alqamah and Masruq, that they asked Ibn Mas'ud about bribery, and he said: It is from the unlawful gain. They said: Is it in judgement? He said: That is disbelief! Then he recited this verse: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers."

12062 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed," he says: And whoever does not judge by what I have revealed, deliberately abandoning it and oppressing while knowing, he is among the disbelievers.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, denying it. As for "injustice" and "defiance", it applies to the one who acknowledges it.

Those who said this:

12063 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, they are the disbelievers," he said: Whoever denies what Allah has revealed has disbelieved. And whoever acknowledges it but does not judge by it, he is a wrongdoer and defiantly disobedient.

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: These verses were revealed concerning the disbelieving People of the Book, because what precedes them and what follows them of verses were revealed concerning them, and they are the ones intended by them. And these verses are the continuation of the report about them, so that they be a report about them is more appropriate.

* *

If someone says: Indeed Allah, exalted is His remembrance, has used the report of that to encompass all who do not judge by what Allah has revealed; so how have you made it specific?

It is said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, used the report of that to encompass a people who, by the judgement Allah had given in His Book, were deniers, and He informed that they, by their abandoning judgement in the manner they abandoned it, are disbelievers. And likewise the statement regarding everyone who does not judge by what Allah has revealed while denying it: he is a disbeliever in Allah, as Ibn Abbas said, because by his denial of Allah's judgement after knowing that He revealed it in His Book, it is akin to his denial of the prophethood of His Prophet after knowing that he is a prophet.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 45 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the life is for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and for wounds is retaliation﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We prescribed for these Jews who come to you for judgment, O Muhammad, and with them is the Torah, in which is the judgment of God.

By His saying "And We prescribed" [[See the explanation of "kataba" (prescribed) above, p. 232, footnote 1, and the references there.]] and "We prescribed for them therein" He means: that they should judge in the matter of a life, if one takes a life without right, "the life for the life", meaning: the killer who kills a soul is to be killed for the soul he killed; "and the eye for the eye", He says: We prescribed for them therein that the eye of the one who blinded another's eye be blinded in the same way, for the blinded eye; "and the nose for the nose", and the ear is cut off for the ear, and the tooth is pulled for the tooth, and the one who wounds is retaliated against for his wound, without wronging the one wounded. [[See the explanation of "qisas" (retaliation) above, vol. 3, pp. 357–366, and then vol. 3, p. 579, footnote 1.]]

This is information from God, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ concerning the Jews, and a consolation from Him to him for the disbelief of those among them who disbelieved in him after acknowledging his prophethood, and who turned away from him after having turned towards him; and it is an informing from Him to him of their audacity, in the past and the present, toward their Lord and the messengers of their Lord, and their advancing over the Book of God with distortion and alteration.

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to him: How would these Jews, O Muhammad, be content with your judgment when they come to you for judgment, while they have the Torah which they acknowledge to be My Book and My revelation to My messenger Moses ﷺ, in which is My judgment of stoning for married adulterers, and My decree among them that whoever kills a soul unjustly is liable to retaliation for it, and whoever blinds an eye without right, his eye is blinded in retaliation, and whoever cuts off a nose, his nose is cut off, and whoever pulls out a tooth, his tooth is pulled out, and whoever wounds another with a wound, he is retaliated against with a wound like the wound he inflicted? Then they, along with the judgment in the Torah that is among My rulings, turn away from it and abandon acting by it. He says: They, by abandoning your judgment and being displeased with your decision between them, are more deserving and more fitting [of censure].

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Those who said so:

They said: As for the reward of the one who pardons and gives charity, it is upon God.

12090. Hannad and Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, both saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim and Mujahid, regarding "But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him," they both said: "for the one to whom it is given as charity, and the reward of the one who was struck is with Allah." 12101. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying: "And wounds are subject to retaliation. But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him," he said: Whoever is wounded and gives charity of the thing with which he was wounded to the one who wounded him, then there is no way against the one who wounded him, no retaliation, no blood money, and no sin upon him, because the one who was wounded gave it to him as charity; so it is an expiation for him for the wrong he committed. [[In the printed edition: "no wound upon him", and the correct reading is what I have written; the manuscript is undotted.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions in this matter, in my view, is the saying of the one who said that it means "But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him" refers to the wounded person. So the pronoun in His saying "for him" referring back to "whoever" is more appropriate than that it refer to someone who has not been mentioned except implicitly rather than explicitly. It is even more fitting, since in all other charities besides this one, it is the charity that expiates the sin of its giver, not of the one to whom it is given. So it is obligatory that this case follow the path of the other charities. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "meaning by it: whoever gives it as charity", and the context requires what I have written.]]

* *

If someone supposes that retaliation (qisas) (the exacting of an equal punishment for a crime, "the law of equal retribution"), since it expiates the sin of the one against whom it is carried out, the one who committed the killing of another unjustly, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ when he took the pledge from his companions: "Do not kill, do not commit adultery, do not steal," then he said: "Whoever does any of that and has its legal penalty (hadd) enforced upon him, it is his expiation." [[In the printed edition: "like the saying of the Prophet ﷺ", and what I have written is correct.]] [[This report was narrated by Abu Ja'far in abridged form, without isnad, and it is a sound report. See Sahih Muslim 11:222-224.]] then it is obligatory that the pardon of the one who pardons, the one who was wronged, or the guardian of the one who was killed, should be similar to it in that it is an expiation for him. [[Context: "If someone supposes that retaliation, since it expiates the sin of its doer ... then it is obligatory that the pardon of the one who pardons ... be similar to it."]] But if that were so, then the pardon of the one falsely accused of adultery toward his accuser, and his abandoning of the legal penalty due to him, while he was accused by his accuser, though he is chaste, Muslim and married, would have to be an expiation for the accuser from his sin that he committed and his disobedience that he perpetrated. And we know of no scholar among the people of knowledge who says that.

So since it is not permissible that the abandonment by the one falsely accused (whom we have described) of enforcing the legal penalty due to him upon his accuser should be an expiation for the accuser from the sin he committed, it is likewise not permissible that the abandonment by the wounded person of enforcing his right of retaliation upon the one who wounded him should be an expiation for the wounder from the sin he committed.

* *

If a speaker says: Do you not hold that the wounded person has the right to take from his wounder blood money for his wound in place of retaliation?
It is said to him: Yes!
If he says: What do you think if he chooses the blood money and then pardons it, would he have a claim against him in the Hereafter?
It is said to him: This statement is, in our view, impossible. That is because in our view one who chooses blood money is not choosing it except while he is taking it. As for pardon, it is pardon of the blood itself. We have proven the soundness of that in another place, with what makes repeating it here unnecessary. [[See what has passed: 3:371, and what came before it.]] Unless what is meant by that is giving it as a gift to the one from whom he took it after taking it. Moreover, even if his pardon of the blood money after choosing it were sound, there would be nothing in its soundness that requires that the one pardoned from it be free from the punishment for his sin before God; because God, mighty is His mention, has threatened the slayer of a believer with what He threatened him with, if he does not repent from his sin, and the blood money is taken from him, whether he likes it or is angry. Repentance from the penitent is only repentance if he chooses it, desires it, and prefers it over persistence.

* *

If a speaker supposes that, even if that is so, it must be an expiation for him, just as retaliation was an expiation for him, then we only hold that retaliation is an expiation for him when he feels remorse and offers himself to take the right from it, as a disassociation from his sin, based on the report of the Prophet ﷺ.

As for blood money, when the wounded person chooses it and then pardons it, and so he is not sentenced to the legal penalty for his sin, he is not among those who fall under the ruling of the Prophet ﷺ and his saying: "Whoever has the legal penalty enforced upon him, it is his expiation." Then, among what confirms the soundness of what we have said on this matter are the reports we mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his saying: "Whoever gives blood as charity," [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "whoever gives it as charity", and what I have written is correct; it is the text of the report that passed, number 12100.]] and what is similar to that among the reports we mentioned earlier.

* *

It may be that those who said that it refers to the wounder intended the meaning that was related from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, which is:

12102. Al-Harith ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Al-Qasim ibn Sallam related to us, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Sallam related to us", and in the manuscript: "al-Qasim al-Harith ibn Sallam", then "al-Qasim" and "al-Harith" were struck through, and beside "al-Qasim" a correction mark was placed, which is (sah).]] Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: If a man strikes another man and the one struck does not know who struck him, and then the one who struck him admits it to him, it is an expiation for the one who struck. He said: Mujahid used to say concerning this: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr struck the eye of a person at the corner (the Black Stone) where they touch (it) [[In the manuscript: "where they greet", and I have left what is in the printed edition as it is, which is close to correct. In Abu Hayyan's tafsir 3:497: "wa-hum yastalimun" (while they touch it), which is better.]], so he said to him: "O man, I am Urwa ibn al-Zubayr. If there is any harm to your eye, then I am responsible for it!"

* *

When the matter of the wounder is like what happened with Urwa, of an unintentional error of action, and then he admits to the one who was struck what befell him, and the one struck pardons him of his right against him, then there is no claim against the one who struck, neither in this world nor in the next. That is because what was due to him from him was property, not retaliation, and he has released him from it. So his release of him is an expiation for the one released from the right which he had to take from him. [[In the printed edition: "an expiation for him from his right", and in the manuscript: "an expiation for *lmtzamr [undotted] from his right", and what I have written is the correct reading.]] Therefore there is no demand for him against him because of that, neither in this world nor in the next, nor a punishment that he is obligated to bear because of what he did to the one who struck him, since he did not intentionally strike him with what he struck him with, so that by his act he would be sinful, deserving punishment from his Lord. [[In the printed edition: "so that by his act he is only deserving of punishment", which is meaningless, and "innama" as in the manuscript, undotted, and the correct reading is what I have written.]] Because Allah, mighty and majestic, has lifted blame from His servants for what they did in error and did not intend in their actions. He said in His Book: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you did in error, but for what your hearts intended﴾. [[In the manuscript and printed edition, the verse is written as: "and there is no blame upon you for what you erred in", and there is nothing in what we recite like this verse; it is the verse of al-Ahzab, as I have written.]] [Surah al-Ahzab: 5]

* *

And "charity" (tasaddaq), in this place, regarding blood, means pardoning it. [[In the printed edition: "and it may be meant in this place by blood, pardoning it", which is a statement with no meaning and no clear sense. In the manuscript: "wa-* in this place by blood, pardoning it", with a blank between the two statements, and in the margin the letter (ṭ) indicating an error, so I deduced the correct wording from the context of the tafsir of this verse.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, mighty is His mention: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers﴾ (45)

Abu Ja'far said: Mighty is His mention says: And whoever does not judge by what Allah revealed in the Torah concerning retaliation for a soul that kills, a soul for a soul that was unjustly killed, and does not gouge out the eye of the one who gouged an eye with the eye of the one whose eye was gouged, unjustly, as retaliation from the one whom Allah commanded in His Book to do so; but he takes retaliation from some and does not take it from others, or he kills two for one in some cases. Indeed, whoever does that is among the "wrongdoers" [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "and indeed whoever does that", and the context requires what I have written.]], meaning: one who has deviated from the judgment of Allah, and has placed his act, in what he did of that, in other than the place that Allah made its place. [[See the explanation of "injustice" (zulm) in the indexes of language earlier.]]
