Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, in His saying: ﴿And We sent after them, following in their footsteps, Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah. And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, and confirming what was before it of the Torah, as guidance and an admonition to the God-fearing﴾ (46).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "We sent after them" [[See the explanation of qaffa (to follow) in what has preceded, 2:318.]], He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: We caused to follow. He says: We caused Jesus son of Mary to follow in the footsteps of the prophets who submitted before you, O Muhammad, and We sent him as a prophet confirming Our Book which We sent down to Moses before him, that it is true, and that acting upon what the Gospel did not abrogate from it is an obligatory duty. "And We gave him the Gospel" — He says: We sent down to him Our Book whose name is "the Gospel" — "in it is guidance and light" — He says: in the Gospel is "guidance," which is the clarification of what people had been ignorant of regarding the judgment of God in his time — "and light," He says: and illumination from the blindness of ignorance. "And confirming what was before it" — He says: We revealed that to him and sent it down to him, confirming what was before it of the Books of God which He had sent down to every nation to whom a book was sent down through its prophet, for acting upon what was sent down to their prophet in that book, including the permission of what He permitted and the prohibition of what He prohibited.

"And guidance and admonition" — He says: We sent down the Gospel to Jesus confirming the Books before it, and as a clarification of the judgment of God which He approved for His God-fearing servants in the time of Jesus. "And admonition" to them — He says: and a deterrent from what God dislikes toward what He loves of deeds, and an alert to them concerning it.

"Al-muttaqun" (the God-fearing) are those who feared God and beware of His punishment, so they guard themselves (ittaqa) against Him by obeying Him in what He commanded them, and beware of Him by abandoning what He forbade them to do. The explanation of this with its evidences has passed before, so repeating it is unnecessary. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the language indices of what preceded.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the words of the Exalted: ﴿And let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein; and whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiant (al-fasiqun)﴾ (5:47)

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in their reading of His words "wa-liyahkum ahl al-Injil" (let the people of the Gospel judge).

The reciters of the Hijaz, Basra, and some of the Kufans read "wa-liyahkum" with the "lam" (of the imperative) pronounced with sukun, in the form of a command from God to the people of the Gospel: that they should judge by what God revealed in it of His rulings. It seems that whoever read it this way intended: "We gave him the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Torah, and We commanded its people to judge by what God revealed in it." So there is an omitted element in the sentence, left out because what is mentioned makes it unnecessary.

* *

Some people of Kufa read it: ﴿wa-liyahkum ahl al-Injil﴾ with the "lam" pronounced with a kasra, from "liyahkum," meaning: "so that the people of the Gospel may judge." The sense for whoever read it this way is: "We gave him the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Torah, so that its people might judge by the ruling of God contained in it."

* *

What we say on this matter is that both are well-known readings, close in meaning; whichever reader recites either of them is correct in doing so.

That is because God, exalted is He, has never sent down a book to any of His prophets except to be acted upon by its people, who were commanded to act upon what is in it. He did not send it down to them except that He had commanded them to act upon what is in it. So it was sent down for acting upon what is in it, and sent down as a command to act upon what is in it. Likewise the Gospel, since it is one of the books of God which He sent down to His prophets: it was sent down to Jesus for acting upon what is in it, and sent down to him as a command to its people to act upon it. Therefore, whether it is read as a command with the "lam" pronounced with sukun, or as a statement with it pronounced with a kasra, both meanings agree.

* *

As for what is reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he read it as ﴿wa-an liyahkum﴾ in the imperative form, this is a report that has not been authentically transmitted from him. Even if it were authentic, it would not follow that the reading differing from it is forbidden, since its meaning is sound, and the earlier leading reciters had read it that way.

* *

Since the matter stands as we have explained, the interpretation of the sentence, when read with a kasra on the "lam" of "liyahkum," is: "We gave Jesus son of Mary the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Torah, and guidance and admonition for the God-fearing; and so that the people of the Gospel might judge by what We revealed in it. But they altered its ruling and opposed it, and they went astray by their opposition to it, in that they did not judge by what God revealed in it and they contradicted it." Then "those are the defiant" means: those who went outside the command of God in it, opposing Him in what He commanded and forbade them in His book.

* *

As for when it is read with sukun on the "lam," its interpretation is: "We gave Jesus son of Mary the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Torah, and We commanded its people to judge by what We revealed in it. But they did not obey Us in our command to them regarding what We had commanded them in it; rather they opposed Our command. So those who opposed Our command which We had commanded them in it, they are the defiant."

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say that "al-fasiqun" in this place and elsewhere means "the liars."

12103 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "And let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein; and whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiant": "And whoever among the people of the Gospel also does not judge by that - then it is those who are the defiant," he said: "the liars." He said this. Ibn Zayd also said: Everything in the Qur'an that is "fasiq" is a liar, except in a few cases. And he recited the saying of God: ﴿O you who have believed, if a defiant (fasiq) comes to you with a report﴾ (49:6), and said: "The fasiq here is a liar."

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "fisq" (defiance, transgression) with its evidences earlier, sufficiently to not repeat it in this place.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 48 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of meaning) of the words of God, the Mighty, the Remembered: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Book and as a guardian over it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an address from God, the Remembered, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). He, the Remembered, says: We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, "the Book," which is the Qur'an that He sent down to him. By His words "in truth," He means in sincerity, with no falsehood in it, and there is no doubt that it is from God. [[See the explanation of "al-haqq" (truth) earlier: 7:97 / 9:227.]] "Confirming what came before it of the Book" means: We sent it down confirming the books of God that He sent down to His prophets before it.

"And as a guardian over it" means: We sent down the Book that We sent down to you, O Muhammad, confirming the books before it, and bearing witness over them that they are true and from God, trustworthy over them, and preserving them.

* *

The root of *al-hayminah* (guardianship, watchfulness) is preservation and vigilant oversight. It is said: when a man watches over a thing, preserves it and witnesses it, "So-and-so has *hayman* over it; he *yuhayminu haymanah*, and he is *muhaymin* over it."

* *

Those who discuss interpretation have said things similar to what we have said, though their expressions differ.

Some of them said: its meaning is "a witness."

Those who said this:

12103. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and as a guardian over it," that he said: "a witness."

12104. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "a witness over it."

12105. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Book": he said, "the books that came before it." "And as a guardian over it": "trustworthy and a witness over the books that came before it."

* *

12106. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "entrusted over the Qur'an, and a witness and confirmer." Ibn Juraij said: others said: the Qur'an is a trustee over the books: when the People of the Book inform us of a matter in their book, if it is in the Qur'an, they are truthful; otherwise, they are lying. [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Juraij and others said," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: its meaning is "trustworthy over it."

Those who said this:

12107. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us; and Hannad ibn al-Sari related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, both from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and as a guardian over it," that he said: "entrusted over it."

12108. Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and as a guardian over it," that he said: "entrusted over it."

12109. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Sufyan and Israil related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

12110. Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan and Israil, from Abu Ishaq, with his chain, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

12111. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Atiyyah related to us, saying: Israil related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

12112. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

12113. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Amr, from Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of Tamim, from Ibn Abbas, the same. [[Traditions 12107–12113: "al-Taymi" and "a man of Tamim" refer to Arbadah al-Taymi, who related the tafsir from Ibn Abbas, and it was transmitted from him by Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i. It appeared earlier under nos. 1928 and 1929. My brother Sayyid Ahmad wrote on tradition no. 2095 and I wrote on traditions 3986–3989 that he was an unknown man from Tamim, but the correct view is that he is well known: he is Arbadah al-Taymi, a trustworthy Successor. See also the following traditions, 12116–12118.]]

12114. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and as a guardian over it," he said: "The *muhaymin* is the trustworthy. The Qur'an is trustworthy over every book before it."

12115. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Book": it is the Qur'an, a witness over the Torah and the Gospel, confirming them. "And as a guardian over it" means: trustworthy over it, judging over the books that came before it.

12116. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Qays, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "entrusted over it."

12117. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of the Banu Tamim, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "entrusted over it."

12118. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Yahya al-Himmani related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, the same. [[Traditions 12116–12118: "al-Taymi" and "a man of the Banu Tamim" is Arbadah al-Taymi; see the note above.]]

12119. Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us; and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us: from Sufyan and Israil, from Ali ibn Badhimah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding "and as a guardian over it," he said: "entrusted over what came before it of the books."

12120. Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I asked al-Husayn about His words "And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Book and as a guardian over it." He said: "confirming these books, and trustworthy over them." And Ikrimah was asked about it while I was listening, and he said: "entrusted over it."

* *

Others said: the meaning of *al-muhaymin* is "confirming."

Those who said this:

12121. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "and as a guardian over it": "confirming over it. Every thing God sent down, whether Torah, Gospel or Psalms, the Qur'an confirms over it. And everything God mentioned in the Qur'an confirms them and what has been related about them as true."

* *

Others said: by His words "confirming what came before it of the Book and as a guardian over it," He means the Prophet of God (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

12122. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "Muhammad (ﷺ), entrusted with the Qur'an."

12123. Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "and as a guardian over it": "Muhammad (ﷺ), entrusted with the Qur'an."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: the meaning of the sentence according to Mujahid's interpretation is: "We sent down to you the Book, confirming the books before it, as a guardian over them." In that case, "confirming" is a state (*hal*, a circumstantial qualifier) of "the Book" and part of it, the "confirmation" is an attribute of "the Book," and "as a guardian" is a state of the "kaf" (the "you") in "to you," which is a reference to the name of the Prophet (ﷺ). The "ha'" in His words "over it" refers back to the Book.

* *

This interpretation is far from the sense in the usage of the Arabs; it is indeed an error. That is because *muhaymin* is conjoined (*'atf*) to *musaddiq* (confirming), so it can only be an attribute of that to which *musaddiq* is an attribute. If the meaning of the sentence were what is reported from Mujahid, it would have been said: "And We have sent down to you the Book, confirming what came before it of the Book, as a guardian over it." [[In the printed and manuscript texts, "and as a guardian" appears with a conjunction "wa," and the correct reading omits it, because he means to omit the conjunction, since "as a guardian" is a state of the "kaf" in "to you," not conjoined to anything before it, as you see in the rest of his statement.]] Because nothing preceding that is an attribute of the "kaf" in "to you" comes after it as a conjoined "as a guardian over it." Rather, it is conjoined to "confirming," because it is an attribute of "the Book," whose attribute is "confirming." [[In the printed edition, "because it is preceded by an attribute of the kaf in 'to you' and there is nothing after it..." adds "and there is nothing," which is not in the manuscript, and changes "yatadamma" to "mutaqaddim," since the manuscript had an error and he misunderstood. The manuscript had the reading I have given, except that the scribe wrote "because it precedes an attribute of the kaf in 'to you,'" dropping the particle "lam," which I have restored, and the sentence is then sound.]]

* *

If someone supposes that "confirming," according to Mujahid's interpretation and this explanation, is an attribute of the "kaf" in "to you," then His words "what came before it of the Book" invalidate that this could be the interpretation, and that "confirming" be an attribute of the "kaf" in "to you." That is because the "ha'" in His words "before it" is a pronoun referring to someone other than the addressee, namely the Prophet (ﷺ) in "to you." [[In the manuscript: "and the Prophet, may God bless him..." without "huwa"; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]] If "confirming" were an attribute of the "kaf," the sentence would be: "And We have sent down to you the Book, confirming what is before you of the Book, and as a guardian over it." The meaning of the sentence would then be as follows. [[In the manuscript: "the meaning of the sentence then would be 'yakun' (would be) like this," with an added "yakun"; the correct reading is that of the manuscript, unless the scribe dropped something from the sentence. Nevertheless, the printed text is sound.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His, the Remembered's, words: ﴿So judge between them by what God has sent down, and do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from God, the Remembered, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to judge between those who bring their disputes to him from the People of the Book and all the other religious communities, by His Book that He sent down to him, which is the Qur'an, which He singled out with His law. He, the Remembered, says: Judge, O Muhammad, between the People of the Book and the polytheists by what has been sent down to you of My Book and My rulings in everything they bring to you for judgment, concerning the prescribed punishments (*hudud*), wounds, retaliation (*qawad*) and killings. Stone the married adulterer, and kill the soul that kills with the soul that is slain unjustly, gouge out the eye for the eye, and slit the nose for the nose. For I have sent down to you the Qur'an, confirming in that what came before it of the books and as a guardian over them, a witness, judging over all the other books before it. Do not follow the desires of these Jews, who say: "If you are given flogging for the married adulterer instead of stoning, and killing the lowly for the noble if he kills him, but not killing the noble for the lowly if he kills him, then take it; and if you are not given it, beware" [[Context: "Do not follow the desires of these Jews... concerning what has come to you from God."]] from what has come to you from God of the truth, which is the Book of God that He sent down to you. He tells him: act by My Book that I have sent down to you when they bring their disputes to you and you choose to judge between them, and do not abandon acting by that out of following their desires and preferring them over the truth that I have sent down to you in My Book, as:

12124. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "So judge between them by what God has sent down," he said: "by the limits of God," and "do not follow their desires away from the truth that has come to you."

12125. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun related to us, from Anbasah, from Jabir, from Amir, from Masruq, that he used to make the Jew and the Christian swear by God. Then he recited: ﴿And that you judge between them by what God has sent down﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:49], [[In the manuscript: "then he recited: 'If they come to you, judge between them by what God has sent down.' The correct proof-text in this verse of al-Ma'idah (5:42) reads: 'If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them,' and it contains no evidence for what you seek concerning making them swear by God, the Mighty and Majestic.]] And God sent down: ﴿Do not associate anything with Him﴾ [Surah al-An'am 6:151].

* *

On the interpretation of His, the Remembered's, words: ﴿For each of you We have made a law (*shir'ah*) and a way (*minhaj*)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, the Remembered, says: For every people among you We have made a law. [[See the explanation of "kull" (each) earlier: 3:193 / 6:209 / 8:269.]]

* *

*Al-shir'ah* is the same as *al-shari'ah* (the sacred law, the path of religion), and the plural of *al-shir'ah* is *shira'*, [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "its plural is *shira'*," which is a clear error by a scribe, for the plural of *fi'lah* (with kasra then sukun) is formed on *fi'al* (kasra then fatha) in the sound and other forms, like *kisr* and *lihan* (paralleling *kasr*, "broken," and *lihan*, "jaws"). The form *fi'lah* also takes *fi'al*, which is rare, as in the plurals of *liqhah* (milch camel) and *liqah*, and *haqqah* (a camel of a certain age) and *haqaq*. So it is possible that *shira'* is a rare plural of *shir'ah*, but in such cases the closer form is to mention the plural prescribed by regular analogy.]] and *al-shari'ah* has the plural *shara'i'*. If *al-shir'ah* were pluralized as *shara'i'*, it would be correct, because its meaning and the meaning of *al-shari'ah* are one, so at the plural it is returned to the form of its equivalent. Whatever you begin (*shara'ta*) in any matter is a *shari'ah*. From this it is said that the watering-place of water is a *shari'ah*, because one approaches the water from it. And from it the sacred laws of Islam are called *shara'i'*, because its adherents begin (*shuru'*) in it. And from it it is said of a people who are equal in something: "They are *shara'*," equal.

* *

As for *al-minhaj*, its root is the clear, evident path. It is said of it: "It is a path that is *nahj* and *manhaj*," clear, as the rajaz poet said: [[Apparently a rajaz poet of the Banu al-Anbar ibn Amr ibn Tamim.]]

*Whoever is in doubt, then this is Falj*
*Water sweet, and a path clearly marked*

[[*Majaz al-Qur'an* of Abu Ubaydah 1:168; *Mu'jam ma Asta'jam* 1027; *al-Lisan* (r-w-y). Their version all reads "Whoever is in doubt" (*man yakun dha shakk*), but it is so given in the manuscript and printed text. "Falj" (with fatha, then sukun) is the water of the Banu al-Anbar ibn Amr ibn Tamim, whose mention is frequent in Tamimi poetry, and they praise its water. Some Bedouin said: "Ah, a drink of water from a cloud over the rock, its news recent from the subjugated clouds / to a rasaf from the belly of Falj, as if when you taste it it is a night-water, sugar-water." "Water sweet" (*ma' rawa'*, with fatha on the *ra'*) is sweet water in which the drinkers find satisfaction.]]

Then it is used of anything that was clear, evident and easy.

* *

So the meaning of the sentence is: For every people among you We have made a path to the truth that they aim for, and a clear way to act by.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about who is meant by His words "For each We have made among you."

Some of them said: by this He means the adherents of different religious communities, that is, God made for each religion a law and a way.

Those who said this:

12126. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "For each of you We have made a law and a way," he said: "a path and a sunnah. The sunnahs differ: the Torah has a law, the Gospel has a law, the Qur'an has a law, in which God makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills, as a trial, to know who among those who obey Him and who among those who disobey Him. But the one religion that is not accepted besides it is: monotheism and sincerity to God, which the messengers brought."

12127. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "For each We have made among you a law and a way," he said: "The religion is one, and the law is different."

12128. Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali, who said: "Faith, since God, the Remembered, sent Adam (ﷺ): the testimony that there is no god but God, and the affirmation of what has come from God. For each people is what has come to them of law or way; so the one who affirms is not an abandoner, but is obedient." [[Tradition 12128: I do not know who "Abdullah ibn Hashim" is. It has passed in the two chains nos. 7329 and 7938 with this same chain. "Sayf ibn Umar al-Tamimi" passed under nos. 7329 and 7938, and he is a discarded transmitter (*saqit al-riwayah*). In the printed edition here as well, as in the two mentioned chains, the name is given as "Sayf ibn Amr," which is a plain error.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, by this he meant the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ). They said: The meaning of the speech is: We have made the Book which We sent down to Our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), O people, for every one of you, i.e., for everyone who has entered Islam and acknowledged that Muhammad (ﷺ) is His Prophet, a shir'ah (law) and a minhaj (way).

Mention of those who said this:

12129 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning his words: "For each We have made a law and a way among you." He said: "Sunnah" (the custom/path). "And a minhaj": the road. "For every one of you": whoever enters the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ), God has made for him a shir'ah and a minhaj. He says: the Qur'an is for him a shir'ah and a minhaj.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: For every community among you, O nations, We have made a shir'ah and a minhaj.

We said that this is more correct because of His words: "And had God willed, He would have made you one community" (﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾). Had He meant by "For each We have made among you" the Ummah of Muhammad, who are one community, then His words "And had God willed, He would have made you one community" would have no clear meaning, since He did make them one community. Rather, the meaning, according to the address God directed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), is this: He mentioned what was prescribed for the Children of Israel in the Torah, and enjoined upon them to act by what is in it. Then He mentioned that He followed up with Jesus son of Mary upon the traces of the prophets before him, and sent down to him the Gospel, and commanded those to whom he was sent to act by what is in it. Then He mentioned our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and informed him that He had sent down to him the Book confirming what lies before it of the Book, and commanded him to act by what is in it and to judge by what was sent down to him in it, rather than by what is in the other books. And He informed him that He had made for him and his Ummah a law different from the laws of the prophets and nations before him, whose stories He related to them. Although their religion and his religion—in the oneness of God, the affirmation of what came to them from Him, and submission to His command and prohibition—are one, they differ in their circumstances: what He prescribed for you differs from what He prescribed for them, and what He made lawful for them and forbade them differs for you.

* *

Those experts in interpretation who said regarding "shir'ah" and "minhaj" what we have said also said the following.

Mention of those who said this:

12130 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Mis'ar related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj": he said: a sunnah and a path.

12131 - Hannad related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj," he said: a sunnah and a path.

12132 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il and his father, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, similarly.

12133 - Hannad related to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Razi related to us, from Abu Sinan, from Abu Ishaq, from Yahya ibn Wathhab who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His words: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj," and he said: a sunnah and a path. [[Note on this report: "Abu Yahya al-Razi" or "Abu Yahya al-Abdi" is Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi, reliable. Passed as no. 6456. "Abu Sinan" is Sa'id ibn Sinan al-Burjumi. He related from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, and Ishaq ibn Sulayman Abu Yahya al-Razi related from him. Passed as nos. 175, 11240. In the printed edition it read "Abu Shaybân", which is a clear error. "Yahya ibn Wathhab al-Asadi" the reciter. He related from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, and Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i related from him. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was reliable, few in narrations, a man of Qur'an." Passed as no. 11488.]]

12134 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Aliyyah related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas: "a shir'ah and a minhaj," he said: a sunnah and a path.

12135 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Amr, from Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of Banu Tamim, from Ibn Abbas, similarly.

12136 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Taymi, from Ibn Abbas, similarly.

12137 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his words: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj," meaning: a path and a sunnah.

12138 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "The shir'ah" is the sunnah.

12139 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid who said: a sunnah and a path. [[Note on this report: "Abu Yahya al-Qattat al-Kinani," whose name is disputed. He is weak and spoken of critically. Entry in al-Tahdhib.]]

12140 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "shir'ah and minhaj," he said: "The shir'ah" is the sunnah, "and minhaj" is the path.

12141 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

12142 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas concerning his words: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj," meaning: a path and a sunnah.

12143 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hawdi related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: Abu Ishaq related to us, saying: I heard a man of Banu Tamim, from Ibn Abbas, similarly. [[Note on this report: "al-Hawdi" is Hafs ibn Umar ibn al-Harith ibn Sakhbarah al-Namari, Abu Umar al-Hawdi, reliable, firm and precise. Passed as no. 11449.]]

12144 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "shir'ah and minhaj," he said: a path and a sunnah.

12145 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas who said: the sunnah and the path.

12146 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning his words: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj," he said: a path and a sunnah.

12147 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed me, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning his words: "shir'ah and minhaj," he said: a path and a sunnah.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: "And had God willed, He would have made you one community, but to try you in what He has given you."

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance is exalted; He says: Had your Lord willed, He would have made your laws one, and would not have made for each community a shir'ah and a minhaj different from the laws and ways of the other nations. You would have been one community whose laws and ways do not differ. But He, may His remembrance be exalted, knows this, and so He made your laws differ in order to test you, so that He may know the obedient among you from the disobedient, and the one who acts by what He commanded in the Book which He sent down to His Prophet (ﷺ) from the one who opposes it.

* *

"Ibtila'" (trial) means testing (ikhtiyar), and I have explained this with its evidences earlier. [[See the explanation of "ibtila'" earlier at 2:49, 3:7, 7:574, note 1, and the references there. In the printed edition and manuscript here it read "wa-qad thabata dhalika" ("and that has been established"), which is nothing; the copyist erred, and the correct reading is what is given here.]]

* *

As for His words "in what He has given you," it means: in what He sent down to you of Books, as related:

12148 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "But to try you in what He has given you." He said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: I do not know it except that he said: "to try you in what He has given you of Books."

* *

If someone says: How did He say "to try you in what He has given you," and who is addressed by that? You have mentioned that the one meant by His words "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj" is our Prophet along with the prophets who passed before him and their nations, and those before our Prophet (ﷺ) separately?

It is said: Although the address is to our Prophet (ﷺ), it is intended to convey news about the prophets before him and their nations. But it is the custom of the Arabs, when they address a person and join to him an absent party, intending to report about that party, to give precedence to the addressed person, so the report about both comes out in the form of address. For this reason, He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "For each We have made among you a shir'ah and a minhaj."

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: "So race to the good deeds. To God is your return, all together, and He will inform you about that in which you used to differ" (﴿فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾) (48).

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance is exalted; He says: So hasten, O people, to the righteous deeds and to the approaches to your Lord, by persistently acting on what is in your Book which He sent down to your Prophet. He sent it down only as a trial and test for you, so that the good-doer among you may be distinguished from the wrongdoer. He will repay each of you for his deed with its recompense when you return to Him, for to Him is your return, all together. He will inform each group of you about what it used to oppose the other groups in, and will judge between them with the judgment of decision. He will make clear the one in the right by rewarding him with the Gardens, and the wrongdoer by punishing him with the Fire. Then each party will clearly see, the one in the right from the one in falsehood.

* *

If someone says: Did our Lord not inform us in this world, before our return to Him, about what we differ over?

It is said: He made that clear in this world through the messengers, the signs, and the proofs, apart from seeing the reward and punishment directly; so some affirm it and some deny it. But at the time of the return to Him, He will inform them of it through the recompense, about which they will have no doubt in recognizing the one in the right and the one in falsehood, and they will not be able to introduce confusion about it into themselves. So likewise His report, may His remembrance be exalted, that He will inform us at the time of return to Him of what we used to differ about in this world. The meaning is only: To God is your return, all together, and then you will recognize, from among you, the one in the right from the one in falsehood, as related:

12149 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab related to us, from Abu Sinan who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: "So race to the good deeds. To God is your return, all together," he said: the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), the righteous and the wicked. [[Note on this report: "Abu Sinan" is Sa'id ibn Sinan, passed shortly before as no. 12133.]]

The interpretation of His words, may His mention be exalted: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins. And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient." [Qur'an 5:49]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His mention be exalted, means by His words "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed," and "We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Book confirming what was before it of the Scripture, and judge between them": "an" (أن) is in a position of accusative governed by "al-tanzil" (the sending down).

* *

And by His words "by what Allah has revealed," He means by the judgment of Allah which He has revealed to you in His Book.

* *

As for His words "and do not follow their desires," it is a prohibition from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that he follow the desires of the Jews who came to him for judgment regarding their slain man and their two adulterers, [[His words "and their two adulterers" mean the Jewish man and Jewish woman who committed adultery, and so he ﷺ stoned them.]] and a command from Him to him to hold fast to acting upon His Book which He sent down to him.

* *

And His words "and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you": He, may His mention be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Beware, O Muhammad, of these Jews who have come to you seeking judgment from you, "lest they tempt you," so that they turn you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you of the judgments of His Book, and make you abandon acting upon it and follow their desires. [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (temptation) in what has passed, 10:317, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And His words "And if they turn away, then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins": He, may His mention be exalted, says: If these Jews who disputed before you turn away from you, abandoning acting upon what you have judged against them and decided concerning them [[See the explanation of "tawalla" (to turn away) in what has passed, 10:336, note 3, and the references there.]], "then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins," meaning: know that they did not turn away from contentment with your judgment, though you have judged with truth, except because Allah wishes to hasten their punishment in the worldly life for some of the sins they committed earlier. [[See the explanation of "al-iṣābah" (affliction) in what has passed, 8:514, 538, 540, 555.]] "And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient": meaning, indeed many of the Jews are those who abandon acting upon the Book of Allah, and who depart from His obedience into disobedience. [[See the explanation of "fisq" (defiant disobedience) in what has passed, 10:393, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

And the narrations from the people of interpretation have come in accordance with what we have said concerning this.

Those who said so:

12150 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ka'b ibn Asad, Ibn Suriya and Shas ibn Qays [[In Ibn Hisham: "Ibn Sulba, and Abdullah ibn Suriya".]] said to one another: Go with us to Muhammad; perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion. So they came to him and said: O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis, nobles and chiefs of the Jews, and that if we follow you, the Jews will follow us and will not oppose us, and that there is a dispute between us and our people, so we will bring them to you for judgment, and you will rule for us against them, and we will believe in you and affirm you! But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused, and Allah sent down concerning them: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you," to His words "for a people who are certain." [[The report: 12150 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 216, and it follows the previous report No. 11974.]]

12151 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words "and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you," he said: that they say "In the Torah it is such-and-such," while we have already made clear to you what is in the Torah. And he recited: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is retaliation﴾ [Qur'an 5:45], some of it for some.

12152 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Magians entered along with the People of the Book into this verse: "And judge between them by what Allah has revealed."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 50:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted and remembered, saying: ﴿Do they seek the judgement of the time of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾ (5:50)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Do these Jews, who have brought their dispute to you and did not accept your judgement, seek [the judgement of the time of ignorance], [[See the explanation of "baghā" and "ibtaghā" above, vol. 10, p. 290, footnote 2, and the references there.]] when you have judged among them with justice? "The judgement of the time of ignorance" means the rulings of the idol-worshippers among the people of polytheism, while they have with them the Book of Allah, which contains a clear statement of the reality of the judgement you have passed upon them, and that it is the truth from which it is not permissible to deviate. [[In the printed edition: "and you have judged", and in the manuscript: "or you have judged"; the correct reading is what has been adopted.]]

Then He, may He be exalted and remembered, said, rebuking those among the Jews who refused to accept the judgement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over them, and deeming their action foolish:

And who is better in judgement than Allah, O Jews, for people who know with certainty the Oneness of Allah and acknowledge His lordship? He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: What judgement is better than the judgement of Allah, if you are certain that you have a Lord, and you are people of monotheism and affirmation of Him?

* *

Mujahid said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

12153 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: "Do they seek the judgement of the time of ignorance?" He said: "the Jews."

12154 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Do they seek the judgement of the time of ignorance?" "The Jews."

12155 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: a shaykh narrated to us, from Mujahid: "Do they seek the judgement of the time of ignorance?" He said: "the Jews."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 51 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (*ta'wil*, the exegetical explanation of the text) of His words, exalted is His mention: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another.﴾

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The people of *ta'wil* (exegetes) differed concerning who is meant by this verse, although all the believers are commanded by it.

Some of them said: It refers to ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit and ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, concerning ‘Ubadah's disavowal of the alliance with the Jews, and concerning ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul's adherence to the alliance with the Jews after their hostility to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) had become apparent. Allah informed [the believers] that whoever allies himself with them and adheres to their alliance is, in his disavowal of Allah and His Messenger, one of them, just as they are disavowed from Them.

Mention of those who said this:

12156. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, from ‘Atiyyah ibn Sa'd, who said: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, of the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have many allies among the Jews, numerous in their number, and I disavow to Allah and His Messenger the alliance of the Jews, and I take Allah and His Messenger as my allies." ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears misfortunes; I will not disavow the alliance of my allies." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy: "O Abu al-Hubab, what you have withheld of the alliance of the Jews from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, is it yours instead of him?" [[In the manuscript: "fa-huwa ila dunahu" (so it is to him, instead of him), and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] He said: "I have accepted." So Allah revealed: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another," up to His words: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease."

12157. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, who said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: "Believe before Allah afflicts you with a day like the day of Badr!" Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Did you become deluded because you struck a party of Quraysh who had no knowledge of fighting? As for us, if we had firmly resolved [[In the printed edition: "asrarna al-‘azimah" (we concealed our resolve), which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript. "Amara al-habl yamurrahu imrarān" means: he twisted the rope firmly and strongly. That is, we have gathered our resolve.]] to gather against you, you would not have had the strength to fight us!" ‘Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, my Jewish allies were fierce in their souls, abundant in their weapons, and mighty in their power, and I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger their alliance, and I have no ally except Allah and His Messenger." ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "But I will not disavow the alliance of the Jews; I am a man who cannot do without them!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Hubab, what you withheld of the alliance of the Jews from ‘Ubadah, is it yours instead of him?" He said: "In that case I accept!" So Allah, exalted is His mention, revealed: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another," up to His words: "And Allah will protect you from the people." [[Report 12157: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Umar ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri, weak, abandoned in narration. Previously mentioned under no. 5754.]]

12158. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When the Banu Qaynuqa' waged war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy clung to their cause and stood in their defence. ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was one of the Banu ‘Awf ibn al-Khazraj and had from their alliance the same as what they had from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and renounced them to him, disavowed to Allah and His Messenger their alliance, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger their alliance, and I take Allah, His Messenger and the believers as my allies, and I disavow the alliance and allegiance of the disbelievers!" Concerning him and ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the verses of "al-Ma'idah" were revealed: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another," the verse. [[Report 12158: Sirat Ibn Hisham, 3:52, 53.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to a people among the believers who, when they were struck at Uhud by what they were struck with from the polytheist enemies, resolved to take from the Jews covenants [[*"al-‘isam"* is the plural of *"‘ismah"*: the ropes and pacts that bind them and protect them from ruin.]], so Allah forbade them from that and informed them that whoever among them did so was one of them.

Mention of those who said this:

12159. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Sudi, concerning: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them." He said: When the Battle of Uhud took place, it weighed heavily on a group of people, and they feared that the disbelievers would gain dominion over them. [[*"Udil ‘alayhi"* (passive): that is, he was given the dominion and victory.]] A man said to his companion: "As for me, I will go to Dahlak the Jew, and I will take from him safe-conduct and become a Jew with him, for I fear that the Jews will gain dominion over us." The other said: "As for me, I will go to so-and-so the Christian in some part of al-Sham, and take from him safe-conduct and become a Christian with him." So Allah, exalted is His mention, revealed to forbid both of them: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." [[*"Dahlak al-Yahudi"*: I have not found any mention of him among the books available to me, and I fear that his name is a distortion.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to Abu Lubabah ibn ‘Abd al-Mundhir, in his informing the Banu Qurayzah, when they accepted the judgement of Sa'd, that the judgement was slaughter.

Mention of those who said this:

12160. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from ‘Ikrimah, concerning his words: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Lubabah ibn ‘Abd al-Mundhir, of the Aws, and he was of the Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf, to Qurayzah when they broke the covenant. When they obeyed him by coming down [from their fortresses], he pointed to his throat: slaughter, slaughter! [[In the manuscript: "ata‘ū Allah bi-al-nuzul" (they obeyed Allah by coming down), and the good reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that it should be said: Allah, exalted is His mention, forbade all the believers to take the Jews and the Christians as helpers and allies against the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and others [[In the printed edition, the phrase "wa-ghayrahum" (and others) is omitted.]]. He informed that whoever takes them as a helper, ally and friend, apart from Allah, His Messenger and the believers, is one of them in the factionalism against Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and that Allah and His Messenger are free of him. It is possible that the verse was revealed concerning ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit and ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and their Jewish allies; it is possible that it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah because of his action toward the Banu Qurayzah; and it is possible that it was revealed concerning the two men whom al-Sudi mentioned, one of whom resolved to join Dahlak the Jew, and the other a Christian in al-Sham. None of these three views has been transmitted by a report that establishes a proof, so that one could accept its soundness and say that it was as stated.

Since this is so, the correct view is to rule by the apparent wording of the revelation as general in what it encompasses, and to permit what the people of *ta'wil* have said about it, of the view which we have no knowledge of contradicting. Nevertheless, there is no doubt that the verse was revealed concerning a hypocrite who was allying himself with Jews or Christians out of fear for himself from the reversals of fortune, for the verse that follows this one indicates that, and that is His words: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us"﴾, the verse.

As for His words, "they are allies of one another": He meant by this that some of the Jews are helpers of one another against the believers, with one hand against all of them; and that the Christians are likewise, some are helpers of others against whoever opposes their religion and creed. He made known to His believing servants that whoever is an ally to them or to some of them, is in fact an ally to them against whoever opposes their creed and religion among the believers, just as the Jews and Christians have war against them. Then the Exalted said to the believers: "So be you also allies of one another, and against the Jew and the Christian be at war, as they are at war with you, and be allies of one another, for whoever allies himself with them has made the war against the people of faith manifest, and disavowal from them is required, and he has made clear the severing of his allegiance." [[See the explanation of *"wali"* and *"awliya'"* earlier, 9:319, note 1, and the references there.]]

* * *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His mention: ﴿And whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His mention, "And whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them," He means: whoever allies himself with the Jews and the Christians, apart from the believers, he is one of them. He says: Whoever allies himself with them and helps them against the believers is of the people of their religion and creed, for no one allies himself with anyone except that he is pleased with him, with his religion and with what he is upon. When he is pleased with him and pleased with his religion, he has become hostile to what opposes it and has become displeased with it, and his judgement becomes their judgement. [[See the explanation of *"al-tawalli"* earlier, 9:319, note 1, and the references there.]] For this reason, some scholars ruled concerning the Christians of the Banu Taghlib, regarding their slaughtered animals, the marriage to their women and other matters, by the rulings for the Christians of the Children of Israel, because of their allegiance to them, their contentment with their creed, and their support of them in it, even though their lineages differ from theirs and the origin of their religion is separate from the origin of theirs.

* * *

In this is clear evidence for the correctness of what we say: that everyone who adheres to a religion has the ruling of the people of that religion, whether his adherence to it was before the coming of Islam or after it. Except that if he is a Muslim of our people who has moved to another religion, he is not left upon what he adhered to when he moved to it; rather, he is to be killed for his apostasy from Islam and his departure from the religion of truth, unless he returns to the religion of truth before being killed. [[His words "and the corruption of what opposes it" are in the genitive, coordinated with his earlier words: "and in this is clear evidence for the correctness of what we say."]] And [this evidence refutes] the corruption of what opposes it, from the view of one who claims that one is not judged by the rulings of the People of the Two Scriptures [Jews and Christians] if he adheres to their religion, unless he is an Israelite or one who moved to their religion from others before the revelation of the Furqan [the Qur'an]. As for one who adheres to their religion after the revelation of the Furqan, of those who were not of them, whose lineage differs from theirs and whose kind differs from theirs, his ruling is different from their ruling. [[See what has passed, 9:573–587.]]

* * *

Mention of those who said by what we have said of the interpretation:

12161. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hamid ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn ‘Abbas was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians, and he recited: "And whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them." [[Report 12161: Hamid ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi, trustworthy. Previously mentioned under nos. 178, 886, 5347.]]

12162. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ‘Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ‘Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ‘Abbas concerning this verse: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them," that it refers to slaughtered animals. Whoever enters the religion of a people is one of them.

12163. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from ‘Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Eat from the slaughtered animals of the Banu Taghlib, and marry their women, for Allah says in His Book: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them." And if they were not of them except by alliance, they would be of them.

12164. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn ‘Ali narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Hisham, who said: al-Hasan did not see any harm in the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians or in marrying their women, and he would recite this verse: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies, they are allies of one another; and whoever of you allies himself with them, then he is one of them." [[Report 12164: Husayn ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Walid al-Ju'fi, mentioned many times previously, including nos. 29, 174, 441, 4415, 7287, 7499, 11463. In the printed edition it was "Hasan ibn ‘Ali," which is an error; in the manuscript it is undotted.
And "Za'idah" is Za'idah ibn Qudamah al-Thaqafi, mentioned previously under nos. 29, 4897, 7287.]]

12165. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Harun ibn Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Sirin was asked about a man who sells his house to Christians who would make it a church. He said: Then he recited this verse: "Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies."

* * *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people (51)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His mention, means: Allah does not grant success to one who places allegiance in other than its proper place, who allies himself with the Jews and the Christians, despite their enmity toward Allah, His Messenger and the believers, against the believers, and becomes for them a supporter and helper, for whoever allies himself with them is at war with Allah, His Messenger and the believers.

We have already explained the meaning of "*al-zulm*" (wrongdoing) in another place, namely that it is putting a thing in other than its proper place, with what suffices so that it need not be repeated.

* * *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them, saying, "We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us"﴾

The people of *ta'wil* differed concerning whom this verse refers to.

Some of them said: It refers to ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

Mention of those who said this:

12166. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, from ‘Atiyyah ibn Sa'd, concerning: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease": ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. "Hastening toward them": in their allegiance. "Saying, 'We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us'," to the end of the verse: "So they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves."

12167. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: My father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, from ‘Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, concerning: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease," meaning ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy: "hastening toward them, saying, 'We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us'," because of his saying: "I fear a reversal that will strike me!" [[Report 12167: Sirat Ibn Hisham, 3:53, abridged, and it continues the previous report no. 12158.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to a people among the hypocrites who used to counsel the Jews and deceive the believers, saying: "We fear that the reversal may be in favour of the Jews over the believers!" [[In the printed edition: "an takūna dā'irah" (that a reversal may be); I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said this:

12168. Muhammad ibn ‘Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, saying: ‘Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, exalted is His mention: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease hastening toward them," he said: The hypocrites, in flattering the Jews, conferring with them, and having their children nursed by them. And Allah's words, exalted is His mention: "We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us," he said: They say: "We fear that the reversal may be in favour of the Jews."

12169. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

12170. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his words: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease," to his words: "regretful," [he said:] these are people among the hypocrites who were friendly toward the Jews and counselled them, to the exclusion of the believers.

12171. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Sudi: "So you see those in whose hearts is a disease, hastening toward them, saying, 'We fear that a reversal of fortune may strike us'." He said: "Doubt" [is the disease]. And "*al-da'irah*" (the reversal) is the ascendancy of the polytheists over them.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is that it should be said: This is a report from Allah about certain people among the hypocrites who used to ally themselves with the Jews and the Christians and deceive the believers, and say: "We fear that reversals of fortune may turn," either in favour of the Jews and Christians, or in favour of the people of polytheism, the worshippers of idols or others, against the people of Islam; or that some calamity may befall these hypocrites, so that we will be in need of them.

It is possible that this was said by ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, and it is possible that it was said by someone else; but there is no doubt that it was said by the hypocrites.

* * *

Then the meaning of the speech is: You see, O Muhammad, those in whose hearts there is doubt, [[In the printed edition: "in their hearts is sickness and doubt of faith," which differs from the manuscript, and the manuscript reading is the pure correct one. For he means: the sickness has entered their faith and their affirmation, after mentioning "doubt."]] and sickness of faith in your prophethood and in affirming what you have brought them from your Lord [[For the explanation of "sickness" see what has preceded, 1: 278-281.]] "they hasten towards them," meaning towards the Jews and the Christians, [and by their hastening towards them he means: their hastening in allying with them and currying favour with them [[For the explanation of "hastening" see what has preceded, 7: 130, 207, 418; 10: 301 and what follows.]] "saying, 'We fear that a reverse may befall us.'" These hypocrites say: We only hasten to ally with these Jews and Christians out of fear of a reversal of fortune that may turn against us from our enemy. [[For the explanation of "befalling" see what has preceded, p. 1393, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

By "the reversal" (al-da'ira) he means the turn of fortune, as the rajaz poet said: [[He is Humayd al-Arqat.]]

"It turns back from you the decreed destiny... and the circling turns of time that they turn"

Meaning: that a turn of fortune may come upon us through time, so we need their support for us, and therefore we ally with them. Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, said to them: "So perhaps God will bring victory or a command from Him, and they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves."

[[Abu 'Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 169; I did not find the rest of the rajaz.]]

The discussion of the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest or a decision from Him, and they will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves﴾ (5:52).

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His saying, "So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest or a decision from Him," that perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest. [[See the explanation of "perhaps" (ʿasā) in what has passed: 4:298/8:579.]]

* *

Then they differed concerning the interpretation of "conquest" (al-fath) in this place.

Some of them said: what is meant here is judgment (al-qadāʾ).

Those who said this:

12172 - Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: "So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest," he said: "by judgment."

* *

Others said: what is meant is the conquest of Mecca.

Those who said this:

12173 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest," he said: the conquest of Mecca.

* *

And "al-fath" in the language of the Arabs means judgment, as Qatadah said, and from it is the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth﴾ (Surah al-Araf: 89).

It is also permissible that this judgment which God promised His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) in His saying, "So perhaps Allah will bring about a conquest," is the conquest of Mecca, because that was among the greatest of God's judgments and the decisive separation of His ruling between the people of faith and the people of disbelief, and it established among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "and it establishes" (wa-yuqarrir), and the correct reading appears to be what is adopted here.]] that Allah exalts His word and weakens the plot of the disbelievers. [[See the explanation of "al-fath" in what has passed: 2:254, 332; 9:323, 324.]]

* *

As for His saying, "or a decision from Him," al-Suddi used to say concerning it:

12174 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "or a decision from Him," he said: "the decision" is the jizya.

* *

It may be that the "decision" which God promised His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to bring is the jizya, and it may be other than it. However, whichever it was, it is of that which involves the victory of the believers over the people of disbelief in God and His Messenger, and of that which grieves the hypocrites and does not please them. This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed of them that when that decision comes, they will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves.

* *

As for His saying, "and they will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves," it refers to these hypocrites who were allied with the Jews and Christians. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Perhaps Allah will bring about a decision from Him by which He gives the believers power over the disbelievers among the Jews, Christians, and others of the people of disbelief, so these hypocrites will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves of friendship with the Jews and Christians and their affection, and of hatred toward the believers and opposition to them, [they will be] "regretful," as:

12175 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and they will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves," [referring to] their friendship with the Jews, and their deceit toward Islam and its people.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by God with their strongest oaths that they were with you?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers (qira'at, the recognised variant readings of the Qur'an) differed over the recitation of His words "And those who believe will say." The reading of the people of Medina is: ﴿So they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves. Those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by God...﴾, without a waw.

The interpretation of the statement according to this reading is: the hypocrites will become, when God brings victory or a command from Him, regretful for what they concealed within themselves. The believers will say, in wonder at them, at their hypocrisy, their lying, and their audacity toward God in their false oaths by God: "Are these the ones who swore to us by God that they were with us, while they were lying in their oaths to us?" This is the meaning that Mujahid intended in his interpretation, which:

12176 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding "Perhaps God will bring victory or a command from Him": then, "those who believe will say, 'Are these the ones who swore by God with their strongest oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become void, and they have become losers.'"

Likewise, it is so in the codices (masahif, sing. mushaf) of the people of Medina, without a waw. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 313.]]

Some of the Basrans read: ﴿And those who believe will say﴾ with a waw, and with "will say" in the accusative, as a conjunction joining it to "Perhaps God will bring victory." The reciter of this reading stated that he would say: "What is intended is: Perhaps God will bring victory, and perhaps those who believe will say—" and nothing else is possible, because it is not permissible to say, "And perhaps God will say, those who believe..." He would say: this is like their saying, "I ate bread and milk," as in the verse of the poet:

"And you saw your husband in the battle, girded with a sword and a spear." [[Its takhrij has passed at 1: 140, 265 / 6: 423.]]

The interpretation of the statement according to this reading: "Perhaps God will bring victory to the believers, or a command from Him by which He will grant them dominion over the disbelievers among their enemies, so the hypocrites will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves." And perhaps those who believe will say at that time: "Are these the ones who swore by God falsely with their strongest oaths that they were with you?"

In the codices of the people of Iraq it is with a waw: ﴿And those who believe will say﴾.

The reading of the Kufans was: ﴿And those who believe will say﴾ with a waw, and with "will say" in the raised case (marfu'), in the future sense and free of the jussive and subjunctive particles.

The interpretation of those who read it thus: "So they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves, and those who believe will say," so the verb "will say" begins a new clause and is therefore raised.

Abu Ja'far said: Our reading, which we adopt, is "And those who believe will say" with the waw in "and will say," because it is so in our codices, the codices of the East, with a waw, and with "will say" in the raised case as a new beginning.

The interpretation of the statement, since the reading according to us is as we have described [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "since the reading was," and the correct form is what is recorded here.]]: "So they will become regretful for what they concealed within themselves, and the believers will say: 'Are these the ones who swore to us by God with their strongest oaths, falsely, that they were with us?'"

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says, informing about their state in His sight because of their hypocrisy and the corruption of their deeds: ﴿Their deeds have become void﴾, meaning: their deeds that they performed in the world have gone in vain, with no reward or recompense for them, because they performed them without certainty that they were obligatory duties from God, and without sound faith in God and His Messenger. Rather, they performed them only to ward off the believers from themselves, their wealth and their families. So God nullified their reward, since it was not for Him. ﴿So they have become losers﴾, meaning: these hypocrites, at the coming of God's command to grant the believers dominion over the people of disbelief, have become those who were cheated in their exchange of the Hereafter for this world, their transaction has failed, and they have perished. [[See the explanation of "habata" previously at 9: 592, note 1, and the references there.]] [[See the explanation of "khasara" previously at p. 224, note 1, and the references there.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 54 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Allah and His Messenger: "O you who believe", that is, those who affirm (saddaqu) Allah and His Messenger, and acknowledge what their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them. "Whoever among you turns back from his religion" means: whoever among you returns from his true religion, which he holds today, and substitutes and changes it by entering into disbelief, whether into Judaism, Christianity, or some other kind of disbelief. [[See the explanation of "irtadda" (turned back) earlier, p. 170, note 1, and the references there.]] "Then He will not harm Allah in anything." "And Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him": that is, Allah will bring, in place of them, the believers who did not substitute, did not change, and did not turn back, a people better than those who apostatized and changed their religion, whom Allah loves and who love Allah. [[The context of this phrase: "Then Allah will bring ... the believers ... a people ...".]]

This threat from Allah was directed at those whom He knew in advance would apostatize after the death of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Likewise, His promise in this verse, to those among the believers whom He promised, is for those for whom it was foreknown that they would not change or alter their religion and would not turn back. When Allah took His Prophet (ﷺ), groups from the Bedouins (ahl al-wabar) and some of the settled people (ahl al-madar) apostatized, so Allah replaced the believers with better people than them, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, said, and He fulfilled His promise to the believers and carried out His threat against those among them who apostatized.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

12177 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ayyash informed me, from Abu Sakhr, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz sent for him one day, while Umar was then governor of Madina, and said: "O Abu Hamza, a verse has kept me awake last night!" Muhammad said: "And what is it, O Amir?" He said: "The words of Allah: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion﴾ until ﴿and who do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾." Muhammad said: "O Amir, Allah meant by 'those who believe' the rulers from Quraysh; whoever of them turns back from the truth." [[The report: 12177 - "Abdullah ibn Ayyash ibn Abbas al-Qitbani", not strong, but trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Abu Sakhr" is "Humayd ibn Ziyad al-Kharrat", who has passed many times, including under nos. 4280, 4325, 5386, 8391, 11867, 11891.
Then see the following report, no. 12199.]] Then the exegetes differed about the specific people whom Allah would bring to replace the apostates among the believers.

Some of them said: They are Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and his companions, who fought the people of apostasy (ahl al-ridda) until they drove them back through the gate from which they had come out.

Those who said that:

12178 - Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Dalham, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: "This is, by Allah, Abu Bakr and his companions." [[The report: 12178 - "al-Fadl ibn Dalham al-Wasiti al-Qassab". His case is disputed. Passed as no. 4928.]]
