12179 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Dalham, from al-Hasan, similarly.

12180 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from Sahl, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: "Abu Bakr and his companions."

12181 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn Ali narrated to us, from Abu Musa, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, and said: "By Allah, it is for Abu Bakr and his companions." [[The report: 12181 - "Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Walid al-Ju'fi", passed shortly before: 12164.
"Abu Musa" is "Isra'il ibn Musa al-Basri", who settled in India. He narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri. Trustworthy, no harm in him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

12182 - Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: "It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and his companions." [[The report: 12182 - "Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi". Here, as also in the manuscript and printed edition, it appears as "al-Awdi". My brother Sayyid Ahmad had earlier discussed it and corrected it to "al-Azdi" as I have written it here, but I am doubtful of this correction, given how often it appears as "al-Awdi" throughout the tafsir. See what has passed: 423, 875, 2859, 8783.
"Ahmad ibn Bashir al-Qurashi al-Makhzumi", Abu Bakr al-Kufi. Passed as no. 7819.
"Hisham" is "Hisham ibn Urwa ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam", passed as nos. 2889, 8461.]]

12183 - Ali ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty toward the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and not fearing the blame of any blamer﴾, he said: "It is Abu Bakr and his companions. When those among the Arabs who apostatized from Islam did so, Abu Bakr and his companions fought them until he returned them to Islam."

12184 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding: ﴿Whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ up to His words: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. Allah revealed this verse knowing that some of mankind would apostatize. When Allah took His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), most of the Arabs turned back from Islam, except for three mosques: the people of Madina, the people of Makka, and the people of Bahrain from Abd al-Qays. They said: "We will pray but not pay zakat; by Allah, our wealth will not be seized!" [[The sayers of "We will pray but not pay zakat" are those among the general Arabs who apostatized.]] Abu Bakr was spoken to about this, and it was said to him: "If they were to understand this, they would give it" - or: "they would pay it". [[In the printed edition it reads: "they would give it or increase it", which is a gross distortion. The correct reading is from the manuscript and his words: "or: they would pay it", as if he said: narrated instead of "give it", "pay it". The pronoun in both refers back to the zakat which they withheld.]] He said: "No, by Allah, I will not separate what Allah has joined together. If they withheld even a 'iqal of what Allah and His Messenger have made obligatory, we would fight them over it!" [["Al-'iqal" (with a kasra on the ʿayn) is the zakat of a year from camels and sheep. It is said: "He took from them the 'iqal of this year", meaning its zakat and charity. Others have explained it as the rope with which the obligatory animal was tied when it was taken in charity, since the owner of camels had to give, with every obligatory animal, a rope to tie it. "Riwa'" means a rope. The report is also narrated as: "if they withheld from me a young she-goat" (anaq). "Al-anaq" is a female kid of goats, once it has reached a year.]] So Allah sent a band with Abu Bakr, and he fought as the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had fought, until he took captives, killed, and burned with fire people who had apostatized from Islam and withheld zakat. He fought them until they acknowledged the ma'un - and it is the zakat - in humiliation and abasement. [["Saghara" is the plural of "sagher", one who accepts humiliation and oppression. "Aqmiya'" is the plural of "qami'", one who is abject, submissive, and shrunken. What is in the lexicons as the plural of "qami'" is "qima'" (with a kasra on the qaf) and "qama'" (with a damma). "Qam'a" passed in the manuscript in report no. 4221; see the note there. "Aqmiya'" here is a rare plural. "Fa'il" as an adjective, when doubled or defective (waw or ya), is analogically pluralized as "af'ila'", as in "shadid" and "ashdda'", and "ghani" and "aghniya'", and "shaqi" and "ashqiya'". The sound form, however, rarely takes "af'ila'", as in "sadiq" and "asdiqa'". So if the report of "aqmiya'" is authentic in this report, it is correct in Arabic, God willing, for this reason and others.]] Then delegations of the Arabs came to him, and he gave them a choice between a shameful arrangement or a war that would uproot them. They chose the shameful arrangement, which was easier for them, to acknowledge that their slain were in the Fire, that the slain of the believers were in Paradise, [[In the printed edition it reads: "that they should prepare that their slain are in the Fire", and in the manuscript likewise without dots. I have not found a closer distortion than what I have written, which I deduced from the report narrated by al-Sha'bi from Ibn Mas'ud, which says: "By Allah, he was not content for them except with the shameful arrangement or the war that uproots. As for the shameful arrangement, it is that they acknowledge that whoever among them was killed is in the Fire, and that what they took of our wealth is returned to us. As for the war that uproots, it is that they leave their homes" (Futuh al-Buldan of al-Baladhuri: 101).]] and that whatever wealth they had taken from the Muslims would be returned to them, and whatever wealth the Muslims had taken from them would be lawful to them.

12185 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: They apostatized when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died, and Abu Bakr fought them.

12186 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali regarding His words: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion﴾, he said: "Allah made the believers known, and the meaning of evil fell upon the mass among them of hypocrites, and those whom He knew would apostatize." [[In the printed edition it reads: "and He made the meaning of evil fall", and I have kept what is in the manuscript; I am doubtful of the whole phrase, though it has some sense and meaning.]] He said: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring﴾ - the apostates in their houses [[In the printed edition it reads: "the apostates from their religion", and in the manuscript: "in their religion". The correct reading is what I have written, from the following report, no. 12201.]] = ﴿a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾ - by Abu Bakr and his companions. [[The report: 12186 - In the printed edition: "Sayf ibn Amr", which is an error; the correct form is what I have written from the manuscript. A similar report has passed as no. 12128, containing "Abdullah ibn Hisham", whom I stated there I did not identify. Number 12187 was accidentally omitted from the numbering.]]

* * *

Others said: It means a people from Yemen. Some of those who said this among them said: They are the kinsmen of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Abdullah ibn Qays. [[At this point, a section of an older division ends. In the manuscript there is the following text:
"Followed by: Those who said that:
And may Allah bless Muhammad."
Then the following text follows:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
My Lord, make it easy by Your mercy."]]

Those who said that:

12188 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Iyad al-Ash'ari, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion, then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured toward Abu Musa with something he had with him, and said: "They are the people of this one!"

12189 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Iyad narrating from Abu Musa that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, and said: "I mean the people of Abu Musa."

12190 - Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janada narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Shu'ba. Abu al-Sa'ib said: Our companions said: it is "from Simak ibn Harb", but I do not remember "Simak" - from Iyad al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the people of this one, meaning Abu Musa."

12191 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Simak, from Iyad al-Ash'ari, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Musa: "They are the people of this one" - regarding His words: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾.

12192 - Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Iyad al-Ash'ari say: When it was revealed: ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are your people, O Abu Musa!" - or he said: "They are the people of this one", meaning Abu Musa. [[The reports: 12188 - 12192 - "Iyad al-Ash'ari" is "Iyad ibn Amr al-Ash'ari", a Successor (tabi'i), disputed as to whether he had companionship (suhba) with the Prophet (ﷺ). He narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) as a mursal report. He saw Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and others. Ibn Sa'd said (6: 104): "He narrated little hadith." He narrated from him al-Sha'bi and Simak ibn Harb. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba, al-Istiab: 498, and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/19.
This report was narrated by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 4/1/79, through Abdullah ibn Idris and Affan ibn Muslim, from Shu'ba, from Simak, from Iyad. Al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 313, through Wahb ibn Jarir and Sa'id ibn Amir, from Shu'ba, from Simak, from Iyad, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Haythami recorded it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 16, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the sound (sahih)." al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 292, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba in his Musnad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 3: 179, 180, from Ibn Abi Hatim, from Umar ibn Shabba, from Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, from Shu'ba.]]

12193 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan al-Himyari narrated to us, from Husayn, from Iyad - or: Ibn Iyad - ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him﴾, he said: "They are the people of Yemen." [[The report: 12193 - "Abu Sufyan al-Himyari" is "Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Mahdi al-Himyari" al-Hadhdha', al-Wasiti. Truthful. al-Daraqutni said: "Of middling state, not strong." Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/477, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/74.
"Husayn" is "Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami", trustworthy, one of the great imams. Passed as nos. 579, 2986.
"Iyad" is al-Ash'ari, as in the preceding reports. As for "Ibn Iyad", I have not found anyone who mentions it; it appears to be a doubt from Abu Sufyan al-Himyari or Sufyan ibn Waki'.
See the takhrij of the earlier reports.]]

12194 - Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, who said: When Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion﴾ to the end of the verse, Umar said: "Are I and my people them, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, rather this one and his people! - meaning Abu Musa al-Ash'ari." [[The report: 12194 - "Muhammad ibn Awf ibn Sufyan al-Ta'i", the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy and a hafiz. Passed as no. 5445.
"Abu al-Mughira" is "Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Khawlani", Abu al-Mughira al-Himsi, trustworthy and truthful. Passed as no. 10371.
"Safwan" is "Safwan ibn Amr ibn Harim al-Sakasiki", who heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr. Passed as no. 7009. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/309, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/422. In his biography in al-Tahdhib there is a clear error: it says he died in the year (100), and the correct year is (155), as in al-Tarikh al-Kabir and elsewhere.
"Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami", a trustworthy Successor. Passed as nos. 186, 187.
"Shurayh ibn Ubayd ibn Shurayh al-Hadrami", a trustworthy Successor, passed as no. 5445. Safwan ibn Amr narrates from Shurayh directly, but here he narrates from him through Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr.
This report was recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 292, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather they are all the people of Yemen.

Those who said that:

12195 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿He loves them and they love Him﴾, he said: "They are people from Yemen."

12196 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

12197 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "They are the people of Saba'."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 54 (part 2 of 2):

١٢١٩٨ - Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, saying: One who heard Shahr ibn Hawshab informed me, saying: "They are the people of Yemen." [[The narration 12198: "Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi," a teacher of al-Tabari, I have found no biography or mention of him. Among those named "Mutar" are "Mutar ibn Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Tamimi al-Harawi," whose biography is in Tarikh Baghdad 3: 275, and "Mutar ibn Muhammad ibn al-Dahhak al-Sukkari," who narrates from Yazid ibn Harun, whose biography is in Lisan al-Mizan 6: 49. I do not think he is either of them, and I fear that some distortion has entered his name.]]

١٢١٩٩ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ayyash informed me, from Abu Sakhr, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz sent for him one day, while he was governor of Madinah, asking him about this. Muhammad said: "Allah will bring a people," and they are the people of Yemen! Umar said: "Would that I were among them!" He said: "Amin!" [[The narration 12199: see the earlier narration no. 12177 and the comment on it.]]

* *

Others said: They are the Helpers (al-Ansar) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٢٠٠ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him," he claims that they are the Helpers.

* *

The interpretation of the verse according to the view of those who said: Allah meant by His saying, "Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him," Abu Bakr and his companions in their fighting against the people of apostasy (ahl al-ridda, i.e., those who abandoned Islam, the "apostasy" wars) after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, Allah will not harm anything [by that]. Allah will bring, in place of those of you who have turned back from their religion, a people whom He loves and who love Him, through whom He will take vengeance upon them at their hands." This has been transmitted by report and narration from some of those who interpreted it this way:

١٢٢٠١ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, from Abu Ruq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali, concerning His saying: "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring a people whom He loves," he said: He says: Allah will bring those who apostatized in their homes, "a people whom He loves and who love Him," [namely] Abu Bakr and his companions. [[Note: "in their homes" is the correct reading. It appeared in the manuscript and the printed edition as "in their religion" and "from their religion" in the earlier narration no. 12186, but the correct reading is what is given here. See the earlier comment, p. 414, note 2.]] [[The narration 12201: this is part of the earlier narration no. 12186. In this position it also had "Sayf ibn Amr," which is an error, as I have shown there.]]

* *

As for the view of those who said: Allah meant by this the people of Yemen, its interpretation is: "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring the believers who have not apostatized a people whom He loves and who love Him, as helpers and supporters for them." This has been transmitted by report from some of those who interpreted it this way.

١٢٢٠٢ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion," to the end of the verse: a warning from Allah that whoever of you apostatizes, He will replace him with better than them.

* *

As for the view of those who said: It means the Helpers, its interpretation in this regard is similar to the interpretation of those who understood it as meaning Abu Bakr and his companions.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the views on this matter, in my opinion, is what has been transmitted by report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that they are the people of Yemen, the people of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Were it not for the report transmitted about this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by the report transmitted from him, my view on this would only be the view of the one who said: "They are Abu Bakr and his companions." That is because he did not fight a people who had professed Islam during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and then turned back on their heels as unbelievers, except Abu Bakr and those with him who fought the people of apostasy with him after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But we have set aside the view on this in favour of the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he (ﷺ) was the source of clarification of the interpretation of what Allah sent down of His revelation and the signs of His Book. [["al-Ma'din" (with a fatha on the m, a sukun on the ‘ayn, and a kasra on the d) is the place in which the origin and beginning of a thing is found. From it comes the phrase "the mine of gold and silver," which we today call "al-manjam," where Allah the Glorified and Exalted caused their substance to grow and established it there. From it, figuratively, comes what is found in the report: "Do you ask me about the mines of the Arabs?" They said: "Yes." That is, their roots, to which they trace themselves and in which they take pride.]]

* *

If someone says to us: If the people whom Allah mentioned that He would bring when some of those who had professed Islam during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) apostatized from their religion are the people of Yemen, then were the people of Yemen during the days of Abu Bakr's fighting against the people of apostasy helpers of Abu Bakr in fighting them, so that you may consider it permissible to direct the interpretation of the verse toward what you have directed it? Or were they not helpers to him against them, so how did you consider it permissible to direct the interpretation of the verse to that, when you know that Allah does not break His promise?

It is said to him: Allah, dhikruhu (He is mentioned), did not promise the believers that He would replace with better than the apostates among them on that day those who fight the apostates. He only informed them that He would bring them better than them as a replacement. He has done that for them soon, not long after, when He brought them in the time of Umar. Their standing in relation to Islam and its people was the best standing, and they were helpers of the people of Islam and more beneficial to them than those of the rough (tagham) of the Bedouin and the uncouth people of the deserts who had apostatized after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and who were a burden (kall) and not a benefit to the people of Islam? [["al-Taghām" (with a fatha on the t) are the lowest and most contemptible of people. "al-Kall" (with a fatha on the k) are dependants and a burden on their companion, or the one who takes charge of his affairs.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters (al-qurra') differed in their recitation (qira'ah) of His saying: "O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion."

The recitation of the people of Madinah is: ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتدد منكم عن دينه﴾, with the doubling made explicit, with two dals, the final dal being jazm (vowelled with a sukun). Likewise it is in their codices.

As for the recitation of the people of Iraq, they recited it: ﴿مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ﴾, with assimilation (idgham), with one dal, and its vowel moved to fatha, on the basis of the dual (tathniyah). That is because the jazm form whose doubling is made explicit in the singular, when put in the dual, is assimilated. It is said to the singular: "Return, O so-and-so, to so-and-so his right," and when it is put in the dual it is said: "Return both of them to him his right," and one does not say: "Ardudā." Likewise in the plural: "Radduu," and one does not say: "Arduduu." So the Arabs sometimes build the singular on the dual, and sometimes make the doubling explicit in the singular because the verb's final radical is sukun. Both dialects are eloquent and well known among the Arabs. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "fi al-‘urf" (in custom); I have preferred the reading given here, which is correct.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation in this matter, in our view, is according to what is in our codices and the codices of the people of the East: with one dal, doubled (shaddah), without making the doubling explicit, and with the dal vowelled with fatha, for the reason I have described.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers]

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, dhikruhu, "humble towards the believers," He means: tender towards them, merciful toward them.

* *

[This is] from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so was humbled (dhalla) before so-and-so," when he submitted to him and became meek. [[See the explanation of "dhull" (humility) earlier, 2: 212 / 7: 171.]]

* *

By His saying, "mighty against the disbelievers," He means: harsh toward them, rough with them.

* *

[This is] from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so has overpowered me (`azzani)," when he shows his might over him and displays harshness and severity toward him. [[See the explanation of "‘izzah" (might) earlier, 9: 319, note 5, and the sources there.]]

* *

In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) also said.

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٢٠٣ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Sayf ibn Umar informed us, from Abu Ruq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali, concerning His saying: "humble towards the believers," the people of tenderness toward the people of their religion, "mighty against the disbelievers," the people of harshness toward those who oppose them in their religion. [[The narration 12203: see the chains of the earlier narrations nos. 12186 and 12201 and the comment on them. In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Sufyan ibn Umar" instead of "Sayf ibn Umar," which is a gross error.]]

١٢٢٠٤ - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers," meaning by "the humble": the merciful. [[In the manuscript it reads "meaning by the humble: the mercy," and in the printed edition "meaning by the humility: the mercy." I have written what is in the manuscript, which is a close misreading.]]

١٢٢٠٥ - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, concerning His saying: "humble towards the believers," he said: merciful among themselves; "mighty against the disbelievers," he said: harsh against them.

١٢٢٠٦ - Al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: I heard al-A'mash say, concerning His saying: "humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers": weak in relation to the believers. [[In the printed edition it reads "weak towards the believers," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is a good reading.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ ذَلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing, All-Knowing.]

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, dhikruhu, "they strive in the way of Allah," He means these believers whom Allah promised the believers He would bring in their place if any of them apostatized, as replacements for them. They strive in fighting the enemies of Allah in the manner that Allah commanded to fight them and the way in which He permitted it to them, and they strive against their enemy. That is their striving in the way of Allah. [[See the explanation of "yujahid" (strives) earlier, 4: 318 / 10: 292, and the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah) earlier in the language indexes (sabil).]] "and do not fear the blame of any blamer," meaning: they do not fear anyone for the sake of Allah, and the blame of a blamer does not prevent them from acting on what Allah commanded them, namely fighting their enemy.

* *

As for His saying, "That is the bounty of Allah," it means this description with which He described them, dhikruhu, that they are humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, strive in the way of Allah, and do not fear the blame of a blamer for the sake of Allah, is the bounty of Allah which He has bestowed on them. [[The sense of the sentence: "this description with which He described them ... is the bounty of Allah ..."]] Allah gives His bounty to whom He wills of His creatures, as a favour and a grace. "And Allah is all-Encompassing," meaning: Allah is generous with His bounty toward whom He is generous to, not fearing the exhaustion of His treasuries so that they would be depleted by His giving. [[In the printed edition it reads "fa-kayfa min ‘ata'ihi" (how, from His giving), which differs from the manuscript, because the latter's reader did not read it well, as it was unpointed. This is the correct reading.]] "All-Knowing," [knowing] the place of His generosity and giving, so He gives only to one who deserves it, and He gives to one who deserves it only in proportion to the benefit, knowing the place of his good in it from the place of his harm. [[See the explanation of "‘alim" (All-Knowing) earlier in the language indexes (‘alima).]]

The interpretation of His words, ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe — those who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾ [5:55]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, He means: you, believers, have no helper except Allah and His Messenger, and the believers whose description is what He, may His remembrance be exalted, has mentioned. [[See the explanation of "wali" (protector, ally) in what has preceded, p. 399, note 1, and the references there.]] As for the Jews and Christians, whom Allah has commanded you to disavow in their allegiance and forbidden you to take as allies, they are not your protectors or helpers. Rather, some of them are protectors of others, and do not take them as a protector or a helper.

* *

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, regarding his disavowal of the allegiance and alliance of the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers.

Among those who said this:

12207 – Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: my father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, on the authority of ʿUbada ibn al-Walid ibn ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, who said: When Banu Qaynuqa' waged war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ʿUbada ibn al-Samit went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) — and he was one of Banu ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj — and he released them to the Messenger of Allah [[In the manuscript: "fa-jaʿalahum ila rasul Allah" ("he made them [answerable] to the Messenger of Allah"); the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, agreeing with what preceded and with what is in the Sira of Ibn Hisham.]] and disavowed to Allah and His Messenger their alliance, and said: I take Allah and His Messenger and the believers as my allies, and I disavow the alliance and allegiance of the disbelievers! Concerning him was revealed: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾ — because of ʿUbada's saying: "I take Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies," and his disavowal of Banu Qaynuqa' and their allegiance — up to His words: ﴿And indeed, the party of Allah — they are the victorious﴾ [5:56]. [[The report: 12207 – Sira of Ibn Hisham 3:52, 53. It is an expanded version of the report previously numbered 12158, and the follow-up report numbered 12167.

In the printed edition and the manuscript here it reads: "my father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated to me, on the authority of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit," which omits what has been restored from the Sira and from the chain of the two reports mentioned above.]]

12208 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, on the authority of ʿAtiyya ibn Saʿd, who said: ʿUbada ibn al-Samit came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he mentioned something similar.

12209 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih narrated to me, on the authority of ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, that is: whoever embraces Islam has taken Allah and His Messenger as protectors.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾, the people of interpretation differed about who is meant by it.

Some of them said: It refers to ʿAli ibn Abi Talib.

* *

Others said: It refers to all the believers.

Among those who said this:

12210 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: Then He informed them of who would be their protector, saying: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾. These are all the believers, but ʿAli ibn Abi Talib was passed by a beggar while he was bowing in the mosque, and he gave him his ring.

12211 – Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: ʿAbda narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Malik, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, who said: I asked him about this verse: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing﴾. I said: Who are "those who believe"? He said: "Those who believe!" We said: It has reached us that it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib! He said: ʿAli is among those who believe. [[This is not a repetition; rather it is an expression of astonishment at his asking about something rather than about its like.]]

12212 – Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: I asked Abu Jaʿfar about the saying of Allah: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger﴾, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Hannad, on the authority of ʿAbda.

12213 – Ismaʿil ibn Israʾil al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us, saying: ʿUtba ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, regarding this verse: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾, he said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. [[The report: 12213 – Ismaʿil ibn Israʾil al-Ramli, mentioned previously under no. 10236. Ayyub ibn Suwayd al-Ramli, mentioned previously under no. 5494. ʿUtba ibn Abi Hakim al-Hamdani, then al-Shaʿbani, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Urdunni: Ibn Maʿin declared him weak, Ahmad considered him slightly unreliable, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

12214 – al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Ghalib ibn ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, who said: I heard Mujahid say regarding His saying: ﴿Your protector is only Allah and His Messenger﴾, the verse, that it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who gave charity while bowing. [[The report: 12214 – Ghalib ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-ʿUqayli al-Jazari: a narrator of rejected reports, abandoned. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/101, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/48.

Furthermore, I think that Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari neglected to discuss His words, "while bowing," and to explain its meaning in this context, together with the objection raised regarding it, because he intended to return to it and add further explanation, but he forgot it afterwards.

Ibn Kathir has said in his Tafsir (3:182): "As for His words, ﴿while bowing﴾, some people have supposed that this clause is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to ﴿and give zakah﴾, meaning: while in a state of bowing. If this were so, giving zakah while bowing would be superior to other times, since it would be praiseworthy. But this is not the case according to any of the scholars known to us among the leading jurists. Some have even mentioned in this regard a report from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that this verse was revealed concerning him..." Then he cited the aforementioned reports and others of similar meaning through various chains.

All these reports cannot stand as proof in religion. The scholars have discussed the placement of this clause and its meaning. The correct view on this matter is that His words ﴿and they are bowing﴾ mean: they are humbling themselves before their Lord, submitting to Him in obedience, bowing to Him by complying with His command to establish prayer in its prescribed limits and obligations, including the completion of bowing and prostration, and prayer with humility; and obeying what He has commanded them regarding giving zakah and disbursing it in the channels He has commanded. It thus has the meaning of "ruku'" (bowing), which in the original linguistic sense means submission. [[See the explanation of "raka'a" (to bow) in what has preceded, 1:574.]] Therefore, His words ﴿and they are bowing﴾ are not a circumstantial clause relating to ﴿and give zakah﴾. This is the pure truth, God willing.]]

Discourse on the interpretation of His saying: "And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - indeed, the party of Allah - they are the victorious" (5:56).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is an announcement from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to all His servants, those who disavowed the alliance of the Jews and renounced them, being content with the guardianship of Allah, His Messenger and the believers, [[In the printed edition: "those who disavowed the Jews and their alliance, being content with the guardianship of Allah ...", which differs from the manuscript, whose reader did not read it well; what I have established is the correct reading.]] and those who held fast to their alliance and feared that the circles of misfortune would turn against them, so they hastened to befriend them: that whoever trusts in Allah and takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies, and whoever is in the same condition as them among the friends of Allah from the believers, will have victory, the upper hand and dominion over those who oppose and oppose them, because they are the party of Allah, and the party of Allah are the victorious, not the party of Satan. As follows:

12215 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He informed them - meaning the Lord, may His remembrance be exalted - of who is the victor, so He said: "Do not fear dominion or misfortune," then He said: "And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - indeed, the party of Allah - they are the victorious." And "the party" (al-hizb) are the Ansar.

* *

By His saying "indeed, the party of Allah" he means: indeed, the supporters of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-hizb" above, 1:244. This interpretation given here is not found in the lexicographical books.]] From it is the saying of the rajaz poet: [[He is Ru'ba ibn al-Ajjaj.]]

"How could I be weakened while Bilal is my party!" [[Diwan: 16; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:169. From a rajaz poem in praise of Bilal ibn Abi Burda, in which he mentions himself at its beginning and then says, referring to one who opposes him and prepares insult and blame against him: "That one, even if the one who prepares against me prepares ... and diligence has scattered the bark of the blameworthy ... I have cast aside the false words of men ... so how could I be weakened while Bilal is my party!" The Diwan version reads: "wa-lastu adwi" (I am not weakened). In the manuscript: "adra" (which is an error). "Tahtaha al-shay'": he scattered it, dispersed it and destroyed it until it perished. "Al-lihaa'": dispute. "Al-qashb" (with fatha then sukun): slander; if it were read "al-qishb" (with kasra then sukun), it would mean a man with no good in him.]]

By his saying "adwa" he means: I am made weak and wronged, from "al-dawi" (the weakened one). [["Al-dawi": the one weakened by emaciation or other things. "Dawa yadwi dawan": he became weak and thin. In the manuscript it was "adra" and "al-dari", which is an error and a misreading.]] By his saying "Bilal is my party" he means: my supporters.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 57:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers, and fear Allah if you are believers﴾ (5:57).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, addressing the believers in Him and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "O you who have believed," that is, who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. "Do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you," meaning the Jews and Christians to whom messengers and prophets came and upon whom Scriptures were revealed before the sending of our Prophet (ﷺ) and before the revelation of our Book. "Allies," He says: do not take them, O believers, as helpers, brothers or confederates. [In the printed edition: "helpers, brothers and confederates," and in the manuscript: "helpers or brothers and confederates." I have made them all with "or," as you see.] For they spare no effort in harming you, even if they show you affection and friendship.

* *

The taking of those Jews whom Allah described to the believers as having taken their religion as ridicule and amusement, as our Lord, exalted is He, described them, was that one of them would show the believers faith while remaining steadfast in his disbelief. Then, after a short time, he would return to disbelief by displaying it with his tongue, after he had been expressing faith with his tongue while concealing disbelief within. This is mockery and ridicule of the religion, as Allah, exalted is He, related about some of them doing so in His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking."  Allah mocks them and extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 14-15].

* *

A report from Ibn Abbas agrees with what we have said on this.

12216 - Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut and Suwayd ibn al-Harith had professed Islam and then turned hypocrite, and some men among the Muslims were friendly with them. So Allah revealed concerning them: "O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and the disbelievers, as allies," up to His saying: "And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal." [Report 12216: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 217, 218.]

* *

This report makes clear the correctness of what we have said: that the taking of those who have made the religion of Allah a ridicule and amusement from among the People of the Book mentioned by Allah in this verse was only through their hypocrisy, their showing the believers faith while concealing disbelief within, and their saying to their devils among the Jews when they were alone with them, "Indeed, we are with you." So Allah forbade their friendship and close alliance, and clinging to their pacts, and considering them as allies; and He informed them that they spare no effort in harming them and in criticising their religion and belittling it. [In the printed edition: "and their alliance," which fails to read the manuscript correctly, as it was undotted; the correct reading is what is given here.]

* *

As for "the disbelievers" mentioned by Allah, exalted is He, in His saying: "from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers as allies," they are the polytheists among the idol worshippers. Allah forbade the believers to take as allies, in place of the believers, those from the People of the Book, the idol worshippers, and all other people of disbelief.

* *

Ibn Mas'ud used to recite:

12217 - Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Ibn Mas'ud: he recited: ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture before you and from among those who associated partners﴾.

* *

This shows the correctness of the interpretation we have given.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

A group of the people of the Hijaz, Basra and Kufa recited: ﴿wal-kuffari awliya'﴾ with the genitive "al-kuffar," meaning: O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and from among the disbelievers, as allies.

* *

Likewise, it is reported that the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b was: ﴿from among those who were given the Scripture before you and from among the disbelievers as allies﴾.

* *

The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited: ﴿wal-kuffara awliya'﴾ with the accusative, meaning: O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement, and the disbelievers, [as allies], coordinating "al-kuffar" with "those who have taken".

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is to say that they are two recitations of agreeing meaning and sound transmission, and each has been recited by scholars among the readers. Whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct. For the prohibition of taking a single disbeliever as an ally is a prohibition of taking all of them as allies, and the prohibition of taking all of them as allies is a prohibition of taking some of them as allies. It is not unclear to any Muslim that when Allah, exalted is He, forbids the believers to take one polytheist as an ally, He has not permitted them to take all of them as allies; and when He forbids taking all of them as allies, He has not specified the permission to take some of them as allies. Therefore there is no need, because of this ambiguity, to seek evidence for which of the two recitations is more correct. Since this is so, whether the reader recites with the genitive or the accusative makes no difference, for the reason we have mentioned.

* *

As for His saying: "And fear Allah if you are believers," it means: fear Allah, O believers, regarding these who have taken your religion as ridicule and amusement, from among those who were given the Scripture and from among the disbelievers, lest you take them as allies and helpers; and dread His punishment for doing so if you do it after it has been forbidden to you, if you truly believe in Allah and affirm His threat for disobeying Him. [See the explanation of "kafara," "awliya'" and "ittaqa" in the earlier language indexes: (kafara), (wala), (waqa).]

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and a game. That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: When your muezzin, O believers, calls to the prayer, those disbelievers among the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists mock your call to it and make a game of it. "That is because they are a people who do not reason." By His words "that," He, may He be exalted and remembered, means their deed, which they do: their mockery and their game made of the call to prayer. They do it only out of ignorance of their Lord, and because they do not reason what benefit there is for them in answering the call to prayer if they were to answer it, and what harm there is for them in mocking and playing with the call to it. Had they reasoned what punishment awaits those among them who do such a thing in the sight of God, they would not have done it.

* *

It has been related from al-Suddi concerning its interpretation:

12218 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And when you call to prayer, they take it as a mockery and a game﴾. A man among the Christians in Medina, whenever he heard the caller call out, "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God," would say, "May the liar be burned!" One night his servant girl came to him with a fire while he was asleep and his family were asleep. A spark fell and burned the house, and he and his family were burned in it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 59:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted One says to His Prophet ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to the People of the Scripture, the Jews and the Christians: O People of the Scripture, do you dislike us or find fault with us for anything, when you mock our religion, and when you, if we call to prayer, take our call as mockery and play? ["In the printed edition: 'or find fault with us until you mock our religion, when you, if we call to prayer,' which does not render the manuscript well; it omitted, altered and substituted, and committed the utmost error."] "Only because we believed in Allah": meaning, only because we affirmed and acknowledged Allah, declaring Him one, and in what has been revealed to us from Allah of the Book, and what was revealed to the prophets of Allah of the scriptures before our Book. "And that most of you are defiantly disobedient": meaning, and only because most of you oppose the command of Allah, depart from His obedience, and lie against Him. ["See the explanation of 'fisq' (defiant disobedience) above, p. 393, note 3, and the references there."]

* *

The Arabs say: "naqimtu 'alayka kadha anqimu" (I resented such-and-such from you, I resent), and with this the reciters of the people of Hijaz and Iraq and others recited it. "Naqimtu anqimu" and "naqima anqimu" are two dialects. ["The first dialect: naqama (with two fathas) yanqimu (with kasra on the qaf). The second dialect: naqima (fatha then kasra) yanqimu (also with kasra on the qaf)."] We do not know of any reciter who recited with both. ["In the printed edition: 'qara'a biha' in the singular; the correct reading is that of the manuscript, meaning 'naqimtu, anqimu' from the second dialect."] It means "found" and "disliked," ["'Wajadat' from the saying: 'wajada 'alayhi yajidu wajdan wa mawjidatan': became angry."] and from it is the verse of Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat: ["His name is disputed: it is said 'Abdullah' and it is said 'Ubayd Allah' with diminutive form, and the latter is more common."]

"They resent of the Banu Umayyah only that they are forbearing when they are angered."

["From his poem: Diwan 70; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:170; Lisan (nqm). He composed it for Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, in a long report mentioned by Abu al-Faraj in al-Aghani 5:76-80. After the verse:
'They are the mine of kings, and none is fit to rule but the Arabs over them;
Indeed the stallion whose father is Abu al-'As, upon him are dignity and veils;
The caliph of Allah above his pulpit, by which the pens and books have dried;
The crown is balanced upon his forehead, upon a brow as if it were gold.'"]

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews.

Mention of those who said so:

12219 - Hannad ibn al-Sari told us, who said: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among them Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, Rafi' ibn Abi Rafi', Azar, ["In the manuscript: 'Azi', the correct form being from the sources cited."] Zayd, Khalid, Azar ibn Abi Azar, and Ushay', and they asked him about whom he believes among the messengers? He said: "I believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord; we do not differentiate between any of them, and we are submissive to Him." ["This is an embedding of the verse of Surah al-Baqarah 2:136."] When he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: "We do not believe in one who believed in him!" ["In the manuscript: 'la nu'min amana bihi', with 'bi-man' omitted."] So Allah revealed concerning them: "Say, O People of the Scripture, do you resent us only because we have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient." ["The report: 12219, Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:216, and it passed with both chains, nos. 2101, 2102."]

* *

[Linking "and that" with the "that" in His words "only that we believed in Allah," ["meaning His words: 'and that most of you are defiantly disobedient,' with the alif of 'wa-anna' vowelled with a fatha, as a conjunction with the 'anna' in His words 'only that we believed in Allah.'"] because the meaning of the statement is: Do you resent us except our belief in Allah and your defiant disobedience.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 60 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as requital from God? Those whom God cursed and with whom He was angry, and some of whom He transformed into apes and swine﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to these who took your religion as mockery and play, from among those who were given the Book before you, and the disbelievers: "Shall I inform you," O people of the Book, of something worse as reward than what you resent us for, our belief in God and in what was sent down to us, the Book of God, and what was sent down before us of His scriptures? [[See the explanation of "mathubah" above, 2:458, 459.]]
* *
["Mathubah" is, in its underlying form, "mafu'ulah." However, since the middle radical of the verb dropped out, its vowel was transferred to the "fa'" [[In the printed edition: "ghayr anna al-'ayn lamma sakanat naqalat harakatuha ila al-fa'," the opening of the sentence has dropped, so what was in the manuscript was changed; I have restored what is given in the brackets, relying on the derivation of the word. What was in the manuscript: "ghayr anna al-fi'l lamma saqata naqalat harakatuha ila al-fa'," the opening of the sentence in brackets has also dropped, and "'ayn" from the phrase "'ayn al-fi'l" has also dropped. I fear that more than this has dropped from the text. See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:170, which is the reading of one who reads "mathubah" (with fatha, then sukun, then fatha).]], which is the "tha'" of "mathubah," so it came out like "maqulah," "mahurah," and "madufah." [[In the printed edition: "mahwazah" with ha and za; in the manuscript: "mahwarah wa musrifah," undotted. The correct reading is what I have given. In some books such as al-Qurtubi 6:243 it appears as "majwazah" with jim and za; all of these are errors, the correct form being what I have given. "Al-mahurah" derives from "al-muhawarah," like "al-mashurah" and "al-mushawarah." One says: "ma ja'atni 'anhu mahurah," meaning no news returned to me from him. Tha'lab related: "iqdi mahwaratak," meaning the matter you are in. It is also said "mahurah" (with fatha on the mim and sukun on the ha'), and from it the poet's verse: "li-hajati dhi bathtin wa mahwarah lahu, ... kafa raj'uha min qisati al-mutakallim."]]
As the poet said: [[He is Abu Jundub al-Hudhali.]]
"Whenever my neighbour called for a mudufah, I would hitch up, until the leg reached half my waistwrap..." [[Ash'ar al-Hudhaliyyin 3:92, Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:170, al-Lisan (dhayf) (nasf), and many others; after it: "But I am a coal of ghada wood behind him, my sword protects me when I do not protect (myself)..." "The people refused anything but evil from me, so leave them, and leave me to what they bring me of wrong..." "When a group rebels against me one day, I rebel against them with a calamity that drops pregnant women, a fuqma' qintir..." "Al-mudufah," "al-mudifah," and "al-mudafah": a matter that a man fears. The verse is related with all of these. "Dhaf al-rajul wa adaf": he feared. "Nasf al-izar saqahu": when it reaches halfway. He means by this his diligence in defending whoever seeks his protection. His saying: "But I am a coal of ghada..." means: I burn in his support with a burning like a remaining flame from a coal of ghada. His saying: "my sword protects me..." means: my sword is my protector when I find no protector to support me. His saying: "masqitat al-ahbal" means: I attack them with a calamity that makes pregnant women miscarry from terror. "Fuqma'" is a description of the terrible calamity, mentioning the ugliness of its appearance; one says "imra'ah fuqma'," who is the one whose upper teeth enter the mouth so that they do not meet the lower incisors, and who also has a sloping palate. "Qintir" is the calamity, and here it appears as a description; its meaning then seems to be a calamity that closes over him completely, like a bridge crossed over water that closes over it. The scholars of language did not mention this derivation; it is my own effort to seek the meaning.
In the manuscript the line of the witness began: "wa kuntu idha jari da'alim," and the line was incomplete; the printed edition completed it.]]
* *
Those who interpret have said something similar to what we have said.
Those who said that:
12220 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Say, shall I inform you of something worse as requital from God," he says: reward from God.
12221 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Shall I inform you of something worse as requital from God," he said: "Al-mathubah" is reward; "mathubat al-khayr" and "mathubat al-sharr," and he recited: ﴿better in reward﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 44]. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "sharr thawaban," and there is no verse in the Book of God with "sharr thawaban," so I have given the verse of al-Kahf, which I estimate Ibn Zayd recited in this place. Al-Suyuti related it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:295 and wrote: "wa qura'a: bi-sharr thawaban," but I did not find this irregular reading, so I relied on what I have given. Also, number 12222 was inadvertently omitted from the numbering.]]
* *
As for "man" in His saying "those whom God cursed," it is in the genitive position, as a continuation of "something worse than that." So the sense of the speech, given that it is so, is: Say, shall I inform you of something worse as requital from God: [the one] whom God cursed.
If it were said that it is in the nominative position, it would also be correct, on the basis of a new sentence, meaning: That is those whom God cursed, or: He is those whom God cursed.
If it were said that it is in the accusative position, it would not be wrong, meaning: Say, shall I inform you of whom God cursed [[See all of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:314.]], so that "unabbi'ukum" governs "man" as its object. [[In the printed edition: "fayuj'alu 'unabbi'ukum 'ala ma fi 'man' waqi'an 'alayhi" and in the manuscript: "fayuj'alu 'unabbi'ukum 'alamatan fiman waqi'an 'alayhi," and both are corrupt; the correct reading is what I have given, but the copyist erred as he sometimes did. "Al-wuqu'" means transitivity, as has been said many times; see the indexes of terms in the earlier volumes.]]
* *
As for the meaning of His saying "whom God cursed," it means: whom God removed and expelled from His mercy [[See the explanation of "al-la'nah" above 9:213, note 3, and the sources there.]], "and He was angry with him and made some of them apes and swine," he says: He was angry with him and made some of them the transformed ones, apes and swine, out of His anger and wrath toward them, hastening for them disgrace and punishment in this world. [[See the explanation of "the anger of God" above 1:188, 189; 2:138, 345; 7:116; 9:57.]]
* *
As for the cause of God's transforming those of them who were transformed into apes, we have mentioned some of it earlier in this book, and we will mention the rest, God willing, in another place. [[See what came before 2:167-172; 8:447, 448; and what will come in the tafsir 9:63-70 (Bulaq).]]
* *
As for the cause of God's transforming those of them who were transformed into swine, it was in what:
12223 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, client of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: I was told that the transformation among the Children of Israel into swine was that a woman among the Children of Israel was in a village of the villages of the Children of Israel, and there was in it the king of the Children of Israel, and they had collectively gathered upon destruction, except that this woman was upon a remnant of Islam, holding fast to it, so she began calling to God; [[In the manuscript: "tad'u Allah" without "ila," and the correct form is what is in the printed edition, as shown by what follows. As for his saying "wa-istajma'u 'ala al-halakah," it means: their gatherings had come close to destruction through their disbelief.]] until people gathered to her and followed her in her matter. She said to them: "There is no escape for you from striving for the religion of God, and you must call your people to it. Go out, for I am going out." She went out, and that king went out with the people against her, and killed all her companions and she escaped from among them. He said: She continued calling to God until people gathered to her, and when she was satisfied with them, she ordered them to go out, so they went out and she went out with them, and all of them were struck and she escaped from among them. Then she called to God until men gathered to her and responded to her; she ordered them to go out, so they went out and she went out, and all of them were struck, and she escaped from among them. She returned, having despaired, saying: "Glory be to God, if this religion had a patron and a helper, He would have made it prevail by now!" He said: So she spent the night in grief, and in the morning the people of the village were going about in its outskirts as swine, which God had transformed in that night. When she awoke and saw what she saw, she said: "Today I know that God has strengthened His religion and commanded His religion!" He said: The transformation into swine among the Children of Israel was only at the hands of that woman. [[The report: 12223: "Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, client of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari," narrated from Ka'b ibn Malik, Ibn 'Umar, Safinah, and others. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, among the followers of the followers. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, and has traditions." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Abdi, Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat, and Abu 'Awn al-Ziyadi narrated from him," but Abu 'Awn said: "'Amr ibn Kathir ibn Aflah," and that is a mistake from him. In the manuscript and printed edition here it was "'Amr ibn Kathir," so I followed Ibn Abi Hatim. He is listed in al-Tahdhib as "Umar," and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/130.]]
12224 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "and made some of them apes and swine," he said: they were transformed from among the Jews.
12225 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
And there is another cause for the transformation, as related, other than what we have mentioned, which we will mention in its proper place, God willing. [[I have not identified its place in the coming tafsir; if I find it I will record it, God willing. Perhaps among it is what will come in the reports numbered 12301-12304. See number 7110.]]
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and some of them worshipped the Taghut; those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ (60)

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed in reading this.
The reading of the people of the Hijaz, Syria, Basra, and some of the Kufans is: ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, meaning: "and made some of them apes and swine, and [some] who worshipped the Taghut," with "'abada" as a past verb, dependent on the implied subject, and "al-taghut" in the accusative, by the governing of "'abada" over it.
* *
And a group of the Kufans read it: ﴿wa 'abuda al-taghut﴾, with fatha on the 'ayn of "'abada" and damma on its ba', and "al-taghut" in the genitive by the "'abud" being annexed to it. They meant by this: "and served the Taghut."
12226 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me this, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Hamzah narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wathhab that he read: ﴿wa 'ubdi al-taghut﴾, saying: served. 'Abd al-Rahman said: Hamzah used to read it in this way.
12227 - Ibn Wakf and Ibn Humayd narrated to me, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, that he used to read it in this way.
* *
Al-Farra' used to say: if there is in it a dialect like "hadhir" and "hadhur," and "'ajil" and "'ajul," then it is a valid form, God knows best; otherwise, if he meant the saying of the poet: [[He is Aws ibn Hajar.]]
"O sons of Lubayna, your mother is a slave-woman, and your father is an 'abud (slave)..."
[[Diwan, the poem 5, verse 4; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:314, 315; al-Lisan (abada); one verse of it has passed earlier, p. 275; before the verse: "O sons of Lubayni, I do not acknowledge you, lest anyone be more base than you."]]
then this is from the necessity of poetry, and this is permissible in poetry for the necessity of rhyme, but in recitation it is not.
[[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:314, 315.]]
* *
Others read it: ﴿wa 'ubuda al-taghut﴾, which was related from al-A'mash.
* *
It seems that whoever read it so intended the plural of the plural of "'abd," as if he made "'abd" into "'abid" in plural, and then made "'abid" into "'ubud," like "thimar" and "thumur."
[[It would have been better to say: "as if he made 'abd into 'ibad in plural, then made 'ibad into 'abd," as is the apparent statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:314.]]
* *
It is also related that Abu Ja'far the reciter used to read it: [[In the printed edition: "annahu yaqra'uhu" without "kana," and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]] ﴿wa 'ubida al-taghut﴾.
12228 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far the grammarian used to read it: ﴿wa 'ubida al-taghut﴾, as one says: "Abd Allah was struck."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This reading has no meaning, because God, may He be exalted, began the report by censuring a people, and among what He censured them for was their worship of the Taghut. As for a report that the Taghut has been worshipped, it is not the kind of report with which the verse began, nor of the kind with which it ended, so that it would have a valid direction to be oriented toward. [[In the printed edition: "min al-sihhah," and what is in the manuscript is correct.]]
* *
It is related that Buraydah al-Aslami used to read it: ﴿wa 'abid al-taghut﴾. [[In the manuscript: "wa 'abid al-shaytan," which is an undoubted error; the printed edition corrected it. See the irregular readings of Ibn Khalawayh: 34.]]
12229 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me this, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: a Basran shaykh narrated to us, that Buraydah used to read it so.
* *
If it were read: ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾ with kasrah, it would have a valid grammatical basis in Arabic, even though I do not today consider it permissible to recite with it, since the authoritative readers' reading is contrary to it. The justification for its permissibility in Arabic is that it means "wa 'abadat al-taghut" (and worshippers of the Taghut), then the ta' was dropped for the annexation, as the rajiz said: [[I did not identify the rajiz.]]
"Its governors stood and gave him Sarkhadi..."
[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:314; his saying "Sarkhad" makes it the Sarkhadi wine itself. As for the people of language, they say "Sarkhad" is a place in Syria, in the region of Hawran, to which good wine is attributed.]]
meaning: its governors stood, so he dropped the ta' from "wulatuha" for the annexation. [[See all of the above in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:314, 315.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for the reading of the readers, it is in one of the two ways I began by mentioning: ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, with "al-taghut" in the accusative and "'abada" governing it, and "'abada" directed as a past verb from "worship."
And the other: ﴿wa 'abud al-taghut﴾, on the pattern of "fa'ul," and "al-taghut" in the genitive by the annexation of "'abud" to it.
Since the readers' reading is in one of these two ways, to the exclusion of other ways which are more valid in Arabic grammar, then the more deserving of the two as correct reading is the reading of him who read ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, meaning: "and made some of them apes and swine, and [some] who worshipped the Taghut," because it is mentioned that this is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿wa ja'ala minhumu al-qiradata wa al-khanazira wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, meaning: "and those who worshipped the Taghut." In that there is clear evidence for the soundness of the meaning we mentioned, that it is intended: "and whoever worshipped the Taghut," and that the accusative with "al-taghut" is more deserving, as I described in the reading, since "'abada" governs it, because the other way is not widespread among the Arabs nor known in their speech.
Moreover, the grammarians disapprove of governing something by "man" and "alladhi" when they are implied together with "min" and "fi," if "min" or "fi" is omitted from them, and they regard it as ugly; some of them even reject it and do not permit it. Whoever rejects it would read ﴿wa 'abada al-taghut﴾, so by his saying it is an error and impermissible solecism.
And others among them permit it with disapproval. So on their saying, the recitation with it must be ugly. Yet despite their disapproval of it in speech, they have chosen to recite with it, and the governing of "ja'ala" over "man," which is omitted with "min."
If we permitted opposing the community regarding anything that they have agreed upon, we would have chosen a reading other than these two readings; but what the Muslims have transmitted widely among themselves, which they do not deny, we do not permit departing from it to something else. Therefore we did not permit reciting contrary to either of the two readings which we mentioned they did not exceed.
* *
Since the recitation, in our view, is what we have mentioned, the interpretation of the verse is: "Say: Shall I inform you of something worse as requital from God: [those] whom God cursed and was angry with, and some of whom He made apes and swine, and those who worshipped the Taghut."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 60 (part 2 of 2):

* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-Taghut" (the false object of worship; idols or anything worshipped besides Allah) earlier, with its supporting reports and other evidence, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. [See the explanation of "al-Taghut" above: 5:416-419 / 8:461-465, 507-513, 546.]
* *
As for His saying, "Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way," by His saying "those" He means those whom He mentioned, may His remembrance be exalted, namely those whose description He gave when He said, "Whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry, and of whom He made apes and swine, and who worshipped the Taghut." All of this is a description of the Jews of the Children of Israel.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this description are "worse in position," in the immediate life of this world and in the Hereafter, with Allah, than those whom you, O assembly of Jews, hold against for their belief in Allah and in what was sent down to them from their Lord in the Book, and in what was sent down to those before them of the Prophets. "And further astray from the right way": He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: and you, O Jews, despite all that, are more deviant from the straight path and further removed from the way of right guidance and moderation than they are. [See the explanation of "al-Dalal" (going astray) in the earlier language indexes, and the explanation of "sawa' al-sabil" (the right way) earlier at 10:124, note 2, and the references there.]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This is from *lahn al-kalam* (the indirect manner of speech). [*Al-lahn* here means allusion and indication, deviating from explicit statement. Ibn Barri said: "*Al-lahn* has six meanings: error in grammatical inflection (i'rab), language, singing, understanding, allusion, and meaning."] This is because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, intended by this report only to inform the Jews whose description He gave in the preceding verses of their ugly deeds and blameworthy characteristics, and of their earning His wrath through the abundance of their sins and disobediences, to the point that He transformed some of them into apes and some into swine. It was an address from Him to them in this manner, an indirect speech with the most gracious wording, and He spoke to them in a manner of *lahn* (allusion) of the finest kind, through what they understood of the meaning of speech. [That is: He alluded to them with the finest indirection and implication.] He taught His Prophet ﷺ the best of manners, so He said to him: Say to them, O Muhammad: Are those who believe in Allah and His books, whom you mock, worse, or those whom Allah has cursed? He meant that this was said to them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿When they come to you, they say, "We believe," but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it; and Allah knows best what they were concealing.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When these hypocrites among the Jews come to you, O believers, they say to you, "We believe" (āmannā): that is, "We affirm what your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ brought, and we follow him in his religion," while they remain upon their disbelief and their misguidance. They have entered upon you with their disbelief, which they hold in their hearts and conceal in their breasts, while they show, falsely, their affirmation of you with their tongues. "And they had left with it": that is, they have left from your presence with disbelief just as they entered upon you with it. Their coming to you did not turn them back from their disbelief and misguidance; they suppose that this deed of theirs is hidden from Allah, out of their ignorance of Allah. "And Allah knows best what they were concealing": that is, Allah knows best what they were concealing from you when they said with their tongues, "We believe in Allah and in Muhammad, and we affirm what he brought," by what they harbour of disbelief within themselves. [[In the printed edition: "mimma yudmirunahu" (of what they harbour), but the correct reading from the manuscript is "bima" (with what). The sense of this sentence, after removing the explanatory parenthetical clauses, is: "And Allah knows best what they were concealing from them ... within themselves," meaning: He knows better than they know themselves. His words "what they harbour of disbelief" relate to his words "what they were concealing," as an explanation of "what they were concealing."

See the explanation of "concealment" above, 2:228, 229.]]

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

12230 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "When they come to you, they say, 'We believe'" — the verse: They were people from among the Jews who used to enter upon the Prophet ﷺ and inform him that they were believers, content with what he had brought, while they clung to their misguidance and disbelief. They would enter with that and leave with it from the presence of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.

12231 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding "When they come to you, they say, 'We believe,' but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it," he said: These were some of the hypocrites who were Jews. He means: they entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers.

12232 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "When they come to you, they say, 'We believe,' but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it." They entered speaking the truth while their hearts concealed disbelief, so He said: "They had entered with disbelief and they had left with it."

12233 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "When they come to you, they say, 'We believe,' but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it" = (And a group of the People of the Book said: "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they may return") [Surah Al 'Imran: 72]. So when they returned to their disbelieving companions among the People of the Book and their devils, they returned with their disbelief. These People of the Book are the Jews.

12234 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Abdullah ibn Kathir regarding "but they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it": that is, it was from their own side.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and their consuming of the unlawful gain. Wretched is what they have been doing.﴾ (5:62)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And you see" O Muhammad, "many" of these Jews whose news I have related to you from the Children of Israel, "hastening toward sin and aggression," meaning: they hasten to commit sin. [See the explanation of "hastening" (al-musara'a) earlier, 10:404, footnote 3, and the references there.]

* *

It has been said that "sin" (al-ithm) in this place refers to disbelief (al-kufr). [See the explanation of "sin" earlier, 9:196, 197, and the rest of the linguistic indexes.]

12235 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: "And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression," he said: "Sin" is disbelief.
