12236 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression," and this was among the judges of the Jews before your eyes. [In the printed edition: "in the rulings of the Jews," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

12237 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "hastening toward sin and aggression," he said: These are the Jews. "Wretched is what they have been doing" = "Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them..." up to His saying: "Wretched is what they used to produce," he said: "producing" and "doing" are the same. He said: [It is said] to these when they did not forbid, as it is said to these when they did [evil].

He said: That is the compromising (al-idhan). [The phrase "That is the compromising" was omitted from the printed edition; in the manuscript, which is poorly written, it reads "He said: That is the ikhran," and the correct reading is what has been given. "Al-idhan" means softness and accommodation, in religion and in everything; in the Revelation: "They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise."]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Although this view reported from al-Suddi is not to be rejected as possibly correct, what is more appropriate as the interpretation of the words is that these people are described as hastening toward all the disobediences of God, not holding back from any of them, neither from disbelief nor from anything else. This is because Exalted is He, in describing them with what He described them, that they hasten toward sin and aggression, generalized without specifying one sin over another.

* *

As for "aggression" (al-'udwan), it is transgressing the limit that God set for them in everything He set limits for.

* *

The interpretation of that: these Jews whom He described in these verses with what Exalted is He described them, many of them hasten toward the disobedience of God and opposition to His command, and transgress His limits which He set for them concerning what He made lawful and unlawful for them, in their consuming of "the unlawful gain" (al-suht), which is the bribery they take from people for judging contrary to God's judgment regarding them. [See the explanation of "al-suht" earlier, 10:317–324.]

* *

Exalted is He says: "Wretched is what they have been doing," meaning: by oath, wretched is the deed that these Jews have been doing, in their hastening toward sin and aggression, and their consuming of the unlawful gain.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? Surely evil is what they have been doing.﴾ (63)

Abu Ja'far said: Mighty and majestic is He, says: Why do they not forbid those who hasten into sin, transgression and the taking of bribes in judgement, from among the Jews of the Children of Israel? [See the explanation of "lawla" in the sense of "halla" (why not), above, 2:552, 553.] Their rabbaniyyun (rabbaniyyun, here meaning: the masters of religious learning, a term with the sense of those devoted to the Lord) — and they are their leaders who are believers, and their politicians who govern by their knowledge of policy — and their ahbar (ahbar, here meaning: scholars and commanders) [See the explanation of "al-rabbaniyyun" above, 5:540–544 / 10:341–343] [See the explanation of "al-ahbar" above, 6:543, 544 / 10:341–343] — "from their speaking of sin," meaning: from speaking falsehood and lies. That is because they used to judge among them by other than God's judgement, and they would write books with their own hands and then say, "This is from God's judgement, and this is from His Book." God says: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 79].

* *

As for His words, "and their consumption of what is unlawful" (al-suht), He means by it the bribes they took for judging, by other than the Book of God, in favour of those for whom they judged.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-rabbaniyyun", "al-ahbar" and "al-suht", with evidence for them earlier, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated in this place. [See the previous comments shortly before.]

* *

"Surely evil is what they have been doing": this is an oath that God swears. He, mighty and majestic, says: I swear, evil is the work that these rabbaniyyun and ahbar were doing, in leaving off forbidding those among them who hasten into sin, transgression and consuming the unlawful, in respect of what they used to do of that.

* *

The scholars used to say: There is no verse in the Qur'an more severe in rebuke of scholars than this verse, and none more frightening for them.

12238 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Nubayt narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words: "Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech?" He said: There is no verse in the Qur'an more frightening to me than it: that we do not forbid. [The report: 12238 - "Abd Allah ibn Dawud ibn Amir ibn al-Rabi' al-Hamdani", Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Khuraybi. He was a trustworthy, devout man, but difficult in narrating. Biographied in al-Tahdhib.]

12239 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from al-Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, from Khalid ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: There is no verse in the Qur'an more severe in rebuke than this verse: "Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? Surely evil is what they have been doing." He said: So he recited it. [The report: 12239 - "Ibn Atiyyah" is: "al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah ibn Najih al-Qurashi", Abu Ali al-Bazzar, previously mentioned as nos. 1939, 4962, 7535, 8961, 8962. He is the one from whom Abu Kurayb narrates, saying "Ibn Atiyyah"; in the printed edition and manuscript it read "Abu Atiyyah", which is an error.

"Qays" is "Qays ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi", previously mentioned as nos. 159, 4842, 5413, 6892, 7535.

"Al-Ala' ibn al-Musayyib ibn Rafi' al-Asadi", previously mentioned as no. 3789.

"Khalid ibn Dinar al-Tamimi al-Sa'di", previously mentioned as no. 44, and he did not meet Ibn Abbas.]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

12240 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, regarding: "Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful": [he said: "The rabbis and the scholars" are their jurists, their reciters and their scholars. He said: Then al-Dahhak would say: How I fear this verse!]. [The report: 12240 - In the printed edition it read "... and their consumption of what is unlawful; surely evil is what they have been doing", completing the verse, with no completion of the report. In the manuscript, neither the completion of the verse nor of the report appears; I have taken what is written from al-Durr al-Manthur 1:296, which says: "Abd ibn Humayd narrated from the route of Salamah ibn Nubayt..." and gave the report as I have written it.]

12241 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful; surely evil is what they have been doing", meaning: the rabbaniyyun, that they: surely evil is what they have been doing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 64 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the Jews say, "The hand of Allah is chained up." Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they have said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Allah, may He be remembered, concerning the audacity of the Jews toward their Lord, and their attributing to Him what is not part of His attributes, as a rebuke to them for that, and as an informing of His Prophet ﷺ of the ancient ignorance and delusion of the Jews concerning Him, and their denial of all of His good favours toward them, and the abundance of His forgiveness and pardon of them for their great crimes; and as an argument in favour of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, that he is a Prophet sent and a Messenger dispatched: for these reports which He informed them of were from among their hidden knowledge and what they kept secret, which none knows except their rabbis and scholars, to the exclusion of other Jews, let alone the unlettered nation of the Arabs, who had not read a book and had not retained any knowledge from the People of the Book. So Allah made His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ aware of that, so that his truthfulness would be established among them and their argument would be cut off thereby.
* *
He, may He be remembered, says: "And the Jews said" – from the Children of Israel – "The hand of Allah is chained up", meaning: that the good of Allah is withheld and His giving is restrained from being expanded upon them, just as He, may He be remembered, said in disciplining His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely outstretched﴾ [Surat al-Isra': 29].
* *
He, may He be remembered, described "the hand" with this, while the meaning is giving, because the giving of people and the bestowal of their kindness is mostly by their hands. So the usage of people in describing one another, when they describe someone with generosity and magnanimity, or with stinginess, niggardliness and restriction, has become to attribute what is from that quality of the one described to his hands, as al-A'sha said in praise of a man:
Your two hands are hands of glory: one palm is bountiful, and a palm that, when it is withheld from provision, spends. [[From his diwan: 150, and elsewhere. From his famous ode which raised al-Muhallaq and carried his fame across the horizons, he says to him: "By my life, many eyes have glimpsed the light of a fire in a height that is kindled, for two shivering men who warm themselves at it, and generosity and the one who was shaved [al-Muhallaq] spent the night beside the fire. Two foster-brothers who sucked the breast of one mother, sworn to one another by a dark-skinned one, the time's exchange, we shall not part." "You see generosity flowing openly upon his face, as a sheen adorns the blade of an Indian sword." "His hands are hands of truth: one palm is bountiful, and a palm that, when wealth is withheld, spends." This is the reading of the manuscript of his diwan that I photographed recently, and the reading of this manuscript differs from the printed reading in many things, especially in the order of the verses.]]
So he attributed to "the hand" what was the quality of its owner, of spending and bestowing. Similar to this in the speech of the Arabs, in their poetry and proverbs, is more than can be counted. So Allah addressed them with what they are familiar with and what they converse about among themselves in their speech, and said: "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up'", meaning by that: they said, "Allah is stingy toward us, and withholds His bounty so that He does not confer favour," like one whose hand is chained up, who cannot extend it with giving or with kindness – "Exalted is Allah above what they say, enemies of Allah!" [[In the printed edition: "above what the enemies of Allah say," and I have retained what is in the manuscript; and his saying "enemies of Allah" is in the accusative as a form of censure.]] Then Allah, rebutting them and informing of His displeasure with them, said: "Their hands are chained up", meaning: their hands were withheld from good things and held back from extending gifts. "And they are cursed for what they have said", and they were removed from the mercy and bounty of Allah because of what they said of disbelief, and they slandered Allah and attributed to Him lies and falsehood. [[See the explanation of "curse" above, vol. 10: 437, note 3, and the references there.]]
"Rather, His two hands are outstretched", meaning: rather, His hands are outstretched with bestowal and giving, and the provision of His servants and the sustenance of His creation, not chained nor withheld. [[See the explanation of "outstretching" above, vol. 5: 288, 290, 313.]] "He spends however He wills", meaning: He gives to this one and withholds from that one, restricting it upon him. [[See the explanation of "spending" above, vol. 7: 134, note 3, and the references there, then the rest of the language indexes.]]
* *
And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that:
12242 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up. Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they have said'", he said: They do not mean by that that the hand of Allah is tied, but they say: He is a miser who withholds what He has. Exalted is Allah far above what they say.
12243 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning the saying of Allah: "The hand of Allah is chained up." He said: They said: "We have exerted ourselves against Allah – O Children of Israel," [[In the printed edition, what I have placed between the two lines is omitted; in the manuscript it reads: "We have exerted ourselves against Allah, i.e., we have exhausted Allah, O Children of Israel," and I have judged its correct form to be as I have given it. The word "tajahhada" (with the h doubled) is not mentioned in the lexicons in the sense of: to press someone in asking until he exhausts what he has; and perhaps for this reason he explained it with his saying (as I read it): "i.e., we exhausted Allah," from the saying "the man exhausted" (triliteral): when he pressed him in asking. This is what I have seen, and above every possessor of knowledge is one who knows. See the following report.]] until Allah made His hand reach his throat! And they lied!
12244 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "The hand of Allah is chained up." He said: The Jews say it: "We have exerted ourselves against Allah, O Children of Israel and O People of the Book," [[See the note above, p. 452, no. 4.]] until His hand is at his throat – "Rather, His two hands are outstretched, He spends however He wills."
12245 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada concerning His saying: "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up. Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they have said'" up to "Allah does not love the corrupters." As for His saying: "The hand of Allah is chained up", they said: Allah is a miser, not generous! Allah said: "Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills."
12246 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up. Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they have said. Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills.'" They said: Allah has placed His hand upon His chest, so He will not extend it until He returns our kingdom to us.
* *
= As for His saying: "He spends however He wills", He says: He provides however He wills.
12247 – Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ikrima said: "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up'" – the verse was revealed concerning Finhas the Jew.
12248 – Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Tumayla related to us, from Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim concerning His saying: "The hand of Allah is chained up", they say: He is stingy, not generous! Allah said: "Their hands are chained up", their hands were withheld from spending and good. Then He said, meaning Himself: "Rather, His two hands are outstretched; He spends however He wills." And He said: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ [Surat al-Isra': 29], meaning: do not withhold your hand from spending.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The people of disputation (ahl al-jadal) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "Rather, His two hands are outstretched." [[This is the first time Abu Ja'far mentions the adherents of kalam and names them "the people of disputation".]] Some of them said: He means by it: His two blessings. And he said: That means "the hand of Allah over His creation", and that is His blessings upon them. And he said: The Arabs say, "You have a hand with me," meaning: a blessing.
* *
Others among them said: He meant by it power. They said: That is like the saying of Allah, may He be remembered: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the possessors of hands﴾ [Surat Sad: 45].
* *
Others among them said: Rather, "His hand" is His dominion. He said: The meaning of His saying: "The hand of Allah is chained up" is His dominion and His treasuries.
They said: That is like the saying of the Arabs about a slave: "He is the possession of his right hand," and "So-and-so has in his hand the knot of marriage to so-and-so," meaning he possesses that; and like the saying of Allah, may He be remembered: ﴿So present a charity before your private conference﴾ [Surat al-Mujadila: 12].
* *
Others among them said: Rather, "the hand of Allah" is one of His attributes, it is a hand, but it is not a limb like the limbs of the children of Adam.
They said: That is because Allah, may He be remembered, informed concerning the special distinction of Adam by what He singled him out with, in creating him with His hand. [[In the printed edition: "concerning the particularity of Adam," and he repeated "particularity" in the genitive in all that follows, which is a mistake by the editor; I have retained what is in the manuscript.]]
They said: And if the meaning of "the hand" were blessing, or power, or dominion, there would be no understandable sense to Adam's distinction by that [this addition between brackets is one required by the sense; I have inferred it from the context of these arguments as best I could, and omitting it corrupts the sentence], since all of His creation is created by His power, and His will in His creation is a blessing, and He is the owner of all of them.
They said: And since He, may He be remembered, singled out Adam by mentioning that He created him with His hand, to the exclusion of His other servants, it is known that He only singled him out for that for a meaning by which he is distinguished from the rest of creation.
They said: And when that is so, the saying of those who claim that the meaning of "hand" from Allah, in this place, is power, or blessing, or dominion, is void.
They said: And more fitting, if it were as those who claim that "the hand of Allah" in His saying "And the Jews said, 'The hand of Allah is chained up'" is His blessing, it would have been said: "Rather, His hand is outstretched," and it would not have said "Rather, His two hands," because the blessings of Allah cannot be counted in abundance. [[In the printed edition: "cannot be counted by abundance," and I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] And so the revelation came, Allah says: ﴿And if you count the blessing of Allah, you cannot enumerate it﴾ [Surat Ibrahim: 34; and Surat al-Nahl: 18].
They said: If they were two blessings, they would have been countable.
They said: If someone suspects that the two blessings mean many blessings, that is an error on his part, because the Arabs may express the plural with a singular word to convey the whole of its genus, as in the saying of Allah, may He be remembered: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [Surat al-Asr: 1–2], and His saying ﴿We have certainly created man﴾ [Surat al-Hijr: 26], and His saying: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever against his Lord a helper﴾ [Surat al-Furqan: 55]. He said: "Man" and "the disbeliever" in these places do not refer to a specific man, nor to a particular disbeliever present and pointed to, but rather all of mankind and all the disbelievers are intended, but the singular expresses its genus, as the Arabs say: "How much the dirham is in the hands of people!" And likewise His saying: ﴿And the disbeliever﴾ means: "And those who disbelieved."
They said: As for when the noun is dualized, it does not express the genus, and it expresses only two specific persons, not all of them and not others.
They said: And it is an error in Arabic to say: "How much the two dirhams are in the hands of people," meaning: how much the dirhams are in their hands.
They said: Because when the dirham is dualized, in their speech it expresses only two specific ones.
They said: It is not impossible to say: "How much the dirham is in the hands of people," and "How much the dirhams are in their hands," because the singular expresses the whole.
They said: So in the saying of Allah, "Rather, His two hands are outstretched," together with His informing His servants that His blessings cannot be counted, along with what we have described, that it is not understood in Arabic speech that two express the whole, [this indicates the error of the saying of those who say the meaning of "hand" in this place is blessing, and the soundness of the saying of those who say that "the hand of Allah" is an attribute of His.]
They said: And with this the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have been mutually reinforcing, and the scholars and the people of interpretation have held it.
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And it will certainly increase many of them in transgression and disbelief through what has been revealed to you from your Lord.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: that this which We have made you aware of from the hidden matters of these Jews, which none knows except their scholars and rabbis, as an argument against them for the soundness of your prophethood, and as a cutting off of the excuse of a speaker among them who would say: "There came to us no bringer of good news nor a warner" = ﴿it will certainly increase many of them in transgression and disbelief through what has been revealed to you from your Lord.﴾ By "transgression" he means: the excess in denying what they had known to be true concerning the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and persisting in that. "And disbelief": He says: and it increases them, along with their excess in denying that, in denying the greatness of Allah and describing Him with other than His attributes, by attributing to Him stinginess and saying "The hand of Allah is chained up." Allah, may He be remembered, only informed His Prophet ﷺ that they are people of rebellion and defiance toward their Lord, and that they do not submit to the truth even if they know it to be true, but rather they oppose it, to console His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ for his grief over them because of their turning away from Allah and their denial of him.
* *
I have already explained the meaning of "transgression" previously with its evidences, in a way that suffices without repeating it. [[See the explanation of "transgression" above, vol. 1: 308, 309 / vol. 5: 419.]]
* *
And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that:
12249 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "And it will certainly increase many of them in transgression and disbelief through what has been revealed to you from your Lord": the envy of Muhammad ﷺ and the Arabs led them to disbelieve in him, while they find him written among them.
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be remembered, means by His saying: "And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection" – among the Jews and the Christians, as:
12250 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection": the Jews and the Christians.
* *
If someone says: How is it said, "And We have cast among them enmity and hatred," when you have made the "ha" and "mim" in His saying "among them" a reference to the Jews and the Christians, while there has been no prior mention of the Jews and the Christians?
It is said: Mention of them has indeed occurred, and that is His saying: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾ [Surat al-Ma'ida: 51]. The report occurred in some verses concerning both groups, and in some concerning one of them, until it reached His saying: "And We have cast among them enmity and hatred"; then by His saying "We have cast among them," He intended the report concerning both groups.
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be remembered, says: every time their affair gathers upon something and becomes firm and stable, and they intend to confront those who oppose them, Allah scatters it upon them and corrupts it, because of their bad deeds and the evil of their intentions, [[See the explanation of "kindled" above, vol. 1: 320, 380 / vol. 6: 222.]] like that which:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 64 (part 2 of 2):

12251 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: ﴿You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely become arrogant with great arrogance. So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they ransacked the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled. Then We gave you the return [of victory] over them﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 4-6]. He said: The first corruption was when an enemy was sent against them, and they plundered the homes, took the women by force, enslaved the young boys, and ruined the Mosque. They "remained" (ghabaru) for a period of time, [[In the printed edition: "fa-ghayyaru" with a ya, which is an error. "Ghabaru zamanan" means they stayed for a time.]] then God sent a prophet among them, and their affairs returned to their best condition. Then the second corruption occurred through their killing of the prophets, until they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya. So God sent Bukht Nassar (Nebuchadnezzar) against them, who killed those of them who were killed, took captive those who were taken captive, and ruined the Mosque. Thus Bukht Nassar was the second corruption. He said: "Corruption" means disobedience. Then He said: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter came, to sadden your faces and to enter the Mosque as they entered it the first time﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And if you return, We will return﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 7, 8]. So God sent them Uzair, who had knowledge of the Torah and had it memorized in his heart, and wrote it down for them. That generation upheld it, and then they remained [in it] and forgot. [[In the printed edition: "wa-nasu" with a waw, and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]] Uzair died, and there were events, and they forgot the covenant and denied their Lord, and said: "The hand of God is chained; their hands were chained, and they were cursed for what they said. Rather, His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills," and they said about Uzair: "God has taken him as a son." They used to criticize the Christians for their saying about the Messiah, yet they opposed what they had been forbidden and did what they had been warned against. So a word from God had already gone forth at that time that they would never prevail over another enemy until the end of time. He said: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it; and they strive throughout the earth to cause corruption, and God does not love the corrupters﴾. So God sent against them the Magians as the third lords, [[In the printed edition: "al-Majus al-thalathata arbaban" (the three Magians as lords), and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, meaning the promise of the Hereafter, which is the third time.]] and they remained so, with the Magians upon their necks, while they said: "Would that we had lived to see this Prophet whom we find written with us; perhaps God will deliver us through him from the Magians and the humiliating punishment!" So God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), whose name is "Muhammad," and whose name in the Gospel is "Ahmad." When he came to them and they recognized him, [[In the printed edition: "fa-lamma jaahum ma 'arafu..." following the wording of al-Baqarah 89; I have restored what is in the manuscript, which is also correct, as he does not mean the verse itself but its meaning.]] they disbelieved in him. He said: ﴿So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 89], and He said: ﴿So they earned wrath upon wrath﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 90]. [[Athar 12251: Abu Ja'far did not mention this report in his tafsir of the verses "Surah al-Isra: 4-8" in his Tafsir, vol. 15, pp. 17-35 (Bulaq edition). This is one of the proofs of the abridgment of the tafsir.]]

12252 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it" — they are the Jews.

12253 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it, and they strive throughout the earth to cause corruption." Those are the enemies of God, the Jews. Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it, so you will not encounter the Jews in any land without finding them among the most humiliated of its people. When Islam came, when it came, they were under the hands of the Magians, the most hated of His creation to Him.

12254 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His saying: "Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it." He said: Whenever they agreed upon a matter, God scattered it, and extinguished their force and their fire, and cast terror into their hearts. [["Al-hadd" means force and sharpness. "Hadd al-zahira" means the intensity of its blazing.]]

* *

Mujahid said, in the following:

12255 - Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Every time they kindle a fire for war, God extinguishes it." He said: It is the war of Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they strive throughout the earth to cause corruption, and God does not love the corrupters﴾ (64)

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted mention says: These Jews and Christians work at disobedience to God, disbelieving in His signs, denying His messengers, and opposing His command and prohibition, and that is their striving in it for corruption. ﴿And God does not love the corrupters﴾ means: God does not love whoever is working at His disobedience on His earth. [[See the explanation of "corruption on the earth" previously: 287, 416; then 10:257 note 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "striving" previously 4:238, and in the other language indexes.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 65:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "And if the People of the Scripture" — and they are the Jews and the Christians — "had believed" in Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), affirming him, following him, and following what was revealed to him, "and had feared Allah" — by avoiding what Allah has forbidden them and staying away from it — "We would have removed from them their misdeeds," meaning: We would have erased their sins for them, covering them over, and not exposed them by them. [[See the explanation of "takfir" (expiation) above, 7:482, 490; and 8:254; and the explanation of "sayyi'at" (misdeeds) in the indices of language above, root (s-w-').]]

"And admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure," meaning: And We would have admitted them to gardens in which they would enjoy delights in the Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "jannah" (garden) above, 8:448, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

12256 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared Allah," meaning: they believed in what Allah revealed, and feared what Allah forbade, "We would have removed from them their misdeeds."

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel, and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel," He, may He be exalted, means: had they acted upon what is in the Torah and the Gospel [[See the explanation of "iqamah" (upholding) in the earlier lexical indexes under (q-w-m), as in "iqamat al-salah" (establishing the prayer).]] "and what was revealed to them from their Lord." He means: and had they acted upon what was revealed to them from their Lord, namely the Furqan (the Criterion) that Muhammad ﷺ brought to them.

* *

If someone says: How could they uphold the Torah and the Gospel together with what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ, given the differences among these books and the abrogation (naskh) of some of them by others?

It is said: Although they differ in some of their rulings and laws, they agree on the command to believe in the messengers of God and to affirm what they brought from God. So the meaning of their upholding the Torah, the Gospel, and what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ is: their affirmation of what is in them, and their acting upon what they all agree on, and each of them at the time when its practice was obligatory. [[In the printed edition: "and each of them in the report that made its practice obligatory," which is a phrase without meaning; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

As for the meaning of His words "they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet," He means: God would have sent down rain upon them from the sky, and the earth would have produced by it its grain and vegetation, and brought forth its fruits.

* *

As for His words "and from beneath their feet," He, may He be exalted, means: they would have eaten from the blessing of what is beneath their feet of the earth, which is what the earth brings forth of its grain, vegetation, fruits, and all other edible things that the earth produces.

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said so:

12257. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih told us, he said: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding "Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them," meaning: He would have sent the sky upon them in abundant rain, "and from beneath their feet," meaning: the earth would have yielded its blessing.

12258. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding "Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." He says: Then the sky would have given them its blessing and the earth its plants.

12259. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." He says: If they had acted upon what was revealed to them, what Muhammad ﷺ brought them, We would have sent down rain upon them, and so the fruit would have grown. [[In the printed edition: "fa-anbatat al-thamar" (then the fruit grew); I have kept the manuscript reading, which is the correct one.]]

12260. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "Had they truly upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord": as for "their upholding the Torah," it is acting upon it; and as for "what was revealed to them from their Lord," it is Muhammad ﷺ and what was revealed to him. He says: "They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." As for "from above them," rain would have been sent down upon them; and as for "from beneath their feet," He says: I would have made the earth grow for them from My provision what would suffice them.

12261. Al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words "they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet." He said: the blessings of the sky and the earth. Ibn Jurayj said: "They would have eaten from above them" is the rain, "and from beneath their feet" is the growth of the earth.

12262. Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words "from above them and from beneath their feet," he says: they would have eaten from the provision that descends from the sky, "and from beneath their feet," he says: from the earth.

* *

Some of them said [[This is the view of al-Farra' in Maʿani al-Quran, vol. 1, p. 315.]] that what is meant by His words "they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet" is abundance (tawsiʿah), as when one says: "He is in good fortune from his horn to his foot." [[In the printed edition: "min farqihi ila qadamihi" (from his parting to his foot); I have kept the manuscript reading. In Maʿani al-Quran and in the lexicon, "al-qarn" is the edge of the head and its sides, and the top of every high thing is its qarn.]]

But the interpretation of those who engaged in interpretation differs from this view, and its unsoundness is sufficiently proven by that.

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do.﴾ (66)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Among them is a community," He, may He be exalted, means: among them is a group. "Moderate" means: moderate in what they say about Jesus, son of Mary, saying the truth about him: that he is the messenger of God, His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him. They are neither excessive, saying that he is the son of God (exalted is God above what they say), nor deficient, saying that he was born out of wedlock. "But many of them," means: among the Children of Israel, from the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. "Evil is what they do" means: the deeds of many of them are evil. [[See the explanation of "saa" (evil) in the earlier volumes, vol. 9, p. 205, note 4, and the references there.]] This is because they disbelieve in God: the Christians deny Muhammad ﷺ and claim that the Messiah is the son of God, and the Jews deny Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless them both. So God, may He be exalted, said about them, censuring them: "Evil is what they do" in their conduct in this matter.

Those who engaged in interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Among those who said so:

12263 [numbering as printed]. "But many of them—evil is what they do." [[The number 12263 was skipped in the numbering by mistake.]]

12264. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir told us, that he heard Mujahid say: The Children of Israel split into sects. One sect said: "Jesus is the son of God." Another said: "He is God." Another said: "He is the servant of God and His spirit." And these are the moderate ones, who are the Muslims among the People of the Book.

12265. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, who said: God said: "Among them is a moderate community," meaning: adhering to His Book and His command. Then He censured most of the people, saying: "But many of them—evil is what they do."

12266. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Among them is a moderate community": he says: believing.

12267. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do": He said: The moderate ones are the people of obedience to God. He said: And these are the People of the Book.

12268. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, regarding His words "Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—evil is what they do," he said: These are the moderate community, who neither were harsh in religion nor did they exceed its bounds. [[In the printed edition: "alladhina la hum fasaqu fi al-din" (who did not transgress in religion); this appears so also in al-Durr al-Manthur, vol. 2, p. 297. The manuscript reading, which I have adopted, is the correct one, God willing. A hadith says: "The bearer of the Quran who is neither excessive in it nor harsh (al-jafi)," and also: "Recite the Quran and do not be harsh toward it," i.e., attend to it and do not neglect its recitation.]] He said: "Ghuluw" (excess) is aversion [from it], and "fisq" (transgression) is falling short of it. [[This addition between the brackets is necessary; I have inferred it from the earlier report, no. 10853, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas's interpretation of the verse in Surat al-Nisa' (4:171).]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 5, verse 67:**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the Qur'anic text) of His saying:** ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), [[In the printed edition: "to His Prophet Muhammad." What is in the manuscript differs from this without any significant consequence.]] to convey to these Jews and Christians, the People of the Two Scriptures, whose accounts Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, relates in this surah, and in which He mentions their faults, the wickedness of their religions, their audacity against their Lord, their assaults upon their prophets, their altering of His Book and their distortion of it, and the vileness of their food and their eating; and to convey also to all other polytheists, what was sent down to him concerning them: their faults, the disparagement and belittling of them, the condemnation of them, what He commanded them and forbade them, [[The phrase "and the rest of the polytheists" is in the genitive, conjoined to his saying "to convey to these Jews and Christians ..." and the object of "to convey to these ..." is "what was sent down to him concerning them."]] and that he should not feel apprehensive, fearing that they might inflict some harm upon him, for standing up among them for the command of Allah, [[In the printed edition: "that harm might befall him," which differs from the manuscript without any significant consequence.]] nor should he be dismayed by the multitude of their numbers and the paucity of those with him; and that he should not fear anyone in the cause of Allah, for Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is sufficient for him against every one of His creatures, and He repels from him the harm of everyone who seeks to harm him. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "everyone who fears his harm," which is thoroughly corrupt; the correct reading is what has been adopted.]] And Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed him that if he falls short in conveying anything of what was sent down to him to them, then by leaving off conveying it, even if it be little of what he has not conveyed, he has incurred a great sin, as though he had not conveyed any of His revelation at all.

* * *

**And those who engaged in ta'wil said in accordance with what we have said:**

**Mention of those who said that:**

12270 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message.﴾ He meant: If you conceal a single verse of what has been sent down to you from your Lord, you will not have conveyed My messages. [[In the printed edition: "My message," which differs from the manuscript.]]

12271 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾, the verse: Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that He would suffice him against the people and protect him from them, and He commanded him to convey. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was told: "If only you would veil yourself!" He said: "By Allah, I will show my heels to the people as long as I accompany them." [[His saying "veil himself" means: veil himself from the people so that those who seek to harm him cannot reach him with their treachery. "Al-'aqib" here means "the heel of the foot," and it is feminine; it is what is at the back. The meaning is: "I will surely show myself to them walking among them, not veiling myself." Whoever goes out to the people has shown them his heel, as he walks among them. This is a fine metaphor. His saying "as long as I accompany them" is for emphasis, as though he had said: "as long as I live."]]

12272 - Al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from a man, from Mujahid, who said: When ﴿Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ was revealed, he said: "I am only one; how shall I act? The people have banded together against me!" [[In the printed edition: "the people gather against him," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. The meaning of "the people banded together against him" is that they united against him and opposed him because of his call to the religion of Allah. This is an expression of wonder.]] Then ﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾, the verse, was revealed.

12273 - Hannad and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Tha'laba, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not guard me, for my Lord has protected me." [[Report 12273: "Jarir" is Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi, who has passed several times. "Tha'laba" is Tha'laba ibn Suhayl al-Tamimi al-Tahawi, who was a physician, trustworthy, with no objection to him, and is listed in the Tahdhib (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, a biographical dictionary). "Ja'far" is Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira al-Khuza'i, who has passed under numbers 87, 617, 4347, and 7269. This is a mursal report (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain). See Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3: 196.]]

12274 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was being guarded by some of his companions in turns. "Malahiq" is the plural of "mulhaq" (with a fatha on the mim, a sukun on the lam, and a fatha on the ha): that is, the place where they alight upon their return.]]

* * *

**The engaged in ta'wil differed regarding the occasion (sabab al-nuzul) for which this verse was revealed.**

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning a Bedouin who had resolved to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but Allah sufficed him against him.

**Mention of those who said that:**

12278 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others, who said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alighted at a place, his companions would choose for him a shady tree, and he would take a midday rest beneath it. A Bedouin came to him, drew his sword [["Drew the sword": pulled it from its sheath.]] and said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah!" The Bedouin's hand trembled and the sword fell from him. [[This is how the report has come down: "the Bedouin's hand trembled," in the passive voice. I have not found the triliteral "ra'ada" in the passive; rather, what they transmitted and agreed upon is "a'rada" (in the passive voice). If this report is sound, then the triliteral passive is among the forms that are added to the linguistic material.]] He said: And he struck his head against the tree until his brain was scattered, and Allah revealed: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾. [[Report 12278: See the report of this Bedouin above under number 11565, and the commentary on it there. It does not say that he struck his head against the tree until his brain was scattered.]]
