**And His saying: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ means: He will prevent you from their reaching you with evil. Its origin is from "'isam al-qirba" (the strap or cord of a waterskin), which is what is tied with a thong or string,**

[[See the explanation of "'asama" and "'isam" previously in volumes 7: 62, 63, 70, and 9: 341.]]

And from this is the saying of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"I said: 'Upon you is Malik; indeed Malik / will protect you, if there is any protector among the people.'" [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubayda 1: 171. "'Alayka" is a verb-form used to urge (ism fi'l al-ighra'), as one says: "'Alayka Zaydan" and "'Alayka bi-Zayd."]]

meaning: He will prevent you.

* * *

**As for His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, it means: Indeed Allah does not grant success in rectitude to whoever deviates from the path of truth, strays from the straight path, denies what I brought from Allah, and does not submit to the command of Allah and His obedience in what He has made obligatory and prescribed for him.** [[See the explanation of "hada" (guidance) previously in the linguistic indices.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 68:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to convey to the Jews and Christians who were living among the people of his place of emigration (muhajar). God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to him: "Say," O Muhammad, to these Jews and Christians, "O People of the Scripture" (the Torah and the Gospel), "you are not standing on anything" of what you claim to be upon, of what Moses ﷺ brought to you, O company of Jews, nor of what Jesus brought to you, O company of Christians, "until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord," of what Muhammad ﷺ brought you of the Criterion (al-Furqan), so that you act upon all of that, and believe in what it contains of faith in Muhammad ﷺ and affirmation of him, and acknowledge that all of it is from God, so that you do not deny any part of it, and do not differentiate between the messengers of God, believing in some and disbelieving in others. For disbelief in one of these is disbelief in all of them, because the books of God confirm one another, and whoever denies some of them has denied all of them.

* *

The report (athar) has come in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

12284 - Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Rafi' ibn Harithah and Sallam ibn Mishkam, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "Sallam ibn Miskin," but I did not find this name among the Jews of the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ; the known name is what I have recorded, and it is what appears in this report in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] and Malik ibn al-Sayf, and Rafi' ibn Huraymilah, [[In the printed edition: "... ibn Harmalah," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript, which matches the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, do you not claim that you are upon the religion and creed of Abraham, and that you believe in what we have of the Torah, and bear witness that it is true from God?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Yes, but you have introduced innovations and denied what is in it of the covenant that was taken from you, and you concealed from it what you were commanded to make clear to the people. I am free of your innovations!" They said: "We hold to what is in our hands, for we are upon the truth and guidance, and we will not believe in you nor follow you!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord"﴾ up to ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ [[The report: 12284 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 217, and it follows the reports that passed, numbers: 2101, 2102, 12219.]]

12285 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not standing on anything until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord"﴾, he said: "So we have become of the People of the Scripture." "The Torah" is for the Jews, and "the Gospel" is for the Christians, and "what has been revealed to you from your Lord" is what has been revealed to us from our Lord. That is: "You are not standing on anything until you establish," until you act upon what is in it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ (68)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, by His words: "And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief," means, and He swears: What has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, of the Book will surely increase many of these Jews and Christians whose stories are related in these verses ﴿in transgression﴾, meaning: excess and extremism in denying you, beyond what they were already doing toward you before the revelation of the Criterion, ﴿and disbelief﴾, meaning: denial of your prophethood.

We have already given the explanation of the meaning of "transgression" earlier. [[See the explanation of "al-tughyan" previously, p. 457, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His words: "So do not grieve over the disbelieving people," by His words "so do not grieve" is meant: do not be sad.

* *

It is said: "Asiya fulan 'ala kadha" when he grieves, "ya'sa asan," and from it is the saying of the rajiz (the poet of the rajaz meter): [[He is al-Ajjaj.]]

"And his eyes flowed from the excess of grief (al-asa)"

[[His Diwan: 31; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 171; al-Kamil 1: 352; al-Lisan (h-l-b), (k-r-s). It is from his well-known rajaz, whose beginning passed in this tafsir 1: 509, where he says: "O companion, do you recognize a faded trace? ... He said: Yes! I recognize it, and it has become desolate."

"And his eyes flowed from the excess of grief"

The explanation of the first two verses has passed. "Inhallabat 'aynahu" and "tahallabatā": their tears flowed and followed one another. In the printed edition it read "wa-anhallat," which contradicts the manuscript, because the manuscript is undotted, so the editor produced something unknown. Then one who wrote on this verse and corrected it wrote "wa-abkhalat" and said: "Meaning: abkhalat: they were found stingy with tears because grief overcame him, i.e., that from the intensity of his grief he did not weep, rather his eyes became dry." He erred in several respects: he neglected to consult and know the poetry, he strove without benefit, and he produced an extremely feeble statement! And God is the One sought for help.]]

* *

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet: Do not grieve, O Muhammad, over the denial of these disbelievers among the Jews and Christians of the Children of Israel toward you, for such conduct from them is a habit and disposition toward their prophets, so how much more toward you?

* *

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

12286 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾, he said: "The Criterion," meaning: "So do not grieve."

12287 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾, he said: "Do not grieve."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 69:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians—whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteousness—no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ (5:69).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger, namely the people of Islam, "and those who were Jews," namely the Jews [[See the explanation of "Hud" (Jews) above, p. 341, note 1, and the references there.]], "and the Sabeans" [[See the explanation of "al-Sabi'un" (the Sabeans) above, vol. 2, pp. 145–147.]], whose matter we have already clarified, "and the Christians—whoever among them believes in Allah and the Last Day," so he affirms the resurrection after death, "and does" from the deed "righteousness" for his return (to Allah), "then no fear will there be concerning them," regarding what they encounter of the terrors of the Resurrection, "nor will they grieve," over what they left behind of the world and its life, after witnessing what Allah has honored them with of His abundant reward.

[[See the explanation of "does righteousness" above, vol. 2, p. 148 (and the lexical indexes); and the explanation of "the Last Day" above, in the lexical indexes (under akhr); and the explanation of "no fear upon them nor will they grieve" above, vol. 2, p. 150, and the rest of the lexical indexes.]]

* *

We have already explained the grammatical construction of this verse earlier, in a manner that suffices without repetition. [[See what was given above, vol. 3, pp. 352–354; then see the place he referred to, vol. 9, pp. 395–399. Then see also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, vol. 1, pp. 105–108; Abu 'Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an, vol. 1, p. 172; and Ibn Qutayba's Mushkil al-Qur'an, pp. 36–39.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 70:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group they denied and a group they killed.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He swears: Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel to be sincere in affirming Our oneness[[In the printed edition: "wa-tawhidina" (and Our oneness); in the manuscript: "al-ikhlas tawhidana" (sincerity, Our oneness). The correct reading appears to be what has been adopted here.]] and to act upon what We commanded them, and to refrain from what We forbade them. We sent to them messengers with that, and We promised them, through the tongues of Our messengers sent to them, great reward for obeying Us, and We threatened them with severe punishment for disobeying Us. Every time a messenger of Ours came to them with what their souls did not desire and what did not accord with their inclinations, they denied a group of them and killed a group of them, breaking Our covenant which We had taken from them, and showing audacity toward Us and opposition to Our command.[[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier language indexes.

At this point, a section of the old division from which our manuscript was copied has ended, and in it is the following text:

"Followed by: The explanation of His words:

﴿And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf﴾

And may Allah bless Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family, and grant them abundant peace."

Then what follows it, its text:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful

My Lord, make it easy"]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 5, verse 71:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil, meaning the explanation of the text's intended sense) of His saying: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them; then many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: And these Israelites [[See the explanation of "ḥasiba" (to think, to reckon) above, 7:384, 421.]] thought, those whose characteristics He, Exalted is His remembrance, described, that He took their covenant, sent messengers to them, and that whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, they denied a group and killed a group, that there would be no trial from Allah for them, no testing through hardships and punishments, because of what they used to do. [[See the explanation of "al-fitnah" (trial, test) above, p. 392, note 2, and the references there.]]

"So they became blind and deaf": He says: they became blind to the truth and to fulfilling the covenant I took from them, namely sincerely worshipping Me, desisting at My command and prohibition, and acting in obedience to Me, through their reckoning that and their thinking so, "and they became deaf" to it. Then I turned to them. He says: then I guided them with a kindness from Me toward them, until they repented and returned from their disobedience to Me and opposition to My command, and from doing what I dislike of them to doing what I love, and to desisting and obeying My command and prohibition. "Then many of them became blind and deaf again." [[See the explanation of "al-'ama" (blindness) and "al-samam" (deafness) above, 1:328–331, 3:315.]] He says: then they became blind again to the truth and to fulfilling My covenant that I took from them: by acting in obedience to Me, desisting at My command, and avoiding My disobedience. "Many of them became deaf": He says: many of those from the Children of Israel whose covenant I had taken became blind, by following My messengers and acting on what I sent down to them in My books [[See the discussion of the case of "kathīr" (many) as a grammatical matter in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:316, and Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1:174.]], to the truth, and became deaf, after My turning to them and My rescuing them from destruction. "And Allah is Seeing of what they do": He says, "Seeing" means He sees their deeds, good and bad, and will requite them on the Day of Resurrection for all of them: if good, with good, and if evil, with evil. [[See the explanation of "baṣīr" (seeing) above in the language indexes.]]

* *

And Ahl al-Ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

12288 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And they thought there would be no trial," the verse: He means: the people thought there would be no affliction. "So they became blind and deaf": whenever an affliction came upon them, with which they were tested, they perished in it.

12289 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf": He means: they thought they would not be tested, so they became blind to the truth and deaf to it.

12290 - Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, regarding "And they thought there would be no trial": he said: affliction.

12291 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "And they thought there would be no trial": he said: polytheism (shirk).

12292 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf": he said: the Jews.

12293 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "so they became blind and deaf": he said: the Jews. Ibn Jurayj said, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, who said: this verse is about the Children of Israel. He said: and "al-fitnah" (trial) means affliction and purification (tamhis).

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Certainly those have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." But the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers."﴾ (72)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may He be remembered, about some of the trials with which He tested the Children of Israel, those whom He informed had thought that there would be no trial. He, may He be remembered, says: Among what I tested them with and examined them by was that they broke My covenant and changed My pact which I had taken from them, that they should not worship other than Me, nor take a lord other than Me, and that they should affirm My oneness and submit to My obedience. [They broke it] regarding My servant Jesus son of Mary, for I created him and performed upon his hand what I performed upon the hand of many of My messengers, yet they said in disbelief, "He is Allah." [See the explanation of "the Messiah" above, 10:146, footnote 4, and the references there.]

This is the saying of the Jacobites among the Christians, may the wrath of Allah be upon them.

Allah, may He be remembered, says: When I tested them and examined them with what I examined them with, they associated others with Me and said of a creature among My creation, a servant like them from among My servants, and a human of known lineage and origin, born of humankind, who calls them to My oneness, commands them to worship and obey Me, acknowledges to them that I am his Lord and their Lord, and forbids them from associating anything with Me: "He is their god," out of ignorance of Allah and disbelief in Him. It is not befitting for Allah to be a parent or to be begotten.

By His saying, "And the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord,'" He means: make worship and humble submission to the One before whom everything is humbled, and to whom every existing thing submits [See the explanation of "worship" above in the language indices (ʿ-b-d)]. "My Lord and your Lord" means: my Owner and your Owner, my Master and your Master, the One who created me and you [See the explanation of "Lord" above, 1:142, then the language indices above]. "Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise," meaning that He forbids him to dwell in it in the Hereafter. "And his refuge is the Fire," meaning: his return and his place, to which he will go and in which he will be in his return, the Fire of Hell, for whoever makes a partner with Allah in His worship. "And there are not for the wrongdoers," meaning: there is not for whoever does other than what Allah has permitted him, and worships other than the One to whom all creatures owe worship, "any helpers," who will help him on the Day of Resurrection against Allah, and rescue him from Him when He brings him to Hell. [See the explanation of "helpers" above, 9:339, footnote 3, and the references there.]

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, they have disbelieved who said, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three," and there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [5:73]

Abu Ja'far said: This is also a report from Allah, may He be remembered, concerning another group of the Children of Israel, whose characteristics He described in the verses before. When He tested them, after they had assumed they would not be tried or put to the test, they said, in disbelief in their Lord and in associating partners with Him: "Allah is the third of three."

* *

This was the saying held by the majority of the Christians before the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites), the Malkiyya (Melkites) and the Nestorians separated. [In the printed edition: "al-Malkaniyya," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.] They were said, as it has reached us, to say: "The eternal God is one substance comprising three hypostases (aqanim): a Father who is begetter and not begotten, a Son who is begotten and not a begetter, and a Spirit who proceeds from them both."

* *

Allah, may He be remembered, says, refuting them in what they said of this: "And there is no god except one God." That is, you have no object of worship, O people, except one object of worship, who is neither a begetter of anything nor begotten, but is rather the Creator of every begetter and every begotten. "And if they do not desist from what they are saying" — that is, if the speakers of this statement do not desist from their saying "Allah is the third of three" [see the explanation of "desist" above: 3:569/6:14]. "There will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment" — that is, there will surely afflict those who say this statement and those who say the other statement, "He is the Messiah, son of Mary," because both groups are disbelievers and associators. Therefore the threat of punishment returned to a general form, and He did not say "there will surely afflict them a painful punishment," because had it been said that way, the threat from Allah, may He be remembered, would have been specific to the speakers of the second statement, namely those who say "Allah is the third of three," and would not have included those who say "The Messiah is God." So He extended the threat, may He be remembered, to every disbeliever, so that those addressed by these verses would know that Allah's threat encompasses both groups of the Children of Israel and whoever among the disbelievers is in the likeness of what they are upon.

* *

If someone says: Even if the matter is as you have described, to whom do the "hā'" and "mīm" in His saying "minhum" refer?

It is said: to the Children of Israel.

* *

So the meaning of the statement, given that the matter is as we have described, is: And if these Israelites do not desist from what they say about Allah of grave speech, there will surely afflict those among them who say, "Indeed the Messiah is God," and those who say, "Indeed Allah is the third of three," and every disbeliever who follows their path, a painful punishment, because of their disbelief in Allah. [See the explanation of "painful punishment" in the preceding lexical indexes (alif-lam-mim).]

* *

A group of the people of interpretation have said, in agreement with what we have said, that these verses are meant to refer to the Christians.

Those who said so:

12294 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Indeed, they have disbelieved who said, 'Indeed, Allah is the third of three'": He said: The Christians said, "He, and the Messiah, and his mother." That is the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah"?﴾ [5:116].

12295 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "Indeed, they have disbelieved who said Indeed Allah is the third of three," similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 74:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ (74)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Will these two disbelieving groups not return [[See the explanation of "repentance" (tawbah) in the preceding linguistic indexes, under the root (t-w-b).]] — the one of them who said, "Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary," and the other who said, "Allah is the third of three" — from what they have said of that, and repent of what they uttered and spoke of their disbelief, [[In the printed edition: "wa-qata'a bihi min kufrihim" (and cut off by it from their disbelief); I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is the correct reading.]] and ask their Lord for forgiveness for what they said? ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward the sins of those among His creatures who repent, who turn back to His obedience after their disobedience, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them, in accepting their repentance and their return to what He loves rather than what He hates, thereby pardoning by it the criminal acts they committed before that. [[See the explanation of "istaghfara" (seek forgiveness) and "ghafur" (forgiving) in the preceding linguistic indexes, under the root (gh-f-r); and the explanation of "rahim" (merciful) under the root (r-h-m).]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 75:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers had passed away before him; and his mother was a truthful woman. They both used to eat food.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, [[The addition between the brackets is necessary for the sentence to be coherent.]] as an argument for His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ against the sects of the Christians in their statements about the Messiah.

He says, refuting the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites) in their saying "He is God," and the others in their saying "He is the son of God": The matter is not as these unbelievers say concerning the Messiah. Rather, he is the son of Mary, whom she bore in the manner that mothers bear their children, and that is a attribute of human beings, not of the Creator of human beings. He is only a messenger of God, like all the messengers before him who passed away and departed. God caused to happen through his hand whatever signs and lessons He willed, as proof of his truthfulness and that he is a messenger of God to those to whom He sent him among His creatures, just as He caused signs and lessons to happen through the hands of those messengers before him, as proof for them of the reality of their truthfulness in being messengers of God. [[See the explanation of "al-Masih" above, p. 480, footnote 1, and the references there.]] "And his mother was truthful": He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the mother of the Messiah was a truthful woman.

* *

"Siddiqa" is the form "fi'ila" from "sidq" (truthfulness), and likewise their saying "fulan siddiq" is "fi'il" from "sidq." From it is His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And the truthful ones and the martyrs﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 70]. [[See the explanation of "al-Siddiq" above, vol. 8, pp. 530–532.]]

It has been said that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was only called "al-Siddiq" for his truthfulness.

It has also been said that he was named "siddiq" for his affirming the Prophet ﷺ regarding his journey in a single night to Bayt al-Maqdis from Mecca and his return to it.

* *

His saying "They both used to eat food" is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about the Messiah and his mother: that they were both in need of what nourishes them and what their bodies depend upon of food and drink, like all other human beings from the children of Adam. Whoever is like this cannot be a god, because one who needs food has his subsistence dependent on another. His dependence on another and his need for what sustains him is clear evidence of his incapacity, and the incapable can only be one who is ruled over, not a lord.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are turned away.﴾ (75)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Look, O Muhammad, at how We make clear to these unbelievers among the Jews and Christians "the signs," which are the proofs, indications and arguments, regarding the falsehood of what they say about the prophets of God, their fabrication against God, their claim that He has a son, and their testimony that some of His creatures are their lord and god. Yet they do not refrain from their lies and false sayings, nor do they desist from their fabrication against their Lord and their great ignorance, even though conclusive proofs have reached them, removing any excuse. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Then look," O Muhammad, "how they are turned away": then look, despite Our making Our signs clear to them regarding the falsehood of their saying, in what direction they are turned away from Our clarification which We make clear to them? [[In the printed edition: "bayyanahu lahum" (we made it clear to them); the correct reading is from the manuscript, which is unpointed.]] And how are they led astray from the guidance toward truth to which We guide them?

* *

The Arabs say of everything turned away from something: "He is ma'fuk 'anhu" (turned away from it). It is said: "I have turned (afaktu) so-and-so away from such-and-such," meaning I diverted him from it; "so I afikuhu afkan, and he is ma'fuk." And "the land has been afikat" when rain has been diverted from it. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1: 174–175.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 76:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Say: Do you worship, besides Allah, that which possesses for you no harm and no benefit? And Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ (76)

Abu Ja'far said: This too is an argument from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, addressed to His Prophet ﷺ against the Christians who speak about the Messiah in the manner of their statements about him described earlier.

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to these disbelievers among the Christians, who claim that the Messiah is their lord and who say that Allah is the third of three: Do you worship, other than Allah, who holds power over your harm and your benefit, who created you and provided for you, who gives you life and causes you to die, something that possesses for you no harm and no benefit? He, may His remembrance be exalted, informs them that the Messiah, whom some of the Christians claim to be God and whom some of them claim to be the son of Allah, possesses no harm to repel from them should Allah inflict it upon them, nor any benefit to bring to them should Allah not decree it for them. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: How then can one be a lord and a god when he has such a description? Rather, the Lord who is worshipped is the one in whose hand is every thing and who is capable of every thing. So worship Him alone and devote worship to Him, apart from others, the powerless ones who neither benefit you nor harm you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by it: "And Allah is the Hearing" of their seeking forgiveness, were they to ask Him to forgive them for their statement about the Messiah that He reported they say, and for other than that of their speech and the speech of His creatures; "the Knowing" of their repentance, were they to repent from it, and of other than that of their affairs. [[See the explanation of "samee'" (Hearing) and "aleem" (Knowing) in the preceding lexical indices.]]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the limits in your religion, going beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray and strayed from the right way."﴾ (77)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is an address from God, may He be exalted and remembered, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). God, may He be exalted and remembered, says: "Say," O Muhammad, to these extremists among the Christians concerning the Messiah, "O People of the Scripture"—meaning by "the Scripture" the Gospel—"do not exceed the limits in your religion," that is, do not go to excess in what you say about the matter of the Messiah in the religion you profess, so that you transgress in it from the truth to falsehood [[See the explanation of "ghala" (exceeding the limits) above, 9: 415–417.]] and say about him, "He is God," or "He is the son of God." Rather, say, "He is the servant of God, His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him." "And do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray," that is: and do not also follow, concerning the Messiah, the desires of the Jews who had gone astray from the path of guidance before you in what they said about him, so that you say about him what they said: "He is of illegitimate birth," and slander his mother as they slandered her with the false accusation, though she is a truthful woman. "And led many astray"—God, may He be exalted and remembered, says: these Jews led many people astray, turning them away from the path of truth and compelling them to disbelieve in God and to deny the Messiah. "And strayed from the right way"—that is: these Jews strayed from the straight path and took a course other than the road of truth. [[See the explanation of "ḍalāl" (straying) above in the indices of language, and the explanation of "sawā' al-sabīl" (the right way) above, p. 443, note 2, and the references there.]]

What God, may He be exalted and remembered, means by this is their disbelief in God, their denial of His messengers, 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ), and their turning away from faith and their distance from it. That was the straying with which God described them.

* *

And those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

12296 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words "and strayed from the right way," he said: the Jews.

12297 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before and led many astray," they are those who went astray and led their followers astray; "and strayed from the right way," from the even path.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 78:

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾ (5:78)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to these Christians, whose description Allah has mentioned: Do not exaggerate and say about the Messiah other than the truth, and do not say about him what the Jews said, those whom Allah has cursed upon the tongue of His prophets and messengers, David and Jesus, son of Mary. [[See the explanation of "la'nah" (curse) above, p. 452, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "i'tida'" (transgression) above, p. 447, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The curse of Allah upon them was on their tongues, as in what has been reported:

12298 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary." He said: They were cursed by every tongue: they were cursed in the time of Moses in the Torah, they were cursed in the time of David in the Psalms (Zabur), they were cursed in the time of Jesus in the Gospel, and they were cursed in the time of Muhammad (ﷺ) in the Qur'an.

12299 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary," he says: They were cursed in the Gospel upon the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, and they were cursed in the Psalms upon the tongue of David.

12300 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from his father, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary." He said: They mixed with them after the prohibition in their trade, so Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and so they are cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary.

12301 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary." He said: They were cursed upon the tongue of David and so became apes, and they were cursed upon the tongue of Jesus and so became swine.

12302 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved": they were cursed by every tongue: in the time of Moses in the Torah, in the time of David in the Psalms, in the time of Jesus in the Gospel, and they were cursed upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ) in the Qur'an. Ibn Jurayj said: Others said: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David" means in his time, so they were cursed by his supplication. He said: David passed by a group of them while they were in a house, and he said: Who is in the house? They said: Swine. He said: "O Allah, make them swine!" And they became swine. He said: Then his curse afflicted them, and Jesus supplicated against them, saying: "O Allah, curse whoever has slandered me and my mother, and make them apes, disgraced!"

12303 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved" - the verse. Allah cursed them upon the tongue of David in his time, so He made them apes, disgraced; and in the Gospel upon the tongue of Jesus, so He made them swine.

12304 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' related to me, saying: Abu Mahsan Husayn ibn Numayr related to us, from Husayn - meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman - from Abu Malik, who said: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David": he said: They were transformed into apes upon the tongue of David, and into swine upon the tongue of Jesus. [[The report 12304: "Abu Mahsan al-Darir" is "Husayn ibn Numayr al-Wasiti," trustworthy, but he used to hold a grudge against 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), so al-Hakim said: "He is not strong among them." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

12305 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, the same.

12306 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: A man from the Children of Israel, when he saw his brother committing a sin, would forbid him from it, "ta'dhiran" [[In the printed edition: "ta'zIran," which is a pure error; its correct form is from the manuscript and Ibn Kathir's tafsir. "Ta'dhir" means doing something without going to the full extent in doing it. The "ta'dhir" of the Children of Israel: they did not go to the full extent in forbidding sins, and they flattered the sinners, and did not reject their sinful deeds with the full rejection, so they forbade them with a prohibition in which they fell short and did not go to the full extent.]] And when the next day came, what he had seen from him did not prevent him from being his table companion, his associate, and his drinking companion. [["Al-akil" is the one who accompanies you in eating; "al-sharib" is the one who accompanies you in drinking; "al-khalit" is the one who mixes with you. All of these are "fa'il" in the sense of "mufa'il."]] So when He saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them upon the tongue of their prophets David and Jesus, son of Mary: "That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress." He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right, you must forbid what is wrong, you must take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, and you must bend him toward the truth, bending him firmly; or Allah will surely strike the hearts of some of you against others, and He will surely curse you as He cursed them. [[The report 12306: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Muharibi" is trustworthy; he passed with numbers 221 and 875.

And "al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab ibn Rafi' al-Asadi" is trustworthy and reliable; he passed with number 3789.

And "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Muradi," who related from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Suqah, and 'Asim ibn Bahdalah.

And "Salim al-Aftas" is "Salim ibn 'Ajlan al-Jazari al-Harrani," who related from 'Amr ibn Murrah, and he was of his contemporaries. The hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned in al-Tahdhib: "It is said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah."

And this chain, from the narration of al-Muharibi, i.e., "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas," was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4:172), and by Ibn Abi Hatim in his tafsir, as transmitted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3:205), who commented on it saying: "It was also narrated by Khalid al-Tahhan - he is Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Wasiti - from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah," and he narrated it before that under number 4337, by way of Khalaf ibn Hisham, from Abu Shihab al-Hannat, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas. So what is here is the narration of al-Muharibi, and there is no doubt that it is "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Murrah," and it seems to be an error by al-Muharibi, since all the other narrators have it as "from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim al-Aftas."

And "'Amr ibn Murrah al-Muradi al-Jamali," "Abu 'Abd Allah al-A'ma," is trustworthy and truthful. He narrates from Abu 'Ubaydah directly, so here he narrated from one of his contemporaries, "Salim al-Aftas," from Abu 'Ubaydah; and Khalid al-Tahhan narrated from al-'Ala', from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah directly, without the intermediary "Salim al-Aftas."

And this chain is weak in any case, due to its discontinuity.]]

12307 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Salman related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When wrongdoing spread among the Children of Israel, a man would meet a man and say: O so-and-so, fear Allah! Then that would not prevent him from eating and drinking with him. So when Allah saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, then He sent down a Book concerning them: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress. They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing they committed; how wretched was what they used to do." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, so he sat up and said: No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until you bend the wrongdoer toward the truth, bending him firmly. [[The report 12307: the report of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, was narrated by Abu Ja'far through five chains. Its detailed takhrij will come later; then see its last one, number 12311.

"Al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Salman al-Nahdi," trustworthy, passed with numbers 1497, 2872, 3014, 6171, 9646. In the printed edition here it was "Ibn Sulayman," which is an error of a kind that has passed before.

And "'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i," passed with numbers 886, 1497, 3956, 6171, 9646. And "'Ali ibn Badhimah al-Jazari," trustworthy, passed with number 629.

And I have not found this report with this chain to 'Ali ibn Badhimah.]]

12308 - 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us, saying: al-Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Badhimah related to us, from Abu 'Ubaydah - I think from Masruq - from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When wrongdoing appeared among the Children of Israel, a man would see his brother, his neighbor, and his companion committing wrongdoing, and would forbid him, but that would not prevent him from being his table companion, his drinking companion, and his boon companion. So Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and they were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary: "That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress," up to "defiantly disobedient." 'Abd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then he sat up straight, became angry, and said: No, by Allah, until you take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and bend him toward the truth, bending him firmly. [[The report 12308: "Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il al-'Adawi" is trustworthy; he passed with numbers 2057, 3337, 5728, 8356, 8367.

And "Sufyan" is al-Thawri.

The route of Sufyan from 'Ali ibn Badhimah also comes with numbers 12309 and 12311, as a mursal narration: "from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said," without mention of "'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud." This is the known narration of Sufyan. al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (in the Book of Tafsir) said: "'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman said: Yazid ibn Harun said: Sufyan al-Thawri would not say in it, 'Abd Allah,' meaning that it is mursal from the report of Abu 'Ubaydah." So al-Tabari informs us here that Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it another time, "from Abu 'Ubaydah, I think from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah," and he did not mention only "'Abd Allah," but was doubtful whether Abu 'Ubaydah narrated it from Masruq from 'Abd Allah. If Sufyan's supposition is correct, then this is a hadith with a sound chain, not discontinuous or mursal.

And I have not found this narration with this chain anywhere else.]]

12309 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: When deficiency ("naqs") befell the Children of Israel, a man would see his brother upon doubtful conduct ("al-raybi") and forbid him from it. Then when the next day came, what he had seen from him did not prevent him from being his table companion, his drinking companion, and his associate. So Allah struck the hearts of some of them against others, and the Qur'an was sent down concerning them, saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary," until: "But many of them are defiantly disobedient." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then sat up and said: No, until you take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and bend him toward the truth, bending him firmly. [[The report 12309: this is the third chain of the report of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, and the second of the report of Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan (Book of Tafsir) through Muhammad ibn Bashshar, in the same form. Ibn Majah also narrated it, number 4006, in the same form.]]

12310 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Dawud - he said: he dictated it to me - said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Wadah related to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same. [[The report 12310: "Muhammad ibn Abi al-Wadah" is attributed to his grandfather, and he is "Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadah al-Qada'i." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated from him. Trustworthy, of sound narration. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.

And this report with this chain was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan in the (Book of Tafsir), and by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, following number 4006, in the same form.]]

12311 - Hannad ibn al-Sarri related to us, saying: Waki' related to us - and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us - from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, who said: I heard Abu 'Ubaydah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar; except that they both said in their narration: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reclining, then sat up straight, and then said: No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until you take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer and bend him toward the truth, bending him firmly. [[The report 12311: this is the third chain of "Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah." It is a mursal report.

The report of 'Ali ibn Badhimah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, was narrated through other routes.

Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, number 3713, through Yazid ibn Harun, from Sharik ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, with a different wording similar to it. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in (Book of Tafsir) through 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Yazid ibn Harun, with a form like Ahmad's narration.

Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (4:172), number 4336, through 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Nufayli, from Yunus ibn Rashid, from 'Ali ibn Badhimah, similar, with a different wording.

All these reports are either discontinuous or mursal, and the report was not connected except in chain number 12308. al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."

See the tafsir of Ibn Kathir (3:205, 206) and al-Durr al-Manthur (2:300).]]

12312 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary," he said: They were cursed in the Gospel and in the Psalms. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed the millstone of faith has turned, so turn with the Qur'an wherever it turns [*for indeed ... Allah has finished with what He made obligatory in it]. [[In the printed edition it was: "...wherever it turns, for indeed Allah has finished with what He made obligatory in it," which arranged the speech in a single sequence after altering it; the wording in the manuscript is what I have recorded, and between the two statements there is a blank space of about a word or two, in whose place I put dots, and I left it so that the report may be found and its completion obtained.]] [And indeed Ibn Marih] was a community from the Children of Israel. [[What is between the brackets is what is confirmed in the manuscript, and I do not know what it is; but the editor of the first printed edition made the statement as: "And indeed it was a community from the Children of Israel," so I saw fit to keep what is in the manuscript as it is, until the report is found in another place and corrected. This and the preceding were in one line in the manuscript, and in front of the line there was the letter (ṭ) in red, indicating an error.]] They were people of justice, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. So their people seized them, sawed them with saws, and crucified them on wood. A remnant of them remained, but they were not content until they mixed with the kings and sat with them, then they were not content until they ate with them. [[Thus in the printed edition and the manuscript, "fa-lam yardawa" and "thumma lam yardawa" in both places; and I am in doubt about them, and I think they are: "fa-lam yarimu" and "thumma lam yarimu," meaning: they did not remain.]] So Allah struck those hearts against one another and made them one. That is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed upon the tongue of David," up to "That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress." What was their disobedience? He said: "They did not forbid one another from wrongdoing they committed; how wretched was what they used to do."

* *

So the interpretation of the speech, then, is: Allah cursed those who disbelieved - from the Jews - in Allah, upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary; and their fathers were cursed by Allah, by Allah, upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary, because they disobeyed Allah and opposed His command, "and they used to transgress," meaning: they used to exceed His limits. [[See the explanation of "i'tida'" (transgression) above, shortly, p. 489, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 79–80:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed; evil indeed was what they used to do﴾ (79).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted, may His remembrance be great, says: These Jews, whom Allah has cursed, "did not forbid one another" — meaning they did not refrain from a wrong they committed, and did not forbid one another from it. [See the explanation of "intaha" (to refrain) earlier in this surah, p. 482, footnote 2, and the references there.] By "munkar" (wrong) is meant the sins by which they disobeyed Allah. [See the explanation of "munkar" earlier in volumes 7: 91, 105, 130.]

* *

So the meaning of the statement is: They did not refrain from a wrong they committed, "evil indeed was what they used to do." This is an oath from Allah, may His remembrance be great, saying, as it were: I swear that evil was the deed they used to do, in their failure to refrain from the disobedience of Allah, the Exalted, their violation of His sacred prohibitions, and their killing of the prophets and messengers of Allah. [See the explanation of "bi'sa" (evil) earlier in volumes 2: 338, 393; 3: 56; 7: 459.] As related:

12313 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj: "They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed": their own souls did not restrain them after they had fallen into disbelief.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿You see many of them making allies of those who disbelieve. Evil indeed is what their souls have put forward for them, that Allah became wrathful toward them, and in the punishment they will abide forever﴾ (80).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted, may His remembrance be great, says: "You see" — O Muhammad — many of the Children of Israel "making allies of those who disbelieve," meaning they take as allies the polytheists, the worshippers of idols, and they show enmity toward the friends of Allah and His messengers. [See the explanation of "tawalli" (taking as allies) in the lexical indices earlier under (w-l-y).] "Evil indeed is what their souls have put forward for them": the Exalted, may His remembrance be great, says, as an oath: Evil indeed is the thing that their souls have sent ahead for them to their return in the Hereafter. [See the explanation of "qaddama" (to send ahead) earlier in volumes 2: 368; 7: 447; 8: 514.] "That Allah became wrathful toward them": meaning their souls have put forward for them the wrath of Allah upon them because of what they did.

* *

The "an" in His saying "that Allah became wrathful toward them" is in the nominative position, as an apposition (badal) to "ma" in His saying "evil indeed is what." [On "al-tarjama" (apposition), see the terminology indices earlier.]

* *

"And in the punishment they will abide forever": meaning, in the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection they will abide forever, lasting in their residence and stay therein. [See the explanation of "khulud" (abiding forever) in the lexical indices earlier under (kh-l-d).]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if they had believed in Allah, and in the Prophet, and in what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: And if these people who take as allies those who disbelieve, from the Children of Israel, "believed in Allah and the Prophet," meaning: affirmed Allah, acknowledged Him and made Him one, and affirmed that His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a prophet sent by Allah and a messenger dispatched, "and what was revealed to him," meaning: and acknowledged what was revealed to Muhammad ﷺ from Allah of the verses of the Criterion (al-Furqan)—

"they would not have taken them as allies," meaning: they would not have taken them as companions and helpers in place of the believers [[See the explanation of "al-awliya'" (allies) in the earlier indices of vocabulary, under (w-l-y).]] — "but many of them are defiantly disobedient," meaning: but many of them are people who depart from the obedience of Allah into His disobedience, and people who consider lawful what Allah has forbidden them in speech and deed. [[See the explanation of "al-fisq" (defiant disobedience) in the earlier indices of vocabulary, under (f-s-q).]]

* *

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

12314 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying: "And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies," that he said: "The hypocrites."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God; and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.﴾ [5:82]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "You will surely find, O Muhammad, the most intense of people in enmity toward those who confirmed you, followed you, and believed in what you brought them, from among the people of Islam, to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God." By "those who associate partners," He means the worshippers of idols, who took idols as gods to worship besides God. "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers": he says, "you will surely find the nearest of people in affection and love."

* *

"Al-mawaddah" (affection) is on the pattern of "al-maf'alah," from a man's saying: "I loved such-and-such, I love it, love (wuddan), love (widdan), love (wadda), and affection (mawaddah)," when you love it. [See the explanation of "wadda" in what preceded: 2:470; 5:542; 6:500; 8:371; 9:17.]

* *

"To those who believe": he says, to those who confirmed God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). "Those who say, 'We are Christians'": "That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant," meaning, they are not arrogant toward accepting the truth, following it, and submitting to it.

* *

It has been said: this verse and the one after it were revealed concerning a group of Christians of Abyssinia (al-Habashah) who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When they heard the Qur'an, they embraced Islam and followed the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

* *

It has also been said: it was revealed concerning the Negus (al-Najashi), the king of Abyssinia, and companions of his who embraced Islam with him.

Those who said this:

12315 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Negus sent a delegation to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) recited to them, and they embraced Islam. He said: God, may He be exalted, revealed concerning them: "You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate partners," to the end of the verse. He said: They returned to the Negus and informed him, and the Negus embraced Islam, and he remained a Muslim until he died. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Your brother the Negus has died, so pray over him!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed over him in Medina, and the Negus was (in fact) there.

12316 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers, those who say, 'We are Christians'," he said: They are the delegation who came with Ja'far and his companions from the land of Abyssinia.

12317 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers, those who say, 'We are Christians'." He said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was in Mecca, he feared for his companions from the polytheists, so he sent Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn Mas'ud, and 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, with a group of his companions, to the Negus, king of Abyssinia. When this reached the polytheists, they sent 'Amr ibn al-'As with a group of them. It is mentioned that they got ahead of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the Negus, and they said: "A man has emerged among us who has made foolish the minds and wisdom of Quraysh. He claims that he is a prophet! He has sent to you a group to corrupt your people against you, so we wished to come to you and inform you of their affairs." He said: "If they come to me, I will consider what they say!" Then the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived and stood at the door of the Negus. They said: "Ask permission for the friends of God!" (The doorkeeper said to the king, "Permit them.") He said: "Admit them; welcome to the friends of God!" When they entered upon him, they greeted him. The group of polytheists said to him: "Do you not see, O King, that we have told you the truth? They did not greet you with your greeting by which you are greeted!" He said to them: "What prevented you from greeting me with my greeting?" They said: "We greeted you with the greeting of the people of Paradise and the greeting of the angels!" He said to them: "What does your companion say about Jesus and his mother?" They said: "He says, 'He is the servant of God, and a word from God which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him,' and he says of Mary, 'She is the virgin, the chaste.'" He said: He took a stick from the ground and said: "Jesus and his mother exceed what your companion says by no more than the size of this stick!" The polytheists disliked his statement, and their faces changed. He said to them: "Do you know anything of what was revealed to you?" They said: "Yes!" He said: "Recite!" They recited, and among them were priests, monks, and all the Christians; he recognized everything they recited, and their tears flowed from what they recognized of the truth. God, may He be remembered, said: "That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger..." to the end of the verse.

12318 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers, those who say, 'We are Christians'," to the end of the verse. He said: The Negus sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) twelve men from Abyssinia, seven priests and five monks, who looked at him and asked him questions. When they met him and he recited to them what God had revealed, they wept and believed. God revealed concerning them: "And they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears from what they recognize of the truth. They say, 'Our Lord, we believe, so record us among the witnesses'." They believed, then returned to the Negus, and the Negus emigrated with them, but he died on the way. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims prayed over him and asked forgiveness for him.

12319 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said concerning God's saying: "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers, those who say, 'We are Christians'," to the end of the verse: they are people from Abyssinia who believed when the emigrants of the believers came to them.

* *

Others said: rather, this is the description of a people who were on the law (shari'ah) of Jesus, from among the people of faith; when God, may He be remembered, sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), they believed in him.

Those who said this:

12320 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers," and he recited until "so record us among the witnesses." (He said:) People of the Scripture who were on a law of truth brought by Jesus, believing in him and adhering to him. When God sent His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), they confirmed him and believed in him, and they recognized that what he brought was the truth, so He praised them for what you hear.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that God, may He be exalted, described a people who said, "We are Christians," that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) would find them the nearest of people in friendly affection toward the people of faith in God and His Messenger, and He did not name them for us. It is possible that what is meant is the companions of the Negus, and it is possible that what is meant is a people who were on the law of Jesus, whom Islam reached, so they embraced Islam when they heard the Qur'an, recognized that it was the truth, and were not arrogant toward it.

* *

As for His saying, "That is because among them are priests and monks": He says that the affection of these people whom God described toward the believers has come near because among them are priests and monks.

* *

"Al-qissisun" (the priests) is the plural of "qissis." The plural of "al-qissis" may also be "qusus" (qusus), because "al-qass" and "al-qissis" have one meaning.

Ibn Zayd used to say about "al-qissis":

12321 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Al-qissis" means their worshippers.

* *

As for "al-ruhban" (monks), it can be singular and plural. When it is plural, its singular is "rahib" (monk), and "al-rahib" then is on the pattern "fa'il" from the speaker's saying: "Such-and-such feared God" (rahiba), meaning he feared Him, "yarhabuhu, rahaban and rahbaan." Then "rahib" is pluralized as "ruhban," like "rakib" and "rukban," and "faris" and "fursan." Among the evidence that it may be a plural among the Arabs is the poet's saying: [The poem is by Jarir; Yaqut in Mu'jam al-Buldan attributed it to Kuthayyir 'Azzah, and it was included in the Kuthayyir collection, p. 240; the correct attribution is to Jarir.]

"The monks of Madyan, had they seen you, would have come down, and the wild goats from the cliffs of the ravine" (The verse "al-'usum" (the wild goats) is the plural of "a'sam." The line is from Jarir's Diwan, p. 305, and will come in the tafsir 20:34 (Bulaq), and in Kuthayyir's Diwan 1:240, and in Lisan al-Arab (rahb), and Mu'jam al-Buldan (Madyan), from a poem in which he satirized al-Akhtal and al-Farazdaq. Before it he says: "O mother of Talhah, we have not met anyone like you among those who go up to the highlands nor in the depths of the valley.")

"Madyan" is the city of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, on the Sea of Qulzum (Red Sea), opposite Tabuk, between Medina and Syria. Kuthayyir also mentioned it in his poetry, saying: "God knows, had I wished to add to my love for 'Azzah, I would not have found an increase."

"The monks of Madyan and those whom I knew, weeping from fear of punishment, sitting."

"Had they heard as I heard her speech, they would have fallen down for 'Azzah, bowing and prostrating."

In my view "al-'uqul" (the cliffs/strongholds) is with an 'ayn vowelled with fatha, from their saying "'aqala al-wa'l ya'qilu 'uqulan" (the mountain goat took refuge at the top of the mountain), so it is "'aqil" (one who takes refuge), and by that it was named; analogy also allows "fahuwa 'aqul" (with fatha on the 'ayn). In the Diwan, it was vowelled with the pen as "al-'uqul" (with damma on the 'ayn), plural of "'aql" (with fatha then sukun), which is the refuge and fortress. I do not accept that here. The author of the Mu'jam narrated "wal-'usum fi sha'af al-jibal" (and the wild goats on the mountain peaks), which agrees in meaning with whoever vowelled "al-'uqul" with damma on the 'ayn, and I think the correct recitation in the Mu'jam is "min sha'af al-jibal." "Al-sha'af" is the plural of "sha'fah" (with two fathas), meaning the top of the mountain. "Al-fadir" is the wild goat that takes refuge and is inaccessible at the top of the mountain, and then it is an old goat restrained at the top of its mountain. "Al-'usum" is the plural of "a'sam," which is the wild goat, named by its dominant attribute, because in one of its forelegs there is whiteness; "al-'usm" and "al-'usmah" mean whiteness in the two forearms or one of them.

Since "al-'usum" is plural, I refused to make "al-fadir" a description of it, even if "al-'uqul" were recited with damma on the 'ayn meaning fortresses and refuges. Rather, I made it with fatha on the 'ayn, meaning that the young wild goats also descended from the refuge to which the old wild goats retreat in avoidance of hunting, because of their lack of concern for leaving their refuge, like the concern of the young wild goats.

* *

Among the interpreters there was disagreement about who is meant by His saying: "That is because among them are priests and monks."

Some of them said: It refers to a people who responded to Jesus son of Mary when he called them and followed him in his law.

Those who said this:

12321 (repeated number, bis) - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "That is because among them are priests and monks," he said: They were sailors (nawatiyy) on the sea, meaning: boatmen (mallahin). [In Ibn al-Athir, then in Lisan al-Arab: "kanu nawwatin, i.e., mallahin", its explanation in the hadith; and Taj al-'Arus similarly transmitted it from them. I fear it may be a copyist's error, and that the correct reading is "kanu nawati, i.e., mallahin," as it comes here and in the manuscript too. I did not find anyone mentioning it as "nawata" (with fatha on the nun and shaddah on the waw); had it been so, the lexicographers would have addressed it, but they did not mention it except what they transmitted from Ibn al-Athir. The singular of "al-nawati" (with fatha on the nun and fatha on the waw not doubled) is "nawti" (with damma on the nun, and a doubled ya' at the end). What is in the manuscript of al-Tabari indicates that what Ibn al-Athir wrote is an error or a misreading of the letter. Ibn al-Athir alone is not relied upon for the transmission of his book unless it is vocalized and attested with its chain and source. Then, after I wrote this, I found it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:17, as it comes in Ibn al-Athir and Lisan: "nawatin, meaning mallahin." It mentions the report there at length and says: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat and al-Kabir, and in it is al-'Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari, who is weak." It is undoubtedly a chain other than Abu Ja'far's chain; see Ibn Kathir 3:212, 213.] He said: Then 'Isa ibn Maryam passed by them, and called them to Islam, and they answered him. He said: That is His saying: "Qissisin and ruhban."

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the people whom the Negus had sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

12322 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, saying: 'Anbasah narrated to us, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Salih concerning His saying: "That is because among them are priests and monks," he said: Sixty-six, or sixty-seven, or sixty-eight [the printed edition has "or two and sixty"; in the manuscript it is "two and sixty" without "or", undotted; I think the correct reading is "or eight and sixty"... which the context indicates, and so I record it as such], from Abyssinia, all of them owners of hermitages, wearing woolen garments.

12323 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "That is because among them are priests and monks," he said: The Negus sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) fifty or seventy of their best, and they began to weep, and he said: "These are they!"

12324 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "That is because among them are priests and monks," he said: They were the messengers of the Negus whom he sent with his and his people's submission to Islam. They were seventy men whom he chose, the best of the best, and they came in to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he recited to them: "Ya Sin. By the wise Qur'an" [Surah Ya Sin 36:1, 2]; they wept and recognized the truth, and God revealed concerning them: "That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant," and He revealed concerning them: "Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it, they believe in it..." to His saying: "They will be given their reward twice, because they were patient" [Surah al-Qasas 28:53, 54].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, according to us, is that it should be said: God, may He be remembered, reported about the group among the Christians whom He praised, that the nearness of their affection toward the people of faith in God and His Messenger was only from them because among them are people of diligence in worship and asceticism in the monasteries and hermitages [the printed edition has "wa-tarhib" (intimidation); in the manuscript "wa-tarahhub", undotted, and the correct reading is what I recorded, for one does not say "rahiba tarhiban"; rather one says "tarahhaba tarahhuban" when one becomes a monk who fears God and worships in his hermitage], and that among them are scholars of their books and people who recite them. They are not distant from the believers because of their humility toward the truth when they recognize it, and they are not arrogant to accept it when they discern it, because they are people of religion and diligence in it, and sincere advisers to themselves for the sake of God. They are not like the Jews, who have become accustomed to killing the prophets and messengers, opposing God in His command and prohibition, and distorting His revelation which He sent down in His Books. [Al-Jassas said in Ahkam al-Qur'an 2:451: "Some of the ignorant think that in this verse there is praise of the Christians, and a report that they are better than the Jews. That is not so, for what is in the verse about that is only the description of a people who believed in God and the Messenger. What indicates this is what is mentioned in the sequence of recitation, of their reporting about themselves their belief in God and the Messenger. It is known to everyone of sound understanding who considers carefully the two statements of these two groups that the statement of the Christians is uglier and more absurd, and more manifestly corrupt, than the statement of the Jews. For the Jews acknowledge tawhid in general, though among them are anthropomorphists who undo what they hold in general of tawhid by likening God to creation."]

and this was quoted by Abu Hayyan in his tafsir (4:4, 5), after which he said: "The apparent meaning is what the exegetes and others have said, that the Christians, in general, are in a better state than the Jews. The exegetes have already mentioned, in what preceded, the nobility of character with which the Christians were distinguished over the Jews, and their quick entry into Islam. The speech was not revealed on account of creedal beliefs; it was revealed on account of the emotional response of the Muslims. As for his statement, 'because what is in the verse of that is only the description of a people who have believed in God and the Messenger,' it is not as he mentioned. Rather, the beginning of the verse requires generality, for He said: 'And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believed are those who say, "We are Christians"'; then He informed that among this group are scholars and ascetics who are humble, quick to respond to Islam, and frequent in weeping upon hearing the Qur'an. The Jews are otherwise. And experience confirms the nearness of the Christians to the Muslims and the distance of the Jews."

This is a statement that calls for lengthy scrutiny, which is not the place for its detailed treatment; I have quoted it to you so that you may reflect on it and ponder it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 83:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ (5:83)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: And when these people who said, "We are Christians" (the ones I have described to you, O Muhammad, as those whom you will find closest in affection to the believers) hear [[The context of the speech: "When these hear ... what has been revealed to you of the Book being recited," and between the verb and its object there is a long separation.]] what has been revealed to you of the Book being recited, "you see their eyes overflowing with tears."

* *

The "overflowing of the eye with tears" means its being filled with them and then their flowing out of it, like the overflowing of a river with water, or of a vessel, and that is its flowing out due to the intensity of its filling. Among its examples is the verse of al-A'sha:

Then my tears overflowed, and the veins [al-shu'un] remained: either a trickle or a flowing down [[His Diwan: 35. From his qasida on Qays ibn Ma'di Karib al-Kindi. Before the verse, which is its beginning: "Have you resolved, from the family of Layla, to depart abruptly, and has the visit become distant for one who is in love..." ... "And the strange distances of separation parted from her, and I was given longing and remembrance in place of her..." "Then my tears overflowed..." "As a string releases its pearls from its thread, small pearls falling down..." In the manuscript and the printed edition the verse reads: "fa-fada'at dumu'i fa-tall al-shu'un dama hidaran", which is a pure error. "Al-shu'un" is the plural of "sha'n", the channel of tears to the eye, and they are its veins. The reading in the Diwan is "kafayd al-ghurub", and "al-ghurub" is the plural of "gharb" (with a fatha and then sukun), which is the large bucket with which water is drawn from the waterwheel.
