His saying "fa-tall" is with the dotted letter ẓ, not the ṭ. Whoever made it with the undotted ṭ has erred and corrupted it, and explained it accordingly, and that is extremely weak. "Al-wakif" is that the tears flow little by little, dripping drop by drop; one says "wakafa al-dam'u yakifu wakfan wa wakifan". As for "inhidar al-dam'," it is its flowing in succession, as water pours down from a slope.]]

And His saying, "because of the truth they have recognized", means: the overflowing of their tears is due to their knowledge that what is recited to them from the Book of God, which He has sent down to the Messenger of God, is true, as:

12325 - Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi, who said: The Negus sent twelve men to the Prophet ﷺ to ask him and bring back news of him. The Messenger of God ﷺ recited the Qur'an to them, and they wept. Among them were seven monks and five priests [[In the printed edition: "wa-khamsatu qissisun", and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is pure correctness.]] — or: five monks and seven priests [[In the manuscript: "aw sab'atun" without mention of "qissisin", but this is an addition that cannot be done without. Its correct form is also "wa-sab'atun" with the waw.]] — so God revealed concerning them: "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears," to the end of the verse.

12326 - Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Ali ibn Muqaddam narrated to us, saying: I heard Hisham ibn Urwa narrating from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: It was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions: "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears." [[Narration 12326: "Umar ibn Ali ibn Muqaddam" is "Umar ibn Ali ibn Ata ibn Muqaddam al-Muqaddami". Trustworthy, but he used to commit tadlis (concealment). Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, but he practised severe tadlis, saying: I heard, and narrated to us, then he would fall silent and say: Hisham ibn Urwa, or al-A'mash. He was a righteous man, and they did not object to him except for tadlis; otherwise nothing else, and I would not accept from him until he said 'narrated to us'." Biography in al-Tahdhib.]]

12327 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, concerning His saying: "you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized," who said: That was concerning the Negus.

12328 - Hannad and Ibn Wakif narrated to us, both saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, who said: They used to hold that this verse was revealed concerning the Negus: "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears."

12329 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: I asked al-Zuhri about the verses: "That is because among them are priests and monks, and that they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears," to the end of the verse, and His saying: "And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace'" [Al-Furqan 25:63]. He said: I have always heard our scholars say: It was revealed concerning the Negus and his companions. [[Narration 12329: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:33, but it does not contain mention of the verse of Surat al-Furqan which Abu Ja'far cited in this report from Ibn Ishaq. Moreover, Abu Ja'far did not mention this report in his explanation of the verse in Surat al-Furqan (19:21, 22, Bulaq), nor did he indicate that it was revealed concerning anyone other than the Negus and his companions.]]

* *

As for His saying, "they say", if it were in the form of a noun, it would be in the accusative as a circumstantial state, because the meaning of the speech is: "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized, saying, 'Our Lord, we have believed'."

* *

By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "they say, 'Our Lord, we have believed'", He means that they say: O our Lord, we have affirmed what we heard of what You sent down to Your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Your Book, and we acknowledge that it is from You, and that it is the truth without doubt.

* *

As for His saying, "so register us among the witnesses", it has been related from Ibn Abbas and others as its interpretation that:

12330 - Hannad narrated to us with it, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Wakif narrated to us, saying: My father and Ibn Numayr narrated to us = all from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, "register us with the witnesses," who said: The community of Muhammad ﷺ.

12331 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "so register us with the witnesses," with the community of Muhammad ﷺ.

12332 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "so register us with the witnesses," meaning by "the witnesses," Muhammad ﷺ and his community.

12333 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, "so register us with the witnesses," who said: Muhammad ﷺ and his community, for they bear witness that he has conveyed, and they bear witness that the messengers have conveyed.

12334 - Al-Rabi' narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to me, from Simak, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, like the report of al-Harith ibn Abd al-Aziz, except that he said: and they bear witness for the messengers that they have conveyed. [[Narrations 12330–12334: al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak 2:313, through Yahya ibn Adam from Isra'il, in the same wording, then said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:18 and said: "al-Tabarani related it from his shaykh Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam, who is weak." But these are sound chains, related by al-Tabari and others.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that the one who gives this interpretation intended by his interpretation the meaning of God's saying: "And thus We have made you a middle community that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you" [Al-Baqarah 2:143]. So Ibn Abbas went to the view that "the witnesses" are "the witnesses" in His saying, "that you may be witnesses over the people," and they are the community of Muhammad ﷺ. [[See what has preceded of the explanation of the verse of Surat al-Baqarah 3:141–155.]]

* *

If the interpretation is that, then the meaning of the speech is: "They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us with the witnesses'," who bear witness for Your prophets on the Day of Resurrection, that they have conveyed Your messages to their communities.

* *

If someone said: the meaning of that is: "so register us with the witnesses" who testify that what You have sent down to Your Messenger of the Books is true, it would be correct, because that is the conclusion of His saying: "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized, saying, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so register us with the witnesses'." That is a description by God, may His remembrance be exalted, of their faith when they heard the Book of God, so their request is also that God make them among those whose testimony to that is accepted by Him, and join them in reward and recompense to their stations.

And the meaning of "al-Kitab" in this place is: the placing (al-ja'l). [[See the explanation of "al-Kitab" in what has preceded in the indexes of language, (k-t-b).]]

* *

That is: "So make us with the witnesses, and set us down with them in their number."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 84:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth, and hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about those people whose description He has given in these verses: that when they hear what has been sent down to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) of His Book, they believe in it and confirm the Book of God, and say: ﴿why should we not believe in God﴾, meaning: we do not acknowledge the oneness of God; ﴿and in what has come to us of the truth﴾, meaning: and in what has come to us from God of His Book and the signs of His revelation. And we hope, by our belief in that, that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people.

* *

By "the righteous people" is meant the believers in God, who obey Him, and who have deserved Paradise from God through their obedience to Him. [[See the explanation of "al-salih" (the righteous) above, 8:532, note 2, and the references there.]]

What is meant by this is: "and we hope that our Lord will admit us into the place of those who obey Him in His Garden on the Day of Resurrection, join our dwellings with their dwellings, and our ranks with their ranks in His gardens."

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

12335 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth, and hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people?﴾ : "The righteous people" are the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 85:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance, means: Allah rewarded them for their saying: "Our Lord, we believe, so register us among the witnesses. And why should we not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, and aspire that our Lord would admit us [to paradise] with the righteous people?"

﴿Gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: orchards beneath whose trees rivers flow. ﴿Abiding therein eternally﴾, meaning: they will remain therein forever; they will not leave it nor be moved from it.

﴿And that is the reward of the doers of good﴾, meaning: this which I have rewarded these speakers, for what I have described of their saying, with the gardens in which they abide eternally, is the reward of every doer of good in his speech and his action.

* *

The "good-doing" of the good-doer in this matter is that he affirms the oneness of Allah with pure and sincere monotheism, without any association with Him, acknowledges the prophets of Allah and what they brought from Allah of the scriptures, performs His obligations, and avoids His prohibitions. (See the explanation of "ihsan" above, vol. 8, p. 334, note 2, and the references there.) That is the perfection of the good-doing of the doers of good about whom Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally﴾. (I fear that the correct wording may be: "those whom Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said that He rewarded for what they said with gardens ..."; but I have left what is in the manuscript and the printed edition as it is.)

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 5, verses 86–87 (part 1 of 2)**

**On His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Hellfire (al-Jahim).﴾ (5:86)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted remembrance says: As for those who denied the Oneness of God, rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and denied the signs of His Book, then ﴿those are the companions of the Hellfire (al-Jahim)﴾. He means: they are its inhabitants and those who remain in it. [[See the explanation of "companions of the Fire" in what has preceded, p. 217, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And "al-Jahim" is the fire whose heat is intense. It is also called "al-jaahim" and "al-jahim." [[See the explanation of "al-Jahim" in what has preceded, vol. 2, p. 562.]]

**On His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors.﴾ (5:87)**

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what their Prophet (ﷺ) brought, that it is the truth from God, ﴿do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you﴾. By "the good things" (al-tayyibat) He means the delicious things that souls desire and hearts incline toward, [[See the explanation of "al-tayyibat" in what has preceded, p. 84, footnote 1, and the references there.]] so that you deprive yourselves of them, like what the priests (qissisun) and monks (ruhban) did, who forbade themselves women, good foods and pleasant drinks, and some of whom confined themselves in monasteries (sawami'), while others wandered across the earth. His exalted remembrance says: So do not do, O believers, as those did. ﴿And do not transgress﴾ the limit God has set for you concerning what He has made lawful for you and what He has forbidden to you, so that you exceed His limit that He set, thereby disobeying Him. Indeed, God does not love the one who transgresses the limit He has set for His creatures concerning what He has made lawful and unlawful for them.

* *

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

12336 – Abu Husayn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: ʿAbthar Abu Zubayd narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik regarding this verse: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse. He said: ʿUthman ibn Maz'un and some Muslims forbade themselves women and abstained from good food, and some of them wanted to cut off their male organs, so this verse was revealed. [[The report 12336: "Abu Husayn," ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yunus al-Yarbuʿi, the teacher of al-Tabari. He narrated from his father, and he and his father narrated from ʿAbthar ibn al-Qasim. Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Hatim and others narrated from him. Trustworthy and truthful. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "ʿAbthar ibn al-Qasim al-Zubaydi," "Abu Zubayd": trustworthy and truthful. Ibn Mu'in said: "Trustworthy, Sunni." Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/94, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/43. In the manuscript alone it read "ʿAbthar ibn Zubayda," which is a pure error.
And "Husayn" is Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who passed as numbers 579 and 2986.]]

12337 – Hamid ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to me, from ʿIkrima, who said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) resolved to castrate themselves and to abandon meat and women, so this verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors."

12338 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrima: that men wanted such-and-such and wanted such-and-such, and wanted to castrate themselves, so this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," up to His saying: "in whom you are believers."

12339 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: They had forbidden good things and meat, so God the Exalted revealed this concerning them.

12340 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrima: that some people said: "We will not marry, we will not eat, and we will not do such-and-such!" So God the Exalted revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors."

12341 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to renounce the world, abandon women, and adopt monasticism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up and spoke harshly to them, then said: "Those before you were destroyed only through excessive strictness. They were strict upon themselves, so God was strict upon them. So those are their remnants in the dwellings (diyar) and the monasteries (sawami')!" [[The word "diyar" is the plural of "dayr," and what the lexicographers mentioned is that its plural is "adyar," and they limited themselves to this plural. Yaqut, in Mu'jam al-Buldan (dayr), mentioned many plurals, of which this is not one, but he reported that al-Jawhari said: "Dayr al-nasara originally was dar." If that is so, then its plural as "diyar" is undoubtedly correct and analogical. See also "al-dur" in report no. 12344, p. 516, footnote 2.]] Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, perform the pilgrimage (hajj) and the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumra), and be upright, and He will make you upright. He said: And this verse was revealed concerning them: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse.

12342 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada concerning His saying: "Do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: It was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who wanted to withdraw from the world, [[In the printed edition: "an yatakhallu min al-libas" (that they divest themselves of clothing), which is a confused statement. In the manuscript: "wa-yatahallu min al-libsa," unpointed; its correct reading is what is established here, from al-Durr al-Manthur 2:308.]] abandon women, and practice asceticism (yatazahhadu). Among them were ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un.

12343 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not command you to be priests and monks."

12344 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada concerning His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse. It was mentioned to us that some men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) rejected women and meat, and wanted to take up monasteries. When this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he said: "There is no abandonment of women and meat in my religion, nor taking up monasteries." And we were informed that three men in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) agreed together. One of them said: "As for me, I will pray all night and never sleep!" Another said: "As for me, I will fast by day and never break my fast!" And the other said: "As for me, I will not approach women!" So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for them and said: "Was I not informed that you agreed upon such-and-such?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we intended only good!" He said: "But I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break my fast, and I approach women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." And in some recitations it was: ﴿Whoever turns away from your Sunnah is not of your community, and has strayed from the right way.﴾ [[In the printed edition: "ʿan sawa' al-sabil" with an added "ʿan," which is not in the manuscript.]] It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said to some of his Companions: "Those before you were strict upon themselves, so God was strict upon them. These are their brothers in the dwellings (dur) and the monasteries!" [["Al-dur," meaning the plural of "dayr"; I mentioned the discussion of it on p. 515, footnote 1.]] Worship God, do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, perform the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, and be upright, and He will make you upright. [[Report 12344: Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-ʿAqadi, passed as number 352, 2616.
As for "Jami' ibn Hammad," I have not found a biography of him in the references available to me. And this is the first time the isnad of Bishr ibn Mu'adh appears in his narration from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ through "Jami' ibn Hammad." As for the isnad "Bishr ibn Mu'adh, from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ, from Sa'id, from Qatada," it is an isnad that has recurred in the tafsir from its beginning up to this point, in the narration of "Bishr ibn Mu'adh" from "Yazid ibn Zurayʿ" directly.
This new isnad will recur after this many times, in numbers 12367, 12423, 12507, and 12524. In this last isnad there is an explicit statement that he narrated the report once through this "Jami' ibn Hammad," and then narrated it again from "Yazid ibn Zurayʿ" directly.]]

12345 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors." The reason was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat one day and admonished the people, then stood up and did not add to them beyond warning. Some men among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who were ten, including ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, said: "We do not fear, unless we introduce some deed!" [[In the printed edition: "ma haqqana," and in the manuscript: "ma hafana." The correct reading is what is established here. That is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) warned them of God's punishment, so they said: "We have not reached the level of fear that our Lord would be pleased with, unless we do some deed that shows intense fear."]] For the Christians have forbidden things to themselves, so we will forbid! So some of them forbade eating meat and fat (wadak), and eating during the day. [["Al-wadak" (with two fatha vowels): the fat and grease of meat that is extracted from it.]] And some of them forbade sleep, and some forbade women. ʿUthman ibn Maz'un was among those who forbade women, and he would not come near his wife, nor would she come near him. His wife came to ʿA'isha, and she was called "al-Hawla'" (the Squinting One). ʿA'isha and the other wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) who were present said to her: "What is wrong with you, O Hawla', with your complexion changed, not combing your hair or using perfume?" She said: "How can I perfume myself and comb my hair, when my husband has not come to me, nor lifted a garment from me, since such-and-such time!" So they began laughing at her words. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered while they were laughing, and said: "What makes you laugh?" She said: "O Messenger of God, Hawla'! I asked her about her matter, and she said: 'My husband has not lifted a garment from me since such-and-such time!'" So he sent for ʿUthman and summoned him and said: "What is wrong with you, O ʿUthman?" He said: "I have abandoned it for God, so that I may devote myself to worship," and he related his matter to him. ʿUthman had intended to castrate himself, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I swear to you, unless you return and lie with your wife!" He said: "O Messenger of God, I am fasting!" He said: "Break your fast!" So he broke his fast and went to his wife. Then Hawla' returned to ʿA'isha, having applied kohl, combed her hair, and perfumed herself. ʿA'isha laughed and said: "What is wrong with you, O Hawla'?" She said: "He came to her yesterday!" Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, and sleep? Indeed, I sleep and I pray, I break my fast and I fast, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me!" Then this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress," meaning to ʿUthman: do not castrate yourself, for this is transgression. [[And He commanded them to expiate their oaths, saying: "God will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths."]]

12346 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: They were a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "We will cut off our male organs, abandon the desires of this world, and wander across the earth as the monks do!" When this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he sent for them, and mentioned that to them, and they said: "Yes!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "But I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever takes my Sunnah is from me, and whoever does not take my Sunnah is not from me."

12347 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." The reason was that some men among the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), including ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, forbade women and meat to themselves, and took up razors (shifar) to cut off their male organs, so that desire would be cut off and they could devote themselves to worshipping their Lord. The Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of this, and said: "What did you intend?" They said: "We intended that desire be cut off from us, and that we devote ourselves to worshipping our Lord, and be free from women!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was not commanded to that. Rather, I was commanded in my religion to marry women!" They said: "We obey the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." So God the Exalted revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors," up to His saying: "in whom you are believers."

12348 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Men, including ʿUthman ibn Maz'un and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, wanted to devote themselves (yatabattal) to worship, to castrate themselves, and to wear coarse woolen garments (masuh). [["Al-masuh," plural of "misḥ" (with a kasra and sukun): a garment of hair that monks wear.] So this verse was revealed, up to His saying: "and fear God in whom you are believers." Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿIkrima: that ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, along with companions, devoted themselves, sat in their houses, withdrew from women, wore coarse garments, forbade the good food and clothing except what the wandering monks (ahl al-siyaha) of the Children of Israel ate and wore, and resolved upon castration, and they agreed upon standing in prayer at night and fasting by day. So this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors." It means: do not go by other than the Sunnah of the Muslims. [[In the printed edition: "la tastannu bi-ghayr sunnat al-muslimin," and I have established what is in the manuscript, which is unpointed. This is the correct reading of it.]] He means: what they forbade of women, food, and clothing, what they resolved upon of fasting by day and standing in prayer at night, and what they intended of castration. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "hammu lahu," and it seems the correct reading is what is established.]] When it was revealed concerning them, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them and said: "Indeed, your souls have a right, and your eyes have a right! Fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, for whoever abandons my Sunnah is not of us!" They said: "O God, we have submitted, and we follow what You have sent down!"

12349 – Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Zayd regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: My father said: A guest came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, and Ibn Rawaha returned without having eaten supper. He said to his household: "What did you give him for supper?" She said: "The food was little, so I waited for you to come!" He said: "You have detained my guest on my account! Your food is forbidden to me if I taste it!" She said: "And it is forbidden to me if I taste it, unless you taste it!" And the guest said: "It is forbidden to me if I taste it, unless you all taste it!" When Ibn Rawaha saw that, he said: "Bring your food forward, eat in the name of God!" In the morning he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "You have done well!" Then this verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," and he recited until he reached: "God will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths." When you say: "By God, I will not taste it," that is the binding.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verses 86–87 (part 2 of 2):

12350 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: Ikrimah related to us, from Ibn Abbas: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, when I eat meat, my desire is aroused and my lust seizes me, so I have forbidden myself meat." Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾ [[Report 12350: al-Tirmidhi transmitted this report in the Book of Tafsir with its chain and wording, then said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Some narrators transmitted it other than through Uthman ibn Sa'd as a mursal report, without mention of Ibn Abbas. Khalid al-Hadhdha transmitted it from Ikrimah as a mursal report." He means by the following report, which is 12351.
"Uthman ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi, the scribe and teacher" is trustworthy (thiqah). It has passed as number 2155. In the printed edition here it read "Uthman ibn Sa'id," which is a pure error. The manuscript had the same, except that the two dots of the ya' were struck through, and the copyist intended to join the 'ayn to the dal, but the editor misread this.
Furthermore, consider the reports on castration and celibacy in Sahih al-Bukhari (al-Fath 9: 100–103) and what Hafiz Ibn Hajar commented on it. Then what is also mentioned there (al-Fath 8: 207), Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3: 213–217, and Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/1/286–288 in the biography of "Uthman ibn Maz'un."]]

12351 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' related to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha related to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Some people among the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved to abandon women and to castrate themselves, so God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

They differed concerning the meaning of "transgression" (i'tida') in God, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: ﴿and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾

Some of them said: The "transgression" which God forbade in this place is what Uthman ibn Maz'un resolved upon, namely castrating himself, so he was forbidden from that, and it was said to him: "This is the transgression."
Among those who said this was al-Suddi.

12352 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from him.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is what the body of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved upon, namely forbidding women, food, clothing and sleep, so they were forbidden to do that and to follow a practice other than the practice of their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Among those who said this was Ikrimah.

12353 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from him.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is a prohibition from God, may His remembrance be exalted, against going beyond the lawful to the unlawful.
Mention of those who said this:

12354 - Ibn Wakie related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from Asim, from al-Hasan: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress﴾, he said: "Do not transgress to what has been forbidden to you."

* *

We have already explained that the meaning of "transgression" is a person's going beyond what is his to what is not his, in every matter, as stated earlier, with what suffices instead of repeating it. [[See the explanation of "transgression" above, p. 489, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

Abu Ja'far said: Since this is so, and since God, may His remembrance be exalted, has made general by His saying "do not transgress" the prohibition of all transgression, it is obligatory that what is general by generality be judged accordingly, until something specifies it that must be accepted. No one may exceed God's limit in any matter, whether of what He has made lawful or unlawful. Whoever exceeds it is included among those of whom God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾

It is not impossible that the verse was revealed concerning the matter of Uthman ibn Maz'un and the group of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who resolved upon forbidding some of what God had made lawful for them to themselves, and that its ruling would apply to everyone who was in a similar situation to theirs, who forbade himself what God had made lawful for him, or made lawful what God had forbidden him, or transgressed a limit God had set for him. That is because those who resolved to forbid some of what was lawful for them upon themselves were only rebuked for their resolve to go beyond what had been prescribed and limited for them, to something other than it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 5, verses 86–87 (part 1 of 2)**

**On His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs — those are the companions of the Hellfire (al-Jahim).﴾ (5:86)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His exalted remembrance says: As for those who denied the Oneness of God, rejected the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and denied the signs of His Book, then ﴿those are the companions of the Hellfire (al-Jahim)﴾. He means: they are its inhabitants and those who remain in it. [[See the explanation of "companions of the Fire" in what has preceded, p. 217, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And "al-Jahim" is the fire whose heat is intense. It is also called "al-jaahim" and "al-jahim." [[See the explanation of "al-Jahim" in what has preceded, vol. 2, p. 562.]]

**On His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors.﴾ (5:87)**

Abu Ja'far said: His exalted remembrance says: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger, and acknowledged what their Prophet (ﷺ) brought, that it is the truth from God, ﴿do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you﴾. By "the good things" (al-tayyibat) He means the delicious things that souls desire and hearts incline toward, [[See the explanation of "al-tayyibat" in what has preceded, p. 84, footnote 1, and the references there.]] so that you deprive yourselves of them, like what the priests (qissisun) and monks (ruhban) did, who forbade themselves women, good foods and pleasant drinks, and some of whom confined themselves in monasteries (sawami'), while others wandered across the earth. His exalted remembrance says: So do not do, O believers, as those did. ﴿And do not transgress﴾ the limit God has set for you concerning what He has made lawful for you and what He has forbidden to you, so that you exceed His limit that He set, thereby disobeying Him. Indeed, God does not love the one who transgresses the limit He has set for His creatures concerning what He has made lawful and unlawful for them.

* *

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

12336 – Abu Husayn ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: ʿAbthar Abu Zubayd narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik regarding this verse: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse. He said: ʿUthman ibn Maz'un and some Muslims forbade themselves women and abstained from good food, and some of them wanted to cut off their male organs, so this verse was revealed. [[The report 12336: "Abu Husayn," ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yunus al-Yarbuʿi, the teacher of al-Tabari. He narrated from his father, and he and his father narrated from ʿAbthar ibn al-Qasim. Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Hatim and others narrated from him. Trustworthy and truthful. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "ʿAbthar ibn al-Qasim al-Zubaydi," "Abu Zubayd": trustworthy and truthful. Ibn Mu'in said: "Trustworthy, Sunni." Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/94, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/43. In the manuscript alone it read "ʿAbthar ibn Zubayda," which is a pure error.
And "Husayn" is Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who passed as numbers 579 and 2986.]]

12337 – Hamid ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha' narrated to me, from ʿIkrima, who said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) resolved to castrate themselves and to abandon meat and women, so this verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors."

12338 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Khalid, from ʿIkrima: that men wanted such-and-such and wanted such-and-such, and wanted to castrate themselves, so this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," up to His saying: "in whom you are believers."

12339 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: They had forbidden good things and meat, so God the Exalted revealed this concerning them.

12340 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrima: that some people said: "We will not marry, we will not eat, and we will not do such-and-such!" So God the Exalted revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors."

12341 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to renounce the world, abandon women, and adopt monasticism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up and spoke harshly to them, then said: "Those before you were destroyed only through excessive strictness. They were strict upon themselves, so God was strict upon them. So those are their remnants in the dwellings (diyar) and the monasteries (sawami')!" [[The word "diyar" is the plural of "dayr," and what the lexicographers mentioned is that its plural is "adyar," and they limited themselves to this plural. Yaqut, in Mu'jam al-Buldan (dayr), mentioned many plurals, of which this is not one, but he reported that al-Jawhari said: "Dayr al-nasara originally was dar." If that is so, then its plural as "diyar" is undoubtedly correct and analogical. See also "al-dur" in report no. 12344, p. 516, footnote 2.]] Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, perform the pilgrimage (hajj) and the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumra), and be upright, and He will make you upright. He said: And this verse was revealed concerning them: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse.

12342 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada concerning His saying: "Do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: It was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who wanted to withdraw from the world, [[In the printed edition: "an yatakhallu min al-libas" (that they divest themselves of clothing), which is a confused statement. In the manuscript: "wa-yatahallu min al-libsa," unpointed; its correct reading is what is established here, from al-Durr al-Manthur 2:308.]] abandon women, and practice asceticism (yatazahhadu). Among them were ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un.

12343 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not command you to be priests and monks."

12344 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada concerning His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," to the end of the verse. It was mentioned to us that some men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) rejected women and meat, and wanted to take up monasteries. When this reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he said: "There is no abandonment of women and meat in my religion, nor taking up monasteries." And we were informed that three men in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) agreed together. One of them said: "As for me, I will pray all night and never sleep!" Another said: "As for me, I will fast by day and never break my fast!" And the other said: "As for me, I will not approach women!" So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent for them and said: "Was I not informed that you agreed upon such-and-such?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, we intended only good!" He said: "But I pray and I sleep, I fast and I break my fast, and I approach women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me." And in some recitations it was: ﴿Whoever turns away from your Sunnah is not of your community, and has strayed from the right way.﴾ [[In the printed edition: "ʿan sawa' al-sabil" with an added "ʿan," which is not in the manuscript.]] It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said to some of his Companions: "Those before you were strict upon themselves, so God was strict upon them. These are their brothers in the dwellings (dur) and the monasteries!" [["Al-dur," meaning the plural of "dayr"; I mentioned the discussion of it on p. 515, footnote 1.]] Worship God, do not associate anything with Him, establish the prayer, give zakat, fast Ramadan, perform the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, and be upright, and He will make you upright. [[Report 12344: Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-ʿAqadi, passed as number 352, 2616.
As for "Jami' ibn Hammad," I have not found a biography of him in the references available to me. And this is the first time the isnad of Bishr ibn Mu'adh appears in his narration from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ through "Jami' ibn Hammad." As for the isnad "Bishr ibn Mu'adh, from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ, from Sa'id, from Qatada," it is an isnad that has recurred in the tafsir from its beginning up to this point, in the narration of "Bishr ibn Mu'adh" from "Yazid ibn Zurayʿ" directly.
This new isnad will recur after this many times, in numbers 12367, 12423, 12507, and 12524. In this last isnad there is an explicit statement that he narrated the report once through this "Jami' ibn Hammad," and then narrated it again from "Yazid ibn Zurayʿ" directly.]]

12345 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors." The reason was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat one day and admonished the people, then stood up and did not add to them beyond warning. Some men among the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who were ten, including ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, said: "We do not fear, unless we introduce some deed!" [[In the printed edition: "ma haqqana," and in the manuscript: "ma hafana." The correct reading is what is established here. That is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) warned them of God's punishment, so they said: "We have not reached the level of fear that our Lord would be pleased with, unless we do some deed that shows intense fear."]] For the Christians have forbidden things to themselves, so we will forbid! So some of them forbade eating meat and fat (wadak), and eating during the day. [["Al-wadak" (with two fatha vowels): the fat and grease of meat that is extracted from it.]] And some of them forbade sleep, and some forbade women. ʿUthman ibn Maz'un was among those who forbade women, and he would not come near his wife, nor would she come near him. His wife came to ʿA'isha, and she was called "al-Hawla'" (the Squinting One). ʿA'isha and the other wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) who were present said to her: "What is wrong with you, O Hawla', with your complexion changed, not combing your hair or using perfume?" She said: "How can I perfume myself and comb my hair, when my husband has not come to me, nor lifted a garment from me, since such-and-such time!" So they began laughing at her words. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered while they were laughing, and said: "What makes you laugh?" She said: "O Messenger of God, Hawla'! I asked her about her matter, and she said: 'My husband has not lifted a garment from me since such-and-such time!'" So he sent for ʿUthman and summoned him and said: "What is wrong with you, O ʿUthman?" He said: "I have abandoned it for God, so that I may devote myself to worship," and he related his matter to him. ʿUthman had intended to castrate himself, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I swear to you, unless you return and lie with your wife!" He said: "O Messenger of God, I am fasting!" He said: "Break your fast!" So he broke his fast and went to his wife. Then Hawla' returned to ʿA'isha, having applied kohl, combed her hair, and perfumed herself. ʿA'isha laughed and said: "What is wrong with you, O Hawla'?" She said: "He came to her yesterday!" Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What is the matter with people who forbid women, food, and sleep? Indeed, I sleep and I pray, I break my fast and I fast, and I marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me!" Then this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress," meaning to ʿUthman: do not castrate yourself, for this is transgression. [[And He commanded them to expiate their oaths, saying: "God will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths."]]

12346 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: They were a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "We will cut off our male organs, abandon the desires of this world, and wander across the earth as the monks do!" When this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he sent for them, and mentioned that to them, and they said: "Yes!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "But I fast and I break my fast, I pray and I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever takes my Sunnah is from me, and whoever does not take my Sunnah is not from me."

12347 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." The reason was that some men among the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), including ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, forbade women and meat to themselves, and took up razors (shifar) to cut off their male organs, so that desire would be cut off and they could devote themselves to worshipping their Lord. The Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of this, and said: "What did you intend?" They said: "We intended that desire be cut off from us, and that we devote ourselves to worshipping our Lord, and be free from women!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I was not commanded to that. Rather, I was commanded in my religion to marry women!" They said: "We obey the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." So God the Exalted revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors," up to His saying: "in whom you are believers."

12348 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Men, including ʿUthman ibn Maz'un and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, wanted to devote themselves (yatabattal) to worship, to castrate themselves, and to wear coarse woolen garments (masuh). [["Al-masuh," plural of "misḥ" (with a kasra and sukun): a garment of hair that monks wear.] So this verse was revealed, up to His saying: "and fear God in whom you are believers." Ibn Jurayj said, from ʿIkrima: that ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas'ud, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, along with companions, devoted themselves, sat in their houses, withdrew from women, wore coarse garments, forbade the good food and clothing except what the wandering monks (ahl al-siyaha) of the Children of Israel ate and wore, and resolved upon castration, and they agreed upon standing in prayer at night and fasting by day. So this was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors." It means: do not go by other than the Sunnah of the Muslims. [[In the printed edition: "la tastannu bi-ghayr sunnat al-muslimin," and I have established what is in the manuscript, which is unpointed. This is the correct reading of it.]] He means: what they forbade of women, food, and clothing, what they resolved upon of fasting by day and standing in prayer at night, and what they intended of castration. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "hammu lahu," and it seems the correct reading is what is established.]] When it was revealed concerning them, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them and said: "Indeed, your souls have a right, and your eyes have a right! Fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, for whoever abandons my Sunnah is not of us!" They said: "O God, we have submitted, and we follow what You have sent down!"

12349 – Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Zayd regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you." He said: My father said: A guest came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, and Ibn Rawaha returned without having eaten supper. He said to his household: "What did you give him for supper?" She said: "The food was little, so I waited for you to come!" He said: "You have detained my guest on my account! Your food is forbidden to me if I taste it!" She said: "And it is forbidden to me if I taste it, unless you taste it!" And the guest said: "It is forbidden to me if I taste it, unless you all taste it!" When Ibn Rawaha saw that, he said: "Bring your food forward, eat in the name of God!" In the morning he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "You have done well!" Then this verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things that God has made lawful for you," and he recited until he reached: "God will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with oaths." When you say: "By God, I will not taste it," that is the binding.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verses 86–87 (part 2 of 2):

12350 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: Ikrimah related to us, from Ibn Abbas: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, when I eat meat, my desire is aroused and my lust seizes me, so I have forbidden myself meat." Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾ [[Report 12350: al-Tirmidhi transmitted this report in the Book of Tafsir with its chain and wording, then said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. Some narrators transmitted it other than through Uthman ibn Sa'd as a mursal report, without mention of Ibn Abbas. Khalid al-Hadhdha transmitted it from Ikrimah as a mursal report." He means by the following report, which is 12351.
"Uthman ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi, the scribe and teacher" is trustworthy (thiqah). It has passed as number 2155. In the printed edition here it read "Uthman ibn Sa'id," which is a pure error. The manuscript had the same, except that the two dots of the ya' were struck through, and the copyist intended to join the 'ayn to the dal, but the editor misread this.
Furthermore, consider the reports on castration and celibacy in Sahih al-Bukhari (al-Fath 9: 100–103) and what Hafiz Ibn Hajar commented on it. Then what is also mentioned there (al-Fath 8: 207), Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3: 213–217, and Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 3/1/286–288 in the biography of "Uthman ibn Maz'un."]]

12351 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' related to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha related to us, from Ikrimah, who said: Some people among the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved to abandon women and to castrate themselves, so God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

They differed concerning the meaning of "transgression" (i'tida') in God, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: ﴿and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾

Some of them said: The "transgression" which God forbade in this place is what Uthman ibn Maz'un resolved upon, namely castrating himself, so he was forbidden from that, and it was said to him: "This is the transgression."
Among those who said this was al-Suddi.

12352 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from him.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is what the body of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) resolved upon, namely forbidding women, food, clothing and sleep, so they were forbidden to do that and to follow a practice other than the practice of their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Among those who said this was Ikrimah.

12353 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from him.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is a prohibition from God, may His remembrance be exalted, against going beyond the lawful to the unlawful.
Mention of those who said this:

12354 - Ibn Wakie related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from Asim, from al-Hasan: ﴿O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress﴾, he said: "Do not transgress to what has been forbidden to you."

* *

We have already explained that the meaning of "transgression" is a person's going beyond what is his to what is not his, in every matter, as stated earlier, with what suffices instead of repeating it. [[See the explanation of "transgression" above, p. 489, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

Abu Ja'far said: Since this is so, and since God, may His remembrance be exalted, has made general by His saying "do not transgress" the prohibition of all transgression, it is obligatory that what is general by generality be judged accordingly, until something specifies it that must be accepted. No one may exceed God's limit in any matter, whether of what He has made lawful or unlawful. Whoever exceeds it is included among those of whom God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, God does not love transgressors.﴾

It is not impossible that the verse was revealed concerning the matter of Uthman ibn Maz'un and the group of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who resolved upon forbidding some of what God had made lawful for them to themselves, and that its ruling would apply to everyone who was in a similar situation to theirs, who forbade himself what God had made lawful for him, or made lawful what God had forbidden him, or transgressed a limit God had set for him. That is because those who resolved to forbid some of what was lawful for them upon themselves were only rebuked for their resolve to go beyond what had been prescribed and limited for them, to something other than it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 88:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good. And fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His mention be exalted, says to those believers whom He forbade from prohibiting the good things which Allah has made lawful for them: "Eat, O believers, of the provision of Allah which He has provided you and made lawful for you, lawful and good," [see the explanation of "lawful and good" in what has preceded, 3:300, 301], as related:

12355 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah: "And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good," meaning: what Allah has made lawful for them of food.

* *

As for His saying: "And fear Allah, in whom you are believers," He says: Fear, O believers, lest you transgress against His limits, so that you make lawful what has been forbidden to you, and forbid what has been made lawful for you; and beware of Him in that, lest you oppose Him, so that His wrath descends upon you, or you incur His punishment through it [see the explanation of "taqwa" in what has preceded in the indices of vocabulary (w-q-y)]. "In whom you are believers" means: in whose oneness you acknowledge and in whose lordship you affirm.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 89 (part 1 of 5):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have bound by your oaths﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, He says to those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had forbidden themselves the good things, and who had forbidden that by oaths they had sworn, that He forbade them from prohibiting them and said to them: Your Lord will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, [[See the explanation of "al-mu'akhadhah" (taking to task) in what has preceded, 4:427 and following / 6:132 and following.]] as:

12356 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse was revealed, "O you who believe, do not forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful for you," concerning the people who had forbidden women and meat upon themselves, they said: O Messenger of Allah, how should we act regarding our oaths which we swore? So Allah, Exalted is His mention, revealed: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," the verse.
* *
= This indicates what we have said, that the people had forbidden what they forbade upon themselves by oaths they swore, and this verse was revealed concerning them.
* *
The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.
The common readers of the Hijaz and some of the Basrans recited: ﴿بِمَا عَقَّدْتُمُ الأيْمَانَ﴾ with a doubled "qaf", meaning: you emphasized the oaths and repeated them.
* *
The readers of the Kufans recited: ﴿بِمَا عَقَدْتُمُ الأيْمَانَ﴾ [[In the printed edition: "wa-qura' al-Kufiyyin"; in the manuscript: "wa-qarah al-Kufiyyin"; the correct wording should add "wa-qara'ahu" as I have done.]] with a single "qaf", meaning: you made them obligatory upon yourselves, and your hearts resolved upon them.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who recites with a single "qaf". This is because the Arabs hardly use "fa''ala" in speech except for what involves repetition again and again, such as their saying "shaddadtu 'ala fulanin fi kadhā" (I pressed hard upon so-and-so in such-and-such), when the hardship is repeated upon him time after time. When they wish to report the doing of a single act, it is said "shadadtu 'alayhi" with the single consonant.
It is also agreed by all, without any disagreement among them, that the oath in which breaking it requires expiation is binding by breaking it upon one who swore it once, even if the swearer did not repeat it several times. It was thus known that Allah takes to task the swearer whose heart binds itself to his oath, even if he did not repeat or reiterate it.
And if this is so, there is no understandable reason for doubling the "qaf" in "'aqqadtum".
* *
The meaning of the speech, then, is: Allah will not take you to task, O believers, for the oaths in which you spoke idly, but He will take you to task for what you have made obligatory upon yourselves by them, and what your hearts have resolved upon.
* *
We have already explained the oath that is "lagh" (idle), and the oath for which Allah takes the servant to task, and the oath in which there is breaking (hinth), and the oath in which there is no breaking, in what has passed in this book of ours, so we disliked repeating that in this place. [[See the explanation of "al-laghw" and what was said concerning it, 4:427–455.]]
* *
As for His saying: "for what you have bound by oaths," [[See the explanation of "'aqd al-aymān" (binding of oaths) in what has preceded, 8:272–274.]] Hannad narrated to us:

12357 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "but He will take you to task for what you have bound by oaths," he said: for what you intended.

12358 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So its expiation is feeding ten needy persons﴾

As for the oath that is expiated, a man swears upon a matter he does not do, then he does it, upon him is expiation. As for the oath that is not expiated, a man swears upon a matter in which he deliberately lies, so there is no expiation in it. As for the oath for which its swearer is not taken to task, a man swears upon a matter he thinks is as he swore, but it is not so, so there is no expiation upon him in it. And this is "lagh" (idle). * *
Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech on this interpretation is: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have bound by oaths," so the expiation for what you have bound of them is feeding ten needy persons.
* *
Others said: The "ha'" in His saying "fa-kaffaratuhu" refers back to "al-laghw" (the idle), and it is a pronoun referring to it. They said: The meaning of the speech is only: Allah will not take you to task for the idle in your oaths when you expiate it, but He will take you to task when you bind the oaths and persist in going through with them by not breaking them and not expiating them. Persisting in carrying them out is not permitted for you. So the expiation of the idle among them, if you break it, is feeding ten needy persons.
Those who said this:

12370 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," it is the man who swears to do a harmful matter and does not do it, then he sees what is better than it, so Allah commands him to expiate his oath and do what is better. He said again concerning His saying: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," up to His saying "for what you have bound by oaths," he said: and the idle among oaths is that which is expiated; Allah does not take one to task for it. But whoever persists in forbidding what Allah has made lawful for him, and does not turn from it, and does not expiate his oath, that is what he is taken to task for. [[In the printed edition: "yu'akhadh bihā"; I have kept the manuscript reading.]]
12371 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," he said: it is the one who swears upon disobedience and does not fulfill it, so he expiates. [[Narration 12371: given in full earlier at no. 4436.]]
12372 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," he said: it is the man who swears upon disobedience, so Allah, Exalted is His mention, does not take him to task; he expiates his oath and does what is better. "But He will take you to task for what you have bound by oaths," the man who swears upon disobedience and then persists in it, so his expiation is feeding ten needy persons. [[Narration 12372: given in abridged form at no. 4440.]]
12373 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said concerning the idle oath: it is the oath in disobedience. He said: Do you not recite and understand? "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have bound by oaths." He said: So He does not take him to task for nullifying it, but He takes him to task for persisting in it. [[In the printed edition: "bi-l-muqam 'alayha"; the correct reading is that of the manuscript, consistent with his narration given earlier, as will come in the takhrij. "Tamma 'ala al-amr tamaman": he persisted in it and carried it through.]] He said, and he said: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 224]. [[Narration 12373: this narration was given earlier with its chain and wording, at no. 4445.]]
12374 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," he said: it is the man who swears upon disobedience, so Allah does not take him to task for abandoning it if he abandons it. I said: And how should he act? He said: He expiates his oath and abandons the disobedience. [[Narration 12374: given earlier with its chain and wording, at no. 4443.]]
12375 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim who said: "The idle": an oath for which its swearer is not taken to task, and in it there is expiation. [[Narration 12375: in the printed edition this came after the following one; I have moved it as in the manuscript.]]
12376 - Yahya ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," he said: the expiated oath. [[Narration 12376: also given earlier at no. 4464.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: What is more correct in my view on this matter is that the "ha'" in His saying "fa-kaffaratuhu" refers back to the "ma" in His saying "bima 'aqqadtum al-aymān," because of what we have already mentioned earlier, that whoever is obligated by an expiation in his oath and is taken to task for it, it is not permissible to say of one who has been taken to task: "Allah does not take him to task for the idle." And in His saying, Exalted is His mention, "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," there is clear evidence that one who is informed by Exalted Allah that He will not take him to task is not taken to task in any way.
If someone supposes that by His saying, Exalted is His mention, "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths," He meant punishment for them in the Hereafter when you break them and expiate them, but He does not take them to task for them in this world by expiation, then the information of Allah, Exalted is His mention, His command and His prohibition in His Book, upon the general apparent meaning in our view, which we have shown to be correct to hold in other places, so there is no need to repeat it, and not upon the general inward meaning for which there is no indication of its particularity in reason or report. There is no indication from reason or report that He, Exalted is His mention, meant by His saying "Allah will not take you to task for what is unintentional in your oaths" some of the meanings of taking to task rather than all of them.
Since this is so, and since whoever is obligated by an expiation for an oath which he broke is taken to task by a punishment in his property immediately, it is known that he is other than the one whom Exalted Allah informed us He will not take to task for it.
* *
Since the correct interpretation in this matter is what we have said, supported by what we have shown, the meaning of the speech is therefore: Allah will not take you to task, O people, for idle speech and oaths when you did not intend by them disobedience to Allah, Exalted is His mention, nor opposition to His command, nor did you intend by them sin; but He will take you to task for what you intended in them sin, and made obligatory upon yourselves, and what your hearts resolved upon; and that will be expiated for you, covering over the evil of what was from you of lying and false speech, and erasing it from you so that your Lord does not follow you with it [[See the explanation of "al-kaffārah" (expiation) and "al-takfīr" in what has preceded, p. 461, note 2, and the references there.]] = "feeding ten needy persons from the middle of what you feed your families."
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿From the middle of what you feed your families﴾
Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention means by His saying "from the middle of what you feed your families" the most just of it, as:

12377 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I heard 'Ata' say concerning this verse: "from the middle of what you feed your families or clothe them," 'Ata' said: "its middle" is its most just.
* *
The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying "from the middle of what you feed your families."
Some of them said: its meaning is: from the middle of what is fed from kinds of food which the people of the expiator's land eat as their staple, to their families. [[See the explanation of "al-wasat" (middle) in what has preceded, 3:141–145 / 5:227.]]
Those who said this:

12378 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Hanash, from al-Aswad who said: I asked him about "from the middle of what you feed your families," he said: bread, dates, olive oil, clarified butter, and the best of it is meat. [[Narration 12378: 'Abd Allah ibn Hanash al-Awdi. He narrated from al-Bara', Ibn 'Umar, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, and others. Al-Thawri, Shurayk, Shu'bah and Abu 'Awanah narrated from him. Ibn Ma'in said: "trustworthy"; Abu Hatim said: "there is no harm in him." Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/39. "Al-Aswad" is al-Aswad ibn Yazid ibn Qays al-Nakha'i, mentioned at nos. 3299, 4888, 8267.]]

He said: and I think it is vinegar.

[[In the printed edition: "So what do you think of a mukkuk of wheat? He said: A mukkuk of wheat, no, or a mukkuk of dates, no. Ya'qub said..." In the manuscript: "So what do you think of a mukkuk of wheat? He said: A mukkuk of wheat, no, or a mukkuk of wheat, no. Ya'qub said." The editor of the printed edition wanted to correct it, and corrected it!! But the whole statement remained meaningless, a confusion upon confusion. The reason is that the copyist of the manuscript saw in the copy he was transcribing from "no, or a mukkuk of wheat, no", and the words "no" in both places were written above the line, above "or" before it, and above "wheat" after it. That means the words between the first "no" and the second "no" were removed and inserted into the text, which took the statement out of being intelligible.
The fact is that Jabir ibn Zayd said: "A mukkuk of wheat is sufficient", and he paused the statement and indicated with his hand that it was good and adequate.]] = Ya'qub said: Ibn 'Ulayyah said: Abu Maslamah gestured with his hand, [["Gestured with his hand": pointed and signaled. He means he indicated with his hand that this is sufficient and valid.]] as if he considered it good, and Abu Bishr turned his hand. [[The report 12406: "Ibn 'Ulayyah" is Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Miqsam al-Asadi, Abu Bishr, who appeared several times before, the last being 9913.
And "Abu Maslamah" of Basra is Sa'id ibn Yazid ibn Maslamah al-Azdi, who appeared under nos. 797, 5559, 5561. In the printed edition it was "Sa'd ibn Yazid Abu Salamah", and then also "Abu Salamah", all of which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.

Then in the printed edition here it read: "and Abu Salamah turned his hand", different from the manuscript, which is what I have adopted, because he did not see any mention of Abu Bishr in the chain!! Rather, "Abu Bishr" is "Ibn 'Ulayyah" himself; this is his kunya.]]
