* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning the interpretation of His words, ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾, in our view, is the saying of one who said: "From the average of what you feed your families in scarcity and abundance." That is because the rulings of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning all expiations came in accordance with that. Such as his ruling (ﷺ) concerning the expiation for shaving the head because of harm: a faraq (a measure of about three sa's) of food among six needy persons, [["Al-faraq" (with the first and second letter vowelled, or the first vowelled and the second sukun): a measure for the people of Medina, equal to three sa's.]] for each needy person half a sa'. [[See what has passed of the reports 3334–3359 in the fourth volume, pages 58–69.]] And like his ruling concerning the expiation for intercourse during Ramadan: fifteen sa's among sixty needy persons, for each needy person a quarter sa'. [[See al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi, 4: 221–228.]] Nothing is known from him (ﷺ) of any expiation in which he ordered feeding with bread and condiment, or with lunch and dinner. [[In the manuscript: "amran bil-ta'am khubz wa-idam" ("ordering food, bread and condiment"), but the printed reading is more consistent with the context.]]

Since this is so, and since the expiation for oaths is one of the expiations that bind whoever is bound by them, its course is the course of what the Prophet (ﷺ) decided: that the obligation on the one who makes expiation is food, specified for ten needy persons and measured by a measure, not gathering them for lunch or dinner of baked, seasoned food, since his (ﷺ) practice in all the other expiations was like that. [[In the printed edition: "min al-ta'am miqdar lil-masakin al-'ashara mahdud bi-kayl" ("food, an amount for the ten needy measured by a measure"). The correct reading is from the manuscript. The printed edition misunderstood Abu Ja'far's words, for by "al-ta'am" he meant wheat or dates. Ibn al-Athir said: "Al-ta'am is general for everything one lives on, such as wheat, barley, dates, and other things." The people of the Hijaz, when they used the word "al-ta'am" without qualification, meant wheat specifically. In the hadith of Abu Sa'id: "We used to give the zakat al-fitr in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a sa' of food, or a sa' of barley." It was said he meant wheat, and it was said dates. They said: "The latter is closer to it, because wheat was scarce among them, not enough to give the zakat al-fitr."]]

* *

Since what we have said is correct, with what we used as evidence, [[In the printed edition: "mimma bihi istashhadna" ("of what we cited as evidence"), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] it is clear that the meaning of the speech is: "But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn; so its expiation is feeding ten needy persons from the most moderate of what you feed your families," and that the "ma" in His words, ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾, is in the sense of the verbal noun, not in the sense of a noun.

Given that, the most moderate staple of the one who is well-off with his family is two mudds, which is half a sa' with a condiment in a quarter of it. This is the highest of what the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled concerning an expiation in feeding the needy. The most moderate staple of the one who is in straitened circumstances with his family is one mudd, which is a quarter of a sa', and it is the lowest of what he ruled concerning an expiation in feeding the needy.

* *

As for those who considered feeding the needy in the expiation for oaths to be bread and meat, and what we mentioned earlier about them, and those who considered lunch or dinner, and those who considered lunch and dinner, they went to an interpretation of His words, ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ as: from the average of the food that you feed your families. So they made the "ma" in His words, ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ a noun, not a verbal noun, and they obligated the one making expiation to feed the needy from the most moderate of the foods on which he feeds his family. That would be a view, were it not for what we have mentioned of the practices of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the other expiations, whose kinds must be joined to them, and that the expiation for oaths has a counterpart and a similar one to which it must be joined. [[See the interpretation of "al-masakin" in what has passed, 8: 334, note 5, and the references there.]]

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿or clothing them﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "So the expiation for what you have bound by oaths is feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them." That is, "either you feed them or you clothe them." The choice in that belongs to the one making expiation.

* *

12459. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "Two garments." [[In the printed edition: "qala" ("both said"), and the correct reading is from the manuscript. A printing error.]]

12460. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, the same.

12461. Abu Kurayb and Hannad narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "Two garments, two garments for each needy person."

12462. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Musa: that he swore an oath, then clothed two garments of mu'aqqada (a kind of striped cloth) from Bahrayn. [[The two reports 12462 and 12463: Al-Bayhaqi narrated them in al-Sunan, 10: 56, by another route, through Salama ibn Alqama, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with a different wording, in full.
"Al-mu'aqqad" (with the qaf shaddah and fathah): a kind of cloth of Hajar. I have not found its description.]]

12463. Hannad and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Sirin: that Abu Musa clothed two garments of mu'aqqada from Bahrayn. [[The two reports 12462 and 12463: Al-Bayhaqi narrated them in al-Sunan, 10: 56, by another route, through Salama ibn Alqama, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with a different wording, in full.
"Al-mu'aqqad" (with the qaf shaddah and fathah): a kind of cloth of Hajar. I have not found its description.]]

12464. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la: that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari swore an oath, and considered that he should make expiation, so he did it, and clothed ten persons, two garments each.

12465. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad: that Abu Musa swore an oath and made expiation, so he clothed ten needy persons, two garments each.

1246) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "A cloak and a turban for every poor person."

1247) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the same.

1248) Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, saying: A man said in the presence of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: ﴿or [the expiation is] the clothing of them﴾, [[This is an irregular reading (shadha), recited by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqa' al-Yamani. Ibn Khalawayh mentioned it in Shawadh al-Qira'at (p. 34) and attributed it to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib rather than Sa'id ibn Jubayr, which is an error on his part. This report indicates that, for Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib denied it. The correct attribution was given by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6: 279) and Abu Hayyan in his tafsir (4: 11).]] so Sa'id said: "No, it is only: 'aw kiswatuhum' ('or their clothing')." I said: "O Abu Muhammad, what is their clothing?" He said: "For every poor person, a cloak and a turban: a cloak to wrap himself in, and a turban to tie around his head."

1249) I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿or their clothing﴾: "The clothing, for every poor person, is a wrapper and an izar (lower garment), in accordance with what is available in ease and in want."

* *

Others said: Rather, by it is meant their clothing as "a comprehensive garment" (thawb jami'), such as a mantle, a blanket, and whatever is suitable for wearing and sleeping in.

Mention of those who said this:

1250) Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, who said: "The clothing is a comprehensive garment (thawb jami')."

1251) Hannad and Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying ﴿or their clothing﴾: "A comprehensive garment." He said: Mughirah said: "The comprehensive garment is a mantle, or a blanket, or the like. We do not consider the coat of mail, the shirt, or the head-covering, or the like, to be 'comprehensive'."

1252) Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "A comprehensive garment."

1253) Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "A comprehensive garment."

1254) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: ﴿or their clothing﴾, he said: "A comprehensive garment for every poor person."

1255) Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan and Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying ﴿or their clothing﴾, he said: "A comprehensive garment."

1256) Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Addi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Mughirah, the same.

* *

Others said: By it is meant the clothing of an izar, a rida' (upper garment), and a shirt.

Mention of those who said this:

1257) Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Burdah, from Rafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said concerning the clothing: "In the expiation: an izar, a rida', and a shirt." [[The report 1257: "Burdah" — I have found no mention of him, and it appears to be a distortion. "Rafi'" — I do not know who he is, and so it is in the manuscript. In the printed edition it was "Nafi'", altered without any evidence. I have preserved the chain as it is in the manuscript, until someone qualified can identify its correct form.]]

* *

Others said: Whatever one clothes [someone with] is sufficient, and the verse is general in its meaning.

Mention of those who said this:

1258) Hannad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "Anything is sufficient in the expiation for an oath except the tubban." ["Al-tubban" (with a vowel on the tā' and a doubled bā'): a small pair of trousers, about a span in length, that covers only the most intimate part of the body; it is worn by sailors.]

1259) Hannad and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ashath, from al-Hasan, who said: "A turban is sufficient in the expiation for an oath."

1260) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Uways al-Sayrafi, from Abu al-Haytham, who said: Salman said: "The best garment is the tubban." [[Report 1260: I have not found "Uways al-Sayrafi," and I do not know him. As for "Abu al-Haytham," I was not able to determine which of those known by the kunyah "Abu al-Haytham" is meant. And "Salman" too, I was unable to identify in this chain.]]

1261) Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from al-Hakam, who said: "A turban wrapped around his head."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter according to us, and the most fitting with the interpretation of the Qur'an, is the view of the one who said: By His saying "or their clothing" is meant whatever falls under the name of clothing, being a garment or more. This is because whatever is less than a garment, there is no disagreement among all the knowledgeable authorities (hujjah) that it is not among those included in the ruling of the verse. Therefore, anything less than that measure is excluded from what God, exalted is He, intended, by way of a widely transmitted report. [[Context: "There is no disagreement among all the knowledgeable authorities ... by way of a widely transmitted report."]] The garment and what is above it fall within the ruling of the verse, since no revelation came from God, exalted is He, nor any report from His Messenger (ﷺ), nor was there a consensus (ijma') among the community that it is not included in its ruling. It is not permissible to exclude from the ruling of the verse what the apparent meaning of the verse may include, except by a proof that must be accepted. And there is no proof for that.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿or the freeing of a slave﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, remembered is He, means by this: or the release of a slave from the bondage and humiliation of servitude.

The root meaning of "tahrir" (liberation) is release from captivity, [[See "tahrir raqabah" in what preceded, 9: 30 and following. Abu Ja'far did not explain it there, but he explained it here. This is one form of his abridgment in this tafsir.]] and from it is the saying of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib:

O Banu Ghudanah, indeed I have freed you,
and so I gifted you to 'Atiyyah ibn Ji'al.

[[His Diwan, 726; al-Naqa'id, 275; and Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', 424, from his qasidah in satire of Jarir.
"Banu Ghudanah" are the descendants of Ghudanah ibn Yarbu', brother of Kulayb ibn Yarbu', the grandfather of Jarir. "'Atiyyah ibn Ji'al ibn Qutn ibn Malik ibn Ghudanah ibn Yarbu'" was one of the chiefs of Banu Ghudanah and a friend and close companion of al-Farazdaq. When this poetry reached 'Atiyyah, he said: "May God reward my friend on my behalf with good! How quickly my friend has retracted his gift!" because he had satirized them, while claiming that he had gifted their honour to his companion. After this he says:
So I gifted you to the most deserving of you by precedence,
and the most generous of all who give gifts.
Had it not been for 'Atiyyah, I would have cut off your noses
from among the basest of noses and moustaches.
Thus am I: when I satirize a tribe,
I slit their noses with the sharpest of proverbs.]]

By his saying "I freed you," he means: I released your necks from the humiliation of satire and the obligation of disgrace.

* *

It was said: "tahrir raqabah" (freeing a neck), and the one freed is the one who has the neck, [[In the printed edition: "the owner of the neck" — the reader misread the manuscript.]] because it was the custom of the Arabs, when they captured a captive, to tie his hands to his neck with a leather strap, a rope, or something else. [[In the printed edition: "with a fetter or a rope," which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. "Al-qidd" (with a vowel on the qāf and a doubled dāl): a strip cut lengthwise from untanned hide. As for "al-qayd," it is most commonly used for the legs.]] When they released the captive from his captivity, they freed his hands and untied them from what had bound them to the neck. So when they spoke of releasing a captive, the discourse was about freeing his hands from his neck, and they meant news of releasing him from his captivity, [[See the interpretation of "wa fi al-riqab" (and for the captives) in what preceded, 3: 347. The interpretation there is brief, while here it is detailed. This is a form of Abu Ja'far's abridgment in this tafsir.]] just as one says: "So-and-so withheld his hand from so-and-so," when he withheld his hand from giving him a gift, [[And "wa basata fihi lisanahu" (and extended his tongue against him), see what preceded of similar expressions in the interpretation of His saying "Rather, both His hands are outstretched" (p. 451 and before it), and in the interpretation of "bima qaddamat aydihim" (2: 368).]] when he said something bad about him. The action is attributed to the limb through which that action is performed, rather than to its doer, because people use it among themselves and know its meaning. Likewise in the saying of God, remembered is He: "or the freeing of a neck," the "freeing" is attributed to the "neck," even though there is no shackle on his neck nor any binding of his hands to it, and the intended meaning of "freeing" is the slave himself, as we have described, owing to the usage of people among themselves, since they know its meaning.

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "from the course of the use of ..." The correct reading is "min jara'" (from because of), as it is written, for what is in Abu Ja'far's speech is "jara" (the shortened form of "jara'"). Hence it is written with a yā'. One says: "I did that because of you, and because of your sake," meaning: for your sake. Both forms occur together in one verse of poetry: "Are you angry because of the Banu Asad, though if you willed, you would have an alliance? And because of our sake you became slaves to a people, after the best of you had been trampled."]]

* *

If someone says: Is every neck intended by this, or only some of them?
[[In the printed edition: "or some of them." The manuscript's reading is entirely correct.]]

It is said: Rather, what is intended is every neck that is free from paralysis, ["Al-iq'ad" and "al-qi'ad" (with a vowel on the qāf): a disease that causes one to sit. "Uqad al-rajul fa huwa muqad" means that the man was afflicted with qi'ad and it prevented him from walking.] blindness, muteness, loss or paralysis of the hands, permanent insanity, and similar conditions. For one who has any of these, or some part of them, from among the necks, there is no disagreement among all the knowledgeable authorities that it is not sufficient in the expiation for an oath. Thus it is known that God, remembered is He, did not intend by "tahrir" in this verse such a person. As for the young and the old, the Muslim and the disbeliever, they are all intended by it.

* *

Of the same view as what we have said on this matter, a group of the people of knowledge has spoken.

Mention of those who said this:

1262) Hannad ... narrated to us, saying: Mughirah narrated to us, from Ibrahim: that he used to say: "Whoever has an obligatory neck (raqabah) to free, and buys a soul (nasamah), if he rescues it from [its] work, it suffices him; but it is not permissible to free one who does not work. As for the one who works, such as one who is one-eyed and similar, [it is sufficient]. But one who does not work, the blind and the paralysed, is not sufficient." [[Report 1262: Hannad ibn al-Sari does not narrate from Mughirah; there is one man or two between them in the chain. See the two reports immediately preceding: 1256, 1257, and what follows, number 1264. In the printed edition it was "kal-a'ma" (like the blind man); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

1263) Hannad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: "He disliked freeing a mukhabbal (one afflicted in his mind) in any of the expiations." ["Al-mukhabbal" (with a doubled bā'): the insane, from "al-khabl" (with a sukun on the bā'): paralysis, or corruption of the limbs, or corruption of the mind.]

1264) Hannad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: that he did not consider the freeing of one whose intellect is overcome to be sufficient in any of the expiations.

* *

Some of them said: In the expiation, only a sound (sahih) neck is sufficient from among the necks, and a child is sufficient in it.

Mention of those who said this:

1265) Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: "Only a sound person is sufficient as a neck."

1266) Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: "A child born in Islam is sufficient as a neck."

1267) Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "Whatever is in the Qur'an as 'a believing neck' (raqabah mu'minah), only one who fasts and prays is sufficient. And whatever is not 'believing,' a child is sufficient." [[Report 1267: it has passed with its chain and wording at number 10096.]]

Some of them said: The term "raqabah" is not applied to an infant until after a period of time has passed over him.

Mention of those who said this:

1268) Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Rifa'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shabur, from al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, from Sulayman, who said: "When a child is born, he is a nasamah; when he turns from back to belly, he is a raqabah; and when he prays, he is a mu'minah." [[Report 1268: "Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shabur al-Umawi," one of the great scholars, who lived in Beirut. He narrated from al-Awza'i, Yazid ibn Abi Maryam, and al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir. Trustworthy and firm; the four compilers narrated from him. His biography is in al-Tahdhib.
"Al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir al-Ghassani al-Lakhmi," known as "Abu al-Wazir." He narrated from 'Ata', Mujahid, al-Zuhri, Tawus, and Makhul. Trustworthy. His biography is in al-Tahdhib.
"Sulayman" seems to be "Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi," but I have not verified this.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter, according to us, is to say that God, exalted is He, has generalized by mentioning "the neck" to every neck. So whichever neck the one making expiation for his oath frees in his expiation, he has fulfilled what was required of him, except what we have mentioned, that the knowledgeable authorities are unanimous that God, remembered is He, did not intend it by "freeing," so such a case is excluded from the ruling of the verse. Whatever else is freed in expiation is permissible according to the apparent meaning of the revelation.

The one making expiation is given the choice in expiating his oath, which he broke, by one of these three options which God named in His Book, namely: feeding ten poor people from the average of what one feeds one's family, or clothing them, or freeing a neck. This is by the unanimous consensus of all, with no disagreement among them on this. If someone suspects that what we have said, that this is a consensus of all, is not as we have stated, then [consider] what:

1269) Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Duha narrated to us, from Masruq, who said: Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin came to 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) and said: "I have sworn to abstain from women and from the bed!" 'Abd Allah then recited this verse: ﴿Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you, and do not transgress; indeed God does not love the transgressors﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 87]. Ma'qil said: "I asked you about this, since I came upon this verse tonight?" 'Abd Allah said: "Go to your women and sleep, and free a slave, for you are wealthy." [[Report 1269: "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib," trustworthy; it has passed at numbers 6256, 8136. "'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad al-'Abdi," one of the great authorities; it has passed at numbers 2616, 3136. "Sulayman al-Shaybani" is Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani. Trustworthy. He has appeared many times, most recently at number 8869. "Abu al-Duha" and "Masruq" have both appeared many times. "Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani," Abu 'Amrah. Al-Baghawi said: "He settled in Kufa and narrated hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ)." His biography is in al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghabah, al-Isabah, Ibn Sa'd 6: 11, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/285. He is the brother of "al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin." In the printed edition here it was "al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin" in place of "Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin"; this was an unwarranted alteration of the name, since it was taken from the one following it, although they are two different reports. Also in the printed edition: "I asked you because I came upon this verse, so 'Abd Allah said," which is a corrupt colloquial alteration of the wording. The correct reading is in the manuscript, which reads "I asked you about (sa'altuka 'an)," with an "a" written in the middle of the letter "ayn" of "'an," so that it is read as "an" (that), and I have so given it. This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2: 309), from Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin, and he said: "It was transmitted by Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani through multiple chains, from Ibn Mas'ud."]]

1270) Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me: that Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to him, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i, from Hammam ibn al-Harith: that Nu'man ibn Muqarrin asked 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, saying: "I swore that I would not sleep on my bed for a year?" So Ibn Mas'ud said: "O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you," make expiation for your oath, and sleep on your bed! He said: "With what should I make expiation for my oath?" He said: "Free a neck, for you are wealthy." [[Report 1270: See the comment on the previous report, but here it attributes the story to "Nu'man ibn Muqarrin," the brother of "Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin."]]

* *

= And similar reports have been transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar, and others. Their instruction to those whom they ordered to make expiation by freeing necks was an expression of recommendation (istihbab), not a claim that for the wealthy expiation is valid only by freeing a neck. No one has transmitted from any of them that they said: "Expiation for the wealthy is not valid except by freeing a neck." And all the scholars of the cities, past and present, are unanimous that expiation by means other than freeing necks is permissible for the wealthy. Therefore, there is no need to cite anything else in support of what we have said on this matter.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then fasting for three days﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Whoever does not find" (the means) for the expiation of his oath, which he is obligated to expiate by food, clothing, or freeing a slave, by which he may expiate it according to what We have enjoined upon him and made obligatory in Our Book and upon the tongue of Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), "then fasting for three days" means: then it is incumbent upon him to fast three days.

* *

Then the scholars differed concerning the meaning of His words "whoever does not find," and when the one who breaks his oath, for which expiation has become obligatory upon him, becomes deserving of the designation "one who does not find," such that fasting is permitted for him in this matter.

Some of them said: If the one who breaks his oath, at the time of expiating his oath, has only enough for his own sustenance and the sustenance of his dependents for the day and night, then he may expiate by fasting. But if at that time he has, beyond the sustenance of himself and his dependents for that day and night, enough to feed ten needy persons or to clothe them, then expiation by feeding or clothing becomes obligatory for him, and fasting does not suffice for him at that time.

Among those who said this was al-Shafi'i:

12491 - Al-Rabi' narrated this to us from him.

* *

This view, God willing, was intended by those who made feeding obligatory upon one who has two dirhams, and by those who made it obligatory upon one who has three dirhams. [[In the printed edition, other than this sentence, the text reads: "from those who made feeding obligatory ... and from those who made it obligatory upon one who has," which disrupts the sense; the correct reading is that of the manuscript. I have vocalized the sentence so that its meaning is clear and easy to follow.]] And in similar terms:

12492 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abd al-Karim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "If he has only three dirhams, he feeds [others]." He said: meaning in the expiation.

12493 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, saying: I said to Umar ibn Rashid: "A man swears an oath and has nothing of food beyond what is sufficient for expiation?" He said: Qatadah used to say: "He fasts three days." [[The report 12493: "Umar ibn Rashid," apparently meaning "Umar ibn Rashid al-Sulami." He narrated from al-Sha'bi, and from him Sufyan al-Thawri. Biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/107.]]

12494 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "If he has two dirhams."

12495 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from Hammad, from Abd al-Karim Abu Umayyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Three dirhams." [[The report 12495: "Abd al-Karim," "Abu Umayyah," is: "Abd al-Karim Abi al-Makhariq," already passed as no. 9679. In the printed edition it read: "Abd al-Karim ibn Abi Umayyah," which is a pure error and an pointless alteration of what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: It is permissible for one who does not have two hundred dirhams to fast, and he is among those who do not find.

* *

Others said: It is permissible for one who does not have, beyond his capital with which he trades for his livelihood, what he could use for expiation by feeding, to fast; unless he has sufficiency, and from the wealth there is that with which he conducts his livelihood, and from the surplus beyond that there is that with which he expiates his oath. This is a view that some of the later jurists used to hold.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that whoever, at the time of breaking his oath, has only enough for his own sustenance and the sustenance of his dependents for the day and night, with no surplus beyond that, fasts three days, and he is among those included in the category of one who does not find food to feed, clothing to clothe, or a slave to free. But if at that time he has, beyond the sustenance of himself and his dependents for the day and night, what suffices to feed ten needy persons, or clothe them, or free a slave, then fasting does not suffice for him at that time, because one of the three alternatives at that time—feeding, clothing, or freeing—is a right which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, has made obligatory upon his wealth as a debt is obligatory. It has been established as proof that when a bankrupt man distributes his wealth among his creditors, he leaves for himself on that day only what is indispensable for his sustenance and that of his dependents for the day and night. Likewise is the ruling for one who is destitute, regarding the debt which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, has made obligatory upon his wealth by reason of the expiation which has become binding upon his wealth.

* *

* *

Others said: It is permissible for one who fasts them to fast them however he wishes, together or separated.

Mention of those who said this:

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter in our opinion is that it should be said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, made obligatory upon the one who is bound by an expiation of oath, when he does not find a way to expiate it by feeding, clothing, or freeing, that he expiate it by fasting three days, and He did not stipulate consecutiveness in this. Whichever way the one making expiation fasts them, separated or consecutive, it suffices him, because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only made obligatory upon him fasting three days, so however he performs their fasting, it suffices.

* *

As for what is reported from Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud in their recitation, "Then fasting three days consecutively," that is contrary to what is in our codices, and it is not permissible for us to bear witness that something which is not in our codices of speech is from the Book of Allah. [[In the printed edition: "an tashhad bi-shay'," and the correct reading is that of the manuscript.]] Nevertheless, I prefer for the one fasting in expiation of an oath that he follow the three days consecutively and not separate them, because there is no disagreement among all that if he does so, it suffices for him as his expiation, whereas they differ otherwise. Doing what is agreed upon as permissible is more beloved to me, although the other is also permissible.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: "That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear. And guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs, that you may be grateful" (5:89).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "That," Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, means this which I have mentioned to you as the expiation of your oaths: feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them, or freeing a slave, and fasting three days when you do not find any of that—this is the expiation of your oaths which you have bound yourselves to when you swear. "And guard your oaths," O you who believe, lest you break them, then neglect the expiation for them by what I have described to you. "Thus does Allah make clear to you His signs," as He has made clear to you the expiation of your oaths, so Allah makes clear to you all His signs, meaning the markers of His religion, and He clarifies them for you, lest the negligent one who neglects what Allah has obligated him say: "I did not know the ruling of Allah in this!" "That you may be grateful," meaning: that you may thank Allah for His guidance of you and His granting you success. [[See the explanation of the terms of this verse in the lexical indexes mentioned earlier.

And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and upon his family, and greet them abundantly."
Then there follows the text:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, help, O Generous One."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 90:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an explanation from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning those among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who had forbidden upon themselves women, sleep, and meat, imitating the priests and monks. So Allah sent down His Book to His Prophet ﷺ, forbidding them from that, and said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 87].

Thus He forbade them from prohibiting the good things that Allah had made lawful for them. Then He said: "And do not transgress [the limits]; also, do not transgress in My limits, so that you make lawful what I have prohibited for you, for that is not permissible for you, just as it is not permissible for you to prohibit what I have made lawful. Indeed, I do not love the transgressors." Then He informed them about what He had prohibited for them, which, if they regarded it as lawful and went ahead with it, would make them transgressors of His limits. So He said to them: "O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, indeed the intoxicants you drink, the gambling you engage in, the stone altars you slaughter at, and the divining arrows you seek decisions by" are "defilement", meaning: sin and filth, which Allah has detested and abhorred for you, "from the work of Satan", meaning: your drinking of intoxicants, your gambling with the slaughtered camel parts, your slaughtering at the altars, and your seeking decisions by arrows, are from Satan's adornment for you, his calling you to it, and his making it appealing to you, not from the deeds to which your Lord has urged you, nor from what He is pleased with for you, but rather it is from what He is displeased with for you. "So avoid it", meaning: leave it and abandon it, and do not do it, "that you may be successful", meaning: so that you may prosper and attain success with your Lord by leaving that. [[See the explanation of "al-Falah" above, 10:292, note 3, and the references there.]] [[See the explanation of "ijtanaba" above, 8:233, where it is unexplained there, and then 8:340.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-khamr", "al-maysir", and "al-azlam" earlier, so we dislike repeating it. [[See the explanation of "al-khamr" above, 4:320, 321.

= And the explanation of "al-maysir" above, 4:321, 322-325.

= And the explanation of "al-azlam" above, 9:510-515.]]

* *

As for "al-ansab", it is the plural of "nusub", and we have already explained the meaning of "al-nusub" with its evidence earlier. [[See the explanation of "al-nusub", 9:507-509.]]

* *

Ibn Zayd said regarding this, that:

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 91 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?﴾ (5:91)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: Satan only wants for you the drinking of wine and the playing of maysir (gambling) with the arrows (qidah), and he beautifies that for you, wanting by it to cause animosity and hatred between you through your drinking of wine and your gambling with the arrows,[[See the explanation of "al-baghda'" (hatred) in what has preceded, 7:145 and 10:136.]] so that some of you become hostile to one another and make one another detested, thereby scattering your affairs after Allah has united you through faith and joined you together through the brotherhood of Islam. "And to avert you from the remembrance of Allah," he says: and to turn you away, through the overpowering of this wine by its intoxication over you, and through your being occupied with this gambling, from the remembrance of Allah, by which lies the welfare of your worldly life and your Hereafter. "And from prayer," which your Lord has enjoined upon you. "So will you not desist?" he says: Will you not desist from drinking this and from gambling with it,[[See the explanation of "al-intihaa'" (desisting) in what has preceded, p. 482, note 3, and the references there.]] and act upon what your Lord has commanded you: performing what He has made obligatory upon you of prayer at its appointed times, and persisting in His remembrance, by which your requests are granted in your worldly life and your Hereafter?

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the occasion (sabab al-nuzul) for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed because of an incident involving 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He mentioned the harmful consequence of drinking it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and asked Allah to make it forbidden.[[See what has preceded on the prohibition of wine, 4:330–336 and 8:376, 377.]]

Those who said this:

12512 – Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: 'Umar said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a satisfying clarification!" So the verse in al-Baqarah was revealed: ﴿They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both there is great sin and benefit for people﴾ (2:219). He said: 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a satisfying clarification!" Then the verse in al-Nisa' was revealed: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾ (4:43). He said: The herald of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to call out when the prayer was due: "No intoxicated person shall approach the prayer!" He said: 'Umar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: "O Allah, make clear to us regarding wine a satisfying clarification!" He said: Then the verse in al-Ma'idah was revealed: "O you who have believed, indeed intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous stones, and divining arrows are an abomination," up to His words: "So will you not desist?" When he reached His words "So will you not desist?" 'Umar said: "We have desisted, we have desisted!"[[Report 12512: Abu Maysarah is 'Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani, who heard 'Umar and 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and others of the Companions. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, no. 378, through the route of Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, in similar form. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, 3:444, no. 3670, in similar form, and in it: "a clarification that is a cure" (shifa'). Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Sunan, 8:286, 287, in similar form. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, through the route of Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Isra'il, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report; then through the route of Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', from Waki', from Isra'il, as a mursal (broken at the Companion level) report. But here it came in the narration of Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Waki', as marfu'. Al-Tirmidhi said after mentioning the narration of Abu Kurayb: "This is more authentic than the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yusuf," meaning that it is more authentic as a mursal report. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, 2:278, through the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, in similar form, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Ibn Kathir took it up in his Tafsir, 1:499, 500, and then 3:225. My brother, al-Sayyid Ahmad, has authenticated this hadith in the Musnad, no. 378, and then said: "Ibn Kathir mentioned it in the Tafsir, 1:499, 500 and 3:226, and said: Thus did Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrate it through various routes from Abu Ishaq. Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, whose name is 'Amr ibn Shurahbil al-Hamdani al-Kufi, from 'Umar, and he has no other narration from him. But Abu Zur'ah said: He did not hear from him. And Allah knows best. 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: This is a sound, authentic isnad (chain). al-Tirmidhi also authenticated it. 12515 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father = and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, similar to it.

12516 – Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, similar to it.[[Reports 12514–12516: See the takhrij at no. 12512.]]

12517 – Hannad narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar al-Madani narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, the people came to him, and they used to drink wine and eat maysir. Others said: This verse was revealed because of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Others said: It was revealed concerning two tribes among the tribes of the Ansar.

I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] Then Allah revealed: "Indeed intoxicants and gambling..." up to His words: "So will you not desist?" Then some of the self-styled scholars said: "The abomination is in the stomach of So-and-so, who was killed on the day of Badr, and So-and-so, who was killed at Uhud!" Then Allah revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who have believed and done righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ (5:93), the verse.[[In the printed text: "hiya rijs, wa hiya fi batn fulan" ("it is an abomination, and it is in the stomach of So-and-so"), and so it is in all other sources. I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which seems also to be correct.

Report 12522: "Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum ibn Jabr," al-Dayli al-Basri, from whom Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated. He was spoken of critically, but he is trustworthy. He has passed as no. 6240. In the printed text it reads "Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum from Jubayr, from his father," which is an error. In the manuscript it reads "Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum from Jabr, from his father," which is also an error, although in the manuscript "Jabr" is correct. In al-Mustadrak the error "Jubayr" appears, which must be corrected. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/266, where no criticism is mentioned, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/477, 478; Yahya ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy. In it, from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, who said: "I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: I asked: 'Did Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum in a hadith from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, really say "from Ibn 'Abbas"?' He said: 'Did Sa'id ibn Jubayr ever narrate except from Ibn 'Abbas?'"

His father, "Kulthum ibn Jabr ibn Mu'ammal al-Dayli," is trustworthy; Ahmad declared him trustworthy. He has passed as no. 6240. He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/227, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/164.

This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 8:285, 286, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 4:141, without mentioning anything in it. But al-Dhahabi said in his comment on al-Mustadrak: "I say: It is sound according to the conditions of Muslim." Al-Haythami took it out in Majma' al-Zawa'id, 7:18, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, p. 40, in abridged form, without an isnad.

Ibn Kathir took it out in his Tafsir, 3:230, from the narration of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, and said: "al-Nasa'i narrated it in the Tafsir, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim Sa'iqah, from Hajjaj ibn Minhal."

Al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur, 2:315, and added its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

**Part 2 of 2**

12523. Muhammad ibn Khalaf said: Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Jarmi narrated to us, from Abu Tamilah, from Salam, the client of Hafs ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: "While we were sitting over a drink of ours, [and we were on sand, three or four of us, and we had a large jar of ours,] and we were drinking wine openly, I got up and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to greet him. The prohibition of wine had been revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [idolatrous] sacrifices on stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it⦆ up to the end of the two verses, ﴿So will you not desist?﴾. So I came to my companions and recited it to them up to His saying, ﴿So will you not desist?﴾." He said: "Some of the people had a cup in his hand, having drunk some of it, and some remained in the vessel. He placed the vessel under his upper lip, as a cupper does." Then they poured out what was in their jars and said: "We have desisted, our Lord! We have desisted, our Lord!"

[Narration 12523: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Ammar al-'Asqalani, the teacher of al-Tabari, has passed under no. 126 and no. 6534.
Sa'id ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Jarmi: a Kufan, trustworthy (thiqah). Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from him. Abu Zur'ah said: "I discussed hadiths with Ahmad about him, and he recognized him," and he said: "Sadduq (truthful), and he used to seek hadith with us." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/471, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/59.
And "Abu Tamilah" is Yahya ibn Wadih al-Ansari, who has passed many times, the last under no. 9009.
And "Salam, client of Hafs, Abu al-Qasim al-Laythi," a Marwazi, is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/134, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/262. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir: "He heard Abdullah ibn Buraydah from his father: it was revealed concerning the prohibition of wine," and Sa'id al-Jarmi said: "He heard Yahya ibn Wadih, he heard Salam," an indication of this report. Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him. The editor of Ibn Abi Hatim's al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil said: "In al-Thiqat: Salam al-Laythi, the father of Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam." In the printed edition here it read "client of Hafs ibn Abi Qays," and I do not know how he permitted himself to change what was correct in the manuscript into an error we cannot identify.
And "Ibn Buraydah" is Abdullah ibn Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, judge of Marw. His brother Sulayman ibn Buraydah was his twin. He narrated from his father, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Amr, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and others of the Companions. Ahmad ibn Hanbal spoke about him. Al-Jawzajani said: "I said to Abu Abdullah: Did Abdullah hear anything from his father? He said: I do not know; most of what is narrated from Buraydah is from him," and he weakened his narration. Ibn Ma'in and Abu Hatim declared him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/13. In the printed edition it read "Abi Buraydah," which is a pure error; its correct form is in the manuscript.
And his father, "Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami," was an early Companion who embraced Islam before Badr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed him over the alms of his people.
Ibn Kathir mentioned this report in his Tafsir 3:230, from the narration of Abu Ja'far, and in it is "from Abu Buraydah," the error of the printed edition. Also al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:315.
The addition between the brackets is from the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, which did not transmit this from anyone other than al-Tabari, so I added it; and it appears that it fell out from the copyist of our manuscript, although al-Suyuti mentioned the report without this addition.
As for his saying, "we were on sand," meaning: on fertile, lush sand. "Al-Batiyah" is the jar of wine, a large vessel of glass, filled with drink and placed among the drinkers, from which they ladle and drink. As for his saying, "he spoke of the vessel," meaning: he tilted it and then withdrew it, like the cupper who removes the cupping glass.]

* *

Others said: The enmity and hatred that occurred among those concerning whom this verse was revealed was caused by gambling, not by the intoxication that came to them from drinking wine. Therefore Allah forbade them from gambling.

Those who said this:

12524. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us. Bishr said: "I have heard it from Yazid, and he narrated it to me." He said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: "A man in the Jahiliyyah would gamble away his family and his wealth, and he would sit, plundered and despoiled, looking at his wealth in the hands of others. [In the printed edition: "ḥazīnan salīban" (grieved and despoiled), but in the manuscript it is undotted, and the correct reading is what I have established: "ḥaraba al-rajulu māluhu, fa-huwa maḥrūb wa ḥarīb," meaning: when his property which he lived by is taken and he is left with nothing.] So this produced enmity and hatred among them, and Allah forbade that and made it precedent." And Allah knows best what suits His creation.

[Narration 12524: Jami' ibn Hammad, see what I noted on the narration no. 12344.
I recall that this narration had passed earlier, but its place escaped me.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter, in our view, is to say that Allah the Exalted has named these things mentioned in this verse "defilement," and commanded that they be avoided.

The interpreters have differed concerning the cause for which this verse was revealed. It is permissible that its revelation was due to the supplication of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the matter of wine; and it is permissible that it was due to what befell Sa'd from the Ansar when they were intoxicated with drink; and it is permissible that it was due to what would befall one of them when he lost his wealth to gambling, of enmity from the one who despoiled him and hatred for him. [""Yasarahu" means: he overcame him in gambling and took his wealth. Al-Zamakhshari said: "From the figurative usage: they despoiled him (asarūhu) and took his wealth (yasarū mālahu). And the desires (tayāsarat al-ahwā') seized his heart," Dhu al-Rummah said: "By the separation of camels' litters that seized his heart, and the staff's rebellion, from the swift separation, a striker..." This expression, as Abu Ja'far used it, the lexicographers have not specified, but al-Zamakhshari's statement indicates its correctness, just as they said from "qimār" (gambling): "qamarahu" (he gambled him).] But we do not hold that any of these causes is a decisive excuse. Nevertheless, whichever of these it was, the ruling of the verse has become binding on all those who are responsible (ahl al-taklīf), and ignorance of the cause for which this verse was revealed does not harm them. Thus, intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous sacrifices on stone altars, and divining arrows are defilement from the work of Satan, and it is obligatory upon everyone who has received the verse to avoid all of that, as He the Exalted said: ﴿So avoid it that you may be successful⦆.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 92:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware. But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, wine, gambling, the stone altars, and the divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it" [and] "obey Allah and obey the Messenger" in your avoidance of that and your following of His command regarding what He has commanded you concerning refraining from what He has forbidden you of these matters which He has explained to you in this verse and others. Oppose Satan in his command to you to disobey Allah in that and in other matters, for he only seeks to bring about enmity and hatred among you through wine and gambling.

"And beware": he says, fear Allah and be watchful of Him, lest He see you doing what He has forbidden you of these matters which He has prohibited for you in this verse and others, or lose you when He has commanded you, so that you destroy and ruin yourselves. "But if you turn away": he says, if you do not act upon what We have commanded you and refrain from what We have forbidden you, and you turn back in retreat from what you are upon of faith and belief in Allah and His Messenger, and following what your Prophet brought you [[See the explanation of "al-tawalli" (turning away) above: 393, note 1, and the references there.]] "then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance": he says, know that upon the one whom We have sent to you with warning there is nothing but conveying to you the message with which he was sent to you, [["al-nidhara" (with a kasra on the nun). The author of al-Qamus said: "al-nadhir: al-indhar, like al-nadhara, with a kasra. And this is from Imam al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him." See al-Shafi'i's Risala, p. 14, paragraph 35, and the note of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad upon it.]] making it clear to you with a clarity that shows you the path of truth and the way you were commanded to follow. [[See the explanation of "mubin" (clear) above: 9: 428, note 1, and the references there.]] As for punishment for turning away and for taking vengeance through disobedience, it falls upon the one to whom the messenger was sent, not upon the messengers.

This is a threat from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever turns away from His command and prohibition. He, exalted is His mention, says to them: If you turn away from My command and My prohibition, then expect My punishment and beware of My wrath.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 93:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate, when they fear God, believe, and do righteous deeds, then fear God and believe, then fear God and do good; and God loves the good-doers﴾ (93).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to the people who said, when God revealed the prohibition of wine with His saying, "Wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are only an abomination of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it" (5:90): "What of those of our brothers who died while drinking it? What of us, when we used to drink it?" God, exalted is His remembrance, says: There is no blame on those of you who believe and do righteous deeds for what they drank of that, in the state in which God had not forbidden it to them [[See the explanation of "al-junah" (blame) in vol. 9, p. 268, note 4, and the references there. And the explanation of "ta'ima" (ate) in what has preceded, vol. 5, p. 342.]] = "when they fear God, believe, and do righteous deeds." He says: when those of them who were alive feared God and were mindful of Him in abstaining from what He had forbidden them, and affirmed God and His Messenger in what they commanded and forbade them, obeying them in all of that = "and do righteous deeds," he says: and acquired of the deeds what God is pleased with in that, from what their Lord imposed on them through that obligation [[See the explanation of "al-salihat" (righteous deeds) in what has preceded in the language indexes (root ṣ-l-ḥ).]] = "then fear God and believe," he says: then they feared God and were mindful of Him by abstaining from His prohibitions after that imposition too, so they remained steadfast in guarding against God in that and in faith in Him, and did not alter or change. = "then fear God and do good," he says: then they feared God, and their fear of God led them to goodness (iḥsan). That "goodness" is acting by what He did not make obligatory upon them of deeds, but rather supererogatory acts by which they drew near to their Lord, seeking His pleasure and fleeing His punishment [[See the explanation of "al-ihsan" (goodness) in what has preceded: vol. 5, p. 512, note 1, and the references there.]] = "and God loves the good-doers," he says: and God loves those who draw near to Him by supererogatory deeds that He is pleased with.

So the first guarding (ittiqa') is guarding by receiving God's command with acceptance and affirmation, and submitting to it and acting by it; the second guarding is guarding by steadfastness in affirmation and abandoning alteration and change; and the third guarding is guarding by goodness and drawing near by supererogatory deeds.

* *

If someone says: What is the evidence that the third "guarding" is guarding by supererogatory deeds, and not by obligatory ones?

It is said: He, exalted is His remembrance, has informed of the lifting of blame from those who drank the wine they drank before its prohibition, if they feared God in drinking it after its prohibition, affirmed God and His Messenger in its prohibition, and did the righteous deeds of obligation. There is no point in repeating that, since it has been mentioned in a single verse.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said, that this verse was revealed concerning what we have mentioned it was revealed about, reports have come from the Companions and the Successors.

Mention of those who said that:

12525 - Hannad ibn al-Sari and Abu Kurayb related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us; and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the prohibition of wine was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of God, what of our companions who died while drinking wine?" Then it was revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds," [the verse]. [[The two reports: 12525 and 12526 — their chain of transmission is sound (sahih).

It was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad: 2088, 2452, 2691 in full, 2775.

Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it in his Sunan (Book of Tafsir) and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith" (good, sound).

Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 4: 143 and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him, saying: "Sahih."

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 3: 233, from Ahmad's Musnad.

al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 320, adding its attribution to al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

12526 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Isra'il with his chain, similarly.

12527 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Kabir ibn 'Abd al-Majid related to me, saying: 'Abbad ibn Rashid informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talhah, Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Suhayl ibn Bayda', and Abu Dujanah, until their heads were inclined from a mixture of unripe and ripe dates. ["Al-busr" (with a dammed b and sukun on s): dates before they soften; it is what has begun to color but has not ripened, and when it ripens it is rutab.]] We heard a crier calling: "Verily, wine has been forbidden!" He said: No one entered upon us and no one left us, until we poured out the drink and broke the jars. ["Al-qilal" is the plural of "qullah" (with a dammed q): the large jar.] Some of us performed ablution, and some bathed, and we applied the perfume of Umm Sulaym, then we went out to the mosque, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was reciting: "O you who believe, wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are only an abomination of Satan's handiwork, so avoid it that you may prosper" [5:90], until his saying: "So will you not desist?" [5:91]. A man said: "O Messenger of God, what is the status of those of us who died while drinking it?" So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate" [the verse]. A man said to Qatadah: "Did you hear it from Anas ibn Malik?" He said: "Yes!" A man said to Anas ibn Malik: "Did you hear it from the Messenger of God ﷺ?" He said: "Yes! And one who does not lie related it to me; by God, we did not lie, nor did we know what lying was!" [[The report 12527: 'Abd al-Kabir ibn 'Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi al-Basri is trustworthy (thiqah). Previously numbered 6822, 10317.

'Abbad ibn Rashid al-Tamimi: Ahmad said: "Trustworthy, truthful." Yahya ibn Ma'in weakened him, and Yahya al-Qattan abandoned him. Al-Bukhari related from him in conjunction with others. Previously numbered 11060.

Umm Sulaym mentioned in the report is Umm Sulaym bint Milhan al-Ansariyyah; she had companionship (sahabiyyah). She was the mother of Anas ibn Malik and the wife of Abu Talhah al-Ansari. Abu Talhah proposed to her while he was a polytheist, and she refused unless he embraced Islam, so he did.

Ibn Kathir mentioned this report in his Tafsir 3: 228, attributing it to no one but Ibn Jarir; likewise al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 320.

This report of Anas was transmitted by al-Bukhari through another route with different wording (Fath 8: 209). Muslim transmitted it in his Sahih with different wording through several routes, 13: 148-151. And al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 8: 287, 288.]]

12528 - Hannad related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When wine was prohibited, they said: "What of our companions who died while drinking wine?" Then it was revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate," [the verse]. [[The two reports 12528 and 12529: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi transmitted it in his Musnad: 97, no. 715, through the route of Shu'bah, with the same chain.

Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it in his Sunan (Book of Tafsir) through the route of 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq (Abu Ja'far's route no. 12528), and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Then he transmitted it through the route of "Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah" (Abu Ja'far's route no. 12529), then said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

Ibn Kathir took it out in his Tafsir 3: 231, from the Musnad of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi.

al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 320, adding its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

12529 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: al-Bara' said: Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ died while drinking wine. When its prohibition was revealed, some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "What of our companions who died while drinking it?" Then this verse was revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds," [the verse]. [[The two reports 12528 and 12529 are the same as the note above; see the note under 12528.]]

12530 - Hannad related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate" was revealed concerning those who were killed at Badr and Uhud with Muhammad ﷺ.

12531 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Mushir related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: When "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate" was revealed, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "It was said to me: You are among them." [[The report 12531: Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatwani is trustworthy; previously numbered 2206, 4577, 8166, 8397.

'Ali ibn Mushir al-Qurashi is trustworthy; previously numbered 4453, 5777.

This report was transmitted by Muslim in his Sahih (16: 14) through several routes, from 'Ali ibn Mushir, from al-A'mash, with its like.

Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it through the route of Sufyan ibn Waki', from Khalid ibn Makhlad, and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 4: 143, 144, through the route of Sulayman ibn Qarm, from al-A'mash, with an addition in its wording, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two did not record it; they only agreed on the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', an abridged version of this meaning." I did not find the hadith of al-Bara' in the two Sahihs, as al-Hakim said. As for al-Dhahabi, he added nothing in his comment on the Mustadrak except to say: "Sahih." I did not find anyone who attributed the hadith of al-Bara' to the two Shaykhs (Bukhari and Muslim), which is the one that passed as 12528 and 12529. It was taken out by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 18, with the same wording as al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, then he said: "Part of it is in the Sahih; al-Tabarani transmitted it, and its narrators are trustworthy." This is the correct view, not what al-Hakim said.

Ibn Kathir took it out in his Tafsir 3: 233 and said: "Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i transmitted it through his route."

al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 321, in two places. He said, with wording like al-Hakim's: "al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim took it out and graded it sound." Then he transmitted it abridged like Abu Ja'far's report, and attributed it to Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

12532 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate," [up to] His saying: "and God loves the good-doers," when God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed the prohibition of wine in "Surat al-Ma'idah," after "Surat al-Ahzab," [[His saying "after Surat al-Ahzab" apparently means after the revelation of Surat al-Ahzab, but there is no mention of the prohibition of wine in Surat al-Ahzab. He apparently meant "after the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Ahzab)." I fear that his saying "Surat al-Ahzab" is an error of the copyist, and the correct reading is "Ghazwat al-Ahzab." But it came thus in al-Durr al-Manthur too, 2: 321, and the report is attributed to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir.]] some men among the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "So-and-so was struck down at Badr, and so-and-so at Uhud, and they were drinking it! We testify that they are among the people of Paradise!" So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate when they fear God, believe and do righteous deeds, then fear God and believe, then fear God and do good, and God loves the good-doers," meaning: the people drank it in fear of God and goodness, and it was lawful for them at that time; then it was prohibited after them, so there is no blame on them for that.

12533 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate." They said: "O Messenger of God, what shall we say of our brothers who passed away? They used to drink wine and eat gambling!" So God revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate," meaning before the prohibition, "when they fear God and do good," after it was prohibited, and that is His saying: "Whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what has passed" [2:275]. [[The Arabic here is: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate" of the forbidden thing before it was forbidden to them.]]

12534 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate," meaning by that men from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who died while drinking wine before wine was prohibited, so there was no blame on them for it before it was prohibited. When it was prohibited, they said: "How can it be forbidden to us, when our brothers died while drinking it?" So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate when they fear God, believe and do righteous deeds," meaning: there is no sin on them for what they used to drink before I prohibited it, if they were good-doers and God-fearing; "and God loves the good-doers."

12535 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they ate," [applying] to those who used to drink wine among those killed with Muhammad ﷺ at Badr and Uhud.

12536 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: "There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds," [the verse]: this is about the matter of wine when it was prohibited. They asked the Prophet of God ﷺ and said: "Our brothers who died while drinking it?" So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed this verse.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game﴾, meaning: Allah will try you ﴿with something of the game﴾, meaning: with some of the game. [[See the discussion of "bala" (to test) above: 389, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

He, the Exalted, informed them that He would test them with "something" because He did not test them with the game of the sea; rather, He tested them with the game of the land. So the test is with some, not with all. [[In the printed edition: "fal-ibtila' bi-ba'd lam yamtani'" ("so the test with some was not prevented"), which is meaningless. In the manuscript: "fal-ibtila' bi-ba'd la yakhsha'" ("so the test with some does not humble"), where the scribe erred in the writing and the editor erred in the handling. The correct wording is what I have established, because Abu Ja'far intended to say that His saying "with something of the game" refers to the game of the land specifically, not the game of the sea, and that the prohibition did not cover all game. This is quite clear in what follows in the explanation of these verses. Thus what I have established from the manuscript, despite its poor writing, is correct.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿that your hands can reach﴾, it means either by the hand, such as eggs and chicks, or by striking with arrows and lances, such as donkeys, cattle and gazelles, and He tests you with it while you are in the state of ihram for your 'umrah or your Hajj.

* *

Similar to this was said by a group of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

12537 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Warqa' informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach﴾, he said: "Your hands" refers to the small game, taking chicks and eggs; "lances" he said refers to the large game.

12538 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Dawud, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

12539 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿that your hands and your lances can reach﴾, he said: The arrows; "your lances" reach the large game, and "your hands" reach the small game, taking the chick and the egg.

12540 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach﴾, he said: That which cannot escape.

12541 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, similarly.

12542 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿your hands and your lances﴾, he said: It is the weak of the game and its small ones; Allah, the Exalted, tests His servants with it in their ihram, so that if they wished they could reach it with their hands. Then Allah forbade them to approach it.

12543 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, and Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and your lances can reach﴾, he said: The chicks and the eggs, and that which cannot escape.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿That Allah may know who fears Him in the unseen. And whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment﴾ (94)

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, means: Allah will test you, O believers, with some of the game while you are in the state of ihram, so that He may know the people of obedience to Allah and faith in Him, those who keep to His limits and His command and prohibition, and who among them fears Allah so that he avoids what He has forbidden and refrains from it out of fear of His punishment, ﴿in the unseen﴾, meaning: in this world, such that He does not see him. [[Abu Ja'far means: such that the punishment is not seen directly in this world, as it is seen directly in the Hereafter.]]

* *

We have already explained that "al-ghayb" (the unseen) is the verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "This matter has become hidden from me, so it is hidden, a hiding (ghayban wa-ghaybah)," and that what is not witnessed, the Arabs call "ghayb."

* *

The meaning of the statement, then, is: That the friends of Allah may know who fears Allah, so that he avoids His prohibitions which He has forbidden him, of game and other things, in a way that He does not see him and does not witness him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And whoever transgresses after that﴾, it means: whoever exceeds the limit of Allah which He has set for him, after being tested with the prohibition of game upon him while he is in ihram, so he makes lawful what Allah has forbidden him of it, by taking it and killing it, ﴿then he will have a punishment from Allah, painful﴾, meaning: painful and afflicting.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 95 (part 1 of 7):

The explanation of His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram. And whoever kills it intentionally among you — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, "do not kill game" which I have made clear to you, which is the game of the land rather than the game of the sea, "while you are in the state of ihram" — he says: while you are in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah.
* *
The word "ḥurum" is the plural of "ḥarām," and the masculine and feminine are expressed in it with one form. You say: "This is a man who is ḥarām" and "This is a woman who is ḥarām." When it is said "muḥrim," the feminine is "muḥrimah." And "iḥrām" (the state of ihram) is entering into it. It is said: "aḥram al-qawm" (the people entered ihram) when they entered the sacred month (al-shahr al-ḥarām) or the sacred precinct (al-ḥaram).
* *
So the meaning of the statement is: Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah.
* *
As for His words: "And whoever kills it intentionally among you," this is an announcement from Allah, Exalted is He, to His servants of the ruling on the one in ihram who kills game, which He forbade him to kill intentionally. [See the explanation of "intentionally" (al-ta'ammud) above, 9:57.]
* *
Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the nature of the "intent" (al-'amd) which Allah made the one who has it liable for expiation and compensation for killing game.
Some of them said: It is intent to kill game, along with the slayer forgetting his ihram at the time of killing. And he said: If he kills it while remembering his ihram, intending to kill it, then there is no ruling upon him, and his matter is left to Allah.
They said: This matter is too grand for a ruling to be issued concerning it, or for it to have an expiation.
Mention of those who said that:
