12544 - Sufyan ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And whoever kills it intentionally among you — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock." Whoever kills it among you forgetting his ihram, intending to kill it, that is the one upon whom a ruling is issued. But if he kills it remembering its sanctity, intending to kill it, no ruling is issued upon him.
12545 - Ibn WakI' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning one who kills game intentionally while knowing he is in ihram and intending to kill it, he said: No ruling is issued upon him, and he has no hajj. And His words: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," he said: it is the intent which makes expiation obligatory, and in it is expiation; and the error is that he strikes it while forgetting his ihram intending to kill it, or he strikes it while intending something else. This is the one upon whom a ruling is issued once. [His words "once" mean one time; if he returns, no ruling is issued upon him, and whoever returns, Allah will take vengeance on him.]
12546 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram, and whoever kills it among you intentionally," not forgetting his ihram nor intending something else, then he has been released, and he has no concession. And whoever kills it forgetting, or intends something else and errs with it, that is the intent which is expiated.
12547 - Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," he said: intending to kill it, forgetting his ihram.
12548 - Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, saying: al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: The intentional act is the expiated error.
12549 - al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Layth narrated to us, saying: Mujahid said: The saying of Allah: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock." He said: So the intent which Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, mentioned is: that he strikes game while intending something else, and so he strikes it. This is the expiated intent. As for one who strikes it neither forgetting nor intending something else, this one is not ruled upon. This matter is too grand for a ruling to be issued upon it. [The report 12549: "Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Baghdadi," the memorizer, passed under number 5090.]
12550 - Ibn WakI' and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Haytham, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: that he said concerning this verse: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," he said: he kills it intentionally, intending to kill it, forgetting his ihram.
12551 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Haytham, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.
12552 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," not forgetting his ihram nor intending something else, then he has been released, and he has no concession. And whoever kills it forgetting his ihram, or intends something else and errs with it, that is the expiated intent.
12553 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from 'Amr, from al-Hasan: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," for game, forgetting his ihram — "then whoever transgresses after that," intentionally for game while remembering his ihram. [The report 12553: "Sahl ibn Yusuf al-Anmati" passed in a similar chain under number 10648.]
12554 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan used to issue fatwa concerning one who kills game intentionally while remembering his ihram: no ruling is issued upon him. Isma'il said: Hammad also said, from Ibrahim, the like of that.
12555 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah instructed me to ask 'Amr ibn Dinar about this verse: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock," the verse. So I asked him, and he said: 'Ata' used to say: he has the option, whichever he wishes to do: if he wishes he gives a sacrificial animal, and if he wishes he feeds, and if he wishes he fasts. So I informed Ja'far and said: What did you hear about it? He hesitated for a moment, then began to laugh and did not inform me. Then he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr used to say: a ruling is issued upon him of livestock, a sacrificial animal (hadyan) reaching the Ka'bah. And the feeding and fasting are only expiation [kaffarah]. If he does not find it, a ruling is issued upon him for its value, and he feeds the poor with it, and gives it in charity. If he does not find that, a ruling is issued upon him for fasting for three days to ten. [In the printed edition: "... a sacrificial animal reaching the Ka'bah, and if he does not find it, a ruling is issued upon him for its value, so he estimates food and gives it in charity, and if he does not find it, a ruling is issued upon him for fasting three to ten days," which differs entirely from what is in the manuscript. What is in the manuscript is what I have recorded; I added the words between the brackets as an inference from the context of the verse so the statement is consistent. His words "this does not reach the value of the sacrificial animal" seem to mean feeding the poor. The sentence after that needs careful reflection, and I did not find the report in any place other than this one.] And fasting is for three days to ten.
12556 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, saying: Mujahid said: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," not forgetting his ihram, nor intending something else, then he has been released, and he has no concession. And whoever kills it forgetting, or intends something else and errs with it, that is the expiated intent.
12557 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: As for one who intends game while forgetting his ihram, or ignorant that killing it is not forbidden, these are the ones upon whom a ruling is issued. But as for one who kills it intentionally after Allah's prohibition, while knowing that he is in ihram and that it is forbidden, that is left to the vengeance of Allah, and this is the one upon whom Allah has placed vengeance.
12558 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid concerning His words: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally," he said: intending to kill it, forgetting his ihram.
* *
Others said: Rather, that is the intent of the one in ihram to kill game, remembering his ihram.
Mention of those who said that:
12559 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us = from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: a ruling is issued upon him in intent, error, and forgetting.
12560 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us = and 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Tawus said: By Allah, Allah did not say anything but "And whoever kills it among you intentionally."
12561 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: some of our companions informed me, from al-Zuhri, that he said: The Qur'an was revealed with the intentional case, and the Sunnah established the ruling for error = meaning: the one in ihram who strikes game.
12562 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: "O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram," he said: If he kills it intentionally or forgetfully, a ruling is issued upon him. And if he returns intentionally, the punishment is hastened for him, unless Allah pardons.
12563 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Expiation was prescribed only for intentional acts, but it was made severe for them in error so that they would be mindful.
12564 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, both saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.
12565 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: Tawus used to say: By Allah, Allah did not say anything but "And whoever kills it among you intentionally."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is to say: Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, forbade the killing of land game for every one in ihram during the state of ihram as long as he is in ihram, by His words: "O you who have believed, do not kill game." Then He explained the ruling for one who kills some of that in the state of ihram intentionally, and He did not restrict it to the one who intentionally kills it while forgetting his ihram, nor to the one who errs in killing it while remembering his ihram. Rather, in the revelation He made it general in imposing compensation on every slayer of game in the state of ihram who does so intentionally. [Context: "Rather it is general ... every slayer of game": "kull" is the object of "'amma".] It is not permissible to turn the apparent meaning of the revelation to an inner interpretation for which there is no indication from the text of the Book, nor a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor a consensus of the Community, nor an indication from any of these aspects.
Since that is so, whether the slayer of game among those in ihram kills it intentionally while remembering his ihram, or intentionally kills it while forgetting his ihram, or intends something else and kills it while remembering his ihram — all of them are equal in that upon all of them is the compensation that our Lord, Exalted is His remembrance, mentioned, which is: the like of what he killed from the livestock, judged by two just men from among the Muslims, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or expiation of feeding the poor, or the equivalent of that in fasting.
* *
This is the view of 'Ata' and al-Zuhri which we have mentioned from them, [meaning reports 12559 and 12561], apart from the view which Mujahid stated [meaning reports 12544–12551 and 12556, 12558].
As for what is required for one who kills by error, we have explained the view on it in our book: ﴿A Gentle Book on the Rulings of the Sharia﴾, with what suffices from mentioning it in this place. This place is not the place for mentioning it, because our aim in this book is to clarify the interpretation of the revelation, and there is no mention of error in the revelation, so we mention its rulings.
* *
As for His words: "then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock," He means: and upon him is a counterpart (kifa') and a substitute (badal) [in the printed edition: "expiation and substitute," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. "Kifa' al-shay'" (with a kasra on the kaf) means its like and equivalent, from the saying: "kafa'ahu 'ala al-shay' mukafa'atan wa-kifa'an," meaning he repaid him for it], meaning by that: the compensation for the game killed. He, Exalted is His remembrance, says: upon the slayer of game is the compensation of the game killed, the like of what he killed from the livestock. [See the explanation of "al-jaza'" (compensation) above, 2:27, 28, 314; 6:576; 7:2279; 57.]
* *
It has been mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is: ﴿فَجَزَاؤُهُ مِثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾ ("then his compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock").
* *
The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this.
The common reciters of Medina and some of the Basrans recited it: ﴿فَجَزَاءُ مِثْلِ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾, with "al-jaza'" annexed to "al-mithl" and "al-mithl" in the genitive (khafd).
* *
The common reciters of Kufa recited it: ﴿فجزاء مثل ما قتل﴾ with "al-jaza'" indefinite (tanwin) and "al-mithl" in the nominative (raf'), interpreting: upon him is a compensation which is the like of what he killed.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recites: ﴿فجزاء مثل ما قتل﴾ with "al-jaza'" indefinite and "al-mithl" in the nominative, because the compensation is the like, so there is no sense in annexing a thing to itself.
I think that those who recited it with annexation saw that what is obligatory upon the slayer of game is that he repay its like from game with a like from livestock. That is not what they took it to mean; rather, what is obligatory upon its slayer is that he repay the killed animal with its counterpart from livestock. Since that is so, "al-mithl" is the compensation which Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, imposed upon the slayer of game, and a thing cannot be annexed to itself. [In the printed edition: "and a thing will not be annexed ..." which is not good; in the manuscript: "fa-inna yudaf," and I preferred that its correct form is what I recorded.]
For this reason no reciter whom we know has recited it with tanwin on "al-jaza'" and naṣb on "al-mithl." [Rather, Abu al-Fath Ibn Jinni transmitted this in his book "al-Muhtasab" and attributed it to Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Sulami, as I think. Ibn Khalawayh also mentioned it in "Shawadhdh al-Qira'at," p. 34, and attributed it to Muhammad ibn Muqatil, though in the printed text it reads "fa-jaza' mith," with "jaza'" in the accusative, and the correct reading is "mith" in the accusative.] If "al-mithl" were other than "al-jaza'," then naṣb on "al-mithl" would be permissible when "al-jaza'" is indefinite, just as "al-yatim" was put in the accusative when it was other than "al-ita'am" in His words: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger, an orphan of near relationship﴾ [Surah al-Balad: 14, 15], and just as "al-amwat" and "al-ahya'" were put in the accusative and "al-kifat" was made indefinite in His words: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?﴾ [Surah al-Mursalat: 25, 26], since "al-kifat" is other than "al-ahya'" and "al-amwat." Likewise, if "al-jaza'" were other than "al-mithl," the recitation with naṣb on "al-mithl" would be permissible when "al-jaza'" is indefinite. But that was restricted, so no one recited it with tanwin on "al-jaza'" and naṣb on "al-mithl," since "al-mithl" is "al-jaza'," and the meaning of the statement is: whoever kills it among you intentionally, then upon him is a compensation which is the like of what he killed from the livestock. [In the manuscript: "is what he killed from the livestock," and the printed version is correct.]
* *
Then the people of knowledge differed concerning the nature of the "jaza'" and how the slayer of game among those in ihram repays what he killed with its like from livestock. [In the printed edition: "with its like from livestock," and in the manuscript: "like from livestock," so I saw its reading as I have recorded it.]
Some of them said: One looks to the animal most similar to it in form from livestock, and repays it with that, and sends it as an offering to the Ka'bah.
Mention of those who said that:
12566 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning His words: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock." He said: As for "compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock": if he kills an ostrich or a donkey, upon him is a camel (badanah). If he kills a cow, or a stag (ayyil), or an antelope (arwa) [the "ayyil" (with a fatha on the hamza and a shadda on the kasra-ya) is the male of the wild goats (wu'ul). "Arwa" is the female of the wild goats and a collective name for them, its singular being "aruwiyah." Here it is used to mean "aruwiyah"], then upon him is a cow. Or if he kills a gazelle or a hare, upon him is a sheep. And if he kills a lizard, a chameleon, or a jerboa, upon him is a young sheep (sakhlah) which has eaten grass and drunk milk. [The "sakhlah" (with a fatha and then sukun) is the young of a goat or sheep, whether male or female.]
12567 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Ibn Mujahid, who said: Ata' was asked: Is one made to pay for small game as he is made to pay for large game? He said: Does not Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, say: "then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock"? [The report 12567: "Harun ibn al-Mughirah ibn Hakim al-Bajali" passed under numbers 3356 and 5526. As for "Ibn Mujahid," I was unable to determine who he is; the printed text reads "Abi Mujahid," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript, which is likely correct, though I could not establish the first part of his name.]
12568 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally — then compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock," he said: upon him is its like from livestock.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 95 (part 2 of 7):

12569 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle﴾. He said: When the muhrim (one in the state of ihram) kills game, its penalty of cattle becomes due from him. If he finds its penalty, he slaughters it and gives it in charity. If he does not find its penalty, he assesses the penalty in dirhams, then assesses the dirhams as wheat, then fasts one day in place of every half sa' (of food). He said: "Food" is only meant as fasting; so when he finds food, he has found the penalty.

12570 - Ibn Wakic and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle, judged by two just men among you as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting﴾. He said: When the muhrim kills game, its penalty of cattle is judged upon him. If he does not find it, he looks at its price (Ibn Humayd said: he looks at its value), and assesses its price as food, and fasts one day in place of every half sa'. "Or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting." He said: "Food" is only meant as fasting; so when he finds food, he has found its penalty.

12571 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle﴾. If he does not find an offering, the offering is assessed upon him as food, and he fasts for every sa' two days.

12572 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle, judged by two just men among you as an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾. He said: When a man kills game, it is judged upon him. If he does not have it, its price is assessed upon him as food, then he fasts one day for every half sa'.

12573 - Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub narrated to us, both saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr informed us, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: My companion and I raced toward a gazelle at al-Aqabah, and we struck it. We came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. A man beside him turned toward me and they both considered the matter. He said: "Slaughter a ram."
[[The report: 12573 - "Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr ibn Suwayd al-Qurashi," known as al-Qibti and "Ibn al-Qibtiyyah." He saw Ali and Abu Musa. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib.
And "Qabisah ibn Jabir ibn Wahb al-Asadi" narrated from Umar and witnessed his sermon at al-Jabiyah. He is trustworthy, among the jurists of the first generation of the jurists of the people of Kufa after the Companions. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib.
This report of Qabisah ibn Jabir will be narrated by Abu Ja'far through several routes, numbered 12573-12577 and then 12586-15288, with different wordings. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5: 181, through the route of Sufyan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, and through the route of Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Malik.
Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 3: 237, 238, and it is number 12588, from this place in Abu Ja'far's Tafsir, and he indicated some of its routes here. Al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 329 with words similar to number 12588, and attributed it further to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Hakim, saying: "and he authenticated it," but I did not find it in its place in al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim.]]

12574 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Qabisah ibn Jabir informed me, similar to what Abd al-Malik narrated.

12575 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: A companion of mine killed a gazelle while in ihram, so Umar ordered him to slaughter a sheep and give its meat in charity, and to let its hide be given to drink. [[The report: this is an abridgement of report 12588, and the explanation of "yusqa ihabuha" will come in the commentary on it there.]]

12576 - Hannad narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: A man from among the Bedouins, while in ihram, killed a gazelle, so he asked Umar, and Umar said to him: "Offer a sheep." [[The report: this is a mursal report from Umar; Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani did not hear it from Umar. But it is the story of Qabisah ibn Jabir mentioned before.]]

12577 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn; and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Qabisah ibn Jabir said: "I struck a gazelle while I was in ihram, so I came to Umar and asked him about it, and he sent for Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, its matter is easier than that!' He said: So he struck me with the durrah until I outran him on foot!" [["Al-durrah" (with a kasrah on the dal): a short staff carried by the ruler or others to beat with. The durrah of the Commander of the Faithful Umar is the most famous durrah in history.]] He said: Then he said: "You killed game while in ihram, then you belittle the fatwa!" [["Ghamasa al-shay' yaghmisuhu ghamsan": he despised, belittled, and disdained it. That is: do you look down on the fatwa and scorn it?]] He said: Then Abd al-Rahman came, and they ruled a sheep.

12578 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally, then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle﴾. He said: When the muhrim kills some game, a ruling is made upon him concerning it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, then upon him is a sheep slaughtered in Makkah. If he does not find it, then feeding six needy persons. If he does not find it, then fasting three days. If he kills a deer (ayyil) or the like, then upon him is a cow. If he kills an ostrich or a wild ass or the like, then upon him is a camel as a badanah.

12579 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata': "What if I kill game and it turns out to be one-eyed, or lame, or defective; must I compensate with its like?" He said: "Yes, if you wish." I said: "Is a sound one more beloved to you?" He said: "Yes." And Ata' said: "If you kill the young of a gazelle, then upon it is the young of a sheep. And if you kill the young of a wild cow, then upon it is the young of a domestic cow like it; so all of that is according to that."

12580 - I was told, from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman al-Bahili informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: ﴿The penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle﴾: whatever is game of the land that has no horn, the donkey or the ostrich, then upon him is its like of camels. And whatever has a horn of the game of the land, such as the wild goat (wa'l) or the deer (ayyil), its penalty is of cattle. And whatever is of the gazelle, then its like is of sheep. And whatever is of the hare, then in it is a thaniyyah. [["Al-thaniyyah" means a thaniyyah of goats, which is what has entered its second or third year.] And whatever is of the jerboa or the like, in it is a young lamb. And whatever is of a locust or the like, in it is a handful of food. And whatever is of the birds of the land, in it is that it is assessed and its price given in charity, and if he wishes, he fasts one day for every half sa'. If he strikes the young of a wild bird or its egg, its value is food or fasting, according to what applies to the bird. Except that it has been mentioned regarding ostrich eggs, if the muhrim strikes them, that a stallion should be made to mount a number of camels corresponding to the eggs he struck, [["Al-bikarah" (with a kasrah on the ba') is the plural of "bakr" and "bakrah" (with a fathah on the ba'): a young camel, the equivalent of a boy among people.] and what of them becomes pregnant he offers to the House, and what of them is spoiled, there is nothing upon it.

12581 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, saying: Mujahid said: "Whoever kills it" (meaning the game) "forgetfully, or intends something else and misses his aim, that is the expiated intentional act; upon him is its like as an offering reaching the Ka'bah. If he does not find it, he buys food with its price. If he does not find it, he fasts for every mudd one day." And Ata' said: "If a person strikes an ostrich, it is his, if he is of means, widened (for him), he may, if he wishes, offer a she-camel or its equivalent in food or its equivalent in fasting, whichever of them he wishes, because of His saying: 'then the penalty,' or this or that." He said: "So in the Qur'an, every 'or' ('aw') is for the one concerned to choose whatever he wishes from it."

12582 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muslim informed me, who said: Whoever strikes game that reaches the value of a sheep or more, that is what God, may He be remembered, said: "then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle." As for "an expiation of feeding the needy," that is what does not reach the level of an offering; one who kills a sparrow owes nothing for it. He said: "or the equivalent of that in fasting": the equivalent of the ostrich, or the equivalent of the sparrow, or the equivalent of all of that.

* *

Others said: Rather, the killed game is assessed at its value in dirhams, then the killer buys with its value a counterpart of cattle, then offers it to the Ka'bah.

Mention of those who said that:

12583 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abdah informed us, from Ibrahim, who said: Whatever the muhrim strikes of anything, its value is ruled upon it.

12584 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hammad, who said: I heard Ibrahim say: "For every kind of game, its price."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views concerning the interpretation of the verse is what Umar and Ibn Abbas said, and whoever holds their view: that the killed game is recompensed with its like of cattle, as God, may He be remembered, said: "then the penalty is the like of what he killed of the cattle." It is not permissible that the like of the killed game be dirhams, since God said: "of the cattle," for dirhams are not of the cattle in any way.

* *

If someone says: Even if dirhams are not a like of the killed game, one buys with them the like of cattle and the killer offers it, so by that act he is recompensing with a like of cattle what he killed of game!

It is said to him: Tell me, if the killed game was young, or defective, and with its value one cannot obtain from cattle anything except one that is large, or sound [or defective, and it is not compensated by its value in cattle except...] — are you permitted to buy with its value something other than it, and other than its description, and offer it, or is that not permitted for him, while he is permitted only its like? If he claims that he is not permitted to buy with its value except its like, he abandons his statement on that, because the people of this view claim that he is not permitted to buy with its value and offer it, except what is permissible in sacrifices. And if he permits buying the like of the killed game with its value and offering it, while the killed game may be young and defective, he has permitted in the offering what is not permitted in the sacrificial animals.

And if he claims that it is not permitted to buy with its value and offer it except what is permitted in sacrifices, he makes clearer, by that, a contradiction of the apparent sense of the revelation. That is because God, may He be remembered, obligated upon the killer of game among the muhrimun, intentionally, the like of cattle if he finds it, and the claimant of this view has claimed that the like of cattle is not obligatory upon him, while he is able to it.

It is said to the one who says that: Tell me, if another speaker says: "Upon the killer of game whose value does not reach what one could obtain of cattle that is permissible in sacrifices, there is no feeding or fasting" — because God only gave the killer of game among the muhrimun a choice among the three things He named in His Book; so if he has no way to any one of them, the obligation of the other two falls from him, because the choice was only his, and he has a way to the three. But if he has no way to some of that, the obligation of recompense is void for him, because he is not among those intended by the verse — analogous to what you yourself said: "If the killed game's value does not reach what one could obtain of cattle permissible in sacrifices, then the obligation of recompense with the like of cattle has fallen from him, and upon him is only recompense by feeding or fasting" — is there between you and him any difference in principle or analogy? He will say nothing about one of them except that it binds him regarding the other in the same way.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿judged by it two just men among you as an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may He be remembered, says: the recompense that is the like of the killed game of cattle is judged by two just men among you, meaning: two learned jurists from the people of religion and virtue [see the explanation of "just" above, 6: 51, 60] — "as an offering": that is, they judge the recompense, two just men, so that it is offered and reaches the Ka'bah. [In the printed edition: "that he offers," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.] The "hu" in His words "judged by it" refers to "the recompense." [See the explanation of "the offering" above, 4: 34, 35 / 9: 466.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The manner of the judgment of the two just men, when they wish to rule upon the killer the like of the killed game from cattle, is that they look at the killed game and ask for its description; if he mentions that he struck a young gazelle, they rule upon him from the young of sheep, of the same kind as what he killed in age and body. If what he struck was large, they rule upon him from the sheep something large. If what he struck was a wild ass, they rule upon him a cow, if what he struck was a large cow, then a large one, and if it was small, then a small one. If the killed game was male, its like is from the male cattle; if it was female, its like is a female of cattle. Then likewise they look at what is most similar in kind to the killed game among cattle, and rule upon him by it, as God, may He be remembered, said.

* *

In agreement with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them.

Mention of those who said in the manner we have said:

12585 - Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: Two men from among the Bedouins were in ihram; one of them startled a gazelle, and the other killed it. [In the printed edition: "fa-ajash" with a jim, which is an error; in the manuscript it is unpointed. "Hasha al-sayd hawshan wa-hiyashan" and "ahashahu" and "ahwashahu" and "hashtu 'alayhi al-sayd" and "ahashtahu": when you frighten it toward him and take it from around him so as to direct it to the snare, then drive it toward him and gather it upon him.] They came to Umar, and with him was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Umar said to him: [In the manuscript, in both places: "Amr," which is a pure error; in the printed edition, in the latter of them, "Amr," which is an error.] "And what do you see?" He said: "A sheep." He said: "I also see that. Go and offer a sheep." When the two had departed, one of them said to his companion: "The Commander of the Faithful did not know what to say until he asked his companion!" Umar heard them, so he called them back and said: "Do you two recite Surat al-Ma'idah?" They said: "No!" So he recited it to them: "judged by it two just men among you," then he said: "You have sought help from this companion of mine."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 95 (part 3 of 7):

12586 - Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub related to us, both saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr informed us, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: I and a companion of mine raced after a gazelle on the mountain pass, and we hit it. So I came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. He turned to a man beside him, and they both considered the matter. He said: Slaughter a ram— Ya'qub said in his narration: He said to me: Slaughter a sheep. So I departed and came to my companion and said: "The Commander of the Faithful did not know what he was saying!" My companion said: "Sacrifice your she-camel." Umar ibn al-Khattab heard it, so he turned to me and struck me with the whip (durrah), and said: "You kill game while you are in the state of ihram, and you belittle the verdict! [See the explanation of "ghamasa al-futya" above, p. 17, note 4.] Indeed, Allah the Exalted says in His Book: ﴿judged by two just men among you﴾. This is Ibn Awf, and I am Umar!" [Report 12586 – see the commentary on the earlier report no. 12573.]

12587 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Qabisah ibn Jabir informed me, with something similar to what Abd al-Malik related.

12588 - Hannad and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Qabisah ibn Jabir, who said: We set out as pilgrims [in the printed edition and manuscript: "we set out" without "pilgrims", but Ibn Kathir transmitted it from this place and it reads "hujjaj" there, and likewise in the narration of al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 5:181. So the word "hujjaj" had been dropped by the copyist, and therefore I have restored it.] So when we prayed the dawn prayer, we would mount our riding-beasts and walk along, talking. He said: Then one morning, while we were so, a gazelle appeared to us, coming from the left, or from the right. [A gazelle that "sanaha" comes to you from your left, and one that "baraha" comes to you from your right.] A man among us threw a stone at it, and he did not miss its khusha' [in the printed edition: "khushshaa'", and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is with a damma on the kha' and a shadda on the shin with a fatha; both are correct and the report is transmitted with both. "Al-khasha'" and "al-khusha'" are the thin bone, bare of hair, protruding behind the ear.] So it fell dead on its side [in the printed edition: "fa-rakiba wa-wad'ahu mayyitan", which is utterly corrupt. In the manuscript: "fa-rakiba wa-da'ahu mayyitan", which is a scribal error; the correct reading is what I have given. It is said of a slain animal: "rakiba radi'ahu" when it falls on its face in its blood. Its "rakhb" (lying upon it) means that the blood flows and it falls upon it prostrate. The root of "radi'" is what a thing is smeared with, of saffron or other, and it is its trace and color.] He said: We regarded it as a great matter. When we reached Makkah, I went out with him until we came to Umar, and he related the story to him. He said: And beside him was a man whose face was like a silver bracelet [al-qalb (with a damma and sukun): a bracelet consisting of a single piece, i.e., a single strand. In the hadith: "that Fatimah adorned al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, with two silver bracelets (qalbayn)." The description of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with him, in Tabaqat ibn Sa'd 3/1/94: "He was a tall man, of handsome face, fine skin, broad-chested (fayh: a slight curvature in the back or neck), fair, tinged with redness; he did not dye his beard or his hair."] = meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf = so he turned to his companion and spoke to him. He said: Then the man turned to me and said: "Did you kill it intentionally or by mistake?" The man said: "I intentionally threw at it, but I did not intend to kill it." Umar said: "I see you have combined intention and error. Go to a sheep and slaughter it, give its meat in charity, and give its hide [as a gift]." [His saying "asqi ihaba-ha" means: give its hide to someone who will tan it and make a waterskin from it. The "siqa'" is a container of water made of leather. The "ihab" is the hide of cattle, sheep, and wild animals that has not been tanned.] He said: So we rose from his presence, and I said: "Sir, honor the rites of Allah!" [In the manuscript: "a'zam sha'a'ir Allah", but what is in the printed edition agrees with al-Bayhaqi's Sunan, and it is preferable, since it matches the verse of Surat al-Hajj: "That, and whoever honors the rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts."] "The Commander of the Faithful did not know what to rule for you until he asked his companion! Go to your she-camel and slaughter it." He did so. [In the printed edition: "fa-ff'ala dhalika", but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. Ibn Kathir says: "Perhaps that is the recompense for the like of what you killed of game." And in Ibn Kathir: "meaning that it suffices for you," but this text is not in the manuscript, so I have not added it here, lest it be a statement of Ibn Kathir's.] Qabisah said: I do not recall the verse from Surat al-Ma'idah: "judged by two just men among you." He said: Umar's words reached me, and suddenly there he was with the whip! He said: Then he struck my companion with the whip, and began saying: "You killed in the sacred precinct and made the judgment foolish!" He said: Then he turned to me, and I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I shall not make lawful for you today anything that is forbidden to you from me!" [This means that when Umar turned to him, Awf (i.e., Qabisah) threatened that he would strike him as he struck his companion; Umar feared and was intimidated by his saying that he would not make lawful for him the striking of a skin that is forbidden to him except by its right. Therefore Umar was reluctant to strike him as he had struck his companion. So observe what our forebears were disposed to of freedom of disposition, and how Islam had restrained their wildness, until Umar withheld his hand, fearing he might strike the skin of a Muslim unlawfully, which is not permitted except by its right.] He said: "O Qabisah ibn Jabir, I see that you are young in years, broad of chest [his saying "fasih al-sadr" means wide of chest, and that is one of the signs of strength and soundness of constitution; and this statement from Umar is among the most eloquent that can be offered to the young, for affliction comes only from bad character, and one bad trait drags behind it all the other vices of character.] eloquent of tongue. Indeed the young man may have nine good qualities and one bad quality, and the bad quality corrupts the good qualities. So beware the stumbles of youth!" [Report 12588 – see the takhrij of the report of Qabisah ibn Jabir above in the note on no. 12573. Al-Bayhaqi concluded this report (al-Sunan 5:181), and it is from the narration of Ibn Abi Umar, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr: "Ibn Abi Umar said: Sufyan said: When Abd al-Malik related this hadith, he would say: I have not omitted from it an alif nor a waw."]

12589 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah related to us, from Mukhariq, from Tariq, who said: Arbad trampled a lizard (dabb) [ "awta'a" means: he caused his mount to step until it trampled the lizard, i.e., trod upon it. I explained it so because they say: "wati'a al-shay'" and "wat'atahu" with the meaning of trampling it, and they have not mentioned "awta'ahu," though I see that analogy supports it.] so that it died — while he was in ihram. He came to Umar to have a judgment passed on him. Umar said to him: "Judge with me!" So they judged concerning it a young male goat (jaday) which had gathered water and trees. [His saying "jama'a al-ma' wa-al-shajar" means: it had been weaned and grazed on water and trees. This is an explanation I have not found in any of the reference works of language or its figurative usage. It should be recorded.] Then Umar said: "judged by two just men among you." [Report 12589 – "Mukhariq" is "Mukhariq ibn Khalifah ibn Jabir" and it is said: "Mukhariq ibn Abd Allah" and "Mukhariq ibn Abd al-Rahman" al-Bajali al-Ahmasi, a trustworthy narrator, already passed as no. 11682. And "Tariq" is "Tariq ibn Shihab al-Bajali al-Ahmasi," passed as nos. 9744, 11682, 12073–12075, 12085. And "Arbad" is "Arbad ibn Abd Allah al-Bajali," who attained the Jahiliyyah, so Ibn Hajar described him in al-Isabah in the third section, and mentioned this report specifying his name, then said: "Its chain is sound, and al-A'mash related it from Sulayman ibn Maysarah, from Tariq, without naming the man." It is related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:182 by way of al-Shafi'i from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. It is in al-Umm 2:165 and Musnad al-Shafi'i by al-Sindi: 332, and Ustadh Hamid Mustafa explained it in the same manner as I explained it before.]

12590 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man killed game and came to Ibn Umar and asked him about that, and with him was Abd Allah ibn Safwan. Ibn Umar said to Ibn Safwan: "Either I will speak and you will confirm me, or you will speak and I will confirm you." Ibn Safwan said: "Rather, you speak." So Ibn Umar spoke, and Abd Allah ibn Safwan agreed with him in that.

12591 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, that he said: "If I found a just judge, I would judge a jaday for a fox, and a jaday is more beloved to me than a fox." [In the printed edition: "min al-tha'lab," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the better reading.]

12592 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Mijlaz: that a man asked Ibn Umar about a man who killed game while in ihram, and Ibn Safwan was with him. Ibn Umar said to him: "Either you speak and I will confirm you, or I speak and you confirm me." He said: "Speak, and I will confirm you."

12593 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Ibn Jarir al-Bajali informed me, saying: "I hit a gazelle while I was in ihram, and I mentioned that to Umar, and he said: 'Go to two men of your brethren, and let them pass judgment upon you.' So I went to Abd al-Rahman and Sa'd, and they judged against me a male goat, a'far [Abu Ja'far said: al-a'far is the white one]."

[Report 12593 – "Abu Wa'il" is "Shaqiq ibn Salamah al-Asadi," already passed many times. "Abu Jarir al-Bajali" was not biographed except by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 6:106–107, and he said: "He related from Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd," and he related this report abridged by way of Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq from Sufyan from Mansur from Abu Wa'il, then related it at length with nearly its wording in the report of Abu Ja'far, by way of Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, from Mansur, from Shaqiq. It is related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 5:181–182 by way of Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, nearly in the wording of Abu Ja'far. Then he said at its end: "Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid added in it from Mansur: 'And I was forgetful of my ihram.'" This addition is in the two reports of Ibn Sa'd: in the first, "wa-ana nasin li-ihlali" (and I was forgetful of my ihlal), and in the other, "wa-la adhkuru ihlali" (and I do not recall my ihlal). Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 3:239 transmitted it from this place of al-Tabari's tafsir, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:329 cited it and attributed it additionally to Abu al-Shaykh. In the printed edition: "Ibn Jarir al-Bajali," and the correct reading is from the manuscript, where it is undotted. In Ibn Kathir it is like the printed edition, and in al-Sunan of al-Bayhaqi and al-Durr al-Manthur: "Abu Huraiz," and the correct reading is what is in Tabaqat ibn Sa'd. In the printed edition: "fa-atayt Abd al-Rahman wa-Sa'idan," and the correct reading is what I have given from the manuscript; "Abd al-Rahman" is "Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf" and "Sa'd" is "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas."]

12594 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur with his chain, from Umar, the like of it.

12595 - Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Ibn Sirin, who said: A man was on a she-camel while in ihram, and he saw a gazelle taking refuge at a hillock, and he said: "Let me see whether I reach this hillock first or this gazelle!" [In the printed edition: "li-anzur ana asbaq," and in the manuscript: "li-anzur wa-ana asbaq," and the correct reading is what I have given.] Then a female goat of the gazelles fell beneath the legs of his she-camel and it killed her. ["Al-anz" is the female of goats, wild goats and gazelles.] He came to Umar and mentioned that to him, and he and Ibn Awf judged against him a white she-goat [ 'anzan 'afra']. He said: and it is the white one.

12596 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad: that a man trampled a gazelle while in ihram [see the explanation of "awta'a" above, p. 26, note 1], so he came to Umar and mentioned that to him, and beside him was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. He turned to Abd al-Rahman and spoke with him, then turned to the man and said: "Offer a white she-goat."

12597 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim: that he used to say: "Whatever a muhrim incurs of anything for which no prior judgment has been passed, it is to be taken afresh, and two just men shall judge it." [That is, no prior judgment has been passed on it. And his saying "istaqbil bihi" means: he begins the consideration of it, without a prior judgment.]

12598 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to me, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Ya'la, from Amr ibn Habashi, who said: I heard a man ask Abd Allah ibn Umar about a man who had found a rabbit's young, and he said: "In it is a kid of a goat, in my opinion." Then he said to me: "Is it so?" I said: "You know better than I." He said: "Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: 'judged by two just men among you.'" [Report 12598 – "Amr ibn Habashi" is a trustworthy Successor, already passed, and the vocalization of his name has passed as no. 2340.]

12599 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adiy and Sahl ibn Yusuf related to us, from Humayd, from Bakr: that two men saw a gazelle while both were in ihram, and they wagered on it, and the stake of each of them was for whoever reached it first. ["Al-khatar" (with two fathas) is the stake, the prize that is placed in the wager between the contestants. "Akhtara al-mal" means he made it a stake between the wagerers, and "takhatharu" means they wagered. In the printed edition: "wa-ja'ala kull wahid minhuma," but this word in the manuscript is very poorly written, and I saw fit to read it so from the meaning of the wager, and it is the correct reading, God willing.] One of them reached it first, and struck it with his staff and killed it. When they both came to Makkah, they came to Umar to dispute before him, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was with him, and they told him of that. Umar said: "This is gambling, and I do not permit it!" Then he looked at Abd al-Rahman and said: "What do you see?" He said: "A sheep." Umar said: "And I see that too." When the two men had departed from Umar's presence, one of them said to his companion: "Umar did not know what to say until he asked the man!" Umar recalled them and said: "Indeed Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, did not content Himself with Umar alone, saying: 'judged by two just men among you,' and I am Umar, and this is Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf."

* *

Others said: Rather, the two just men look at the slain game and estimate its value in dirhams, then they order the killer to buy with that an animal of livestock as an offering. So the two judges judge, according to these people, by the value. They are only needed to assess the value of the game at the place where it was hit.

* *

We have previously mentioned from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he used to say: "Whatever a muhrim incurs of game, its value shall be judged," and this is the view of a group of the jurists of Kufa.

* *

As for His saying "as an offering," it is in the accusative of circumstance (hal) from the "ha'" in His saying "judge by it."

* *

His saying "reaching the Ka'bah" is a qualifier (na't) and attribute of "offering." It is permissible for it to qualify it, though it is annexed to a definite noun, because it is in the sense of an indefinite. The meaning of His saying "reaching the Ka'bah" is "reaching the Ka'bah." Although it is annexed, its meaning is that of tanwin, because it has the sense of the future. It is like His saying: ﴿This is a cloud bringing rain to us﴾ [Surat al-Ahqaf: 24], where "a cloud" is described by "bringing rain to us," because "mumtiranā" carries the sense of tanwin, its interpretation being the future; its meaning is "a cloud that will rain upon us." So likewise is it in His saying "an offering reaching the Ka'bah."

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿or expiation: feeding the needy﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Or upon him is an expiation, feeding the needy." And "expiation" is conjoined to the "recompense" in His saying "then a recompense like what he killed of livestock."

The readers differed concerning the reading of this:

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it: ﴿or kaffāratu ṭa'āmi masākīn﴾ with the annexation (idafah). As for the readers of Iraq, most of them recited it with tanwin on "kaffarah" and nominative case on "ta'am": "or kaffarah ta'amu masakin."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited with tanwin on "kaffarah" and nominative on "ta'am," for the reason we mentioned in His saying "then a recompense like what he killed of livestock." [See what has passed, pp. 13–14.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 95 (part 4 of 7):

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words: "or an expiation of feeding the needy" [See the explanation of "expiation" (kaffarah) above, 10:531, footnote 11, and the references there.] Some of them said: the meaning of that is that the one who kills game deliberately while in the state of ihram is not free of the obligation of one of these three things which God, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned: a sacrificial animal (hady) equal to what was killed, to be brought to the Ka'bah, or the feeding of a needy person as expiation for what he did, or the equivalent of that in fasting. However, he is given the choice to do whichever of these he wishes, and whichever of them he performs as expiation, he has discharged his obligation. This is only God's informing His servants that the killer of such game, as described, will not have his ruling fall outside one of the three alternatives. They said: If he is able to match the kill, then his ruling is that he be judged to give an animal of livestock equal to what was killed, and nothing else will suffice him as long as he finds the equivalent. They said: If he does not find it, or if the one killed has no equivalent among livestock, then his expiation is then the feeding of the needy.

Mention of those who said this:

12600 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "And whoever of you kills it intentionally, then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering to reach the Ka'bah, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed." He said: When the muhrim kills some game, a judgment is passed upon him concerning it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, then he must sacrifice a sheep in Makkah. If he does not find one, then he feeds six needy persons. If he does not find that, then he fasts three days. If he kills a deer (ayyil) or the like, then he owes a cow. If he does not find it, he feeds twenty needy persons. If he does not find that, he fasts twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a wild ass or the like, then he owes a camel. If he does not find it, he feeds thirty needy persons. If he does not find that, he fasts thirty days. The measure of food is a mudd for each of them, sufficing them.

12601 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, in his words: "O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in ihram" up to his words: "judged by two just men among you." Then the expiation: for one who kills what is less than a hare, it is feeding.

12602 - Hannad related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If the muhrim hits game, its penalty is judged upon him in livestock. If he finds its penalty, he slaughters it and gives it in charity. If he does not find its penalty, the penalty is valued in dirhams, then the dirhams are valued in wheat, and then he fasts one day for every sa' . He said: By "food" is only meant fasting; so when he finds food, he has found the penalty.

12603 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Zuhayr, from Jabir, from Ata', Mujahid and Amir, concerning "or the equivalent of that in fasting," who said: The food is only for the one who does not find the sacrificial animal.

12604 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he used to say: If the muhrim hits some game, he owes its penalty in livestock. If he does not find it, the penalty is valued in dirhams, then the dirhams are valued as food, then he fasts one day for each half sa'.

12605 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Hammad, who said: If the muhrim hits game and it is judged upon him, and what remains of it is less than half a sa', he fasts one day for it. Fasting is only for one who does not find the price of a sacrificial animal, and then food is judged upon him. If he has no food to give in charity, fasting is judged upon him, so he fasts one day for each half sa'. "An expiation of feeding the needy": he said: for what does not reach the price of a sacrificial animal. "Or the equivalent of that in fasting": of the penalty, when he does not find what to buy a sacrificial animal with, or what to give in charity, of what does not reach the price of a sacrificial animal, fasting is judged upon him, one day for each half sa'.

12606 - Hannad related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Mujahid said: "And whoever of you kills it intentionally, then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock," he said: upon him is an equivalent of livestock, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah. And whoever does not find it, let him buy food with its value, and feed each needy person two mudd. If he does not find it, he fasts one day for every two mudd.

12607 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And whoever of you kills it intentionally," up to his words: "And whoever returns, God will take retribution from him," he said: If he kills game, the penalty upon him is equivalent to what he killed of livestock. If he does not find it, it is judged upon him, then the ransom is valued, how much it is in dirhams, then the price of that is estimated in food for the needy, and he fasts one day for each needy person. The food of the needy is not permitted, for whoever finds the food of the needy has found the ransom.

12608 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Hasan ibn Muslim said to me: Whoever hits game whose penalty is a sheep, that is what God, may His remembrance be exalted, means by: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you." And what is an expiation by feeding the needy, like a sparrow that is killed and does not reach the level of a sacrificial animal: "or the equivalent of that in fasting." He said: the equivalent of an ostrich or a sparrow, or the equivalent of all of that. I mentioned that to Ata', and he said: Everything in the Qur'an that has "or... or," its owner may choose whatever he wishes.

12609 - Amr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Husayn informed us, from al-Hakam, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "Do not kill game while you are in ihram. And whoever of you kills it intentionally, then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock." If he does not find a penalty, the penalty is valued upon him as food, then a sa' for every sa' two days.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is that the one who intentionally kills game while in ihram has the choice between one of the three expiations, namely: the penalty equal to it from livestock, the food, and the fasting. They said: The interpretation of His words: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting," is that he must make the penalty with an equivalent from livestock, or expiate by feeding the needy, or by the equivalent of the food in fasting.

Mention of those who said this:

12610 - Hannad ibn al-Sari related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ata', concerning the word of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting," he said: If a man in ihram hits an ostrich, then for him, and if he is wealthy, he may offer whatever he wishes: a camel, or its equivalent in food, or its equivalent in fasting. He said: Everything in the Qur'an that has "or... or," its owner may choose from it whatever he wishes.

12611 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from Ata', concerning His words: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock," he said: "Whatever is in the Qur'an as 'or such or such,' its owner has the choice, whichever of them he wishes to do."

12612 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Asbat and Abd al-A'la related to us, from Dawud, from Ikrimah, who said: Whatever is in the Qur'an as "or... or," he has the choice in it. And whatever is "then whoever does not find," then the one next to it, then the one after it.

12613 - Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: Hafs related to us, from Amr, from al-Hasan, similarly.

12614 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Layth informed us, from Ata' and Mujahid, that they both said concerning His words: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock," they said: whatever is in the Qur'an as "or such or such," its owner has the choice, whichever of them he wishes to do.

12615 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: Whatever is in the Qur'an as "or such or such," its owner has the choice, whichever of them he wishes to do.

12616 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abu Surrah informed us, from al-Hasan, and he said: Ubaydah informed us, from Ibrahim. Both said: Everything in the Qur'an as "or... or," he has the choice, whichever of them he wishes to do.

12617 - Hannad related to us, saying: Hafs related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Everything in the Qur'an as "or... or," its owner has the choice in it, and everything as "then whoever does not find," then the first, then the one after it.

* *

Those who held that the killer of game among the muhrimun has the choice among the three things differed concerning the nature of what is required of him in expiation by feeding and fasting, when he chooses expiation by one of them rather than the sacrifice.

Some of them said: When he chooses to expiate by that, then what is obligatory upon him is that he values the equivalent from livestock as food, then he fasts one day for each mudd.

Mention of those who said this:

12618 - Hannad related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata': What is "or the equivalent of that in fasting"? He said: If what is its equivalent is a sheep, the sheep is valued as food, then he makes for each mudd a day he fasts.

* *

Others said: Rather, what is obligatory upon him, when he wishes to expiate by feeding or fasting, is that he values the hunted game killed as food, then gives it in charity as food if he chooses charity. And if he chooses fasting, he fasts.

* *

Then they also differed concerning fasting.

Some of them said: He fasts one day for each mudd.

* *

Others said: He fasts one day for each half sa'.

Others said: He fasts one day for each sa'.

* *

Mention of those who said: the thing valued for feeding is the game killed.

12619 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah: "O you who have believed, do not kill game," the verse. He said: Qatadah used to say: Two just men judge concerning livestock; if he does not have what reaches that, they look at its price and value it as food, then he fasts one day for each sa'.

* *

Others said: There is no sense in expiation by feeding, because whoever has a way to expiate by feeding also has a way to the penalty of an equivalent from livestock. And whoever has a way to the penalty of an equivalent from livestock, expiation by something else does not suffice him. They said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, only mentioned expiation by feeding in this place to indicate the manner of expiation by fasting, not that He made expiation by feeding one of the expiations by which the killing of game is expiated. We have already mentioned the interpretation of that earlier.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in my view concerning His words: "then a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock," is that it means: upon the one who kills it intentionally is an equivalent to what he killed of livestock, not its value, if he chooses to make the penalty with an equivalent from livestock. That is because the value is only in dinars or dirhams, and dirhams or dinars are not an equivalent to game, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, only obligated a penalty equivalent from livestock.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings in my view concerning His words: "or an expiation of feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting," is that it is a choice, and that the killer has the option, in his expiation for killing game while in ihram, to choose whichever of these three expiations he wishes. Because God, may His remembrance be exalted, made what He obligated in killing game of penalty and expiation a punishment for his act and an expiation for his sin, for his destruction of the game that was forbidden for him to destroy in the state of his ihram, though it had been lawful for him before his state of ihram. Just as He made the ransom of fasting, almsgiving, or sacrifice obligatory for shaving hair that the muhrim shaved in the state of his ihram, though it had been lawful for him before his state of ihram, [a punishment for his act and an expiation for his sin] and the shaving of hair which the muhrim shaved in the state of his ihram, though it had been lawful for him to shave it before his state of ihram, then he was prevented from shaving it in the state of his ihram, like game. Then He made a penalty for shaving it upon him, as a requital for shaving it. So all agreed that in his shaving it, if he shaves it out of harm, he has the choice in expiating it, doing that by whichever of the three expiations he wishes, with no difference between them. Likewise, God willing, the killer of game among the muhrimun is similar.

And whoever refuses what we have said on this, it is said to him: God, may His remembrance be exalted, ruled upon the killer of game with an equivalent from livestock, or an expiation of feeding the needy, or its equivalent in fasting, just as He ruled upon the one who shaves with a ransom of fasting, almsgiving, or sacrifice. You claim that one of them has the choice in expiating what was prescribed in it, by whichever of the three he wishes, and you deny that this choice is for the other. So is there between you and the one who reverses the matter upon you, so that he gives the choice where you refuse and refuses where you give it to you, any distinction from a principle or a parallel? He will not say anything about one of them except if the same is required of the other.

Then they differed concerning the manner of valuation when one wishes to expiate by feeding.

Some of them said: The game is valued at its price in the place where he hit it. This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Hammad, Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. The narration from Ibrahim and Hammad has already been mentioned earlier with what indicates this, and it is the explicit view of Abu Hanifah and his companions.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is valued at the price in the land where he makes expiation.

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٦٢٠ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Isra'il told us, from Jabir, from ʿAmir, who said concerning a man in the state of ihram who killed game in Khurasan: "He must expiate in Makkah or in Mina." And he said: "The food is to be valued at the market price of the land in which he expiates."

١٢٦٢١ - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Abu Yaman told us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, concerning a man who killed game in Khurasan, who said: "He is to be judged in Makkah."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that the one who kills game while in ihram, if he compensates for it with an animal of the livestock (ni'am), then he is to compensate with its equivalent in kind and its measure in body, from among the things most similar to it in form among the cattle. If he compensates by feeding (the poor), he is to assess its value at the place where he killed it, because it was there that expiation by feeding became obligatory upon him. Then, if he wishes, he may feed (the poor) at the place where he killed it, and if he wishes, in Makkah, and if he wishes, in other places wherever he chooses, because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, only stipulated that the offering (hady) must reach the Ka'bah in the case of killing game, and not in the case of its other compensations. So whoever compensates with other than an offering may compensate by feeding or fasting wherever he wishes on the earth.

* *

Those among the people of knowledge who held the view similar to what we have said on this matter include a group.

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٦٢٢ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿArubah told us, from Abu Maʿshar, from Ibrahim, who said: "Whatever is blood (an animal sacrifice) is in Makkah. Whatever is charity or fasting, (it may be done) wherever he wishes."

* *

Some dissenters opposed this, saying: "Offering (hady) and feeding are valid only in Makkah. As for fasting, if he expiates by it, he may fast wherever he wishes on the earth."

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٦٢٣ - Hannad told us, saying: Waki' told us; and Ibn Waki' told us, saying: my father told us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from ʿAta', who said: "The blood (sacrifice) and the food are in Makkah, and fasting is wherever he wishes."

١٢٦٢٤ - Hannad told us, saying: Waki' told us; and Ibn Waki' told us, saying: my father told us, from Malik ibn Mughawwal, from ʿAta', who said: "The expiation for the pilgrimage is in Makkah."

١٢٦٢٥ - ʿAmr ibn ʿAli told us, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "I said to ʿAta': Where is food to be given in charity if it occurs to him?" He said: "In Makkah, because it has the status of the offering (hady)." He said: "'Or an equivalent of that in fasting' (the compensation) is for the one who kills game, 'the equivalent of what he killed of livestock, or an offering reaching the Ka'bah'" — because he killed it in the sacred territory (haram), meaning the House, so its compensation is at the House.

* *

As for the offering, whoever compensates for what he killed of game with it, it will not suffice him as expiation for what he killed unless it reaches the Ka'bah, as the Exalted has said, and is slaughtered or sacrificed, and given in charity to the poor of the sacred territory. By "the Ka'bah" in this place is meant the entire sacred territory. Whoever has brought forward his obligatory offering of game compensation may slaughter it at any time he wishes, before the day of sacrifice or after it, and feed (the poor) with it. Likewise, if he expiates by food, he may expiate with it whenever he likes and wherever he likes. And if he expiates by fasting, the same applies.

* *

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this matter, apart from what we mentioned of their disagreement about expiation by feeding, as we have explained earlier.

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٦٢٦ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to ʿAta': "Or an equivalent of that in fasting" — does his fasting have a time? He said: "No, whenever he wishes and wherever he wishes, though hastening it is more beloved to me."

١٢٦٢٧ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to ʿAta': "A man who killed game during the Hajj or ʿUmrah, and sent its compensation to the sacred territory in Muharram or another of the months — would it suffice for him?" He said: "Yes," then he recited: "an offering reaching the Ka'bah." Hannad said: Yahya said: "And with it we take." [Note on the report: "Yahya" is Ibn Abi Za'idah, namely Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, who has passed several times.]

١٢٦٢٨ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Sulaym informed us, from ʿAta', who said: "When you come to Makkah with the compensation for game, sacrifice it, for Allah, mighty and majestic, says: 'an offering reaching the Ka'bah'; unless he arrives in the (first) ten (days), in which case he delays it until the day of sacrifice."

١٢٦٢٩ - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj told us, from ʿAta', who said: "The one who kills game gives charity in Makkah, for Allah, mighty and majestic, says: 'an offering reaching the Ka'bah'."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿or an equivalent of that in fasting﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, mighty and majestic is He: "Or upon the one who kills game while in ihram, is the equivalent of the game killed, in fasting." That is, the game is valued alive and not killed, at its worth in food, at the place where the muhrim killed it, and then he fasts one day for every mudd. This is because the Prophet ﷺ made the equivalent of a mudd of food equal to one day of fasting in the expiation of one who had intercourse with his wife in the daytime of Ramadan. [Note: see the reports on the expiation of one who approached his wife during the day in Ramadan while fasting, in al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra 4: 221–225.]

* *

If someone says: "Why did you not make one day of fasting equivalent to every sa' in the compensation for game, by analogy with the Prophet's ruling on its counterpart, namely his ruling concerning Ka'b ibn ʿUjrah, when he commanded him to feed (the poor) if he expiated by feeding, a faraq of food, which is three sa's among six poor persons, [and] if he expiated by fasting, to fast three days — so that the three days of fasting are made the equivalent of feeding three sa's? Is this not more akin to expiation for killing game than the expiation for one who had intercourse with his wife in Ramadan?" It is said: Analogy is only the referring of disputed branches to their like among agreed-upon roots. There is no disagreement among all the proofs that one who has expiated for killing game by fasting may not equate one day of fasting with a sa' of food. Since that is so, and it is impermissible to oppose what has been agreed upon in religion, it is established that the ruling on equating fasting with food in killing game differs from its equating in the expiation for shaving (the head), since it is impermissible to refer one root to another root by analogy. Analogy is only permissible in applying a branch to a root. And whether someone says, "Why did you not refer the ruling on fasting in the expiation for killing game to its ruling in shaving for harm, regarding what it is equated with in food?" — and another says, "Why did you not refer the ruling on fasting in shaving to its ruling in the expiation for killing game, regarding what it is equated with in food, so that you require one day of fasting for every mudd or for every half sa'?"

* *

We have already shown earlier that "al-ʿadl" in the speech of the Arabs, with a fatha, is the measure of a thing from a different kind, and that "al-ʿidl" is its measure from its own kind. [Reference: see the explanation of "al-ʿadl" earlier at 2: 35, 574; then Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 320; then Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbaydah 1: 53, 175, 176.]

Some scholars of Arabic speech said: "al-ʿadl" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I equalized this with a fine equalization" (ʿadaltu bihadha ʿadlan hasanan). He said: "al-ʿadl" also with a fatha means "the like." But they distinguished between "al-ʿadl" in this sense and "ʿidl al-matāʿ" (a pack of goods), by pronouncing the ʿayn of "ʿidl al-matāʿ" with a kasra and opening it in the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿nor will any equivalent (ʿadl) be accepted from it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:123], and the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿or an equivalent (ʿadl) of that in fasting﴾, just as they said "a woman who is razan (grave, dignified)" and "a stone razin (heavy)." [Note: this statement is cited by the author of Lisan al-ʿArab under the root ʿ-d-l and not mentioned under r-z-n, so it is to be noted in the Lisan at its place. The Lisan has "ʿajz razin," which is an error to be corrected; the correct reading is "ḥajar," and "ḥajar razin" means heavy. The author of Asas al-Balaghah explicitly stated: "imra'ah razan," and one does not say "razinah."]

Some of them said: "al-ʿadl" is justice in what is right, and "al-ʿidl" with a kasra is the like. We have shown this with evidence earlier. [Referring to what preceded at 2: 35.]

* *

As for the accusative of "al-siyam" (fasting), it is as an explanatory accusative (tafsir) [the tamyiz; see the terminology index earlier], as one says: "I have a skin full of ghee (ʿindi mil'u ziqqin samnan)" and "the amount of a ratl of honey (qadru raṭlin ʿasalan)." [Reference: al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 320.]

* *

Those among the people of interpretation who said something similar to what we have said on this matter include a group. [At this point the eighth volume of the manuscript of the tafsir that we relied upon ends. There, here, is the following text:
"The eighth volume is completed, by the praise and help of God.
And God's blessings be upon our master Muhammad the Prophet, his family and companions, abundantly.
It is followed in the ninth, God willing:
Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to ʿAta': What is "ʿadl dhalika siyaman"?
He said: The equivalent of the food from the fasting.
