The completion of it was in the month of Rabiʿ al-Akhir, year 715 AH."
Then at the beginning of the ninth volume there follows the text: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. My Lord, make it easy." Remainder of the tafsir of: "or an equivalent of that in fasting."]

١٢٦٣٠ - Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to ʿAta': What is "an equivalent of that in fasting"? He said: "The equivalent of the food from the fasting." He said: "For every mudd, one day, he takes as a basis (yaʾkhudh zaʿama) the fasting of Ramadan and the zihar." [The word "yaʾkhudh" here means he analogizes that to the expiation of one who approaches his wife in the daytime of Ramadan and the expiation of zihar.] And he claimed that this is an opinion he holds, and he did not hear it from anyone, and no sunnah had passed with it. He said: Then I returned to him after some time and said: What is "an equivalent of that in fasting"? He said: "If what is equivalent to it is a sheep, it is valued as food, then he fasts one day in place of every mudd." He said: And I did not ask him: "Is this an opinion, or an established sunnah?"

١٢٦٣١ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿or an equivalent of that in fasting﴾, he said: "By fasting three days up to ten days."

١٢٦٣٢ - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from Hammad: ﴿or an equivalent of that in fasting﴾ — of the compensation, when he does not find what to buy as an offering, or what to give in charity, of what does not reach the price of an offering, it is decreed upon him to fast one day in place of every half sa'.

١٢٦٣٣ - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿or an equivalent of that in fasting﴾, he said: "If the muhrim kills some game, a ruling is imposed upon him concerning it. If he kills a gazelle or the like, he must sacrifice a sheep in Makkah. If he does not find it, then feeding six poor persons. If he does not find (that), then fasting three days. If he kills a deer (ayyil) or the like, he must have a cow. If he does not find (it), he feeds twenty poor persons; if he does not find (that), he fasts twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a wild ass or the like, he must have a camel of the camels. If he does not find (it), he feeds thirty poor persons. If he does not find (that), he fasts thirty days. In the printed edition here it is changed as in the earlier passage, and written "yushbiʿahum."]

١٢٦٣٤ - Ibn al-Barqi told us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah told us, from Sa'id, [I asked him] about the muhrim who kills game, so that the ransom becomes obligatory upon him: a sheep, or the cow, or the camel. If he does not find (them), what is the equivalent of that by fasting or charity? He said: "Its price; and if he does not find its price, he values its price in food to give in charity to each poor person a mudd, then he fasts one day for every mudd."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿so that he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Mighty and majestic is He says: I have imposed upon the one who kills game while in ihram what I have imposed of compensation and expiation that I mentioned in this verse, so that he may taste the consequence of his affair and its punishment.

* *

Its meaning: "by his affair" is his sin and his deed, which is killing what Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade him to kill in the state of ihram.

* *

He says: So I obligate him the expiation that I obligated him with, to make him taste the punishment of his sin, by imposing the fine and the labor of his body, which tires and burdens him. [Reference: see the explanation of "dhaqa" (to taste) earlier at 7: 96, 446, 452; 8: 487.]

* *

The root of "al-wabal" is severity in what is disliked, and from it is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a heavy seizure﴾ [Surah al-Muzzammil 73:16].

* *

Allah, mentioned, by His saying "that he may taste the consequence of his affair," made clear that the expiations which are obligatory in property and bodies are punishments from Him upon His creation, even if they are a purification for them and an expiation for their sins which they have expiated by them.

* *

The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

١٢٦٣٥ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: As for "the consequence of his affair," it is the punishment of his affair.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Mighty and majestic is He, says to His believing servants who believe in Him and His Messenger ﷺ: Allah has pardoned, O believers, what has passed from you in your jahiliyyah, of your hunting game while you were in ihram and killing it, so He will not hold you accountable for what was done by you in that before its prohibition upon you, nor will He impose upon you an expiation in property or person. But whoever of you returns to killing it while in ihram, after its prohibition by the meaning that he used to kill it in his state of disbelief, and before its prohibition upon him, by deeming its killing permissible, then Allah will take retribution from him. [Reference: see the explanation of "ʿafa" (pardon) earlier in the indexes of language, and of "salafa" (pass) earlier at 6: 14; 8: 137, 150.]

* *

It may also be that its meaning is: whoever returns to killing it after its prohibition in Islam, then Allah will take retribution from him in the Hereafter. As for in this world, upon him is the compensation and expiation in it that I have explained.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said something like what we have said regarding it.

Others said: The meaning of that is: Allah has pardoned what was past of your killing game before Allah, may He be remembered, prohibited that for you. And whoever returns to kill it after Allah prohibited it for him, knowingly of its prohibition, intending to kill it, mindful of his ihram, then Allah Himself is the one who takes retribution from him, and there is no expiation for that sin, nor any recompense obligated upon him in this world.

As for the one who intentionally kills game while forgetting his sanctity, or ignorant that killing it is prohibited, these are the ones who are judged. As for one who kills it intentionally after the prohibition of Allah, knowing that it is prohibited and that it is forbidden (haram), that one is left to the retribution of Allah; that is the one for whom Allah has ordained retribution.

* *

This is similar to the saying of Mujahid that we mentioned before.

[[That is, what has passed under no. 12662.]]

* *

Others said: That refers to a specific person.

[[The narration 12666: "Zayd" "Abu al-Mu'alla" is mentioned under "Zayd ibn Murrah" and "Zayd ibn Abi Layla." "Abu al-Mu'alla," client of the Banu al-'Adawiyyah. Abu Hatim said: "Good in narrations." * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings regarding that, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: "And whoever returns in Islam to kill it after Allah, may He be remembered, forbade it, then Allah takes retribution from him, and upon him, in addition to that, is the expiation." Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He informed that He takes retribution from him, did not inform us, and He had obligated upon him, in his intentional killing of game, what He obligated of recompense or expiation by His words: "And whoever kills it among you intentionally, then a recompense of the like of what he killed of the livestock," that He had removed from him the expiation in the second and third time. Rather, He informed His servants of what He obligated of judgment upon the killer of game among the muhrimun intentionally, then informed that He takes retribution from the one who returns, and did not say: "Nor is there an expiation upon him in this world."

* *

If someone supposes that the expiation removes the punishment, and that if the expiation were obligatory upon him in this world, the punishment in the Hereafter would be void, then he has supposed wrongly. That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, differentiates among the punishments for His disobediences as He wills and loves, so He increases the punishment for some of His disobediences beyond what He decreases for others, and decreases for some beyond what He increases for others, as He did in differentiating between the punishment of the unmarried fornicator and the married fornicator, and between the thief of a quarter dinar and the thief of less than that. Likewise, He differentiated between His punishment of the one who intentionally kills game while in ihram at the outset, and His punishment of one who returns after the first time. He obligated upon the initiator the like of the livestock, or the expiation by feeding, or the equivalent in fasting, and made that the punishment of his offence by His words: "that he may taste the consequence of his affair" (5:95). He made upon the one who returns after the first time, and added to his punishment what He informed His servants He would do to him of retribution, as severity from Him, Mighty and Majestic, for returning after the first time. If His punishments for things were uniform, it would be necessary that there be no prescribed penalty in one matter differing from a prescribed penalty in another, and no punishment in the Hereafter more severe than another punishment. That is contrary to what the decisive Furqan brought.

* *

Some who claim have asserted that the meaning of that is: "And whoever returns in Islam after Allah's prohibition of killing it," for killing it in the sense the people used to kill it in their Jahiliyyah, and He pardoned them for it when its killing was prohibited for them, and that is killing it while considering its killing lawful. He said: As for when he kills it in another manner, and that is that he kills it in the manner of wickedness (fusuq), not in the manner of considering it lawful, then upon him is the recompense and the expiation every time he returns.

This is a saying that we do not know anyone among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) to have said. Sufficient as an error is his saying, its departure from the sayings of the people of knowledge, even if there were no proof of its error other than that. How then, when the apparent meaning of the revelation (tanzil) indicates its corruption? That is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by His words: "And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him," generalized to every returner to killing game in the sense whose prohibition was mentioned at the beginning of the verse, and He did not specify it for one returner among them over another returner. Whoever claims in the revelation what is not in its apparent meaning is obligated to provide proof for his claim in a manner that must be accepted.

* *

As for the one who claims that the meaning of that is: "And whoever returns to killing it intentionally after the outset, for a killing that occurred earlier in the state of his ihram, Allah takes retribution from him," then the meaning of His words: "Allah has pardoned what is past," would be: Allah has pardoned what was past of his sin by killing game at the outset. [[His words: "fa-inna qawla Allah..." to the end is the answer to his words: "As for the one who claims..."]] For in the words of Allah, may He be remembered: "that he may taste the consequence of his affair," there is clear evidence that the saying regarding that is other than what he said, because pardon for a crime is leaving off accountability for it. Whoever is made to taste the consequence of his crime has been punished by it. It is not permissible to say of one who has been punished: "He has been pardoned." And the report of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is too truthful to contain contradiction.

* *

If someone says: What prevents the killer of game among the muhrimun from being made to taste the consequence of his affair the first time, by what is obligated of recompense and expiation, and being pardoned from punishment with more than that, which it would have been for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to punish him with?

It is said to him: If that is permissible in your view to be the interpretation of the verse, even though it contradicts the saying of the people of interpretation, then what prevents you from saying that the retribution which Allah, may He be remembered, promised upon returning after the outset is that additional punishment He pardoned him for the first time, of what He would have done to him along with what He made him taste of the consequence of his affair; so He makes him taste in his return after the outset the consequence of his affair that He made him taste the first time, and leaves off His pardon of what He pardoned him for at the outset, and holds him accountable for it? Then he will not say anything about that except that he would be obligated in the end with its like.

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says: "And Allah is Almighty (ʿAzīz) in His dominion," none can overpower Him, and none can prevent Him from taking vengeance on whomever He takes vengeance upon, nor from punishing whomever He wishes to punish, as a preventer. For the creation is His creation, and the command is His command; to Him belong might (ʿizzah) and invincibility (manaʿah). [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" above, 10:289, note 1, and the references there.]]

As for His saying, "Possessor of retribution" (dhū intiqām), it means: His punishing those who disobey Him for their disobedience toward Him.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 2 of 5):**

12706. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr, who said: Abu Ayyub was asked about the words of Allah, may He be mentioned, ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you﴾. He said: "It is what the sea casts up."

* *

Others said: By His words "and its food," He meant *al-mulih* (salted fish). *Al-mulih*, on the pattern of *fa'il*, means *al-mumallah* (salted). It is said: "*samak mal* and *mulih* and *mamlul* and *mumallah*" (fish that is salted). Accordingly, the meaning of the statement in their interpretation is: "Lawful for you is the fish of the sea and its salted fish, at all times, whether you are in a state of *ihlal* (non-*ihram*) or *ihram*."

*[Editor's note: In the printed edition the phrase "fi hal" ("in a state of") was omitted; I have restored it from the manuscript.]*

Those who said this:

12707. Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and its food," that he said: "Its food" is its salted part.

*[Editor's note: "Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi" was mentioned under no. 12670, and so it is in the manuscript; the printed edition has "Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Khalid al-Barqi," which is an error in two places. The correct form is what I have adopted. As for his statement "its salted part," al-Jawhari and others disapproved of saying "salted fish (samak maliḥ)." Yunus said: "I have not heard any Arab say *maliḥ*." What Yunus did not hear, others did hear; it occurs in eloquent poetry and in the reports here, and it is, in my view, correct beyond doubt. The correct position is that of Ibn Barri: the justification from the standpoint of Arabic is that it is in the relative sense, like their saying *ma' dafiq* ("gushing water"), meaning "possessing gushing"; and likewise *ma' maliḥ* meaning "possessing salt." Similarly, *rajul tāris* means "possessing *nars*" and *rajul dāri'* means "possessing armour." He said: this does not follow the verbal pattern, and that is the correct view, God willing. (See Lisan al-Arab, root m-l-ḥ.)]*

12708. Haddathani al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you," meaning: with its food, its salted part, and what the sea casts up of it, its salted part.

*[Editor's note: "Al-sir" (with a kasra on the sad) is also called *al-ṣaḥnāt*. It is said that it refers to salted fish made into *ṣaḥnāt*, which is like *fasikh* in our country. Jarir mentioned it in his poetry, when he satirised the family of al-Muhallab, who were of the Azd tribe:

"The caliphate was not destined to be possessed
by a slave of an Azdi woman with a crooked clitoris."

"When they put onions in their *sir,*
then roasted a *kun'ad* of salted fish, they ate *jadf.*"

*Al-kun'ad* is a kind of fish. His words "jadafu" mean they ate *al-jadf* (with two fatha vowels), which is found in Yemen, and camels eat it, so that it substitutes for water, and one needs no water to drink after eating it.

12727. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Hurayth, from Ikrimah, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you," he said: what the sea brings with its waves, like this.

*[Editor's note: In the printed edition it reads "ma' bihi al-bahr bi-wajhihi" and the word "hakadha" ("like this") is omitted, as though the editor thought "hakadha" pointed to a difficulty in the word "bi-mawjihi." This is strange. His words "like this" intend to point out that it came floating.]*

12728. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Hasan ibn Salih, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "Its food" is everything hunted from it.

*[Editor's note: "Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd al-Rasi" was mentioned under nos. 4926 and 8770. "Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy al-Thawri" was mentioned under nos. 178, 5347 and 7594.]*

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in our opinion is the view of those who said: "Its food" is what the sea casts up, or what recedes from it and is found dead on its shore. This is because Allah, may He be mentioned, first mentioned the hunting of what is hunted, saying: "Lawful for you is the game of the sea," so what must be understood by the implication is what is not hunted from it. Thus He said: Lawful for you is what you hunt from the sea, and what you do not hunt from it.

As for the "salted," it is what was salted after being hunted, and so it is included in the general sense of His words "Lawful for you is the game of the sea." There is no reason to repeat it, since there is no benefit in it. Allah, may He be exalted, has already informed His servants of the permissibility of what is hunted from the sea by His words "Lawful for you is the game of the sea." So there is no benefit in saying to them afterwards: "And its salted part, which is hunted, is lawful for you," because what is hunted from it has already been declared lawful, whether fresh or salted, by His words "Lawful for you is the game of the sea." And God is exalted above addressing His servants with what gives them no benefit.

* *

A report has also been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a sense similar to what we have said, though some of its transmitters stop it at the Companion who transmitted it from him. It is this:

12729. Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Salama narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you," and he said: "Its food is what it casts up dead; so whatever it casts up dead is its food."

*[Editor's note: For nos. 12729 and 12730: "Abdah ibn Sulayman al-Kalabi": Ahmad said: "Trustworthy, trustworthy, and more so, righteous in his body." The authors of the six books narrated from him. He has been mentioned many times under nos. 222, 2323, 2758, 3022 and elsewhere. Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi is trustworthy; the authors of the six books narrated from him, and he has been mentioned under nos. 8 and 3015. "Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf" is a great and trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) and imam; he has been mentioned under nos. 8, 67, 3015, 8394 and elsewhere. I have not found anyone who mentioned this report except al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:331, and he attributed this raised (marfu') report only to Ibn Jarir. As for the following report, which is halted (mawquf), he attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim. As for the second halted report, no. 12730, it contains "Ibn Abi Za'ida," who is Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida, one of the memorisers of the Kufans, firm and reliable, a man of the Sunna, upright in narration. The authors of the six books narrated from him, and he has been mentioned under nos. 850 and 4246. Thus the chain of both the raised and the halted report is sound, and its men are trustworthy memorisers. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]*

Some of them stopped this report at Abu Hurayra.

12730. Hannad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, regarding His words "Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food," he said: "Its food is what it casts up dead."

*[Editor's note: See the comment on the preceding report.]*
