The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "as a provision for you," may He be mentioned, He means: a benefit for whoever among you is resident or present in his town, who takes enjoyment in eating it and benefits from it. "And for the travelling caravan" means: a benefit and enjoyment also for those travelling from land to land, and for travellers who take salted food as provision on their journeys.

*[Editor's note: For the explanation of "mata'" (provision), see the earlier discussion, vol. 8, p. 551, note 1, and the references there.]*

* *

"Al-sayyara" is the plural of "sayyar" (travelling caravan). The lexicographers confined themselves to saying that "al-sayyara" means the caravan or the people who travel, and that it is feminine in the sense of a company or group. Abu Ja'far treated it as a plural, as in their saying *jamal* and *jamala* (with the *mim* doubled), and *himar* and *himara.*

Those who interpret the Qur'an said in accordance with what we have said, and this is what was reported:

12731. Haddathani Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq informed me, from Ikrimah, that he said regarding His words "as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan": "For whoever is in the presence of the sea"; "and for the travelling caravan" means the journey.

12732. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arūba, from Qatada, regarding His words "and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan": what the sea casts up, and what they take as provision on their journeys of this salted food. He interpreted it in this way.

12733. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Jami' narrated to us, from Hammad, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan": salted fish, which they take on their journeys.

12734. Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: Miskin ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Salam ibn Habib al-Najjari narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words "and for the travelling caravan," he said: They are those in the state of *ihram*.

*[Editor's note: "Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi" was mentioned under nos. 6254, 12670 and 12707. In the printed edition he was altered as before to "Sulayman ibn Amr ibn Khalid al-Barqi," which is a plain error; the correct form is in the manuscript. "Miskin ibn Bukayr al-Harrani" (Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadhdha') was narrated from by Ahmad ibn Hanbal, a trustworthy narrator; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. As for "Abd al-Salam ibn Habib al-Najjari," I have not found anyone of that name among the narrators from al-Hasan or others. I found among the narrators from al-Hasan al-Basri "Abd al-Salam ibn Abi al-Janub al-Madani," a Medinan shaykh who is abandoned (matruk); he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/45, and in Mizan al-I'tidal 2:129. Perhaps he is the one.]*

12735. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan": As for "its food," it is the salted part of it, a *balagh* (provision) from which the traveller eats on journeys. [*"Balagh" means "bulgha"* (with a damma on the ba), which is what a person subsists on from provisions, that is, what suffices him until he reaches his destination. In the printed edition it reads "al-sayyara" with a ta' at the end; I have followed the manuscript.]

12736. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan," he said: "Its food" is its salted part, and what the sea casts up of it, which the traveller takes as provision. He said on another occasion: its salted part, and what the sea casts up. The salted part is what the traveller takes as provision.

12737. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan": meaning the salted, which he takes as provision.

*[Editor's note: In the printed edition it reads "fa-yatazawwaduhu," and the correct reading is that of the manuscript.]*

Mujahid used to say about this:

12738. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "and its food, as a provision for you": he said: the people of the villages; "and for the travelling caravan": the people of the cities.

12739. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words "as a provision for you": he said: for the people of the villages; "and for the travelling caravan": he said: the people of the cities; and the fish are for all people.

*[Editor's note: In the printed edition it reads "the people of the cities and the kinds of people, all of them," which is what came in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:232 from Mujahid: "and its food, he said: its fish, as a provision for you, for the people of the villages, and for the travelling caravan, the people of journeys and all kinds of people." Then comes what is in the manuscript, which has suffered distortion: "the people of the cities and the *hibab* are for all people." Al-Durr al-Manthur cannot be trusted in its printing, and its sentence is clearly an error. The word "the people of journeys" is certainly "the people of the cities." As for his words "its fish" here, this comes from al-Suyuti's poor abridgement, since "its fish" is an explanation of His words "the game of the sea," as passed in the report no. 12681, from Mujahid's explanation of the game of the sea. As for "its food," Mujahid explained it as "salted fish," as passed under no. 12720, and that is what is meant here. It is evident that he meant: "its food, salted fish = as a provision for you, for the people of the villages = and for the travelling caravan, the people of the cities = and the fish for all people." That is, His words "as a provision for you and for the travelling caravan" do not enter into explaining His words "Lawful for you is the game of the sea," but into explaining His words "and its food," which is salted fish. This is the correct view. What is in al-Durr al-Manthur and in the printed edition of this interpretation is a statement that does not hold together.]*

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 3 of 5):

As for what Mujahid said, that "the travellers" (al-sayyarah) are the people of the cities (amsar), it has no clear meaning, unless he meant by his words "they are the people of the cities" that they are the travellers from among the people of the cities. In that case, every traveller would be included, whether from the people of the cities or from the people of the villages. But as for "the travellers," we cannot understand it to mean those who remain in their cities. [[In the printed edition: "As for the travellers, it does not include those who remain in their cities, and this is a sick statement." In the manuscript, as I have established, it is unpointed, and this is the correct reading. The meaning: we do not understand it to mean those who remain in their cities. The author's use of "we cannot understand" (nu'aqilahu) in such expressions has occurred in earlier passages, which I cannot now recall.]]
* *
The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And the hunting of land game is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾
Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "And Allah has forbidden to you, O believers, the hunting of land game, as long as you are in the state of ihram (haram)," meaning: as long as you are in the state of ihram, not having come out of your ihram. [[See the explanation of "as long as" (ma dama) in earlier passages, 10:185, and the explanation of "forbidden" (harrama) in earlier passages, 7.]]
* *
Then the scholars differed regarding the meaning Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, intended by His words: "And the hunting of land game is forbidden to you."

Some of them said: By that He meant that He forbade us every aspect of the hunting of land game: hunting, eating, killing, selling, buying, keeping, and possessing it.

Those who said this:

12740 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from his father, who said: Uthman ibn Affan performed the Hajj, and Ali performed it with him. He said: Meat of game that a lawful (halal, non-muhrim) man had hunted was brought to Uthman, and he ate of it, but Ali did not eat. Uthman said: "By Allah, we did not hunt it, nor did we order it, nor did we point to it!" Ali said: "And the hunting of land game is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram." [[The report: 12740. Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Kufi, a mawla of the Banu Hashim, is truthful, but his memory declined in old age. It has passed as number 2028.
As for Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, his epithet was "Ubbah." He was born in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ placed a date on his palate (tahnik). He related from a group of the Companions. The authors of the six canonical collections related from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Abdullah ibn al-Harith an Nawfal," which is a plain error.
His father, al-Harith ibn Nawfal ibn al-Harith, related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from Aisha. The Prophet ﷺ appointed him over some affairs of Makkah, and he died in Basra during the caliphate of Uthman. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:232, and he attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Abu al-Shaykh.
His words "whom a lawful (halal) man hunted" mean: a man who is lawful, not in the state of ihram for Hajj.
This report will come again with a different wording and a different chain, at numbers 12745 and 12746.]]
12741 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Sammak, from Subay ibn Abdullah al-Absi, who said: Uthman ibn Affan sent Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith to al-Arud. [["Al-Arud" (with a fatha on the ayn) refers to Makkah and Madinah and their surroundings.]] He alighted at Qudayd, and a man from the people of Syria passed by him with a falcon and a sakr hawk. He borrowed them from him, and with them he hunted some ya'aqib. [["Al-Ya'aqib" is the plural of "Ya'qub," a bird, the male of the partridge (hajal) and the sand grouse (qata).]] He placed them in an enclosure. When Uthman passed by him, he cooked them and presented them to him. Uthman said: "Eat!" Some of them said: "Wait until Ali ibn Abi Talib comes, may Allah have mercy on him." When he came and saw what was in front of them, Ali said: "We will not eat of it!" Uthman said: "What is the matter with you that you do not eat?" He said: "It is game, and it is not lawful to eat it while I am in the state of ihram!" Uthman said: "Explain it to us!" Ali said: "O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram," and Uthman said: "Did we kill it?" So he recited to him: "Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers, and forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram." [[The report: 12741. Harun ibn al-Mughirah ibn Hakim al-Bajali is trustworthy, as has passed, numbers 6656 and 5526. Amr ibn Abi Qays al-Razi is trustworthy, as has passed, numbers 6887 and 9346.
As for Sammak, he is Sammak ibn Harb, who is trustworthy, as has passed many times.
Subay ibn Abdullah al-Absi related from Ali, and Sammak ibn Harb related from him. He is biographed in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 2/2/319 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/449, and neither of them mentions any criticism of him. His mention has passed in the note on number 7595 (an error occurred there in what I quoted from al-Tarikh al-Kabir, "on al-Furud," and its correct form is "on al-Arud," so let it be corrected there and in al-Bukhari's Tarikh). In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Subayh ibn Ubaydullah," and the correction is from al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim.
This report was related by al-Bukhari in abridged form in al-Tarikh, saying: "Hasan ibn Khalaf related to me, Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from Sammak, from Subayh ibn Abdullah al-Absi." This is the chain that follows this one.]]
12742 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir and Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Qanna related to us, both saying: Ishaq al-Azraq informed us, from Shurayk, from Sammak ibn Harb, from Subayh ibn Ubaydullah al-Absi, who said: Uthman ibn Affan appointed Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith over al-Arud. Then he mentioned something similar, and added to it, saying: Uthman remained as long as Allah willed him to remain, then he came, and it was said to him in Makkah: "Would you like to know about Ibn Abi Talib? A dried strip of meat (saffid himar) was presented to him, and he is eating from it!" [["Al-Saffid" is meat cut into thin broad strips until a piece becomes so thin that one sees through it, and it is stretched like a cloth and then dried in the sun until it is dry. When it is crushed, it becomes "al-qadid" (sun-dried meat). In the manuscript at this place it reads "tasaff," and in the following one "al-tasfif," unpointed, which is a mistaken writing; its correct form is in the printed edition.]] Uthman sent for him and asked him about eating the saffid. He said: "As for you, you eat it, and as for us, you forbid us?" He said: "It is game that was hunted before, and I am lawful, so there is no harm for me in eating it. And the game of that, meaning the ya'aqib, was hunted while I was in the state of ihram, and it was slaughtered while I was unlawful (haram)." [[The report: 12742. Ishaq al-Azraq is Ishaq ibn Yusuf ibn Mirdas al-Makhzumi al-Wasiti, as has passed, numbers 3339 and 4224. In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Abu Ishaq al-Azraq," which is an error and a slip of a copyist; it is correct in the chain of al-Bukhari that I quoted just before, in the takhrij of the report above.]]
12743 - Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan: that Umar ibn al-Khattab did not see any harm in the meat of game for the muhrim, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, disliked it. [[The report: 12743. Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id ibn Dhakwan al-Anbari, as has passed, numbers 2154, 6589, 6591, 6819.
As for Yunus, he is Yunus ibn Ubayd ibn Dinar al-Abdi, as has passed, numbers 2616, 4931.]]
12744 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that Ali disliked the meat of game for the muhrim in every circumstance.
12745 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith: that he witnessed Uthman and Ali being brought meat. Uthman ate, but Ali did not eat. Uthman said: "Did we hunt it, or was it hunted for us?" Ali recited this verse: "Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers, and forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram." [[The report: 12745. This report has passed through the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal from his father al-Harith ibn Nawfal, number 12740, and it will come at number 12747.]]
12746 - Yaqub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah informed us, from his father, who said: Uthman ibn Affan performed the Hajj, and Ali performed it with him. Meat of game that a lawful man had hunted was brought to him, and he ate of it while he was in the state of ihram, but Ali did not eat from it. Uthman said: "It was hunted before we entered the state of ihram!" Ali said to him: "We have dismounted, and our families are lawful for us. Are they lawful for us today?" [[In the printed edition: "and we have decided." In the manuscript: "and we have passed through" (mur), unpointed, and this, as I judge, is its reading.]] [[The report: 12746. Amr ibn Abi Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: his narrations are feeble; his hadith is written down but not used as proof, as has passed, numbers 3911, 12667.
This report will come with another chain at number 12755, abridged and not in this wording.]]
12747 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun related to us, from Amr, from Abd al-Karim, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal: that Ali was brought a piece of a donkey's rump while he was in the state of ihram, and he said: "I am in the state of ihram." [[The report: 12747. "Harun" is Harun ibn al-Mughirah, as has passed shortly before, number 12741.
"Amr" is Amr ibn Abi Qays, also passed, number 12741.
"Abd al-Karim" is Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, as has passed, numbers 892, 1566. In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "from Amr ibn Abd al-Karim," which is an error; no narrator among the transmitters bears that name.
This report has passed with both its chains, numbers 12740 and 12745.]]
12748 - Ibn Bazi' related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that he disliked it in every circumstance, while he was in the state of ihram. [[The report: 12748. "Sa'id" is Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah.
Ya'la ibn Hakim al-Thaqafi related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Nafi' the mawla of Ibn Umar, and others. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah, and al-Nasa'i declared him trustworthy, and Abu Hatim said: "There is no harm in him." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]
12749 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Ibn Juraij related to us, saying: Nafi' informed us: that Ibn Umar disliked every kind of game while he was in the state of ihram, whether it was hunted for him or not, and the washiqah and other things. [["Al-Washiqah" is meat boiled in water and salt in a single boil, not cooked through until it falls apart; then it is taken out and placed in a jubjubah, which is a camel's hide that has been tanned, and the meat is put into it, and it becomes provisions for them on their journeys.]]
12750 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, from Abdullah, who said: Nafi' informed me: that Ibn Umar would not eat game while in the state of ihram, even if it was hunted by a lawful man.
12751 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Ibn Juraij informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muslim ibn Yanaq informed me: that Tawus used to forbid the muhrim to eat game, the washiqah and other things, whether it was hunted for him or not.
12752 - Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Ash'ath related to us, saying: al-Hasan said: If someone hunts game and then enters the state of ihram, he may not eat of its meat until he is released from ihram. But if he eats of it while in the state of ihram, al-Hasan did not hold anything against him. [[The report: 12752. Khalid ibn al-Harith ibn Ubayd al-Hujaymi is trustworthy, as has passed, numbers 7507, 7818, 9878.]]
12753 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam and Harun related to us, from Anbasah, from Salim, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about game that a lawful man hunts: may the muhrim eat of it? He said: "I will mention to you something about that. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: 'O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram,' and He forbade killing it. Then He said: 'Whoever of you kills it intentionally, the compensation is the like of what he killed of the livestock,' then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: 'Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travellers.'" He said: "A man comes to the people of the sea and says: 'Feed me.' If he says: 'Fresh,' they cast their nets and hunt for him. And if he says: 'Feed me from your food,' they feed him from their salted fish. Then He said: 'And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram,' and it is forbidden to you, whether you hunted it or a lawful man hunted it." [[The report: 12753. This report has passed in abridged form, number 12713.]]
* *
Others said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only meant by His words: "And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram" what the muhrim newly hunts during his state of ihram, or slaughters, or what is newly done for him in that state. As for what a lawful man slaughtered, and for lawful men, there is no harm in the muhrim eating it. Likewise, what was in his possession before his state of ihram is not forbidden to him to keep.

Those who said this:

12754 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' related to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, saying: Qatadah related to us: that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related to him, from Abu Hurayrah: that he was asked about game hunted by a lawful man: may the muhrim eat it? He said: So he gave him a fatwa that he may eat it. Then he met Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, and informed him of what he had done, and he said: "If you had given them a fatwa other than this, I would have given you a headache." [[The report: 12754. Its chain is sound. Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur with slight variation in wording, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Shaybah. This report will come with other chains at numbers 12756, 12757, 12762.]]
12755 - Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi related to us, saying: Abu Awanah related to us, from Amr ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah have mercy on him, alighted at al-Araj while he was in the state of ihram. [["Al-Araj" (with a fatha and then a sukun) is a town on the road to Makkah from Madinah, on the pilgrims' main route.]] The owner of al-Araj presented him with qata. He said: He said to his companions: "Eat, for it was only hunted in my name." [[His words "it was only hunted in my name" mean: on my account. It is an old expression that persists on the tongues of common people to this day, and it is correct and eloquent. See what explains it in Malik's report in the Muwatta, p. 354, and it will come at number 12764.]] He said: So they ate, and he did not eat. [[The report: 12755. Amr ibn Abi Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf has passed shortly before, number 12746. It will come by another route at number 12771, with wording other than this, from Abu Salamah's own action.]]
12756 - Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that Abu Hurayrah was at al-Rabadhah, and they asked him about meat of game hunted by a lawful man, then he mentioned something like the hadith of Ibn Bazi' from Bishr. [[The reports: 12756 and 12757. These have passed at number 12754.]]
12757 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from Umar, similarly. [[The reports: 12756 and 12757. These have passed at number 12754.]]
12758 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Sha'tha', who said: I asked Ibn Umar about the meat of game that a lawful man gives as a gift to a muhrim. He said: "Umar ate it, and he did not see any harm in it." I said: "Will you eat it?" He said: "Umar is better than me." [[The reports: 12758 and 12759. "Abu Ishaq" is Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i al-Hamdani.
As for "Abu al-Sha'tha'," in report 12763 he is identified as "Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi," and he is not "Abu al-Sha'tha', Jabir ibn Zayd," who has passed at numbers 5136, 5472, 12406, 12725.
"Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi" is Yazid ibn Mahasir, a Kufan who related from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas. al-Bukhari biographed him in al-Kabir 4/2/363 under "Yazid ibn Mahasir," and said: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr gave him the kunyah," and he added nothing to that. Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him in 4/2/287 under "Yazid ibn Mahasir Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi," then said: "Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, Abu al-Anbas, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, and Abu Sinan al-Shaybani related from him." Then he returned and biographed him again at 4/2/391 and said: "Abu Sinan al-Shaybani and Sa'id ibn Sa'id al-Tha'labi related from him. I heard my father say this, and he said: 'He is not named, and he is Kufan.'" Ali ibn al-Madini said: "Abu al-Sha'tha' from whom Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu al-Anbas, and Abu Sinan related is al-Kindi, and not Sulaym [meaning Sulaym ibn Aswad al-Muharibi]. I heard my father say: Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi's name is Yazid ibn Mahasir." And he [Ibn al-Madini] disagreed with Ali in that.
The apparent meaning of this is that he is other than "Abu al-Sha'tha', Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi." But I saw that al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said, in the biography of "Abu al-Anbas" in al-Tahdhib 8:189, that he related from "Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Yazid al-Kindi." So I do not know whether al-Hafiz made a mistake or whether he was thus disputed over it.
This report was related by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 5:189 through the route of Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq: "I heard Abu al-Sha'tha'."
It will come at number 12763, in wording other than this, in abridged form. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 4 of 5):**

12759. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu al-Sha'tha', who said: I asked Ibn 'Umar about game that a lawful (non-Muharram) person hunted, of which a person in the state of ihram (muhrim) eats. He said: 'Umar used to eat it. I said: "And you?" He said: "'Umar was better than me."

12760. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Hisham, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man from the people of Syria asked me for a ruling (istaftani) about the meat of game that he had hunted while in ihram. I ordered him to eat it. Then I came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and said to him: "A man from the people of Syria asked me for a ruling about the meat of game that he had hunted while in ihram." He said: "And what did you rule for him?" I said: "I ruled that he should eat it." He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you had ruled otherwise, I would have struck you with the whip (al-durrah)!" And 'Umar said: "You were only forbidden to hunt it."

[[Report 12760: It has passed in abbreviated form as no. 12754, but not with this isnad. "Hisham" is Hisham Sahib al-Dastuwa'i. "Yahya" is Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Ta'i, a trustworthy narrator from whom the authors of the six canonical books narrated. It has passed as nos. 9189, 11505–11507. "Abu Salamah" is Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf; it has passed many times, including no. 12667. This report was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:188, through the route: "Hafs ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sulami, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Hisham," with similar wording.]]

12761. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Kharijah narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata', from Ka'b, who said: I came with some people who were in ihram, and we came upon the meat of a wild donkey. People asked me about eating it, and I ruled for them that they could eat it while they were in ihram. Then we came to 'Umar, and they informed him that I had ruled for them to eat the meat of the wild donkey while they were in ihram. 'Umar said: "I have appointed him as your commander until you return."

[[Report 12761: "Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam al-Khath'ami" is trustworthy, though some have criticized him; Muslim narrated from him. It has passed as nos. 1291 and 3001. "Kharijah" is Kharijah ibn Mus'ab ibn Kharijah al-Khurasani, who has passed as no. 9668. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad said there: "He is heavily disputed, and most scholars consider him weak, but the most balanced statement about him is that of al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1:499: 'Kharijah was criticized only for narrating from unknown transmitters; when he narrates from reliable, established transmitters, his narration is accepted.'" "Zayd ibn Aslam" is trustworthy and established; he has passed many times. "'Ata'" is 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who has passed many times. "Ka'b" is Ka'b al-Ahbar. This report is authentic; Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' p. 352, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, in a longer form. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 5:189 through Malik's route.]]

12762. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I passed by al-Rabadhah, and its people asked me about a muhrim eating what a lawful person had hunted. So I ruled for them that they could eat it. Then I met 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. He said: "With what did you rule for them?" [[In the manuscript: "bima aftaytahum" (with what did you rule for them), so I wrote it as "bim" according to what we have followed; in the printed edition: "fabim".]] He said: "I ruled for them that they should eat it." He said: "If you had ruled for them otherwise, I would have opposed you."

[[Report 12762: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib's hadith from Abu Hurayrah has passed through two other routes, nos. 12754 and 12756. This report was narrated by Malik in the Muwatta' p. 351, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with different wording; then he narrated it again through the route: "Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah: that he heard Abu Hurayrah narrate to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar," and its wording is closer to the wording of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) here.]]

12763. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from Yunus, from Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi, who said: I said to Ibn 'Umar: "What is your view about a group in ihram who met a group that is lawful, and they had the meat of game with them, and they either sold it to them or fed it to them?" He said: "It is lawful."

[[Report 12763: "Yunus" is Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i; he has passed many times, and see the commentary on nos. 12758 and 12759. "Abu al-Sha'tha' al-Kindi": his name and status were discussed earlier in the commentary on the two reports nos. 75 and 12, 12759, and his takhrij (sourcing) was given there.]]

12764. Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Hisham, meaning Ibn 'Urwah, narrated to us, saying: 'Urwah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib: that 'Abd al-Rahman told him that he performed 'umrah with 'Uthman ibn 'Affan in a caravan in which 'Amr ibn al-'As was present, until they stopped at al-Ruwayha'. A bird was brought to them while they were in ihram. 'Uthman said to them: "Eat, for I will not eat it!" 'Amr ibn al-'As said: "Are you ordering us to do what you yourself will not eat?" 'Uthman said: "If I did not think that it had been hunted for my sake, I would have eaten it!" [[In the printed edition: "sayd min ajli" (game for my sake); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] So the people ate.

[[Report 12764: "Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah al-Lakhmi" is an trustworthy, eminent Successor (tabi'i), and he is ascribed to his grandfather, so he is called "Yahya ibn Hatib"; it has passed as no. 8367. "'Abd al-Rahman" is his father, "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah al-Lakhmi," who belongs to the first generation of the Successors of the people of Medina and their jurists; he was trustworthy and narrated little. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:191, through the route of Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hatib, from his father, in similar wording.]]

12765. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: that al-Zubayr used to take provisions of wild animal meat while he was in ihram.

[[Report 12765: Its isnad is authentic. Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' p. 350, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: "That al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam used to take provisions of ṣafif (dried strips of meat) of gazelles while in ihram." That is his wording. By "the meat of wild animals" he meant gazelles, for they are wild animals.]]

12766. 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whatever is hunted or slaughtered while you are lawful (halal) is lawful for you, and whatever is hunted or slaughtered while you are unlawful (haram, i.e., in ihram) is forbidden to you.

12767. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whatever game is hunted while you are unlawful (in ihram) is forbidden to you, and whatever game is hunted while you are lawful is lawful for you.

12768. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the verse: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram﴾. So he made game forbidden to the muhrim, both hunting it and eating it, as long as he is in ihram. If the game was hunted before the man entered ihram, it is lawful. But if a person in ihram hunted it for a lawful person, it is not lawful for him to eat it.

12769. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: I asked Abu Bishr about a muhrim eating what a lawful person had hunted? He said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid used to say: "Whatever was hunted before he entered ihram, he may eat from it; and whatever was hunted after he entered ihram, he may not eat from it."

12770. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraydj narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' used to say, when he was asked publicly: Does a muhrim eat the "washiqah" (dried meat) and the dry thing? [["Washiqah" has been explained previously on p. 78, note 1.] He would say (privately, between himself and the questioner): "I cannot explain to you in a gathering. If it was slaughtered before we entered ihram, eat it; otherwise, do not sell its meat and do not buy it."

[[The manuscript has this report exactly like this, except that it reads "wa-in dhubiha qabla an tuhrim" with a waw. I am in doubt about the context of this report; I fear that something may have dropped from it, because the context seems to require that one say: "If he was asked publicly, he would say: No." But it is written this way, and I have not found it elsewhere, so I have left it as it is until someone who finds it corrects it.]]

* *

Others said: Allah, exalted is He, meant by His saying: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram﴾ only that hunting it is forbidden to you. They said: As for buying it from someone who owns it, slaughtering it, and eating it, after it has become his property in a way other than hunting it himself, selling and buying it is permissible. They said: The prohibition from Allah, exalted is His mention, concerns hunting it while in the state of ihram, and nothing beyond that.

The mention of who said that:

12771. 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Yahya informed me that Abu Salamah bought a sandgrouse (qata) while he was at al-'Araj and in ihram, and Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir was with him, and he ate it. [[In the printed edition: "fa-akalahu" (he ate it); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]]
The people criticized him for that.

[[Report 12771: "'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh al-Khuza'i" is the teacher of al-Tabari; it has passed as nos. 1909, 4612, 4923. "Ibn Abi Maryam" is Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, which has passed as nos. 160, 5455, 8335. "Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi" has passed as nos. 3877, 4330. "Yahya" is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Qays al-Ansari; it has passed as nos. 4859, 9679. "Abu Salamah" is Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf; he has passed recently.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter, in our view, is to say: Allah, exalted is His mention, made the prohibition of every kind of hunting of land game general for the muhrim during his state of ihram, without specifying any part of it over another. So every form of hunting is forbidden to the muhrim as long as he is in ihram: selling it, buying it, hunting it, killing it, and other forms of it. The exception is if he finds it already slaughtered by a lawful person for another lawful person, in which case it is permissible for him to eat it, based on the authentic report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which:

12772. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated it to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Juraydj; and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to me, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Juraydj narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed me, from Mu'adh ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman, from his father 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman, who said: We were with Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah while we were in ihram, and a bird was presented to us as a gift. Some of us ate it, and some of us refrained out of caution and did not eat. When Talhah woke up, he approved (wafaqa) the one who ate. [[In the printed edition: "wafaqa man akala" (approved those who ate); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct and agrees with what is in Sahih Muslim. The phrase "wafaqa man akala" means: he prayed for him to be successful and endorsed his action.]] And he said: "We ate it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

[[Report 12772: "Yahya ibn Sa'id" is al-Qattan. "Makki ibn Ibrahim ibn Bashir ibn Farqad al-Tamimi" is the memorizer (al-Hafiz); the authors of the six canonical books narrated from him; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Mu'adh ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Uthman al-Taymi" is trustworthy. His father "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah al-Taymi" is the "Shariba al-Dhahab" (drinker of gold), a Companion who embraced Islam on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and it was said on the day of the Conquest. This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 8:111–112, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:188.]]

* *

If someone says: What do you say about what was reported regarding al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah, that he presented the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the leg of a wild donkey dripping blood, and he returned it, saying: "We are in ihram" [[The hadith of al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih through several routes, 8:103–106, and in al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:191, 194; the takhrij is fully given there.]] = and regarding what was reported from 'A'ishah: that the "washiqah" of a gazelle was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in ihram, and he returned it [[The report of 'A'ishah was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6:40. The explanation of "washiqah" has passed previously on p. 78, note 1.]] and other similar reports?

It is said: In none of these reports that came with this meaning is there evidence that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned any of it after the slaughterer had slaughtered it while he was lawful for a lawful person, and then it was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was unlawful, and he returned it and said: "It is not lawful for us, because we are in ihram." Rather, it only mentions that game meat was presented as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he returned it. It is possible that his returning it was because the slaughterer slaughtered it, or the hunter hunted it, for his sake (ﷺ) while he was in ihram.

The hadith of Jabir from the Prophet ﷺ clarifies all of this by his saying: "The meat of game [of the land] is lawful for the muhrim, except what he hunts or what is hunted for him." [[The hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:190; see what he said about it there. al-Suyuti narrated it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:333 and said: "Ahmad and al-Hakim narrated it and declared it sahih." I added what is between the brackets from the hadith, which is omitted from the manuscript and the printed edition.]]

Since both reports are authentic in their transmission, it is obligatory to affirm both of them and to direct each one toward its correct interpretation: that his returning what he returned was because it had been hunted for his sake; and his permission regarding everything that he permitted to eat from it was because it had not been hunted for a muhrim nor hunted by a muhrim. Thus the meaning of both reports is consistent.

* *

They differed about the description of the game which Allah, exalted is He, meant by the prohibition in His saying: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram﴾.

Some of them said: "The game of the land" refers to everything that lives on land and in the sea, while "the game of the sea" is what lives in water and not on land, and shelters in it.

The mention of who said that:

12773. Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram﴾: He said: "Whatever lives on land and in the sea, do not hunt it; and whatever's life is in water, that is permitted." [[In the printed edition: "la tasiduhu" (do not hunt it); in the manuscript: "wa-la tasduhu" (and do not hunt it); this is the correct reading.]]

[[Report 12773: In the manuscript: "hal kana hayatuhu fi al-ma' fa-dhalika" (if its life was in the water, that is it), and I do not know whether the "hal" here is correct; what is in the printed edition seems closer to the correct reading. This report was narrated by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:332 in a similar form to what is in the printed edition, and he attributed it additionally to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh.]]

12774. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj informed us, from 'Ata', who said: "Whatever lives on land, if the muhrim hits it, he must pay its compensation (jaza'), such as the tortoise, the crab, and the frogs."

12775. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj, from 'Ata', who said: "Everything that lives on land and in the sea, if the muhrim hits it, he owes expiation (kaffarah)."

12776. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: We went out on pilgrimage with us was a man from the people of al-Sawad (Iraq) who had bundles of water birds. My father said to him when we entered ihram: "Set this aside from us."

[[Report 12776: "Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Kufi" has passed recently as no. 12740, and he had some weakness in his memory after he grew old. "'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr al-Asadi" narrated from his father and from 'Ikrimah, and Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from him; he is trustworthy but rarely narrates. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "'Abd al-Malik 'an Sa'id ibn Jubayr," which is a plain error.]]

12777. And Abu Kurayb narrated it to us again, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad say: Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Ata': that he disliked for the muhrim to slaughter the Zanji chicken, because it has a root on land. [[The report in the manuscript and printed edition reads: "wa-haddathana bihi Abu Kurayb marratan ukhra" (and Abu Kurayb narrated it to us again), which indicates that he would narrate the earlier hadith from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr from his father, but the matter differs greatly. It is actually from "Hajjaj from 'Ata'," and its meaning is totally unrelated to the preceding hadith. Rather, its meaning is that of hadith no. 12775, and it is also from Hajjaj from 'Ata', but that is from the narration of "Ibn Humayd," not from the narration of "Abu Kurayb." This shows that it cannot be correct that this latter report was displaced from its place. I fear that the copyist became confused, and so the correction of this place became confused.]]

* *

Some said: The game of the land is what lives mostly on land more than in the sea.

The mention of who said that:

12778. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraydj informed us, saying: I asked 'Ata' about Ibn al-Ma' (a water-bird) — is it land game or sea game? And about similar ones? He said: "Wherever it mostly is, that is its game."

12779. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to me, from Sufyan, from a man, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: "Mostly where it lays its eggs, that is where it belongs."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, to Whom you will be gathered﴾ [96].

Abu Ja'far said: This is a warning from Allah, exalted is His mention, to His creation to beware of His punishment for their disobedience.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 5 of 5):

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Fear God, O people, and be wary of Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you of His obligations [[See the entry on "ittaqa" (to fear/guard against) in the earlier word indexes, under (w-q-y).]] and in what He has forbidden you in these verses which He sent down to your Prophet ﷺ: the prohibition of wine, gambling, the stone altars, and the divining arrows, and the prohibition of hunting and killing game on land while you are in the state of ihram and at other times. Indeed, to God is your return and your final destination, [[See the entry on "al-hashr" (gathering) in the earlier volumes: 4: 228-229, 6/9: 425.]] so He will punish you for your disobedience to Him, and He will recompense you, rewarding you for your obedience to Him.
* *
On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands﴾
Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support (qiwam) for people who have no support from a ruler who would restrain the strong among them from the weak, [[See the entry on "ja'ala" (to make/appoint) in the earlier volumes: 3: 18.]] the wrongdoer from the one he wrongs, and the evil-doer from the good-doer. "And the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands": by each of these He restrained some of them from others, since they had no support other than these, and He made them markers of their religion and the means of the welfare of their affairs.
* *
As for "al-Ka'bah," it was said that it was named "Ka'bah" because of its squareness (tarbi'uha).
* *
Those who said this:
12780 - Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The Ka'bah was only named "al-Ka'bah" because it is square.
12781 - Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Hisham ibn al-Qasim told us, from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib, from al-Nadr ibn Arabi, from Ikrimah, who said: The Ka'bah was only named "al-Ka'bah" because of its squareness. [[The narration 12781: Hisham ibn al-Qasim ibn Muslim al-Laythi, Abu al-Nadr, the imam and hafiz, has passed as no. 184 and 8239. And Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Wadah al-Qada'i, trustworthy and reliable, has passed as nos. 8239 and 12310.]]
* *
It was also said "qiyaman lil-nas" with a yā' (qiyām), though the root is of the w-type, because of the kasrah on the qāf, which is the first radical of the verb. So the middle radical was changed into a yā' because of the kasrah on its first radical, just as it is said of the verbal noun: "qumtu qiyaman" (I stood, standing) and "sumtu siyaman" (I fasted, fasting). The middle radical of the verb, which is a wāw, was changed into a yā' because of the kasrah on its first radical. In origin it is "qumtu qiwaman" and "sumtu siwaman." Likewise His words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a qiyam for the people": its wāw was changed into a yā', though it is qiwam. [[See the entry on "qiyam" in the earlier volumes: 7: 568-569.]]
This form has also come in their speech with the original wāw, as the rajaz poet (Humayd al-Arqat) said:
"Qiwam dunya wa qiwam din" [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah: 1: 177.]]
So he used the wāw, in its original form.
* *
God, may His remembrance be exalted, made the Ka'bah, the sacred month, the offerings, and the garlands a support for those among the Arabs who would hold these sacred and honour them, [[In the printed edition: "yahtarim dhalika" (respect that), and the correct reading is from the manuscript. In the manuscript: "yu'tihi" (give it), and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] like a ruler by whom the affairs of his followers are sustained.
As for "al-Ka'bah," it refers to the whole sacred precinct (al-haram). God named it "haram" (sacred/forbidden) because He forbade that its game be hunted, its grass be cut, or its trees be felled. [["Al-khalā": soft, fresh vegetation. "Ikhtalā al-khalā": to cut and pull it up. "A'ḍada al-shajarah": to cut the tree.]] We have already explained this with its evidence in an earlier place. [[See what has passed: 3: 45-51.]]
* *
As for His words "and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands": He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He also made the sacred month, the offerings, and the garlands a support for the people, just as He made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for them.
* *
The "people" for whom He made these a support are a matter of disagreement.
Some said: God made that a support for all people in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah).
* *
Others said: Rather, He meant only the Arabs.
* *
The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) agreed with what we have said regarding the interpretation of "qiwam."
Those who said that God, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by His words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people" the qiwam, in the manner we have stated:
12782 - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: someone who heard Khusayf narrating told us, from Mujahid, regarding "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people," who said: a support for the people.
12783 - Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ubayd Allah told us, from Israil, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding "a support for the people," who said: a welfare for their religion.
12784 - Hannad told us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people," who said: at a time when they did not hope for Paradise nor fear Hellfire, and God strengthened this with Islam.
12785 - Hannad told me, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah told us, from Israil, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, his words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people," who said: a firmness for their religion.
12786 - Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Israil, from Abu al-Haytham, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.
12787 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people," who said: its support is that whoever faces towards it is safe.
12788 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands," meaning a support for their religion and markers for their pilgrimage.
12789 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands": God made these four a support for the people; it is the support of their affairs.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Although the wording of these sayings differs among those who said them, their meanings return to what we have said on this, namely that the "qiwam" of a thing is that by which its welfare is achieved, just as the great king is the support of his subjects and those under his authority, since he manages their affairs and restrains their wrongdoer from the one he wrongs, and repels from them the harm of those who seek to harm and oppose them. Likewise, the Ka'bah, the sacred month, the offerings, and the garlands were the support of the affairs of the Arabs by which their welfare was achieved in the time of ignorance, and in Islam they are, for its adherents, the markers of their pilgrimage and rites, the direction of their prayers, and their qiblah, by facing which their obligation is completed.
* *
The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) as a body also said in agreement with what we have said on this:
12790 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Jami' ibn Hammad told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding his words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands": barriers that God placed between people in the time of ignorance. [[It seems to me that the correct reading here and in the following is "alqāhā Allāh" (God placed them) with the lām, but it is so in the manuscript.]] A man who committed any crime and then sought refuge in the sacred precinct would not be seized or approached. And if a man met the killer of his father in the sacred month, he would not confront him or approach him. And when a man wanted to go to the House, he would wear a garland of hair, which protected him and kept him from people. And when he departed, he would wear a garland of idhkhir or of the bark of the samur tree, which kept him from people until he reached his family. [["Al-idhkhir": a fragrant grass with which houses are roofed over wooden beams, and which is ground and added to perfume. "Al-liḥā'": the bark of a tree. "Al-samur" (with a fatḥah on the sīn and a ḍammah on the mīm): a tree of the acacia kind.]] These are barriers that God placed between people in the time of ignorance.
12791 - Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "God has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a support for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings, and the garlands": the people as a whole had kings among them who repelled some of them from others. He said: There were no kings among the Arabs who repelled some of them from others, so God, may He be exalted, made the Sacred House a support for them, by which some of them are repelled from others, and the sacred month likewise, by which God repels some of them from others through the sacred months, and the garlands. He said: A man would meet the killer of his brother or his cousin and would not confront him. All of this has been abrogated (nusikh).
12792 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "and the garlands": some people used to wear bark of trees in the time of ignorance when they wanted to perform the Hajj, and they were recognised by it.
* *
We have already presented the explanation concerning the mention of "the sacred month," "the offerings," and "the garlands" in what has passed, sufficient to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[See the entry on "al-shahr al-ḥarām" in the earlier volumes: 3: 575-579, 4: 299-300 and what follows, 9: 466. And the entry on "al-hady" in the earlier volumes: 4: 24-25, 9: 466, 11: 22. And the entry on "al-qalā'id" in the earlier volumes: 9: 467-470.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ (97).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words "That," the Exalted means His making the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of standing (qiyam) for the people, and the sacred month, the offering animals, and the garlands. The Exalted says: I have made that a means of standing for you, O people, so that you may know that He who has brought about for you what sustains your worldly interests, [out of] His knowledge of your benefits and harms, knows likewise all that is in the heavens and in the earth, of what contains the welfare of your present and your future; and so that you may know that He is "Knowing" of all things, nothing of your affairs and deeds is hidden from Him, and He records them against you, until He recompenses the good-doer among you for his good and the evil-doer among you for his evil. [[See the explanation of "Knowing" in the earlier lexical indexes.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (98)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Know, O people, that your Lord, who knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and nothing of the secrets of your deeds or their open manifestations is hidden from Him, and He counts them against you in order to recompense you for them, is severe in His punishment toward whoever disobeys Him and rebels against Him in His disobedience to Him; and He is Forgiving toward the sins of whoever obeys Him and turns back to Him, covering them over for him and not exposing him for them; and He is Merciful toward him, not punishing him for the sins that preceded his repentance and his turning back from them. [See the explanation of "severe in punishment," "Forgiving," and "Merciful" in the earlier linguistic indexes.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The Messenger's duty is only to convey (the message), and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾ (99)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a threat and warning from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Our Messenger, whom We have sent to you, O people, is not responsible for warning you of Our punishment before a severe torment, and for giving you notice of what cuts off your proofs, except that he conveys Our message to you; then, to Us is the reward for obedience, and upon Us is the punishment for disobedience. ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾: meaning, the obedient among you, who accepts Our message and acts by what We have commanded you to do, is not hidden from Us, nor is the one who disobeys, who refuses Our message and abandons acting by what We have commanded, because We know what the doer among you has done, which he manifests with his limbs and expresses with his tongue. ﴿And what you conceal﴾ means what you hide within yourselves of faith and disbelief, or certainty and doubt, or hypocrisy. [See the explanation of "reveal" and "conceal" in the linguistic indexes under "bada" and "katama."]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever is like this, nothing is hidden from Him of the inmost thoughts of hearts and the outward actions of souls, of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and in His hand are the reward and the punishment. Therefore He is worthy to be feared and obeyed, and not disobeyed.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (98)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Know, O people, that your Lord, who knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and nothing of the secrets of your deeds or their open manifestations is hidden from Him, and He counts them against you in order to recompense you for them, is severe in His punishment toward whoever disobeys Him and rebels against Him in His disobedience to Him; and He is Forgiving toward the sins of whoever obeys Him and turns back to Him, covering them over for him and not exposing him for them; and He is Merciful toward him, not punishing him for the sins that preceded his repentance and his turning back from them. [See the explanation of "severe in punishment," "Forgiving," and "Merciful" in the earlier linguistic indexes.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is a threat and warning from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Our Messenger, whom We have sent to you, O people, is not responsible for warning you of Our punishment before a severe torment, and for giving you notice of what cuts off your proofs, except that he conveys Our message to you; then, to Us is the reward for obedience, and upon Us is the punishment for disobedience. ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾: meaning, the obedient among you, who accepts Our message and acts by what We have commanded you to do, is not hidden from Us, nor is the one who disobeys, who refuses Our message and abandons acting by what We have commanded, because We know what the doer among you has done, which he manifests with his limbs and expresses with his tongue. ﴿And what you conceal﴾ means what you hide within yourselves of faith and disbelief, or certainty and doubt, or hypocrisy. [See the explanation of "reveal" and "conceal" in the linguistic indexes under "bada" and "katama."]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever is like this, nothing is hidden from Him of the inmost thoughts of hearts and the outward actions of souls, of what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and in His hand are the reward and the punishment. Therefore He is worthy to be feared and obeyed, and not disobeyed.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 100:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of the evil may please you.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: The bad and the good, the righteous and the wicked, and the obedient and the disobedient are not equal [[See the discussion of "istawa" (to be equal) above, 9:85; the discussion of "al-khabith" (the evil/bad) above, 5:558–559 and 7:424, 527; and the discussion of "al-tayyib" (the good) above, 10:513, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿even though the abundance of the evil may please you﴾, meaning: the disobedient and the one obedient to God are not equal in the sight of God, even if the people of disobedience are many and you are impressed by their number, because the people of obedience to God are the successful, who win God's reward on the Day of Resurrection even if they are few, unlike the people of His disobedience, who are the losers and the failed even if they are many.

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Do not be impressed by the multitude of those who disobey God, whom He gives respite and does not hasten to punish, for the good outcome belongs to the people of His obedience in His sight, not to them, as related:

12793 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "The evil and the good are not equal, even though the abundance of the evil may please you," he said: "The evil are the polytheists, and the good are the believers."

* *

Although this statement is addressed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), what is meant by it is some of his followers, as indicated by His words: ﴿So fear God, O people of understanding, that you may succeed.﴾

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So fear God, O people of understanding, that you may succeed (100)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Fear God by obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you, and beware lest Satan gain mastery over you through your being impressed by the abundance of the evil, so that you become of them. ﴿O people of understanding﴾ means by this the people of intellect and judgment, who understood God's signs and recognized the places of His proofs. [[See the discussion of "ulu al-albab" (people of understanding) above, 3:383; 4:162; 5:580; 6:211; and the note on the earlier passages contains an error, corrected here.]] ﴿that you may succeed﴾, meaning: fear God so that you may prosper, that is, so that you may attain success in seeking what He has.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of questions which some people would ask him, sometimes to test him and sometimes to mock him. One of them would say to him, "Who is my father?" and another, when his she-camel had strayed, would say, "Where is my she-camel?" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, said to them: Do not ask about such things, such as the question which 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah asked him, "Who is my father?" ﴿if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾, meaning: if We were to disclose to you the reality of what you ask about, its disclosure and manifestation would distress you.

Reports from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) have been widely transmitted in agreement with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

**12794.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Baghayl narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Juwayriyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Abbas said to a Bedouin of the Banu Sulaym: "Do you know about what this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾?" — until he finished the verse. He said: "There were people who would ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in mockery. A man would say, 'Who is my father?' and a man whose she-camel had strayed would say, 'Where is my she-camel?' So Allah revealed this verse concerning them."

[[Report 12794: "Hafs ibn Baghayl al-Hamdani al-Murhibi" is trustworthy; he was mentioned earlier under no. 9639. In the printed edition here it reads "Ba'd Banu Nufayl," and in the manuscript "Ba'd ibn Nufayl," both of which are errors. Likewise "Hafs ibn Nufayl" with the letter fa' in Fath al-Bari is an error; the name is "Baghayl" with a ghayn, in diminutive form.

**12795.** Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amir and Abu Dawud narrated to us, both saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The people questioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until they pressed him with questions. Others said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of a questioner who asked him about something concerning the matter of the Hajj.

Mention of those who said that:

**12803.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And for Allah, of mankind, is a duty to visit the House, for whoever is able to find a way thereto﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 97], they said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it every year?" He was silent. Then they said: "Is it every year?" He was silent. Then he said: "No. Had I said 'Yes,' it would have become obligatory!" So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾.

[[Report 12803: "Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi," the perfumer of Kufa, the teacher of Ahmad. He narrated from Fitr ibn Khalifah and 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and Ahmad declared him trustworthy. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "His hadith is written down." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir 4/1/347, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/180.
"'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la ibn 'Amir al-Tha'labi," Abu al-Hasan al-Ahwal. al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi declared him trustworthy, and al-Daraqutni said: "He is not strong." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. 905, through the line of Mansur ibn Wardan al-Asadi, from 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from his father, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from 'Ali, in the same wording as Abu Ja'far's narration but without a continuous chain.
al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir from Abu Sa'id, from Mansur ibn Wardan, with its chain in the same wording as Ahmad's, and said: "This is a good, strange hadith from the hadith of 'Ali."
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:293, 294, through the line of Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Ishaq al-Tamimi, from Mukhawwal ibn Ibrahim al-Nahdi, from Mansur ibn Wardan. al-Hakim said nothing about it, and al-Dhahabi said in his commentary: "Mukhawwal is a Rafidi; 'Abd al-A'la is Ibn 'Amir, whom Ahmad declared weak."
Ibn Majah narrated it in his Sunan, no. 2884, through the line of Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Mansur ibn Wardan, in similar wording.
Ibn Kathir took it out in his Tafsir 2:195/3:250, and mentioned the report of al-Tirmidhi and what he said, then said: "There is doubt about what he said, because al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Bakhtari did not hear from 'Ali."
"My brother, al-Sayyid Ahmad, said in the commentary on the Musnad (no. 905): 'Its chain is weak, due to its discontinuity, and due to the weakness of 'Abd al-A'la ibn 'Amir al-Tha'labi.'"]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 101 (part 2 of 3):

12804 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, from Ibn ʿIyad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, "God has prescribed the Hajj for you." A man said, "Every year, O Messenger of God?" He turned away from him until he had come back two or three times. Then he said, "Who is the questioner?" He said, "So-and-so!" He said, "By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I had said 'yes,' it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory upon you, you would not have been able to bear it, and if you had left it, you would have disbelieved!" So God revealed this verse: "O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you..." up to the end of the verse. [[The narration: 12804 - "ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman al-Ta'i al-Razi", al-Ashall. Trustworthy; it has passed under nos. 2028, 2030, 2254, 8156, 8157, 8161. In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman", and the correct form is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir.
"Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri" is weak, a lenient transmitter of hadith, biographed in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 1/1/326, where he is weakened; Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/131; and al-Dhahabi's Mizan al-I'tidal 1: 31.
"Abu ʿIyad" is ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad al-ʿAnsi, said also to be ʿUmayr ibn al-Aswad, trustworthy, passed under no. 11255. In the printed edition it reads "Ibn ʿIyad", and the correct form is from the manuscript.
This report is weak in its isnad, because of the weakness of Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri.
al-Jassas mentioned it in Ahkam al-Qur'an 2: 483, and Ibn Kathir quoted it from this place in his Tafsir 3: 250.
al-Suyuti takes it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 335, adding its attribution to al-Firyabi and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

12805 - Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to me, saying: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) addressed us and said: "O people, God has prescribed the Hajj for you." Mihsan al-Asadi stood up and said: "Every year, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Indeed, if I had said 'yes,' it would have become obligatory; and if it had become obligatory and then you abandoned it, you would have gone astray. Be silent about me as I have been silent about you, for those before you were destroyed by their questioning and their disputing with their prophets!" So God, exalted, revealed: "O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you," to the end of the verse. [[The narration: 12805 - "Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq al-ʿAbdi", trustworthy, passed under nos. 1591, 2575, 9951.
His father "ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq" is also trustworthy, passed under nos. 1591, 2575.
In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "ibn al-Husayn ibn Shaqiq", which is an error.
"al-Husayn ibn Waqid al-Marwazi", trustworthy, passed under nos. 4810, 6311.
"Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Qurashi al-Jumahi" Abu al-Harith, whom the authors of the six books narrated from. He narrated from Abu Hurayrah, ʿAyshah and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/82, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/257.
This report has been narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, both abridged and in full. The abridged version through the route of Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abu Hurayrah does not mention the Hajj, the question, or the questioner, in the Musnad 2: 447, 448, via Waki from Hammad from Muhammad ibn Ziyad. Then he narrated it at 2: 467 via ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi from Hammad ibn Salamah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad.
Then he narrated it in full, mentioning the Hajj, the question about it, and the questioner as "a man" whose name is not specified in the report (2: 508), via Yazid ibn Harun from al-Rabiʿ ibn Muslim al-Qurashi from Muhammad ibn Ziyad. It does not mention the verse or its revelation.
Through this route Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (9: 100), from Zuhayr ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn Harun, similarly.
al-Bukhari also narrated it abridged (al-Fath 13: 219-224) via Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 4: 325, 326 via ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Muslim al-Qurashi, and via ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father, from Yazid ibn Harun.
al-Suyuti takes it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 335, adding its attribution to Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh, similar to the narration of Abu Ja'far here.
In all of these, it reads "a man said," unspecified, without naming him. Al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Muslim (9: 101): "This man is al-Aqra' ibn Habis." This is specified in other narrations, and the narration in which it is specified is from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, in which: "Then al-Aqra' ibn Habis stood up and said..." It was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad through several routes from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, at nos. 2304, 2642, 3303, 3510, 3520. Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 4: 326.
Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in al-Fath (13: 220), pointed to the hadith of Muslim and what it contains of the addition of the question about the Hajj, then said: "al-Daraqutni took it out abridged and added to it 'O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would trouble you.' It has a supporting narration from Ibn ʿAbbas, in al-Tabari's Tafsir." I say: he means the earlier narration no. 12794, not this one. Al-Hafiz did not point to the report of al-Husayn ibn Waqid from Muhammad ibn Ziyad.
The identity of the questioner has been disputed on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Waqid. In this report it is "Mihsan al-Asadi," and in the following one, "ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi." Ibn Kathir mentioned in his Tafsir 3: 250, 251 the earlier report no. 12804, then said: "Then Ibn Jarir narrated it through the route of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah, and said: 'Mihsan al-Asadi stood up,' and in another narration through this route: 'ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan,' and this is more similar," and he added nothing further.
This is a disagreement over the name of the man: "al-Aqra' ibn Habis" or "ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi". The most reliable is that it was "al-Aqra' ibn Habis", since it came through sound isnads whose soundness is beyond doubt. As for the flaw in the narration of Abu Ja'far, it is that "al-Husayn ibn Waqid al-Marwazi" is trustworthy; al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him," and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. But Ibn Hibban said: "Among the best of people, and he sometimes errs in narrations." Ahmad said: "There are additions in his hadith, I do not know what they are!" and shook his hand. al-Saji said: "There is a problem with him; he is truthful but makes mistakes."
The narration of the trustworthy memorizers from "Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah" does not mention "ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan" and does not specify the man. But al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and specified the man, contradicting the specification reported through sound routes from Ibn ʿAbbas that it was "al-Aqra' ibn Habis." This is from the doing of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, which confirms what Ahmad and others said: that in his hadith there are additions whose nature is not known. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

12806 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) addressed us= he mentioned the like of it, except that he stood up: "ʿUkkashah ibn Mihsan al-Asadi stood up." [[The narration: 12806 - it is a repetition of the earlier narration, and I have discussed it there.]]

12807 - Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abu Zayd ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ghamr narrated to us, saying: Abu Mati' Muʿawiyah ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Safwan ibn ʿAmr, who said: Salim ibn ʿAmir narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among the people and said: "The Hajj has been prescribed for you!" A man from the Bedouins stood up and said: "Every year?" He said: The speech of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was obstructed, and he fell silent, and became angered, and he remained silent for a long time, then he spoke and said: "Who is the questioner?" The Bedouin said: "It is I!" He said: "Woe to you! What makes you secure that I would say 'yes'? If I had said 'yes,' it would have become obligatory, and if it had become obligatory you would have disbelieved!
