Though I incline to think Abu Ja'far's context requires his phrasing to be: "and when you create from clay as the form of a bird, meaning by 'create': work and shape 'from clay as the form of a bird': as the image of a bird: 'by My permission': meaning by My help in that... and with knowledge from Me of it" — nevertheless, I have left what is in the manuscript as it is.] ﴿by My permission﴾, meaning by "create": work and shape, ﴿from clay as the form of a bird by My permission﴾, means: as the image of a bird, ﴿by My permission﴾, meaning: by My help in that and with knowledge from Me of it; ﴿then you breathe into it﴾, means: you breathe into the form, so the form and the image become a bird ﴿by My permission﴾; ﴿and you heal the blind﴾, means: you cure "the blind," who is one who cannot see anything, whose sight is obliterated; ﴿and the leper by My permission﴾.

* *

I have already explained the meanings of these terms earlier in this book with their evidence, with what suffices from repeating it here. [See the explanation of "cradle" in what preceded: 6:417; and "maturity" 6:417, 418; the explanation of "Book" and "wisdom" in the lexical indices (k-t-b) and (h-k-m); as for the explanation of "create" and "form" in this sense, he did not mention it earlier, though it passed at 6:424; the explanation of "heal" 6:428; the explanation of "blind" 6:428–430; as for "leper," he did not explain it; the explanation of "permission" in what preceded 10:145, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs﴾ means: remember also My favour upon you by My restraining the Children of Israel from you when I held them back from you, [See the explanation of "restraint" in what preceded: 8:548, 579 / 9:29 / 10:101], ﴿and they had resolved to kill you﴾, ﴿when you came to them with clear proofs﴾, means: when you came to them with evidence and miraculous signs for your prophethood, [See the explanation of "clear proofs" in the lexical indices (b-y-n).] and the reality of what I sent you with to them. [In the printed edition: "wa haqiyat ma arsaltuka", changed as it has been done many times before; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript; see what preceded 10:242, note 1, and the references there.] ﴿Then those who disbelieved among them said﴾, means, exalted is His remembrance: those among the Children of Israel who denied your prophethood and called you a liar said ﴿This is nothing but clear magic.﴾

* *

The reciters differed in reading this.

The reading of the people of Medina and some of the people of Basra is: ﴿in hadha illa sihrun mubin﴾, meaning: it makes clear to whoever sees it and looks at it that it is magic that has no reality.

* *

And the common reciters of Kufa recited it: ﴿in hadha illa sahirun mubin﴾, meaning: "this is not," referring to Jesus, ﴿but a clear sorcerer﴾, He says: he makes clear by his deeds and by what he brings of these wondrous matters about himself, that he is a sorcerer and not a truthful prophet. [See the explanation of "clear" in the lexical indices (b-y-n).]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is that these are two well-known readings, both sound in meaning, agreeing and not contradicting. This is because whoever is described with the act of "magic" is described as "a sorcerer," and whoever is described as "a sorcerer" is described with the act of "magic." The act points to its doer, the attribute points to what it describes, what is described points to its attribute, and the doer points to his act. So whichever reading the reciter uses, he is correct in his recitation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 111:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples, saying: Believe in Me and in My Messenger, they said: We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says: Remember also, O Jesus, when I cast [into their hearts] [[See the explanation of "awhā" (inspired) in earlier passages: 6:405, 406; 9:399.]] "to the disciples" (al-Hawariyyun), who were the helpers (wuzara') of Jesus in his religion.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of this and why they were called "al-Hawariyyun" (the disciples), in an earlier place, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "al-Hawariyyun" in earlier passages: 6:449–451.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed in their wording concerning His saying "And when I inspired", though their meanings are agreed.

Some of them said, in the following manner:

12992 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And when I inspired the disciples", he says: "I cast into their hearts."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "I inspired them."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the sense of the speech is then: "And when I cast to the disciples that they should believe in Me and in My Messenger Jesus, and they said: 'We believe'," meaning: we have affirmed what You commanded us to believe, O our Lord. "And bear witness" against us "that we are Muslims", meaning: bear witness against us that we are submissive to You in humility, listening and obeying Your command.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿When the disciples said: "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" He said: "Fear God, if you are believers."﴾ (5:112)**

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: Remember, O Jesus, also My blessing upon you, when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and in My Messenger, when they said to Jesus, son of Mary: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" The second ﴿when﴾ (idh) is connected to "I inspired."

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words "can your Lord":

A group of the Companions (ṣaḥāba) and the Successors (tābiʿūn) recited it as ﴿Can you﴾ with the taʾ, and ﴿your Lord﴾ in the accusative, meaning: "Can you ask your Lord?" or "Can you call upon your Lord?" or "Are you able and willing to call upon Him?" They said: The disciples were not doubting that God, may His remembrance be exalted, was able to send that down to them; rather, they said to Jesus: "Are you able to do that?" [[See Maʿānī al-Qurʾān of al-Farrāʾ, 1:325.]]

12993 – Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from Ibn Abī Mulayka, who said: ʿĀʾisha said: "The disciples did not doubt that God was able to send down a table upon them, but they said: 'O Jesus, can you ask your Lord?'"

12994 – Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf al-Taghlibī narrated to me, saying: al-Qāsim ibn Sallām narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Jābir ibn Yazīd ibn Rifāʿa, from Ḥassān ibn Mukhāriq, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: that he recited it thus, ﴿Can you ask your Lord﴾, and he said: "You are able to ask your Lord." And he said: "Do you not see that they are believers?" [[The report 12994: "Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf al-Taghlibī" passed shortly before as no. 12957. In the printed edition here also appeared "al-Thaʿlabī," which is an error.

"Jābir ibn Yazīd ibn Rifāʿa al-ʿIjlī" is a trustworthy narrator of rare narrations. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/2/210, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/498.

"Ḥassān ibn Mukhāriq." al-Bukhārī said: "I think he is al-Shaybānī," and he is mentioned in al-Kabīr 2/1/31, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/2/235. The commentator on the History of al-Bukhārī said: "Among the trustworthy (thiqāt) there are two men: one of them among the Successors, Ḥassān ibn Mukhāriq al-Kūfī, who narrates from Umm Salama; Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī narrated from him. The other is among the Successors of the Successors: Ḥassān ibn Mukhāriq al-Shaybānī, and it has been said: Ḥassān ibn Abī al-Mukhāriq, Abū al-ʿAwwām, who narrates from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he used to recite: 'Can you ask your Lord.' Jābir ibn Yazīd narrated from him." Ibn Abī Ḥātim considered them to be one person.

In the printed edition it was "Ḥayyān ibn Mukhāriq," which is a misreading of what is correct in the manuscript.]]

* *

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq recited it as ﴿Can your Lord﴾ with the yāʾ, and ﴿your Lord﴾ in the nominative, meaning: "Can your Lord send down to us?" As a man says to his companion: "Are you able to rise with us in such-and-such?" while he knows that he is able, but he only means: "Will you rise with us in it?" It is also possible that the intent of the one who recites it this way is: "Will your Lord respond to you and obey you by sending down to us?"

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿Can your Lord﴾ with the yāʾ and ﴿your Lord﴾ with the nominative "rabb," meaning: "Will He respond to you if you ask Him that, and obey you in it?"

We say this is the more correct of the two readings because of what we have explained before: that His words "when the disciples said" are connected to "when I inspired," and the meaning of the speech is: "And when I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and My Messenger, when the disciples said: 'O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord?'" So it is clear, since this is the case, that God, may His remembrance be exalted, disliked what they said and considered it grave, and commanded them to repent and return to faith from their statement, and to acknowledge God's power over everything, and to affirm His Messenger in what he informed them of their Lord's reports. Jesus also said to them, when they said that to him, considering what they said grave: "Fear God, if you are believers." In God's requiring them to repent, and His calling them to faith in Him and His Messenger ﷺ when they said what they said, and the Prophet of God's ﷺ considering their word grave, there is sufficient evidence, apart from anything else, for the soundness of the reading with the yāʾ and the nominative "rabb," since there would be no sense in their saying to Jesus, had they said to him: "Can you ask your Lord to send down to us a table from heaven?" that this would be considered so grave.

If someone supposes that their saying that to him was considered grave only because that request from them was a request for a sign, [[In the printed edition: "it is in fact a consideration of their part," different from the manuscript, and it added to its text, so he struck through the speech as a meaningless corruption!! And "istaʿẓama" is in the passive voice.]] [then he is mistaken]. [[This addition between brackets is necessary; I have no doubt the copyist omitted it through carelessness, so the context of the speech and the context of Abu Ja'far's argument became disordered, and the editor was forced to tamper with Abu Ja'far's words so that they would fit, thereby clearly corrupting the speech, which is not permissible. I have restored the text to its original, as you will see in the following notes.]] For a sign is only requested by the prophets from one who denies it, so that the reality of its established occurrence and the soundness of its matter become certain to him, just as the request of the Quraysh from our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that he turn al-Ṣafā into gold for them, and make the valleys of Mecca rivers, was made by polytheists of his people; and just as the request of Ṣāliḥ for a she-camel was made by the deniers of his people; and the request of Shuʿayb that a piece of heaven fall down was made by the unbelievers to whom he was sent. [[In the printed edition: "from those to whom he was sent," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is purely correct.]]

But if those who asked Jesus to ask his Lord to send down to them a table from heaven, [[In the printed edition: "And those who asked…", deleting "fa-inna" and joining the speech together, so it became extremely disordered.]] asked it in this way, then they had placed the one who recited with the taʾ and the accusative "rabb" in a station greater than the station they thought they were keeping away from, [[In the printed edition: "from which they thought they had exalted their Lord from," meaning glorified and exalted be He, but what the editor did to the text of the manuscript made this whole speech meaningless. In the manuscript it was: "they praised their Lord," written in unclear script, which the editor misread, and he compounded the error when he altered the speech in the form in which he published it.]] or they asked that of Jesus while certain that he was a prophet sent by God and a messenger dispatched, and that God, may His remembrance be exalted, was able to do what they asked.

But if they asked that while they were in that state, and their request was only made in the manner in which one of them asks his prophet, when he is poor, to ask his Lord to make him rich, or when a need befalls him, to ask his Lord to fulfill it, then this has nothing to do with the request for a sign, but is rather the request of one with a need that has befallen him, asking his prophet to ask his Lord to fulfill it for him. [[In the printed edition: "How is that from the request of the sign," and in the manuscript: "for that," and the correct form is what I have written.]]

God's report about the people, may His remembrance be exalted, indicates otherwise. For they said to Jesus, when he said to them: "Fear God, if you are believers": "We want to eat from it, and our hearts to be reassured, and to know that you have spoken the truth to us." This statement of theirs informs us [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "informs us about their statement," which is a pure error, disrupting the context.]] that they did not know that Jesus had told them the truth, nor were their hearts reassured of the reality of his prophethood. There is no clearer statement than this, showing that the people had sickness and doubt mixed into their hearts regarding their religion and the affirmation of their Messenger, and that they asked what they asked of that as a test.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-taʾwīl) said what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

12995 – al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Layth, from ʿAqīl, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he used to narrate about Jesus ﷺ that he said to the Children of Israel: "Would you like to fast for God thirty days, then ask Him, and He will give you what you ask? For the wage of the worker is upon the one for whom he works!" So they did it, then said: "O teacher of good, you told us: 'The wage of the worker is upon the one for whom he works,' and you commanded us to fast thirty days, and we did it, and we did not work for anyone for thirty days without feeding us when we finished the food. So can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" Jesus said: "Fear God, if you are believers" – "They said: We want to eat from it, and our hearts to be reassured, and to know that you have told us the truth, and to be among its witnesses," up to His words: "I will punish him with a punishment with which I shall not punish anyone among the worlds." He said: Then the angels came flying with a table from heaven upon which were seven fishes and seven loaves, until they placed it before them, and the last of the people ate from it just as the first of them did.

12996 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me, saying: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" They said: "Will your Lord obey you if you ask Him?" So God sent down to them a table from heaven containing all food except meat, and they ate from it.

* *

As for "al-māʾida" (the table): it is the active form (fāʿila) from "māda fulān al-qawm yamīduhum maydan," when he fed them and provided for them, and from it is the verse of Ruʾba:

"We present the heads of the luxurious rivals
to the Commander of the Believers, the one who feeds [the people]" [[His Dīwān: 40; Majāz al-Qurʾān of Abū ʿUbayda 1:183; al-Lisān (mayd); and it will come in the tafsīr 12:84 (Bulaq), from a rajaz in which he praises himself and praises his people Tamīm, Saʿd and Khindif. Before it, at its end, he mentions his people:

"We suffice Quraysh against him who strives by corruption,
from every feared, obstinate, denying one,
and a heretic who mixed in the affair of atheism."

His saying "nuhdī" is with the nūn, not the tāʾ as in Lisān al-ʿArab, and as was in the printed edition here. "al-Mutrafūn": those who are pampered, who expand in the pleasures and desires of the world. "al-Andād" is the plural of "nidd" (with a kasra on the nūn), which here means "opposite": it is said of a man who opposes you, when you wanted a direction to go in and he disputes you in its opposite: "He is my nidd and my nudīdī." It also comes in the sense of "equal and like." The reading of the Dīwān, and the reading of Abu Ja'far in the place that comes after, is "al-ṣidād," the plural of "ṣādd," meaning the one who opposes and contradicts. He says: We kill those who rebel against the Commander of the Believers, then we present their heads to him, and he is the one asked, not the people.]]

By His words "al-mumtād" he means: the one who is asked for food. So "al-māʾida" is that which feeds, and the table was named "khiwān" for this reason, because it feeds the one who eats from what is upon it. And "al-māʾid" is the one turned around in the sea; it is said: "māda yamīdu maydan."

* *

As for His words: "He said: Fear God, if you are believers," it means: Jesus said to the disciples who said to him: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" – "Be mindful of God, O people, and fear Him, lest a punishment from God descend upon you for this statement of yours, for God cannot be overcome by anything He wills. In your doubt about God's power to send down a table from heaven there is disbelief in Him, so fear God lest He send down His vengeance upon you" – "if you are believers," meaning: if you affirm me regarding what I threaten you with, of God's punishment upon you for your saying: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?"

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They said: "We wish to eat from it, and that our hearts may be reassured, and that we may know that you have indeed told us the truth, and that we may be among its witnesses."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: The disciples (al-Hawariyyun), responding to Jesus' saying to them, "Fear God, if you are believers" (5:112), and their saying to him, "Can your Lord send down to us a table (ma'idah) from heaven?" (5:112), stated: We only said that, and asked you to request of our Lord for us that we may eat from the table, so that we may know with certainty His power over everything. "And that our hearts may be reassured," meaning: and that our hearts may be calm and settled in His oneness and His power to do whatever He wills and desires. [See the explanation of "al-iṭmi'nan" (reassurance) in what has preceded: 5:492 / 9:165.] "And that we may know that you have indeed told us the truth," meaning: and that we may know that you have not lied to us in your report that you are a sent messenger of God and a commissioned prophet. "And that we may be among its witnesses," meaning: and that we may be among the ones on the table, meaning: among those who testify that God sent it down as a proof for Himself against us, regarding His oneness and His power over whatever He wills, and as a proof for you, regarding the truthfulness of your prophethood. [See the explanation of "al-shahid" (witness) in the preceding linguistic indices (sh-h-d).]

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, said: "O God, our Lord, send down to us a table spread from heaven to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers."﴾ (5:114)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about His prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) that he answered the people in what they asked of him, by asking his Lord for a table spread to descend upon them from heaven.

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us." Some of them said: its meaning is: we will take the day on which it descends as a festival, which we and those after us will honour.

Those who said this:

12997 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us", he says: we will take the day on which it descended as a festival, which we and those after us will honour.

12998 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying "to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us", he said: They intended that it be for their descendants after them.

12999 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His saying: "send down to us a table from heaven to be a festival for the first of us", he said: those among them who were alive at that time; "and the last of us", those who come after them among them.

13000 - al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, who said: Sufyan said, concerning "to be a festival for us": they said: we will pray in it. It descended twice.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: we will all eat from it.

Those who said this:

13001 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Layth, from Aqil, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: He ate from it - meaning: from the table - when it was placed before them, the last of the people, just as the first of them ate from it.

* *

Others said: the meaning of His saying "festival" is a bounty from God, may His remembrance be exalted, upon us, and a proof and evidence.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: "its meaning is: it will be for us a festival, on the day it descends we shall worship our Lord and pray to Him in it, as people worship on their festivals," because what is known of the speech of people, used among them concerning "festival", is what we have mentioned, not the saying of the one who said: "its meaning is: a bounty from God upon us." Directing the meanings of God's speech toward what is known of the speech of those addressed by it is better than directing it toward what is unknown, where a way to it is found.

* *

As for His saying "for the first of us and the last of us", the more correct interpretation of it is the saying of the one who said: "its meaning: for those of us alive today, and those among us who come after us," for the reason we mentioned concerning His saying "it will be a festival for us", because that is the more predominant meaning of it.

* *

As for His saying "and a sign from You", its meaning is: a sign and proof from You, O Lord, for Your servants concerning Your oneness, and concerning the truth of my being a messenger to them with what You have sent me with [[See the explanation of "sign" in the previous indices of language (ayy).]] "And provide for us, and You are the best of providers": give us of Your bounty, for You, O Lord, are the best of givers and the most generous of benefactors, since no reproach or grudge enters into Your giving. [[And see the explanation of "provision" in the previous indices of language (rizq).]]

* *

The people of interpretation have differed concerning "the table": whether it was sent down to them or not, and what it was?

Some of them said: it was sent down, and it was fish and food; the people ate from it, but it was lifted up after it had descended because of innovations they introduced among themselves, between them and God, may His remembrance be exalted.

Those who said this:

13002 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: The table descended: bread and fish.

13003 - al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to us, from al-Fudayl, from Atiyyah, who said: "The table" was a fish in which was the taste of every food.

13004 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Fudayl, from Masruq, from Atiyyah, who said: "The table": fish in which was the taste of every food.

13005 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: The table descended, bread and fish.

13006 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It descended upon Jesus son of Mary and the disciples: a tray upon which was bread and fish, from which they ate wherever they alighted, whenever they wished.

13007 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: al-Mundhir ibn al-Nu'man informed us, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say concerning His saying: "send down to us a table from heaven to be a festival for us," he said: There descended upon them a loaf of barley and small fish. - al-Hasan said: Abu Bakr [[Abu Bakr is 'Abd al-Razzaq, namely 'Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam ibn Nafi' al-Himyari.]] said: I narrated it to Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil, and he said: I heard Wahb, and it was said to him: And did that avail them anything? He said: Nothing, but God scattered among their morsels blessing, so that a group would eat and then leave, and others would come and eat and then leave, until all of them had eaten and there was surplus.

13008 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: It is food that descended upon them wherever they alighted.

13009 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "a table from heaven," he said: a table upon which was food, which was brought to them when the punishment was presented to them if they disbelieved: varieties of food descended upon them. [[In the printed edition, this phrase was changed so thoroughly that its meaning was removed, writing: "a table upon which was food, its father when the punishment was presented to them if they disbelieved, so they refused that it descend upon them." I have kept what is in the manuscript. The meaning the first editor corrected this report to is completely opposed to this, since it is from the saying of the one who said: "no table descended upon the Children of Israel," a view narrated from Mujahid, as will come later, number 13021.]]

13010 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah: that the table descended upon Jesus son of Mary, upon it seven loaves and seven small fish, from which they ate whatever they wished. He said: Some of them stole from it and said: "Perhaps it will not descend tomorrow!" So it was lifted up.

13011 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Dawud narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from a man of the Banu Ajl, who said: I prayed beside Ammar ibn Yasir, and when he finished he said: Do you know how the matter of the table of the Children of Israel was? I said: No! He said: They asked Jesus son of Mary for a table upon which would be food they could eat from that would never run out. It was said to them: "It will remain for you as long as you do not hoard, or betray, or lift it up; but if you do, I will punish you with a punishment I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds!" So their day had not ended before they hoarded, lifted it up, and betrayed, and they were punished with a punishment that no one among the worlds had suffered. And you, company of Arabs, you used to follow the tails of camels and sheep, then God sent among you a messenger from yourselves, whose lineage and descent you know, and he informed you through the tongue of your prophet that you would prevail over the Arabs, and forbade you to hoard gold and silver. By God, the night and day will not pass until you hoard them, and He will punish you with a painful punishment.

13012 - al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah al-Basri narrated to us, who said: Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Khallas ibn Amr, from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: The table descended, bread and meat, and they were commanded not to betray, nor to store, nor to lift it up for the morrow; but they betrayed, stored, and lifted it up, so they were transformed into apes and swine. [[Report 13012: al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah ibn Ubayd al-Hashimi al-Basri, trustworthy. Passed as number 8281. Sufyan ibn Habib al-Basri, trustworthy, passed as numbers 11302, 11321. Khallas ibn Amr al-Hajari, passed several times, including 4557, 5134, and others. In the printed edition it read "Jallas ibn Amr", which is an error. Al-Tirmidhi related this report in the Book of Tafsir of his Sunan, with its chain from al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, then said: "This hadith was related by Abu Asim and others, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Khallas, from Ammar, as a mawquf report. We do not know it as marfu' except from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah. Hamid ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, similar, and did not raise it. This is more correct than the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Qaza'ah, and we do not know a basis for the marfu' hadith." See the following report, number 13014, which is the mawquf report.]]

13013 - al-Husayn ibn Qaza'ah narrated to me, who said: Yusuf ibn Khalid narrated to us, who said: Nafi' ibn Malik narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas concerning the table, he said: It was food that descended upon them from heaven wherever they alighted.

* *

Those who said this:

13014 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Khallas ibn Amr, from Ammar, who said: The table descended, and upon it was fruit of the fruits of Paradise, and they were commanded not to hide, not to betray, and not to store. He said: So the people betrayed, hid, and stored, and God transformed them into apes and swine. [[Report 13014: see the note on number 13012. In the printed edition here too it read "Jallas ibn Amr", which is an error.]]

13015 - Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that it was a table upon which fruit of the fruits of Paradise descended, and they were commanded not to hide, not to betray, and not to store for the morrow, a trial with which God tested them; and whenever they did any of that, Jesus informed them of it, but the people betrayed in it, hid, and stored for the morrow. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "abla hum Allah bihi" (a tribulation God inflicted on them), which is not correct; the correct reading is what I have written.]]

* *

Others said: upon it was every food except meat.

Those who said this:

13016 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from Maysarah, who said: When the table was placed for the Children of Israel, the hands would contend over it with every food.

13017 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ata', from Maysarah and Zadhan, who both said: The hands would contend over it with every food.

13018 - al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, who said: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Zadhan and Maysarah, concerning: "Can your Lord send down to us a table from heaven?" They both said: They saw the hands contending over it with everything except meat. [[The two reports 13017 and 13018: Zadhan al-Kindi al-Darir, passed as number 9508.]]

* *

Others said: God did not send down a table upon the Children of Israel.

* *

Then those who held this view differed.

Some of them said: this is only a parable God, may His remembrance be exalted, struck for His creation, forbidding them through it from asking the prophet of God for signs.

Those who said this:

13019 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sharik, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "send down to us a table from heaven," he said: a parable was struck; nothing descended upon them.

* *

Others said: When it was said to them: "Whoever among you disbelieves after this, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds," they asked to be excused from it, so it did not descend.

Those who said this:

13020 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: When it was said to them: "Whoever among you disbelieves after this," to the end of the verse, they said: We have no need of it, so it did not descend.

13021 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan: that he said concerning the table: It did not descend. [[Report 13021: Mansur ibn Zadhan al-Thaqafi al-Wasiti, Abu al-Mughirah, trustworthy; he related from Abu al-Aliyah, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

13022 - al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: A table upon which was food, its father when the punishment was presented to them if they disbelieved, so they refused that it descend upon them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement in our view on this matter is to say: God, may His remembrance be exalted, sent down the table upon those who asked His prophet Jesus to ask his Lord for it.

We say this because of the report that we have related to that effect from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his companions, and the people of interpretation after them, apart from those who stood alone in what we have mentioned from them.

Moreover, God, may His remembrance be exalted, does not break His promise, and no failure occurs in His report. God, may His remembrance be exalted, has said, reporting in His Book concerning the answer of His prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) when he asked what he asked: "I am sending it down upon you." It is not permissible that God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "I am sending it down upon you," and then does not send it down, for that is a report from Him, may His remembrance be exalted, and there is no contradiction to what He reports. If it were permissible for Him to say, "I am sending it down upon you," and then not send it down upon them, it would be permissible for Him to say, "Whoever among you disbelieves after this, I will punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds," and then one of them disbelieves after that and He does not punish him, so there would be no reality or validity to His promise or His threat. It is not permissible to describe our Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, with that.

* *

As for the correct statement concerning what was upon the table, it should be said: there was upon it food that could be eaten. It is possible that it was fish and bread, and it is possible that it was fruit of the fruits of Paradise; knowing it is neither beneficial nor harmful to ignorance of it, once the reciter of the verse has affirmed the apparent meaning that the revelation allows.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿God said, "Indeed I will send it down to you. But whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will surely punish him with a punishment which I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds."﴾ (5:115)

Abu Ja'far said: This is God's answer, exalted is He, to the people when they asked their Prophet Jesus to ask his Lord to send down a table (ma'idah) for them. God, exalted is He, said: "I will send it down to you, O disciples (al-Hawariyyun), and I will feed you with it. ﴿Whoever among you disbelieves after that﴾" means: whoever among you denies My messenger to him after its descent upon you and its serving as food for you, and denies the prophethood of My Prophet Jesus (ﷺ), and opposes My obedience regarding what I have commanded and forbidden, ﴿I will surely punish him with a punishment which I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds﴾, meaning among the worlds of his time.

The people did so: they denied and disbelieved after it was sent down to them, as has been related to us, and they were punished, as has reached us, by being transformed into apes and swine, as in what follows:

13023 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "Indeed I will send it down to you," (the verse), it was mentioned to us that they were transformed into swine.

13024 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab and Muhammad ibn Abi Adi and Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Awf, from Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: "Indeed the most severely punished of people are three: the hypocrites, those among the companions of the table who disbelieved, and the family of Pharaoh." [[The two reports: 13025, 13026 – "Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas", who narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr. Awf narrated from him. Abu Zur'ah was asked about his name and said: "I know of no one who names him." Sulayman al-Taymi weakened him, and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Bukhari's al-Kuna: 70, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/439.]]

13025 – al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Awf, who said: I heard Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas say: Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Indeed the most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection are: those among the companions of the table who disbelieved, the hypocrites, and the family of Pharaoh." [[The two reports: 13025, 13026 – "Abu al-Mughirah al-Qawwas", who narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr. Awf narrated from him. Abu Zur'ah was asked about his name and said: "I know of no one who names him." Sulayman al-Taymi weakened him, and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Bukhari's al-Kuna: 70, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/439.]]

13026 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: "But whoever among you disbelieves after that," after the table had come to them, "I will surely punish him with a punishment which I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds," meaning: I will punish him with a punishment which I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds other than the people of the table.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And when God says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" He will say, "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: "On the Day when God will gather the messengers and say, 'What response did you receive?'" [Qur'an 5:109] "And when God says, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"'"

* *

It was also said: God said this to Jesus when He raised him to Himself in this world.

Those who said this:

13028. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And when God says, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"'" He said: When God raised Jesus, son of Mary, to Himself, the Christians said what they said, and they claimed that Jesus had commanded them to do so. So He asked him about his words, and he said: "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. You are the Knower of the unseen," up to His words: "And You are a witness over all things."

* *

Others said: Rather, this is a report from God, exalted is He, that He will say this to Jesus on the Day of Resurrection.

Those who said this:

13029. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding "And when God says, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"'" He said: "While the people are listening, He will question him about what you have seen, and he will acknowledge his servitude for himself. Thus whoever was saying about Jesus what he was saying will know that he was only saying falsehood."

13030. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from Maysara, who said: God said: "O Jesus, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" So his joints trembled and he feared that he might have said it, and he said: "Glory be to You! If I had said it, You would have known it," [and so on to the end of the verse].

13031. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" When does this happen? He said: On the Day of Resurrection. Do you not see that He says: "This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness"? [Qur'an 5:119]

= According to this interpretation, which Ibn Jurayj adopted, "wa-idh" must mean "wa-idha" (and when), as He said elsewhere: "If only you could see when they are terrified" [Qur'an 34:51], meaning "when they are terrified." Abu al-Najm said:

"Then God rewarded him on our behalf when He rewarded
gardens of Eden in the highest upper chambers."

[Al-Adhdad by Ibn al-Anbari: 102; Al-Sahibi: 112; Lisan al-Arab (under "t-h-a"); it will come later in this part, p. 317, with an extra verse. "Al-'alali" is the plural of "'aliyyah" (with a kasra on the ayn, a doubled and kasra-marked lam, and a doubled ya): the high upper room of a house. He means by this "in 'Illiyyun," mentioned in the Qur'an. Hadbah ibn Khashram also said, with a change of wording:

"As if a [...], may God reward him with forgiveness
and a garden with upper rooms and porches."

"Al-ashra'" are the roofed porches.]

Its meaning is "when He rewarded." And as al-Aswad said: [He is al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur al-Nahshali, the 'A'sha of the Banu Nahshal.]

"Now, when he jested with them,
they say: 'Has the old man not gone the way he went?'"

[Diwan al-A'shayn: 293; Al-Adhdad by Ibn al-Anbari: 101. It is from a poem of his, most of which has been lost, and not found in printed books except this verse and five other verses in his Diwan and in al-'Ayni (margin of Khizanat al-Adab 4: 103). These are fine verses:

"A long drunkenness from him has sobered with Zaynab,
she has been his trial and his experience and has tested him.

The gray of his temples has restrained him from youth,
so how can he act young when he has become gray?

He had, in what he gained, companions
who hurried, when they met him, to say: 'Welcome!'

So they no longer ask him about what is in him,
whether he has risen in the heights of passion or descended.

Averting their gazes from him, as though
they see upon him the saddle of a black, mangy mare."]

Meaning: "when he jested with them."

It seems that whoever held Ibn Jurayj's view directed the meaning of the verse toward: "Whoever among you disbelieves after this, I will punish him with a punishment I shall not inflict on anyone among the worlds" [Qur'an 5:115] in this world, and also punish him in the Hereafter: "When God says, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?"'"

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Of the two opinions, the most correct in our view is the opinion of the one who said what al-Suddi said: that God, exalted is He, said this to Jesus when He raised him to Himself, and that the report is about something past, for two reasons:

First: "idh" in the most common usage of the Arabic language used among them accompanies the past tense of the verb, although it may occasionally enter into a report about something that will happen, when the listeners know its meaning. That is not widespread or eloquent in their speech. And directing the meanings of God's speech toward the more familiar and well-known sense, where a path to it can be found, is better than directing them toward the more obscure and objectionable.

Second: Jesus, and none of the prophets, did not doubt that God does not forgive a polytheist who dies in his polytheism. So it would be conceivable to suppose that Jesus would say in the Hereafter, answering his Lord, exalted is He: "If You punish those who took me and my mother as two gods besides You, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise."

* *

If someone asks: What was the purpose of God's question to Jesus, "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" when He knows that Jesus did not say it?

It is said: This may have two interpretive aspects. One: a warning to Jesus against saying it and a prohibition of it, as a speaker says to another, "Did you do such and such?" when the one addressed knows that the speaker considers the act he is asked about, "Did you do it?", a grave matter, as a prohibition against doing it and a threat concerning it.

The other: to inform him that his people whom he left have contradicted his covenant and changed their religion after him. Thereby the question combines informing him of their condition after him with a warning against saying it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for the meaning of the speech, it is: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods'?" that is, as two deities you worship besides God. Jesus said: Glory and exaltation be to You, O Lord, that I should do that or speak of it. ["Subhan" is explained earlier: 1: 474-476; 495; 2: 537; 6: 423.] "It is not for me to say what I have no right to say," meaning: it is not for me to say that, because I am a created servant, and my mother is a handmaid of Yours. How could a servant or a handmaid claim lordship? "If I had said it, You would have known it," meaning: nothing is hidden from You, and You know that I did not say that nor did I order them to do it.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. You are the Knower of the unseen.﴾ [5:116]

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, reporting about His prophet Jesus, peace be upon him: he declares himself innocent before Him of what the disbelieving Christians said about him and his mother, that he had called them to it or commanded them to it. So he said: "Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it." Then he said: "You know what is in my soul," meaning: O Lord, nothing is hidden from You of what my soul conceals that I have not spoken or manifested with my limbs, so how much more of what I have spoken and manifested with my limbs? It means: if I had said to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides God," You would have known it, because You know the inner thoughts of souls, what they have not spoken, so how much more what has been spoken? "And I do not know what is in Your soul," meaning: I do not know what You have hidden from me and not disclosed to me, for I only know what You have taught me. "You are the Knower of the unseen," meaning: You are the One who knows the hidden matters that no one but You perceives and that no one else knows. [On "the Knower of the unseen," see earlier: 211. On "the unseen," see 1: 236-237; 6: 405; 10: 585.]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things.﴾ (5:117)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from Allah, may He be exalted, about the words of ʿIsa (Jesus). He says: "I did not say to them except what You commanded me to say to them, which is that I said to them: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.'" ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾, meaning: I was a witness over what they did while I was among them, over their deeds and their words. [[See the explanation of "shahid" (witness) in the earlier lexical indices (sh-h-d), and of "ma dama" (as long as) at 10:185 and 11:74.]] ﴿But when You caused me to die﴾, meaning: when You took me to Yourself [[See the explanation of "tawaffa" (to cause to die / take in full) in earlier volumes: 6:455–461, 8:73, 9:100.]] ﴿You were the Watcher over them﴾, meaning: You were the Guardian over them, rather than me, because I only witnessed the deeds they performed while I was present among them.

In this is a clarification that Allah, may He be exalted, made him aware of the deeds and statements of the people only after He had taken him to Himself and caused him to die, by His words: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'"

﴿And You are Witness over all things﴾, meaning: You bear witness over all things, because nothing is hidden from You. As for me, I only witnessed some things, namely what I observed while I was living among the people. So I bear witness only to that which I observed, saw, and witnessed.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things in agreement with what we have said regarding His words "You were the Watcher over them."

Among those who said this:

13032 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding "You were the Watcher over them": as for "al-raqib" (the watcher), it is "al-hafiz" (the guardian).

13033 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj regarding "You were the Watcher over them": he said: the guardian.

* *

A group of the scholars used to say: the answer ʿIsa gave to his Lord was from Allah, the Exalted, as a form of instruction (tawqif) from Him to him concerning it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "tawfiqan" (with fa' before qaf) in this place and what follows. This is an error by the copyist and the publisher, without doubt; the correct reading is what has been established. It is said: "waqaftu al-rajul ʿala al-kalima tawqifan," when one teaches a man a word he did not know, or it was absent from him. That is, it was from Allah's teaching him, not something he said on his own.]]

Among those who said this:

13034 – Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father regarding "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?' He said: Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what is not mine by right": he said: Allah instructed him (waqqafahu). [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Allah wafaqahu" (granted him success); see the note above, and likewise in the following report.]]

13035 – Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Hafari related to us, saying: It was recited to Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father Tawus, who said: ʿIsa argued, and Allah instructed him: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" – the verse.

13036 – Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from ʿAta', from Maysara, who said: Allah, may He be remembered, said: "O ʿIsa, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah'?" He said: his joints trembled, and he feared that he might have said it, so he said: "Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what is not mine by right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Your soul. Indeed You are the Knower of the unseen."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 118:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (5:118)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If You punish these people who uttered this statement, by causing them to die upon it, ﴿then indeed they are Your servants﴾, submitting to You, unable to resist what You intend for them, and unable to repel from themselves any harm or any matter by which You afflict them; ﴿and if You forgive them﴾, by guiding them to repent from it, so that You conceal them ﴿then indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might﴾ [[See the explanations of "al-ibad" (servants), "al-maghfirah" (forgiveness), "al-aziz" (the Exalted in Might) and "al-hakim" (the Wise) in the earlier word indexes of the language (ʿ-b-d), (gh-f-r), (ʿ-z-z), (ḥ-k-m).]] in His retribution against whoever He wills to requite, none can repel it from Him; ﴿the Wise﴾, in His guidance of whoever of His creation He guides to repentance, and His granting success to whoever of them He grants success to the path of salvation from punishment, like what was narrated:

13037 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You forgive them", that You bring them out of Christianity and guide them to Islam: ﴿then indeed You, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ And this is the statement of Jesus in the world.

13038 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants, and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise", he said: By God, they were not slanderers nor cursers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 119:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿God said, "This is a day on which their truthfulness will benefit the truthful. For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying, "This is a day that benefits the truthful." Some of the people of the Hijaz and Medina recited it: ﴿هَذَا يَوْمَ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾, with "yawm" in the accusative (naṣb).

* *

Some of the people of the Hijaz and some of the people of Medina, along with most of the readers of Iraq, recited: "هَذَا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ", with "yawm" in the nominative (raf'). Whoever reads it in the nominative takes it as the predicate of "hadha" and makes "yawm" the subject, even though its idafa (construction) is not pure (maḥḍah), because it has become like a qualified noun. [[In the printed edition: "because it has become", with "qad" omitted.]]

Some scholars of Arabic grammar claimed that the Arabs treat time expressions such as "al-yawm" (today) and "al-layla" (tonight) in their i'rab (grammatical inflection) in the same way they treat what follows them. If what follows is in the nominative, they put it in the nominative, as in their saying: "Hadha yawmu yarkabu al-amir" (This is a day when the commander rides), "Laylatu yaṣdiru al-ḥājj" (A night when the pilgrim returns), and "Yawmu akhūka munṭaliq" (The day your brother sets out). If what follows is in the accusative, they put it in the accusative, as in their saying: "Hadha yawma kharaja al-jaysh, wa sara al-nas" (This is the day the army went out and the people travelled), and "Laylata qutila Zayd" (The night Zayd was killed), and similar expressions, and in both cases the meaning is "idh" and "idha".

* *

It seems that whoever reads it this way in the nominative directs the speech to being the words of God on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

Likewise, al-Suddi used to say this.

13039 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said concerning God's words, "This is a day when their truthfulness will benefit the truthful": this is a separate part of the speech of Jesus, and this is the Day of Resurrection.

* *

al-Suddi, by his saying, "This is a separate part of the speech of Jesus," means that His saying, "Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to say..." up to His saying, "Indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise," is God's report about Jesus that he said it in this world after He had raised him to Himself, and that what follows that is the speech of God to His servants on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for the accusative in this, it can be justified in two ways:

First: the idafa of "yawm" when it is not to a noun makes it accusative, because the idafa is not pure. A pure idafa occurs only when it is to a definite noun. Similar to "al-yawm" in this are "al-ḥīn" (the time) and "al-zamān" (the era), and similar time expressions, as al-Nabigha said:

"At the time I reproached old age for youth, and said: Will you not yet awaken, while grey hair restrains?"

* *

Second: the speech may be intended as: "This matter and this affair, a day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful," so "al-yawm" is then accusative as a time and as a description, meaning: this matter is on a day when the truthfulness of the truthful benefits them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is ﴿هَذَا يَوْمَ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ with "al-yawm" in the accusative, as being accusative for time and description. This is because the meaning of the speech is that God, exalted is His remembrance, answered Jesus when he said, "Glory be to You, it is not for me to say what I have no right to say... if I had said it, You would have known it... Indeed You are the Almighty, the Wise," so God said to him: this is the beneficial speech, or this is the beneficial truthfulness, on a day when the truthfulness of the truthful benefits them. So "al-yawm" is the time of the speech and the beneficial truthfulness.

* *

If someone says: What is the position of "hadha"?

It is said: it is in the nominative.

If he asks: Where is its governing element? It is said: it is implied. It is as if He said: God said: This, this is a day when their truthfulness benefits the truthful, just as the poet said: [[I do not know this rajiz (poet)]]

"Do you not see how the clouds move? This, and not your horses, O son of Bishr!"

He means: this, this, and not your horses.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the speech, given that the matter is as we have described it for the reasons we have shown, is: God said to Jesus: this is the beneficial speech, on a day when the truthfulness of the truthful benefits them in the world, that is, in the Hereafter with God. "For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow" means: for the truthful in this world are gardens beneath which rivers flow in the Hereafter, as a reward for them from God, exalted is He, for their truthfulness in what they promised God, and they fulfilled it for God, and God fulfilled for them what He had promised them of His reward. "Abiding therein forever" means: remaining in the gardens which He gave them, "forever," lasting, and they have in them a bliss that does not move from them and does not cease.

* *

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of "khulūd" (abiding) is permanence and continuance.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great triumph.﴾ (119)

Abu Ja'far said: May He, exalted is His remembrance, say: God is pleased with these truthful ones who were true in fulfilling what they promised Him, by acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience. "And they are pleased with Him" means: and they are pleased with God, exalted is His remembrance, in His fulfilment to them of what He promised them for their obedience to Him in what He commanded and forbade, of His abundant reward. "That is the great triumph" means: this which God gave them of the gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, being pleased with them and well pleased with their Lord, is the great success in attaining what they sought, and the fulfilment of the need which they used to seek in the world and for which they used to work, so they attained what they sought and reached what they hoped for.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 120:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things Competent.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says: O Christians, "To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth," meaning: to Him belongs authority over the heavens and the earth [see the explanation of "al-mulk" (dominion) above, 8:480, footnote 3, and the references there] "and whatever is in them," apart from Jesus, whom you claim to be your god, and apart from his mother, and apart from all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth. For the heavens and the earth are creatures of His creation, and so are whatever is in them; and Jesus and his mother are among that, by indwelling and movement. Their being in the place they occupy, by indwelling in it and moving, proves that they are two servants owned by the One who has dominion over the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. He draws their attention, and that of all His creation, to the place of His proof against them, so that they may reflect upon it, take heed of it, and understand from it. "And He is over all things Competent" [see the explanation of "qadir" (competent) above in the lexical indexes, under the root q-d-r]. The Exalted says: Allah, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, is able to annihilate them and to destroy them, and to destroy Jesus, his mother, and all who are on the earth together, just as He originated their creation. That is not beyond His power, nor anything else He wills, because His power is a power to which no power is comparable, and His authority is an authority which no authority or kingdom resembles.

* *

﴿End of the commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah﴾ [At this point ends a section of the old division from which our copy was taken, and in it is the following text:

"End of the commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah. May Allah bless our master Muhammad, his family, and grant them abundant peace. There is no power nor might except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty. Following it, God willing, is the Tafsir of Surah al-An'am. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."]
